abaeis nicippe.name: Orange-tip
abaeis nicippe.desc: Orange-tip (Abaeis nicippe): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
abaeis nicippe.about: Eurema nicippe, the sleepy orange, is a North American butterfly in the family Pieridae.

abies.name: Fir and conifer forest
abies.desc: Conifer forest covers the high slopes where the monkeys live and gives seeds, shade and winter shelter.
abies.about: Firs are coniferous trees belonging to the genus Abies (Latin: [ˈabieːs]) in the family Pinaceae.

abies alba.name: Silver fir
abies alba.desc: A conifer that grows with beech in the mixed beech-fir stands that cover much of the Poloniny uplands.

abies balsamea.name: Balsam fir
abies balsamea.desc: A northern conifer of the spruce-fir forest that covers most of the park's vegetated land. Deer, hares and squirrels all feed on it.
abies balsamea.about: Abies balsamea or balsam fir is a North American fir, native to most of eastern and central Canada and the northeastern United States.

abies concolor.name: Colorado White-fir
abies concolor.desc: Colorado White-fir (Abies concolor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 761 times near the park in GBIF.

abies fargesii.name: Farges's fir
abies fargesii.desc: A conifer of the cool upper slopes. Conifer forest at higher elevations shelters the wildlife of the Qionglai range.
abies fargesii.about: Abies fargesii (Chinese: 巴山冷杉) is a species of fir, a coniferous tree in the family Pinaceae.

abies fraseri.name: Fraser fir
abies fraseri.desc: Grows near the highest summits. The balsam woolly adelgid killed most mature firs from the 1960s on, though young firs are regrowing on some peaks.
abies fraseri.about: Abies fraseri, commonly known as Fraser's fir, or Fraser fir, is an endangered species of fir in the order Pinales native to the Appalachian Mountains of the southeastern United States.

abies grandis.name: Giant Fir
abies grandis.desc: Giant Fir (Abies grandis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
abies grandis.about: Abies grandis is a fir native to northwestern North America, occurring at altitudes of sea level to 1,700 metres (5,600 ft).

abies lasiocarpa.name: Subalpine fir
abies lasiocarpa.desc: Grows at and just below the tree line. Its seeds feed birds and squirrels, and its clumps trap snow and help form meadows.
abies lasiocarpa.about: Abies lasiocarpa, the subalpine fir or Rocky Mountain fir, is a western North American fir tree.

abies magnifica.name: Red fir
abies magnifica.desc: A tall fir of the snowy Cascade slopes, and a common conifer in the park forests.
abies magnifica.about: Abies magnifica, the red fir or silvertip fir, is a western North American fir, native to the mountains of southwest Oregon and California in the United States.

abies nordmanniana.name: Nordmann fir
abies nordmanniana.desc: A tall mountain conifer growing at roughly 900 to 2,200 m. The Caucasus reserve was founded in 1924 partly to protect its giant firs.
abies nordmanniana.about: Abies nordmanniana, the Nordmann fir or Caucasian fir, is a fir indigenous to the mountains south and east of the Black Sea, in Turkey, Georgia and the Russian Caucasus.

abies religiosa.name: Oyamel fir
abies religiosa.desc: A cloud-forest conifer of central Mexican mountains. Overwintering monarchs gather in its forests, and UNESCO says keeping the standing forest and its microclimates is the key management need.
abies religiosa.about: Abies religiosa, the oyamel fir or sacred fir, (known as oyamel in Spanish) is a fir native to the mountains of central and southern Mexico and western Guatemala.

abies spectabilis, juniperus.name: Fir and juniper
abies spectabilis, juniperus.desc: Conifers of the subalpine forest, which Wikipedia says holds fir, birch and rhododendron above about 3,000 m.
abies spectabilis, juniperus.about: Abies spectabilis, the East Himalayan fir, is a conifer species in the family Pinaceae and the genus Abies. It is sometimes held to include the Bhutan fir (A. densa) as a variety.

abronia fragrans.name: Heart's-delight
abronia fragrans.desc: Heart's-delight (Abronia fragrans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
abronia fragrans.about: Abronia fragrans, the sweet sand-verbena, snowball sand-verbena, prairie snowball or fragrant verbena, is a species of sand verbena.

abrothrix olivaceus.name: Olive grass mouse
abrothrix olivaceus.desc: A small rodent of steppe and forest edge, eating seeds, plants and insects. It is staple prey for foxes and raptors.
abrothrix olivaceus.about: Abrothrix olivacea, also known as the olive grass mouse or olive akodont, is a species of rodent in the genus Abrothrix of family Cricetidae.

abrus precatorius.name: Crab's eye vine
abrus precatorius.desc: A climbing legume recorded on the island. GloBI lists it as food for the Common Blue butterfly.
abrus precatorius.about: Abrus precatorius, commonly known as jequirity bean or rosary pea, is a herbaceous flowering plant in the bean family Fabaceae.

acacia aneura.name: Mulga
acacia aneura.desc: A shrub or small tree of arid Australia that gives its name to the mulga woodlands. Listed as a dominant tree of the park.
acacia aneura.about: Acacia aneura, commonly known as mulga, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to inland Australia.

acacia dealbata.name: Silver wattle
acacia dealbata.desc: A wattle that colonises gaps and burnt ground at forest edges; black cockatoos are recorded eating its seeds.
acacia dealbata.about: Acacia dealbata, commonly known as silver wattle, blue wattle or mimosa, is a species of flowering plant in the legume family, Fabaceae.

acacia koa.name: Koa
acacia koa.desc: A native forest tree whose leaves feed caterpillars and other insects, and whose crowns shelter forest birds.
acacia koa.about: Acacia koa, commonly known as koa, is a species of flowering tree in the family Fabaceae. It is endemic to the Hawaiian Islands, where it is the second most common tree.

acacia ligulata.name: Dune wattle
acacia ligulata.desc: A common scrub of coastal dunes and sandplains. Banded hare-wallabies favour thickets of it for shelter, and its seeds and foliage feed other animals.
acacia ligulata.about: Acacia ligulata is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae. It is a dense, rounded shrub with bright yellow flower heads and is widespread in all states of mainland Australia.

acalypha radians.name: Cardinal feather
acalypha radians.desc: Cardinal feather (Acalypha radians): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

acanthacris ruficornis.name: Garden locust
acanthacris ruficornis.desc: A large grasshopper that chews grasses and other plants and feeds reptiles and birds.
acanthacris ruficornis.about: Locusts are various species of short-horned grasshoppers in the family Acrididae that have a swarming phase.

acanthaster planci.name: Crown-of-thorns starfish
acanthaster planci.desc: A starfish that eats hard coral polyps. Outbreaks can strip large areas of living coral.
acanthaster planci.about: The crown-of-thorns starfish is a large starfish that preys upon hard coral polyps.

acanthis flammea.name: Common redpoll
acanthis flammea.desc: A small finch that eats seeds and shoots. GloBI records it eating grasses and horsetail.
acanthis flammea.about: The redpoll is a species of small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Acanthis.

acanthocercus annectans.name: Eritrean ridgeback agama
acanthocercus annectans.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard that eats insects and is itself prey for snakes and raptors.
acanthocercus annectans.about: Acanthocercus is a genus of lizards in the family Agamidae. The genus is endemic to Africa and the Arabian Peninsula.

acanthodactylus boskianus.name: Bosc's fringe-toed lizard
acanthodactylus boskianus.desc: A fast, insect-eating lizard of sandy and gravelly ground. Lizards are a major food for birds and snakes here.
acanthodactylus boskianus.about: Bosc's fringe-toed lizard or Bosk's [sic] fringe-fingered lizard is a species of lizard in the family Lacertidae. The species is endemic to North Africa and Western Asia.

acanthogammarus and relatives.name: Baikal amphipods
acanthogammarus and relatives.desc: A very diverse endemic group. Some are mostly carnivorous, others eat detritus, and the high oxygen of the lake is linked to the giant size of some.

acanthosicyos horridus.name: Nara melon
acanthosicyos horridus.desc: A spiny, leafless melon plant of coastal dunes that fruits for animals and people. Its roots tap deep water.
acanthosicyos horridus.about: Acanthosicyos horridus is an unusual melon that is endemic to the Namib desert.

acanthuridae.name: Surgeonfish
acanthuridae.desc: Grazes algae in schools so seaweed does not overgrow corals.
acanthuridae.about: The Acanthuridae are a family of ray-finned fishes, which includes surgeonfishes, tangs, and unicornfishes.

acanthurus.name: Surgeonfish
acanthurus.desc: Schooling fish that graze algae around coral reefs.
acanthurus.about: The Acanthuridae are a family of ray-finned fishes, which includes surgeonfishes, tangs, and unicornfishes.

accipiter cooperii.name: Cooper's hawk
accipiter cooperii.desc: A bird-hunting hawk that nests in urban parks. Robins and starlings are the most commonly reported prey, with doves and house sparrows also taken.
accipiter cooperii.about: Cooper's hawk is a medium-sized hawk native to the North American continent and found from southern Canada to Mexico. This species was formerly placed in the genus Accipiter.

accipiter nisus.name: Eurasian sparrowhawk
accipiter nisus.desc: A woodland hawk that hunts small birds such as finches and tits.
accipiter nisus.about: The Eurasian sparrowhawk, also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.

accipiter rufitorques.name: Fiji goshawk
accipiter rufitorques.desc: Fiji's top forest raptor; it takes birds up to pigeon size, reptiles, insects and rodents.
accipiter rufitorques.about: The Fiji goshawk is a species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. It was once considered to be the same species (conspecific) as the brown goshawk of Australia and New Caledonia.

accipiter striatus.name: Sharp-shinned hawk
accipiter striatus.desc: A small woodland hawk that hunts birds and small mammals, including red squirrels.
accipiter striatus.about: The sharp-shinned hawk or northern sharp-shinned hawk, colloquially often nicknamed sharpie, is a small hawk, with males being the smallest hawks in the United States and Canada, but with the species…

acer.name: Maples & other broadleaf trees
acer.desc: Maples, limes and other broadleaf trees mixed into the forest, offering leaves, twigs and bark to browsers.
acer.about: Acer pictum, commonly known as yellow-paint maple, is an Asian species of maple. It widespread across much of China as well as Korea, Japan, Mongolia, and eastern Russia.

acer circinatum.name: Vine maple
acer circinatum.desc: Vine maple (Acer circinatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 66 times near the park in GBIF.
acer circinatum.about: Acer circinatum, or vine maple, is a species of maple native to northwestern North America.

acer davidii.name: Father David's maple
acer davidii.desc: A broadleaf tree of the mid-elevation mixed forest; leaves and buds feed browsers.
acer davidii.about: Acer davidii, or Père David's maple, is a species of maple in the snakebark maple group. It is native to China, from Jiangsu south to Fujian and Guangdong, and west to southeastern Gansu and Yunnan.

acer macrophyllum.name: Pacific maple
acer macrophyllum.desc: Pacific maple (Acer macrophyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
acer macrophyllum.about: Acer macrophyllum, the bigleaf maple or Oregon maple, is a large deciduous tree in the genus Acer. It is native to western North America.

acer negundo.name: Ashleaf Maple
acer negundo.desc: Ashleaf Maple (Acer negundo): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 56 times near the park in GBIF.
acer negundo.about: Acer negundo, also known as the box elder, boxelder maple, Manitoba maple or ash-leaved maple, is a species of maple native to North America from Canada to Honduras.

acer pensylvanicum.name: Goosefoot
acer pensylvanicum.desc: Goosefoot (Acer pensylvanicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
acer pensylvanicum.about: Acer pensylvanicum, known as the striped maple, moosewood, whistlewood, moose maple or goosefoot maple, is a North American species of maple.

acer platanoides.name: Norway Maple
acer platanoides.desc: Norway maple (Acer platanoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 891 times near the park in GBIF.
acer platanoides.about: Acer platanoides, commonly known as the Norway maple, is a species of maple native to eastern and central Europe and western Asia, from Spain east to Russia, north to southern Scandinavia and…

acer rubrum.name: Red maple
acer rubrum.desc: Red maple (Acer rubrum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
acer rubrum.about: Acer rubrum, the red maple, also known as swamp maple, water maple, or soft maple, is a North American tree species. Many of its features, especially its deciduous leaves, are quite variable in form.

acer saccharinum.name: Red Maple
acer saccharinum.desc: Red Maple (Acer saccharinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
acer saccharinum.about: Acer saccharinum, commonly known as silver maple, creek maple, silverleaf maple, soft maple, large maple, water maple, swamp maple, or white maple, is a species of maple native to the eastern and…

acer saccharum.name: Sugar maple
acer saccharum.desc: Sugar maple (Acer saccharum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
acer saccharum.about: Acer saccharum, the sugar maple, is a species of flowering plant in the soapberry and lychee family, Sapindaceae.

acer spicatum.name: Mountain maple
acer spicatum.desc: A shrubby understory maple, also called moose maple. Moose, hares and beavers browse it.
acer spicatum.about: Acer spicatum, the mountain maple, dwarf maple, moose maple, or white maple, is a species of maple native to northeastern North America from Saskatchewan to Newfoundland, and south to Pennsylvania.

acer spp..name: Maples & other street trees
acer spp..desc: Maples, along with ash and other street trees, shade neighborhoods and feed leaf-eating insects, with buds and seeds for squirrels.
acer spp..about: Acer is a genus of trees and shrubs commonly known as maples. The genus is placed in the soapberry family Sapindaceae.

acharia stimulea.name: Saddleback Caterpillar Moth
acharia stimulea.desc: Saddleback Caterpillar Moth (Acharia stimulea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.
acharia stimulea.about: The saddleback caterpillar is the larva of a species of moth native to eastern North America. It is also found in Mexico.

achillea millefolium.name: Yarrow
achillea millefolium.desc: Yarrow (Achillea millefolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
achillea millefolium.about: Achillea millefolium, commonly known as yarrow () or common yarrow, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

achlys triphylla.name: Deerfoot
achlys triphylla.desc: Deerfoot (Achlys triphylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.
achlys triphylla.about: Achlys triphylla, with the common names deer foot, vanilla leaf, or sweet after death, is a plant species native to the mountains of the West Coast of North America.

achnatherum hymenoides.name: Indian ricegrass
achnatherum hymenoides.desc: A tufted desert grass of sandy soils that is listed among the common plants of Arches. Its seeds are food for desert rodents.
achnatherum hymenoides.about: Eriocoma hymenoides is a cool-season, perennial bunchgrass. It is native to western North America.

achyrachaena mollis.name: Blow wives
achyrachaena mollis.desc: Blow wives (Achyrachaena mollis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
achyrachaena mollis.about: The only species in the monotypic genus Achyrachaena is the annual herb Achyrachaena mollis, which bears the common name blow-wives. The genus name is both singular and plural.

achyranthes bidentata.name: Pig's knee
achyranthes bidentata.desc: Pig's knee (Achyranthes bidentata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

acidic forest soil.name: Acidic forest soil
acidic forest soil.desc: Needle litter makes cool, acidic soils that break down slowly.

acidic peat soil.name: Acidic peat soil
acidic peat soil.desc: Buttongrass moor grows on damp, nutrient-poor, acidic peat soils in western Tasmania.

acinonyx jubatus.name: Cheetah
acinonyx jubatus.desc: Sprints after gazelles on open plains, often losing kills to larger predators.
acinonyx jubatus.about: The cheetah is a species of large feline and the only living member of the genus Acinonyx.

acinonyx jubatus hecki.name: Saharan cheetah
acinonyx jubatus hecki.desc: A critically endangered cheetah that hunts desert antelope and gazelles and gets water from its prey.
acinonyx jubatus hecki.about: The Northwest African cheetah, also known as the Saharan cheetah, is a cheetah subspecies living in the Sahara and the Sahel. It is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.

acleisanthes longiflora.name: Angel trumpet
acleisanthes longiflora.desc: Angel trumpet (Acleisanthes longiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

acmella repens.name: Oppositeleaf spotflower
acmella repens.desc: Oppositeleaf spotflower (Acmella repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
acmella repens.about: Acmella repens is a North American species of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.

acmispon glaber.name: California broom
acmispon glaber.desc: California broom (Acmispon glaber): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 373 times near the park in GBIF.

acomys dimidiatus.name: Spiny mouse
acomys dimidiatus.desc: A rocky-desert rodent that eats seeds and small invertebrates and is prey for foxes and owls.
acomys dimidiatus.about: The term spiny mouse refers to any species of rodent within the genus Acomys.

acraea.name: Acraea butterflies
acraea.desc: A large genus of butterflies, many species recorded in the Nyungwe area. Adults visit flowers for nectar.
acraea.about: Acraea (Ancient Greek: Ἀκραία means 'of the heights' from akraios) was a name that had several uses in Greek and Roman mythology.

acrantophis madagascariensis.name: Madagascar ground boa
acrantophis madagascariensis.desc: A ground-dwelling constrictor that preys on ring-tailed lemurs and other small animals.
acrantophis madagascariensis.about: Acrantophis madagascariensis is a species of boid snake in the subfamily Sanziniinae that is endemic to the island of Madagascar.

acrididae.name: Grasshoppers
acrididae.desc: Plant-eating insects that feed on grasses. They are prey for lizards, birds and small mammals.
acrididae.about: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.

acrocephalus griseldis.name: Basra reed warbler
acrocephalus griseldis.desc: Breeds in dense reed and papyrus beds of the Tigris-Euphrates system. Drainage nearly destroyed its habitat and it is endangered.
acrocephalus griseldis.about: The Basra reed warbler is a "warbler" of the genus Acrocephalus.

acrocodia indica.name: Malayan tapir
acrocodia indica.desc: Solitary herbivore that eats shoots and leaves from over a hundred plant species; recorded repeatedly in the reserve.
acrocodia indica.about: The Malayan tapir, also called Asian tapir, Asiatic tapir, oriental tapir, Indian tapir, piebald tapir, or black-and-white tapir, is the only living tapir species outside of the Americas.

acromyrmex versicolor.name: Desert Leaf-cutter Ant
acromyrmex versicolor.desc: Desert Leaf-cutter Ant (Acromyrmex versicolor): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
acromyrmex versicolor.about: Acromyrmex versicolor is known as the desert leafcutter ant. A. versicolor is found during the summer months in the Colorado and Sonoran deserts when there is precipitation.

acronicta americana.name: American Dagger Moth
acronicta americana.desc: American Dagger Moth (Acronicta americana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
acronicta americana.about: Acronicta americana, the American dagger moth, is a moth of the family Noctuidae. It was originally described by Thaddeus William Harris in 1841 and is native to North America.

acronicta insita.name: Large Gray Dagger
acronicta insita.desc: Large Gray Dagger (Acronicta insita): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
acronicta insita.about: Acronicta insita, the large gray dagger or fingered dagger, is a moth of the family Noctuidae. The species was first described by Augustus Radcliffe Grote in 1874.

acronicta longa.name: Long-winged Dagger
acronicta longa.desc: Long-winged Dagger (Acronicta longa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
acronicta longa.about: Acronicta longa, the long-winged dagger moth, is a moth of the family Noctuidae. The species was first described by Achille Guenée in 1852.

acropora.name: Reef-building corals
acropora.desc: Branching corals build the reef structure. They catch plankton and shelter many fish.
acropora.about: Acropora is a genus of small polyp stony coral in the phylum Cnidaria. Some of its species are known as table coral, elkhorn coral, and staghorn coral.

acropora palmata.name: Elkhorn coral
acropora palmata.desc: Branching reef-builder of the shallow reef crest. It takes in food from plankton as well as from its algal partners.
acropora palmata.about: Elkhorn coral is an important reef-building coral in the Caribbean. The species has a complex structure with many branches which resemble that of elk antlers; hence, the common name.

acropora spp..name: Reef-building coral
acropora spp..desc: Builds the limestone reef that shelters thousands of other species. It bleaches when warm water drives out its algae.
acropora spp..about: Acropora is a genus of small polyp stony coral in the phylum Cnidaria. Some of its species are known as table coral, elkhorn coral, and staghorn coral.

actaea pachypoda.name: Baneberry
actaea pachypoda.desc: Baneberry (Actaea pachypoda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

actaea rubra.name: Red Baneberry
actaea rubra.desc: Red Baneberry (Actaea rubra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

actias luna.name: Luna Moth
actias luna.desc: Luna Moth (Actias luna): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
actias luna.about: The luna moth, also called the American moon moth, is a Nearctic moth in the family Saturniidae, subfamily Saturniinae, a group commonly named the giant silk moths.

actinopterygii.name: Forest river fish
actinopterygii.desc: Salonga holds dozens of fish species. They feed on insects and other small animals and are the main food of dwarf crocodiles in the Congo basin.
actinopterygii.about: A fish is an aquatic, anamniotic, gill-bearing vertebrate with a tough cranium to protect the brain. Many fish have fins that they use for directional stability and propulsion.

adalia bipunctata.name: Two-spot Ladybird
adalia bipunctata.desc: Two-spot Ladybird (Adalia bipunctata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

adansonia digitata.name: Baobab
adansonia digitata.desc: A huge, long-lived tree of dry savanna, recorded in the park.
adansonia digitata.about: Adansonia digitata, the African baobab, is the most widespread tree species of the genus Adansonia, the baobabs, and is native to the African continent and the southern Arabian Peninsula (Yemen,…

adansonia grandidieri.name: Grandidier's baobab
adansonia grandidieri.desc: Giant water-storing tree of seasonal dry forest. Its flowers open at dusk and are pollinated by hawk moths and nocturnal lemurs.
adansonia grandidieri.about: Adansonia grandidieri is the biggest and most famous of Madagascar's six species of baobabs. It is sometimes known as Grandidier's baobab or the giant baobab.

addax nasomaculatus.name: Addax
addax nasomaculatus.desc: A critically endangered antelope that grazes desert grasses and browses shrubs, and can go a very long time without drinking.
addax nasomaculatus.about: The addax, also known as the white antelope and the screwhorn antelope, is an antelope native to the Sahara.

adelges tsugae.name: Hemlock Woolly Adelgid
adelges tsugae.desc: Hemlock Woolly Adelgid (Adelges tsugae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

adelinia grande.name: Grand Hound's Tongue
adelinia grande.desc: Grand Hound's Tongue (Adelinia grande): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 398 times near the park in GBIF.

adenostoma fasciculatum.name: Chamise
adenostoma fasciculatum.desc: A fire-adapted shrub that makes up much of the park chaparral. Wikipedia says it resprouts from its base after fire and its seeds germinate after burns.
adenostoma fasciculatum.about: Adenostoma fasciculatum, commonly known as chamise or greasewood, is a flowering plant native to California and Baja California.

adesmia cancellata.name: Pitted beetle
adesmia cancellata.desc: A darkling beetle of arid Middle Eastern habitats, recorded in the Al Reem area. It is food for lizards, birds and shrikes.
adesmia cancellata.about: Adesmia cancellata, the pitted beetle, is a species of desert beetle of the Tenebrionidae family that inhabits arid environments in the Middle East.

adiantum aleuticum.name: Aleutian maidenhair
adiantum aleuticum.desc: Aleutian maidenhair (Adiantum aleuticum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
adiantum aleuticum.about: Adiantum aleuticum, the western maidenhair fern or Aleutian maidenhair, is a species of deciduous fern in the genus Adiantum.

adiantum capillus-veneris.name: Maidenhair Fern
adiantum capillus-veneris.desc: Maidenhair Fern (Adiantum capillus-veneris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
adiantum capillus-veneris.about: Adiantum capillus-veneris, the maidenhair fern, southern maidenhair fern, black maidenhair fern and venus hair fern, is a species of ferns in the genus Adiantum and the family Pteridaceae with a…

adiantum pedatum.name: Northern maidenhair
adiantum pedatum.desc: Maidenfern (Adiantum pedatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.
adiantum pedatum.about: Adiantum pedatum, the northern maidenhair fern, is a species of fern in the family Pteridaceae, native to moist forests in eastern North America.

aedes vexans.name: Vexans Mosquito
aedes vexans.desc: Vexans Mosquito (Aedes vexans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
aedes vexans.about: Aedes vexans, commonly known as the inland floodwater mosquito or tomguito, is a widespread and frequently encountered pest mosquito with a cosmopolitan distribution, occurring across North America,…

aegilops.name: Steppe grasses
aegilops.desc: Wild goatgrasses and other grasses grow on the dry steppe and meadows, which together are a large part of the reserve.
aegilops.about: Aegilops is a genus of Eurasian and North American plants in the grass family, Poaceae. They are known generally as goatgrasses.

aegypius monachus.name: Cinereous vulture
aegypius monachus.desc: A huge vulture that feeds mostly on carrion, such as dead wild and domestic hoofed animals, and also takes marmots.
aegypius monachus.about: The cinereous vulture, also known as the black vulture, Eurasian black vulture, and monk vulture, is a very large raptor in the family Accipitridae distributed through much of temperate Eurasia.

aeorestes semotus.name: ʻŌpeʻapeʻa (Hawaiian hoary bat)
aeorestes semotus.desc: The native land mammal. It is a generalist insect eater that mainly takes moths and beetles, in open areas and in forest.
aeorestes semotus.about: The Hawaiian hoary bat, also known as ʻōpeʻapeʻa, is a species of bat endemic to the islands of Hawaiʻi.

aepyceros melampus.name: Impala
aepyceros melampus.desc: A very common antelope, eaten by lions, leopards, wild dogs and hyenas.
aepyceros melampus.about: The impala or rooibok is a medium-sized antelope found in eastern and southern Africa.

aesculus glabra.name: Ohio buckeye
aesculus glabra.desc: Ohio buckeye (Aesculus glabra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

aesculus pavia.name: Red Buckeye
aesculus pavia.desc: Red Buckeye (Aesculus pavia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.
aesculus pavia.about: Aesculus pavia, known as red buckeye or firecracker plant, is a species of deciduous flowering plant.

aethopyga temminckii.name: Temminck's sunbird
aethopyga temminckii.desc: A small nectar-feeding bird of Bornean mountain forest, among the most recorded birds near the park.
aethopyga temminckii.about: Temminck's sunbird is a species of sunbird. It is found in up to 1800 m altitude in Borneo, Sumatra, West Malaysia, and south west Thailand in tropical moist montane forests.

aetobatus narinari.name: Spotted eagle ray
aetobatus narinari.desc: Ray that crushes conch and other shelled prey on sandy flats near the reef.
aetobatus narinari.about: The spotted eagle ray is a cartilaginous fish of the eagle ray family, Aetobatidae.

aframomum.name: Aframomum herbs
aframomum.desc: Ground-layer herbs of the ginger family. On Afi Mountain they made up most of the diet of Cross River gorillas.
aframomum.about: Aframomum is a genus of flowering plants in the ginger family, Zingiberaceae.

afropavo congensis.name: Congo peafowl
afropavo congensis.desc: Endemic to the Congo Basin and found in both old and regrowing forest in Salonga. Eats fruit, insects, spiders, snails and worms.
afropavo congensis.about: The Congo peafowl, also known as the African peafowl or mbulu by the Bakôngo, is a species native to the Congo Basin.

afruca tangeri.name: West African fiddler crab
afruca tangeri.desc: Burrowing crab of muddy flats that feeds on organic matter in the sediment and is itself prey for birds and octopus.
afruca tangeri.about: Afruca is a genus of fiddler crabs belonging to the family Ocypodidae. Afruca tangeri, the only species in this genus, lives along the Atlantic coasts of western Africa and southwestern Europe.

agalinis fasciculata.name: Beach false foxglove
agalinis fasciculata.desc: Beach false foxglove (Agalinis fasciculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

agalinis purpurea.name: Purple False Foxglove
agalinis purpurea.desc: Purple False Foxglove (Agalinis purpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

agama agama.name: Common agama
agama agama.desc: A sun-loving lizard that eats mainly ants, grasshoppers, beetles and termites. Males hold territories around trees or rocks.
agama agama.about: The common agama or red-headed rock agama is a species of lizard from the family Agamidae found in most of sub-Saharan Africa and in Florida where it has spread.

agama atra.name: Southern rock agama
agama atra.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard that feeds mainly on insects and is prey for raptors.

agama picticauda.name: Red-headed agama
agama picticauda.desc: Red-headed agama (Agama picticauda): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 187 times near the park in GBIF.

agapostemon texanus.name: Texas Agapostemon
agapostemon texanus.desc: Texas Agapostemon (Agapostemon texanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
agapostemon texanus.about: Agapostemon texanus is a species of bee found in North America.

agarista populifolia.name: Pipeplant
agarista populifolia.desc: Pipeplant (Agarista populifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

agastache foeniculum.name: Blue giant-hyssop
agastache foeniculum.desc: Blue giant-hyssop (Agastache foeniculum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

agave deserti.name: Desert agave
agave deserti.desc: Desert agave (Agave deserti): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1,172 times near the park in GBIF.

agave lechuguilla.name: Lechuguilla
agave lechuguilla.desc: An indicator plant of the Chihuahuan Desert that spreads by underground offshoots into large colonies. Collared peccaries eat much of it in some areas.
agave lechuguilla.about: Agave lechuguilla (common name in Chihuahua: lechuguilla, meaning "small lettuce") is an Agave species found only in the Chihuahuan Desert. The plant flowers once in its life and then dies.

agave palmeri.name: Century plant
agave palmeri.desc: Century plant (Agave palmeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 113 times near the park in GBIF.
agave palmeri.about: Agave palmeri (also known as Palmer's century plant) is an especially large member of the genus Agave, in the family Asparagaceae.

agave parryi.name: Parry's agave
agave parryi.desc: Parry's agave (Agave parryi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 91 times near the park in GBIF.
agave parryi.about: Agave parryi, known as Parry's agave or mescal agave, is a flowering plant in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Agavoideae.

agelaius phoeniceus.name: Red-winged Blackbird
agelaius phoeniceus.desc: Red-winged Blackbird (Agelaius phoeniceus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 129 times near the park in GBIF.
agelaius phoeniceus.about: The red-winged blackbird is a passerine bird of the family Icteridae found in most of North America and much of Central America.

ageratina altissima.name: Richweed
ageratina altissima.desc: Richweed (Ageratina altissima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

agkistrodon conanti.name: Florida cottonmouth
agkistrodon conanti.desc: A venomous water snake that eats frogs, fish and other small animals around swamp water.
agkistrodon conanti.about: The Florida cottonmouth is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.

agkistrodon contortrix.name: Copperhead
agkistrodon contortrix.desc: Copperhead (Agkistrodon contortrix): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
agkistrodon contortrix.about: The eastern copperhead, also known simply as the copperhead, is a widespread species of venomous snake, a pit viper, endemic to eastern United States of America; it is a member of the subfamily…

agkistrodon piscivorus.name: Cottonmouth
agkistrodon piscivorus.desc: Cottonmouth (Agkistrodon piscivorus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.
agkistrodon piscivorus.about: Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.

aglaia.name: Rainforest fruit trees
aglaia.desc: Fruiting trees such as Aglaia, whose fruits are recorded as eaten by macaques, fruit bats and civets.

aglaia elliptica.name: Segera
aglaia elliptica.desc: A rainforest tree well recorded near the park. GloBI has a record of the Asian palm civet eating its fruit.

aglais io.name: Peacock butterfly
aglais io.desc: A butterfly well recorded near the mountain. Its caterpillars feed on nettles.
aglais io.about: Aglais io, the European peacock, or the peacock butterfly, is a colourful butterfly, found in Europe and temperate Asia as far east as Japan.

aglais urticae.name: Small tortoiseshell
aglais urticae.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on nettle leaves; adults drink nectar from many flowers.
aglais urticae.about: The small tortoiseshell is a colourful Eurasian butterfly in the family Nymphalidae. Adults feed on nectar and may hibernate over winter; in warmer climates they may have two broods in a season.

agrilus cyanescens.name: Bluish borer beetle
agrilus cyanescens.desc: Bluish borer beetle (Agrilus cyanescens): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 190 times near the park in GBIF.

agrostis elliottiana.name: Elliott's bent
agrostis elliottiana.desc: Elliott's bent (Agrostis elliottiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

agrostis stolonifera.name: Creeping Bent
agrostis stolonifera.desc: Creeping Bent (Agrostis stolonifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.
agrostis stolonifera.about: Agrostis stolonifera is a perennial grass species in the family Poaceae. It is widely used as turf for golf courses.

aguadas and bajos.name: Aguadas and bajos
aguadas and bajos.desc: The area has little permanent surface water, so seasonal ponds and swampy low spots are vital wildlife water sources.

ahaetulla nasuta.name: Green vine snake
ahaetulla nasuta.desc: A slender tree snake that eats lizards and frogs. GloBI records show it eating red-vented bulbuls.
ahaetulla nasuta.about: Ahaetulla nasuta, also known as Sri Lankan green vine snake, long-nosed whip snake, and long-nosed tree snake, is a venomous, slender green tree snake endemic to Sri Lanka.

ailanthus altissima.name: Tree of heaven
ailanthus altissima.desc: Tree of heaven (Ailanthus altissima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 389 times near the park in GBIF.
ailanthus altissima.about: Ailanthus altissima ( ay-LAN-thəss al-TIH-sim-ə), commonly known as tree of heaven or ailanthus tree, is a deciduous tree in the quassia family. It is native to northeast, central China, and Taiwan.

ailuropoda melanoleuca.name: Giant panda
ailuropoda melanoleuca.desc: About 99% of the diet is bamboo. This site holds a large share of the wild population. Adults have few predators, but cubs and sub-adults can be taken.
ailuropoda melanoleuca.about: The giant panda, also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China. It is characterised by its white coat with black patches around the eyes, ears, legs and shoulders.

ailurus fulgens.name: Red panda
ailurus fulgens.desc: Eats mainly bamboo leaves, plus fruit, blossoms and acorns. Leopards are its only documented predator.
ailurus fulgens.about: The red panda, also known as the lesser panda, is a small mammal native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China.

aix sponsa.name: Wood Duck
aix sponsa.desc: Wood Duck (Aix sponsa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 50 times near the park in GBIF.
aix sponsa.about: The wood duck or Carolina duck is a partially migratory species of perching duck found in North America. The male is one of the most colorful North American waterfowls.

akodon cursor.name: Cursor grass mouse
akodon cursor.desc: A common small forest rodent, one of the most frequently recorded mammals here. It feeds on seeds, fruit and insects.
akodon cursor.about: The cursor grass mouse, or cursorial akodont, is a sigmodontine rodent from South America.

albizia julibrissin.name: Powderpuff Tree
albizia julibrissin.desc: Powderpuff Tree (Albizia julibrissin): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

alcelaphus buselaphus.name: Western hartebeest
alcelaphus buselaphus.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of open savanna, taken by leopards and hyenas.
alcelaphus buselaphus.about: The hartebeest, also known as kongoni or kaama, is an African antelope. It is the only member of the genus Alcelaphus.

alces alces.name: Moose
alces alces.desc: Moose (Alces alces): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
alces alces.about: The moose or elk is the world's tallest, largest and heaviest extant species of deer and the only extant species in the genus Alces.

alces americanus.name: Moose
alces americanus.desc: Moose (Alces americanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
alces americanus.about: The moose or elk is the world's tallest, largest and heaviest extant species of deer and the only extant species in the genus Alces.

aldabrachelys gigantea.name: Aldabra giant tortoise
aldabrachelys gigantea.desc: About 100,000 live here, the largest population anywhere. They eat grasses, leaves and woody stems, and like elephants they shape the landscape.
aldabrachelys gigantea.about: The Aldabra giant tortoise, Aldabra tortoise, or simply giant tortoise, is a species of tortoise in the family Testudinidae and genus Aldabrachelys.

alectoris chukar.name: Chukar
alectoris chukar.desc: A ground-nesting partridge of dry rocky slopes that eats seeds and plant matter.
alectoris chukar.about: The chukar partridge, or simply chukar, is a Palearctic upland gamebird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.

alectura lathami.name: Australian brushturkey
alectura lathami.desc: Builds a large nest mound of rotting leaf litter. Its eggs are a favourite food of goannas, snakes and dingoes.
alectura lathami.about: The Australian brushturkey, Australian brush-turkey, or gweela, also commonly called the bush turkey, scrub turkey, or just brushturkey, is a large mound-building bird of the family Megapodiidae.

algae.name: Reef algae
algae.desc: Algae growing on reef rock feed turtles, parrotfish and surgeonfish. They spread when corals die.
algae.about: Algae are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. It excludes the land plants (embryophytes).

algae and cyanobacteria.name: Phytoplankton
algae and cyanobacteria.desc: Drifting algae in the shallow lagoon. Nutrient-rich water has led to confirmed algal blooms there.
algae and cyanobacteria.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

algae, cyanobacteria and microbes.name: Periphyton
algae, cyanobacteria and microbes.desc: A living mat of algae and microbes on submerged plants and surfaces. In the Everglades it grows where sawgrass is sparse and feeds larval insects and amphibians.
algae, cyanobacteria and microbes.about: Periphyton is a complex mixture of algae, cyanobacteria, heterotrophic microbes, and detritus that is attached to submerged surfaces in most aquatic ecosystems.

algal turf and macroalgae.name: Reef algae and macroalgae
algal turf and macroalgae.desc: Algae growing on reef rock and sand. Grazers such as parrotfish and conch keep it from smothering corals.
algal turf and macroalgae.about: Seaweed, or macroalgae, refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.

aliger gigas.name: Queen conch
aliger gigas.desc: A large snail that grazes algae and seagrass films on sandy flats and meadows.
aliger gigas.about: Aliger gigas, originally known as Strombus gigas or more recently as Lobatus gigas, commonly known as the queen conch, is a species of large sea snail, a marine gastropod mollusc in the family of…

alkaline soils.name: Alkaline soils
alkaline soils.desc: Salty, alkaline soils on the Great Plain keep much of the puszta treeless and favour salt-tolerant grasses and herbs.

allactaga sibirica.name: Mongolian five-toed jerboa
allactaga sibirica.desc: A hopping desert rodent that eats seeds and plants and is hunted by foxes, falcons and eagles.
allactaga sibirica.about: The Mongolian five-toed jerboa or Siberian jerboa is a species of rodent in the family Dipodidae. It is found in China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.

alle alle.name: Little auk
alle alle.desc: A sparrow-sized seabird nesting in huge scree-slope colonies, feeding chiefly on copepods. Its colonies are raided by Arctic foxes and glaucous gulls.
alle alle.about: The little auk (Europe) or dovekie (North America) is a small auk, the only member of the genus Alle. It breeds in huge numbers on islands in the high Arctic of the North Atlantic Ocean.

allenrolfea occidentalis.name: Iodine-bush
allenrolfea occidentalis.desc: Iodine-bush (Allenrolfea occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
allenrolfea occidentalis.about: Allenrolfea occidentalis, the iodine bush, is a low-lying shrub of the Southwestern United States, California, Idaho, and northern Mexico.

alliaria petiolata.name: Garlic Mustard
alliaria petiolata.desc: Garlic mustard (Alliaria petiolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 336 times near the park in GBIF.
alliaria petiolata.about: Alliaria petiolata, or garlic mustard, is a biennial flowering plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae).

alligator mississippiensis.name: American alligator
alligator mississippiensis.desc: Digs gator holes that keep water through the dry season, giving fish and other animals a refuge. An opportunistic top predator.
alligator mississippiensis.about: The American alligator, sometimes referred to as a common alligator or just gator, is a large crocodilian reptile native to the Southeastern United States.

allionia incarnata.name: Trailing allionia
allionia incarnata.desc: Trailing allionia (Allionia incarnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

allium acuminatum.name: Hooker's onion
allium acuminatum.desc: Hooker's onion (Allium acuminatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

allium cernuum.name: Wild onion
allium cernuum.desc: Wild onion (Allium cernuum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

allium falcifolium.name: Scytheleaf onion
allium falcifolium.desc: Scytheleaf onion (Allium falcifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
allium falcifolium.about: Allium falcifolium is a North American species of wild onion known by the common name scytheleaf onion or coast flatstem onion.

allium stellatum.name: Autumn onion
allium stellatum.desc: Autumn onion (Allium stellatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
allium stellatum.about: Allium stellatum, commonly known as the autumn onion, prairie onion, cliff onion, or glade onion, is a North American species of wild onion in the Amaryllidaceae family that is native to central…

allium textile.name: Textile onion
allium textile.desc: Textile onion (Allium textile): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

allium tolmiei.name: Tolmie's onion
allium tolmiei.desc: Tolmie's onion (Allium tolmiei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
allium tolmiei.about: Allium tolmiei (Tolmie's onion) is a plant species native to Idaho, eastern and central Oregon, southeastern Washington, northwestern Nevada and northeastern California.

allium tricoccum.name: Ramp
allium tricoccum.desc: Ramp (Allium tricoccum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

allocasuarina decaisneana.name: Desert oak
allocasuarina decaisneana.desc: A tall, drought-tolerant tree of the sand dunes and sandplains of central Australia, frequently recorded around the park.
allocasuarina decaisneana.about: Allocasuarina decaisneana, commonly known as desert oak, desert sheoak, or kurkara by the Aṉangu peoples, is a species of flowering plant in the family Casuarinaceae and is endemic to Central…

allochrocebus lhoesti.name: L'Hoest's monkey
allochrocebus lhoesti.desc: Mostly plant eater of fruit, leaves, roots and mushrooms, occasionally eggs and small animals. Favours dense undergrowth in mountain forest.
allochrocebus lhoesti.about: L'Hoest's monkey, also known as the mountain monkey, is a guenon found in the upper eastern Congo Basin. They mostly live in mountainous forest areas in small, female-dominated groups.

alluvial soil & nutrients.name: Alluvial soil & nutrients
alluvial soil & nutrients.desc: River-borne silt and leaf litter build the rich, wet soils of the floodplain.

alnus alnobetula.name: Green alder
alnus alnobetula.desc: A shrub that colonises ground left bare by retreating ice. Alders host nitrogen-fixing root bacteria that enrich young soils.
alnus alnobetula.about: Alnus alnobetula, the green alder, is a common shrub or small tree widespread across much of Europe, Asia, and North America.

alnus glutinosa.name: Common alder
alnus glutinosa.desc: Alders and willows form the deciduous wet forest on the Colchic plain, rooted in waterlogged soil.
alnus glutinosa.about: Alnus glutinosa, the common alder, black alder, European alder, European black alder, or just alder, is a species of tree in the family Betulaceae, native to most of Europe, southwest Asia and…

alnus serrulata.name: Brook-side Alder
alnus serrulata.desc: Brook-side Alder (Alnus serrulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

aloe perryi.name: Socotrine aloe
aloe perryi.desc: A succulent of Socotra's dry slopes and cliffs, with bright flower spikes that offer nectar to birds.
aloe perryi.about: Aloe perryi is a species of plant in the genus Aloe. It is endemic to the island of Socotra in Yemen, and may be known by the common name, Socotrine aloe.

aloidendron eminens.name: Somali tree aloe
aloidendron eminens.desc: A tall tree aloe, one of the most frequently recorded plants of the Erigavo highlands in GBIF data.
aloidendron eminens.about: Aloidendron eminens, formerly Aloe eminens, is a species of succulent plant in the genus Aloidendron, endemic to Somalia.

alopochen aegyptiaca.name: Egyptian goose
alopochen aegyptiaca.desc: A grazing waterbird of river banks and pools. Eaten by pythons.
alopochen aegyptiaca.about: The Egyptian goose is an African member of the Anatidae family including ducks, geese, and swans.

alosa pseudoharengus.name: Alewife
alosa pseudoharengus.desc: An invasive herring that eats zooplankton. It became the main prey for stocked salmon and trout.
alosa pseudoharengus.about: The alewife or river herring is a species of herring found in North America. It is commonly anadromous but there are also significant landlocked populations.

alosa sapidissima.name: American shad
alosa sapidissima.desc: A plankton-feeding fish that runs up the Connecticut River to spawn. Striped bass are its main predator and harbor seals take some.
alosa sapidissima.about: The American shad is a species of anadromous clupeid fish naturally distributed on the North American coast of the North Atlantic, from Newfoundland to Florida, and as an introduced species on the…

alouatta caraya.name: Black howler
alouatta caraya.desc: A mostly leaf-eating, tree-living monkey. GloBI records it eating caranday palm.
alouatta caraya.about: The black howler or black-and-gold howler, is among the largest New World monkeys and a member of the Alouatta genus.

alouatta macconnelli.name: Guyanan red howler
alouatta macconnelli.desc: A howler monkey native to Guyana and neighbouring countries, living in the forest canopy.
alouatta macconnelli.about: The Guyanan red howler is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, native to Suriname, Guyana, Trinidad, French Guiana, Venezuela and Brazil.

alouatta palliata.name: Mantled howler
alouatta palliata.desc: A leaf-eating monkey that also takes fruit, especially figs, and helps spread and germinate seeds.
alouatta palliata.about: The mantled howler is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, from Central and South America. It is one of the monkey species most often seen and heard in the wild in Central America.

alouatta spp..name: Howler monkey
alouatta spp..desc: Eats leaves, flowers and fruit, and announces its territory with a roar that carries for miles.
alouatta spp..about: Howler monkeys (genus Alouatta, monotypic in subfamily Alouattinae) are the most widespread primate genus in the Neotropics and are among the largest of the platyrrhines along with the muriquis…

alpine soil.name: Alpine soil
alpine soil.desc: Thin mountain soils hold the nutrients that meadow plants and dwarf shrubs draw on.

alpine soils.name: Alpine soils
alpine soils.desc: Thin soils on rock and moraine supply nutrients to alpine plants and are topped up as dead matter is broken down.

alternanthera philoxeroides.name: Alligatorweed
alternanthera philoxeroides.desc: Alligatorweed (Alternanthera philoxeroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
alternanthera philoxeroides.about: Alternanthera philoxeroides, commonly referred to as alligator weed, is a native species to the temperate regions of South America, which includes Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.

alticola argentatus.name: Silver mountain vole
alticola argentatus.desc: A small rodent of rocky mountain ground, recorded near the park. It eats plant material and is prey for foxes and snakes.
alticola argentatus.about: The silver mountain vole is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae. They are distinguished by their silver-grey pelage, long vibrissae, rootless hypsodont molars and angular skull shape.

alypia octomaculata.name: Eight-spotted Forester
alypia octomaculata.desc: Eight-spotted Forester (Alypia octomaculata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
alypia octomaculata.about: Alypia octomaculata, the eight-spotted forester, is a moth of the family Noctuidae, first described by Johan Christian Fabricius in 1775.

amara quenseli.name: Amara quenseli
amara quenseli.desc: Amara quenseli (Amara quenseli): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

amaranthus retroflexus.name: Common Amaranth
amaranthus retroflexus.desc: Common Amaranth (Amaranthus retroflexus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

amauropelta noveboracensis.name: New York fern
amauropelta noveboracensis.desc: New York fern (Amauropelta noveboracensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

amazona aestiva.name: Turquoise-fronted parrot
amazona aestiva.desc: A parrot of Chaco woodland that eats seeds and fruit.
amazona aestiva.about: The blue-fronted amazon, also called the blue-fronted parrot, the turquoise-fronted amazon and the turquoise-fronted parrot, is a South American species of amazon parrot and one of the most common…

amazona vittata.name: Puerto Rican parrot
amazona vittata.desc: Critically endangered. Eats flowers, fruit, leaves and bark, and nests in tree cavities, favouring palo colorado trees. Hurricanes have repeatedly cut its numbers.
amazona vittata.about: The Puerto Rican amazon, also known as the Puerto Rican parrot (Spanish: cotorra puertorriqueña) or iguaca (Taíno), is the only extant parrot endemic to Puerto Rico.

amblyopsis spelaea.name: Northern cavefish
amblyopsis spelaea.desc: An eyeless fish of caves in Kentucky and southern Indiana. Related cavefish eat small crustaceans, so crayfish are likely prey.
amblyopsis spelaea.about: The northern cavefish or northern blindfish is found in caves through Kentucky and southern Indiana. The International Union for Conservation of Nature lists the species as near threatened.

amblyrhynchus cristatus.name: Marine iguana
amblyrhynchus cristatus.desc: The only sea-going lizard. It feeds almost entirely on red and green seaweed, and populations crash when El Niño kills off its algae.
amblyrhynchus cristatus.about: The marine iguana, also known as the sea iguana, saltwater iguana, or Galápagos marine iguana, is a species of iguana found only on the Galápagos Islands (Ecuador).

ambrosia artemisiifolia.name: Ragweed
ambrosia artemisiifolia.desc: Ragweed (Ambrosia artemisiifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

ambrosia bidentata.name: Southern ragweed
ambrosia bidentata.desc: Southern ragweed (Ambrosia bidentata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

ambrosia chamissonis.name: Beachbur
ambrosia chamissonis.desc: Beachbur (Ambrosia chamissonis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

ambrosia dumosa.name: White bursage
ambrosia dumosa.desc: A low shrub that often grows alongside creosote bush across the desert floor.
ambrosia dumosa.about: Ambrosia dumosa, the burro-weed or white bursage, a North American species of plants in the family Asteraceae.

ambrosia psilostachya.name: Perennial Ragweed
ambrosia psilostachya.desc: Perennial Ragweed (Ambrosia psilostachya): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

ambrosia trifida.name: Perennial Ragweed
ambrosia trifida.desc: Perennial Ragweed (Ambrosia trifida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
ambrosia trifida.about: Ambrosia trifida, the giant ragweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is native to North America, where it is widespread in Canada, the United States, and northern Mexico.

amelanchier alnifolia.name: Saskatoon serviceberry
amelanchier alnifolia.desc: A berry-bearing shrub of open slopes. Bears, birds and browsing ungulates use its fruit and leaves.
amelanchier alnifolia.about: Amelanchier alnifolia, the saskatoon berry, Pacific serviceberry, western serviceberry, western shadbush, or western juneberry, is a shrub native to North America.

amelanchier arborea.name: Allegheny Serviceberry
amelanchier arborea.desc: Allegheny Serviceberry (Amelanchier arborea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
amelanchier arborea.about: Amelanchier arborea, is a small tree native to eastern North America from the Gulf Coast north to Thunder Bay in Ontario and Lake St. John in Quebec, and west to Texas and Minnesota.

amelanchier utahensis.name: Utah serviceberry
amelanchier utahensis.desc: Utah serviceberry (Amelanchier utahensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
amelanchier utahensis.about: Amelanchier utahensis, the Utah serviceberry, is a species of serviceberry forming a shrub or small tree. It is native to western North America.

amia calva.name: Bowfin
amia calva.desc: A predatory fish that copes with the acidic, low-oxygen tannic water. The refuge names it among its common fish.
amia calva.about: The ruddy bowfin is a ray-finned fish native to North America. Common names include mudfish, mud pike, dogfish, grindle, grinnel, swamp trout, and choupique.

ammelaphus imberbis.name: Lesser kudu
ammelaphus imberbis.desc: A shy browser of thornbush and dense cover. Tree and shrub foliage makes up most of its diet, and it is found across most of Somalia.
ammelaphus imberbis.about: The lesser kudu is a medium-sized antelope found in East Africa.

ammodramus savannarum.name: Grasshopper Sparrow
ammodramus savannarum.desc: Grasshopper Sparrow (Ammodramus savannarum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,333 times near the park in GBIF.
ammodramus savannarum.about: The grasshopper sparrow is a small New World sparrow. It belongs to the genus Ammodramus, which contains three species that inhabit grasslands and prairies.

ammodytes americanus.name: American sand lance
ammodytes americanus.desc: A small schooling fish that eats plankton and is a key prey of seals, whales and seabirds.
ammodytes americanus.about: Ammodytes americanus, also known as American sand lance, American sand eel, and sand launce, is a small fish in the family Ammodytidae.

ammodytes personatus.name: Pacific sand lance
ammodytes personatus.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is prey for many seabirds, fish and marine mammals.

ammomanes deserti.name: Desert lark
ammomanes deserti.desc: Eats seeds and insects, with more insects in the breeding season. A common small bird that predators of the desert hunt.
ammomanes deserti.about: The desert lark breeds in deserts and semi-deserts from Morocco to western India.

ammophila arenaria.name: European marram grass
ammophila arenaria.desc: A tough dune grass whose roots bind loose sand on the beach and foredunes.
ammophila arenaria.about: Ammophila arenaria is a species of grass in the family Poaceae. It is known by the common names marram grass and European beachgrass.

ammophila breviligulata.name: American beachgrass
ammophila breviligulata.desc: A beach grass native to Great Lakes shores. Wikipedia says its genus builds coastal dunes and stabilises the sand with creeping rhizomes.
ammophila breviligulata.about: Ammophila breviligulata is a species of grass native to eastern North America, where it grows on sand dunes along the Atlantic Ocean and Great Lakes coasts.

ammospermophilus harrisii.name: Harris' antelope squirrel
ammospermophilus harrisii.desc: Harris' antelope squirrel (Ammospermophilus harrisii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.
ammospermophilus harrisii.about: Harris's antelope squirrel is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae. It is found in Arizona and New Mexico in the United States, and in Sonora in Mexico.

ammospermophilus leucurus.name: White-tailed antelope squirrel
ammospermophilus leucurus.desc: A day-active omnivore that eats mostly plants and seeds, plus arthropods. Raptors, canids and snakes prey on it.
ammospermophilus leucurus.about: The white-tailed antelope squirrel is a diurnal species of ground squirrel, scientifically classified in the order Rodentia and family Sciuridae, found in arid regions of the southwestern United…

ammotragus lervia.name: Barbary sheep (aoudad)
ammotragus lervia.desc: A North African wild sheep introduced to the Southwest and heavily recorded near the park. It grazes and browses desert plants, competing with native herbivores.
ammotragus lervia.about: The Barbary sheep, also known as aoudad (pronounced [ˈɑʊdæd]), is a species of caprine native to rocky mountains in North Africa and parts of West Africa.

amorpha canescens.name: Leadplant
amorpha canescens.desc: A deep-rooted prairie shrub in the pea family, listed among the hills' characteristic flowering plants and visited by bumble bees.
amorpha canescens.about: Amorpha canescens, known as leadplant, downy indigo bush, prairie shoestring, or buffalo bellows, is a small, perennial semi-shrub in the pea family (Fabaceae), native to North America.

amorpha fruticosa.name: Desert false indigo
amorpha fruticosa.desc: Desert false indigo (Amorpha fruticosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
amorpha fruticosa.about: Amorpha fruticosa is a species of flowering plant in the legume family Fabaceae, known by several common names, including desert false indigo, false indigo-bush, and bastard indigobush.

ampelopsis cordata.name: Heart-leaf ampelopsis
ampelopsis cordata.desc: Heart-leaf ampelopsis (Ampelopsis cordata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

amphibolis antarctica.name: Wire weed
amphibolis antarctica.desc: A seagrass of southern and western Australian coasts that forms extensive meadows in shallow water on sand, gravel and rock.
amphibolis antarctica.about: Amphibolis antarctica is a species of flowering plant in the family Cymodoceaceae.

amphicarpaea bracteata.name: American Hogpeanut
amphicarpaea bracteata.desc: American Hogpeanut (Amphicarpaea bracteata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

amphion floridensis.name: Nessus Sphinx
amphion floridensis.desc: Nessus Sphinx (Amphion floridensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

amphipoda.name: Amphipods and small crustaceans
amphipoda.desc: Small crustaceans that live among the kelp and feed on its tissue and drift. Food for small fish.
amphipoda.about: Amphipoda () is an order of malacostracan crustaceans characterized by sessile eyes and the absence of a carapace.

amsonia hubrichtii.name: Hubricht's bluestar
amsonia hubrichtii.desc: Hubricht's bluestar (Amsonia hubrichtii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
amsonia hubrichtii.about: Amsonia hubrichtii, commonly known as Hubricht's bluestar, Arkansas bluestar, or thread-leaf bluestar, is a North American species of perennial flowering plant in the Apocynaceae (dogbane) family,…

amsonia tabernaemontana.name: Texas-star
amsonia tabernaemontana.desc: Texas-star (Amsonia tabernaemontana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
amsonia tabernaemontana.about: Amsonia tabernaemontana, the eastern bluestar, is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae, found in central and eastern North America.

anabas testudineus.name: Climbing perch
anabas testudineus.desc: A hardy small fish of ponds, swamps and paddies; prey for otters and many wading birds.

anableps anableps.name: Four-eyed fish
anableps anableps.desc: Surface-dwelling fish of the brackish waters of the swamp, with eyes adapted to look above and below the water.
anableps anableps.about: Anableps anableps, the largescale four-eyes, is a species of four-eyed fish found in fresh and brackish waters of northern South America and Trinidad.

anabrus simplex.name: Mormon cricket
anabrus simplex.desc: A flightless shrub-dwelling katydid that eats plants and is eaten by bears and birds.
anabrus simplex.about: The Mormon cricket is a large insect native to western North America in rangelands dominated by sagebrush and forbs.

analeptura lineola.name: Lined Longhorn Beetle
analeptura lineola.desc: Lined Longhorn Beetle (Analeptura lineola): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

anaphalis margaritacea.name: Pearly everlasting
anaphalis margaritacea.desc: Common pearlyeverlasting (Anaphalis margaritacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
anaphalis margaritacea.about: Anaphalis margaritacea, commonly known as the western pearly everlasting or pearly everlasting, is an Asian and North American species of flowering perennial plant in the family Asteraceae.

anartia jatrophae.name: White Peacock
anartia jatrophae.desc: White Peacock (Anartia jatrophae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

anas crecca.name: Green-winged Teal
anas crecca.desc: Green-winged Teal (Anas crecca): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

anas platyrhynchos.about: The mallard () or wild duck is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout temperate and subtropical North America, Eurasia, and North Africa.

anax junius.name: Green Darner
anax junius.desc: Green Darner (Anax junius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

anax parthenope.name: Lesser emperor
anax parthenope.desc: Large dragonfly of still and slow water that catches other insects in flight; its larvae live in the water.
anax parthenope.about: Anax parthenope, the lesser emperor, is a dragonfly of the family Aeshnidae. It is found in Southern Europe, North Africa, West Asia.

anaxyrus americanus.name: American toad
anaxyrus americanus.desc: American toad (Anaxyrus americanus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

anaxyrus terrestris.name: Southern toad
anaxyrus terrestris.desc: Southern toad (Anaxyrus terrestris): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

anchoa mitchilli.name: Bay anchovy
anchoa mitchilli.desc: A small schooling fish that eats zooplankton and is a key forage fish for larger fish and birds.
anchoa mitchilli.about: Anchoa mitchilli is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Engraulidae, the anchovies. Its common names include bay anchovy and common anchovy.

andersonglossum virginianum.name: Giant-forget-me-not
andersonglossum virginianum.desc: Giant-forget-me-not (Andersonglossum virginianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
andersonglossum virginianum.about: Andersonglossum virginianum, known as southern wild comfrey, is a flowering plant in the borage family native to North America. It is also sometimes called blue houndstongue.

andrena balsamorhizae.name: Mojave Gypsum Bee

andrena carlini.name: Carlin's Andrena

andrena crataegi.name: Hawthorn Andrena

andrena cressonii.name: Cresson's Andrena
andrena cressonii.desc: Cresson's Andrena (Andrena cressonii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

andrena erigeniae.name: Spring Beauty Andrena
andrena erigeniae.desc: Spring Beauty Andrena (Andrena erigeniae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.
andrena erigeniae.about: Andrena erigeniae, the spring beauty miner bee or spring beauty andrena is a species of miner bee native to North America.

andrena hirticincta.name: Hairy-banded Andrena
andrena hirticincta.desc: Hairy-banded Andrena (Andrena hirticincta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

andrena wilkella.name: Andrenine Bee

andricus quercusflocci.about: Andricus quercusflocci is a species of gall wasp in the family Cynipidae.

andropogon.name: Bluestem grasses
