andropogon canaliculatus.desc: A bunchgrass of the open savanna. Grasses like this carpet the plains and feed the park's grazers.
andropogon canaliculatus.about: Andropogon (common names: beard grass, bluestem grass, broomsedge) is a widespread genus of plants in the grass family, native to much of Asia, Africa, and the Americas, as well as Southern Europe…

andropogon gayanus.name: Gamba grass
andropogon gayanus.desc: A tall tussock grass of West African savannas, recorded often near the park. It is a staple of grazers and carries the dry-season fires.
andropogon gayanus.about: Andropogon gayanus, commonly known as gamba grass, Rhodesian blue grass, tambuki grass, and other names, is a species of grass native to most of the tropical and subtropical savannas of Africa.

andropogon gerardi.name: Big bluestem
andropogon gerardi.desc: A tall dominant prairie grass. The MDC says prairie species such as prairie-chickens and Henslow's sparrows indirectly depend on it, and it is excellent forage for livestock.
andropogon gerardi.about: Andropogon gerardi, commonly known as big bluestem, is a species of tall grass native to much of the Great Plains and grassland regions of central and eastern North America.

anemonastrum canadense.name: Canada anemone
anemonastrum canadense.desc: Canada anemone (Anemonastrum canadense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
anemonastrum canadense.about: Anemonastrum canadense, synonym Anemone canadensis, the Canada anemone, round-headed anemone, round-leaf thimbleweed, meadow anemone, windflower, or crowfoot, is a herbaceous perennial flowering…

anemone cylindrica.name: Candle anemone
anemone cylindrica.desc: Candle anemone (Anemone cylindrica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
anemone cylindrica.about: Anemone cylindrica, also known as thimbleweed, is an upright growing, clump forming herbaceous species of flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.

anemone oregana.name: Blue windflower
anemone oregana.desc: Blue windflower (Anemone oregana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
anemone oregana.about: Anemonoides oregana is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family known by the common names blue windflower, Oregon anemone, and western wood anemone.

anemone quinquefolia.name: Wood Anemone
anemone quinquefolia.desc: Wood Anemone (Anemone quinquefolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
anemone quinquefolia.about: Anemonoides quinquefolia (French: anémone à cinq folioles), a flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae, is native to North America.

anemone tuberosa.name: Desert anemone
anemone tuberosa.desc: Desert anemone (Anemone tuberosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

anemone virginiana.name: Thimbleweed
anemone virginiana.desc: Thimbleweed (Anemone virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
anemone virginiana.about: Anemone virginiana is an upright growing herbaceous species of flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.

angiopteris evecta.name: Tree fern
angiopteris evecta.desc: A large fern of the damp forest floor and stream edges, shading the ground and sheltering small animals.
angiopteris evecta.about: Angiopteris evecta, commonly known as the king fern, giant fern, elephant fern, oriental vessel fern, Madagascar tree fern, or mule's foot fern, is a very large rainforest fern in the family…

anguilla anguilla.name: European eel
anguilla anguilla.desc: Eats worms, fish, molluscs and crustaceans. Critically endangered, with numbers reaching Europe down by about 90% since the 1970s.
anguilla anguilla.about: The European eel is a species of eel. Their life history was a mystery for thousands of years, and mating in the wild has not yet been observed.

anhinga melanogaster.name: Oriental darter
anhinga melanogaster.desc: Swims with only its neck above water and spears fish; nests in mixed waterbird colonies in trees standing in water.
anhinga melanogaster.about: The Oriental darter is a water bird of tropical South Asia and Southeast Asia.

anodorhynchus hyacinthinus.name: Hyacinth macaw
anodorhynchus hyacinthinus.desc: A giant parrot that in the Pantanal feeds almost entirely on nuts of the acuri and bocaiuva palms.
anodorhynchus hyacinthinus.about: The hyacinth macaw, or hyacinthine macaw, is a large parrot native to central and eastern South America.

anogeissus pendula.name: Dhok
anogeissus pendula.desc: Wikipedia calls it the characteristic tree of Ranthambore. It looks dry and brown in summer but greens up after a little rain.
anogeissus pendula.about: Terminalia pendula is an Asian species of tree in the family Combretaceae. It is a medium-sized tree found in both primary and secondary tropical and sub-tropical forests.

anolis carolinensis.name: Green anole
anolis carolinensis.desc: Green anole (Anolis carolinensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
anolis carolinensis.about: Anolis carolinensis or green anole (US: ) (among other names below) is a tree-dwelling species of anole lizard native to the southeastern United States and introduced to islands in the Pacific and…

anolis chlorocyanus.name: Hispaniolan green anole
anolis chlorocyanus.desc: A tree-dwelling lizard that hunts insects such as ants on trunks and foliage.
anolis chlorocyanus.about: Anolis chlorocyanus, the Tiburon green anole or Hispaniolan green anole or Jeremie anole, is a species of anole endemic to Haiti, primarily the Tiburon Peninsula and Jérémie and Hispaniola.

anolis distichus.name: Bark anole
anolis distichus.desc: A small lizard on trunks and branches that hunts insects and other arthropods.
anolis distichus.about: Anolis distichus, the bark anole, North Caribbean bark anole, or Hispaniolan gracile anole, is a species of anole lizard (US: ) native to Hispaniola and the Bahamas, and introduced to Florida, where…

anolis equestris.name: Knight anole
anolis equestris.desc: Large Cuban tree lizard of forest and mangrove that eats insects, snails and fruit, and sometimes small vertebrates.
anolis equestris.about: The knight anole is the largest species of anole (US: ) in the Dactyloidae family.

anolis fuscoauratus.name: Brown-eared anole
anolis fuscoauratus.desc: A small forest lizard that eats insects. The blunthead treesnake is recorded in GloBI eating it.
anolis fuscoauratus.about: Anolis fuscoauratus, commonly known as the slender anole, slender Amazon anole, or brown-eared anole, is a species of lizard in the family Dactyloidae.

anolis gundlachi.name: Gundlach's anole
anolis gundlachi.desc: A common forest anole that eats small invertebrates. Young Puerto Rican boas feed mainly on anoles.
anolis gundlachi.about: Anolis gundlachi, also commonly known as the yellow-chinned anole, Gundlach's anole, and the yellow-beard anole, is an oviparous, sexually dimorphic species of lizard in the family Dactyloidae.

anolis lineatopus.name: Stripefoot anole
anolis lineatopus.desc: A common Jamaican lizard that hunts insects, including ants, and is itself eaten by snakes and mongooses.
anolis lineatopus.about: Anolidae are a family of lizards commonly known as anoles (singular anole US: ) and native to warmer parts of the Americas, ranging from southeastern United States to Paraguay.

anolis sagrei.name: Brown anole
anolis sagrei.desc: Brown anole (Anolis sagrei): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 57 times near the park in GBIF.

anolis townsendi.name: Cocos anole
anolis townsendi.desc: An endemic lizard of Cocos Island, one of the most recorded animals there, that hunts small insects.
anolis townsendi.about: Anolis townsendi, Townsend's anole or Cocos Island anole, is a species of lizard in the family Dactyloidae. The species is endemic to Cocos Island in Costa Rica.

anopheles aquasalis.name: Salt-marsh mosquito
anopheles aquasalis.desc: A mosquito whose larvae develop in brackish water; its larvae and adults are prey for fish and insect-eating bats.
anopheles aquasalis.about: Anopheles () is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818, and are known as nail mosquitoes and marsh mosquitoes.

anous stolidus.name: Brown noddy
anous stolidus.desc: A tropical seabird that nests on the atoll islets and catches small fish at the sea surface.
anous stolidus.about: The brown noddy, common noddy or noddy tern is a seabird in the family Laridae.

anser albifrons.name: Greater white-fronted goose
anser albifrons.desc: A winter visitor that grazes grasses, clover and dandelion in open fields.
anser albifrons.about: The greater white-fronted goose is a species of goose, closely related to the smaller lesser white-fronted goose (A. erythropus).

anser anser.name: Greylag goose
anser anser.desc: A large grazing goose of wetland and meadows that eats reed shoots and grasses.
anser anser.about: The greylag goose is a species of large goose in the waterfowl family Anatidae and the type species of the genus Anser.

anser brachyrhynchus.name: Pink-footed goose
anser brachyrhynchus.desc: Breeds in the Icelandic highlands, using wetlands near the glacier, and eats tundra plants in summer. The Arctic fox is its main land predator.
anser brachyrhynchus.about: The pink-footed goose is a goose which breeds in eastern Greenland, Iceland, Svalbard, and recently Novaya Zemlya.

anser caerulescens.name: Snow goose
anser caerulescens.desc: Nests on the tundra in summer and grazes sedges.
anser caerulescens.about: The snow goose is a species of goose native to North America. Both white and dark morphs exist, the latter often known as blue goose.

anseranas semipalmata.name: Magpie goose
anseranas semipalmata.desc: Floodplain bird that eats grass seeds, grass blades and spike-rush bulbs. It is the most recorded bird near the park and a seasonal food for people and crocodiles.
anseranas semipalmata.about: The magpie goose is the sole living representative species of the family Anseranatidae. This waterbird is found in northern Australia and southern New Guinea.

antarctic convergence.name: Antarctic Convergence
antarctic convergence.desc: The Southern Ocean boundary where cold and warmer waters meet, which concentrates plankton and the fish and squid that feed on it.

antheraea polyphemus.name: Polyphemus Moth
antheraea polyphemus.desc: Polyphemus Moth (Antheraea polyphemus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
antheraea polyphemus.about: Antheraea polyphemus, the Polyphemus moth, is a North American member of the family Saturniidae, the giant silk moths. It is a tan-colored moth, with an average wingspan of 15 cm (6 in).

anthophora bomboides.name: Bumble-bee-mimic Anthophora
anthophora bomboides.desc: Bumble-bee-mimic Anthophora (Anthophora bomboides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 34 times near the park in GBIF.

anthophora urbana.name: Urbane Digger Bee
anthophora urbana.desc: Urbane Digger Bee (Anthophora urbana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
anthophora urbana.about: Anthophora urbana, the urbane digger bee, is a species of anthophorine bee in the family Apidae. It is found in Central America and North America.

anthornis melanura.name: New Zealand bellbird
anthornis melanura.desc: A common forest bird that feeds on nectar, fruit and insects.
anthornis melanura.about: The New Zealand bellbird, also known by its Māori language names korimako, makomako and kōmako, is a medium-sized species of honeyeater endemic to New Zealand.

anthracoceros albirostris.name: Oriental pied hornbill
anthracoceros albirostris.desc: A large forest bird that eats figs and other fruit as well as lizards and insects, and so spreads fig seeds.
anthracoceros albirostris.about: The oriental pied hornbill is an Indo-Malayan pied hornbill, a large canopy-dwelling bird belonging to the family Bucerotidae.

anthropoides virgo.name: Demoiselle crane
anthropoides virgo.desc: A small crane nesting on the steppe and wetland edge, eating seeds, shoots and insects. Recorded often near the lake.
anthropoides virgo.about: The demoiselle crane is a species of crane found in central Eurosiberia, ranging from the Black Sea to Mongolia and Northeast China. There is also a small breeding population in Turkey.

anthus rubescens.name: American Pipit
anthus rubescens.desc: American Pipit (Anthus rubescens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
anthus rubescens.about: The American pipit, formerly known as the buff-bellied pipit, is a small songbird native to North America. It was first described by Marmaduke Tunstall in his 1771 Ornithologia Britannica.

antidesma montanum.name: Antidesma
antidesma montanum.desc: A forest tree recorded near the park whose small fruits are eaten by macaques, according to GloBI records.
antidesma montanum.about: Antidesma is a genus of tropical plant in the family Phyllanthaceae formally described by Linnaeus in 1753. It is native to tropical Africa, S + E + SE Asia, Australia, and various oceanic islands.

antidorcas marsupialis.name: Springbok
antidorcas marsupialis.desc: A small antelope of arid plains that grazes and browses and needs little free water.
antidorcas marsupialis.about: The springbok or springbuck is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.

antilocapra americana.name: Pronghorn
antilocapra americana.desc: Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
antilocapra americana.about: The pronghorn (UK: , US: ) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.

antrozous pallidus.name: Pallid bat
antrozous pallidus.desc: Pallid bat (Antrozous pallidus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
antrozous pallidus.about: The pallid bat is a species of bat that ranges from western Canada to central Mexico.

apatelodes torrefacta.name: Spotted Apatelodes
apatelodes torrefacta.desc: Spotted Apatelodes (Apatelodes torrefacta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

aphelocoma californica.name: California scrub-jay
aphelocoma californica.desc: California scrub-jay (Aphelocoma californica): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 698 times near the park in GBIF.
aphelocoma californica.about: The California scrub jay is a species of scrub jay native to western North America.

aphelocoma woodhouseii.name: Woodhouse's scrub-jay
aphelocoma woodhouseii.desc: A common oak-scrub bird that eats acorns, seeds and insects, and is among the most recorded birds here.

apis dorsata.name: Giant honey bee
apis dorsata.desc: A wild bee that hangs open combs from high branches and feeds on flower nectar. It is one of the best-recorded insects near the park.
apis dorsata.about: Apis dorsata, the rock bee or giant honey bee, is a honey bee of South and Southeast Asia.

apis mellifera.name: Western honey bee
apis mellifera.desc: Western honey bee (Apis mellifera): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
apis mellifera.about: The western honey bee is the most common of the 7–12 species of honey bees worldwide.

aplectrum hyemale.name: Adam and Eve
aplectrum hyemale.desc: Adam and Eve (Aplectrum hyemale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 192 times near the park in GBIF.

aplodinotus grunniens.name: Freshwater drum
aplodinotus grunniens.desc: Crushes mussels and eats insect larvae and, later in the year, young gizzard shad.
aplodinotus grunniens.about: The freshwater drum, Aplodinotus grunniens, is a fish endemic to North and Central America. It is the only species in the genus Aplodinotus, and is a member of the family Sciaenidae.

apocynum androsaemifolium.name: Bitterroot
apocynum androsaemifolium.desc: Bitterroot (Apocynum androsaemifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
apocynum androsaemifolium.about: Apocynum androsaemifolium, the fly-trap dogbane or spreading dogbane, is a flowering plant in the Gentianales order.

apocynum cannabinum.name: American-hemp
apocynum cannabinum.desc: American-hemp (Apocynum cannabinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

apodemus agrarius.name: Striped field mouse
apodemus agrarius.desc: A small rodent of fields and forest edges that eats seeds and plant material. It is prey for stoats, gulls and wolves.
apodemus agrarius.about: The striped field mouse is a rodent in the family Muridae. The range of this species stretches from Eastern Europe to Eastern Asia.

apodemus draco.name: South China field mouse
apodemus draco.desc: A well-recorded forest rodent of the Hengduan mountains and a staple small prey for carnivores.
apodemus draco.about: The South China field mouse is a species of rodent in the family Muridae. It is found in China, India, and Myanmar.

apodemus flavicollis.name: Yellow-necked mouse
apodemus flavicollis.desc: A forest rodent that eats seeds and is a main prey of wildcats in the Carpathians.
apodemus flavicollis.about: The yellow-necked mouse, also called yellow-necked field mouse or yellow-necked wood mouse, is closely related to the wood mouse, with which it was long confused.

apodemus sylvaticus.name: Wood mouse
apodemus sylvaticus.desc: A small woodland rodent that eats seeds and fruit, and is food for foxes, martens and snakes.
apodemus sylvaticus.about: The wood mouse is a murid rodent native to Europe and northwestern Africa. It is closely related to the yellow-necked mouse (A.

apodemus uralensis.name: Ural field mouse
apodemus uralensis.desc: Small ground-dwelling rodent recorded near the park; a staple prey for herons, harriers and mammals.
apodemus uralensis.about: The Ural field mouse is a species of rodent in the family Muridae. It is also known as the pygmy field mouse.

aporosaura anchietae.name: Sand-diving lizard
aporosaura anchietae.desc: A dune lizard that dives into sand to escape heat and enemies. It eats wind-blown seeds and insects and is itself prey for snakes.

aptenodytes patagonicus.name: King penguin
aptenodytes patagonicus.desc: Breeds in large colonies at Kerguelen, about 240,000 to 280,000 pairs. Eats mostly lanternfish and squid.
aptenodytes patagonicus.about: The king penguin is the second largest species of penguin, smaller than but somewhat similar in appearance to the emperor penguin. King penguins mainly eat lanternfish, squid, and krill.

apteryx australis.name: Southern brown kiwi
apteryx australis.desc: Flightless forest bird found almost entirely in Fiordland and nearby areas; it probes soil for invertebrates.
apteryx australis.about: The southern brown kiwi, tokoeka, or common kiwi is a species of kiwi from South Island of New Zealand.

aquarius cordifolius.name: Creeping burhead
aquarius cordifolius.desc: Creeping burhead (Aquarius cordifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
aquarius cordifolius.about: Aquarius cordifolius, the spade-leaf sword or creeping burhead, is a species of aquatic plants in the Alismatales.

aquatic macrophytes.name: Floodplain plants & algae
aquatic macrophytes.desc: Floating meadows and algae in flooded forest that feed capybaras and fish.
aquatic macrophytes.about: Aquatic plants, also referred to as hydrophytes, are vascular plants and non-vascular plants that have adapted to live in aquatic environments.

aquifer water.name: Aquifer water
aquifer water.desc: The Kirkwood-Cohansey aquifer under the Barrens feeds its bogs, swamps and vernal pools.

aquila adalberti.name: Spanish imperial eagle
aquila adalberti.desc: An endangered eagle that eats rabbits and, where rabbits are scarce, water birds such as coots and ducks.
aquila adalberti.about: The Spanish imperial eagle, Spanish eagle, Iberian imperial eagle or Adalbert's eagle is a species of eagle native to the Iberian Peninsula. The binomial commemorates Prince Adalbert of Bavaria.

aquila audax.name: Wedge-tailed eagle
aquila audax.desc: A large eagle that takes rabbits, young kangaroos, lizards and birds, and feeds on carrion and roadkill.
aquila audax.about: The wedge-tailed eagle is the largest bird of prey in the continent of Australia. It is also found in southern New Guinea to the north and is distributed as far south as the state of Tasmania.

aquila audax fleayi.name: Tasmanian wedge-tailed eagle
aquila audax fleayi.desc: A large endangered eagle that takes wallabies, possums and rabbits, and feeds on carrion in winter.
aquila audax fleayi.about: The Tasmanian wedge-tailed eagle is an endangered bird of Tasmania. It is a subspecies of the more common wedge-tailed eagle.

aquila chrysaetos.name: Golden eagle
aquila chrysaetos.desc: Large raptor that takes marmots and, from general knowledge, pikas and game birds.
aquila chrysaetos.about: The golden eagle is a bird of prey living in the Northern Hemisphere. It is the most widely distributed species of eagle.

aquila fasciata.name: Bonelli's eagle
aquila fasciata.desc: Cyprus diet studies show it taking chukar, pigeons, black rats, jackdaws and lizards, mostly caught alive.
aquila fasciata.about: Bonelli's eagle is a large bird of prey. The common name of the bird commemorates the Italian ornithologist and collector Franco Andrea Bonelli.

aquila nipalensis.name: Steppe eagle
aquila nipalensis.desc: A large eagle of open country that hunts ground squirrels, marmots, voles and hares.
aquila nipalensis.about: The steppe eagle is a large bird of prey. Like all eagles, it belongs to the family Accipitridae.

aquila rapax.name: Tawny eagle
aquila rapax.desc: A raptor that hunts and also feeds at carcasses; it is known to take young springbok.
aquila rapax.about: The tawny eagle is a large bird of prey. Like all eagles, it belongs to the family Accipitridae.

aquila verreauxii.name: Verreaux's eagle
aquila verreauxii.desc: A hyrax specialist: in many areas hyraxes make up most of its diet, so its range follows theirs.
aquila verreauxii.about: Verreaux's eagle is a large, mostly African, bird of prey. It is also called the black eagle, especially in southern Africa, not to be confused with the black eagle of south and southeast Asia.

aquilegia canadensis.name: Wild columbine
aquilegia canadensis.desc: Wild columbine (Aquilegia canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
aquilegia canadensis.about: Aquilegia canadensis, the Canadian columbine, Canada columbine, eastern red columbine, or wild columbine, is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family.

aquilegia coerulea.name: Rocky Mountain columbine
aquilegia coerulea.desc: Colorado columbine (Aquilegia coerulea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 89 times near the park in GBIF.
aquilegia coerulea.about: Aquilegia coerulea, commonly called the Colorado columbine, Rocky Mountain columbine, or blue columbine, is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family, native to the Rocky Mountains in the…

aquilegia micrantha.name: Alcove columbine
aquilegia micrantha.desc: Alcove columbine (Aquilegia micrantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
aquilegia micrantha.about: Aquilegia micrantha, the Mancos columbine or Bluff City columbine, is a perennial species of flowering plant in the family Ranunculaceae. It is native to Utah, Colorado, and Arizona.

ara ambiguus.name: Great green macaw
ara ambiguus.desc: A large parrot that cracks hard nuts. It relies heavily on almendro trees and Indio Maiz is a main refuge for it.
ara ambiguus.about: The great green macaw, also known as Buffon's macaw or the great military macaw, is a critically endangered Central and South America parrot found in Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica, Panama, Colombia…

ara macao.name: Scarlet macaw
ara macao.desc: Cracks open hard seeds and fruits high in the canopy.
ara macao.about: The scarlet macaw also called the red-and-yellow macaw, red-and-blue macaw or red-breasted macaw, is a large yellow, green, red and blue Neotropical parrot native to humid evergreen forests of the…

aralia elata.name: Japanese Angelica Tree
aralia elata.desc: Japanese Angelica Tree (Aralia elata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.

aralia hispida.name: Bristly Sarsaparilla
aralia hispida.desc: Bristly Sarsaparilla (Aralia hispida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

aralia nudicaulis.name: Wild Sarsaparilla
aralia nudicaulis.desc: Wild Sarsaparilla (Aralia nudicaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

aralia racemosa.name: Indianroot
aralia racemosa.desc: Indianroot (Aralia racemosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

aralia spinosa.name: American angelica-tree
aralia spinosa.desc: American angelica-tree (Aralia spinosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

aramus guarauna.name: Limpkin
aramus guarauna.desc: A wading bird that specializes in extracting apple snails from their shells.
aramus guarauna.about: The limpkin is a large wading bird related to rails and cranes, and the only extant species in the family Aramidae.

arapaima gigas.name: Arapaima
arapaima gigas.desc: One of the largest freshwater fish. It breathes air and eats other fish.
arapaima gigas.about: The arapaima, pirarucu, or paiche is a large species of bonytongue in the genus Arapaima native to the Amazon and Essequibo basins of South America.

arbutus menziesii.name: Pacific madrone
arbutus menziesii.desc: Pacific madrone (Arbutus menziesii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.
arbutus menziesii.about: Arbutus menziesii, or Pacific madrone, is a species of broadleaf evergreen tree in the family Ericaceae. It has waxy foliage, a contorted growth habit, and flaky bark.

archilochus alexandri.name: Black-chinned Hummingbird
archilochus alexandri.desc: Black-chinned Hummingbird (Archilochus alexandri): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 301 times near the park in GBIF.

arctia caja.name: Garden Tiger
arctia caja.desc: Garden Tiger (Arctia caja): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

arctocephalus australis.name: South American fur seal
arctocephalus australis.desc: Breeds on the Islas de Torres. Eats fish such as anchovies and squid, and is hunted by sharks, orcas and sea lions.
arctocephalus australis.about: The South American fur seal breeds on the coasts of Peru, Chile, the Falkland Islands, Argentina, Uruguay and Brazil. South American fur seals are of least concern on the IUCN Red List.

arctocephalus gazella.name: Antarctic fur seal
arctocephalus gazella.desc: Eats krill, among other prey. Its pups are taken by leopard seals.
arctocephalus gazella.about: The Antarctic fur seal is one of eight seals in the genus Arctocephalus, and one of nine fur seals in the subfamily Arctocephalinae.

arctocephalus pusillus.name: Cape fur seal
arctocephalus pusillus.desc: Large colonies breed on the Namib coast and feed on fish at sea. Their pups and carcasses feed jackals, hyenas and lions on land.
arctocephalus pusillus.about: Arctocephalus pusillus, commonly known as the Afro-Australian fur seal, or brown fur seal is a species of fur seal.

arctonyx collaris.name: Greater hog badger
arctonyx collaris.desc: A rooting forest omnivore that feeds on invertebrates and plant matter in leaf litter.
arctonyx collaris.about: The greater hog badger is a very large terrestrial mustelid native to Southeast Asia.

arctostaphylos andersonii.name: Santa Cruz manzanita
arctostaphylos andersonii.desc: Santa Cruz manzanita (Arctostaphylos andersonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 447 times near the park in GBIF.

arctostaphylos glauca.name: Bigberry manzanita
arctostaphylos glauca.desc: A chaparral shrub with berry-like fruit. Wikipedia says its seeds need exposure to fire before they germinate.
arctostaphylos glauca.about: Arctostaphylos glauca is a species of manzanita known by the common name bigberry manzanita.

arctostaphylos nevadensis.name: Pinemat manzanita
arctostaphylos nevadensis.desc: A low evergreen shrub whose berries are eaten by Sierra Nevada red foxes when in season.
arctostaphylos nevadensis.about: Arctostaphylos nevadensis, commonly known as pinemat manzanita, is a species of manzanita native to western North America.

arctostaphylos patula.name: Greenleaf manzanita
arctostaphylos patula.desc: A shrub of mid-elevation forest and chaparral whose flowers feed bumble bees and whose berries are food for wildlife.
arctostaphylos patula.about: Arctostaphylos patula is a species of manzanita known by the common name greenleaf manzanita. This manzanita is native to western North America where it grows at moderate to high elevations.

arctostaphylos pringlei.name: Pringle's manzanita
arctostaphylos pringlei.desc: Pringle's manzanita (Arctostaphylos pringlei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 494 times near the park in GBIF.

arctostaphylos pungens.name: Pointleaf manzanita
arctostaphylos pungens.desc: Pointleaf manzanita (Arctostaphylos pungens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 173 times near the park in GBIF.
arctostaphylos pungens.about: Arctostaphylos pungens, with the common name pointleaf manzanita, is a species of manzanita.

arctostaphylos silvicola.name: Bonny Doon manzanita
arctostaphylos silvicola.desc: Bonny Doon manzanita (Arctostaphylos silvicola): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 440 times near the park in GBIF.

arctostaphylos uva-ursi.name: Bearberry
arctostaphylos uva-ursi.desc: Bearberry (Arctostaphylos uva-ursi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 43 times near the park in GBIF.
arctostaphylos uva-ursi.about: Arctostaphylos uva-ursi is a plant species of the genus Arctostaphylos widely distributed across circumboreal regions of the subarctic Northern Hemisphere.

arctostaphylos viscida.name: WHITELEAF MANZANITA
arctostaphylos viscida.desc: WHITELEAF MANZANITA (Arctostaphylos viscida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 90 times near the park in GBIF.
arctostaphylos viscida.about: Arctostaphylos viscida, with the common names whiteleaf manzanita and sticky manzanita, is a species of manzanita.

ardea alba.name: Great Egret
ardea alba.desc: A tall wader that stalks fish, frogs, crayfish and insects in shallow water. It also takes young alligators.
ardea alba.about: The great egret, also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.

ardea cinerea.name: Grey heron
ardea cinerea.desc: Wading predator of frogs, small mammals, coots and fish; GloBI also records it taking coypu. The European eel page lists herons as eel predators.
ardea cinerea.about: The grey heron is a long-legged wading bird of the heron family, Ardeidae, native throughout Europe, Asia, and most of Africa.

ardea herodias.name: Great blue heron
ardea herodias.desc: Wades the shallows spearing fish. The NPS notes herons depend on fish.
ardea herodias.about: The great blue heron is a large wading bird in the heron family (Ardeidae), common near shores of open water and wetlands over most of North and Central America, as well as Northwestern South…

ardea melanocephala.name: Black-headed heron
ardea melanocephala.desc: A heron that hunts in open grassland and at water edges, eating frogs, reptiles and small animals.
ardea melanocephala.about: The black-headed heron is a wading bird of the heron family Ardeidae, common throughout much of sub-Saharan Africa and Madagascar.

ardea purpurea.name: Purple heron
ardea purpurea.desc: A reed-bed wader that stalks fish and frogs in shallow water.
ardea purpurea.about: The purple heron is a wide-ranging heron species. It breeds in Africa, central and southern Europe, and southern and eastern Palearctic.

ardenna carneipes.name: Flesh-footed shearwater
ardenna carneipes.desc: A burrow-nesting seabird. Lord Howe holds about 22,000 breeding pairs, though numbers on the island have been declining.
ardenna carneipes.about: The flesh-footed shearwater, also called sable shearwater or toanui, is a medium-large shearwater that mainly inhabits the Indo-Pacific.

ardenna pacifica.name: Wedge-tailed shearwater
ardenna pacifica.desc: A seabird that nests in burrows on Lord Howe and hunts fish, squid and crustaceans at sea, diving to depths of up to 66 m.
ardenna pacifica.about: The wedge-tailed shearwater is a medium-large shearwater in the seabird family Procellariidae.

ardisia crenata.name: Spiceberry
ardisia crenata.desc: Spiceberry (Ardisia crenata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 123 times near the park in GBIF.

ardisia escallonioides.name: Marlberry
ardisia escallonioides.desc: Marlberry (Ardisia escallonioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 101 times near the park in GBIF.

arenaria and calidris spp..name: Migratory shorebirds
arenaria and calidris spp..desc: Nest on the tundra for a few summer weeks, feeding on insects, seeds and eggs. Many then fly to coasts and reef flats as far south as Australia.
arenaria and calidris spp..about: The ruddy turnstone is a small cosmopolitan wading bird, one of two species of turnstone in the genus Arenaria.

arenga obtusifolia.name: Arenga palm
arenga obtusifolia.desc: A fast-growing palm that shades the forest floor and reduces the food available to rhinos, so authorities work to remove it.
arenga obtusifolia.about: Arenga obtusifolia is a flowering plant in the palm family Arecaceae native to Thailand, Malaysia, Borneo and Java.

arenicola marina.name: Lugworm
arenicola marina.desc: A burrowing worm that swallows sand and digests the organic matter in it. Its coiled casts are visible at low tide.
arenicola marina.about: The blow lugworm, also known as sandworm, is a large species of marine worm.

argemone pleiacantha.name: Southwestern pricklypoppy
argemone pleiacantha.desc: Southwestern pricklypoppy (Argemone pleiacantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

argemone polyanthemos.name: Plains prickly-poppy
argemone polyanthemos.desc: Annual pricklypoppy (Argemone polyanthemos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.
argemone polyanthemos.about: Argemone polyanthemos, the crested pricklypoppy, also known as bluestem prickly poppy, pricklypoppy, white prickly poppy, annual pricklypoppy, or as thistle poppy is an annual plant with yellow sap…

argia vivida.name: Vivid Dancer
argia vivida.desc: Vivid Dancer (Argia vivida): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.
argia vivida.about: Argia vivida, the vivid dancer, is a species of narrow-winged damselfly in the family Coenagrionidae. This species is commonly found in springs and forests of Central America and North America.

argyrochosma dealbata.name: Powdery false cloak fern
argyrochosma dealbata.desc: Powdery false cloak fern (Argyrochosma dealbata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
argyrochosma dealbata.about: Argyrochosma dealbata, the powdery false cloak fern, is a small fern endemic to the central and southern United States. It grows on calcareous rocks, such as limestone.

argyroxiphium sandwicense.name: Haleakalā silversword
argyroxiphium sandwicense.desc: A silver-leaved plant found only on Haleakalā, above about 2,100 m. It is federally threatened, and introduced hoofed animals are a major reason it declined.
argyroxiphium sandwicense.about: Argyroxiphium sandwicense, the Hawaiʻi silversword, or hinahina is a species of silversword. It is endemic to Hawaii.

arilus cristatus.name: Wheel Bug
arilus cristatus.desc: Wheel Bug (Arilus cristatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
arilus cristatus.about: Arilus cristatus, also known as the North American wheel bug or simply wheel bug, is a species of large assassin bug in the family Reduviidae and the only species of wheel bug found in the United…

ariolimax columbianus.name: Pacific banana slug
ariolimax columbianus.desc: A big forest-floor slug that eats leaves, moss, dung and dead plant matter, and recycles them into soil. Snakes and small mammals sometimes eat it.
ariolimax columbianus.about: Ariolimax columbianus, the Pacific banana slug, is a species of slug found on the Pacific coast of North America.

arisaema dracontium.name: Dragon-arum
arisaema dracontium.desc: Dragon-arum (Arisaema dracontium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

arisaema triphyllum.name: Indian-turnip
arisaema triphyllum.desc: Indian-turnip (Arisaema triphyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
arisaema triphyllum.about: Arisaema triphyllum, the Jack-in-the-pulpit, is a species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae.

aristolochia watsonii.name: Indian root
aristolochia watsonii.desc: Indian root (Aristolochia watsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

arizona elegans.name: Glossy snake
arizona elegans.desc: A nocturnal desert snake. GloBI records show it eating kangaroo rats, deer mice and lizards.
arizona elegans.about: Arizona elegans is a species of medium-sized colubrid snake commonly referred to as the glossy snake or the faded snake, which is native to southwestern United States and northern Mexico.

armeria maritima.name: Thrift
armeria maritima.desc: Thrift (Armeria maritima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 127 times near the park in GBIF.

arnoglossum atriplicifolium.name: Pale Indian-plantain
arnoglossum atriplicifolium.desc: Pale Indian-plantain (Arnoglossum atriplicifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
arnoglossum atriplicifolium.about: Arnoglossum atriplicifolium, the pale Indian plantain, is a perennial herbaceous wildflower in the sunflower family (Asteraceae). native to the central and eastern United States.

arnoglossum plantagineum.name: Arnoglossum
arnoglossum plantagineum.desc: Arnoglossum (Arnoglossum plantagineum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
arnoglossum plantagineum.about: Arnoglossum plantagineum also known as tuberous Indian-plantain, groovestem Indian plantain or prairie Indian plantain, is a North American species of Arnoglossum in the sunflower family.

artemia.name: Brine shrimp
artemia.desc: Tiny crustaceans of salt lakes and brine ponds. Their tolerance of very salty water helps them escape most fish predators.
artemia.about: Artemia is a genus of aquatic crustaceans also known as brine shrimp. It is the only genus in the family Artemiidae.

astrocaryum standleyanum.name: Black palm
astrocaryum standleyanum.desc: A spiny lowland palm of Pacific Central America whose large seeds are eaten and buried by forest rodents.
astrocaryum standleyanum.about: Astrocaryum standleyanum, commonly known as the black palm or chunga, is a species of palm native to Central and South America, where its distribution extends from Costa Rica to Ecuador.

astrochelys radiata.name: Radiated tortoise
astrochelys radiata.desc: Grazing tortoise of the southern spiny thickets that feeds on plants.
astrochelys radiata.about: The radiated tortoise is a tortoise species in the family Testudinidae.

atalopedes campestris.name: Sachem
atalopedes campestris.desc: Sachem (Atalopedes campestris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

ateles geoffroyi.name: Geoffroy's spider monkey
ateles geoffroyi.desc: Fruit takes most of its feeding time, with leaves, flowers and insects as extras. Jaguars and pumas are its main adult predators.
ateles geoffroyi.about: Geoffroy's spider monkey, also known as the black-handed spider monkey or the Central American spider monkey, is a species of spider monkey, a type of New World monkey, from Central America, parts of…

ateles paniscus.name: Red-faced spider monkey
ateles paniscus.desc: A large canopy primate that eats mostly fruit and young leaves, plus some insects. A prey of harpy eagles.
ateles paniscus.about: The red-faced spider monkey, also known as the Guiana spider monkey or red-faced black spider monkey, is a species of spider monkey found in the rain forests in northern South America.

athene cunicularia.name: Burrowing owl
athene cunicularia.desc: Nests underground and is associated with prairie dog colonies. Hunts small mammals, birds, frogs and insects.
athene cunicularia.about: The burrowing owl is a small, long-legged, primarily terrestrial—though not flightless—species of owl native to the open landscapes of North and South America.

athene noctua.name: Little owl
athene noctua.desc: A small owl of open dry country that hunts small birds, rodents and insects, often at dusk.
athene noctua.about: The little owl, also known as the owl of Athena or owl of Minerva, is a bird that inhabits much of the temperate and warmer parts of Europe, the Palearctic east to Korea, and North Africa.

atheris nitschei.name: Great Lakes bush viper
atheris nitschei.desc: A tree-dwelling viper of Albertine Rift forests, recorded eating Temminck's mouse.
atheris nitschei.about: Common names: Great Lakes bush viper, Nitsche's bush viper, more. Atheris nitschei is a species of venomous snake, a viper in the subfamily Viperinae of the family Viperidae.

atlantic rain.name: Atlantic rain
atlantic rain.desc: Wet Atlantic weather feeds the plants of the thin soils and the Burren's seasonal lakes.

atlantic rainfall.name: Atlantic rainfall
atlantic rainfall.desc: Mountains block moist Atlantic air, giving very heavy rain, roughly 1,600 mm a year low down and about 3,200 mm on the heights.

atlides halesus.name: Great Purple Hairstreak
atlides halesus.desc: Great Purple Hairstreak (Atlides halesus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

atractosteus spatula.name: Alligator gar
atractosteus spatula.desc: An ambush predator of slow river backwaters and brackish marsh. Eats mainly shad and other fish, and blue crabs in brackish water.
atractosteus spatula.about: The alligator gar is a euryhaline ray-finned fish in the clade Ginglymodi of the infraclass Holostei , being most closely related to the bowfins.

atriplex argentea.name: Saltbush
atriplex argentea.desc: Saltbush (Atriplex argentea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
atriplex argentea.about: Atriplex argentea is a species of saltbush known by the common names silverscale saltbush and silver orache.

atriplex canescens.name: Four-wing saltbush
atriplex canescens.desc: Four-wing saltbush (Atriplex canescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
atriplex canescens.about: Atriplex canescens (or chamiso, chamiza, four-wing saltbush) is a species of evergreen shrub in the family Amaranthaceae (subfamily Chenopodioideae) native to the western and midwestern United States.

atriplex gardneri.name: Gardner's saltbush
atriplex gardneri.desc: Gardner's saltbush (Atriplex gardneri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
atriplex gardneri.about: Atriplex gardneri is a species of flowering plant in the amaranth family known by the common name Gardner's saltbush.

atriplex halimus.name: Shrubby orache
atriplex halimus.desc: A salt-tolerant evergreen shrub of dry, saline ground that provides browse in arid areas.
atriplex halimus.about: Atriplex halimus is a species of fodder shrub in the family Amaranthaceae.

atriplex lampa.name: Saltbush
atriplex lampa.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of dry ground that suits the salty soils. Maras are reported to eat it.
atriplex lampa.about: Atriplex () is a plant genus of about 250 species, known by the common names of saltbush and orache. It belongs to the subfamily Chenopodioideae of the family Amaranthaceae s.l..

atriplex micrantha.name: Twoscale Saltbush
atriplex micrantha.desc: Twoscale Saltbush (Atriplex micrantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

atriplex parishii.name: Parish's saltbush
atriplex parishii.desc: Parish's saltbush (Atriplex parishii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
atriplex parishii.about: Atriplex parishii is an uncommon species of saltbush known by the common names Parish's saltbush and Parish's brittlescale.

atriplex prostrata.name: Spear-leaved Orache
atriplex prostrata.desc: Spear-leaved Orache (Atriplex prostrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
atriplex prostrata.about: Atriplex prostrata, called the spear-leaved orache, hastate orache, thin-leaf orache, triangle orache, and fat hen, is a widespread species of flowering plant in the saltbush genus Atriplex, native…

atriplex rosea.name: Redscale
atriplex rosea.desc: Redscale (Atriplex rosea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

atrytone delaware.name: Atrytone delaware
atrytone delaware.desc: Atrytone delaware (Atrytone delaware): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

atta.name: Leafcutter ants
atta.desc: Cut leaves to feed fungus gardens. Wikipedia says nests reach densities of up to 4,000 per hectare in the Cerrado.
atta.about: Leafcutter ants are several species of fungus-growing ants that share the behaviour of cutting leaves which they carry back to their nests to farm fungus.

atta cephalotes.name: Leafcutter ants
atta cephalotes.desc: Carry leaf fragments to underground gardens of fungus, which they eat.
atta cephalotes.about: Atta cephalotes, commonly known as the hairy-headed leafcutter ant, is a species of leafcutter ant in the tribe Attini (fungus-growing ants).

attalea phalerata.name: Acuri palm
attalea phalerata.desc: A palm whose very hard nuts are the main food of hyacinth macaws in the Pantanal. Collared peccaries and many birds also eat its fruit.
attalea phalerata.about: Attalea phalerata is a species of palm tree known by the English common name urucuri palm, the Portuguese common name urucurizeiro, and the Spanish common name shapaja.

augochlora pura.name: Pure Green Augochlora
augochlora pura.desc: Pure Green Augochlora (Augochlora pura): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 207 times near the park in GBIF.
augochlora pura.about: Augochlora pura is a solitary sweat bee found primarily in the Eastern United States. It is known for its bright green color and its tendency to forage on a variety of plants.

augochlorella aurata.name: Golden Sweat Bee
augochlorella aurata.desc: Golden Sweat Bee (Augochlorella aurata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 216 times near the park in GBIF.
augochlorella aurata.about: Augochlorella aurata is a primitively eusocial species of sweat bee (bees attracted by the salt in human sweat) in the family Halictidae.

aulacoseira baicalensis.name: Diatoms (Aulacoseira)
aulacoseira baicalensis.desc: Microscopic glassy algae that bloom in and under the ice. Over 400 diatom species live in Baikal, and about half are found nowhere else.
aulacoseira baicalensis.about: Aulacoseira is a genus of diatoms belonging to the family Aulacoseiraceae. The genus has cosmopolitan distribution.

auriparus flaviceps.name: Verdin
auriparus flaviceps.desc: Verdin (Auriparus flaviceps): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,590 times near the park in GBIF.
auriparus flaviceps.about: The verdin is a species of penduline tit. It is the only species in the genus Auriparus and the only representative of the Old World family Remizidae to be found in North America.

austrostipa.name: Spear grasses
austrostipa.desc: Tussock grasses of the sandy mainland and island country, grazed and seeded on by ground-dwelling mammals.
austrostipa.about: Austrostipa is a primarily Australian genus of plants in the grass family, commonly called speargrass. The genus includes species formerly included in the genus Stipa.

automeris io.name: Io Moth
automeris io.desc: Io Moth (Automeris io): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

autumn-winter rain.name: Autumn-winter rain
autumn-winter rain.desc: Rainfall drives the flooding of the marshes. Wikipedia notes that very low water in January 2024 gave the lowest bird count on record.

avena.name: Wild oats and grasses
avena.desc: Grasses of clearings, forest edges and farmland, recorded in large numbers near the forest.
avena.about: Avena sterilis (animated oat, sterile oat, wild oat, wild red oat, winter wild oat; syn. Avena ludoviciana Durieu; Avena macrocarpa Moench; Avena sterilis ssp.

avena sterilis.name: Wild oat
avena sterilis.desc: A wild annual grass of the Mediterranean and steppe zones that sprouts after winter rain and feeds grazers and seed eaters.
avena sterilis.about: Avena sterilis (animated oat, sterile oat, wild oat, wild red oat, winter wild oat; syn. Avena ludoviciana Durieu; Avena macrocarpa Moench; Avena sterilis ssp.

avenella flexuosa.name: Wavy hair-grass
avenella flexuosa.desc: A fine grass of acidic, sandy forest soils and open ground, where it grows in tufts.
avenella flexuosa.about: Avenella flexuosa, commonly known as wavy hair-grass, is a species of bunchgrass in the grass family widely distributed in Eurasia, Africa, South America, and North America.

avicennia germinans.name: Black mangrove
avicennia germinans.desc: Black mangrove (Avicennia germinans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.
avicennia germinans.about: Avicennia germinans, the black mangrove, is a shrub or small tree growing up to 12 meters (39 feet) in the acanthus family, Acanthaceae.

avicennia marina.name: Grey mangrove
avicennia marina.desc: One of the few mangroves of arid Red Sea shores; its aerial roots trap sediment and it excretes salt through its leaves.
avicennia marina.about: Avicennia marina, commonly known as grey mangrove or white mangrove, is a species of mangrove tree classified in the plant family Acanthaceae.

awash river inflow.name: Awash River inflow
awash river inflow.desc: The Awash is the lake's main source of water. It has no outflow, so salts build up and the level swings with river supply.

axis axis.name: Chital
axis axis.desc: The main large prey of the Sundarbans tiger. Browses and grazes on the forest floor.
axis axis.about: The chital, also called spotted deer and axis deer, is a deer species native to the Indian subcontinent. It was first described by Johann Christian Polycarp Erxleben in 1777.

axis porcinus.name: Hog deer
axis porcinus.desc: A small deer of the floodplain grasslands, recorded as prey of tigers and leopards.
axis porcinus.about: Axis is a genus of deer occurring in South and Southeast Asia. As presently defined by most authorities, four species are placed in the genus.

axonopus, paspalum.name: Cerrado grasses
axonopus, paspalum.desc: Grasses form most of the herb layer of the open savanna, which Wikipedia says typically reaches about 60 cm. Golden carpetgrass is well recorded here.
axonopus, paspalum.about: Paspalum is a genus of plants in the grass family. The group is widespread across much of Asia, Africa, Australia, and the Americas.

aythya collaris.name: Ring-necked Duck
aythya collaris.desc: Ring-necked Duck (Aythya collaris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

aythya valisineria.name: Canvasback
aythya valisineria.desc: A diving duck that migrates along the Mississippi Flyway. It eats tubers, buds, seeds, snails and insect larvae, favoring wild celery. The FWS says the upper river supports up to half the world's canvasbacks.
aythya valisineria.about: The canvasback is a species of diving duck, the largest found in North America.

azolla caroliniana.name: Mosquito fern
azolla caroliniana.desc: Mosquito fern (Azolla caroliniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
azolla caroliniana.about: Azolla cristata, the Carolina mosquito fern, Carolina azolla, or water velvet, is a species of the Azolla genus native to the Americas, in eastern North America from southern Ontario southward, from…

azolla cristata.name: Atlantic azolla
azolla cristata.desc: Atlantic azolla (Azolla cristata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
azolla cristata.about: Azolla cristata, the Carolina mosquito fern, Carolina azolla, or water velvet, is a species of the Azolla genus native to the Americas, in eastern North America from southern Ontario southward, from…

azolla filiculoides.name: Water Fern
azolla filiculoides.desc: Water Fern (Azolla filiculoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
azolla filiculoides.about: Azolla filiculoides (water fern) is a species of aquatic fern.

azorella compacta.name: Yareta
azorella compacta.desc: A dense, cushion-forming evergreen of the high Andes that grows only a centimetre or so a year. Local people burn it for fuel, which is hard for it to withstand.
azorella compacta.about: Yareta or llareta (in Spanish), known scientifically as Azorella compacta, is a velvety, chartreuse cushion plant in the family Apiaceae which is native to South America.

azorella selago.name: Cushion azorella
azorella selago.desc: Compact cushion plant common in the islands fellfield and rocky ground, and eaten by introduced rabbits.
azorella selago.about: Azorella selago is a species of cushion plant native to the sub-Antarctic islands of the Southern Ocean, including the Crozet Islands, the Possession Islands, the Heard Island and McDonald Islands,…

baccaurea parviflora.name: Baccaurea trees
baccaurea parviflora.desc: Understory fruit tree recorded in the reserve; its fruit is eaten by macaques and mouse-deer according to GloBI records.
baccaurea parviflora.about: Baccaurea is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Phyllanthaceae.

baccharis halimifolia.name: Tree Groundsel
baccharis halimifolia.desc: Groundsel tree (Baccharis halimifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 98 times near the park in GBIF.
baccharis halimifolia.about: Baccharis halimifolia is a North American species of shrubs in the family Asteraceae.

baccharis pilularis.name: Coyote Brush
baccharis pilularis.desc: Coyote Brush (Baccharis pilularis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 714 times near the park in GBIF.
baccharis pilularis.about: Baccharis pilularis, called coyote brush (or bush), chaparral broom, and bush baccharis, is an evergreen shrub in the family Asteraceae native to California, Oregon, Washington, and Baja California.

baccharis salicifolia.name: Sticky baccharis
baccharis salicifolia.desc: Sticky baccharis (Baccharis salicifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 125 times near the park in GBIF.

baccharis sarothroides.name: Desert-broom
baccharis sarothroides.desc: Desert-broom (Baccharis sarothroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

bacillariophyceae.name: Phytoplankton
bacillariophyceae.desc: Microscopic drifting algae, including diatoms, that capture sunlight in the bay and fjord waters and feed the marine food chain.
bacillariophyceae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

bacillariophyceae and other microalgae.name: Phytoplankton and algae
bacillariophyceae and other microalgae.desc: Drifting microscopic algae, including about 20 endemic algae species in Ohrid, feed the zooplankton and snails.
bacillariophyceae and other microalgae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

bacillariophyta.name: Marsh algae & diatoms
bacillariophyta.desc: Microscopic algae in the shallow marsh water. Flamingos filter algae and diatoms from the mud and water.
bacillariophyta.about: A diatom is any member of a large group comprising several genera of algae, specifically microalgae, found in the oceans, waterways and soils of the world.

bacillariophyta (diatoms).name: Stream algae
bacillariophyta (diatoms).desc: Films of diatoms on stream stones. They feed the mayflies and other grazers that trout depend on.
bacillariophyta (diatoms).about: A diatom is any member of a large group comprising several genera of algae, specifically microalgae, found in the oceans, waterways and soils of the world.

bacteria and fungi.name: Decomposers
bacteria and fungi.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

bacteria, fungi and worms.name: Decomposers
bacteria, fungi and worms.desc: Break down mangrove leaf litter, dead seagrass and carcasses, returning nutrients to the bay.

bacteria, worms, snails.name: Bacteria & decomposers
bacteria, worms, snails.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the water. Decaying blooms use up oxygen.

badland and clay soils.name: Badland and clay soils
badland and clay soils.desc: Erodible clay soils of the Painted Desert hold little water and nutrients, so the grassland on better soils is a prized, slow-recovering resource.

badlands soil.name: Badlands soil
badlands soil.desc: Nutrients in the soil feed the grasses and shrubs.

baeolophus bicolor.name: Tufted Titmouse
baeolophus bicolor.desc: Tufted Titmouse (Baeolophus bicolor): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 86 times near the park in GBIF.
baeolophus bicolor.about: The tufted titmouse is a small songbird native to eastern North America. The species belongs to the tit and chickadee family (Paridae).

baeolophus inornatus.name: Oak Titmouse
baeolophus inornatus.desc: Oak Titmouse (Baeolophus inornatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2,627 times near the park in GBIF.

baikiaea plurijuga.name: Zambezi teak
baikiaea plurijuga.desc: A dry-woodland tree. Wikipedia says dense stands of it once covered the Chobe riverfront before elephants thinned them.
baikiaea plurijuga.about: Baikiaea plurijuga, known as African teak, Mukusi, Rhodesian teak, Zambian teak, or Zambesi redwood, is a species of Afrotropical tree from the legume family, Fabaceae.

balaeniceps rex.name: Shoebill
balaeniceps rex.desc: A giant wading bird for which the Sudd is a major stronghold; it hunts large fish such as lungfish in papyrus swamp.
balaeniceps rex.about: The shoebill, also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird. It is named for its enormous, shoe-shaped bill.

balaenoptera musculus.name: Blue whale
balaenoptera musculus.desc: The largest animal; feeds on krill by filtering swarms.
balaenoptera musculus.about: The blue whale is a species of baleen whale and the largest marine mammal in the rorqual family Balaenopteridae.

balaenoptera physalus.name: Fin whale
balaenoptera physalus.desc: Fin whale (Balaenoptera physalus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

balearica pavonina.name: Black crowned crane
balearica pavonina.desc: A wetland crane that feeds on seeds, insects and small animals in grasslands and shallow water of the Sudd.
balearica pavonina.about: The black crowned crane is a part of the family Gruidae, along with its sister species, the grey crowned crane. It is topped with its characteristic bristle-feathered golden crown.

balsamorhiza careyana.name: Carey's balsamroot
balsamorhiza careyana.desc: Carey's balsamroot (Balsamorhiza careyana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
balsamorhiza careyana.about: Balsamorhiza careyana is a species of flowering plant in the tribe Heliantheae of the family Asteraceae known by the common name Carey's balsamroot.

bambusoideae.name: Bamboo & forest grasses
bambusoideae.desc: Grasses and bamboo grow in clearings, gaps and secondary growth. Grass is a regular food of large deer such as sambar.
bambusoideae.about: Bamboos are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

baptisia australis.name: Baptisia
baptisia australis.desc: Baptisia (Baptisia australis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
baptisia australis.about: Baptisia australis, commonly known as blue wild indigo or blue false indigo, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae (legumes).

barkleyanthus salicifolius.name: Willow ragwort
barkleyanthus salicifolius.desc: Willow ragwort (Barkleyanthus salicifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 54 times near the park in GBIF.

barringtonia acutangula.name: Flooded-forest tree
barringtonia acutangula.desc: A tree of the seasonally flooded forest that rings the lake and shelters young fish when the water rises.
barringtonia acutangula.about: Barringtonia acutangula is a species of plant in the family Lecythidaceae native to coastal areas from Afghanistan east to mainland Southeast Asia and south to northern Australia.

barringtonia edulis.name: Cutnut
barringtonia edulis.desc: An evergreen tree of humid forests found only in Fiji and Vanuatu. Moths and bats pollinate its flowers and its seeds are edible.
barringtonia edulis.about: Barringtonia edulis is a species of tree with edible fruits from the southwestern Pacific region, being found on Fiji and Vanuatu.

basilinna leucotis.name: White-eared hummingbird
basilinna leucotis.desc: A very commonly recorded bird of the highland forests, feeding on nectar from sages and other flowers.
basilinna leucotis.about: The white-eared hummingbird is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of subfamily Trochilinae. It is found from the southwestern U.S. to Nicaragua.

batis maritima.name: Saltwort
batis maritima.desc: Saltwort (Batis maritima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 68 times near the park in GBIF.

battus philenor.name: Blue Swallowtail
battus philenor.desc: Blue Swallowtail (Battus philenor): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
battus philenor.about: Battus philenor, the pipevine swallowtail or blue swallowtail, is a swallowtail butterfly found in North America and Central America. This butterfly is black with iridescent-blue hindwings.

bay nutrients.name: Bay nutrients
bay nutrients.desc: Nutrients released from dead plants and animals feed seagrass, mangroves and algae again.

bay water and tides.name: Bay water and tides
bay water and tides.desc: Salt water from San Lorenzo Bay floods the mangrove roots and carries the plankton and small fish the seabirds depend on.

bebbia juncea.name: Sweetbush
bebbia juncea.desc: Sweetbush (Bebbia juncea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

bejaria racemosa.name: Tarflower
bejaria racemosa.desc: Tarflower (Bejaria racemosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

benguela current algae.name: Phytoplankton
benguela current algae.desc: Drifting algae in the cold, productive Benguela Current, the base of the offshore food chain.
benguela current algae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

berberis microphylla.name: Calafate
berberis microphylla.desc: A spiny shrub of the steppe and forest edge that bears dark berries in summer.
berberis microphylla.about: Berberis microphylla, common name box-leaved barberry and Magellan barberry, in Spanish calafate and michay and other names, is an evergreen shrub, with simple, shiny box-like leaves.

berberis thunbergii.name: Thunberg's Barberry
berberis thunbergii.desc: Thunberg's Barberry (Berberis thunbergii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

bertholletia excelsa.name: Brazil nut tree
bertholletia excelsa.desc: A towering canopy tree whose hard-shelled seeds are opened only by agoutis.
bertholletia excelsa.about: Brazil nut refers to a South American tree of the monotypic genus Bertholletia in the family Lecythidaceae as well as the tree's commercially-harvested edible seeds.

bettongia lesueur.name: Boodie
bettongia lesueur.desc: Burrowing bettong that eats seeds, roots, fungi, grasses and more. Its digging turns over soil and spreads seeds and fungi.
bettongia lesueur.about: The boodie, also known as the burrowing bettong or Lesueur's rat-kangaroo, is a small, furry, rat-like mammal native to Australia.

betula alleghaniensis.name: Yellow Birch
betula alleghaniensis.desc: A major tree of the Green Mountains hardwood forest. Browsed by deer and eaten by beavers, porcupines and red squirrels.
betula alleghaniensis.about: Betula alleghaniensis, the yellow birch, golden birch, or swamp birch, is a large species of birch native to northeastern North America.

betula ermanii.name: Erman's birch
betula ermanii.desc: A birch that forms the tree line on the mountain, growing where conifers thin out below the tundra.
betula ermanii.about: Betula ermanii, or Erman's birch, is a species of birch tree belonging to the family Betulaceae.

betula papyrifera.name: Paper birch
betula papyrifera.desc: A pale-barked northern hardwood recorded in the park; browsed by deer, hares and beavers and a common pioneer after disturbance.
betula papyrifera.about: Betula papyrifera (paper birch, also known as (American) white birch and canoe birch) is a short-lived species of birch native to northern North America.

betula pendula.name: Silver birch
betula pendula.desc: A pioneer tree of clearings and disturbed ground, browsed by roe deer and gnawed by beavers.
betula pendula.about: Betula pendula, the silver birch, is a species of tree in the flowering plant family, Betulaceae. The trees can reach a height of 30 m, and have white bark that sheds regularly.

betula pubescens.name: Mountain birch
betula pubescens.desc: A pale-barked tree that forms the open woodland on the lower mountain slopes. Moose and hares eat its twigs and buds.
betula pubescens.about: Betula pubescens, commonly known as downy birch and also as moor birch, white birch, European white birch or hairy birch, is a species of deciduous tree, native and abundant throughout northern…

betula tianschanica.name: Tien Shan birch
betula tianschanica.desc: A shrubby birch of sheltered Pamir valleys, one of the few tree-like plants in the park.
betula tianschanica.about: A birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula (), in the family Betulaceae, which also includes alders, hazels, and hornbeams.

bidens alba.name: Beggarticks
bidens alba.desc: A common wildflower of open ground. GloBI records it as food for the eastern lubber grasshopper.
bidens alba.about: Bidens alba is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, commonly known as shepherd's needles, beggarticks, Spanish needles, or butterfly needles.

bidens frondosa.name: Beggarticks
bidens frondosa.desc: Beggarticks (Bidens frondosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

bignonia capreolata.name: Crossvine
bignonia capreolata.desc: Crossvine (Bignonia capreolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
bignonia capreolata.about: Bignonia capreolata is a vine commonly referred to as crossvine.

birgus latro.name: Coconut crab
birgus latro.desc: The largest land arthropod. It eats fruit and carrion and also kills tortoise hatchlings and other crabs. Adults have almost no predators.
birgus latro.about: The coconut crab is a terrestrial species of giant hermit crab, and is also known as the robber crab or palm thief. It is the largest living terrestrial arthropod, with a weight up to 4.1 kg (9.0 lb).

bison bison.name: American bison
bison bison.desc: About 50 bison were released in 1963 and the herd has grown to over 1,200. They graze grasses such as western wheatgrass.
bison bison.about: The American bison, commonly known as the American buffalo, or simply buffalo (not to be confused with true buffalo), is a species of bison that is endemic to North America.

bison bonasus.name: European bison
bison bonasus.desc: Europe's heaviest land animal eats grasses, herbs and tree bark and leaves. The forest holds the largest free-living herd, restored after reintroduction in 1929.
bison bonasus.about: The European bison (pl.: bison) or the European wood bison, also known as the wisent, the zubr (), or sometimes colloquially as the European buffalo, is a European species of bison.

bistorta bistortoides.name: American bistort
bistorta bistortoides.desc: American bistort (Bistorta bistortoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 75 times near the park in GBIF.

bistorta vivipara.name: Alpine bistort
bistorta vivipara.desc: A small tundra herb whose leaves and bulbils are eaten by birds such as the rock ptarmigan.
bistorta vivipara.about: Bistorta vivipara is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the knotweed and buckwheat family Polygonaceae, commonly known as alpine bistort.

bitis nasicornis.name: Rhinoceros viper
bitis nasicornis.desc: A forest viper recorded in the Nimba circle. GloBI records it eating the striped grass mouse.
bitis nasicornis.about: Bitis nasicornis is a viper species belonging to the genus Bitis, part of a subfamily known as "puff-adders", found in the forests of West and Central Africa.

bitis peringueyi.name: Peringuey's adder
bitis peringueyi.desc: A small sidewinding viper that buries itself in sand and ambushes lizards. Dune lizards with high water content help it get water.
bitis peringueyi.about: Bitis peringueyi, also known commonly as Peringuey's adder, Peringuey's desert adder, and the desert sidewinding adder, is a species of venomous snake in the subfamily Viperinae of the family…

bivalves and polychaetes.name: Bottom clams & worms
bivalves and polychaetes.desc: Seafloor dwellers that feed on plankton and detritus. Summer low-oxygen zones kill them, which removes a key food source for blue crabs.
bivalves and polychaetes.about: Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc. The word is often applied only to those that are deemed edible and live as infauna, spending most of their lives halfway buried in the…

bivalvia.name: Seafloor clams
bivalvia.desc: Bottom-living clams and other bivalves. Pacific walruses prefer them, and benthic invertebrates make up most of the walrus diet.
bivalvia.about: Bivalvia () or bivalves, in previous centuries referred to as the Lamellibranchiata and Pelecypoda, is a class of aquatic molluscs (marine and freshwater) that have laterally compressed soft bodies…

black sea rain.name: Black Sea rain
black sea rain.desc: Moist air from the Black Sea coast waters the northern slopes and supports their forests.

blackwater and rain.name: Blackwater and rain
blackwater and rain.desc: The swamp depends on rainfall, and decaying plants stain the water tea-coloured. The Suwannee and St. Marys rivers drain it.

blarina brevicauda.name: Northern short-tailed shrew
blarina brevicauda.desc: Northern short-tailed shrew (Blarina brevicauda): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
blarina brevicauda.about: The northern short-tailed shrew is the largest shrew in the genus Blarina, and occurs in the northeastern region of North America.

blastocerus dichotomus.name: Marsh deer
blastocerus dichotomus.desc: South America's largest deer lives only in shallow marsh. The reserve is a stronghold for this Vulnerable species, which eats mostly aquatic plants.
blastocerus dichotomus.about: The marsh deer is a species of deer native to South America. It is the largest living species of South American deer.

blephilia ciliata.name: Downy wood-mint
blephilia ciliata.desc: Downy wood-mint (Blephilia ciliata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
blephilia ciliata.about: Blephilia ciliata is a species of herbaceous perennial plant in the Lamiaceae (mint) family native to central and eastern North America. It is commonly called downy wood mint.

blitum nuttallianum.name: Poverty-weed
blitum nuttallianum.desc: Poverty-weed (Blitum nuttallianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

boa constrictor.name: Boa constrictor
boa constrictor.desc: Ambushes agoutis, birds and small mammals.
boa constrictor.about: The boa constrictor, also known as the common boa, is a species of large, non-venomous, heavy-bodied snake that is frequently kept and bred in captivity.

boa imperator.name: Boa constrictor
boa imperator.desc: A constricting snake. GloBI records it eating fruit bats, agoutis, black iguanas and gray foxes.
boa imperator.about: The boa constrictor, also known as the common boa, is a species of large, non-venomous, heavy-bodied snake that is frequently kept and bred in captivity.

bocconia frutescens.name: Parrot weed
bocconia frutescens.desc: A fast-growing shrub of forest openings whose seeds are eaten by small birds.

boerhavia coccinea.name: Scarlet Spiderling
boerhavia coccinea.desc: Scarlet Spiderling (Boerhavia coccinea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

boisea trivittata.name: Boxelder Bug
boisea trivittata.desc: Boxelder Bug (Boisea trivittata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
boisea trivittata.about: Boisea trivittata, also called the eastern boxelder bug, box bug, or maple bug, is a species of true bug native to eastern North America.

bolbometopon muricatum.name: Bumphead parrotfish
bolbometopon muricatum.desc: A large reef fish that scrapes and crunches live coral and algae; its feeding produces coral sand and clears space on the reef.
bolbometopon muricatum.about: The green humphead parrotfish is the largest species of parrotfish, growing to lengths of 1.3 m (4.3 ft) and weighing up to 46 kg (101 lb), though some sources report a total length of 1.5 m (4 ft 11…

bolboschoenus maritimus.name: Sea Club-rush
bolboschoenus maritimus.desc: Sea Club-rush (Bolboschoenus maritimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
bolboschoenus maritimus.about: Bolboschoenus maritimus is a species of flowering plant from family Cyperaceae.

boleophthalmus boddarti.name: Mudskipper
boleophthalmus boddarti.desc: Fish that crawls over mudflats at low tide scraping green algae, and is also found in Kuwait Sulaibikhat Bay.
boleophthalmus boddarti.about: Boleophthalmus boddarti, commonly known as Boddart's goggle-eyed goby, is a species of mudskipper native to the Indo-Pacific, and the type species of the genus Boleophthalmus.

boloria selene.name: Small Pearl-bordered Fritillary
boloria selene.desc: Small Pearl-bordered Fritillary (Boloria selene): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
boloria selene.about: Boloria selene, known in Europe as the small pearl-bordered fritillary, is a species of butterfly of the family Nymphalidae.

bombus.name: Bumble bees
bombus.desc: Many bumble bee species are recorded in the park. They feed on nectar and pollen from fireweed and other wildflowers.
bombus.about: A bumblebee is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.

bombus affinis.name: Rusty-patched Bumble Bee
bombus affinis.desc: Rusty-patched Bumble Bee (Bombus affinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus affinis.about: Bombus affinis, commonly known as the rusty patched bumble bee, is a species of bumblebee endemic to North America.

bombus auricomus.name: Black And Gold Bumble Bee
bombus auricomus.desc: Black And Gold Bumble Bee (Bombus auricomus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus auricomus.about: Bombus auricomus is a species of bumblebee known by the common name black and gold bumblebee.

bombus balteatus.name: High Country Bumble Bee
bombus balteatus.desc: High Country Bumble Bee (Bombus balteatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus balteatus.about: Bombus balteatus, the golden-belted bumble bee, is a species of bumblebee with a boreal and high altitude distribution in northern Eurasia and North America.

bombus bifarius.name: Black-notched Bumble Bee
bombus bifarius.desc: Black-notched Bumble Bee (Bombus bifarius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 90 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus bifarius.about: Bombus bifarius, the two-form bumblebee, is a species of eusocial bumblebee of the subgenus Pyrobombus. B.
