bombus bimaculatus.about: The two-spotted bumble bee is a species of social bumble bee found in the eastern half of the United States and the adjacent south-eastern part of Canada.

bombus borealis.name: Northern Amber Bumble Bee
bombus borealis.desc: Northern Amber Bumble Bee (Bombus borealis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus borealis.about: Bombus borealis is a species of bumblebee known commonly as the northern amber bumblebee.

bombus centralis.name: Central Bumble Bee
bombus centralis.desc: Central Bumble Bee (Bombus centralis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus centralis.about: Bombus centralis, the central bumblebee, is a species of bumble bee found in parts of Canada and the western United States. The species was first described by Ezra Townsend Cresson in 1864.

bombus citrinus.name: Lemon Cuckoo Bumble Bee
bombus citrinus.desc: Lemon Cuckoo Bumble Bee (Bombus citrinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus citrinus.about: Bombus citrinus is a species of bumblebee known commonly as the lemon cuckoo bumblebee due to its lemon-yellow color. It is native to eastern North America.

bombus crotchii.name: Crotch Bumble Bee
bombus crotchii.desc: Crotch Bumble Bee (Bombus crotchii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus crotchii.about: Bombus crotchii, commonly called Crotch's bumble bee or the Golden State bumble bee, is a species of bumblebee named after the entomologist George Robert Crotch.

bombus fervidus.name: Yellow Bumble Bee
bombus fervidus.desc: Yellow Bumble Bee (Bombus fervidus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus fervidus.about: Bombus fervidus, the golden northern bumble bee or yellow bumblebee, is a species of bumblebee native to North America. It has a yellow-colored abdomen and thorax.

bombus festivus.name: Festive bumble bee
bombus festivus.desc: A bumble bee recorded often in the area. It collects nectar and pollen from mountain flowers.
bombus festivus.about: A bumblebee is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.

bombus flavifrons.name: Yellow Head Bumble Bee
bombus flavifrons.desc: Yellow Head Bumble Bee (Bombus flavifrons): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus flavifrons.about: Bombus flavifrons, the yellow-fronted bumble bee or yellowhead bumblebee, is a species of bumblebee.

bombus fraternus.name: Southern Plains Bumble Bee
bombus fraternus.desc: Southern Plains Bumble Bee (Bombus fraternus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus fraternus.about: Bombus fraternus is an endangered species of bumblebee known commonly as the Southern Plains bumblebee. It is native to the United States east of the Rocky Mountains.

bombus frigidus.name: Frigid Bumble Bee
bombus frigidus.desc: Frigid Bumble Bee (Bombus frigidus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus frigidus.about: Bombus frigidus, the frigid bumblebee, is a rare species of bumblebee largely found in Canada and parts of the United States.

bombus griseocollis.name: Brown-belted Bumble Bee
bombus griseocollis.desc: Brown-belted Bumble Bee (Bombus griseocollis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus griseocollis.about: Bombus griseocollis is a species of bumblebee known commonly as the brown-belted bumblebee.

bombus huntii.name: Hunt Bumble Bee
bombus huntii.desc: A bumble bee that gathers nectar and pollen from mountain wildflowers, and is a pollinator.

bombus impatiens.name: Common Eastern Bumble Bee
bombus impatiens.desc: Common Eastern Bumble Bee (Bombus impatiens): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus impatiens.about: Bombus impatiens, the common eastern bumblebee, is the most commonly encountered bumblebee across much of eastern North America.

bombus melanopygus.name: Black Tail Bumble Bee
bombus melanopygus.desc: Black Tail Bumble Bee (Bombus melanopygus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus melanopygus.about: Bombus melanopygus, the black-tailed bumble bee, black tail bumble bee or orange-rumped bumblebee, is a species of bumblebee native to western North America.

bombus mixtus.name: Fuzzy-horned Bumble Bee
bombus mixtus.desc: Fuzzy-horned Bumble Bee (Bombus mixtus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus mixtus.about: Bombus mixtus is a species of bumblebee. It is native to western North America, where it occurs in western Canada and the United States.

bombus morrisoni.name: Morrison Bumblebee
bombus morrisoni.desc: Morrison Bumblebee (Bombus morrisoni): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus nevadensis.name: Nevada Bumble Bee
bombus nevadensis.desc: Nevada Bumble Bee (Bombus nevadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus nevadensis.about: Bombus nevadensis, the Nevada bumblebee, is a species of bumblebee.

bombus occidentalis.name: Western Bumble Bee
bombus occidentalis.desc: Western Bumble Bee (Bombus occidentalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus occidentalis.about: Bombus occidentalis, the western bumble bee, is one of around 30 bumble bee species present in the western United States and western Canada.

bombus pascuorum.name: Common carder bee
bombus pascuorum.desc: A bumblebee that feeds on nectar and pollen from many flowers, including bird's-foot-trefoil and devil's-bit scabious.
bombus pascuorum.about: Bombus pascuorum, the common carder bee, is a species of bumblebee present in most of Europe in a wide variety of habitats such as meadows, pastures, waste ground, ditches and embankments, roads, and…

bombus pensylvanicus.name: Bumble bee
bombus pensylvanicus.desc: Bumble bee (Bombus pensylvanicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus pensylvanicus.about: Bombus pensylvanicus, the American bumblebee, is a threatened species of bumblebee native to North America.

bombus perplexus.name: Confusing Bumble Bee
bombus perplexus.desc: Confusing Bumble Bee (Bombus perplexus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus rufocinctus.name: Red-belted bumble bee
bombus rufocinctus.desc: Red-belted bumble bee (Bombus rufocinctus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 53 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus rufocinctus.about: Bombus rufocinctus is a species of bumblebee known commonly as the "red-belted bumblebee".

bombus sandersoni.name: Sanderson Bumble Bee
bombus sandersoni.desc: Sanderson Bumble Bee (Bombus sandersoni): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus sandersoni.about: Bombus sandersoni is a species of bumblebee known commonly as the Sanderson bumblebee. It is native to North America, where it occurs across Canada and in the eastern United States.

bombus sonorus.name: Sonoran Bumble Bee
bombus sonorus.desc: Sonoran Bumble Bee (Bombus sonorus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 115 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus sylvicola.name: Forest Bumble Bee
bombus sylvicola.desc: Forest Bumble Bee (Bombus sylvicola): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus sylvicola.about: Bombus sylvicola is a species of bumblebee native to North America. It occurs throughout most of Canada, its distribution extending into Alaska and the western contiguous United States.

bombus ternarius.name: Tri-colored Bumble Bee
bombus ternarius.desc: Tri-colored bumble bee (Bombus ternarius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus ternarius.about: Bombus ternarius, commonly known as the orange-belted bumblebee or tricolored bumblebee, is a yellow, orange and black bumblebee.

bombus terricola.name: Yellow-banded bumble bee
bombus terricola.desc: Collects nectar and pollen from forest and meadow flowers such as raspberry, fireweed and yarrow.
bombus terricola.about: Bombus terricola, the yellow-banded bumble bee, is a species of bee in the genus Bombus. It is native to southern Canada and the east and midwest of the United States.

bombus vagans.name: Half-black Bumble Bee
bombus vagans.desc: Half-black Bumble Bee (Bombus vagans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
bombus vagans.about: The half-black bumblebee is a small bumblebee with a wide distribution in North America, its range extending from Ontario to Nova Scotia and southward to Georgia.

bombus vancouverensis.name: Vancouver Bumble Bee
bombus vancouverensis.desc: Vancouver Bumble Bee (Bombus vancouverensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

bombus vosnesenskii.name: Vosnesensky Bumble Bee
bombus vosnesenskii.desc: A bumble bee recorded often on the islands; it feeds on nectar and pollen of scrub flowers.
bombus vosnesenskii.about: Bombus vosnesenskii, the yellow-faced bumblebee, is a species of bumblebee native to the west coast of North America, where it is distributed from British Columbia to Baja California.

bombycilla cedrorum.name: Cedar Waxwing
bombycilla cedrorum.desc: Cedar Waxwing (Bombycilla cedrorum): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
bombycilla cedrorum.about: The cedar waxwing is a member of the family Bombycillidae or waxwing family of passerine birds. It is a medium-sized bird that is mainly brown, gray, and yellow.

bonasa umbellus.name: Ruffed Grouse
bonasa umbellus.desc: Ruffed Grouse (Bonasa umbellus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

borassus flabellifer.name: Lontar palm
borassus flabellifer.desc: The palm that gives the dry savanna its scattered skyline. Its fallen fruit feed ground-dwelling animals.
borassus flabellifer.about: Borassus flabellifer, also known as palmyra palm, is a fan palm native to tropical and sub-tropical regions of South Asia and Southeast Asia.

boreal forest soil.name: Boreal forest soil
boreal forest soil.desc: Mostly acidic, thin soils under pine and spruce; the park also has herb-rich patches on more nutrient-rich ground.

boreogadus saida.name: Arctic cod
boreogadus saida.desc: A small fish that links copepods to seals, whales and seabirds.
boreogadus saida.about: Arctogadus glacialis, known also with ambiguous common names Arctic cod and polar cod, is an Arctic species of fish in the cod family Gadidae, related to the true cod (genus Gadus).

borrichia frutescens.name: Bushy seaoxeye
borrichia frutescens.desc: Bushy seaoxeye (Borrichia frutescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.
borrichia frutescens.about: Borrichia frutescens is a North American species of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae known by the common names sea oxeye, sea oxeye daisy, bushy seaside tansy, and sea-marigold.

bos gaurus.name: Gaur (seladang)
bos gaurus.desc: Massive wild ox of Peninsular Malaysia that eats grasses and browse and is a main prey of the Malayan tiger.
bos gaurus.about: The gaur, also known as the Indian bison, is a large bovine native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, and has been listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List since 1986.

bos grunniens.name: Yak
bos grunniens.desc: Grazing livestock herded in the high valleys, which overlap heavily with wild herbivores for pasture.
bos grunniens.about: The yak is a species of long-haired domesticated Asian cattle found throughout the Himalayan region, the Tibetan Plateau, Tajikistan, the Pamir Mountains, and as far north as Mongolia and Siberia.

bos javanicus.name: Banteng
bos javanicus.desc: Wild cattle that compete with rhinos for feeding grounds in the park. Recorded prey of leopards and dholes.
bos javanicus.about: The banteng, also known as the tembadau, is a species of wild bovine found in Southeast Asia, with domestic-wild hybrids present in parts of Northern Australia.

bos taurus.name: Cow
bos taurus.desc: Dark, semi-wild cattle that roam the marshes under the care of gardians and supply the bulls for the local bull-running tradition.
bos taurus.about: Cattle are large, domesticated, bovid ungulates widely kept as livestock. They are prominent modern members of the subfamily Bovinae and the most widespread species of the genus Bos.

boselaphus tragocamelus.name: Nilgai
boselaphus tragocamelus.desc: Asia's largest antelope. Records show tigers, leopards and striped hyenas feeding on it.
boselaphus tragocamelus.about: The nilgai (, literally meaning "blue cow") is the largest antelope in Asia. It is ubiquitous across the northern Indian subcontinent.

boswellia elongata.name: Socotra frankincense
boswellia elongata.desc: A resin tree found only on Socotra, growing in dry forest and shrubland. It is listed as Endangered.
boswellia elongata.about: Boswellia elongata is a species of plant in the Burseraceae family. It is endemic to Socotra.

bothriochloa ischaemum.name: Yellow Bluestem
bothriochloa ischaemum.desc: Yellow Bluestem (Bothriochloa ischaemum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

bothrops asper.name: Terciopelo
bothrops asper.desc: A large pit viper that ambushes rodents and lizards on the forest floor.
bothrops asper.about: The terciopelo is a species of pit viper found from north-east Mexico to northern South America.

bothrops atrox.name: Fer-de-lance
bothrops atrox.desc: A venomous pit viper of lowland forest. GloBI records it eating the lizard Kentropyx calcarata.
bothrops atrox.about: Bothrops atrox — also known as the common lancehead, fer-de-lance, barba amarilla, and mapepire balsain — is a highly venomous pit viper species found in the tropical lowlands of northern South…

bothrops jararaca.name: Jararaca
bothrops jararaca.desc: A venomous pit viper of the Atlantic Forest, ambushing small mammals and frogs. It is the most recorded snake in the area.
bothrops jararaca.about: Bothrops jararaca—known as the jararaca or yarara—is a highly venomous pit viper species endemic to South America in southern Brazil, Paraguay, and northern Argentina.

botrychium matricariifolium.name: Matricary Grapefern
botrychium matricariifolium.desc: Matricary Grapefern (Botrychium matricariifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
botrychium matricariifolium.about: Botrychium matricariifolium (orth.var. B. matricariaefolium) is a species of fern in the Ophioglossaceae family.

botrychium michiganense.name: Michigan moonwort
botrychium michiganense.desc: Michigan moonwort (Botrychium michiganense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

bottom-water oxygen.name: Bottom-water oxygen
bottom-water oxygen.desc: In summer the layered water traps oxygen-poor water near the bottom, where dissolved oxygen can drop to near zero.

bourreria succulenta.name: Pigeon berry
bourreria succulenta.desc: A coastal scrub shrub with fruit. GloBI records show white-crowned pigeons eating its fruit.
bourreria succulenta.about: Bourreria succulenta is a species of flowering plant in the family Ehretiaceae.

bouteloua.name: Desert grasses
bouteloua.desc: Grama grasses of the grasslands on the park's igneous and limestone soils and along the river. Their seeds and leaves feed rodents, doves, rabbits and deer.
bouteloua.about: Bouteloua gracilis, the blue grama, is a long-lived, warm-season (C4) perennial grass, native to North America.

bouteloua curtipendula.name: Tall grama grass
bouteloua curtipendula.desc: Tall grama grass (Bouteloua curtipendula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

bouteloua eriopoda.name: Woolly foot grama
bouteloua eriopoda.desc: Woolly foot grama (Bouteloua eriopoda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 133 times near the park in GBIF.
bouteloua eriopoda.about: Bouteloua eriopoda, commonly known as black grama, is a perennial prairie grass that is native to the Southwestern United States.

bouteloua gracilis.name: Blue grama
bouteloua gracilis.desc: A short prairie grass that prairie dogs eat in spring and summer.
bouteloua gracilis.about: Bouteloua gracilis, the blue grama, is a long-lived, warm-season (C4) perennial grass, native to North America.

brachyteles arachnoides.name: Southern muriqui
brachyteles arachnoides.desc: The largest primate in the Americas, eating mainly fruit plus leaves and flowers. Wikipedia says it has a major role in seed dispersal.
brachyteles arachnoides.about: The southern muriqui is a muriqui (woolly spider monkey) species endemic to Brazil.

brachyura.name: Crabs
brachyura.desc: Crabs of mudflats and mangroves feed on algae, leaf litter and dead matter and are prey for waders, fish and herons.
brachyura.about: Crabs are decapod crustaceans, either the Brachyura (the "true crabs") or various groups within the closely related Anomura (hermit crabs, porcelain crabs etc), characterised by having a heavily…

brackish coastal water.name: Brackish coastal water
brackish coastal water.desc: Salty water along the southern coast and lagoons supports mangroves, which tolerate salt.

brackish lagoon water.name: Brackish lagoon water
brackish lagoon water.desc: A shallow, low-salinity lagoon cut off from the Adriatic by a sand strip, rich in algae and dense aquatic plants.

bradypus variegatus.name: Brown-throated sloth
bradypus variegatus.desc: Moves slowly through the canopy browsing leaves, and comes down about once a week.
bradypus variegatus.about: The brown-throated sloth is a species of three-toed sloth found in the Neotropical realm of Central and South America.

brahmaputra floods.name: Brahmaputra floods
brahmaputra floods.desc: Floods can cover most of the park for days, drive animals to higher ground and leave fresh silt and new grass behind.

braided channels & sandbars.name: Braided channels & sandbars
braided channels & sandbars.desc: The broad, shallow, braided river with shifting sandbars is the open roosting habitat cranes use at night.

branta bernicla.name: Brant goose
branta bernicla.desc: A small sea goose whose winter diet centres on eelgrass, with sea lettuce and marsh plants as alternatives.
branta bernicla.about: The brant or brent goose is a small goose in the genus Branta. There are three subspecies, all of which winter along temperate-zone sea-coasts and breed on the high-Arctic tundra.

branta canadensis.name: Canada goose
branta canadensis.desc: Canada goose (Branta canadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 145 times near the park in GBIF.
branta canadensis.about: The Canada goose is a large species of goose with a black head and neck, white cheeks, white under its chin, and a brown body.

branta leucopsis.name: Barnacle goose
branta leucopsis.desc: Breeds in Svalbard and winters on the Solway Firth. Goslings leap from cliff nests and often fall to Arctic foxes.
branta leucopsis.about: The barnacle goose is a species of goose that belongs to the genus Branta of black geese, which contains species with extensive black in the plumage, distinguishing them from the grey Anser species.

branta sandvicensis.name: Nēnē (Hawaiian goose)
branta sandvicensis.desc: An endangered goose that eats leaves, seeds and fruit of grasses and shrubs. It died out in the park and was reintroduced in 1962.
branta sandvicensis.about: The nene, also known as the nēnē or the Hawaiian goose, is a species of bird endemic to the Hawaiian Islands.

brasenia schreberi.name: Schreber's Watershield
brasenia schreberi.desc: Schreber's Watershield (Brasenia schreberi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

brephidium exilis.name: Western pygmy blue butterfly
brephidium exilis.desc: Western pygmy blue butterfly (Brephidium exilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
brephidium exilis.about: The western pygmy blue is one of the smallest butterflies in the world and the smallest in North America.

brevoortia patronus.name: Gulf menhaden
brevoortia patronus.desc: A filter feeder. Wikipedia says juveniles eat mainly phytoplankton and adults mainly zooplankton. A major forage fish for the Gulf.
brevoortia patronus.about: The Gulf menhaden is a small marine filter-feeding fish belonging to the family Alosidae.

brevoortia tyrannus.name: Atlantic menhaden
brevoortia tyrannus.desc: A schooling filter feeder that strains plankton from the water. Striped bass, bluefish, ospreys, eagles and dolphins all eat it.
brevoortia tyrannus.about: The Atlantic menhaden is a North American species of fish in the herring family, Alosidae.

brickellia californica.name: California brickellbush
brickellia californica.desc: California brickellbush (Brickellia californica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

brickellia microphylla.name: Littleleaf brickellbush
brickellia microphylla.desc: Littleleaf brickellbush (Brickellia microphylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

brickellia oblongifolia.name: Mojave brickellbush
brickellia oblongifolia.desc: Mojave brickellbush (Brickellia oblongifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

bridelia ferruginea.name: Bridelia
bridelia ferruginea.desc: A common savanna woodland tree whose fruit and leaves are eaten by duikers, baboons, warthogs and kob in GloBI records.
bridelia ferruginea.about: Bridelia is a genus of plants in the family Phyllanthaceae first described as a genus in 1806.

bromeliaceae.name: Bromeliads
bromeliaceae.desc: Cloud-forest plants growing on trees and slopes. Their leaf hearts are a main food of the spectacled bear.
bromeliaceae.about: Bromeliaceae, members of which are called bromeliads (), is a family of monocot flowering plants of about 80 genera and 3700 known species, native mainly to the tropical Americas, with several…

bromus inermis.name: Hungarian Brome
bromus inermis.desc: Hungarian Brome (Bromus inermis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
bromus inermis.about: Bromus inermis is a species of the true grass family (Poaceae). This rhizomatous grass is native to Europe and considered invasive in North America.

bromus rubens.name: Foxtail Brome
bromus rubens.desc: Foxtail Brome (Bromus rubens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

bronchocela cristatella.name: Green crested lizard
bronchocela cristatella.desc: A slender tree lizard that hunts insects among the foliage and is in turn eaten by birds and snakes.
bronchocela cristatella.about: Bronchocela cristatella, also known as the green crested lizard, is a species of agamid lizard endemic to Southeast Asia.

brosimum alicastrum.name: Ramon (breadnut)
brosimum alicastrum.desc: One of the dominant trees of the Maya forest. Its fruits and seeds feed many animals, and birds and bats help spread the seeds.
brosimum alicastrum.about: Brosimum alicastrum, commonly known as ojoxitli, ramón (also ramón de vaca), breadnut, Maya nut and many others, is a tree species in the family Moraceae of flowering plants, whose other genera…

brosimum lactescens.name: Milk tree
brosimum lactescens.desc: A lowland forest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for many birds and monkeys here, from macaws to woolly and howler monkeys.
brosimum lactescens.about: Brosimum is a genus of plants in the family Moraceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas. The breadnut (B. alicastrum) was used by the Maya civilisation for its edible nut.

broussonetia papyrifera.name: Wauke
broussonetia papyrifera.desc: Wauke (Broussonetia papyrifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
broussonetia papyrifera.about: The paper mulberry is a species of flowering tree in the family Moraceae.

brunnichia ovata.name: American buckwheat vine
brunnichia ovata.desc: American buckwheat vine (Brunnichia ovata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
brunnichia ovata.about: Brunnichia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Polygonaceae.

bryophyta.name: Mosses
bryophyta.desc: Mosses, with algae and bacteria, give tufa a surface to build on. They help trigger the limestone deposits that form the barriers.
bryophyta.about: Bryophytes () are a group of land plants (embryophytes), sometimes treated as a taxonomic division referred to as Bryophyta sensu lato, that contains three groups of non-vascular land plants: the…

bryophyta, polypodiopsida.name: Mosses and ferns
bryophyta, polypodiopsida.desc: Mosses coat trunks and branches and ferns carpet the floor in the damp understory.
bryophyta, polypodiopsida.about: Mosses are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division Bryophyta (, ) sensu stricto.

bubalus arnee.name: Wild water buffalo
bubalus arnee.desc: Grazes grasses and sedges in wet grasslands and swamps. Adults are preyed on by tigers.
bubalus arnee.about: The wild water buffalo, also called Asian buffalo, Asiatic buffalo and wild buffalo, is a large bovine native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. It was first described in 1792.

bubalus bubalis.name: Feral water buffalo
bubalus bubalis.desc: Introduced grazer that damaged floodplains and wetlands before most were removed. Carcasses feed kites and crows, and crocodiles also take buffalo.
bubalus bubalis.about: The water buffalo, also called domestic water buffalo, Asian water buffalo, and Asiatic water buffalo, is a large domesticated bovine originating in South and Southeast Asia descended from the wild…

bubo ascalaphus.name: Pharaoh eagle-owl
bubo ascalaphus.desc: A large nocturnal owl that hunts small desert mammals and has been recorded taking fennec fox pups.
bubo ascalaphus.about: The Pharaoh eagle-owl is a Middle Eastern and North African species of owl in the family Strigidae.

bubo blakistoni.name: Blakiston's fish owl
bubo blakistoni.desc: A very large owl of old riverside forest that hunts fish, including salmon, plus frogs and small mammals. It needs rivers that stay partly unfrozen in winter.
bubo blakistoni.about: Blakiston's fish owl, the largest living species of owl, is a fish owl, a sub-group of eagle-owls that specialize in hunting in riparian areas. It is native to China, Japan, and the Russian Far East.

bubo scandiacus.name: Snowy owl
bubo scandiacus.desc: Hunts lemmings by day and lays more eggs in years when lemmings are plentiful.
bubo scandiacus.about: The snowy owl, also known as the polar owl, the white owl and the Arctic owl, is a large, white owl of the true owl family.

bubo virginianus.name: Great horned owl
bubo virginianus.desc: Named among the reserve's wildlife. A night hunter of small mammals such as mice.
bubo virginianus.about: The great horned owl, also known as the tiger owl or the hoot owl, is a large owl native to the Americas.

buceros bicornis.name: Great hornbill
buceros bicornis.desc: Eats mostly fruit, especially figs, and gets its water from fruit. Also catches small animals. A seed disperser for many forest trees.
buceros bicornis.about: The great hornbill, also known as the concave-casqued hornbill, great Indian hornbill or great pied hornbill, is one of the larger members of the hornbill family.

buceros rhinoceros.name: Rhinoceros hornbill
buceros rhinoceros.desc: A large forest hornbill whose diet is mostly fruit, plus insects, small reptiles and rodents. GloBI records show it eating figs.
buceros rhinoceros.about: The rhinoceros hornbill is a large species of forest hornbill. In captivity, it can live for up to 35 years.

buchnera americana.name: American bluehearts
buchnera americana.desc: American bluehearts (Buchnera americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.
buchnera americana.about: Buchnera americana, commonly known as American bluehearts or bupleurum, is a locally endangered herbaceous perennial plant of the broomrape family Orobanchaceae.

budorcas taxicolor.name: Sichuan takin
budorcas taxicolor.desc: A heavy goat-antelope that browses leaves and grasses and eats bamboo shoots and flowers. It retreats into thick bamboo when alarmed.
budorcas taxicolor.about: The takin; is a large species of ungulate of the subfamily Caprinae found in the eastern Himalayas. It includes three subspecies, the Mishmi takin (B. t.

bufo bufo.name: Common toad
bufo bufo.desc: An amphibian that spends most of the year on land eating beetles and other invertebrates.
bufo bufo.about: The common toad, also known as European toad or simply the toad in Anglophone parts of Europe, is a toad found throughout most of Europe, western North Asia and a small part of Northwest Africa.

bulbostylis capillaris.name: Densetuft Hairsedge
bulbostylis capillaris.desc: Densetuft Hairsedge (Bulbostylis capillaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
bulbostylis capillaris.about: Bulbostylis capillaris is a species of sedge known by the common names densetuft hairsedge and threadleaf beakseed.

burkea africana.name: Burkea
burkea africana.desc: One of the characteristic trees of the park woodland, and a species elephants injure often.
burkea africana.about: Burkea africana, the wild syringa (Bambara: siri), is a deciduous, medium-sized, spreading, flat-topped tree which grows in the woodlands and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa.

burnsius communis.name: Common Checkered Skipper
burnsius communis.desc: Common Checkered Skipper (Burnsius communis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
burnsius communis.about: Burnsius communis, the common checkered-skipper, formerly known as Pyrgus communis, is a species of butterfly in the family Hesperiidae.

bursera simaruba.name: Gumbo-limbo
bursera simaruba.desc: Gumbo-limbo is a typical tree of the dry to moist forest that covers the island hills. Deer and iguanas browse such foliage.
bursera simaruba.about: Bursera simaruba, the gumbo-limbo, copperwood, tourist tree, turpentine tree, almácigo, or West Indian birch, is a tree species in the family Burseraceae.

buteo augur.name: Augur buzzard
buteo augur.desc: A raptor commonly recorded on the plateau. It mainly eats small ground mammals such as rats and mole-rats, and reptiles.
buteo augur.about: The augur buzzard is a fairly large African bird of prey. This species is distinct in typical adult plumage for its blackish back, whitish underside and orange-red tail, while juvenile augur buzzards…

buteo buteo.name: Common buzzard
buteo buteo.desc: A raptor of forest edges and meadows that hunts rodents and other small animals.
buteo buteo.about: The common buzzard is a medium-sized bird of prey with a large range. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.

buteo galapagoensis.name: Galápagos hawk
buteo galapagoensis.desc: The islands' top land predator. It eats insects, lizards, rodents, small birds and young iguanas and tortoises, and scavenges carrion.
buteo galapagoensis.about: The Galápagos hawk is a large hawk endemic to most of the Galápagos Islands.

buteo jamaicensis.name: Red-tailed hawk
buteo jamaicensis.desc: Red-tailed Hawk (Buteo jamaicensis): a top predator in this web. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
buteo jamaicensis.about: The red-tailed hawk is a bird of prey and one of the most common hawks in North America. In the United States, it is one of three species colloquially known as the "chickenhawk".

buteo japonicus.name: Eastern buzzard
buteo japonicus.desc: Bird of prey, the top flying predator on the islands, taking lizards, rodents and seabirds.
buteo japonicus.about: The eastern buzzard or Japanese buzzard is a medium to large bird of prey that is sometimes considered a subspecies of the widespread common buzzard.

buteo lineatus.name: Red-shouldered/Broad-winged Hawk
buteo lineatus.desc: Red-shouldered/Broad-winged Hawk (Buteo lineatus): a top predator in this web. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

buteo oreophilus.name: Mountain buzzard
buteo oreophilus.desc: A raptor of montane forest, listed for Kibira; it hunts small mammals, reptiles and insects from perches.
buteo oreophilus.about: The mountain buzzard is a bird of prey that lives in montane forests in East Africa, it and the forest buzzard of southern Africa were, until recently, considered to be a single species.

buteo platypterus.name: Broad-winged Hawk
buteo platypterus.desc: Broad-winged Hawk (Buteo platypterus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 62 times near the park in GBIF.
buteo platypterus.about: The broad-winged hawk is a medium-sized hawk of the genus Buteo.

buteo platypterus brunnescens.name: Puerto Rican broad-winged hawk
buteo platypterus brunnescens.desc: A rare forest hawk found in El Yunque's tabonuco forest. Raptors including hawks are listed among natural predators of the parrot.
buteo platypterus brunnescens.about: The Puerto Rican broad-winged hawk is an endangered subspecies of the broad-winged hawk (B. platypterus). It is a small hawk that occurs in Puerto Rico, inhabiting the Toro Negro State Forest.

buteo regalis.name: Ferruginous Hawk
buteo regalis.desc: Ferruginous Hawk (Buteo regalis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

buteo ridgwayi.name: Ridgway's hawk
buteo ridgwayi.desc: A critically endangered Hispaniolan raptor that takes mostly reptiles, plus birds, bats, rodents and frogs. The park holds one of its few surviving wild populations.
buteo ridgwayi.about: Ridgway's hawk is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae endemic to the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean.

buteo rufinus.name: Long-legged buzzard
buteo rufinus.desc: A steppe buzzard that takes mainly rodents and ground squirrels, plus many reptiles, birds and insects.
buteo rufinus.about: The long-legged buzzard is a bird of prey found widely in several parts of Eurasia and in North Africa.

buteo rufofuscus.name: Jackal buzzard
buteo rufofuscus.desc: A mountain raptor that hunts small mammals, snakes and lizards, and eats carrion outside the breeding season.
buteo rufofuscus.about: The jackal buzzard is a fairly large African bird of prey. The taxonomy of this species has caused some confusion in the past and it almost certainly belongs in a species complex with other African…

buteo socotraensis.name: Socotra buzzard
buteo socotraensis.desc: An island-only buzzard that nests on cliffs and hunts mainly reptiles and large invertebrates.
buteo socotraensis.about: The Socotra buzzard is a medium to large bird of prey that is sometimes considered a subspecies of the widespread common buzzard. As its name implies, it is native to the island of Socotra, Yemen.

buteo solitarius.name: ʻIo (Hawaiian hawk)
buteo solitarius.desc: Endemic hawk that breeds only on the Big Island, in ʻōhiʻa forest. It now eats rats, lizards, game birds and insects, hunting mostly from a perch.
buteo solitarius.about: The Hawaiian hawk or ʻio is a raptor in the genus Buteo endemic to Hawaiʻi, currently restricted to the Big Island.

buteo swainsoni.name: Swainson's Hawk
buteo swainsoni.desc: Swainson's Hawk (Buteo swainsoni): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,608 times near the park in GBIF.
buteo swainsoni.about: Swainson's hawk is a large bird species in the Accipitriformes order. This species was named after William Swainson, a British naturalist.

buteogallus meridionalis.name: Savanna hawk
buteogallus meridionalis.desc: A hawk of open country that hunts reptiles, small mammals and other prey from perches.
buteogallus meridionalis.about: The savanna hawk is a large raptor found in open savanna and swamp edges. It was formerly placed in the genus Heterospizias.

butomus umbellatus.name: Flowering-rush
butomus umbellatus.desc: Flowering-rush (Butomus umbellatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.
butomus umbellatus.about: Butomus umbellatus is a Eurasian plant species in the family Butomaceae. It is the only species in the family.

bycanistes fistulator.name: Piping hornbill
bycanistes fistulator.desc: A noisy canopy hornbill, among the best-recorded birds around the park, that mainly eats forest fruit.
bycanistes fistulator.about: The piping hornbill is a bird in the hornbill family. This black-and-white species is found in humid forest and second growth in Central and West Africa, ranging from Senegal east to Uganda and south…

caenurgia chloropha.name: Vetch Looper Moth
caenurgia chloropha.desc: Vetch Looper Moth (Caenurgia chloropha): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
caenurgia chloropha.about: Caenurgia chloropha, the vetch looper moth, is a moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Jacob Hübner in 1818.

caesio.name: Fusiliers
caesio.desc: Schooling fish that feed on zooplankton in the water above the reef, and are prey for larger predators.
caesio.about: Lutjaninae is a subfamily of marine ray-finned fishes, one of four subfamilies classified within the family Lutjanidae, the snappers.

caiman crocodilus.name: Spectacled caiman
caiman crocodilus.desc: Caiman of calm waters in Trinidad and Tobago; adults take fish, crabs and snails, birds and mammals.
caiman crocodilus.about: The spectacled caiman, also known as the white caiman, common caiman, and speckled caiman, is a crocodilian in the family Alligatoridae.

caiman yacare.name: Yacare caiman
caiman yacare.desc: A semi-aquatic reptile of lakes and wetlands. It eats mainly snails and fish, sometimes larger prey such as capybara, and is itself taken by jaguars.
caiman yacare.about: The yacare caiman, also known commonly as the jacare caiman, Paraguayan caiman, piranha caiman, red caiman, and southern spectacled caiman, is a species of caiman, a crocodilian in the family…

cakile edentula.name: American searocket
cakile edentula.desc: American searocket (Cakile edentula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
cakile edentula.about: Cakile edentula, the American searocket, is a species of the flowering Cakile plant. This plant is native to North America.

cakile maritima.name: Sea rocket
cakile maritima.desc: A salt-tolerant pioneer plant of beaches and foredunes, recorded near Cabo Polonio.
cakile maritima.about: Cakile maritima, sea rocket or European searocket (North America), is a common plant in the mustard family Brassicaceae.

calamagrostis canadensis.name: Bluejoint reedgrass
calamagrostis canadensis.desc: A tall moist-ground grass recorded in the park area; a grazing food for bison.
calamagrostis canadensis.about: Calamagrostis canadensis is a species of grass, having three or more varieties, in the family Poaceae.

calamus.name: Rattan palms
calamus.desc: Climbing palms of the forest understory. Wikipedia lists rattan among the park plants that are overharvested.
calamus.about: Calamus is a genus of flowering plants in the palm family Arecaceae, and is one of several genera known as rattan palms.

calanoides and relatives.name: Copepods
calanoides and relatives.desc: Small crustacean grazers of phytoplankton. Krill also eat them.
calanoides and relatives.about: Copepods are a group of small crustaceans found in nearly every freshwater and saltwater habitat.

calanus finmarchicus.name: Copepods
calanus finmarchicus.desc: Small crustaceans that graze phytoplankton in the Gulf of Maine and are food for herring.
calanus finmarchicus.about: Calanus finmarchicus is a species of copepod and a component of the zooplankton, which is found in enormous amounts in the northern Atlantic Ocean.

calanus glacialis.name: Arctic copepods
calanus glacialis.desc: Rich in fat, they link the algae bloom to fish, seabirds and whales.
calanus glacialis.about: Calanus glacialis is an Arctic copepod found in the north-western Atlantic Ocean, adjoining waters, and the northwestern Pacific and its nearby waters.

calcarius lapponicus.name: Lapland longspur
calcarius lapponicus.desc: A tundra songbird that eats seeds and plants and, in summer, insects. A very commonly recorded bird here.
calcarius lapponicus.about: The Lapland longspur, also known as the Lapland bunting, is a passerine bird in the longspur family Calcariidae.

calidris alpina.name: Dunlin
calidris alpina.desc: Small wintering shorebird that probes mudflats in flocks for molluscs, worms and crustaceans.
calidris alpina.about: The dunlin is a small wader in the genus Calidris. The English name is a dialect form of "dunling", first recorded in 1531–1532.

calidris canutus.name: Red knot
calidris canutus.desc: Probes for buried shellfish and swallows them whole. It breeds on Arctic tundra and stops over on coastal mudflats such as the Wadden Sea.
calidris canutus.about: The red knot or just knot is a medium-sized shorebird which breeds in tundra and the Arctic Cordillera in the far north of Canada, Europe, and Russia. It is the type species of the genus Calidris.

calla palustris.name: Bog Arum
calla palustris.desc: Bog Arum (Calla palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

callicarpa americana.name: American beauty-berry
callicarpa americana.desc: A shrub with bright purple berries that birds and mammals eat in autumn.
callicarpa americana.about: Callicarpa americana, commonly called the American beautyberry, is an open-habitat, native shrub of the Southern United States which is often grown as an ornamental in gardens and yards.

calligonum.name: Calligonum shrubs
calligonum.desc: Sand-loving shrubs with thin, nearly leafless stems that grow on dunes of the Karakum.
calligonum.about: Calligonum is a genus of plants in the family Polygonaceae with about 41 species native to Northern Africa, Western, South, and Central Asia, and central China.

callinectes sapidus.name: Blue crab
callinectes sapidus.desc: An omnivore that eats clams, mussels, oysters, worms, small fish and eelgrass, and also scavenges. Striped bass are among its predators.
callinectes sapidus.about: Callinectes sapidus, commonly known as the blue crab, Atlantic blue crab, or, regionally, the Maryland blue crab, is a species of crab native to the waters of the western Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf…

calliopsis andreniformis.name: Eastern Miner Bee
calliopsis andreniformis.desc: Eastern Miner Bee (Calliopsis andreniformis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 167 times near the park in GBIF.
calliopsis andreniformis.about: The eastern miner bee is a species of miner bee in the family Andrenidae. It is found in North America.

calliopsis nebraskensis.name: Nebraska Calliopsis
calliopsis nebraskensis.desc: Nebraska Calliopsis (Calliopsis nebraskensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 57 times near the park in GBIF.

callipepla californica.name: California Quail
callipepla californica.desc: A ground-living bird that feeds on seeds, leaves and berries, and is hunted by hawks, snakes and cats.
callipepla californica.about: The California quail is formally known as and also known as the California valley quail or Valley quail.

callipepla gambelii.name: Gambel's quail
callipepla gambelii.desc: A ground bird that eats seeds, leaves and mesquite beans and is prey for hawks and snakes.
callipepla gambelii.about: Gambel's quail is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family.

callirhoe involucrata.name: Purple poppy-mallow
callirhoe involucrata.desc: Purple poppy-mallow (Callirhoe involucrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
callirhoe involucrata.about: Callirhoe involucrata is a species of flowering plant in the mallow family known by the common names purple poppy-mallow, winecup and buffalo rose.

callophrys affinis.name: Bramble Hairstreak
callophrys affinis.desc: Bramble Hairstreak (Callophrys affinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

callosamia promethea.name: Promethea Silkmoth
callosamia promethea.desc: Promethea Silkmoth (Callosamia promethea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

callosciurus erythraeus.name: Pallas's squirrel
callosciurus erythraeus.desc: A tree squirrel of forests below about 3,000 m that eats seeds, fruit, leaves and flowers, and is regular prey of forest raptors.
callosciurus erythraeus.about: Pallas's squirrel, also known as the red-bellied tree squirrel, is a species of squirrel native to China, Taiwan, India, Bhutan, and Southeast Asia.

callosciurus finlaysonii.name: Finlayson's squirrel
callosciurus finlaysonii.desc: A common tree squirrel. GloBI records it eating jambolan fruit and other fruit.
callosciurus finlaysonii.about: Finlayson's squirrel or the variable squirrel is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae. It is found in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

callosciurus prevostii.name: Prevost's squirrel
callosciurus prevostii.desc: A colourful tree squirrel that eats fruit, seeds and some insects. It is one of the most recorded mammals near the park.
callosciurus prevostii.about: Prevost's squirrel or Asian tri-coloured squirrel is a colourful species of rodent in the family Sciuridae.

callospermophilus lateralis.name: Golden-mantled ground squirrel
callospermophilus lateralis.desc: Golden-mantled ground squirrel (Callospermophilus lateralis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

calluna vulgaris.name: Heather
calluna vulgaris.desc: A low evergreen shrub of mountain heaths, eaten by deer and chamois.
calluna vulgaris.about: Calluna vulgaris, common heather, ling, or simply heather, is the only accepted species in the genus Calluna in the flowering plant family Ericaceae.

calocedrus decurrens.name: Californian Incense-cedar
calocedrus decurrens.desc: Californian Incense-cedar (Calocedrus decurrens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 226 times near the park in GBIF.
calocedrus decurrens.about: Calocedrus decurrens, with the common names incense cedar and California incense cedar, is a species of coniferous tree in the cypress family, Cupressaceae, native to western North America.

calocedrus macrolepis.name: Calocedrus (cypress) forest
calocedrus macrolepis.desc: A stand of these conifers covers about 50 km2 of the park on limestone, and Wikipedia says most of the trees are thought to be 500 to 600 years old.
calocedrus macrolepis.about: Calocedrus macrolepis, commonly known as Chinese incense-cedar; is a species of conifer in the cypress family, Cupressaceae, native to southwest China, northern Vietnam, northern Laos, extreme…

calochortus albus.name: Fairy-lantern
calochortus albus.desc: Fairy-lantern (Calochortus albus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 377 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus gunnisonii.name: Gunnison's mariposa lily
calochortus gunnisonii.desc: Gunnison's mariposa lily (Calochortus gunnisonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
calochortus gunnisonii.about: Calochortus gunnisonii commonly known as Rocky Mountain mariposa or Gunnison mariposa lily is a North American species of flowering plant in the lily family.

calochortus lyallii.name: Lyall's mariposa lily
calochortus lyallii.desc: Lyall's mariposa lily (Calochortus lyallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 90 times near the park in GBIF.
calochortus lyallii.about: Calochortus lyallii, or Lyall's mariposa lily, is a North American species of flowering plant in the lily family.

calochortus macrocarpus.name: Greenband mariposa lily
calochortus macrocarpus.desc: Greenband mariposa lily (Calochortus macrocarpus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
calochortus macrocarpus.about: Calochortus macrocarpus, also known as sagebrush mariposa lily, is a North American species of bulbous perennials in the lily family.

calochortus nuttallii.name: Sego-lily
calochortus nuttallii.desc: Sego-lily (Calochortus nuttallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
calochortus nuttallii.about: Calochortus nuttallii, also known as the sego lily, is a bulbous perennial plant that is endemic to the Western United States. The common name of sego comes from a similar Shoshone word.

calochortus pulchellus.name: Mount Diablo fairy-lantern
calochortus pulchellus.desc: Mount Diablo fairy-lantern (Calochortus pulchellus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 938 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus splendens.name: Splendid mariposa lily
calochortus splendens.desc: Splendid mariposa lily (Calochortus splendens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 458 times near the park in GBIF.

calochortus tolmiei.name: WHITE PUSSY EARS
calochortus tolmiei.desc: WHITE PUSSY EARS (Calochortus tolmiei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.
calochortus tolmiei.about: Calochortus tolmiei is a North American species of flowering plant in the lily family known by the common names Tolmie's star-tulip and pussy ears. It was discovered by and named for Dr.

calochortus venustus.name: Butterfly mariposa lily
calochortus venustus.desc: Butterfly mariposa lily (Calochortus venustus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 890 times near the park in GBIF.

calopogon barbatus.name: Bearded grasspink
calopogon barbatus.desc: Bearded grasspink (Calopogon barbatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 214 times near the park in GBIF.

calopogon tuberosus.name: Tuberous grasspink
calopogon tuberosus.desc: Tuberous grasspink (Calopogon tuberosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.
calopogon tuberosus.about: Calopogon tuberosus, the tuberous grass pink, is an orchid native to eastern North America. It is a perennial forb.

calotes calotes.name: Green forest lizard
calotes calotes.desc: A common agamid lizard of the wet zone that feeds on insects.
calotes calotes.about: Calotes calotes, the common green forest lizard, is an agamid lizard found in the forests of the Western Ghats and the Shevaroy Hills in India, and Sri Lanka.

calotes versicolor.name: Variable agama
calotes versicolor.desc: An insect-eating lizard of forest edges and gardens. Birds and snakes prey on it.
calotes versicolor.about: The oriental garden lizard, also called the eastern garden lizard, Indian garden lizard, common garden lizard, bloodsucker or changeable lizard, is an agamid lizard found widely distributed in…

caltha leptosepala.name: Elkslip marshmarigold
caltha leptosepala.desc: Elkslip marshmarigold (Caltha leptosepala): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.

caltha palustris.name: Marsh-marigold
caltha palustris.desc: Marsh-marigold (Caltha palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

calycopis cecrops.name: Red-banded Hairstreak
calycopis cecrops.desc: Red-banded Hairstreak (Calycopis cecrops): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 149 times near the park in GBIF.

calypso bulbosa.name: Calypso
calypso bulbosa.desc: Calypso (Calypso bulbosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 177 times near the park in GBIF.

calypte anna.name: Anna's Hummingbird
calypte anna.desc: Anna's Hummingbird (Calypte anna): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 114 times near the park in GBIF.

calypte costae.name: Costa's Hummingbird
calypte costae.desc: Costa's Hummingbird (Calypte costae): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.
calypte costae.about: Costa's hummingbird is a species of hummingbird in the family Trochilidae.

calystegia sepium.name: Bearbind
calystegia sepium.desc: Bearbind (Calystegia sepium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

cambaridae and orconectes spp..name: Crayfish
cambaridae and orconectes spp..desc: Scavenging omnivores of stream bottoms. The MDC says crayfish are the main food of Ozark hellbenders and are eaten by smallmouth bass.
cambaridae and orconectes spp..about: Crayfish, crawfish, or crawdads are freshwater crustaceans belonging to the infraorder Astacidea, which also contains lobsters.

camelus dromedarius.name: Dromedary
camelus dromedarius.desc: Domestic camels graze and browse coastal shrubs and mangroves along the Arabian coast; a few records fall in the circle.
camelus dromedarius.about: The dromedary, also known as the dromedary camel, Arabian camel and one-humped camel, is a large camel of the genus Camelus with one hump on its back.

camelus ferus.name: Wild Bactrian camel
camelus ferus.desc: A critically endangered camel of the Gobi that survives on sparse desert plants and can drink salty water.
camelus ferus.about: The wild Bactrian camel or simply the wild camel is an endangered species of camel endemic to Northwest China and southwestern Mongolia.

camissoniopsis cheiranthifolia.name: Beach suncup
camissoniopsis cheiranthifolia.desc: Beach suncup (Camissoniopsis cheiranthifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 80 times near the park in GBIF.

camnula pellucida.name: Clear-winged Grasshopper
camnula pellucida.desc: Clear-winged Grasshopper (Camnula pellucida): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
camnula pellucida.about: Camnula is a genus of band-winged grasshopper in the family Acrididae. It contains one species, Camnula pellucida, the clearwinged grasshopper.

campaea perlata.name: Fringed Looper
campaea perlata.desc: Fringed Looper (Campaea perlata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

campanula rotundifolia.name: Harebell
campanula rotundifolia.desc: Harebell (Campanula rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
campanula rotundifolia.about: Campanula rotundifolia, the harebell or common harebell, Scottish bluebell, or bluebell in Scotland, is a species of flowering plant in the bellflower family Campanulaceae.

campanulastrum americanum.name: American bellflower
campanulastrum americanum.desc: American bellflower (Campanulastrum americanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
campanulastrum americanum.about: Campanula americana, the American bellflower, or tall bellflower, is an herbaceous wildflower and a member of the Campanulaceae family.

campephilus magellanicus.name: Magellanic woodpecker
campephilus magellanicus.desc: A big woodpecker of mature southern beech forest that eats mainly wood-boring grubs and beetles, plus spiders.
campephilus magellanicus.about: The Magellanic woodpecker is a species of large woodpecker found in southern Chile and southwestern Argentina; it is resident within its range.

campsis radicans.name: Trumpet-creeper
campsis radicans.desc: Trumpet-creeper (Campsis radicans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
campsis radicans.about: Campsis radicans, the trumpet vine, yellow trumpet vine, or trumpet creeper, is a species of flowering plant in the trumpet vine family Bignoniaceae, native to eastern North America, and naturalized…

campyloneurum phyllitidis.name: Long Strapfern
campyloneurum phyllitidis.desc: Long Strapfern (Campyloneurum phyllitidis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 62 times near the park in GBIF.

canal freshwater.name: Canal freshwater
canal freshwater.desc: Canals that drain the Everglades send fresh water, sediment and pollutants into the bay and shift its salinity.

canbya aurea.name: Golden pygmypoppy
canbya aurea.desc: Golden pygmypoppy (Canbya aurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
canbya aurea.about: Canbya aurea, common name yellow pygmy-poppy, is a plant species endemic to the relatively cool northern deserts of the western United States.

candoia bibroni.name: Pacific boa
candoia bibroni.desc: A forest snake recorded on Espiritu Santo that eats birds, lizards, rodents and bats; the island has no native land mammal predators.
candoia bibroni.about: Candoia bibroni – commonly known as Bibron's bevel-nosed boa, Bibron's keel-scaled boa, the Pacific tree boa and the Fiji boa – is a species of snake in the subfamily Candoiinae of the family Boidae.

canis adustus.name: Side-striped jackal
canis adustus.desc: An omnivorous canid that takes small prey, fruit and carrion. It is present in the park.
canis adustus.about: The side-striped jackal is a canine native to Central and Southern Africa.

canis aureus.name: Golden jackal
canis aureus.desc: An opportunistic hunter and scavenger, recorded eating deer and wild boar.
canis aureus.about: The golden jackal, also called the common jackal, is a wolf-like canid that is native to Eurasia.

canis dingo.name: Dingo
canis dingo.desc: Top land predator that hunts wallabies, rodents, birds and young buffalo. Dingo predation is a major cause of quoll losses.
canis dingo.about: The dingo is a lineage of dog found in Australia. It is a medium-sized canine that possesses a lean, hardy body adapted for speed, agility, and stamina.

canis familiaris.name: Highland wild dog
canis familiaris.desc: Wild dogs live near the base of Puncak Jaya at roughly 3,900 to 4,200 m. New Guinea wild dogs eat marsupials, rodents, birds and fruit, and are said to steal eagle kills.
canis familiaris.about: The New Guinea singing dog or New Guinea Highland dog is an ancient (basal) lineage of dog native to the New Guinea Highlands, on the island of New Guinea.

canis latrans.name: Coyote
canis latrans.desc: Coyote (Canis latrans): a top predator in this web. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
canis latrans.about: The coyote (/kaɪ(j)oʊt(i)/, KY-(y)oh-t(ee)) is a species of canine also known as the American jackal, prairie wolf, and brush wolf.

canis lupaster.name: African golden wolf
canis lupaster.desc: A generalist canid that eats rodents, hares and carrion. Ethiopian wolves usually win encounters with it, though it is not a rodent specialist.
canis lupaster.about: The African wolf is a canine native to North Africa, West Africa, the Sahel, northern East Africa, and the Horn of Africa. It is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List.

canis lupus.name: Gray wolf
canis lupus.desc: Packs hunt moose, caribou and beaver, mainly taking calves and weak animals, and sometimes hares.
canis lupus.about: The wolf, also known as the grey wolf or gray wolf, is a canine native to Eurasia and North America.

canis lupus arctos.name: Arctic wolf
canis lupus arctos.desc: Follows caribou and muskox herds and hunts lemmings in summer.
canis lupus arctos.about: The Arctic wolf, also known as the white wolf, polar wolf, and the Arctic grey wolf, is a subspecies of grey wolf native to the High Arctic tundra of Canada's Queen Elizabeth Islands, from Melville…

canis lupus chanco.name: Himalayan wolf
canis lupus chanco.desc: Hunts bharal and marmots, and takes livestock where herds overlap its range.
canis lupus chanco.about: The Himalayan wolf is a canine of debated taxonomy. It is distinguished by its genetic markers, with mitochondrial DNA indicating that it is genetically basal to the Holarctic grey wolf, genetically…

canis simensis.name: Ethiopian wolf
canis simensis.desc: Rodent specialist. In Bale it hunts mostly big-headed mole-rats. Bale holds the largest population of this endangered canid.
canis simensis.about: The Ethiopian wolf, also called the red jackal, the Simien jackal or Simien fox, is a canine native to the Ethiopian Highlands, including the Simien Mountains.

cannabis sativa.name: Hemp
cannabis sativa.desc: Hemp (Cannabis sativa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
cannabis sativa.about: Cannabis sativa is an annual herbaceous flowering plant. The species was first classified by Carl Linnaeus in 1753.

canotia holacantha.name: Crucifixion thorn
canotia holacantha.desc: Crucifixion thorn (Canotia holacantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

canyon soil and sediment.name: Canyon soil and sediment
canyon soil and sediment.desc: Thin sandy soils and river-borne sediment give plants a place to root across the canyon floor and mesas.

canyon springs.name: Canyon springs
canyon springs.desc: The range is mostly limestone with little surface water, so seeps, springs and McKittrick Creek sustain the canyon trees.

cap blanc upwelling.name: Cap Blanc upwelling
cap blanc upwelling.desc: Permanent upwelling at Cap Blanc brings nutrients that help make these waters among the richest fishing grounds in the region.

capra aegagrus.name: Bezoar ibex
capra aegagrus.desc: A wild goat of rocky mountain slopes that feeds on plants. It is a main prey of the big cats and wolves of the region.
capra aegagrus.about: The bezoar ibex is a wild goat subspecies that is native to the montane forested areas in the Anatolia, Caucasus and the Zagros Mountains.

capra caucasica.name: West Caucasian tur
capra caucasica.desc: A wild goat found only in the western half of the Caucasus, living on steep, rocky mountain slopes and meadows.
capra caucasica.about: The West Caucasian tur is a mountain-dwelling goat-antelope native to the western half of the Caucasus Mountains range, in Georgia and European Russia.

capra hircus.name: Feral goat
capra hircus.desc: Introduced goats strip vegetation and compete with tortoises for grazing. They were removed from Santiago by 2006.
capra hircus.about: The goat or domestic goat is a species of caprine that is mostly kept as livestock. It was domesticated from the wild goat (C. aegagrus) of Southwest Asia and Eastern Europe.

capra ibex.name: Alpine ibex
capra ibex.desc: A steep-ground grazer living mostly between 1,800 and 3,300 m. It was nearly wiped out by hunting and has been restored by reintroductions.
capra ibex.about: The Alpine ibex, also known as the steinbock, is a European species of goat which lives in the Alps. It is one of ten species in the genus Capra, and its closest living relative is the Iberian ibex.

capra nubiana.name: Nubian ibex
capra nubiana.desc: A cliff-dwelling wild goat that eats grasses and acacia leaves. Captive breeding and reintroduction rebuilt its Jordan population, and Dana is a stronghold.
capra nubiana.about: The Nubian ibex is a desert-dwelling species of goat (genus Capra) found in mountainous areas of northern and northeast Africa, and the Middle East.

capra pyrenaica.name: Spanish ibex
capra pyrenaica.desc: Wild goat that returned to the mountains after the Gerês ibex died out in the 1890s; about 100 animals by 2011.
capra pyrenaica.about: The Iberian ibex, also known as the Spanish ibex, Spanish wild goat and Iberian wild goat, is a species of ibex endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

capra sibirica.name: Siberian ibex
capra sibirica.desc: A wild goat of steep rocky slopes that eats grasses and herbs, and twigs and needles in winter. Snow leopards and wolves prey on it.
capra sibirica.about: The Siberian ibex, also known by regional names including Altai ibex, Asian ibex, Central Asian ibex, Gobi ibex, Himalayan ibex, Mongolian ibex, and Tian Shan ibex, is a polytypic species of ibex, a…

capra walie.name: Walia ibex
capra walie.desc: An endemic wild goat of steep cliffs that browses shrubs, herbs, lichens and grasses; Simien is its main stronghold.
capra walie.about: The Walia ibex is a critically endangered species of ibex. It is sometimes considered an endemic subspecies of the Alpine ibex.

capreolus capreolus.name: European roe deer
capreolus capreolus.desc: A small browsing deer that eats shoots and leaves of oak, spruce and bilberry. It is a favoured prey of lynx where common.
capreolus capreolus.about: The roe deer, also known as the roe, western roe deer, or European roe, is a species of deer. The male of the species is sometimes referred to as a roebuck.

capreolus pygargus.name: Siberian roe deer
capreolus pygargus.desc: A small deer of forest-steppe that browses herbs and woody shoots; wolves and snow leopards prey on it.
capreolus pygargus.about: The Siberian roe deer, eastern roe deer, or Asian roe deer, is a species of roe deer found in northeastern Asia.

capricornis sumatraensis.name: Mainland serow
capricornis sumatraensis.desc: A goat-antelope of steep, rocky forest that browses leaves and herbs. Wikipedia lists it in the park, and bears are reported to kill serow.
capricornis sumatraensis.about: The mainland serow is a species of serow native to the Himalayas, Southeast Asia and China. The mainland serow is related closely to the red serow.

capricornis swinhoei.name: Formosan serow
capricornis swinhoei.desc: A goat-antelope of steep rock and forest that eats leaves, vines, ferns and ground herbs, and licks minerals from cliffs.
capricornis swinhoei.about: The Taiwanese serow also known as the Formosan serow, is a small species of bovid that is endemic to Taiwan.

capromys pilorides.name: Desmarest's hutia
capromys pilorides.desc: Large tree-dwelling rodent eating mostly bark, leaves and fruit. Common where mangroves are abundant and a key prey item.
capromys pilorides.about: Desmarest's hutia or the Cuban hutia is a stout, furry, rat-like mammal found only on Cuba and nearby islands.

caracal aurata.name: African golden cat
caracal aurata.desc: A forest cat that hunts tree hyraxes and rodents, and also takes birds, small monkeys and duikers.
caracal aurata.about: The African golden cat is a wild cat endemic to the rainforests of West and Central Africa. It is threatened due to deforestation and bushmeat hunting and listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

caracal caracal.name: Caracal
caracal caracal.desc: A medium-sized cat that hunts hyraxes, rodents and mongooses. GloBI records it with many species from this site.
caracal caracal.about: The caracal is a wild cat native to Africa, the Middle East, Central Asia, and arid areas of Pakistan and northwestern India.

caracara plancus.name: Southern caracara
caracara plancus.desc: A bold raptor and scavenger of open country. GloBI records it eating hares, birds and carrion.
caracara plancus.about: The crested caracara is a bird of prey (raptor) in the falcon family, Falconidae. It was formerly placed in the genus Polyborus before being given in its own genus, Caracara.

caranx ignobilis.name: Giant trevally
caranx ignobilis.desc: Patrols the reef edge, hunting fish in groups.
caranx ignobilis.about: The giant trevally, also known as the lowly trevally, barrier trevally, giant kingfish, or ulua, is a species of large marine fish classified in the jack family, Carangidae.

carcharhinus amblyrhynchos.name: Grey reef shark
carcharhinus amblyrhynchos.desc: A reef shark that hunts reef fish. The lagoons hold healthy populations of top predators.
carcharhinus amblyrhynchos.about: The grey reef shark or gray reef shark is a species of requiem shark, in the family Carcharhinidae.

carcharhinus galapagensis.name: Galápagos shark
carcharhinus galapagensis.desc: A large reef shark of the islands. It eats fish and is among the sharks that hunt sea lions and occasionally marine iguanas.
carcharhinus galapagensis.about: The Galapagos shark is a species of requiem shark, in the family Carcharhinidae, found worldwide.

carcharhinus leucas.name: Bull shark
carcharhinus leucas.desc: A coastal shark that enters estuaries and river mouths and eats fish and dolphins.
carcharhinus leucas.about: The bull shark, also known as the Zambezi shark (informally zambi) in Africa and Lake Nicaragua shark in Nicaragua, is a species of requiem shark commonly found worldwide in warm, shallow waters…

carcharhinus limbatus.name: Blacktip shark
carcharhinus limbatus.desc: Coastal shark that hunts schooling fish such as mullet and sardines. Sharks and rays in the park are under heavy fishing pressure.
carcharhinus limbatus.about: The blacktip shark is a species of requiem shark in the family Carcharhinidae. It is common to coastal tropical and subtropical waters around the world, including brackish habitats.

carcharhinus melanopterus.name: Blacktip reef shark
carcharhinus melanopterus.desc: A shallow reef shark that eats small bony fish, squid and crabs.
carcharhinus melanopterus.about: The blacktip reef shark is a species of requiem shark, in the family Carcharhinidae, which can be easily identified by the prominent black tips on its fins (especially on the first dorsal fin and its…

carcharhinus perezi.name: Caribbean reef shark
carcharhinus perezi.desc: Top reef predator of bony fishes and rays. Overfishing has reduced its numbers off Belize.
carcharhinus perezi.about: The Caribbean reef shark is a species of requiem shark, belonging to the family Carcharhinidae.

carcharodon carcharias.name: Great white shark
carcharodon carcharias.desc: Preys mainly on seals and sea lions off California. Bites sea otters often but usually does not eat them.
carcharodon carcharias.about: The great white shark, also known as the white shark, white pointer, or great white, is a large shark. It is closely related to the mako sharks, the porbeagle, and the salmon shark.

carcinus maenas.name: Shore crab
carcinus maenas.desc: An omnivore that eats bivalves, worms, small crustaceans and eelgrass seeds. It will also eat other crabs.
carcinus maenas.about: Carcinus maenas is a common littoral crab. It is known by different names around the world.

cardamine concatenata.name: Cut-leaf toothcup
cardamine concatenata.desc: Cut-leaf toothcup (Cardamine concatenata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
cardamine concatenata.about: Cardamine concatenata, the cutleaved toothwort, crow's toes, pepper root or purple-flowered toothwort, is a flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae.

cardinalis cardinalis.name: Northern Cardinal
cardinalis cardinalis.desc: Northern Cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.
cardinalis cardinalis.about: The northern cardinal, also commonly known as the common cardinal, red cardinal, or simply cardinal, is a bird in the genus Cardinalis.

cardisoma carnifex.name: Land crabs
cardisoma carnifex.desc: Burrowing crabs of the mangrove and scrub fringe that eat leaf litter. They also prey on young tortoises.
cardisoma carnifex.about: Cardisoma carnifex is a species of terrestrial crab found in coastal regions from the east coast of Africa and the Red Sea across the Indo-Pacific to the Line Islands and the Tuamotu Archipelago.

carduus nutans.name: Musk Thistle
carduus nutans.desc: Musk Thistle (Carduus nutans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.
carduus nutans.about: Carduus nutans is a biennial plant in the daisy and sunflower family Asteraceae with the common names musk thistle, nodding thistle, and nodding plumeless thistle.

caretta caretta.name: Loggerhead sea turtle
caretta caretta.desc: Yakushima is the largest nesting ground for loggerheads in the North Pacific. Adults eat jellyfish and shellfish; eggs and hatchlings are eaten by crabs, crows and raccoon dogs.
caretta caretta.about: The loggerhead sea turtle, loggerhead turtle or loggerhead, is a species of sea turtle distributed throughout the world. It is a marine reptile, belonging to the family Cheloniidae.

carex.name: Sedges
carex.desc: Grass-like plants of meadows and coastal flats. Wikipedia lists sedges among the main foods of brown bears.
carex.about: Carex is a vast genus of over 2,000 species of grass-like plants in the family Cyperaceae, commonly known as sedges (or seg, in older books).

carex albicans.name: Whitetinge Sedge

cecropia pachystachya.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree of forest edges and clearings. It is among the best-recorded plants near the park and is eaten by tapirs and capuchins in GloBI records.
cecropia pachystachya.about: Cecropia pachystachya, commonly known as Ambay pumpwood, is a species of tree in the family Urticaceae.

cecropia schreberiana.name: Pumpwood (yagrumo)
cecropia schreberiana.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree that recolonizes hurricane-damaged ground. Birds and bats eat its fruit and spread the seeds.
cecropia schreberiana.about: Cecropia schreberiana is a fast-growing tropical tree in the family Urticaceae. It is known by many different common names, including trumpetwood, pumpwood, guarumo, snakewood tree, and downgolog.

cecropia spp..name: Cecropia
cecropia spp..desc: A fast-growing gap tree. Sloths browse its leaves, and ants live in its hollow stems.
cecropia spp..about: Cecropia is a Neotropical genus consisting of 61 recognized species with a highly distinctive lineage of dioecious trees.

cedrus libani.name: Cedar of Lebanon
cedrus libani.desc: The reserve's signature conifer, forming forests on the slopes of Mount Barouk. Goat browsing on young trees hinders its natural regeneration.
cedrus libani.about: Cedrus libani, commonly known as cedar of Lebanon, Lebanon cedar, or Lebanese cedar (Arabic: أرز لبناني, romanized: ʾarz lubnāniyy), is a species of large conifer in the pine family, Pinaceae, and is…

ceiba pentandra.name: Kapok
ceiba pentandra.desc: One of the tallest emergent trees. Its flowers feed bats and monkeys, and its leaves feed leafcutter ants.
ceiba pentandra.about: Ceiba pentandra is a tropical tree of the order Malvales and the family Malvaceae (previously placed in the family Bombacaceae), native to Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, and the northern…

celastrus orbiculatus.name: Asian Bittersweet
celastrus orbiculatus.desc: Asian Bittersweet (Celastrus orbiculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

celtis iguanaea.name: Iguana hackberry
celtis iguanaea.desc: A hackberry shrub or tree. Its fruit is widely eaten by forest mammals and birds in GloBI records.
celtis iguanaea.about: Celtis iguanaea, the iguana hackberry, is a deciduous tree in the genus Celtis. The species is found in the United States (Florida), Central America, the Caribbean, and South America.

celtis laevigata.name: Sugar hackberry
celtis laevigata.desc: Sugar hackberry (Celtis laevigata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
celtis laevigata.about: Celtis laevigata is a medium-sized tree native to North America. Common names include sugarberry, southern hackberry, or in the southern U.S. sugar hackberry or just hackberry.

celtis occidentalis.name: Hackberry
celtis occidentalis.desc: Hackberry (Celtis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
celtis occidentalis.about: Celtis occidentalis, commonly known as the common hackberry, is a large deciduous tree native to North America.

celtis reticulata.name: Netleaf hackberry
celtis reticulata.desc: Netleaf hackberry (Celtis reticulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
celtis reticulata.about: Celtis reticulata, with common names including netleaf hackberry, western hackberry, Douglas hackberry, netleaf sugar hackberry, palo blanco, and acibuche, is a small- to medium-sized deciduous tree…

cenchrus ciliaris.name: Buffel grass
cenchrus ciliaris.desc: Drought-tolerant bunch grass of wadis and lowland plains, grazed when rain brings new growth.
cenchrus ciliaris.about: Cenchrus ciliaris (buffel-grass or African foxtail grass; syn.

centaurea nigra.name: Lesser Knapweed
centaurea nigra.desc: Lesser Knapweed (Centaurea nigra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

centaurea stoebe.name: Panicled Knapweed
centaurea stoebe.desc: Panicled Knapweed (Centaurea stoebe): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
centaurea stoebe.about: Centaurea stoebe, the spotted knapweed or panicled knapweed, is a species of Centaurea native to eastern Europe, although it has spread to North America, where it is considered an invasive species.

centronyx henslowii.name: Henslow's sparrow
centronyx henslowii.desc: A secretive sparrow the MDC says cannot persist without big bluestem prairie. Eats insects and seeds.
centronyx henslowii.about: Henslow's sparrow is a North American passerine bird in the family Passerellidae. It was named by John James Audubon in honor of John Stevens Henslow.

centrosema virginianum.name: Spurred Butterfly Pea
centrosema virginianum.desc: Spurred Butterfly Pea (Centrosema virginianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
centrosema virginianum.about: Centrosema virginianum is known by the common names of spurred butterfly pea, wild blue vine, blue bell, and wild pea. C.

centrostephanus rodgersii.name: Long-spined sea urchin
centrostephanus rodgersii.desc: A large dark urchin that grazes algae on rocky reef. Marine park surveys found it increasing about threefold between 2006 and 2010.
centrostephanus rodgersii.about: Centrostephanus rodgersii, commonly known as the long-spined sea urchin, is a species of sea urchin of the family Diadematidae.

cephalanthus occidentalis.name: Button-willow
cephalanthus occidentalis.desc: Button-willow (Cephalanthus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
cephalanthus occidentalis.about: Cephalanthus occidentalis is a species of flowering plant in the family Rubiaceae that is native to eastern and southern North America.

cephalophus dorsalis.name: Bay duiker
cephalophus dorsalis.desc: A small forest antelope that feeds on fallen fruit and leaves on the forest floor. It is prey for leopards and crowned eagles.
cephalophus dorsalis.about: The bay duiker, also known as the black-striped duiker and the black-backed duiker, is a forest-dwelling duiker native to western and southern Africa.

cephalophus niger.name: Black duiker
cephalophus niger.desc: A small forest antelope of the undergrowth that eats fallen fruit and leaves.
cephalophus niger.about: The black duiker, also known as tuba in Dyula, is a forest-dwelling duiker found in the southern parts of Sierra Leone, Liberia, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Benin, and Nigeria.

cephalophus nigrifrons.name: Black-fronted duiker
cephalophus nigrifrons.desc: A small forest antelope that mostly browses leaves and plant shoots, and also eats fruit.
cephalophus nigrifrons.about: The black-fronted duiker is a small antelope found in central and west-central Africa.

cephalophus rufilatus.name: Red-flanked duiker
cephalophus rufilatus.desc: A small antelope of savanna woodland and forest edges that eats foliage, fallen fruit, seeds and blossoms.
cephalophus rufilatus.about: The red-flanked duiker is a species of small antelope found in western and central Africa in countries as far apart as Senegal and Sudan.

cephalophus spp..name: Forest duikers
cephalophus spp..desc: Small forest antelope that eat fruit and leaves and are common prey for leopards, golden cats, eagles and apes.
