cephalophus spp..about: A duiker (IPA: ) is a small to medium-sized antelope native to sub-Saharan Africa. Most species are forest-dwelling, while the common duiker is the only bush duiker and occupies savannas.

cephalophus zebra.name: Zebra duiker
cephalophus zebra.desc: A small forest antelope that eats fruit, leaves and seeds and can crack hard fruit shells. It is a threatened species of the Upper Guinea forests.
cephalophus zebra.about: The zebra duiker is a small antelope found primarily in Liberia, as well as the Ivory Coast, Sierra Leone, and occasionally Guinea.

cerambycidae.name: Longhorn beetles
cerambycidae.desc: Wood-boring beetle larvae chew into trunks and stems, and adults feed on nectar and fruit. Several species are recorded nearby.
cerambycidae.about: The longhorn beetles (Cerambycidae), also known as long-horned or longicorns (whose larvae are often referred to as roundheaded borers), are a large family of beetles, with over 35,000 species…

cerastes cerastes.name: Horned viper
cerastes cerastes.desc: An ambush snake that buries itself in sand and strikes small rodents and lizards.
cerastes cerastes.about: Cerastes cerastes, commonly known as the Saharan horned viper or the desert horned viper, is a species of viper native to the deserts of Northern Africa and parts of the Arabian Peninsula and Levant.

cerastes gasperettii.name: Arabian horned viper
cerastes gasperettii.desc: A sand-dwelling viper whose diet is thought to be mainly rodents, with beetles and lizards as smaller prey.
cerastes gasperettii.about: Common names: Arabian horned viper, desert horned viper, Middle Eastern horned viper.

cerastoderma edule.name: Common cockle
cerastoderma edule.desc: A shallow-burrowing bivalve that filters food from the water. Red knots and oystercatchers both take it.
cerastoderma edule.about: The common cockle is a species of edible saltwater clam, a marine bivalve mollusc in the family Cardiidae, the cockles.

ceratina calcarata.name: Spurred Ceratina
ceratina calcarata.desc: Spurred Ceratina (Ceratina calcarata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

ceratina dupla.name: Doubled Ceratina
ceratina dupla.desc: Doubled Ceratina (Ceratina dupla): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 198 times near the park in GBIF.
ceratina dupla.about: Ceratina dupla, the doubled ceratina, is a species of small carpenter bee in the family Apidae. It is found in the eastern half of North America.

ceratina mikmaqi.name: Mikmaq Small Carpenter
ceratina mikmaqi.desc: Mikmaq Small Carpenter (Ceratina mikmaqi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 131 times near the park in GBIF.

ceratina strenua.name: Nimble Ceratina
ceratina strenua.desc: Nimble Ceratina (Ceratina strenua): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
ceratina strenua.about: Ceratina strenua, the nimble ceratina, is a species of small carpenter bee in the family Apidae. It is found in North America.

ceratiola ericoides.name: Florida-rosemary
ceratiola ericoides.desc: Florida-rosemary (Ceratiola ericoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
ceratiola ericoides.about: Ceratiola is a genus of flowering plants with a single species, Ceratiola ericoides, a shrub endemic to the Southeastern United States.

ceratogymna atrata.name: Black-casqued hornbill
ceratogymna atrata.desc: A large forest hornbill, the most recorded of the big birds near the reserve, that eats fruit and spreads seeds.
ceratogymna atrata.about: The black-casqued hornbill, or black-casqued wattled hornbill, is a species of hornbill in the family Bucerotidae.

ceratogymna elata.name: Yellow-casqued hornbill
ceratogymna elata.desc: A large canopy hornbill, the most-recorded bird near Gola. It lives in family groups and is listed as Vulnerable.
ceratogymna elata.about: The yellow-casqued hornbill, also known as the yellow-casqued wattled hornbill, is found in the rainforest of coastal regions of West Africa, for example in Côte d'Ivoire.

ceratotherium simum.name: White rhinoceros
ceratotherium simum.desc: A heavy grazer of the short grass layer. Wikipedia lists it among the park herbivores.
ceratotherium simum.about: The white rhinoceros, white rhino or square-lipped rhinoceros is the largest extant species of rhinoceros. It has a wide mouth used for grazing and is the most social of all rhino species.

cercis canadensis.name: Eastern Redbud
cercis canadensis.desc: Eastern Redbud (Cercis canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
cercis canadensis.about: Cercis canadensis, the eastern redbud, is a large deciduous shrub or small tree, native to eastern North America from southern Michigan south to central Mexico, west to New Mexico, but able to thrive…

cercis occidentalis.name: California Redbud
cercis occidentalis.desc: California Redbud (Cercis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

cercocarpus intricatus.name: Dwarf mountain mahogany
cercocarpus intricatus.desc: Dwarf mountain mahogany (Cercocarpus intricatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.
cercocarpus intricatus.about: Cercocarpus ledifolius var. intricatus (little-leaf mountain mahogany, narrowleaf mahogany, dwarf mountain mahogany) is a variety of Cercocarpus ledifolius that is commonly known as little-leaf…

cercocarpus ledifolius.name: Curl-leaf mountain-mahogany
cercocarpus ledifolius.desc: A tough evergreen shrub of dry slopes that mule deer browse, especially in winter.
cercocarpus ledifolius.about: Cercocarpus ledifolius is a North American species of mountain mahogany known by the common name curl-leaf mountain mahogany.

cercocarpus montanus.name: Mountain mahogany
cercocarpus montanus.desc: A tough rocky-slope shrub that elk and deer browse heavily, often keeping it short.
cercocarpus montanus.about: Cercocarpus montanus is a North American species of shrub or small tree in the family Rosaceae native to northern Mexico and the western United States.

cercocebus atys.name: Sooty mangabey
cercocebus atys.desc: A ground-and-canopy monkey of West African forest. GloBI records show it feeding on several Taï forest fruits.
cercocebus atys.about: The sooty mangabey is an Old World monkey found in forests from Senegal in a margin along the coast down to the Ivory Coast.

cercopithecus cephus.name: Moustached guenon
cercopithecus cephus.desc: A small forest monkey that eats fruit and insects; GloBI records it feeding on Strombosia fruit near the park.
cercopithecus cephus.about: The moustached guenon or moustached monkey is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

cercopithecus diana.name: Diana monkey
cercopithecus diana.desc: Eats mainly fruit, flowers and leaves in all levels of the canopy. Its predator-specific alarm calls are understood by other forest species.
cercopithecus diana.about: The Diana monkey is an Old World monkey found in the high canopy forests in Sierra Leone, Liberia, and western Côte d'Ivoire Named for its white brow, which is said to resemble the bow of the Roman…

cercopithecus lhoesti.name: L'Hoest's monkey
cercopithecus lhoesti.desc: A forest guenon recorded in Kibira that feeds mostly on fruit and other plant material.
cercopithecus lhoesti.about: L'Hoest's monkey, also known as the mountain monkey, is a guenon found in the upper eastern Congo Basin. They mostly live in mountainous forest areas in small, female-dominated groups.

cercopithecus mitis.name: Blue monkey
cercopithecus mitis.desc: A common forest monkey that eats fruit and leaves, including cherry and pittosporum fruit.
cercopithecus mitis.about: The blue monkey or diademed monkey is a species of Old World monkey native to Central and East Africa, ranging from the upper Congo River basin east to the East African Rift and south to northern…

cercopithecus nictitans.name: Greater spot-nosed monkey
cercopithecus nictitans.desc: A tree-living guenon recorded near the reserve that eats mainly fruit and is hunted by eagles, leopards and chimpanzees.
cercopithecus nictitans.about: The greater spot-nosed monkey or putty-nosed monkey is one of the smallest Old World monkeys. It is a guenon of the C.

cercyonis pegala.name: Common Wood-nymph
cercyonis pegala.desc: Common Wood-nymph (Cercyonis pegala): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
cercyonis pegala.about: The common wood-nymph is a North American species of butterfly in the family Nymphalidae. It is also known as the wood-nymph, grayling, blue-eyed grayling, and the goggle eye.

cerdocyon thous.name: Crab-eating fox
cerdocyon thous.desc: An opportunistic canid that eats fruit, insects and small vertebrates.
cerdocyon thous.about: The crab-eating fox, also known as the forest dog, wood fox, bushfox (not to be confused with the bush dog) or maikong, is an extant species of medium-sized canid endemic to the central part of South…

cereus hildmannianus.name: Hedge cactus
cereus hildmannianus.desc: A tall cactus of the coastal scrub whose fruit is eaten by birds and lizards.
cereus hildmannianus.about: Cereus hildmannianus is a species of cactus from southern South America. Its distribution is uncertain but probably includes Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Argentina.

cereus insularis.name: Noronha cactus
cereus insularis.desc: A tall columnar cactus recorded very often on the island. It copes with the dry season and provides cover and fruit.
cereus insularis.about: Cereus insularis is a species of columnar cactus in the family Cactaceae. It is found in Brazil.

certhia brachydactyla.name: Short-toed treecreeper
certhia brachydactyla.desc: Small bark-creeping bird recorded in large numbers; GloBI records it eating butterflies such as the large white.
certhia brachydactyla.about: The short-toed treecreeper is a small passerine bird found in woodlands through much of the warmer regions of Europe and into north Africa.

cervus canadensis.name: Elk
cervus canadensis.desc: Mostly grazes native grasses but also browses shrubs. Bears and coyotes take calves, and cougars take adults.
cervus canadensis.about: The elk or wapiti (pronounced ) is the second largest species within the deer family, Cervidae, and one of the largest terrestrial mammals in its native range of North America and Central and East…

cervus canadensis roosevelti.name: Roosevelt elk
cervus canadensis roosevelti.desc: Browses shrubs and grazes grasses, and eats conifer seedlings in winter. Olympic protected much of its range.
cervus canadensis roosevelti.about: The Roosevelt elk, also known commonly as the Olympic elk and Roosevelt's wapiti, is the largest of the four surviving subspecies of elk in North America by body mass.

cervus canadensis xanthopygus.name: Manchurian wapiti
cervus canadensis xanthopygus.desc: Adapted to mixed deciduous forest. Tiger distribution has been found to follow wapiti distribution closely.
cervus canadensis xanthopygus.about: The Manchurian wapiti is a putative subspecies of the wapiti native to East Asia. It may be identified as its own species, Cervus xanthopygus.

cervus elaphus.name: Elk
cervus elaphus.desc: Elk (Cervus elaphus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
cervus elaphus.about: The red deer is a species of deer in the genus Cervus. It is one of the largest deer species.

cervus elaphus maral.name: Caspian red deer
cervus elaphus maral.desc: A large deer that eats grasses and leaves. The leopard is its main predator, and wolves and bears take fewer.
cervus elaphus maral.about: The Caspian red deer, is one of the easternmost subspecies of red deer that is native to areas between the Black Sea and Caspian Sea such as Crimea, Asia Minor, the Caucasus Mountains region…

cervus nippon.name: Sika deer
cervus nippon.desc: Sika Deer (Cervus nippon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 219 times near the park in GBIF.
cervus nippon.about: The sika deer, also known as the northern spotted deer or the Japanese deer, is a species of deer native to much of East Asia and introduced to other parts of the world.

ceryle rudis.name: Pied kingfisher
ceryle rudis.desc: A fish-eating bird that hovers over open water and dives for small fish.
ceryle rudis.about: The pied kingfisher is a species of water kingfisher widely distributed across Africa and Asia.

cethosia cydippe.name: Eastern red lacewing
cethosia cydippe.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on passion-flower vines. GloBI records it feeding on Passiflora aurantia.
cethosia cydippe.about: Cethosia cydippe, the eastern red lacewing, is a species of butterfly from Australia, New Guinea and nearby islands. The Australian subspecies, C. c.

cetonia aurata.name: Rose chafer
cetonia aurata.desc: A metallic green beetle. Its larvae live in rotting wood and humus, and adults visit flowers.
cetonia aurata.about: Cetonia aurata, called the rose chafer or the green rose chafer, is a beetle, 20 millimetres (3⁄4 in) long, that has a metallic structurally coloured green and a distinct V-shaped scutellum.

chaerephon plicatus.name: Wrinkle-lipped bat
chaerephon plicatus.desc: Lives in large cave colonies and flies out to feed on night-flying insects. Its droppings enrich cave and soil nutrients.
chaerephon plicatus.about: The wrinkle-lipped free-tailed bat is a species of bat in the family Molossidae.

chaetadelpha wheeleri.name: Dune wirelettuce
chaetadelpha wheeleri.desc: Dune wirelettuce (Chaetadelpha wheeleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
chaetadelpha wheeleri.about: Chaetadelpha is a genus of plants in the family Asteraceae containing the single species Chaetadelpha wheeleri, or Wheeler's skeletonweed.

chaetoceros.name: Phytoplankton
chaetoceros.desc: Microscopic algae drifting in the bay. They use sunlight and dissolved nutrients and feed the plankton, oysters and fish that fill the water.
chaetoceros.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

chaetodipus baileyi.name: Bailey's pocket mouse
chaetodipus baileyi.desc: Bailey's pocket mouse (Chaetodipus baileyi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
chaetodipus baileyi.about: Bailey's pocket mouse is a species of rodent of the subfamily Perognathinae, family Heteromyidae.

chaetodontidae.name: Butterflyfish
chaetodontidae.desc: Nips at coral polyps and small invertebrates.
chaetodontidae.about: The butterflyfish are a group of conspicuous tropical marine fish of the family Chaetodontidae; the bannerfish and coralfish are also included in this group.

chaetura pelagica.name: Chimney swift
chaetura pelagica.desc: Catches flying insects in the air and nests in chimneys. Peregrines and some other raptors catch adults in flight.
chaetura pelagica.about: The chimney swift is a bird belonging to the swift family Apodidae.

chalcomitra balfouri.name: Socotra sunbird
chalcomitra balfouri.desc: An endemic bird that feeds on nectar and insects, and helps pollinate Socotra's flowering plants.
chalcomitra balfouri.about: The Socotra sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is endemic to Socotra.

chalcosoma moellenkampi.name: Three-horned rhinoceros beetle
chalcosoma moellenkampi.desc: A large beetle of the montane forest. Rhinoceros beetle larvae of this kind develop in rotting wood; adults are prey for forest birds and frogs.
chalcosoma moellenkampi.about: The Moellenkampi beetle, is one of four large species of rhinoceros beetles from Southeast Asia belonging to the genus Chalcosoma.

chamaea fasciata.name: Wrentit
chamaea fasciata.desc: Wrentit (Chamaea fasciata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 61 times near the park in GBIF.
chamaea fasciata.about: The wrentit is a small bird that lives in chaparral, oak woodlands, and bushland on the western coast of North America, from Oregon south through California to northern Baja California.

chamaebatia foliolosa.name: Mountain misery
chamaebatia foliolosa.desc: Mountain misery (Chamaebatia foliolosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 167 times near the park in GBIF.

chamaebatiaria millefolium.name: Desert sweet
chamaebatiaria millefolium.desc: Desert sweet (Chamaebatiaria millefolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 228 times near the park in GBIF.
chamaebatiaria millefolium.about: Chamaebatiaria is a monotypic genus of aromatic shrub in the rose family containing the single species Chamaebatiaria millefolium, which is known by the common names fern bush and desert sweet.

chamaecrista fasciculata.name: Golden Cassia
chamaecrista fasciculata.desc: Golden Cassia (Chamaecrista fasciculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
chamaecrista fasciculata.about: Chamaecrista fasciculata, the partridge pea, is a species of legume native to most of the eastern United States. It is an annual which grows to approximately 0.5 meters (1 ft 8 in) tall.

chamaeleo monachus.name: Socotra chameleon
chamaeleo monachus.desc: An island endemic that lives in scrub and along seasonal stream beds, catching insects.
chamaeleo monachus.about: The Socotran chameleon is a species of chameleon endemic to the island of Socotra. When alarmed, it makes a hissing noise, and depending on its mood, it may change color.

chamaeleonidae.name: Chameleons
chamaeleonidae.desc: Slow-moving lizards that catch insects with a sticky tongue and are eaten by lemurs, raptors and the fossa.
chamaeleonidae.about: Chameleons (family Chamaeleonidae) are a distinctive and highly specialized clade of Old World lizards with 200 species described as of June 2015.

chamaenerion angustifolium.name: Fireweed
chamaenerion angustifolium.desc: A tall pink wildflower of open and disturbed ground that deer and pikas eat.
chamaenerion angustifolium.about: Chamaenerion angustifolium is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the willowherb family, Onagraceae.

channa micropeltes.name: Giant snakehead
channa micropeltes.desc: A voracious freshwater predator that eats nearly anything small enough to fit in its mouth and can gulp air in poor water.
channa micropeltes.about: Channa micropeltes, giant snakehead, giant mudfish or toman harimau, is among the largest species in the family Channidae, capable of growing to 1.8 m (5.9 ft) in length and a weight of 30 kg (66…

chaoborus edulis.name: Lake fly (kungu)
chaoborus edulis.desc: Its larvae eat zooplankton and are food for fish. Adult swarms feed birds and are harvested by people.
chaoborus edulis.about: Chaoborus edulis is a species of phantom midges (flies in the family Chaoboridae). Colloquially, the larval stage is termed a glassworm.

chaoborus punctipennis.name: Chaoborus punctipennis
chaoborus punctipennis.desc: Chaoborus punctipennis (Chaoborus punctipennis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

chara.name: Stoneworts and pondweeds
chara.desc: Underwater plants and algae that carpet the lake bed below the reeds. Slate-colored coots feed on them, especially Chara.
chara.about: Chara is a genus of charophyte green algae in the family Characeae. They are multicellular and superficially resemble land plants because of stem-like and leaf-like structures.

characiformes.name: Characin fishes
characiformes.desc: Piranha and relatives, the main food of giant otters in Amazon rivers and oxbow lakes.
characiformes.about: Characiformes is an order of ray-finned fish, comprising the characins and their allies.

charadrius vociferus.name: Killdeer
charadrius vociferus.desc: Killdeer (Charadrius vociferus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,175 times near the park in GBIF.
charadrius vociferus.about: The killdeer is a large plover found in the Americas. Its shrill, two-syllable call is often heard, sounding like "kill deer".

charina bottae.name: Northern rubber boa
charina bottae.desc: Northern Rubber Boa (Charina bottae): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
charina bottae.about: The rubber boa is a species of snake in the family Boidae and is native to western North America.

charonia tritonis.name: Giant triton
charonia tritonis.desc: A large sea snail that eats crown-of-thorns starfish.
charonia tritonis.about: Charonia tritonis, common name the Triton's trumpet, the giant triton, the Pacific triton or pū is a species of very large sea snail, a marine gastropod mollusc in the family Charoniidae, the…

chasiempis sandwichensis.name: Hawaiʻi ʻelepaio
chasiempis sandwichensis.desc: A native flycatcher that hunts insects in the forest, and is prey for introduced cats and rats.
chasiempis sandwichensis.about: The Hawaiʻi ʻelepaio, also Hawaiian ʻelepaio, is a monarch flycatcher found on the Big Island of Hawaii.

chasmanthium latifolium.name: Broadleaf chasmanthium
chasmanthium latifolium.desc: Broadleaf chasmanthium (Chasmanthium latifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
chasmanthium latifolium.about: Chasmanthium latifolium, known as fish-on-a-fishing-pole, northern wood-oats, inland sea oats, northern sea oats, and river oats is a species of grass native to the central and eastern United States,…

chauliognathus pensylvanicus.name: Soldier Beetle
chauliognathus pensylvanicus.desc: Soldier Beetle (Chauliognathus pensylvanicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
chauliognathus pensylvanicus.about: The goldenrod soldier beetle or Pennsylvania leatherwing is a species of soldier beetle (Cantharidae).

chauna torquata.name: Southern screamer
chauna torquata.desc: A goose-like wetland bird that grazes leaves, stems and seeds of aquatic plants in marshes and flooded meadows.
chauna torquata.about: The southern screamer is a species of bird in family Anhimidae of the waterfowl order Anseriformes. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, Peru, and Uruguay.

cheilinus undulatus.name: Napoleon wrasse
cheilinus undulatus.desc: A large, endangered reef wrasse that eats molluscs, crustaceans, fish and toxic prey including crown-of-thorns starfish.
cheilinus undulatus.about: The humphead wrasse is the largest species of wrasse mainly found on coral reefs in the Indo-Pacific region. It is also known as the Māori wrasse, Napoleon wrasse, and Napoleonfish.

cheilopogon.name: Flyingfish
cheilopogon.desc: Open-water fish that feed on plankton and glide above the surface to escape predators. A classic prey of frigatebirds.
cheilopogon.about: The Exocoetidae are a family of saltwater ray-finned fish in the order Beloniformes, known colloquially as flying fish or flying cod, with about 64 species in seven genera.

chelone glabra.name: White Turtlehead
chelone glabra.desc: White Turtlehead (Chelone glabra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

chelonia mydas.name: Green sea turtle
chelonia mydas.desc: Adults graze seagrass and algae in shallow water. Tiger sharks are their main predator.
chelonia mydas.about: The green sea turtle, also known as the green turtle, black sea turtle, and Pacific green turtle, is a species of large sea turtle of the family Cheloniidae.

chelonoidis species.name: Galápagos giant tortoise
chelonoidis species.desc: A huge herbivore that eats cactus, grasses, leaves and lichens and gets much of its water from Opuntia and dew. Long-lived adults have no natural predators.
chelonoidis species.about: The Galápagos tortoise, also called the Galápagos giant tortoise, is a very large species of tortoise in the genus Chelonoidis (which also contains three smaller species from mainland South America).

chenopodium album.name: Fat-hen
chenopodium album.desc: Fat-hen (Chenopodium album): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.
chenopodium album.about: Chenopodium album is a fast-growing annual plant in the flowering plant family Amaranthaceae. Though cultivated in some regions, the plant is elsewhere considered a weed.

chilabothrus angulifer.name: Cuban boa
chilabothrus angulifer.desc: Large constrictor; top land predator in Cuba, eating mostly mammals and birds, including hutias and fruit bats.
chilabothrus angulifer.about: The Cuban boa, also known as the Cuban tree boa and by locals as Majá de Santa María, is a very large species of snake in the family Boidae.

chilabothrus subflavus.name: Jamaican boa
chilabothrus subflavus.desc: Jamaica's top native predator. It kills by constriction and eats birds, bats and lizards, and hunts from ambush in vines and bromeliads.
chilabothrus subflavus.about: The Jamaican boa, Jamaican yellow boa, yellow snake or Jamaican green snake; in Jamaican Patois: nanka) is a boa species endemic to Jamaica. No subspecies are recognized.

chilopsis linearis.name: Desert-willow
chilopsis linearis.desc: Desert-willow (Chilopsis linearis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

chimaphila maculata.name: Striped Prince's Pine
chimaphila maculata.desc: Pipsissewa (Chimaphila maculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 108 times near the park in GBIF.
chimaphila maculata.about: Chimaphila maculata is a small, perennial, evergreen herb native to eastern North America and Central U.S., from southern Quebec west to Illinois, and south to Florida and Panama.

chimaphila umbellata.name: Pipsissewa
chimaphila umbellata.desc: Pipsissewa (Chimaphila umbellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
chimaphila umbellata.about: Chimaphila umbellata, the umbellate wintergreen, pipsissewa, or prince's pine, is a small perennial flowering plant found in dry woodlands, or sandy soils.

chinavia hilaris.name: Green Stink Bug
chinavia hilaris.desc: Green Stink Bug (Chinavia hilaris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

chindwin headwaters.name: Chindwin headwaters
chindwin headwaters.desc: The Tanai and other streams drain the valley and form the head of the Chindwin River, watering the lowlands.

chiococca alba.name: West Indian milkberry
chiococca alba.desc: A shrub or climber with small white berries. GloBI records show bats, doves, thrushes and other birds eating its fruit.
chiococca alba.about: Chiococca alba is a species of flowering plant in the coffee family (Rubiaceae) native to Florida and the extreme southern tip of Texas in the United States, Bermuda, Mexico, Central America, the…

chionochloa.name: Snow tussock
chionochloa.desc: Tall alpine tussock grasses. Their leaves are the main food of takahe and are also grazed by red deer.
chionochloa.about: Chionochloa is a genus of tussock grass in the family Poaceae, found primarily in New Zealand with one known species in New Guinea and another on Lord Howe Island (part of Australia).

chionochloa rubra.name: Red tussock
chionochloa rubra.desc: Dominant tall tussock of the volcanic plateau, growing on pumice soils. Its flower heads host fly larvae and moth caterpillars.
chionochloa rubra.about: Chionochloa rubra, known commonly as red tussock grass, is a species of tussock grass in the grass family, endemic to New Zealand.

chionomys nivalis.name: European snow vole
chionomys nivalis.desc: Small rodent of rocky alpine ground that eats grasses and other plants.
chionomys nivalis.about: The European snow vole or snow vole is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae.

chironomidae.name: Midge larvae
chironomidae.desc: Aquatic insect larvae in lagoon mud and shallows. Flamingos and ibises list insect larvae such as chironomids among their food.
chironomidae.about: Chironomidae , commonly known as non-biting midges or chironomids , are a family of Nematoceran flies with a global distribution.

chironomus.name: Non-biting midges
chironomus.desc: Midge larvae live in the mud and water of the delta and are eaten by dragonflies, damselflies, fish and frogs.
chironomus.about: Chironomidae , commonly known as non-biting midges or chironomids , are a family of Nematoceran flies with a global distribution.

chiroxiphia linearis.name: Long-tailed manakin
chiroxiphia linearis.desc: The most recorded bird near the site. It eats small fruits such as those of alligatorwood and wax mallow.
chiroxiphia linearis.about: The long-tailed manakin is a species of bird in the family Pipridae native to Central America where it inhabits both wet and dry tropical and subtropical forests.

chloephaga hybrida.name: Kelp goose
chloephaga hybrida.desc: A shoreline goose of southern South America that grazes seaweed on rocky coasts. It was one of the most recorded birds here.
chloephaga hybrida.about: The kelp goose is a species of waterfowl in tribe the Tadornini of the subfamily Anserinae. It is found in Argentina, Chile, and the Falkland Islands.

chloephaga melanoptera.name: Andean goose
chloephaga melanoptera.desc: A large goose of high grassland, bogs and lake shores, living almost entirely above 3,000 m. It eats mostly grasses.
chloephaga melanoptera.about: The Andean goose is a species of waterfowl in tribe Tadornini of subfamily Anserinae. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

chloephaga picta.name: Upland goose
chloephaga picta.desc: A grazing goose of grassland and wet meadows, one of the best-recorded birds around the park.
chloephaga picta.about: The upland goose or Magellan goose is a sheldgoose of the shelduck-sheldgoose subfamily of the Anatidae, the biological family that includes the ducks and most duck-like waterfowl such as the geese…

chlorocebus sabaeus.name: Green monkey
chlorocebus sabaeus.desc: A common, widely recorded monkey of the area that feeds on fruit and other plant foods.
chlorocebus sabaeus.about: The green monkey, also known as the sabaeus monkey, is an Old World monkey with golden-green fur and pale hands and feet.

chlorodrepanis virens.name: Hawaiʻi ʻamakihi
chlorodrepanis virens.desc: A native honeycreeper that drinks nectar from ʻōhiʻa and māmane flowers and hunts insects and spiders. It is among the most recorded birds near the park.
chlorodrepanis virens.about: The Hawaiʻi ʻamakihi, also known as the common ʻamakihi, is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper.

chlorogalum pomeridianum.name: Amole
chlorogalum pomeridianum.desc: Amole (Chlorogalum pomeridianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.
chlorogalum pomeridianum.about: Chlorogalum pomeridianum, the wavy-leafed soap plant, California soaproot, or Amole, is the most common and most widely distributed of the soap plants, soaproots or amoles, which make up the genus…

chlosyne gorgone.name: Gorgone Checkerspot
chlosyne gorgone.desc: Gorgone Checkerspot (Chlosyne gorgone): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
chlosyne gorgone.about: Chlosyne gorgone, the gorgone checkerspot, is a species of Nymphalinae butterfly that occurs in North America.

chlosyne palla.name: Northern Checkerspot
chlosyne palla.desc: Northern Checkerspot (Chlosyne palla): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
chlosyne palla.about: Chlosyne palla, the northern checkerspot, is a butterfly of the family Nymphalidae that is found in North America.

choeropsis liberiensis.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
choeropsis liberiensis.desc: A secretive forest hippo that eats ferns, herbs and fallen fruit. Wikipedia lists Taï as one of the few areas holding it in Côte d'Ivoire.
choeropsis liberiensis.about: The pygmy hippopotamus or pygmy hippo is a small hippopotamid which is native to the forests and swamps of West Africa, primarily in Liberia, with small populations in Sierra Leone, Guinea, and Ivory…

choloepus didactylus.name: Linnaeus's two-toed sloth
choloepus didactylus.desc: A slow leaf-eater of the canopy. In the harpy eagle article sloths are the most important prey group.
choloepus didactylus.about: Linnaeus's two-toed sloth, also known as the southern two-toed sloth, unau, or Linne's two-toed sloth is a species of sloth from South America, found in Venezuela, Suriname, Guyana, French Guiana,…

chorispora tenella.name: Bluemustard
chorispora tenella.desc: Bluemustard (Chorispora tenella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
chorispora tenella.about: Chorispora tenella is a species of flowering plant in the mustard family known by several common names, including purple mustard, blue mustard, musk mustard, and crossflower.

choristoneura fumiferana.name: Spruce budworm
choristoneura fumiferana.desc: A moth whose caterpillars feed on conifer needles. Outbreaks defoliate large areas of forest and feed many nesting warblers.
choristoneura fumiferana.about: Choristoneura is a genus of moths in the family Tortricidae. Several species are serious pests of conifers, such as spruce and are known as spruce budworms.

chorthippus biguttulus.name: Bow-winged grasshopper
chorthippus biguttulus.desc: A very common grassland grasshopper, a main summer food for choughs and other insect eaters.
chorthippus biguttulus.about: Chorthippus biguttulus, the bow-winged grasshopper, is one of the most common species of grasshopper found in the dry grassland of northern and central Europe.

chortophaga viridifasciata.name: Green-striped Grasshopper
chortophaga viridifasciata.desc: Green-striped Grasshopper (Chortophaga viridifasciata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

chroicocephalus serranus.name: Andean gull
chroicocephalus serranus.desc: An opportunistic feeder at highland lakes, taking insects, amphibians, small fish and sometimes waterbird eggs and chicks.
chroicocephalus serranus.about: The Andean gull is a species in subfamily Larinae of the family Laridae, the gulls, terns, and skimmers. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

chromolaena odorata.name: Siam weed
chromolaena odorata.desc: A fast-spreading invasive shrub of disturbed ground. GloBI has records of elephants eating it.
chromolaena odorata.about: Chromolaena odorata is also known as jack in the bush. It is a tropical and subtropical species of flowering shrub in the family Asteraceae.

chrysanympha formosa.name: Formosa Looper
chrysanympha formosa.desc: Formosa Looper (Chrysanympha formosa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.
chrysanympha formosa.about: Chrysanympha formosa, the Formosa looper, is a moth of the family Noctuidae. The species was first described by Augustus Radcliffe Grote in 1865.

chrysaora quinquecirrha.name: Sea nettle
chrysaora quinquecirrha.desc: A stinging jellyfish of the bay's summer waters that feeds on zooplankton.
chrysaora quinquecirrha.about: The Atlantic sea nettle, also called the East Coast sea nettle in the United States, is a species of jellyfish that inhabits the Atlantic coast of the United States.

chrysobalanus icaco.name: Cocoplum
chrysobalanus icaco.desc: A coastal and wetland shrub whose fruit is eaten by bats and fruit-eating birds in GloBI records.
chrysobalanus icaco.about: Chrysobalanus icaco, the cocoplum, paradise plum, abajeru or icaco is a low shrub or bushy tree found near sea beaches and inland throughout tropical Africa, tropical Americas and the Caribbean, and…

chrysocyon brachyurus.name: Maned wolf
chrysocyon brachyurus.desc: An omnivore that eats mostly plant matter, especially wolf apple, plus armadillos, rodents and birds. Its dung helps leafcutter fungus gardens and seed germination.
chrysocyon brachyurus.about: The maned wolf is a large canine of South America. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, and Paraguay, and is almost locally extinct in Uruguay.

chrysothamnus viscidiflorus.name: Sticky-leaf rabbitbrush
chrysothamnus viscidiflorus.desc: Sticky-leaf rabbitbrush (Chrysothamnus viscidiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

chunga burmeisteri.name: Black-legged seriema
chunga burmeisteri.desc: A long-legged ground bird of the Chaco that hunts insects, snakes and other small animals.
chunga burmeisteri.about: The black-legged seriema is one of two living species of seriemas in the family Cariamidae. It is found from southeastern Bolivia and northern Paraguay south into north-central Argentina.

chuquiraga.name: Chuquiraga shrubs
chuquiraga.desc: Spiny evergreen shrubs of dry Patagonian steppe. GBIF records several species around the peninsula.
chuquiraga.about: Chuquiraga is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae. The genus is distributed in the Andes from Colombia to Chile, with most species occurring in Patagonia.

chylismia.name: Desert wildflowers
chylismia.desc: Annual flowers such as browneyes burst out after good rains and provide leaves and nectar for many desert animals.
chylismia.about: Chylismia is a plant genus in the evening primrose family Onagraceae.

cibotium glaucum.name: Hāpuʻu tree fern
cibotium glaucum.desc: A native tree fern of the wet forest understory, growing slowly to a few metres tall.
cibotium glaucum.about: Cibotium glaucum, the hāpu‘u pulu, is a species of fern in the family Cyatheaceae, native to Hawaii.

cicadella viridis.name: Green leafhopper
cicadella viridis.desc: Sap-feeding insect that lives on sedges, rushes and other herbs of damp ground.
cicadella viridis.about: Cicadella viridis, sometimes called the "green leafhopper" (but not to be confused with Nephotettix a genus that includes rice pests), is a species of European leafhoppers belonging to the subfamily…

cichlids, catfish and others.name: River fish
cichlids, catfish and others.desc: River fish feed on invertebrates and organic matter and take up nutrients from hippo dung. Crocodiles eat them.
cichlids, catfish and others.about: A fish is an aquatic, anamniotic, gill-bearing vertebrate with a tough cranium to protect the brain. Many fish have fins that they use for directional stability and propulsion.

cichorium intybus.name: Chicory
cichorium intybus.desc: Chicory (Cichorium intybus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
cichorium intybus.about: Common chicory is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink.

cicindela theatina.name: Great Sand Dunes tiger beetle
cicindela theatina.desc: A predatory beetle found only on sparsely vegetated sand in this park. Its whole range lies inside the protected park.
cicindela theatina.about: Cicindela theatina, commonly known as the Great Sand Dunes tiger beetle, is a predatory beetle found in sparsely vegetated sandy habitats.

ciconia ciconia.name: White stork
ciconia ciconia.desc: Hunts frogs, reptiles, small mammals and crayfish in marsh and pasture, and is a summer visitor that winters in Africa.
ciconia ciconia.about: The white stork is a large bird in the stork family, Ciconiidae. Its plumage is mainly white, with black on the bird's wings.

cinclus cinclus.name: White-throated dipper
cinclus cinclus.desc: Walks into fast streams to feed on caddis larvae, shrimps and other invertebrates, and sometimes on small fish.
cinclus cinclus.about: The white-throated dipper, also known as the European dipper or just dipper, is an aquatic, passerine bird found in Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

cinnyris chalybeus.name: Southern double-collared sunbird
cinnyris chalybeus.desc: A small nectar-feeding bird, one of the most recorded birds near the site, that visits heath and protea flowers.
cinnyris chalybeus.about: The southern double-collared sunbird or lesser double-collared sunbird is a small passerine bird which breeds in southern Africa.

cinnyris regius.name: Regal sunbird
cinnyris regius.desc: An Albertine Rift endemic sunbird that feeds on nectar from montane flowers.
cinnyris regius.about: The regal sunbird is a species of bird in the family Nectariniidae. It is native to the Albertine Rift montane forests.

circaetus gallicus.name: Short-toed snake eagle
circaetus gallicus.desc: A raptor that specialises in catching snakes, and is recorded often around the gorge.
circaetus gallicus.about: The short-toed snake eagle, also known as the short-toed eagle, is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as kites, buzzards and…

circus aeruginosus.name: Western marsh harrier
circus aeruginosus.desc: Raptor that hunts over the flats in winter and has been recorded taking shorebirds such as red knot.
circus aeruginosus.about: The western marsh harrier is a large harrier, a bird of prey from temperate and subtropical western Eurasia and adjacent Africa. It is also known as the Eurasian marsh harrier.

circus approximans.name: Swamp harrier
circus approximans.desc: Bird of prey recorded eating possums and rabbits; it hunts and scavenges across open ground.
circus approximans.about: The swamp harrier, also known as the Australasian marsh harrier or Australasian harrier, is a large, slim bird of prey widely distributed across Australasia.

circus cyaneus.name: Hen Harrier
circus cyaneus.desc: Hen Harrier (Circus cyaneus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.
circus cyaneus.about: The hen harrier is a bird of prey. It breeds in open areas such as marshes and grasslands in Eurasia and is migratory, moving further south outside of the breeding season.

circus hudsonius.name: Northern harrier
circus hudsonius.desc: Glides low over the grass hunting voles and small birds.
circus hudsonius.about: The northern harrier, also known as the marsh hawk or ring-tailed hawk, is a bird of prey.

cirsium arizonicum.name: Arizona thistle
cirsium arizonicum.desc: Arizona thistle (Cirsium arizonicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium arvense.name: Creeping Thistle
cirsium arvense.desc: Creeping Thistle (Cirsium arvense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.
cirsium arvense.about: Cirsium arvense is a perennial species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, native throughout Europe and western Asia, northern Africa and widely introduced elsewhere.

cirsium horridulum.name: Bristly Thistle
cirsium horridulum.desc: Yellow thistle (Cirsium horridulum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 62 times near the park in GBIF.
cirsium horridulum.about: Cirsium horridulum, called bristly thistle, purple thistle, or yellow thistle is a North American species of plants in the tribe Cardueae within the family Asteraceae.

cirsium mohavense.name: Mojave thistle
cirsium mohavense.desc: Mojave thistle (Cirsium mohavense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium pitcheri.name: Pitcher's thistle
cirsium pitcheri.desc: Pitcher's thistle (Cirsium pitcheri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.
cirsium pitcheri.about: Cirsium pitcheri, sometimes called Pitcher's thistle or dune thistle, is a species of thistle native to sand dune shorelines along the upper Great Lakes.

cirsium scariosum.name: Meadow thistle
cirsium scariosum.desc: Meadow thistle (Cirsium scariosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium scopulorum.name: Mountain Thistle
cirsium scopulorum.desc: Mountain Thistle (Cirsium scopulorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
cirsium scopulorum.about: Cirsium eatonii, commonly known as Eaton's thistle or mountaintop thistle, is a North American species of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.

cirsium vulgare.name: Spear Thistle
cirsium vulgare.desc: Spear Thistle (Cirsium vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

cirsium wheeleri.name: Wheeler's thistle
cirsium wheeleri.desc: Wheeler's thistle (Cirsium wheeleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
cirsium wheeleri.about: Cirsium wheeleri is a North American species of plants in the tribe Cardueae within the family Asteraceae. Common names include Wheeler's thistle.

cissus verticillata.name: Seasonvine
cissus verticillata.desc: A climbing vine whose fruit and foliage are eaten by several forest animals.
cissus verticillata.about: Cissus verticillata, the princess vine or seasonvine, is an evergreen perennial vine in the grapevine family Vitaceae.

cistus salviifolius.name: Rockrose scrub
cistus salviifolius.desc: Sage-leaved rockrose, one of many shrubs of the dry scrub, grazed by red deer and other herbivores.
cistus salviifolius.about: Cistus salviifolius, common names sage-leaved rock-rose, salvia cistus or Gallipoli rose, is a shrub of the family Cistaceae.

citheronia regalis.name: Hickory Horned Devil
citheronia regalis.desc: Hickory Horned Devil (Citheronia regalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
citheronia regalis.about: Citheronia regalis, the regal moth or royal walnut moth, is a North American moth in the family Saturniidae. The caterpillars are called hickory horned devils.

citrus trifoliata.name: Chinese bitter orange
citrus trifoliata.desc: Chinese bitter orange (Citrus trifoliata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
citrus trifoliata.about: The trifoliate orange, Citrus trifoliata, is a member of the family Rutaceae.

civettictis civetta.name: African civet
civettictis civetta.desc: A nocturnal omnivore that eats rodents, insects, millipedes, small reptiles, carrion and fruit.
civettictis civetta.about: The African civet is a large viverrid native to sub-Saharan Africa, where it is considered common and widely distributed in woodlands and secondary forests.

cladium jamaicense.name: Sawgrass
cladium jamaicense.desc: Dominates the marshes and grows best in slow-moving water. Dense stands hold few animals, but alligators nest in them.
cladium jamaicense.about: Cladium mariscus is a species of flowering plant in the sedge family known by the common names swamp sawgrass, great fen-sedge, saw-sedge or sawtooth sedge. Previously it was known as elk sedge.

cladocera and copepods.name: Zooplankton
cladocera and copepods.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae and feed paddlefish, gizzard shad and silver carp.
cladocera and copepods.about: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive.

cladonia.name: Lichens
cladonia.desc: Slow-growing ground lichens, including reindeer lichen, are a staple winter food for caribou, which dig down through snow to reach them.
cladonia.about: Cladonia rangiferina, also known as reindeer cup lichen, reindeer lichen (cf. Sw.

cladonia rangiferina.name: Reindeer lichen
cladonia rangiferina.desc: A slow-growing winter food for caribou.
cladonia rangiferina.about: Cladonia rangiferina, also known as reindeer cup lichen, reindeer lichen (cf. Sw.

cladonia, sphagnum and others.name: Lichens & mosses
cladonia, sphagnum and others.desc: Ground cover of the forest floor and peatland. Woodland caribou rely on lichens, especially in winter.
cladonia, sphagnum and others.about: A lichen ( LY-kən, UK also LITCH-ən) is a hybrid colony of algae or cyanobacteria living symbiotically among filaments of multiple fungus species, along with bacteria embedded in the cortex, or…

clarkia cylindrica.name: Speckled clarkia
clarkia cylindrica.desc: Speckled clarkia (Clarkia cylindrica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
clarkia cylindrica.about: Clarkia cylindrica is a species of flowering plant in the evening primrose family known by the common name speckled fairy fan, or speckled clarkia.

clarkia pulchella.name: Pinkfairies
clarkia pulchella.desc: Pinkfairies (Clarkia pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
clarkia pulchella.about: Clarkia pulchella, also known as pinkfairies, ragged robin, and deerhorn clarkia, is a species of flowering plant in the family Onagraceae.

clay floodplain soil.name: Clay floodplain soil
clay floodplain soil.desc: Heavy, poorly draining clays hold floodwater and trap sediment and nutrients that feed the swamp plants.

clay licks.name: Clay licks
clay licks.desc: Exposed riverbank clay where parrots and some mammals come to eat soil. Reasons are still debated.

claytonia rosea.name: Rocky Mountain spring-beauty
claytonia rosea.desc: Rocky Mountain spring-beauty (Claytonia rosea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 82 times near the park in GBIF.

claytonia sibirica.name: Candy-striped Claytonia
claytonia sibirica.desc: Candy-striped Claytonia (Claytonia sibirica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 547 times near the park in GBIF.
claytonia sibirica.about: Claytonia sibirica is a flowering plant in the family Montiaceae, commonly known as pink purslane, candy flower, Siberian spring beauty or Siberian miner's lettuce. A synonym is Montia sibirica.

claytonia virginica.name: Spring beauty
claytonia virginica.desc: Spring beauty (Claytonia virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
claytonia virginica.about: Claytonia virginica, the Virginia springbeauty, eastern spring beauty, grass-flower narrowleaf springbeauty or fairy spud, is an herbaceous perennial plant in the family Montiaceae.

claytosmunda claytoniana.name: Interrupted Fern
claytosmunda claytoniana.desc: Interrupted Fern (Claytosmunda claytoniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
claytosmunda claytoniana.about: Claytosmunda is a genus of fern. It has only one extant species, Claytosmunda claytoniana, the interrupted fern, native to Eastern Asia, Eastern United States, and Eastern Canada.

clear fast streams.name: Clear fast streams
clear fast streams.desc: Cold, oxygen-rich mountain streams with permanent flow are the home of aquatic insect larvae and of the desman.

clear mountain streams.name: Clear mountain streams
clear mountain streams.desc: Cold, fast, clean streams drain the granite uplands and support trout, otters and the rare Pyrenean desman.

clear, low-nutrient water.name: Clear, low-nutrient water
clear, low-nutrient water.desc: Ohrid is oligotrophic, with very low phosphorus and clarity to about 22 m, which suits its many endemic species.

clematis drummondii.name: Texas virgin's bower
clematis drummondii.desc: Texas virgin's bower (Clematis drummondii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
clematis drummondii.about: Clematis drummondii is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family, Ranunculaceae, that is native to the Southwestern United States (Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas) and northern Mexico.

clematis fremontii.name: Fremont's clematis
clematis fremontii.desc: Fremont's clematis (Clematis fremontii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
clematis fremontii.about: Clematis fremontii is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family known as Fremont's leather flower.

clematis terniflora.name: Sweet Autumn Clematis
clematis terniflora.desc: Sweet Autumn Clematis (Clematis terniflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.
clematis terniflora.about: Clematis terniflora (sweet autumn clematis, sweet autumn virginsbower) is a plant in the buttercup family, Ranunculaceae. It is native to northeastern Asia.

cleomella lutea.name: Spiny Caper
cleomella lutea.desc: Spiny Caper (Cleomella lutea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
cleomella lutea.about: Cleomella lutea is a species of flowering plant known by the common names yellow bee plant and yellow spiderflower.

cleomella serrulata.name: Rocky Mountain Beeweed
cleomella serrulata.desc: Rocky Mountain Beeweed (Cleomella serrulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
cleomella serrulata.about: Cleomella serrulata, commonly known as Rocky Mountain beeplant/beeweed, stinking-clover, bee spider-flower, skunk weed, Navajo spinach, and guaco, is a species of annual plant in the genus Cleomella.

clethrionomys glareolus.name: Bank vole
clethrionomys glareolus.desc: A small rodent of woodland floors eating seeds, berries and green plants; prey of wildcats and adders.
clethrionomys glareolus.about: The bank vole is a small vole with red-brown fur and some grey patches, with a tail about half as long as its body.

clinopodium coccineum.name: Scarlet calamint
clinopodium coccineum.desc: Scarlet calamint (Clinopodium coccineum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

clinopodium talladeganum.name: Talladega Wild Basil
clinopodium talladeganum.desc: Talladega Wild Basil (Clinopodium talladeganum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.
clinopodium talladeganum.about: Clinopodium talladeganum, commonly known as the Talladega wild basil, is a perennial vascular shrub in the mint family. C. talladeganum is endemic to a small area in three counties of Alabama.

clintonia andrewsiana.name: Red clintonia
clintonia andrewsiana.desc: Red clintonia (Clintonia andrewsiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 220 times near the park in GBIF.

clintonia borealis.name: Bluebead
clintonia borealis.desc: Bluebead (Clintonia borealis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
clintonia borealis.about: Clintonia borealis is a species of flowering plant in the lily family.

clitoria mariana.name: Butterfly-pea
clitoria mariana.desc: Butterfly-pea (Clitoria mariana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
clitoria mariana.about: Clitoria mariana, known by the common names butterfly pea and Atlantic pigeon wings, is a perennial herbaceous plant in the pea family, Fabaceae. The plant is native to the United States.

cloud and mist.name: Cloud and mist
cloud and mist.desc: Cloud wraps the montane forest and moorland, giving moisture to fog-dependent mosses and trees.

cloud and rain.name: Cloud and rain
cloud and rain.desc: Moist air rising over the high peaks feeds the humid broadleaf cloud forest and the streams that drain the massif.

clupea harengus.name: Atlantic herring
clupea harengus.desc: A schooling fish that eats copepods. It is food for seals and many seabirds.
clupea harengus.about: Atlantic herring is a herring in the family Clupeidae. It is one of the most abundant fish species in the world.

clupea pallasii.name: Pacific herring
clupea pallasii.desc: A schooling fish that feeds on plankton and is eaten by whales, seals, birds and salmon-eating predators.
clupea pallasii.about: The Pacific herring is a species of the herring family associated with the Pacific Ocean environment of North America and northeast Asia.

clupeidae.name: Small schooling fish
clupeidae.desc: Herring-like fish of warm bays that graze plankton. Pelicans elsewhere in the Caribbean rely on such fish.
clupeidae.about: Clupeidae is a small family of clupeiform ray-finned fishes, comprising the true herrings and sprats, inhabiting temperate marine habitats in both hemispheres.

cnidoscolus stimulosus.name: Bull-nettle
cnidoscolus stimulosus.desc: Bull-nettle (Cnidoscolus stimulosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.
cnidoscolus stimulosus.about: Cnidoscolus stimulosus, the bull nettle, spurge nettle, stinging nettle, tread-softly or finger rot, is a perennial herb covered with stinging hairs, native to southeastern North America.

coastal fog.name: Coastal fog
coastal fog.desc: Cold Benguela Current air makes thick fog for much of the year. Plants and beetles drink from it where almost no rain falls.

coastal sand dunes.name: Coastal sand dunes
coastal sand dunes.desc: A sandy barrier separates the lagoon from the sea; salt-tolerant plants and later pines settle and stabilise it.

coastal summer fog.name: Coastal summer fog
coastal summer fog.desc: Wikipedia says fog supplies a large share of the water redwoods use, and that its summer consistency matters more to tree health than rainfall.

coccinella septempunctata.name: Seven-spot Ladybird
coccinella septempunctata.desc: Seven-spot Ladybird (Coccinella septempunctata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
coccinella septempunctata.about: Coccinella septempunctata, commonly known as the seven-spot ladybird (in North America, seven-spotted ladybug, seven-spotted lady beetle), often abbreviated C-7, is a carnivorous beetle native to…

coccoloba diversifolia.name: Pigeon Plum
coccoloba diversifolia.desc: Pigeon Plum (Coccoloba diversifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 244 times near the park in GBIF.

coccoloba uvifera.name: Seagrape
coccoloba uvifera.desc: Seagrape (Coccoloba uvifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.
coccoloba uvifera.about: Coccoloba uvifera is a species of tree and flowering plant in the buckwheat family, Polygonaceae. Its common names include seagrape and baygrape.

coccothraustes coccothraustes.name: Hawfinch
coccothraustes coccothraustes.desc: A heavy-billed finch able to crack hard seeds and fruit stones, including hornbeam and beech seeds.
coccothraustes coccothraustes.about: The hawfinch is a passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is the only extant species placed in the genus Coccothraustes.

coccyzus longirostris.name: Hispaniolan lizard-cuckoo
coccyzus longirostris.desc: A large forest cuckoo that hunts lizards and other small animals in the canopy.
coccyzus longirostris.about: The Hispaniolan lizard cuckoo is a species of bird in the tribe Phaenicophaeini, subfamily Cuculinae of the cuckoo family Cuculidae.

cochemiea grahamii.name: Graham's nipple cactus
cochemiea grahamii.desc: Graham's nipple cactus (Cochemiea grahamii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 147 times near the park in GBIF.

cocos nucifera.name: Coconut palm
cocos nucifera.desc: A coastal palm found around the shores of the islands. Flying foxes and rats eat its fruit.
cocos nucifera.about: The coconut is a member of the palm family (Arecaceae) and the only living species of the genus Cocos.

coenonympha california.name: Common Ringlet
coenonympha california.desc: Common Ringlet (Coenonympha california): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
coenonympha california.about: Coenonympha california, also known as the California ringlet or common ringlet, is a species of butterfly native to North America.

coenonympha tullia.name: Large Heath
coenonympha tullia.desc: Large Heath (Coenonympha tullia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
coenonympha tullia.about: Coenonympha tullia, the large heath or common ringlet, is a butterfly in the family Nymphalidae.

coereba flaveola.name: Bananaquit
coereba flaveola.desc: The most recorded bird near the park; a small nectar, fruit and insect eater that GloBI records feeding on Miconia fruit.
coereba flaveola.about: The bananaquit is a species of passerine bird in the tanager family Thraupidae.

colaptes auratus.name: Northern Flicker
colaptes auratus.desc: Northern Flicker (Colaptes auratus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
colaptes auratus.about: The northern flicker or common flicker is a medium-sized bird of the woodpecker family.

cold and winter snow.name: Cold and winter snow
cold and winter snow.desc: High summits are cold, and snow can lie on the peaks in winter. Cold sets the upper limit of trees and shapes the subalpine shrubs and cane.

cold deep water.name: Cold deep water
cold deep water.desc: Cold bottom water below the thermocline is the home of Mysis, Diporeia and lake trout.

cold dry continental climate.name: Cold dry continental climate
cold dry continental climate.desc: Cold winters and dry air shape the semi-desert, steppe and spruce zones, so water supply sets where plants can grow.

cold forest and steppe soil.name: Cold forest and steppe soil
cold forest and steppe soil.desc: Young glacial soils that recycle nutrients slowly in the cold.

cold gulf of maine water.name: Cold Gulf of Maine water
cold gulf of maine water.desc: Cold, nutrient-bearing water along the coast feeds plankton and seaweed.

cold nights & frost.name: Cold nights & frost
cold nights & frost.desc: On the high plateaus frost kills forest seedlings, which helps keep grassland open between shola patches.

cold nutrient-rich water.name: Cold nutrient-rich water
cold nutrient-rich water.desc: Cool, nutrient-bearing Atlantic water feeds plankton, and plankton feed the fish that the seals depend on.

cold soils and nutrients.name: Cold soils and nutrients
cold soils and nutrients.desc: Permafrost and cold slow decay, so nutrients recycle slowly. Salmon carcasses add marine nitrogen along streams.

cold, nutrient-rich current.name: Cold, nutrient-rich current
cold, nutrient-rich current.desc: Cold water of the Falkland Current flows north along the Patagonian Shelf and carries nutrients that feed plankton and kelp.

cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters.name: Cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters
cold, nutrient-rich gulf waters.desc: The sheltered gulfs of the peninsula hold the plankton and fish that the whales, seals and penguins depend on.

cold, nutrient-rich water.name: Cold, nutrient-rich water
cold, nutrient-rich water.desc: Cold water holds nutrients that feed spring blooms when sunlight returns.

cold, short growing season.name: Cold, short growing season
cold, short growing season.desc: Harsh weather and a brief summer shape which plants can grow and when animals can feed.

cold, snowy winters.name: Cold, snowy winters
cold, snowy winters.desc: Deep cold and snow shape which plants survive and push animals such as ibex to lower slopes in winter.

coleogyne ramosissima.name: Blackbrush
coleogyne ramosissima.desc: A dense, dark shrub that is among the most recorded plants of the park and a common cover on its higher, drier ground.
coleogyne ramosissima.about: Coleogyne ramosissima or blackbrush, is a low lying, dark grayish-green, aromatic, spiny, perennial, soft wooded shrub, native to the deserts of the southwestern United States.

coleomegilla maculata.name: Spotted lady beetle
coleomegilla maculata.desc: Spotted lady beetle (Coleomegilla maculata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

coleoptera.name: Wood-boring beetles
coleoptera.desc: Beetle grubs tunnelling in trees. They are the main food of the Magellanic woodpecker.
coleoptera.about: Beetles are insects that form the order Coleoptera (), in the superorder Holometabola. Their front pair of wings are hardened into wing-cases, elytra, distinguishing them from most other insects.

colias eurytheme.name: Alfalfa Butterfly
colias eurytheme.desc: Alfalfa Butterfly (Colias eurytheme): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

colias fieldii.name: Dark clouded yellow
colias fieldii.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes. Many butterflies fly over the plateau meadows in spring and summer.
colias fieldii.about: Colias fieldii, the dark clouded yellow, is a butterfly in the family Pieridae. It is found in southern Iran, India, southern China, Indochina, and Ussuri.

colias philodice.name: Clouded Sulphur
colias philodice.desc: Clouded Sulphur (Colias philodice): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
colias philodice.about: Colias philodice, the common sulphur or clouded sulphur, is a North American butterfly in the family Pieridae, subfamily Coliadinae.

collembola.name: Leaf-litter invertebrates
collembola.desc: Springtails, mites and other tiny animals of the leaf litter that feed on decaying leaves and fungi.
collembola.about: Springtails (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.

colletes inaequalis.name: Unequal Cellophane Bee
colletes inaequalis.desc: Unequal Cellophane Bee (Colletes inaequalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

colletes kincaidii.name: Kincaid's Cellophane Bee
colletes kincaidii.desc: Kincaid's Cellophane Bee (Colletes kincaidii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.
colletes kincaidii.about: Colletes kincaidii, or Kincaid's cellophane bee, is a species of hymenopteran in the family Colletidae. It is found in North America.

colletes thoracicus.name: Rufous-backed Cellophane Bee
colletes thoracicus.desc: Rufous-backed Cellophane Bee (Colletes thoracicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

collinsia heterophylla.name: Chinese-houses
collinsia heterophylla.desc: Chinese-houses (Collinsia heterophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 818 times near the park in GBIF.

collinsia verna.name: Spring blue eyed Mary
collinsia verna.desc: Spring blue eyed Mary (Collinsia verna): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
collinsia verna.about: Collinsia verna, or blue-eyed Mary, is a winter annual that is native to the eastern and central parts of North America but has become endangered in the states of New York and Tennessee.

collomia linearis.name: Narrow-leaf mountain-trumpet
collomia linearis.desc: Narrow-leaf mountain-trumpet (Collomia linearis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
collomia linearis.about: Collomia linearis is a species of flowering plant in the phlox family known by the common names tiny trumpet and slenderleaf collomia.

colobus angolensis.name: Ruwenzori colobus
colobus angolensis.desc: A leaf-eating monkey of the park. It also takes fruit and flowers, and its digestion lets it use food other primates cannot.
colobus angolensis.about: The Angola colobus, Angolan black-and-white colobus, or Angolan colobus is a primate species of Old World monkey belonging to the genus Colobus.

colobus guereza.name: Mantled guereza
colobus guereza.desc: A leaf-eating black-and-white monkey with a multi-chambered stomach for digesting tough plant matter.
colobus guereza.about: The mantled guereza, also known simply as the guereza, historically the eastern black-and-white colobus, and Abyssinian black-and-white colobus, is a black-and-white colobus, a type of Old World…

colobus satanas.name: Black colobus
colobus satanas.desc: A leaf- and seed-eating monkey of Central African forest, named among the primates of Monte Alen National Park.
colobus satanas.about: The black colobus, or satanic black colobus, is a species of Old World monkey belonging to the genus Colobus. The species is found in a small area of western central Africa.

colophospermum mopane.name: Mopane
colophospermum mopane.desc: The most common tree in Etosha, making up most of its trees. Elephants, giraffes and antelopes browse the leaves.
colophospermum mopane.about: Colophospermum mopane, commonly called mopane, mopani, butterfly tree, turpentine tree, or balsam tree, is a tree in the legume family (Fabaceae), that grows in hot, dry, low-lying areas, 200 to…

colossoma macropomum.name: Tambaqui
colossoma macropomum.desc: A big fish that swims into flooded forest to eat fallen fruit and seeds.
colossoma macropomum.about: The tambaqui is a large species of freshwater fish in the family Serrasalmidae. It is native to tropical South America, but kept in aquaculture and introduced elsewhere.

coluber constrictor.name: Black racer
coluber constrictor.desc: Black racer (Coluber constrictor): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

columba arquatrix.name: Rameron pigeon
columba arquatrix.desc: A fruit-eating forest pigeon. GloBI records it eating African juniper.
columba arquatrix.about: The African olive pigeon or Rameron pigeon is a pigeon which is a resident breeding bird in much of eastern and southern Africa from Ethiopia to the Cape.

columba janthina.name: Japanese wood pigeon
columba janthina.desc: A dark pigeon of island forests that feeds mainly on fruits, berries, leaves, buds and conifer seeds.
columba janthina.about: The black wood pigeon or Japanese wood pigeon is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

columba livia.name: Rock Pigeon
columba livia.desc: Rock Pigeon (Columba livia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2,362 times near the park in GBIF.
columba livia.about: The rock dove, also known as the common pigeon or rock pigeon (but see also Petrophassa), is a member of the bird family Columbidae (doves and pigeons).

columba palumbus.name: Common wood pigeon
columba palumbus.desc: A large pigeon that feeds mostly on seeds, buds and berries.
columba palumbus.about: The common wood pigeon, also known simply as the wood pigeon, is a large pigeon native to the western Palearctic.

comandra umbellata.name: Bastard Toadflax
comandra umbellata.desc: Bastard Toadflax (Comandra umbellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

comephorus spp..name: Golomyanka (oilfish)
comephorus spp..desc: Translucent, live-bearing deep-water fish and the most numerous fish in the lake. They rise toward the surface at night to feed on copepods and amphipods.
comephorus spp..about: Comephorus, known as the golomyankas or Baikal oilfish, are a genus comprising two species of peculiar sculpin fishes endemic to Lake Baikal in Russia.

commelina erecta.name: Erect Dayflower
commelina erecta.desc: Erect Dayflower (Commelina erecta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
commelina erecta.about: Commelina erecta, commonly known as white mouth dayflower, slender dayflower, or widow's tears. C. erecta is a blue flower often recognized by its two large blue petals and smaller white petal.

commelina virginica.name: Virginia Dayflower
commelina virginica.desc: Virginia Dayflower (Commelina virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
commelina virginica.about: Commelina virginica, commonly known as the Virginia dayflower, is a perennial herbaceous plant in the dayflower family.

comptonia peregrina.name: Sweet Fern
comptonia peregrina.desc: Sweet Fern (Comptonia peregrina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
comptonia peregrina.about: Comptonia peregrina is a species of flowering plant in the family Myricaceae native to eastern North America.

condalia ericoides.name: Javelina bush
condalia ericoides.desc: Javelina bush (Condalia ericoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

conicosia pugioniformis.name: Narrow-leaf iceplant
conicosia pugioniformis.desc: Narrow-leaf iceplant (Conicosia pugioniformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 157 times near the park in GBIF.

conifers, shrubs and berries.name: Taiga shore forest
conifers, shrubs and berries.desc: Forest and shrub cover around the lake that feeds and shelters shore animals such as bears and sables.
conifers, shrubs and berries.about: Taiga or tayga, also known as boreal forest or snow forest, is a biome characterized by coniferous forests consisting mostly of pines, spruces, and larches.

conium maculatum.name: Hemlock
conium maculatum.desc: Hemlock (Conium maculatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 49 times near the park in GBIF.

connecticut river discharge.name: River flow
connecticut river discharge.desc: Spring floods bring fresh water, silt and nutrients down to the estuary and Long Island Sound.

connochaetes taurinus.name: Blue wildebeest
connochaetes taurinus.desc: More than a million migrate in a loop around the ecosystem, following the rains and the new grass.
connochaetes taurinus.about: The blue wildebeest, also called the common wildebeest, white-bearded gnu or brindled gnu, is a large antelope and one of the two species of wildebeest.

conocarpus erectus.name: Button Mangrove
conocarpus erectus.desc: Button Mangrove (Conocarpus erectus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 227 times near the park in GBIF.

conoclinium coelestinum.name: Blue mistflower
conoclinium coelestinum.desc: Blue mistflower (Conoclinium coelestinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
conoclinium coelestinum.about: Conoclinium coelestinum, commonly known as blue mistflower, mistflower, wild ageratum, or blue boneset, is a North American species of herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

conopholis americana.name: Squawroot
conopholis americana.desc: Squawroot (Conopholis americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

conophthorus ponderosae.name: Lodgepole cone beetle
conophthorus ponderosae.desc: Lodgepole cone beetle (Conophthorus ponderosae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
conophthorus ponderosae.about: Conophthorus ponderosae, known generally as the lodgepole cone beetle or sugar pinecone beetle, is a species of typical bark beetle in the family Curculionidae. It is found in North America.

conraua goliath.name: Goliath frog
conraua goliath.desc: The largest frog in the world; it lives in fast rivers in the southern part of the park and is protected from hunting. It eats insects and other small animals.
conraua goliath.about: The goliath frog, otherwise known commonly as the giant slippery frog and the goliath bullfrog, is a species of frog in the family Conrauidae. The goliath frog is the largest living frog.

contopus virens.name: Eastern Wood-Pewee
contopus virens.desc: Eastern Wood-Pewee (Contopus virens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

convolvulus arvensis.name: Field Bindweed
convolvulus arvensis.desc: Field Bindweed (Convolvulus arvensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
convolvulus arvensis.about: Convolvulus arvensis, or field bindweed, is a species of bindweed in the Convolvulaceae native to Europe and Asia.

cool maritime climate.name: Cool maritime climate
cool maritime climate.desc: A cool, wet oceanic climate suits cool temperate rainforest, which can regenerate without large catastrophic events.

cool mountain air.name: Cool mountain air
cool mountain air.desc: Temperature falls with height, so forest type changes from lowland to montane oak, rhododendron and conifer zones.

cool nutrient-rich ocean water.name: Cool nutrient-rich ocean water
cool nutrient-rich ocean water.desc: Cool, nutrient-bearing water from the open Pacific supports plankton, kelp and the animals that feed on them.

cool nutrient-rich water.name: Cool nutrient-rich water
cool nutrient-rich water.desc: Cold, nutrient-bearing water from the deep ocean feeds the algae and plankton of the bay.

cool ocean nutrients.name: Cool ocean nutrients
cool ocean nutrients.desc: Cool, nutrient-rich water from the Pacific feeds plankton blooms along the coast. This is general ecology and illustrative.

cool upland air.name: Cool upland air
cool upland air.desc: Cooler air at high elevation keeps mosquitoes and avian malaria down, so it is a refuge for native forest birds.

cool water temperature.name: Cool water temperature
cool water temperature.desc: Giant kelp does best in cool water, mostly below about 21 C. Warm El Nino water has been known to kill it.

cool, wet mountain climate.name: Cool, wet mountain climate
cool, wet mountain climate.desc: Rain and snow on the Carpathian slopes keep the beech and fir forest moist.

copadichromis.name: Utaka
copadichromis.desc: Open-water cichlids that feed in schools on zooplankton.
copadichromis.about: Copadichromis is a genus of haplochromine cichlids endemic to Lake Malawi in Eastern Africa.

copepoda.name: Zooplankton
copepoda.desc: Tiny animals of the plankton that graze phytoplankton and feed corals and fish.
copepoda.about: Copepods are a group of small crustaceans found in nearly every freshwater and saltwater habitat.

copepoda and relatives.name: Zooplankton
copepoda and relatives.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae in the lakes. Sockeye salmon feed extensively on them.
copepoda and relatives.about: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive.

copepods and larvae.name: Zooplankton
copepods and larvae.desc: Tiny animals that graze phytoplankton. Young menhaden and bay anchovies feed on them.
copepods and larvae.about: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive.

copepods and water fleas.name: Zooplankton
copepods and water fleas.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae. Alewife and juvenile fish eat them, and so do filtering mussels.
copepods and water fleas.about: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive.

copernicia alba.name: Caranday palm
copernicia alba.desc: A fan palm of seasonally flooded plains. GloBI records its fruit or foliage eaten by howler monkeys, maned wolves and many birds.
copernicia alba.about: Copernicia alba is a South American species of palm tree, which is found in the Humid Chaco ecoregion in Bolivia, Paraguay, Colombia, Brazil and Argentina (especially the province of Formosa, and…

copestylum avidum.name: Yellow-spotted Bromeliad Fly
copestylum avidum.desc: Yellow-spotted Bromeliad Fly (Copestylum avidum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 38 times near the park in GBIF.

coragyps atratus.name: Black vulture
coragyps atratus.desc: Black Vulture (Coragyps atratus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
coragyps atratus.about: The black vulture, also known as the American black vulture, Mexican vulture, zopilote, urubu, or gallinazo, is a bird in the New World vulture family whose range extends from the northeastern United…

corallorhiza wisteriana.name: Spring coralroot
corallorhiza wisteriana.desc: Spring coralroot (Corallorhiza wisteriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
corallorhiza wisteriana.about: Corallorhiza wisteriana, the spring coralroot or Wister's coralroot, is a species of coralroot orchid. It is widespread through much of Mexico as well as parts of the United States.

corallus hortulana.name: Amazon tree boa
corallus hortulana.desc: Eats a wide range of prey, including frogs, lizards, birds and mammals such as bats. GloBI records it eating a sac-winged bat.
corallus hortulana.about: Corallus hortulana, previously known as Corallus hortulanus, and commonly known as the Amazon tree boa, common tree boa, garden tree boa, and macabrel, is a boa species found in South America.

corallus ruschenbergerii.name: Trinidad tree boa
corallus ruschenbergerii.desc: Tree-climbing snake reported in the swamp. GloBI records it eating green iguanas.
