corallus ruschenbergerii.about: Corallus ruschenbergerii, commonly known as the Central American tree boa, common tree boa, and Trinidad tree boa, is a boa species found in lower Central America and northern South America.

coregonus clupeaformis.name: Lake whitefish
coregonus clupeaformis.desc: Young fish eat plankton and larger ones eat bottom animals like snails and mussels. Its condition fell as Diporeia declined.
coregonus clupeaformis.about: The lake whitefish is a species of freshwater whitefish from North America.

coregonus migratorius.name: Omul
coregonus migratorius.desc: An endemic whitefish and the lake's main commercial fish. It eats zooplankton, algae and some small fish, and spawns in the rivers feeding the lake.
coregonus migratorius.about: The omul, Coregonus migratorius, also known as Baikal omul (Russian: байкальский омуль), is a whitefish species of the salmon family endemic to Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia.

coreopsis rosea.name: Pink Tickseed
coreopsis rosea.desc: Pink Tickseed (Coreopsis rosea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
coreopsis rosea.about: Coreopsis rosea, known as the pink tickseed, is a North American species of Coreopsis in the family Asteraceae.

coreopsis tripteris.name: Tall coreopsis
coreopsis tripteris.desc: Tall coreopsis (Coreopsis tripteris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

corispermum villosum.name: Hairy bugseed
corispermum villosum.desc: Hairy bugseed (Corispermum villosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

cornufer vitiensis.name: Fiji tree frog
cornufer vitiensis.desc: A small native frog of forest floors and streams, hunting insects at night.
cornufer vitiensis.about: Platymantis vitiensis is a species of frog in the family Ceratobatrachidae. It is one of two endemic frogs in Fiji, the other being the related Cornufer vitianus.

cornus amomum.name: Silky cornel
cornus amomum.desc: Silky cornel (Cornus amomum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus canadensis.name: Canadian Bunchberry
cornus canadensis.desc: Canadian Bunchberry (Cornus canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
cornus canadensis.about: Cornus canadensis is a species of flowering plant in the dogwood family Cornaceae, native to eastern Asia and North America.

cornus drummondii.name: Drummond's dogwood
cornus drummondii.desc: Drummond's dogwood (Cornus drummondii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus florida.name: Flowering Dogwood
cornus florida.desc: Flowering Dogwood (Cornus florida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
cornus florida.about: Cornus florida, the flowering dogwood or American dogwood, is a species of flowering tree in the family Cornaceae native to eastern North America and northern Mexico.

cornus foemina.name: Stiff dogwood
cornus foemina.desc: Stiff dogwood (Cornus foemina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus mas.name: Cornelian cherry
cornus mas.desc: A shrub or small tree of forest edges and clearings with early spring flowers and edible red fruit.
cornus mas.about: Cornelian cherry, also known as the European cornel, is a species of shrub or small tree in the dogwood family Cornaceae native to Western Europe, Southern Europe, and Southwestern Asia.

cornus nuttallii.name: Nuttall's dogwood
cornus nuttallii.desc: Nuttall's dogwood (Cornus nuttallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
cornus nuttallii.about: Cornus nuttallii, the Pacific dogwood, western dogwood, or mountain dogwood, is a species of dogwood native to western North America. The tree's name used by Halkomelem-speaking nations is Kwi’txulhp.

cornus rugosa.name: Round-leaf dogwood
cornus rugosa.desc: Round-leaf dogwood (Cornus rugosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus sericea.name: Red-osier Dogwood
cornus sericea.desc: Red-osier Dogwood (Cornus sericea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

cornus unalaschkensis.name: Unalaska bunchberry
cornus unalaschkensis.desc: Unalaska bunchberry (Cornus unalaschkensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
cornus unalaschkensis.about: Cornus × unalaschkensis is a species of flowering plant in the Cornaceae, the dogwood family.

coronilla varia.name: Crown Vetch
coronilla varia.desc: Crown Vetch (Coronilla varia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
coronilla varia.about: Securigera varia, commonly known as crownvetch or purple crown vetch, is a low-growing legume vine.

corvus albicollis.name: White-necked raven
corvus albicollis.desc: Large crow named on the park page as a bird of the mountain; it scavenges carrion and eats insects.
corvus albicollis.about: The white-necked raven, also known as the collared raven, is a species of raven native to eastern and southern Africa.

corvus brachyrhynchos.name: American Crow
corvus brachyrhynchos.desc: American Crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 138 times near the park in GBIF.
corvus brachyrhynchos.about: The American crow is a large passerine bird species of the family Corvidae. It is a common bird found throughout much of North America, only absent from the tundra biome.

corvus corax.name: Common raven
corvus corax.desc: Common Raven (Corvus corax): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 447 times near the park in GBIF.
corvus corax.about: The common raven or northern raven is a large all-black passerine bird. It is the most widely distributed of all corvids, found across the Northern Hemisphere.

corvus cornix.name: Hooded crow
corvus cornix.desc: An opportunistic bird that cleans up carrion left by larger predators.
corvus cornix.about: The hooded crow, also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow in the genus Corvus.

corvus corone.name: Carrion crow
corvus corone.desc: Omnivorous scavenger and predator of small animals; also eats berries and seeds.
corvus corone.about: The carrion crow is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.

corvus crassirostris.name: Thick-billed raven
corvus crassirostris.desc: A large highland raven that is commonly seen in the park.
corvus crassirostris.about: The thick-billed raven is a large passerine bird in the family Corvidae. It is endemic to the Horn of Africa, including parts of Ethiopia, Eritrea, Sudan, and Somalia.

corvus cryptoleucus.name: Chihuahuan raven
corvus cryptoleucus.desc: A scavenging crow that eats insects, small animals and carrion in open desert country.
corvus cryptoleucus.about: The Chihuahuan raven is a species in the family Corvidae that is native to the United States and Mexico.

corvus macrorhynchos.name: Large-billed crow
corvus macrorhynchos.desc: An opportunistic bird that feeds at carcasses; one GloBI record shows it eating chital.
corvus macrorhynchos.about: The large-billed crow, formerly referred to widely as the jungle crow, is a widespread Asian species of crow.

corvus orru.name: Torresian crow
corvus orru.desc: Opportunistic scavenger and omnivore, often at carcasses.
corvus orru.about: The Torresian crow, also called the Australian crow or Papuan crow, is a passerine bird in the crow family native to the north and west of Australia and nearby islands in Indonesia and Papua New…

corvus ossifragus.name: Fish Crow
corvus ossifragus.desc: Fish Crow (Corvus ossifragus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 99 times near the park in GBIF.

corvus ruficollis.name: Brown-necked raven
corvus ruficollis.desc: A desert raven that scavenges carcasses and hunts small animals and eggs.
corvus ruficollis.about: The brown-necked raven is a larger bird (52–56 cm in length) than the carrion crow though not as large as the common raven.

corvus tasmanicus.name: Forest raven
corvus tasmanicus.desc: The most-recorded bird near the site. It feeds on carrion such as dead wallabies and pademelons.
corvus tasmanicus.about: The forest raven, also commonly known as the Tasmanian raven, is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae native to Tasmania and parts of southern Victoria, such as Wilsons Promontory and Portland.

corydalis curvisiliqua.name: Curvepod Fumewort
corydalis curvisiliqua.desc: Curvepod Fumewort (Corydalis curvisiliqua): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

corydalis scouleri.name: Scoulers corydalis
corydalis scouleri.desc: Scoulers corydalis (Corydalis scouleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

corylus americana.name: American Hazelnut
corylus americana.desc: American Hazelnut (Corylus americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
corylus americana.about: Corylus americana, the American hazelnut or American hazel, is a species of deciduous shrub in the genus Corylus, native to the eastern and central United States and extreme southern parts of eastern…

corylus avellana.name: Common hazel
corylus avellana.desc: A very widely recorded understory shrub whose nuts are eaten by boar, squirrels and mice.
corylus avellana.about: Corylus avellana, the common hazel, is a species of flowering plant in the birch family Betulaceae. The shrubs usually grow 3–8 metres (10–26 feet) tall.

corylus colurna.name: Turkish hazel
corylus colurna.desc: A Tertiary relict tree named by Wikipedia among the park's notable plants. Its nuts are food for small forest animals.
corylus colurna.about: Corylus colurna, the Turkish hazel, Byzantine hazel or Constantinople Hazel, is a species of hazel (Corylus) in the birch family (Betulaceae).

corylus cornuta.name: Beaked Hazel
corylus cornuta.desc: Beaked Hazel (Corylus cornuta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
corylus cornuta.about: Corylus cornuta, the beaked hazelnut (or just beaked hazel), is a deciduous shrubby hazel with two subspecies found throughout most of North America.

corymbia papuana.name: Ghost gum
corymbia papuana.desc: A eucalypt of open, grassy woodland. Its pale cream flowers appear around October to November and, as a Myrtaceae tree, offer nectar and pollen to birds and bats.
corymbia papuana.about: Corymbia papuana, commonly known as ghost gum, is a species of evergreen tree native to New Guinea, some Torres Strait Islands and the northern part of the Cape York Peninsula in Australia.

corynorhinus townsendii.name: Townsend's big-eared bat
corynorhinus townsendii.desc: Wikipedia says it feeds almost entirely on moths. Pinnacles lists it as breeding in its talus caves, which close during pupping season.
corynorhinus townsendii.about: Townsend's big-eared bat is a species of vesper bat.

corythaeola cristata.name: Great blue turaco
corythaeola cristata.desc: A large forest bird that eats fruit, flowers and leaves, and spreads seeds in its droppings.
corythaeola cristata.about: The great blue turaco is a bird species of the family Musophagidae. At 70–76 cm (28–30 in) in length, it is the largest species of turaco.

costus scaber.name: Spiral ginger
costus scaber.desc: A forest-understorey plant with showy flowers; GloBI records show birds such as the bananaquit feeding on it.
costus scaber.about: Costus scaber is a species of plant in the family Costaceae. Its native range is Mexico to Tropical America.

cotinis nitida.name: Common Green June Beetle
cotinis nitida.desc: Common Green June Beetle (Cotinis nitida): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.
cotinis nitida.about: Cotinis nitida, commonly known as the green June beetle, June bug or June beetle, is a beetle of the family Scarabaeidae.

cottocomephorus spp..name: Baikal sculpins
cottocomephorus spp..desc: Small endemic bottom and open-water fish. Baikal seals eat them, especially in autumn.
cottocomephorus spp..about: The Cottidae are a family of fish in the superfamily Cottoidea, the sculpins.

cotula coronopifolia.name: Buttonweed
cotula coronopifolia.desc: Buttonweed (Cotula coronopifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
cotula coronopifolia.about: Cotula coronopifolia is a species of flowering plant in the aster family (Asteraceae). Commonly known as brass buttons, golden buttons, and buttonweed, it is native to southern Africa.

coula edulis.name: Coula nut tree
coula edulis.desc: A rainforest tree with very hard nuts. Taï chimpanzees crack such nuts open with stones and branches.
coula edulis.about: Coula is a monotypic genus of flowering plants. It contains the sole species Coula edulis, a tree native to western and west-central tropical Africa, ranging from Guinea to the Democratic Republic of…

crangon crangon.name: Brown shrimp
crangon crangon.desc: A small shrimp that moves onto the flats to feed. Young plaice eat shrimp, and seals take them occasionally.
crangon crangon.about: Crangon crangon is a species of caridean shrimp found across the northeastern Atlantic Ocean.

craspedocephalus malabaricus.name: Malabar pit viper
craspedocephalus malabaricus.desc: An ambush snake of Ghats forests that takes frogs, lizards and small mammals.
craspedocephalus malabaricus.about: Craspedocephalus malabaricus, commonly known as Malabar pit viper, Malabar rock pit viper, or rock viper, is a venomous pit viper species endemic to the high-moderate elevations of Western Ghats of…

crassostrea.name: Oysters
crassostrea.desc: Filter-feeding molluscs. Wikipedia lists oysters among the shellfish of the bay, and they strain phytoplankton from the water.
crassostrea.about: Crassostrea is a genus of true oysters (family Ostreidae) containing some of the most important oysters used for food.

crassostrea virginica.name: Eastern oyster
crassostrea virginica.desc: A filter feeder that strains plankton from the water, clearing it as it feeds. Its reefs give hard surfaces and shelter to many other species.
crassostrea virginica.about: The eastern oyster—also called the Atlantic oyster, American oyster, or East Coast oyster—is a species of true oyster native to eastern North and South America.

crataegus crus-galli.name: Cockspurthorn
crataegus crus-galli.desc: Cockspurthorn (Crataegus crus-galli): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
crataegus crus-galli.about: Crataegus crus-galli is a species of hawthorn known by the common names cockspur hawthorn, cockspur thorn, Newcastle hawthorne, Newcastle thorn, hog apple.

crataegus macrosperma.name: Bigfruit Hawthorn
crataegus macrosperma.desc: Bigfruit Hawthorn (Crataegus macrosperma): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 134 times near the park in GBIF.

crataegus marshallii.name: Parsley-hawthorn
crataegus marshallii.desc: Parsley-hawthorn (Crataegus marshallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

crataegus mollis.name: Red haw
crataegus mollis.desc: Red haw (Crataegus mollis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

crataegus ouachitensis.name: Ouachita hawthorn
crataegus ouachitensis.desc: Ouachita hawthorn (Crataegus ouachitensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.

crataegus spathulata.name: Littlehip hawthorn
crataegus spathulata.desc: Littlehip hawthorn (Crataegus spathulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

crataegus viridis.name: Southernthorn
crataegus viridis.desc: Southernthorn (Crataegus viridis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
crataegus viridis.about: Crataegus viridis, the green hawthorn or southern thorn, is a species of hawthorn that is native to the southeastern United States. The tree tends to grow to be 5–15 meters tall.

crater lake water.name: Crater Lake water
crater lake water.desc: A very deep caldera lake with no streams flowing in or out; its water comes from rain and snow falling directly on it.

crepis occidentalis.name: Gray hawk's-beard
crepis occidentalis.desc: Gray hawk's-beard (Crepis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
crepis occidentalis.about: Crepis occidentalis is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names western hawksbeard, or largeflower hawksbeard.

cricetomys gambianus.name: Gambian pouched rat
cricetomys gambianus.desc: A large forest-edge rodent that eats fruit, nuts and other plant matter and is prey for many carnivores.
cricetomys gambianus.about: The Gambian pouched rat, also commonly known as the African giant pouched rat, is a species of nocturnal pouched rat of the giant pouched rat genus Cricetomys, in the family Nesomyidae.

cricetulus migratorius.name: Gray dwarf hamster
cricetulus migratorius.desc: A small seed- and plant-eating rodent recorded near the park. GloBI records red foxes eating it.
cricetulus migratorius.about: The grey dwarf hamster, grey hamster or migratory hamster is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae.

cricetus cricetus.name: European hamster
cricetus cricetus.desc: A burrowing rodent of grassland and fields that eats seeds and plants and is taken by foxes and many raptors.
cricetus cricetus.about: The European hamster, also known as the common hamster, is the only living species of hamster in the genus Cricetus.

crocanthemum corymbosum.name: Pinebarren sun-rose
crocanthemum corymbosum.desc: Pinebarren sun-rose (Crocanthemum corymbosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

crocodylus acutus.name: American crocodile
crocodylus acutus.desc: A threatened mangrove-shore predator found in Biscayne Bay; adults eat fish, crabs and small mammals.
crocodylus acutus.about: The American crocodile is a species of crocodilian found in the Neotropics.

crocodylus johnstoni.name: Freshwater crocodile
crocodylus johnstoni.desc: Smaller crocodile of billabongs and creeks. It eats insects and fish, and ambushes larger prey like wallabies. Cane toads have hit its numbers hard.
crocodylus johnstoni.about: The freshwater crocodile, also known commonly as the Australian freshwater crocodile, Johnstone's crocodile, Johnstone river crocodile and the freshie, is a species of crocodile native to the…

crocodylus niloticus.name: Nile crocodile
crocodylus niloticus.desc: Ambushes fish and animals at the water's edge, including hippo calves. Wikipedia notes crocodiles may threaten gorillas at Mbeli Bai.
crocodylus niloticus.about: The Nile crocodile is a large crocodilian native to freshwater habitats in Africa, where it is present in 26 countries.

crocodylus palustris.name: Mugger crocodile
crocodylus palustris.desc: Eats mainly fish but also snakes, birds and mammals up to chital size. Shares the Rapti and Narayani with gharials.
crocodylus palustris.about: The mugger crocodile is a medium-sized broad-snouted crocodile, also known as mugger and marsh crocodile.

crocodylus porosus.name: Saltwater crocodile
crocodylus porosus.desc: An ambush predator that eats mud crabs, fish and large mammals such as deer and boar.
crocodylus porosus.about: The saltwater crocodile is a crocodilian native to saltwater habitats, brackish wetlands and freshwater rivers from India's east coast across Southeast Asia and the Sundaland to northern Australia…

crocodylus rhombifer.name: Cuban crocodile
crocodylus rhombifer.desc: Endemic crocodile whose only wild population is in Zapata Swamp. Adults eat small mammals, fish and turtles.
crocodylus rhombifer.about: The Cuban crocodile is a small-medium species of crocodile endemic to Cuba. Typical length is 2.1–2.3 m (6 ft 11 in – 7 ft 7 in) and typical weight 70–80 kg (150–180 lb).

crocodylus siamensis.name: Siamese crocodile
crocodylus siamensis.desc: Critically endangered freshwater crocodile that eats fish and snakes plus amphibians and small mammals.
crocodylus siamensis.about: The Siamese crocodile is a medium-sized freshwater crocodile native to Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam and Kalimantan in Indonesia. It is critically endangered.

crocodylus suchus.name: West African crocodile
crocodylus suchus.desc: Large reptile reported in large numbers in the sanctuary; it is mainly a fish-eating ambush predator of the river and lakes.
crocodylus suchus.about: The West African crocodile, desert crocodile, or sacred crocodile is a species of crocodile related to, and often confused with, the larger Nile crocodile (C. niloticus).

crocothemis servilia.name: Scarlet skimmer
crocothemis servilia.desc: A dragonfly recorded in the marshes, hunting smaller flying insects over open water.
crocothemis servilia.about: The scarlet skimmer or ruddy marsh skimmer is a species of dragonfly of the family Libellulidae, native to east and southeast Asia and introduced to Jamaica, Florida, and Hawaii.

crocuta crocuta.name: Spotted hyena
crocuta crocuta.desc: A powerful hunter in its own right, as well as a scavenger of lion kills.
crocuta crocuta.about: The spotted hyena, also known as the laughing hyena, is a hyena species, currently classed as the sole extant member of the genus Crocuta, native to sub-Saharan Africa.

cromwell current and humboldt current.name: Cold upwelling
cromwell current and humboldt current.desc: Seamounts push the nutrient-rich Cromwell Current upward near the islands. El Niño shuts this upwelling off and warms the water.

crossarchus obscurus.name: Common kusimanse
crossarchus obscurus.desc: A small social mongoose of West African forest floors that forages for insects and other small animals.
crossarchus obscurus.about: The common kusimanse, also called long-nosed kusimanse and kusimanse, is a small, diurnal member of the Mungotinae.

crossopteryx febrifuga.name: African bark
crossopteryx febrifuga.desc: A small savanna tree. GloBI records show baboons, duikers, elephants and civets using it as food.
crossopteryx febrifuga.about: Crossopteryx is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. The genus contains only one species, viz.

crotalus adamanteus.name: EASTERN DIAMONDBACK RATTLESNAKE
crotalus adamanteus.desc: EASTERN DIAMONDBACK RATTLESNAKE (Crotalus adamanteus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
crotalus adamanteus.about: The eastern diamondback rattlesnake is a species of pit viper in the family Viperidae. The species is endemic to the Southeastern United States.

crotalus atrox.name: Western Diamond-backed Rattlesnake
crotalus atrox.desc: Ambush predator of rodents, rabbits and birds. Young snakes are eaten by roadrunners, and coyotes also take it.
crotalus atrox.about: The western diamondback rattlesnake or western diamond-backed rattlesnake, is a rattlesnake species and member of the viper family, found in the southwestern United States and Mexico.

crotalus cerastes.name: Sidewinder
crotalus cerastes.desc: A small desert rattlesnake that hunts rodents and lizards, moving by a looping sidewinding motion over sand.

crotalus horridus.name: Timber rattlesnake
crotalus horridus.desc: Ambush predator of deciduous forest that winters in limestone crevices. Eats mostly small mammals, especially mice.
crotalus horridus.about: The timber rattlesnake, also known commonly as the banded rattlesnake, and the canebrake rattlesnake in the southern United States, is a species of pit viper in the family Viperidae.

crotalus lutosus.name: Great Basin rattlesnake
crotalus lutosus.desc: A venomous snake listed among the park's reptiles that hunts small rodents and lizards.
crotalus lutosus.about: The Great Basin rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper species found in the Great Basin region of the United States.

crotalus molossus.name: Black Tailed Rattlesnake
crotalus molossus.desc: Black Tailed Rattlesnake (Crotalus molossus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 69 times near the park in GBIF.

crotalus oreganus.name: Western rattlesnake

dasiphora fruticosa.about: Dasiphora fruticosa is a species of hardy deciduous flowering shrub in the family Rosaceae, native to the cool temperate and subarctic regions of the northern hemisphere, often growing at high…

dasycercus.name: Mulgara
dasycercus.desc: A burrowing marsupial carnivore of spinifex deserts that eats mainly insects, as well as reptiles and small mammals. Listed as vulnerable in the park.
dasycercus.about: Mulgara are small rat-sized species in the genus Dasycercus. They are marsupial carnivores, related to the Tasmanian devil and quolls, that live in deserts and spinifex grasslands of the Australian…

dasylirion wheeleri.name: Wheeler sotol
dasylirion wheeleri.desc: Wheeler sotol (Dasylirion wheeleri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.

dasymutilla occidentalis.name: Common Eastern Velvet Ant
dasymutilla occidentalis.desc: Common Eastern Velvet Ant (Dasymutilla occidentalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

dasyochloa pulchella.name: Fluffgrass
dasyochloa pulchella.desc: Fluffgrass (Dasyochloa pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.
dasyochloa pulchella.about: Dasyochloa is a monotypic genus containing the single species Dasyochloa pulchella, also known as desert fluff-grass or low woollygrass.

dasyprocta azarae.name: Azara's agouti
dasyprocta azarae.desc: A forest rodent that eats palm fruit and seeds, and often buries them, which can start new palms.
dasyprocta azarae.about: Azara's agouti is an agouti species from the family Dasyproctidae. Found in Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina, it is named after Spanish naturalist Félix de Azara.

dasyprocta fuliginosa.name: Black agouti
dasyprocta fuliginosa.desc: A forest rodent that eats fruit and seeds. It is prey for jaguars, ocelots and harpy eagles.
dasyprocta fuliginosa.about: The black agouti is a South American species of agouti from the family Dasyproctidae.

dasyprocta leporina.name: Red-rumped agouti
dasyprocta leporina.desc: A rodent that eats mostly seeds, fruit pulp, leaves and roots, and disperses the seeds of some trees by carrying them off.
dasyprocta leporina.about: The red-rumped agouti, also known as the golden-rumped agouti, orange-rumped agouti or Brazilian agouti, is a species of agouti from the family Dasyproctidae.

dasyprocta punctata.name: Central American agouti
dasyprocta punctata.desc: Eats fruit and seeds and buries surplus seeds for later, which helps spread forest trees.
dasyprocta punctata.about: The Central American agouti is a species of agouti from the family Dasyproctidae.

dasyprocta spp..name: Agouti
dasyprocta spp..desc: Gnaws open Brazil nuts and buries spares, planting new trees.
dasyprocta spp..about: The agouti ( , ə-GOO-tee) or common agouti is any of several rodent species of the genus Dasyprocta, from Ancient Greek δασύς (dasús), meaning "hair", and πρωκτός (prōktós), meaning "anus".

dasypus novemcinctus.name: Nine-banded armadillo
dasypus novemcinctus.desc: Digs for insects such as ants and termites. It is prey for maned wolves, ocelots and big cats in GloBI records.
dasypus novemcinctus.about: The nine-banded armadillo, also called the nine-banded long-nosed armadillo or common armadillo, is a species of armadillo native to South America.

dasyurus albopunctatus.name: New Guinea quoll
dasyurus albopunctatus.desc: A climbing marsupial hunter of forests up to about 3,300 m. It takes birds, rats, other marsupials, reptiles and insects, and also scavenges.
dasyurus albopunctatus.about: The New Guinean quoll, also known as the New Guinea quoll or New Guinea native cat, is a carnivorous marsupial mammal native to New Guinea.

dasyurus hallucatus.name: Northern quoll
dasyurus hallucatus.desc: Small carnivorous marsupial that eats invertebrates, small mammals, lizards and frogs. Cane toads have caused steep local declines in Kakadu.
dasyurus hallucatus.about: The northern quoll, also known as the northern native cat, the North Australian native cat or the satanellus is a carnivorous marsupial native to Australia.

dasyurus maculatus.name: Spotted-tailed quoll
dasyurus maculatus.desc: Tasmania's top hunting mammal, living in rainforest and wet forest and taking possums, pademelons, wombats and crayfish.
dasyurus maculatus.about: The tiger quoll, also known as the spotted-tailed quoll, spotted quoll, spotted-tailed dasyure, or tiger cat, is a carnivorous marsupial of the quoll genus Dasyurus native to Australia.

dasyurus viverrinus.name: Eastern quoll
dasyurus viverrinus.desc: A small spotted marsupial carnivore that hunts possums and smaller wallabies and takes carrion.
dasyurus viverrinus.about: The eastern quoll is a medium-sized, carnivorous marsupial (dasyurid), and one of six extant species of quolls.

datura wrightii.name: Sacred datura
datura wrightii.desc: Sacred datura (Datura wrightii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 67 times near the park in GBIF.
datura wrightii.about: Datura wrightii, commonly known as sacred datura, is a poisonous perennial plant species and ornamental flower of the family Solanaceae native to the Southwestern United States and northwestern…

daucus carota.name: Queen Anne's Lace
daucus carota.desc: Queen Anne's Lace (Daucus carota): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
daucus carota.about: Daucus carota, whose common names include wild carrot, European wild carrot, bird's nest, bishop's lace, carrot flower, and Queen Anne's lace (North America), is a flowering plant in the family…

davilla kunthii.name: Davilla liana
davilla kunthii.desc: A woody climber whose fruits feed a range of birds in GloBI feeding records.

deadwood and forest soil.name: Deadwood and forest soil
deadwood and forest soil.desc: Almost half the forest wood is dead, far more than in managed forests, and it slowly returns nutrients to the soil.

decapoda.name: Reef crustaceans
decapoda.desc: Crabs, shrimps and similar animals living among the algae and coral, an important food for many reef fishes.
decapoda.about: A decapod is a crustacean in the large order of Decapoda (from Ancient Greek δέκά déka 'ten' + πούς poús 'foot') within the class Malacostraca, including crabs, lobsters, crayfish, shrimp, and…

decodon verticillatus.name: Swamp Loosestrife
decodon verticillatus.desc: Swamp Loosestrife (Decodon verticillatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

decomposer community.name: Fungi and bacteria
decomposer community.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.

decomposers.name: Decomposers
decomposers.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

deep cold lakes.name: Deep cold lakes
deep cold lakes.desc: Over 25,000 lakes, many hundreds of metres deep, fill the plateau valleys and hold a large store of Russian fresh water.

deep oxygenated water.name: Deep oxygenated water
deep oxygenated water.desc: Unlike many deep lakes, Baikal keeps oxygen at depth, which lets animals live throughout the water column.

deep prairie soil.name: Deep prairie soil
deep prairie soil.desc: Dense roots hold the soil, with big bluestem roots saturating the top two feet and reaching about twelve feet deep, per the MDC.

dejongia lobidactylus.name: Lobed Plume Moth
dejongia lobidactylus.desc: Lobed Plume Moth (Dejongia lobidactylus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

delphinapterus leucas.name: Beluga
delphinapterus leucas.desc: A white whale that hunts cod and other fish in shallow Arctic waters.
delphinapterus leucas.about: The beluga whale () or the white whale is an Arctic and sub-Arctic cetacean.

delphinium barbeyi.name: Subalpine larkspur
delphinium barbeyi.desc: Subalpine larkspur (Delphinium barbeyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.
delphinium barbeyi.about: Delphinium barbeyi is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family known by the common names subalpine larkspur, tall larkspur, and Barbey's larkspur.

delphinium nuttallianum.name: Nuttall's larkspur
delphinium nuttallianum.desc: Nuttall's larkspur (Delphinium nuttallianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 96 times near the park in GBIF.

delphinium tricorne.name: Dwarf larkspur
delphinium tricorne.desc: Dwarf larkspur (Delphinium tricorne): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
delphinium tricorne.about: Delphinium tricorne, known by the common names dwarf larkspur or spring larkspur, is a species of flowering plant in the Ranunculaceae (buttercup) family.

delta silt & nutrients.name: Delta silt & nutrients
delta silt & nutrients.desc: The Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna deliver mud and nutrients that feed the forest and the tidal flats.

delta silt and nutrients.name: Delta silt and nutrients
delta silt and nutrients.desc: Sediment from the Tigris-Euphrates river system built the muddy delta coast of the northern Gulf, and river water carries nutrients to the bays.

dendrelaphis caudolineatus.name: Striped bronzeback
dendrelaphis caudolineatus.desc: A slender tree snake. GloBI records it eating the common tree frog and a skink.
dendrelaphis caudolineatus.about: Dendrelaphis caudolineatus, commonly known as the striped bronzeback or grey bronzeback, is a species of colubrid snake found in Southeast Asia.

dendrelaphis punctulatus.name: Common tree snake
dendrelaphis punctulatus.desc: Feeds on frogs, skinks and other small reptiles.
dendrelaphis punctulatus.about: Dendrelaphis punctulatus, also known commonly as the Australian tree snake, the common tree snake, and the green tree snake, is a species of slender, large-eyed, diurnal, non-venomous snake in the…

dendroaspis jamesoni.name: Jameson's mamba
dendroaspis jamesoni.desc: A tree-living venomous snake recorded near the park that hunts birds, small mammals and lizards.
dendroaspis jamesoni.about: Jameson's mamba is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Elapidae. The species is native to equatorial Africa.

dendrobates leucomelas.name: Bumblebee poison dart frog
dendrobates leucomelas.desc: A small yellow-and-black frog of the Gran Sabana region that eats tiny insects, especially ants, on the forest floor.
dendrobates leucomelas.about: The yellow-banded poison dart frog, also known as yellow-headed poison dart frog or bumblebee poison frog, is a poison dart frog from the genus Dendrobates of the family Dendrobatidae.

dendrobates tinctorius.name: Dyeing poison frog
dendrobates tinctorius.desc: A bold-patterned poison frog of leaf litter that eats small invertebrates such as ants.
dendrobates tinctorius.about: The cobalt dyeing poison dart frog, also known as the cobalt poison frog or tinc, is a species of poison dart frog.

dendrocitta cinerascens.name: Bornean treepie
dendrocitta cinerascens.desc: The most recorded bird near the park; an omnivorous crow relative that takes fruit and small animals.
dendrocitta cinerascens.about: The Bornean treepie is a passerine bird belonging to the treepies genus, Dendrocitta, of in the crow family, Corvidae. It is endemic to the island of Borneo.

dendrocopos leucotos.name: White-backed woodpecker
dendrocopos leucotos.desc: Feeds mainly on wood-boring beetles and larvae and needs plenty of standing and fallen dead wood in mature broadleaf forest.
dendrocopos leucotos.about: The white-backed woodpecker is a Eurasian woodpecker belonging to the genus Dendrocopos.

dendrocopos major.name: Great spotted woodpecker
dendrocopos major.desc: Takes seeds and insects and, in GloBI records, small birds and nestlings.
dendrocopos major.about: The great spotted woodpecker is a medium-sized woodpecker with pied black and white plumage and a red patch on the lower belly. Males and young birds also have red markings on the neck or head.

dendroctonus ponderosae.name: Mountain pine beetle
dendroctonus ponderosae.desc: A bark beetle that kills conifers. The park page says warmer winters let it survive and reproduce faster, raising tree mortality.
dendroctonus ponderosae.about: The mountain pine beetle is a species of bark beetle native to the forests of western North America from Mexico to central British Columbia.

dendrocygna viduata.name: White-faced whistling duck
dendrocygna viduata.desc: Abundant wetland duck recorded eating cattail; it feeds on plant matter in shallow water.
dendrocygna viduata.about: The white-faced whistling duck is a whistling duck that breeds in sub-Saharan Africa and much of South America.

dendrohyrax arboreus.name: Southern tree hyrax
dendrohyrax arboreus.desc: A nocturnal, tree-living hyrax of the forest belt, browsing leaves and twigs.
dendrohyrax arboreus.about: The southern tree hyrax, also known as the southern tree dassie, is a species of mammal in the family Procaviidae. The southern tree hyrax is mainly found in the south central eastern side of Africa.

dendrohyrax validus.name: Kilimanjaro tree hyrax
dendrohyrax validus.desc: Leaf-eater of the foothill and montane forest, reaching about 3,000 m on Kilimanjaro. Leopards and crowned eagles prey on it.
dendrohyrax validus.about: The eastern tree hyrax is a species of mammal within the family Procaviidae.

dendrolagus bennettianus.name: Bennett's tree-kangaroo
dendrolagus bennettianus.desc: Eats leaves of dozens of rainforest plants, especially umbrella tree, in a small range north of Cooktown.
dendrolagus bennettianus.about: Bennett's tree-kangaroo is a large tree-kangaroo. Males can weigh from 11.5 kg up to almost 14 kg (25 to 31 lbs), while the females range between about 8 to 10.6 kg (18 to 23 lb).

dendrolagus mbaiso.name: Dingiso
dendrolagus mbaiso.desc: A tree-kangaroo of subalpine forest and shrubland at about 3,250 to 4,200 m, mostly living on the ground. Endangered, mainly because of hunting and habitat loss.
dendrolagus mbaiso.about: The dingiso (), also known as the bondegezou or bakaga, is an endangered, long-tailed marsupial found only in mountain forests on the west of the island of New Guinea (in Indonesia).

dendromecon rigida.name: Tree-poppy
dendromecon rigida.desc: Tree-poppy (Dendromecon rigida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 290 times near the park in GBIF.

dendropanax caucanus.name: Dendropanax tree
dendropanax caucanus.desc: A forest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for monkeys, toucans and other birds.
dendropanax caucanus.about: Dendropanax is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araliaceae, consisting of 92 species of evergreen trees and shrubs, first described by Joseph Decaisne & Jules Émile Planchon in 1854.

dendrosenecio keniodendron.name: Giant groundsel
dendrosenecio keniodendron.desc: A tree-like rosette plant of the high alpine valleys. Its leaves fold over the central bud at night, keeping it above freezing.
dendrosenecio keniodendron.about: Dendrosenecio keniodendron or giant groundsel is a species of the genus Dendrosenecio of the large family Asteraceae and is one of the several species of giant groundsels endemic to the high…

dendrosenecio kilimanjari.name: Giant groundsel
dendrosenecio kilimanjari.desc: Giant groundsel endemic to the mountain, growing below about 4,000 m.
dendrosenecio kilimanjari.about: Dendrosenecio kilimanjari is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is a giant groundsel found on Mount Kilimanjaro in Africa, below 4,000 metres (13,000 ft).

dendrosicyos socotranus.name: Cucumber tree
dendrosicyos socotranus.desc: The only tree in the gourd family. It stores water in its swollen trunk to survive long dry spells.
dendrosicyos socotranus.about: Dendrosicyos is a monotypic genus in the plant family Cucurbitaceae. The only species is Dendrosicyos socotranus, the cucumber tree.

deparia acrostichoides.name: Silver false spleenwort
deparia acrostichoides.desc: Silver false spleenwort (Deparia acrostichoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
deparia acrostichoides.about: Deparia acrostichoides, commonly called silvery glade fern or silvery spleenwort, is a perennial species of fern.

dericorys.name: Saxaul locusts
dericorys.desc: Locusts of this genus are recorded as pests of saxaul in Turkmenistan and neighbouring countries.
dericorys.about: Locusts are various species of short-horned grasshoppers in the family Acrididae that have a swarming phase.

deschampsia cespitosa.name: Tufted hairgrass
deschampsia cespitosa.desc: A tussock grass of the island's warmer, drier valleys, where steppe-like meadows grow. Muskoxen prefer grasses when they are plentiful.
deschampsia cespitosa.about: Deschampsia cespitosa, commonly known as tufted hairgrass or tussock grass, is a perennial tufted plant in the grass family Poaceae.

desert soil.name: Desert soil
desert soil.desc: Thin soils of igneous and limestone origin. Nutrients return to them from dead plants and animals.

desert soil & nutrients.name: Desert soil & nutrients
desert soil & nutrients.desc: Sandy, thin soil that holds nutrients plants draw on, topped by the crust.

desert soil and nutrients.name: Desert soil and nutrients
desert soil and nutrients.desc: Thin rocky soils hold the minerals and organic matter that annual plants use after winter rains.

desert sunlight.name: Desert sunlight
desert sunlight.desc: Intense sun powers desert plants, but heat sends many animals underground for the day.

desmanthus illinoensis.name: Illinois bundle-flower
desmanthus illinoensis.desc: Illinois bundle-flower (Desmanthus illinoensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

diabrotica undecimpunctata.name: Southern Corn Rootworm
diabrotica undecimpunctata.desc: Southern Corn Rootworm (Diabrotica undecimpunctata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

diadasia australis.name: Diadasia australis
diadasia australis.desc: Diadasia australis (Diadasia australis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 338 times near the park in GBIF.
diadasia australis.about: Diadasia australis is a species of chimney bee in the family Apidae. It is found in Central America and North America.

diadema antillarum.name: Long-spined sea urchin
diadema antillarum.desc: A spiny urchin that grazes algae on reef surfaces.
diadema antillarum.about: Diadema antillarum, also known as the lime urchin, black sea urchin, or the long-spined sea urchin, is a species of sea urchin in the family Diadematidae.

dialium.name: Velvet tamarind trees
dialium.desc: Forest trees whose fruit is eaten by bonobos. Seeds that pass through a bonobo can germinate better, and some Dialium seem to rely on that.
dialium.about: Dialium is a genus of flowering plants in the family Fabaceae, subfamily Dialioideae. Velvet tamarind is a common name for several species.

diama dam.name: Diama Dam
diama dam.desc: Operating since 1988, the downstream dam changed the water balance and salinity, and invasive reeds and floating plants spread afterwards.

dianthera americana.name: American water-willow
dianthera americana.desc: American water-willow (Dianthera americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
dianthera americana.about: Dianthera americana, commonly known as the American water-willow, is an herbaceous, aquatic flowering plant in the family Acanthaceae.

dianthus armeria.name: Deptford Pink
dianthus armeria.desc: Deptford Pink (Dianthus armeria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
dianthus armeria.about: Dianthus armeria, the Deptford pink or grass pink, is a species of Dianthus ("pink") native to most of Europe, from Portugal north to southern Scotland and southern Finland, and east to Ukraine and…

dianthus barbatus.name: Sweet William
dianthus barbatus.desc: Sweet William (Dianthus barbatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

diatoms and dinoflagellates.name: Phytoplankton
diatoms and dinoflagellates.desc: Drifting algae that bloom where river nutrients arrive. When a bloom dies and sinks, bacteria break it down and use up oxygen.
diatoms and dinoflagellates.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

diatoms and flagellates.name: Phytoplankton
diatoms and flagellates.desc: Drifting algae that bloom in open water and near the ice edge. Growth is often limited by a shortage of iron.
diatoms and flagellates.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

diatoms and green algae.name: Phytoplankton and algae
diatoms and green algae.desc: Microscopic algae in the open water and on the lake bottom. They feed the lake's small grazers and filter feeders.
diatoms and green algae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

diatoms and other algae.name: Phytoplankton
diatoms and other algae.desc: Drifting algae that feed the bay's filter feeders and zooplankton. Too many nutrients cause blooms that block light and use up oxygen when they die and decay.
diatoms and other algae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

diatoms living in and under ice.latin: Diatoms living in and under ice
diatoms living in and under ice.name: Sea-ice algae
diatoms living in and under ice.desc: Algae growing in channels and on the underside of sea ice, a spring food supply for krill.

dicentra cucullaria.name: Dutchman's-breeches
dicentra cucullaria.desc: Dutchman's-breeches (Dicentra cucullaria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
dicentra cucullaria.about: Dicentra cucullaria, Dutchman's britches, or Dutchman's breeches, is a perennial herbaceous plant, native to rich woods of eastern North America, with a disjunct population in the Columbia Basin.

dicerorhinus sumatrensis.name: Sumatran rhinoceros
dicerorhinus sumatrensis.desc: A critically small population lives in the park. Wikipedia reports a 2011 camera-trap survey and an estimate of no more than 27 animals.
dicerorhinus sumatrensis.about: The Sumatran rhinoceros, also known as the Sumatran rhino, hairy rhinoceros or Asian two-horned rhinoceros, is a rare member of the family Rhinocerotidae and one of five extant species of rhinoceros;…

diceros bicornis.name: Black rhinoceros
diceros bicornis.desc: A selective browser that strips leaves and twigs with its prehensile lip, favouring acacias. Etosha is a major stronghold for the species.
diceros bicornis.about: The black rhinoceros, also called the black rhino or the hooked-lip rhinoceros, is a species of rhinoceros native to East and Southern Africa, including Angola, Botswana, Eswatini, Kenya, Lesotho,…

dichanthelium acuminatum.name: Tapered Rosette Grass
dichanthelium acuminatum.desc: Tapered Rosette Grass (Dichanthelium acuminatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
dichanthelium acuminatum.about: Dichanthelium acuminatum, the tapered rosette grass, is a species of grass from the genus Dichanthelium, in North America.

dichanthelium boscii.name: Bosc's panic grass
dichanthelium boscii.desc: Bosc's panic grass (Dichanthelium boscii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dichanthelium linearifolium.name: Narrowleaf Witchgrass
dichanthelium linearifolium.desc: Narrowleaf Witchgrass (Dichanthelium linearifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

dichanthelium scoparium.name: Velvety Panic Grass
dichanthelium scoparium.desc: Velvety Panic Grass (Dichanthelium scoparium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
dichanthelium scoparium.about: Dichanthelium scoparium is a species of grass known by the common names velvet panicum, velvety panicgrass, and broom panicgrass.

dichanthelium scribnerianum.name: Scribner's Panicgrass
dichanthelium scribnerianum.desc: Scribner's Panicgrass (Dichanthelium scribnerianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dichanthelium sphaerocarpon.name: Roundfruit Panicgrass
dichanthelium sphaerocarpon.desc: Roundfruit Panicgrass (Dichanthelium sphaerocarpon): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
dichanthelium sphaerocarpon.about: Dichanthelium sphaerocarpon, also called Panicum polyanthes, common name round-seed panic grass, is a plant found in North America. It is listed as endangered in Michigan.

dichelostemma congestum.name: Fork-tooth ookow
dichelostemma congestum.desc: Fork-tooth ookow (Dichelostemma congestum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dichomeris ligulella.name: Moth
dichomeris ligulella.desc: Moth (Dichomeris ligulella): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

dichrostachys cinerea.name: Sicklebush
dichrostachys cinerea.desc: A thorny shrub of African savanna. GloBI records many local browsers eating it, including impala, elephant, warthog and waterbuck.
dichrostachys cinerea.about: Dichrostachys cinerea, known as sicklebush, bell mimosa, Chinese lantern tree or Kalahari Christmas tree (South Africa), is a legume of the genus Dichrostachys in the family Fabaceae.

dicksonia antarctica.name: Soft tree fern
dicksonia antarctica.desc: A tree fern that forms an open, park-like understorey in many rainforest stands.
dicksonia antarctica.about: Dicksonia antarctica, commonly known as the soft tree fern, is a species of fern native to eastern Australia, ranging from south-east Queensland to Tasmania.

dicotyles tajacu.name: Collared peccary
dicotyles tajacu.desc: Called javelina locally. Feeds on cactus such as prickly pear and is taken by cougars and eaten as carrion by vultures in GloBI records.
dicotyles tajacu.about: The collared peccary is a peccary, a species of artiodactyl (even-toed) mammal in the family Tayassuidae. It is the only extant member of the genus Dicotyles.

dicranopteris linearis.name: Forkedfern
dicranopteris linearis.desc: A tangle-forming fern of forest clearings and openings, recorded in the Gola area. Ferns and herbs are staple foods of the pygmy hippo.
dicranopteris linearis.about: Dicranopteris linearis is a common species of fern known by many common names, including Old World forked fern, uluhe (Hawaiian), and dilim (Filipino).

dicrostonyx groenlandicus.name: Collared lemming
dicrostonyx groenlandicus.desc: Tunnels under the snow all winter. Its boom-and-bust numbers drive owls and foxes.
dicrostonyx groenlandicus.about: Dicrostonyx is a genus of rodent in the family Cricetidae. Its members are known as collared lemmings or varying lemmings.

dicrostonyx vinogradovi.name: Wrangel Island collared lemming
dicrostonyx vinogradovi.desc: The island has unusually dense lemming populations. Lemmings are the key prey of Arctic foxes, snowy owls and wolverines.
dicrostonyx vinogradovi.about: Dicrostonyx is a genus of rodent in the family Cricetidae. Its members are known as collared lemmings or varying lemmings.

dicrurus adsimilis.name: Fork-tailed drongo
dicrurus adsimilis.desc: A black insect-eating bird, recorded in GBIF data near the reserve. It hunts flying insects from perches.
dicrurus adsimilis.about: The fork-tailed drongo, also called the common drongo or African drongo, is a small bird found from the Sahel to South Africa that lives in wooded habitats, particularly woodlands and savannas.

dicrurus lophorinus.name: Sri Lanka drongo
dicrurus lophorinus.desc: An insect-eating bird that hunts from open perches. Related drongos are noisy members of the mixed-species flocks that Sinharaja is known for.
dicrurus lophorinus.about: The Sri Lanka drongo or Ceylon crested drongo, is a species of bird in the family Dicruridae. It is endemic to Sri Lanka.

didelphis aurita.name: Big-eared opossum
didelphis aurita.desc: An omnivorous marsupial that eats fruit and small animals. GloBI records show it eating many of the same fruits as other forest animals.
didelphis aurita.about: The big-eared opossum, also known as a saruê, or the gambá, is an opossum species from South America. It is found in Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay.

didelphis virginiana.name: Virginia opossum
didelphis virginiana.desc: Virginia opossum (Didelphis virginiana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
didelphis virginiana.about: The Virginia opossum, also known as the North American opossum, is a member of the opossum family found from southern Canada to northern Costa Rica, making it the northernmost marsupial in the world.

didiereaceae.name: Spiny forest plants
didiereaceae.desc: Woody, spiny, drought-adapted plants of the south-west that are only distantly related to cacti.
didiereaceae.about: Didiereaceae is a family of flowering plants found in continental Africa and Madagascar. It contains 20 species classified in three subfamilies and six genera.

dieunomia nevadensis.name: Nevada Nomia
dieunomia nevadensis.desc: Nevada Nomia (Dieunomia nevadensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
dieunomia nevadensis.about: Dieunomia nevadensis, the Nevada nomia, is a species of sweat bee in the family Halictidae. It is found in Central America and North America.

dillenia indica.name: Elephant apple
dillenia indica.desc: A fruiting tree of the open woodland. A GloBI record shows Asian elephants eating it.
dillenia indica.about: Dillenia indica, commonly known as elephant apple or ou tenga, is a species of Dillenia (Family Dilleniaceae) native to China, India, and tropical Asia. It is found in stony river banks.

dilophus spinipes.name: Dilophus spinipes
dilophus spinipes.desc: Dilophus spinipes (Dilophus spinipes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

dimorphocarpa wislizenii.name: Touristplant
dimorphocarpa wislizenii.desc: Touristplant (Dimorphocarpa wislizenii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

dinaromys bogdanovi.name: Balkan snow vole
dinaromys bogdanovi.desc: A rock-dwelling rodent of the Dinaric mountains that eats plants. Small mammals like this feed foxes, eagles and bears.
dinaromys bogdanovi.about: The Balkan snow vole, also known as Martino's snow vole, is the only living member of the genus Dinaromys.

diodia virginiana.name: Virginia buttonweed
diodia virginiana.desc: Virginia buttonweed (Diodia virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

dione vanillae.name: Gulf Fritillary
dione vanillae.desc: Gulf Fritillary (Dione vanillae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
dione vanillae.about: The Gulf fritillary or passion butterfly is a bright orange butterfly in the subfamily Heliconiinae of the family Nymphalidae.

diospyros.name: Ebony trees
diospyros.desc: A genus of forest trees with fleshy fruit and hard dense wood; Diospyros conocarpa is among the most recorded plants near the reserve.
diospyros.about: Diospyros is a genus of over 700 species of deciduous and evergreen trees and shrubs, which are typically dioecious. The majority are native to the tropics and many are of local ecological importance.

diospyros cauliflora.name: Ebony relatives
diospyros cauliflora.desc: Understory tree of the ebony genus recorded in the reserve; its fruit is eaten by mouse-deer in GloBI records.
diospyros cauliflora.about: Diospyros is a genus of over 700 species of deciduous and evergreen trees and shrubs, which are typically dioecious. The majority are native to the tropics and many are of local ecological importance.

diospyros lotus.name: Date plum
diospyros lotus.desc: A fruit tree of the Hyrcanian forest. Its fruit is eaten by birds and mammals.
diospyros lotus.about: The date-plum, also known by the common names Caucasian persimmon and lilac persimmon, is a widely cultivated species of the genus Diospyros, native to Eurasia. The ripe fruit is edible.

diospyros mespiliformis.name: African ebony
diospyros mespiliformis.desc: A savanna and riverine tree whose fruit and leaves are recorded in the diets of antelope, elephants, warthogs and baboons.
diospyros mespiliformis.about: Diospyros mespiliformis, the jackalberry, is a large dioecious evergreen tree found mostly in the savannas of Africa. Jackals are fond of the fruit, hence the common names.

diospyros virginiana.name: Eastern Persimmon
diospyros virginiana.desc: Eastern Persimmon (Diospyros virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
diospyros virginiana.about: Diospyros virginiana is a persimmon species commonly called the American persimmon, common persimmon, eastern persimmon, simmon, possumwood, possum apples, or sugar plum.

diphasiastrum digitatum.name: Fan Clubmoss
diphasiastrum digitatum.desc: Fan Clubmoss (Diphasiastrum digitatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
diphasiastrum digitatum.about: Diphasiastrum digitatum is known as groundcedar, running cedar or crowsfoot, along with other members of its genus, but the common name fan clubmoss can be used to refer to it specifically.

diplacus aurantiacus.name: Bush monkey-flower
diplacus aurantiacus.desc: Bush monkey-flower (Diplacus aurantiacus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 99 times near the park in GBIF.
diplacus aurantiacus.about: Diplacus aurantiacus, the sticky monkey-flower or orange bush monkey-flower, is a flowering plant that grows in a subshrub form, native to western North America from southwestern Oregon south through…

diplacus longiflorus.name: Southern bush monkeyflower
diplacus longiflorus.desc: Southern bush monkeyflower (Diplacus longiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 180 times near the park in GBIF.

dipodomys compactus.name: Gulf Coast Kangaroo Rat
dipodomys compactus.desc: Gulf Coast Kangaroo Rat (Dipodomys compactus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.
dipodomys compactus.about: The Gulf Coast kangaroo rat is a species of rodent in the family Heteromyidae found in Mexico and the state of Texas in the United States.

dipodomys deserti.name: Desert kangaroo rat
dipodomys deserti.desc: A seed-eater that lives in sand burrows. NPS notes it gets all its water from its food and never needs to drink.
dipodomys deserti.about: The desert kangaroo rat is a rodent species in the family Heteromyidae that is found in desert areas of southwestern North America.

dipodomys merriami.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
dipodomys merriami.desc: Eats mostly seeds and stores them in its burrow. It rarely drinks, getting water from its food and its humid burrow.
dipodomys merriami.about: Merriam's kangaroo rat is a species of rodent in the family Heteromyidae. The species name commemorates Clinton Hart Merriam.

dipodomys ordii.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
dipodomys ordii.desc: A nocturnal seed-eater that stores seeds in burrows and gets most of its water from its food. Coyotes, bobcats, owls and snakes eat it.
dipodomys ordii.about: Ord's kangaroo rat is a kangaroo rat native to western North America, specifically the Great Plains and the Great Basin, with its range extending from extreme southern Canada to central Mexico.

dipodomys venustus.name: Narrow-faced kangaroo rat
dipodomys venustus.desc: A nocturnal seed-eating rodent of chaparral slopes, and an important prey animal for snakes, cats and canids.
dipodomys venustus.about: The narrow-faced kangaroo rat is one of almost 20 species of kangaroo rats, a rodent in the family Heteromyidae. It is endemic to California in the United States.

diporeia hoyi.name: Diporeia
diporeia hoyi.desc: A native lake-bottom amphipod that fell sharply from the 1990s, which invasive mussels are thought to have caused.
diporeia hoyi.about: Diporeia is a North American genus of freshwater amphipod that was formerly a dominant form of zooplankton in the Great Lakes.

dipterocarpaceae.name: Dipterocarp trees
dipterocarpaceae.desc: Tall hardwood trees that dominate much of the lowland rainforest of Sumatra and shape the forest structure.
dipterocarpaceae.about: Dipterocarpaceae is a family of flowering plants with 22 genera and about 695 known species of mainly lowland tropical forest trees.

dipterocarpus.name: Dipterocarp trees
dipterocarpus.desc: Tall emergent and canopy trees that dominate lowland rainforest in Peninsular Malaysia and shape the structure of the forest.
dipterocarpus.about: Dipterocarpaceae is a family of flowering plants with 22 genera and about 695 known species of mainly lowland tropical forest trees.

dipterocarpus zeylanicus.name: Hora dipterocarp
dipterocarpus zeylanicus.desc: A giant endemic rainforest tree, up to about 40 to 45 m tall, with winged seeds carried by wind. It grows in the wet lowlands including Sinharaja, where dipterocarps dominate the valleys and lower slopes.
dipterocarpus zeylanicus.about: Dipterocarpus zeylanicus, commonly known as හොර - Hora in Sinhalese and සරල - Sarala or කිරිපලු - Kiripalu, is a species of Dipterocarpus that is endemic to Sri Lanka.

dipterostemon capitatus.name: Indian-hyacinth
dipterostemon capitatus.desc: Indian-hyacinth (Dipterostemon capitatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

dipteryx oleifera.name: Almendro (mountain almond)
dipteryx oleifera.desc: A tall rainforest tree with hard nuts. Its seeds are the core food and the main nesting tree of the great green macaw.
dipteryx oleifera.about: Dipteryx oleifera, the tonka bean, eboe, choibá, or almendro tree (almond in Spanish), is a species of emergent rainforest tree up to 55 m (180 ft) tall in the family Fabaceae (the subfamily…

dipus sagitta.name: Northern three-toed jerboa
dipus sagitta.desc: A small hopping rodent of sandy ground that shelters in burrows. Foxes, shrikes and snakes take it.
dipus sagitta.about: The northern three-toed jerboa is a species of rodent in the family Dipodidae. It is the only extant species within the genus Dipus.

dirca palustris.name: Leatherwood
dirca palustris.desc: Leatherwood (Dirca palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
dirca palustris.about: Dirca palustris, or eastern leatherwood, is a flowering shrub in the family Thymelaeceae native to eastern North America.

dissolved nutrients.name: Dissolved nutrients
dissolved nutrients.desc: River inflow and recycled nutrients feed algal growth in the lake.

dissostichus mawsoni.name: Antarctic toothfish
dissostichus mawsoni.desc: Large fish that eats shrimp, silverfish and other fish. Weddell seals and orcas eat big adults.
dissostichus mawsoni.about: The Antarctic toothfish, also known as the Antarctic cod, is a large, black or brown fish found in very cold (even subzero) waters of the Southern Ocean near Antarctica.

distichlis spicata.name: Inland Saltgrass
distichlis spicata.desc: Inland Saltgrass (Distichlis spicata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
distichlis spicata.about: Distichlis spicata is a species of grass known by several common names, including seashore saltgrass, inland saltgrass, and desert saltgrass.

diverse microalgae.name: Phytoplankton
diverse microalgae.desc: Blooms in open water as ice retreats, feeding zooplankton and the sea floor.
diverse microalgae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

dja river and swamps.name: Dja River and swamps
dja river and swamps.desc: The Dja River loops around almost the whole reserve, forming its natural boundary, and its banks and swamps hold water-loving plants and animals.

dodecatheon clevelandii.name: Padre's shootingstar
dodecatheon clevelandii.desc: Padre's shootingstar (Dodecatheon clevelandii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

dodecatheon hendersonii.name: Mosquito bills
dodecatheon hendersonii.desc: Mosquito bills (Dodecatheon hendersonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 428 times near the park in GBIF.

dodecatheon meadia.name: Common shootingstar
dodecatheon meadia.desc: Common shootingstar (Dodecatheon meadia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 87 times near the park in GBIF.
dodecatheon meadia.about: Primula meadia, known by the common names shooting star, eastern shooting star, American cowslip, roosterheads, and prairie pointers is a species of flowering plant in the primula family Primulaceae.

dodecatheon pulchellum.name: Dark-throat shootingstar
dodecatheon pulchellum.desc: Dark-throat shootingstar (Dodecatheon pulchellum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 64 times near the park in GBIF.

doellingeria umbellata.name: Parasol Whitetop
doellingeria umbellata.desc: Parasol Whitetop (Doellingeria umbellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

dolichophis jugularis.name: Large whip snake
dolichophis jugularis.desc: A fast, large snake; GloBI records it eating mice. Hunted by jackals, foxes and snake eagles.
dolichophis jugularis.about: Dolichophis jugularis, also known commonly as the black whipsnake and the large whip snake, is a species of snake in the family Colubridae. The species is native to West Asia.

dolichotis patagonum.name: Patagonian mara
dolichotis patagonum.desc: A large cavy that eats mostly grasses and shrubs such as Atriplex lampa and Lycium. Foxes and birds of prey hunt the young.
dolichotis patagonum.about: The Patagonian mara is a rodent in the mara genus Dolichotis. It is also known as the Patagonian cavy or Patagonian hare.

dolichovespula maculata.name: Baldfaced Hornet
dolichovespula maculata.desc: Baldfaced Hornet (Dolichovespula maculata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

dorcopsis luctuosa.name: Gray dorcopsis
dorcopsis luctuosa.desc: A forest wallaby of southern New Guinea that lives in forest and disturbed ground such as old gardens. It browses vegetation.
dorcopsis luctuosa.about: The gray dorcopsis or gray forest wallaby is a species of marsupial in the family Macropodidae. It is found in West Papua and Papua New Guinea.

dorcopsis muelleri.name: Brown dorcopsis
dorcopsis muelleri.desc: A forest wallaby of lowland and hill rainforest that feeds on plant matter on the forest floor. Forest wallabies are a main prey of the Papuan eagle.
dorcopsis muelleri.about: The brown dorcopsis, also known as the brown forest wallaby, is a species of marsupial in the family Macropodidae.

dorosoma cepedianum.name: Gizzard shad
dorosoma cepedianum.desc: A filter-feeding fish and the most important forage fish in the river. Herons, cormorants, pelicans, ospreys, eagles and catfish all eat it.

doryteuthis gahi.name: Patagonian squid
doryteuthis gahi.desc: A small squid fished in Falklands waters and an important prey for seabirds, seals and fish.
doryteuthis gahi.about: Doryteuthis gahi, also known as Loligo, the Patagonian longfin squid and Patagonian squid, is a small-sized squid belonging to the family Loliginidae.

downingia bicornuta.name: Doublehorn calicoflower
downingia bicornuta.desc: Doublehorn calicoflower (Downingia bicornuta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
downingia bicornuta.about: Downingia bicornuta is a species of flowering plant in the bellflower family known by the common name doublehorn calicoflower and double-horned downingia.

downingia pulchella.name: Flatface calicoflower
downingia pulchella.desc: Flatface calicoflower (Downingia pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
downingia pulchella.about: Downingia pulchella is a species of flowering plant in the bellflower family known by the common names flatface calicoflower and valley calicoflower.

dracaena cinnabari.name: Dragon's blood tree
dracaena cinnabari.desc: An umbrella-crowned tree whose red resin is famous. Goats stop seedlings from growing, so many stands are ageing with little new growth.
dracaena cinnabari.about: Dracaena cinnabari, the Socotra dragon tree, or dragon blood tree, is a dragon tree native to the Socotra archipelago, part of Yemen, located in the Arabian Sea.

dreissena bugensis, d. polymorpha.name: Quagga & zebra mussels
dreissena bugensis, d. polymorpha.desc: Invasive filter feeders that strip plankton from the water and clear it. They are now the main drain on the lake's food supply.
dreissena bugensis, d. polymorpha.about: The quagga mussel is a species of freshwater mussel, an aquatic bivalve mollusc in the family Dreissenidae. It has a lifespan of 3 to 5 years.

drepanis coccinea.name: ʻIʻiwi
drepanis coccinea.desc: A scarlet honeycreeper with a long curved bill, recorded in GloBI feeding on ʻōhiʻa flowers.
drepanis coccinea.about: The ʻiʻiwi or scarlet honeycreeper is a species of Hawaiian honeycreeper. The ʻiʻiwi is a highly recognizable symbol of Hawaii.

drepanotermes.name: Harvester termites
drepanotermes.desc: Termites eat dead plant material such as grass and wood, recycling nutrients in arid soils, and are food for ants, lizards and many others.
drepanotermes.about: Termites are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

drift detritus.name: Wind-blown plant debris
drift detritus.desc: Dry plant matter carried by wind from the interior feeds dune invertebrates, which in turn support reptiles.

drift sea ice.name: Drift sea ice
drift sea ice.desc: Ice from the Sea of Okhotsk is carried south each winter and reaches Shiretoko. As it melts in spring it releases nutrients that help start the plankton bloom.

drifting algae.name: Phytoplankton
drifting algae.desc: Microscopic algae that bloom where cold, nutrient-rich water is pushed up around the islands. They feed the zooplankton and small fish that the marine food web rests on.
drifting algae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

drifting sand and dunes.name: Drifting sand and dunes
drifting sand and dunes.desc: The spit is a long sand ridge with some of Europe's highest moving dunes. Sand shapes which plants can grow and where forest can take hold.

dromas ardeola.name: Crab-plover
dromas ardeola.desc: A crab specialist that nests in burrows in sandy banks; Bubiyan reportedly hosts the largest breeding colony in the world.
dromas ardeola.about: The crab-plover or crab plover is a coastal wader (shorebird). It is the only member of the genus Dromas and the family Dromadidae.

drosera capillaris.name: Pink sundew
drosera capillaris.desc: Pink sundew (Drosera capillaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.
drosera capillaris.about: Drosera capillaris, also known as the pink sundew, is a species of carnivorous plant belonging to the family Droseraceae.

drosera intermedia.name: Oblong-leaved Sundew
drosera intermedia.desc: Oblong-leaved Sundew (Drosera intermedia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.
drosera intermedia.about: Drosera intermedia, commonly known as the oblong-leaved sundew, spoonleaf sundew, or spatulate leaved sundew, is an insectivorous plant species belonging to the sundew genus.

drosera rotundifolia.name: Round-leaved Sundew
drosera rotundifolia.desc: Round-leaved Sundew (Drosera rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

drought and fire.name: Drought and fire
drought and fire.desc: Cycles of drought and fire have shaped the wetland, shifting plants and pushing fish into deeper water.

dry westerly wind & low rain.name: Dry westerly wind & low rain
dry westerly wind & low rain.desc: The peninsula is a cold desert with roughly 240 mm of rain a year and winds mainly from the west, which keeps the vegetation low and shrubby.

dry-season fire.name: Dry-season fire
dry-season fire.desc: Savanna vegetation here is adapted to periodic fire, which helps keep trees from taking over open grassland.

dryas iulia.name: Julia Heliconian
dryas iulia.desc: Julia Heliconian (Dryas iulia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 518 times near the park in GBIF.

dryas octopetala.name: Mountain avens
dryas octopetala.desc: A low, mat-forming tundra wildflower that is one of the well-recorded plants of the coast.
dryas octopetala.about: Dryas octopetala, the mountain avens, eightpetal mountain-avens, white dryas or white dryad, is an Arctic–alpine flowering plant in the family Rosaceae.

dryobates pubescens.name: Downy Woodpecker
dryobates pubescens.desc: Downy Woodpecker (Dryobates pubescens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3,386 times near the park in GBIF.
dryobates pubescens.about: The downy woodpecker is a species of woodpecker, the smallest in North America. Length ranges from 14 to 18 cm (5.5 to 7.1 in).

dryobates scalaris.name: Ladder-backed Woodpecker
dryobates scalaris.desc: Ladder-backed Woodpecker (Dryobates scalaris): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2,905 times near the park in GBIF.

dryocampa rubicunda.name: Rosy Maple Moth
dryocampa rubicunda.desc: Rosy Maple Moth (Dryocampa rubicunda): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

dryocopus pileatus.name: Pileated Woodpecker
dryocopus pileatus.desc: Pileated Woodpecker (Dryocopus pileatus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.
dryocopus pileatus.about: The pileated woodpecker is a large, crow-sized woodpecker with a prominent red crest, white neck stripe, and a mostly black body.

dryolimnas cuvieri.name: Aldabra rail
dryolimnas cuvieri.desc: The last flightless bird of the Indian Ocean region, a flightless form of the white-throated rail found here.
dryolimnas cuvieri.about: The white-throated rail or Cuvier's rail is a species of bird in the family Rallidae. It is a fairly large rail, and has a flightless subspecies.

dryophytes andersonii.name: Pine Barrens treefrog
dryophytes andersonii.desc: Breeds in shallow acidic pools, and the New Jersey Pine Barrens hold its largest populations. It is a threatened species in the state.
dryophytes andersonii.about: The Pine Barrens tree frog is a species of New World tree frog. It is becoming rare due to habitat loss.

dryopteris intermedia.name: Intermediate Woodfern
dryopteris intermedia.desc: Intermediate Woodfern (Dryopteris intermedia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

dryopteris marginalis.name: Marginal Fern
dryopteris marginalis.desc: Marginal Fern (Dryopteris marginalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
dryopteris marginalis.about: Dryopteris marginalis, vernacularly known as the marginal shield fern or marginal wood fern, is a perennial species of fern found in damp shady areas throughout eastern North America, from Texas to…

drypetes deplanchei.name: Yellow tulipwood
drypetes deplanchei.desc: A fruiting native forest tree recorded very often on the island in GBIF data. It is part of the native forest canopy.
drypetes deplanchei.about: Drypetes deplanchei is a tree of eastern and northern Australia. It also occurs in New Caledonia and Lord Howe Island.

duabanga.name: Forest canopy trees
duabanga.desc: Semi-evergreen and deciduous forest trees such as lampati make up the forest cover of the northern park, feeding leaf and fruit eaters.
duabanga.about: Duabanga is a small genus of lowland evergreen rainforest trees in southeast Asia, with two or three species.

ducula aenea.name: Green imperial pigeon
ducula aenea.desc: A large fruit-eating pigeon of forest canopy that swallows fruit whole, especially figs.
ducula aenea.about: The green imperial pigeon is a large forest pigeon. The large range extends from Nepal, southern India and Sri Lanka eastwards to southern China, Indonesia and the Philippines.

ducula latrans.name: Barking imperial pigeon
ducula latrans.desc: A large fruit-eating pigeon that swallows big fruits, giving trees a way to spread seeds.
ducula latrans.about: The barking imperial pigeon, also known as Peale's imperial pigeon, is a species of bird in the pigeon family Columbidae.

ducula pacifica.name: Pacific imperial pigeon
ducula pacifica.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon that feeds on many fruit species and passes seeds through undamaged, making it an important seed disperser.
ducula pacifica.about: The Pacific imperial pigeon, Pacific pigeon, Pacific fruit pigeon or lupe is a widespread pigeon species in the family Columbidae.

ducula pistrinaria.name: Island imperial pigeon
ducula pistrinaria.desc: A large fruit pigeon of Pacific island forests and coasts that feeds on fruit such as figs.
ducula pistrinaria.about: The island imperial pigeon or floury imperial pigeon is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

ducula rosacea.name: Pink-headed imperial pigeon
ducula rosacea.desc: A large fruit pigeon of Lesser Sunda forests, rated near threatened, and listed among the park's notable birds.
ducula rosacea.about: The pink-headed imperial pigeon is a species of bird in the family Columbidae found in the Lesser Sunda Islands of Indonesia.

dudleya farinosa.name: Powdery liveforever
dudleya farinosa.desc: Powdery liveforever (Dudleya farinosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 85 times near the park in GBIF.

dugong dugon.name: Dugong
dugong dugon.desc: A large marine mammal that feeds almost entirely on seagrass.
dugong dugon.about: The dugong is a marine mammal. It is one of four living species of the order Sirenia, which also includes three species of manatees.

dumetella carolinensis.name: Gray Catbird
dumetella carolinensis.desc: Winter visitor that eats fruit and insects in thickets, including scarletbush and West Indian milkberry.
dumetella carolinensis.about: The gray catbird, also spelled grey catbird, is a medium-sized North American and Central American perching bird of the mimid family. It is the only member of the "catbird" genus Dumetella.

dunaliella.name: Lagoon microalgae
dunaliella.desc: Microscopic algae, including salt-loving types, grow in sunlit lagoons. Brine shrimp feed on planktonic algae; flamingos also take diatoms and blue-green algae.
dunaliella.about: Dunaliella is a genus of single-celled, photosynthetic green algae, that is characteristic for its ability to thrive and outcompete other organisms in hypersaline environments.

dunaliella salina.name: Pink lagoon algae
dunaliella salina.desc: Salt-loving algae that tint Laguna Colorada pink to red. They feed the plankton that the flamingos filter from the water.
