dunaliella salina.about: Dunaliella salina is a species of halophilic, unicellular, green algae found especially in hypersaline environments, such as salt lakes and salt evaporation ponds.

dune sand.name: Dune sand
dune sand.desc: The Gran Desierto de Altar is North America's largest field of active sand dunes, a loose, fast-draining habitat for burrowers and specialised plants.

dupontia fisheri.name: Tundra grass
dupontia fisheri.desc: A grass of wet Arctic tundra, one of the grasses and sedges that grazing reindeer and geese use in summer.
dupontia fisheri.about: Dupontia fisheri, common name tundragrass, is a species of grass.

duttaphrynus melanostictus.name: Asian common toad
duttaphrynus melanostictus.desc: A common amphibian that eats insects. GloBI records water monitors eating it.
duttaphrynus melanostictus.about: Duttaphrynus melanostictus is commonly called Asian common toad, Asian black-spined toad, Asian toad, black-spectacled toad, common Sunda toad, and Javanese toad.

eacles imperialis.name: Imperial Moth
eacles imperialis.desc: Imperial Moth (Eacles imperialis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
eacles imperialis.about: Eacles imperialis, the imperial moth, is a member of the family Saturniidae and subfamily Ceratocampinae.

east australian current.name: East Australian Current
east australian current.desc: Warm water carried south by this current lets the most southerly true coral reef grow, and mixes tropical and temperate marine life.

echinacea angustifolia.name: Prairie wildflowers
echinacea angustifolia.desc: Coneflowers, globemallow and other forbs add diversity to the grassland and feed pronghorn and prairie dogs.
echinacea angustifolia.about: Echinacea angustifolia, the narrow-leaved purple coneflower or blacksamson echinacea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

echinacea pallida.name: Pale echinacea
echinacea pallida.desc: Pale echinacea (Echinacea pallida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
echinacea pallida.about: Echinacea pallida, the pale purple coneflower, is a species of herbaceous perennial plant in the family Asteraceae. It is sometimes grown in gardens and used for medicinal purposes.

echinacea paradoxa.name: Bush's purple-coneflower
echinacea paradoxa.desc: Bush's purple-coneflower (Echinacea paradoxa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.
echinacea paradoxa.about: Echinacea paradoxa, the yellow coneflower, Bush's purple coneflower, or Ozark coneflower, is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

echinacea purpurea.name: Eastern Purple Coneflower
echinacea purpurea.desc: Eastern Purple Coneflower (Echinacea purpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

echinacea simulata.name: Wavy leaf purple coneflower
echinacea simulata.desc: Wavy leaf purple coneflower (Echinacea simulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
echinacea simulata.about: Echinacea simulata, commonly called wavy leaf purple coneflower, glade coneflower, or prairie purple coneflower, is a species of perennial flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

echinacea tennesseensis.name: Tennessee purple-coneflower
echinacea tennesseensis.desc: Tennessee purple-coneflower (Echinacea tennesseensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 184 times near the park in GBIF.

echinacea, silphium and others.name: Prairie wildflowers
echinacea, silphium and others.desc: Coneflowers, rosinweeds and many other flowering plants that feed pollinators and browsers.
echinacea, silphium and others.about: Echinacea purpurea, the eastern purple coneflower, purple coneflower, hedgehog coneflower, or Echinacea, is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

echinocactus horizonthalonius.name: Eagle-claw cactus
echinocactus horizonthalonius.desc: Eagle-claw cactus (Echinocactus horizonthalonius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocactus horizonthalonius.about: Echinocactus horizonthalonius is a species of cactus known by several common names, including devilshead, turk's head cactus, blue barrel cactus, eagle's claw, horse maimer, horse crippler, and…

echinocactus polycephalus.name: Cottontop barrel cactus
echinocactus polycephalus.desc: Cottontop barrel cactus (Echinocactus polycephalus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 76 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocactus polycephalus.about: Homalocephala polycephala, synonym Echinocactus polycephalus, is a cactus that is native to the United States and Mexico.

echinocereus bakeri.name: Baker Kingcup Cactus
echinocereus bakeri.desc: Baker Kingcup Cactus (Echinocereus bakeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus bakeri.about: Echinocereus bakeri, commonly known as Baker kingcup cactus, is a species of cactus native to the Southwestern United States.

echinocereus bonkerae.name: Pinkflower hedgehog cactus
echinocereus bonkerae.desc: Pinkflower hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus bonkerae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus coccineus.name: Scarlet hedgehog cactus
echinocereus coccineus.desc: Scarlet hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus coccineus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 203 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus coccineus.about: Echinocereus coccineus (scarlet hedgehog cactus) is a species of hedgehog cactus. It is native to Northern and Central America.

echinocereus engelmannii.name: Engelmann's hedgehog cactus
echinocereus engelmannii.desc: Engelmann's hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus engelmannii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 92 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus engelmannii.about: Echinocereus engelmannii, the strawberry hedgehog cactus or Engelmann's hedgehog cactus, is a cactus commonly found in desert areas of the southwestern United States and the adjacent areas of Mexico,…

echinocereus fasciculatus.name: Bundle hedgehog
echinocereus fasciculatus.desc: Bundle hedgehog (Echinocereus fasciculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus fasciculatus.about: Echinocereus fasciculatus, commonly known as pinkflower hedgehog cactus, is a clumping cactus (Cactaceae) with brilliant magenta flowers and long spines found in the Sonoran Desert.

echinocereus reichenbachii.name: Classen's cactus
echinocereus reichenbachii.desc: Lace hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus reichenbachii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 80 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus reichenbachii.about: Echinocereus reichenbachii is a perennial plant and shrub in the cactus family.

echinocereus rigidissimus.name: Arizona rainbow cactus
echinocereus rigidissimus.desc: Arizona rainbow cactus (Echinocereus rigidissimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 97 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocereus triglochidiatus.name: Claretcup
echinocereus triglochidiatus.desc: Claretcup (Echinocereus triglochidiatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 173 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus triglochidiatus.about: Echinocereus triglochidiatus is a species of hedgehog cactus known by several common names, including kingcup cactus, claret cup cactus, red-flowered hedgehog cactus and Mojave mound cactus.

echinocereus viridiflorus.name: Nylon hedgehog cactus
echinocereus viridiflorus.desc: Nylon hedgehog cactus (Echinocereus viridiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocereus viridiflorus.about: Echinocereus viridiflorus is a species of cactus known by the common names nylon hedgehog cactus, green pitaya, and small-flowered hedgehog cactus.

echinochloa.name: Wild millet grasses
echinochloa.desc: Floodplain grasses that spread over the semi-flooded plains as water rises, forming rich seasonal pasture.
echinochloa.about: Echinochloa is a very widespread genus of plants in the grass family and tribe Paniceae. Some of the species are known by the common names barnyard grass or cockspur grass.

echinochloa muricata.name: Rough Barnyardgrass
echinochloa muricata.desc: Rough Barnyardgrass (Echinochloa muricata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

echinocystis lobata.name: Wild Mockcucumber
echinocystis lobata.desc: Wild Mockcucumber (Echinocystis lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
echinocystis lobata.about: Echinocystis is a monotypic genus in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae. The sole species is E. lobata, commonly called wild cucumber and prickly cucumber.

echinopepon bigelovii.name: Desert starvine
echinopepon bigelovii.desc: Desert starvine (Echinopepon bigelovii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
echinopepon bigelovii.about: Brandegea is a monotypic genus containing the single species Brandegea bigelovii, the desert starvine.

echium vulgare.name: Viper's Bugloss
echium vulgare.desc: Viper's Bugloss (Echium vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
echium vulgare.about: Echium vulgare, known as viper's bugloss and blueweed, is a species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.

eelgrass and widgeon grass.name: Underwater grasses
eelgrass and widgeon grass.desc: Submerged grass beds that give food and shelter, add oxygen and clear the water. Eelgrass in the southern bay has shrunk by more than half since the early 1970s.
eelgrass and widgeon grass.about: Aquatic plants, also referred to as hydrophytes, are vascular plants and non-vascular plants that have adapted to live in aquatic environments.

egretta caerulea.name: Little blue heron
egretta caerulea.desc: A wading heron that hunts by sight for fish and crabs; in some mangroves crabs make up most of its diet.
egretta caerulea.about: The little blue heron is a small heron of the genus Egretta. It is a small, darkly colored heron with a two-toned bill.

egretta garzetta.name: Little egret
egretta garzetta.desc: The most recorded bird around the lagoon; it stalks shallows for fish, amphibians and insects.
egretta garzetta.about: The little egret is a species of small heron in the family Ardeidae. It is a white bird with a slender black beak, long black legs and, in the western race, yellow feet.

egretta gularis.name: Western reef heron
egretta gularis.desc: Wades in shallows for fish, crustaceans and molluscs; on coasts mudskippers are a regular part of its diet.
egretta gularis.about: The western reef heron, also called the western reef egret, is a medium-sized heron found in Africa and parts of Asia, with vagrancy occurring in Europe and the Americas.

egretta sacra.name: Pacific reef heron
egretta sacra.desc: The second most-recorded bird near the bay. It wades along rocky shores and eats small fish and crustaceans.
egretta sacra.about: The Pacific reef heron, also known as the eastern reef heron or eastern reef egret, is a species of heron found throughout southern Asia and Oceania.

eidolon helvum.name: Straw-coloured fruit bat
eidolon helvum.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, flowers and nectar. It spreads seeds and is the main disperser of the African teak tree.
eidolon helvum.about: The straw-coloured fruit bat is a large fruit bat that is the most widely distributed of all the African megabats.

elaeagnus angustifolia.name: Russian Olive
elaeagnus angustifolia.desc: Russian Olive (Elaeagnus angustifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.
elaeagnus angustifolia.about: Elaeagnus angustifolia, commonly called Russian olive, silver berry, oleaster, or wild olive, is a species of Elaeagnus, native to Asia and limited areas of eastern Europe.

elaeagnus umbellata.name: Spreading Oleaster
elaeagnus umbellata.desc: Spreading Oleaster (Elaeagnus umbellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
elaeagnus umbellata.about: Elaeagnus umbellata is a species of flowering plant known as Japanese silverberry, umbellata oleaster, autumn olive, autumn elaeagnus, spreading oleaster, autumnberry, or autumn berry.

elaeis guineensis.name: Oil palm
elaeis guineensis.desc: A palm whose fruit feeds many animals. GBIF records show it in the area, and palm-nut vultures, chimpanzees and monkeys are all recorded eating it.
elaeis guineensis.about: Elaeis guineensis is a species of palm commonly called oil palm but also sometimes African oil palm or macaw-fat.

elaeocarpus sylvestris.name: Japanese blueberry tree
elaeocarpus sylvestris.desc: A common forest tree whose fruits are eaten by island birds such as the Japanese white-eye.
elaeocarpus sylvestris.about: Elaeocarpus sylvestris, the woodland elaeocarpus, is a species of flowering plant in the family Elaeocarpaceae.

elaphe dione.name: Steppe rat snake
elaphe dione.desc: Widespread snake of grasslands, shrubland and rocky ground up to about 3,580 m, taking small vertebrates.
elaphe dione.about: Elaphe dione, commonly known as Dione's rat snake, the steppe rat snake, or the steppes rat snake, is a species of snake in the family Colubridae. The species is native to Asia and Eastern Europe.

electrona carlsbergi.name: Lanternfish
electrona carlsbergi.desc: Small, abundant deep-sea fish that rise toward the surface at night and are the staple food of king penguins and many other predators.
electrona carlsbergi.about: Lanternfish (or myctophids, from the Greek μυκτήρ myktḗr, "nose" and ophis, "serpent") are small mesopelagic fish of the large family Myctophidae.

eleocharis dulcis.name: Spike-rush & sedges
eleocharis dulcis.desc: Wetland sedge whose bulbs (corms) are eaten by magpie geese in the dry season. It grows in shallow water and mud on the floodplains.
eleocharis dulcis.about: Eleocharis dulcis, the Chinese water chestnut or water chestnut, is a grass-like sedge native to Asia, tropical Africa, and Oceania.

eleocharis obtusa.name: Blunt Spikerush
eleocharis obtusa.desc: Blunt Spikerush (Eleocharis obtusa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
eleocharis obtusa.about: Eleocharis obtusa is a species of spikesedge known by the common name blunt spikerush.

eleocharis palustris.name: Common Spike-rush
eleocharis palustris.desc: Common Spike-rush (Eleocharis palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
eleocharis palustris.about: Eleocharis palustris, the common spike-rush, creeping spike-rush or marsh spike-rush, is a species of mat-forming perennial flowering plants in the sedge family Cyperaceae.

eleocharis quadrangulata.name: Square-stem spike-rush
eleocharis quadrangulata.desc: Square-stem spike-rush (Eleocharis quadrangulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

eleodes.name: Darkling beetles
eleodes.desc: Ground beetles of desert country that feed on plant material and detritus and are common food for small predators.
eleodes.about: Eleodes is a genus of darkling beetles in the family Tenebrionidae.

eleodes armata.name: Armored stink beetle
eleodes armata.desc: Flightless darkling beetle that scavenges plant litter and is a common ground insect on desert sand.
eleodes armata.about: Eleodes is a genus of darkling beetles in the family Tenebrionidae.

eleodes hirtipennis.name: Darkling beetle
eleodes hirtipennis.desc: Eleodes beetles mostly eat plant and animal debris, scavenging at night. They spray a foul liquid, yet coyotes and owls still eat them.
eleodes hirtipennis.about: Eleodes is a genus of darkling beetles in the family Tenebrionidae.

elephas maximus.name: Asian elephant
elephas maximus.desc: A huge grazer and browser of grass, leaves and bark that moves through forest and grassland.
elephas maximus.about: The Asian elephant, also known as the Asiatic elephant, is the only living species in the genus Elephas.

eleutherodactylus.name: Robber frogs
eleutherodactylus.desc: Small, direct-developing forest frogs that eat arthropods in leaf litter and are recorded in the park.
eleutherodactylus.about: Eleutherodactylus is a genus of frogs in the family Eleutherodactylidae.

eleutherodactylus coqui.name: Common coquí
eleutherodactylus coqui.desc: A nocturnal sit-and-wait frog that mainly eats arthropods and can reach very high densities. It lays eggs on land and has no tadpole stage.
eleutherodactylus coqui.about: The common coquí, widely known as the coquí, is a species of frog native to Puerto Rico belonging to the family Eleutherodactylidae.

elkalyce comyntas.name: Elkalyce comyntas
elkalyce comyntas.desc: Elkalyce comyntas (Elkalyce comyntas): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

ellisia nyctelea.name: False Babyblueeyes
ellisia nyctelea.desc: False Babyblueeyes (Ellisia nyctelea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
ellisia nyctelea.about: Ellisia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Hydrophyllaceae, containing the sole species Ellisia nyctelea.

elymus glaucus.name: Blue wild rye
elymus glaucus.desc: Blue wild rye (Elymus glaucus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.
elymus glaucus.about: Elymus glaucus is a species of grass known as blue wild rye or blue wildrye. This grass is native to North America from Alaska to New York to northern Mexico.

elymus smithii.name: Western Wheat Grass
elymus smithii.desc: Western Wheat Grass (Elymus smithii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

emoia concolor.name: Fiji green emo skink
emoia concolor.desc: A native skink, a small lizard of Fiji forests that eats small invertebrates.
emoia concolor.about: Emoia concolor, the Fiji green emo skink or Viti slender treeskink, is a species of lizard in the family Scincidae. It is found on Rotuma in Fiji.

emoia cyanura.name: Copper-tailed skink
emoia cyanura.desc: A common small Pacific skink that hunts small invertebrates on the forest floor and in clearings.
emoia cyanura.about: Emoia cyanura, the copper-tailed skink, is a species of skink. It is found in Borneo, Clipperton Island and other South Pacific islands.

empetrum nigrum.name: Black crowberry
empetrum nigrum.desc: A low evergreen tundra shrub with black berries that ptarmigan, caribou and other animals eat, as recorded in GloBI.
empetrum nigrum.about: Empetrum nigrum, the crowberry, black crowberry, mossberry, rockberry, or, in western Alaska, Labrador, etc., blackberry, is a flowering plant species in the heather family Ericaceae with a near…

empetrum rubrum.name: Diddle-dee
empetrum rubrum.desc: A low evergreen shrub of heath and above the tree line; GloBI records upland geese eating it.
empetrum rubrum.about: Empetrum rubrum, known as red crowberry or diddle-dee (Chilean Spanish: Murtilla de Magallanes), is a species of plant in the heath family, Ericaceae.

empidonax minimus.name: Least Flycatcher
empidonax minimus.desc: Least Flycatcher (Empidonax minimus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
empidonax minimus.about: The least flycatcher is a small insect-eating bird. It is the smallest Empidonax flycatcher in eastern North America.

enallagma civile.name: Familiar Bluet
enallagma civile.desc: Familiar Bluet (Enallagma civile): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
enallagma civile.about: The familiar bluet is a narrow-winged damselfly of the family Coenagrionidae, which is native to much of the United States and southern Canada. In a broader sense, it is a part of the order Odonata.

encelia.name: Desert shrubs
encelia.desc: Low, sun-loving shrubs of the sandy plains. Browsers eat the foliage, and rodents eat seeds of desert plants like these.
encelia.about: Encelia is a genus of the plant family Asteraceae whose members are frequently called brittlebushes.

encelia californica.name: California brittlebush
encelia californica.desc: California brittlebush (Encelia californica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.

encelia farinosa.name: Brittlebush
encelia farinosa.desc: A silvery shrub with yellow flowers that grows on rocky desert slopes.
encelia farinosa.about: Encelia farinosa, is a common desert shrub of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It has a variety of historical uses.

encelia virginensis.name: Virgin River brittlebush
encelia virginensis.desc: Virgin River brittlebush (Encelia virginensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

enemion biternatum.name: Eastern false rue anemone
enemion biternatum.desc: Eastern false rue anemone (Enemion biternatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.
enemion biternatum.about: Enemion biternatum, commonly known as the false rue-anemone, is a spring ephemeral native to moist deciduous woodland in the eastern United States and extreme southern Ontario.

engelmannia peristenia.name: Engelmann's daisy
engelmannia peristenia.desc: Engelmann's daisy (Engelmannia peristenia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

engraulis anchoita.name: Argentine anchoita
engraulis anchoita.desc: A small schooling fish of the Argentine coast that feeds on zooplankton and is prey for larger fish, squid, sea lions and penguins.
engraulis anchoita.about: The Argentine anchoita or Argentine anchovy is an anchovy of the genus Engraulis, found in and around waters of Argentina, Uruguay and southern Brazil.

engraulis encrasicolus, sardinops sagax.name: Cape anchovy & sardine
engraulis encrasicolus, sardinops sagax.desc: Small schooling fish that eat plankton and feed the seals and seabirds of the Skeleton Coast.

engraulis mordax.name: Northern anchovy
engraulis mordax.desc: A schooling fish that eats plankton and is a main food for sea lions and seabirds.
engraulis mordax.about: The Californian anchovy or northern anchovy is a species of anchovy found in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, ranging from Mexico to British Columbia.

enhydra lutris.name: Sea otter
enhydra lutris.desc: A marine weasel that eats shellfish and other seafloor animals. It is recorded in the park and is preyed on by orcas.
enhydra lutris.about: The sea otter is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.

enhydra lutris nereis.name: Southern sea otter
enhydra lutris nereis.desc: Eats urchins, abalone, crabs and mussels, which keeps urchin numbers down and lets kelp grow. Great white sharks are its main predator in California.
enhydra lutris nereis.about: The sea otter is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.

enhydris enhydris.name: Rainbow water snake
enhydris enhydris.desc: A freshwater snake of Southeast Asian wetlands that hunts fish and frogs.
enhydris enhydris.about: The rainbow water snake is a species of mildly venomous, rear-fanged, colubrid snake, endemic to Asia.

environment.name: River floods
environment.desc: Water from the Congaree and Wateree rivers regularly covers the forest floor.

eolophus roseicapilla.name: Galah
eolophus roseicapilla.desc: A pink and grey cockatoo that feeds on seeds and plant material, including pink mulla mulla in GloBI records.
eolophus roseicapilla.about: The galah, less commonly known as the pink and grey cockatoo, galah cockatoo, or rose-breasted cockatoo, is an Australian species of cockatoo and the only member of the genus Eolophus.

epargyreus clarus.name: Silver-spotted Skipper
epargyreus clarus.desc: Silver-spotted Skipper (Epargyreus clarus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
epargyreus clarus.about: Epargyreus clarus, the silver-spotted skipper, is a butterfly of the family Hesperiidae. It is claimed to be the most recognized skipper in North America.

epeolus scutellaris.name: Notch-backed Cellophane-cuckoo Bee
epeolus scutellaris.desc: Notch-backed Cellophane-cuckoo Bee (Epeolus scutellaris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

eperua falcata.name: Wallaba
eperua falcata.desc: A legume tree of northern South America, also called bootlace tree, that can grow even in pure white sand. Its timber resists decay.
eperua falcata.about: Eperua falcata, the bootlace tree, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae, native to northern South America.

ephedra intermedia.name: Ephedra
ephedra intermedia.desc: A low, leafless shrub of dry rocky ground whose berries are eaten by Himalayan snowcocks.
ephedra intermedia.about: Ephedra is a genus of gymnosperm shrubs. As of July 2025, 74 species, and two hybrids, are accepted.

ephedra trifurca.name: Longleaf joint-fir
ephedra trifurca.desc: Longleaf joint-fir (Ephedra trifurca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
ephedra trifurca.about: Ephedra trifurca is a species of Ephedra known by the common names longleaf jointfir and Mexican tea.

ephedra viridis.name: Green ephedra
ephedra viridis.desc: Green ephedra (Ephedra viridis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 85 times near the park in GBIF.
ephedra viridis.about: Ephedra viridis, known by the common names green Mormon tea, Brigham tea, green ephedra, and Indian tea, is a species of Ephedra.

ephemeroptera.name: Mayflies
ephemeroptera.desc: Mayfly and other insect larvae live in the cold, fast Tara and mountain streams. They feed fish and other stream animals.
ephemeroptera.about: Mayflies are aquatic insects belonging to the order Ephemeroptera. This order is part of an ancient group of insects termed the Palaeoptera, which also contains dragonflies and damselflies.

epicauta puncticollis.name: Punctate blister beetle
epicauta puncticollis.desc: Punctate blister beetle (Epicauta puncticollis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
epicauta puncticollis.about: Epicauta puncticollis, the punctate blister beetle, is a species of blister beetle in the family Meloidae. It is found in Central America and North America.

epicrates inornatus.name: Puerto Rican boa
epicrates inornatus.desc: The island's largest snake. Adults eat mostly mammals (rats and bats), plus birds, anoles and a few frogs.
epicrates inornatus.about: The Puerto Rican boa, most commonly known as Culebrón ("big snake"), is a large species of boa endemic to Puerto Rico.

epigaea repens.name: Trailing Arbutus
epigaea repens.desc: Trailing Arbutus (Epigaea repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

eucalyptus tetrodonta.about: Eucalyptus tetrodonta, commonly known as Darwin stringybark or messmate, and known to the Yolngu peoples of Arnhem Land as gaḏayka, meaning "the word" or "message", is a species of medium-sized to…

euchaetes egle.name: Milkweed Tussock Moth
euchaetes egle.desc: Milkweed Tussock Moth (Euchaetes egle): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 38 times near the park in GBIF.

euchloe olympia.name: Olympia Marble
euchloe olympia.desc: Olympia Marble (Euchloe olympia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
euchloe olympia.about: Euchloe olympia, the Olympia marble, is a butterfly in the family Pieridae. Its range is southern Canada and the Midwest, down into the southwestern United States.

eudocimus ruber.name: Scarlet ibis
eudocimus ruber.desc: The swamp is the largest roost for this bird, which feeds on crustaceans, small fish, molluscs and insects; its red colour comes from the shellfish it eats.
eudocimus ruber.about: The scarlet ibis, sometimes called red ibis, is a species of ibis in the bird family Threskiornithidae. It inhabits tropical South America and part of the Caribbean.

eudorcas thomsonii.name: Thomson's gazelle
eudorcas thomsonii.desc: A small, fast grazer of the short-grass plains and the main food of cheetahs.
eudorcas thomsonii.about: Thomson's gazelle is one of the best known species of gazelles. It is named after explorer Joseph Thomson and is sometimes referred to as a "tommie".

eudyptes chrysocome.name: Southern rockhopper penguin
eudyptes chrysocome.desc: Breeds in colonies on the Falklands and eats mainly krill and other crustaceans, plus squid and some fish.
eudyptes chrysocome.about: The western rockhopper penguin is a species of rockhopper penguin. It occurs in subantarctic waters around the southern coast of South America and nearby islands.

eudyptes pachyrhynchus.name: Fiordland crested penguin
eudyptes pachyrhynchus.desc: Nests in coastal rainforest and feeds at sea, mostly on squid, krill and some fish.
eudyptes pachyrhynchus.about: The Fiordland penguin, also known as the Fiordland crested penguin (in Māori, tawaki), is a crested penguin species endemic to New Zealand.

eumetopias jubatus.name: Steller sea lion
eumetopias jubatus.desc: An opportunistic predator of schooling fish, including pollock, herring, sand lance and salmon. Orcas are the main predator.
eumetopias jubatus.about: The Steller sea lion, also known as Steller's sea lion or the northern sea lion, is a large, near-threatened species of sea lion, predominantly found in the coastal marine habitats of the northeast…

eunectes murinus.name: Green anaconda
eunectes murinus.desc: A heavy water snake that ambushes capybaras, fish and other snakes.
eunectes murinus.about: The green anaconda is a species of snake in the family Boidae (boas). The species is native to northern South America.

eunectes notaeus.name: Yellow anaconda
eunectes notaeus.desc: A generalist that hunts in shallow wetland water for wading birds, apple snails, reptiles and mammals, mostly as floods recede.
eunectes notaeus.about: The yellow anaconda, also known as the Paraguayan anaconda, is a boa species endemic to southern South America.

euonymus alatus.name: Burning Bush
euonymus alatus.desc: Burning Bush (Euonymus alatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

euonymus americanus.name: Bursting-heart
euonymus americanus.desc: Bursting-heart (Euonymus americanus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

euonymus atropurpureus.name: Bitter-ash
euonymus atropurpureus.desc: Bitter-ash (Euonymus atropurpureus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
euonymus atropurpureus.about: Euonymus atropurpureus is a species of shrub in the genus Euonymus and the larger bittersweet family. It has the common names American wahoo, eastern wahoo, burningbush and hearts bursting with love.

euonymus fortunei.name: Winter Creeper
euonymus fortunei.desc: Winter Creeper (Euonymus fortunei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

eupatorium capillifolium.name: Dog-fennel
eupatorium capillifolium.desc: Dog-fennel (Eupatorium capillifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

eupatorium rotundifolium.name: Roundleaf thoroughwort
eupatorium rotundifolium.desc: Roundleaf thoroughwort (Eupatorium rotundifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
eupatorium rotundifolium.about: Eupatorium rotundifolium, commonly called roundleaf thoroughwort, is a North American species of plant in the family Asteraceae.

eupatorium serotinum.name: Fall boneset
eupatorium serotinum.desc: Fall boneset (Eupatorium serotinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
eupatorium serotinum.about: Eupatorium serotinum, also known as late boneset or late thoroughwort, is a fall-blooming, perennial, herbaceous plant native to North America.

eupeodes volucris.name: Bird Hover Fly
eupeodes volucris.desc: Bird Hover Fly (Eupeodes volucris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.
eupeodes volucris.about: Eupeodes volucris, the large-tailed aphideater or bird hover fly, is a species of hover fly in the family Syrphidae.

euphagus cyanocephalus.name: Brewer's Blackbird
euphagus cyanocephalus.desc: Brewer's Blackbird (Euphagus cyanocephalus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

euphausia.name: Krill and zooplankton
euphausia.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and feed fish, penguins and seabirds.
euphausia.about: Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.

euphausia superba.name: Antarctic krill
euphausia superba.desc: Swarming crustacean that filters phytoplankton and scrapes ice algae. Whales, seals, penguins, squid and fish all eat it.
euphausia superba.about: Antarctic krill is a species of krill found in the Antarctic waters of the Southern Ocean.

euphausiacea.name: Krill
euphausiacea.desc: Small shrimp-like crustaceans that graze plankton and swarm in coastal water. A main food for humpbacks and schooling fish.
euphausiacea.about: Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.

euphorbia carunculata.name: Sand-dune spurge
euphorbia carunculata.desc: Sand-dune spurge (Euphorbia carunculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia corollata.name: Poison-milkweed
euphorbia corollata.desc: Poison-milkweed (Euphorbia corollata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
euphorbia corollata.about: Euphorbia corollata is an herbaceous perennial plant in the family Euphorbiaceae that is native to North America. A common name for the species is flowering spurge.

euphorbia davidii.name: David's Spurge
euphorbia davidii.desc: David's Spurge (Euphorbia davidii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia geyeri.name: Geyer's spurge
euphorbia geyeri.desc: Geyer's spurge (Euphorbia geyeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia glyptosperma.name: Ridgeseed Spurge
euphorbia glyptosperma.desc: Ridgeseed Spurge (Euphorbia glyptosperma): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia heterophylla.name: Painted Euphorbia
euphorbia heterophylla.desc: Painted Euphorbia (Euphorbia heterophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
euphorbia heterophylla.about: Euphorbia heterophylla, also known under the common names of Mexican fireplant, painted euphorbia, Japanese poinsettia, paintedleaf, painted spurge and milkweed, is a plant belonging to the…

euphorbia hyssopifolia.name: Hyssopleaf Sandmat
euphorbia hyssopifolia.desc: Hyssopleaf Sandmat (Euphorbia hyssopifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia marginata.name: Snow-On-The-Mountain
euphorbia marginata.desc: Snow-On-The-Mountain (Euphorbia marginata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia missurica.name: Missouri spurge
euphorbia missurica.desc: Missouri spurge (Euphorbia missurica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
euphorbia missurica.about: Euphorbia missurica, commonly called prairie sandmat, or Missouri spurge, is a species of flowering plant in the spurge family (Euphorbiaceae).

euphorbia nutans.name: Eyebane
euphorbia nutans.desc: Eyebane (Euphorbia nutans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia ouachitana.name: Ouachita spurge
euphorbia ouachitana.desc: Ouachita spurge (Euphorbia ouachitana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
euphorbia ouachitana.about: Euphorbia ouachitana, commonly called Ouachita spurge, is a species of flowering plant in the spurge family (Euphorbiaceae).

euphorbia prostrata.name: Prostrate Sandmat
euphorbia prostrata.desc: Prostrate Sandmat (Euphorbia prostrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia radians.name: Sun spurge
euphorbia radians.desc: Sun spurge (Euphorbia radians): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia serpens.name: Matted Sandmat
euphorbia serpens.desc: Matted Sandmat (Euphorbia serpens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
euphorbia serpens.about: Euphorbia serpens is a species of Euphorbia known by the common name matted sandmat. It is native to the Americas but it can be found on most continents as an introduced species and often a weed.

euphorbia serpillifolia.name: Thyme-leaf spurge
euphorbia serpillifolia.desc: Thyme-leaf spurge (Euphorbia serpillifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

euphorbia stictospora.name: Mat spurge
euphorbia stictospora.desc: Mat spurge (Euphorbia stictospora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

euphydryas phaeton.name: Baltimore Checkerspot
euphydryas phaeton.desc: Baltimore Checkerspot (Euphydryas phaeton): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
euphydryas phaeton.about: The Baltimore checkerspot is a North American butterfly of the family Nymphalidae.

euphyes conspicua.name: Black Dash
euphyes conspicua.desc: Black Dash (Euphyes conspicua): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

euplagia quadripunctaria.name: Jersey tiger moth
euplagia quadripunctaria.desc: A day-flying moth whose caterpillars feed on plants such as dwarf elder.
euplagia quadripunctaria.about: Euplagia quadripunctaria, the Jersey tiger, or Spanish flag, is a diurnal moth of the family Erebidae. The species was first described by Nikolaus Poda von Neuhaus in 1761.

euplexia benesimilis.name: American Angle Shade
euplexia benesimilis.desc: American Angle Shade (Euplexia benesimilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
euplexia benesimilis.about: Euplexia benesimilis, the American angle shades, is a species of cutworm or dart moth in the family Noctuidae. It is found in North America.

euploea.name: Crow butterflies
euploea.desc: Forest butterflies whose caterpillars feed on plants such as figs. Adults and young are food for lizards.
euploea.about: Euploea is a genus of milkweed butterflies. The species are generally dark in colouration, often quite blackish, for which reason they are commonly called crows.

euploea core.name: Common crow butterfly
euploea core.desc: A common butterfly whose caterpillars feed on fig and other milky-sapped plants, in turn eaten by frogs and birds.
euploea core.about: Euploea core, also known as the common crow, is a common butterfly found in South Asia to Australia.

euploea darchia.name: Small brown crow
euploea darchia.desc: A butterfly of the crow group, whose caterpillars feed on forest plants such as figs, and adults take nectar.
euploea darchia.about: Euploea is a genus of milkweed butterflies. The species are generally dark in colouration, often quite blackish, for which reason they are commonly called crows.

euptoieta claudia.name: Variegated Fritillary
euptoieta claudia.desc: Variegated Fritillary (Euptoieta claudia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
euptoieta claudia.about: Euptoieta claudia, the variegated fritillary, is a North and South American butterfly in the family Nymphalidae.

eurema daira.name: Barred Yellow
eurema daira.desc: Barred Yellow (Eurema daira): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

eurillas latirostris.name: Yellow-whiskered greenbul
eurillas latirostris.desc: The most-recorded bird near the park. It eats fruit and insects and so helps spread seeds.
eurillas latirostris.about: The yellow-whiskered greenbul or yellow-whiskered bulbul is a species of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is found in western and central Africa.

eurybia macrophylla.name: Bigleaf aster
eurybia macrophylla.desc: Bigleaf aster (Eurybia macrophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

eustoma russellianum.name: Eustoma russellianum
eustoma russellianum.desc: Eustoma russellianum (Eustoma russellianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
eustoma russellianum.about: Eustoma russellianum is a species of flowering plant in the gentian family. One of its previous binomial names was Eustoma grandiflorum.

euterpe edulis.name: Juçara palm
euterpe edulis.desc: An Atlantic Forest palm harvested for heart of palm until it became uncommon. Its fruits are a food for forest birds and mammals.
euterpe edulis.about: Euterpe edulis, commonly known as juçara, jussara (an archaic alternative spelling), açaí-do-sul or palmiteiro, is a palm species in the genus Euterpe. It is now predominantly used for hearts of palm.

euterpe oleracea.name: Açaí palm
euterpe oleracea.desc: Clusters of dark fruit feed toucans, tapirs and fish in flooded forest.
euterpe oleracea.about: The açaí palm, Euterpe oleracea, is a species of palm tree (Arecaceae) cultivated for its fruit, hearts of palm (a vegetable), leaves, and trunk wood.

eutrochium dubium.name: Coastal Plain Joe-pyeweed
eutrochium dubium.desc: Coastal Plain Joe-pyeweed (Eutrochium dubium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

eutrochium fistulosum.name: Trumpetweed
eutrochium fistulosum.desc: Trumpetweed (Eutrochium fistulosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

eutropis multifasciata.name: Brown mabuya skink
eutropis multifasciata.desc: A common forest-floor lizard that eats small invertebrates. GloBI records it eaten by the brown shrike, the common mock viper and the little egret.
eutropis multifasciata.about: Eutropis multifasciata, commonly known as the East Indian brown mabuya, many-lined sun skink, many-striped skink, common sun skink or (ambiguously) as golden skink, is a species of skink that…

euxoa auxiliaris.name: Army cutworm
euxoa auxiliaris.desc: Army cutworm (Euxoa auxiliaris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 155 times near the park in GBIF.

euxoa ochrogaster.name: Redbacked Cutworm
euxoa ochrogaster.desc: Redbacked Cutworm (Euxoa ochrogaster): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
euxoa ochrogaster.about: Euxoa ochrogaster, the red-backed cutworm, is a moth of the family Noctuidae. It is found from Iceland and northern Europe, through the Baltic to the Amur region.

excoecaria agallocha.name: Gewa
excoecaria agallocha.desc: A salt-tolerant mangrove tree that grows alongside sundri, goran and keora in the tidal forest.
excoecaria agallocha.about: Excoecaria agallocha, a mangrove species, belongs to the genus Excoecaria of the family Euphorbiaceae.

exocoetidae.name: Flying fish
exocoetidae.desc: Plankton-feeding fish of the open sea. They are the most common prey of great frigatebirds.
exocoetidae.about: The Exocoetidae are a family of saltwater ray-finned fish in the order Beloniformes, known colloquially as flying fish or flying cod, with about 64 species in seven genera.

exomala orientalis.name: Oriental Beetle
exomala orientalis.desc: Oriental Beetle (Exomala orientalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

fagus grandifolia.name: American Beech
fagus grandifolia.desc: A hardwood of the moister forest whose nuts and leaves feed deer, beavers and caterpillars.
fagus grandifolia.about: Fagus grandifolia, the American beech or North American beech, is a species of tree growing to 16–35 meters (52–115 feet) tall.

fagus orientalis.name: Oriental beech
fagus orientalis.desc: A dominant broadleaf tree of the Caucasus mid-mountain forests; its nuts feed boar and rodents.
fagus orientalis.about: Fagus orientalis, the Oriental beech, is a deciduous tree in the family Fagaceae. It is native to Thrace in the southeastern Balkans in Europe, and Turkey in Western Asia.

fagus sylvatica.name: European beech
fagus sylvatica.desc: The dominant tree of the site. UNESCO says beech has spread across Europe since the last Ice Age, and these stands show that natural process.
fagus sylvatica.about: Fagus sylvatica, the European beech or common beech, is a species of tree in the flowering plant family Fagaceae.

faidherbia albida.name: Winter thorn
faidherbia albida.desc: A tree that sheds its leaves in the rainy season. Elephants, antelope, buffalo and baboons eat its pods, and it fixes nitrogen.
faidherbia albida.about: Faidherbia is a genus of fabaceous plants containing one species, Faidherbia albida, which was formerly widely included in the genus Acacia as Acacia albida.

faidherbia albida, salvadora and others.name: Ana tree & riverbed shrubs
faidherbia albida, salvadora and others.desc: Trees and shrubs along dry rivers. Desert elephants feed on the leaves and seedpods of ana trees in the dry season.
faidherbia albida, salvadora and others.about: Faidherbia is a genus of fabaceous plants containing one species, Faidherbia albida, which was formerly widely included in the genus Acacia as Acacia albida.

falco berigora.name: Brown falcon
falco berigora.desc: A widespread raptor that hunts lizards, small birds and other prey in open country; GloBI records show it taking several lizard species.
falco berigora.about: The brown falcon is a relatively large falcon native to Australia and New Guinea. A number of plumage morphs occur, with the primary distinction being between the pale morph and the dark morph.

falco biarmicus.name: Lanner falcon
falco biarmicus.desc: A fast falcon that hunts birds over open country.
falco biarmicus.about: The lanner falcon is a medium-sized bird of prey that breeds in Africa, southeast Europe and just into Asia.

falco cherrug.name: Saker falcon
falco cherrug.desc: A falcon of open steppe whose main prey in Europe is ground squirrels and pigeons; it often nests in old stick nests in trees.
falco cherrug.about: The saker falcon is a large falcon species. It breeds from Central Europe eastwards across the Palearctic to Manchuria.

falco mexicanus.name: Prairie falcon
falco mexicanus.desc: Nests on cliff ledges, and Pinnacles has some of the highest breeding densities in North America. Hunts ground squirrels and birds.
falco mexicanus.about: The prairie falcon is a medium-sized falcon found in Western North America.

falco novaeseelandiae.name: Kārearea (NZ falcon)
falco novaeseelandiae.desc: Bush falcons hunt forest edges in North Island forests. They catch mostly birds in flight, plus some hares and rabbits.
falco novaeseelandiae.about: The New Zealand falcon is New Zealand's only falcon, and one of only four living native and two endemic birds of prey. It is frequently mistaken for the larger and more common swamp harrier.

falco peregrinus.name: Peregrine falcon
falco peregrinus.desc: A migrant visitor that hunts birds over the keys. GloBI records it eating sooty terns and ruddy turnstones.
falco peregrinus.about: The peregrine falcon, sometimes referred to simply as the peregrine, is a bird of prey (raptor) in the family Falconidae known for its speed.

falco rupicolus.name: Rock kestrel
falco rupicolus.desc: A small falcon that hunts lizards and insects from cliffs and open ground.
falco rupicolus.about: The rock kestrel is a bird of prey species belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae. It was previously considered a subspecies of the common kestrel.

falco sparverius.name: American Kestrel
falco sparverius.desc: American Kestrel (Falco sparverius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 425 times near the park in GBIF.
falco sparverius.about: The American kestrel is the smallest and most common falcon in the Americas.

falco tinnunculus.name: Eurasian kestrel
falco tinnunculus.desc: A small falcon, recorded here nearly 200 times. GloBI lists jirds and blackbirds among its prey.
falco tinnunculus.about: The common kestrel, also known as the European kestrel, Eurasian kestrel, Old World kestrel, is a species of predatory bird belonging to the kestrel group of the falcon family Falconidae.

fallugia paradoxa.name: Apache plume
fallugia paradoxa.desc: A shrub of rocky desert slopes and canyons, recorded in GloBI as browse for mule deer.
fallugia paradoxa.about: Fallugia is a monotypic genus of flowering plants containing the single species Fallugia paradoxa, which is known by the common names Apache plume and póñil.

farfantepenaeus aztecus.name: Brown shrimp
farfantepenaeus aztecus.desc: Young shrimp grow in coastal marshes and then move offshore, where trawlers first reported the dead zone in 1950.

farfantepenaeus duorarum.name: Pink shrimp
farfantepenaeus duorarum.desc: Young shrimp use seagrass and mangrove shallows as nurseries and feed on small bottom matter.
farfantepenaeus duorarum.about: Farfantepenaeus duorarum is a species of marine penaeid shrimp found around Bermuda, along the east coast of the United States and in the Gulf of Mexico.

fargesia.name: Arrow bamboo
fargesia.desc: Evergreen mountain bamboo that forms the understory. Wild pandas eat about 25 bamboo species, including Fargesia ones, so it underpins much of this web.
fargesia.about: Fargesia is a genus of flowering plants in the grass family. These bamboos are native primarily to China, with a few species in Vietnam and in the eastern Himalayas.

fejervarya limnocharis.name: Asian grass frog
fejervarya limnocharis.desc: A common frog of paddies and wet ground that eats insects and is itself prey for snakes and birds.
fejervarya limnocharis.about: Fejervarya limnocharis is a species of frog found in South East Asia and parts of Indochina. It is known under many common names, including Boie's wart frog, rice field frog, and Asian grass frog.

felis catus.name: Cat
felis catus.desc: Cat (Felis catus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
felis catus.about: A feral cat is an unowned domestic cat that lives freely outdoors and avoids human contact; it does not allow itself to be handled or touched, and usually remains hidden from humans.

felis chaus.name: Jungle cat
felis chaus.desc: A small wild cat of wet grassland and scrub that hunts deer fawns, rodents and birds.
felis chaus.about: The jungle cat, also called reed cat and swamp cat, is a medium-sized cat native from the Eastern Mediterranean region and the Caucasus to parts of Central, South and Southeast Asia.

felis margarita.name: Sand cat
felis margarita.desc: A small desert cat that hunts at night for rodents and birds, and also kills lizards and venomous snakes. It gets most of its water from prey.
felis margarita.about: The sand cat is a small wild cat that inhabits sandy and stony deserts far from water sources. With its sandy to light grey fur, it is well camouflaged in a desert environment.

felis silvestris.name: European wildcat
felis silvestris.desc: A shy forest cat. In the Carpathians it feeds mainly on yellow-necked mice and voles.
felis silvestris.about: The European wildcat is a small wildcat species that was described in the late 18th century. Its fur is brownish to grey with stripes on the forehead and on the sides.

fendlera rupicola.name: Fendlerbush
fendlera rupicola.desc: Fendlerbush (Fendlera rupicola): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 70 times near the park in GBIF.
fendlera rupicola.about: Fendlera rupicola, commonly known as the cliff fendlerbush or the false mockorange, is a shrub that grows in dry locations in the south central mountain regions of North America.

ferocactus cylindraceus.name: Le Conte barrel cactus
ferocactus cylindraceus.desc: Le Conte barrel cactus (Ferocactus cylindraceus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 183 times near the park in GBIF.
ferocactus cylindraceus.about: Ferocactus cylindraceus is a species of barrel cactus which is known by several common names, including California barrel cactus, Desert barrel cactus, compass barrel cactus, and miner's compass.

ferocactus wislizeni.name: Arizona barrel cactus
ferocactus wislizeni.desc: Arizona barrel cactus (Ferocactus wislizeni): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

festuca.name: Bunchgrasses
festuca.desc: Fescue-type grasses cover open slopes and meadows and are staple grazing for elk, sheep and goats.
festuca.about: Festuca (fescue) is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the grass family Poaceae (subfamily Pooideae).

festuca and other grasses.name: Afroalpine grasses
festuca and other grasses.desc: Tussock grasses and herbs of the high moorland and montane grassland. They feed the root-rats, hares and grazing antelope.
festuca and other grasses.about: Festuca (fescue) is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the grass family Poaceae (subfamily Pooideae).

festuca campestris.name: Rough fescue & montane grasses
festuca campestris.desc: Bunchgrass of montane and foothill grassland that feeds elk, bighorn sheep and ground squirrels.
festuca campestris.about: Festuca campestris, also known as the mountain rough fescue, is a species of grass in the family Poaceae. This species prefer subalpine grasslands and grow in higher elevations.

festuca caprina.name: Goat-beard grass
festuca caprina.desc: The most frequently recorded plant near the reserve, a tussock grass of the Afromontane grassland.
festuca caprina.about: Festuca caprina is a species of grass in the family Poaceae. This species is native to Cape Provinces, Eswatini, Free State, KwaZulu-Natal, Lesotho, Malawi, Northern Provinces, Tanzania, Zambia, and…

festuca gracillima.name: Coirón fescue
festuca gracillima.desc: The main grass of the Patagonian steppe, tolerant of wind and harsh weather; grazed by guanaco, hares and geese.
festuca gracillima.about: Festuca gracillima is a species of grass in the family Poaceae. This species is native to southern Argentina, and southern Chile.

festuca kashmiriana.name: Kashmir fescue
festuca kashmiriana.desc: A tussock grass of the alpine steppe that forms part of the pasture grazed by plateau herbivores.
festuca kashmiriana.about: Festuca (fescue) is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the grass family Poaceae (subfamily Pooideae).

festuca rubra.name: Meadow grasses and herbs
festuca rubra.desc: Grasses and flowers of glades and mountain meadows, grazed by deer and bison.
festuca rubra.about: Festuca rubra is a species of grass known by the common name red fescue, creeping red fescue or the rush-leaf fescue.

ficus.name: Fig trees
ficus.desc: Fig trees bear fruit that fruit-eating bats, birds and primates eat. Ficus luschnathiana is among the well-recorded plants here.
ficus.about: Ficus is a genus of about 850 species of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae.

ficus abutilifolia.name: Rock fig
ficus abutilifolia.desc: A fig that grows on rocky outcrops near the shore. Its fruit is recorded in the diet of birds such as the bulbul.
ficus abutilifolia.about: Ficus abutilifolia, the large-leaved rock fig, is a species of African rock-splitting fig that occurs in two disjunct regions, one population north, and another south of the equator.

ficus benghalensis.name: Banyan
ficus benghalensis.desc: A large fig tree whose fruit is eaten by many birds and mammals, including golden jackals in GloBI records.
ficus benghalensis.about: Ficus benghalensis, Ficus indica, or Ficus audrey commonly known as banyan, banyan fig, audrey fig and Indian banyan, is a tree native to the Indian subcontinent.

ficus carica.name: Common fig
ficus carica.desc: A fruit tree that grows wild on rocky slopes and near water; its fruit is eaten by many birds and mammals.
ficus carica.about: The fig is the edible fruit of Ficus carica (the common fig), a species of tree or shrub in the flowering plant family Moraceae, native to the Mediterranean region, and to western and southern Asia.

ficus spp..name: Strangler fig
ficus spp..desc: Fruits through much of the year, so it feeds monkeys, birds and fish when little else is ripe.
ficus spp..about: Ficus is a genus of about 850 species of woody trees, shrubs, vines, epiphytes and hemiepiphytes in the family Moraceae.

ficus variegata.name: Variegated fig
ficus variegata.desc: A fig tree of tropical forest whose fruit is eaten by monkeys, bats and fruit-eating birds, and was recorded in the park area.

fifth season.name: Spring flood
fifth season.desc: Snowmelt from the uplands spreads over meadows and forests each spring, flooding up to 175 square kilometres.

fimbristylis autumnalis.name: Slender Fimbry
fimbristylis autumnalis.desc: Slender Fimbry (Fimbristylis autumnalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

fimbristylis vahlii.name: Vahl's Fimbry
fimbristylis vahlii.desc: Vahl's Fimbry (Fimbristylis vahlii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

fiord seawater.name: Fiord seawater
fiord seawater.desc: Glaciers carved deep fiords along the coast, and their cool, steep-sided waters feed the marine plankton.

fire.name: Fire
fire.desc: Lightning fires, mostly in the wet season, and deep peat fires in dry spells renew sawgrass marshes.

flood pulse & river flow.name: Flood pulse & river flow
flood pulse & river flow.desc: Spring floods spread water, silt and fish across the floodplain. When the water drops, bare mud flats grow moist-soil plants.

floodplain silt.name: Floodplain silt
floodplain silt.desc: Soil laid down by the river on the terraces. It supports the riverine woodland and grasses.

floodplain silt and nutrients.name: Floodplain silt and nutrients
floodplain silt and nutrients.desc: Silt and dissolved nutrients left by the river and by decaying plants feed the wetland vegetation.

floodplain soil.name: Floodplain soil
floodplain soil.desc: Soil that stores the nutrients plants draw on.

floodplain soil & nutrients.name: Floodplain soil & nutrients
floodplain soil & nutrients.desc: Sediment and rotting plant matter left by the floods feed new growth.

floodwater.name: Floodwater
floodwater.desc: Rain fills the wetland, which is rainfall-fed. Shallow water supports the aquatic plants that deer and capybara eat.

foeniculum vulgare.name: Fennel
foeniculum vulgare.desc: Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 61 times near the park in GBIF.
foeniculum vulgare.about: Fennel is a flowering plant species in the carrot family. It is a hardy, perennial herb with yellow flowers and feathery leaves.

fomes fomentarius.name: Deadwood fungi
fomes fomentarius.desc: Bracket fungi such as tinder fungus rot dead beech wood, returning nutrients and making wood softer for beetles.

forelius pruinosus.name: High Noon Ant
forelius pruinosus.desc: High Noon Ant (Forelius pruinosus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.
forelius pruinosus.about: Forelius pruinosus, commonly known as the high noon ant, is a species of ant in the genus Forelius.

forest soil.name: Forest soil
forest soil.desc: Nutrient-rich soil built from leaf litter and dead matter supports the forest plants.

forest soil & leaf litter.name: Forest soil & leaf litter
forest soil & leaf litter.desc: Thin mountain soils and fallen leaves hold the nutrients that trees, shrubs and the small animals of the forest floor depend on.

forest soil & litter.name: Forest soil & litter
forest soil & litter.desc: Leaf litter and soil hold nutrients that plants take up again.

forest soil & nutrients.name: Forest soil & nutrients
forest soil & nutrients.desc: Leaf litter and decaying wood build the soil that the trees and shrubs draw on.

forest soil & peat.name: Forest soil & peat
forest soil & peat.desc: Soils and peat swamps store nutrients and carbon. Wikipedia notes the park peat swamp forests hold carbon at high density.

forest soil and deadwood.name: Forest soil and deadwood
forest soil and deadwood.desc: Forest soil and rotting wood store nutrients that trees and shrubs draw on once decomposers release them.

forest soil and fallen logs.name: Forest soil and fallen logs
forest soil and fallen logs.desc: Fallen redwoods hold moisture and slowly return nutrients to the soil, and act as nursery sites for seedlings and homes for salamanders.

forest soil and leaf litter.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
forest soil and leaf litter.desc: Nutrients released from dead leaves, fruit and animals are taken up again by roots in the litter layer.

forest soil and litter.name: Forest soil and litter
forest soil and litter.desc: Leaf litter and soil hold the nutrients that the rainforest trees draw back up.

forest soil and nutrients.name: Forest soil and nutrients
forest soil and nutrients.desc: Leaf litter and dead wood break down into the nutrients that feed the beech and fir forest.

forest soil nutrients.name: Forest soil nutrients
forest soil nutrients.desc: Fallen logs, needles and carcasses break down into nutrients that the trees take up again.

formica obscuripes.name: Western thatching ant
formica obscuripes.desc: Western thatching ant (Formica obscuripes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

formicidae.name: Desert ants
formicidae.desc: Ants eat saguaro fruit, so few saguaro seeds survive to sprout, and they also gather seeds from annual plants.
formicidae.about: Ants are eusocial insects of the family Formicidae and, along with the related wasps and bees, belong to the order Hymenoptera. Ants evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the Cretaceous period.

foulehaio procerior.name: Kikau (wattled honeyeater)
foulehaio procerior.desc: A lively nectar-feeding honeyeater of Fijian forest and gardens, likely a pollinator of flowers.
foulehaio procerior.about: The kikau or western wattled honeyeater is a species of bird in the honeyeater family Meliphagidae.

fouquieria splendens.name: Ocotillo
fouquieria splendens.desc: Vine-cactus (Fouquieria splendens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
fouquieria splendens.about: Fouquieria splendens, commonly known as ocotillo, is a plant indigenous to the Mojave, Sonoran, Chihuahuan and Colorado deserts in the Southwestern United States (southern California, southern…

fragaria vesca.name: Wild Strawberry
fragaria vesca.desc: Wild Strawberry (Fragaria vesca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

fragaria virginiana.name: Thickleaved Wild Strawberry
fragaria virginiana.desc: Thickleaved Wild Strawberry (Fragaria virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
fragaria virginiana.about: Fragaria virginiana, known as Virginia strawberry, wild strawberry, common strawberry, or mountain strawberry, is a perennial North American strawberry that grows across much of the United States and…

frangula alnus.name: Glossy Buckthorn
frangula alnus.desc: Glossy Buckthorn (Frangula alnus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

frangula caroliniana.name: Indian-cherry
frangula caroliniana.desc: Indian-cherry (Frangula caroliniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
frangula caroliniana.about: Frangula caroliniana, commonly called the Carolina buckthorn, is a North American species of shrub or small tree.

frasera albicaulis.name: Whitestem elkweed
frasera albicaulis.desc: Whitestem elkweed (Frasera albicaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
frasera albicaulis.about: Frasera albicaulis is a species of flowering plant in the family Gentianaceae. It is known by the common name whitestem frasera.

frasera caroliniensis.name: American columbo
frasera caroliniensis.desc: American columbo (Frasera caroliniensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

frasera speciosa.name: Showy green gentian
frasera speciosa.desc: A tall flowering plant of mountain meadows. GloBI records Hunt's bumble bee feeding on it.
frasera speciosa.about: Frasera speciosa is a species of flowering plant in the gentian family (Gentianaceae) known by the common names elkweed, monument plant, and green gentian.

fratercula cirrhata.name: Tufted puffin
fratercula cirrhata.desc: A diving seabird that nests in burrows on cliffs and islands. Adults eat squid and krill, and chicks are fed mostly fish such as sand lance.
fratercula cirrhata.about: The tufted puffin, also known as crested puffin, is a relatively abundant medium-sized pelagic seabird in the auk family (Alcidae) found throughout the North Pacific Ocean.

fraxinus latifolia.name: Oregon ash
fraxinus latifolia.desc: Oregon ash (Fraxinus latifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

fraxinus velutina.name: Arizon ash
fraxinus velutina.desc: Arizon ash (Fraxinus velutina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

fregata magnificens.name: Magnificent frigatebird
fregata magnificens.desc: Takes fish, often flying fish, from the surface, and also harasses other seabirds until they drop their catch.
fregata magnificens.about: The magnificent frigatebird, frigate petrel or man o' war is a seabird of the frigatebird family Fregatidae.

fregata minor.name: Great frigatebird
fregata minor.desc: Breeds here in large numbers (subspecies aldabrensis). Snatches flying fish from the sea surface and sometimes steals food from other seabirds.
fregata minor.about: The great frigatebird is a large seabird in the frigatebird family.

freshwater algae.name: River algae and plants
freshwater algae.desc: Algae and water plants growing in the rivers and wetlands that cross the dry forest.
freshwater algae.about: Algae are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. It excludes the land plants (embryophytes).

freshwater flooding.name: Freshwater flooding
freshwater flooding.desc: Water covering the low, flat peninsula for much of the year keeps the swamp a wetland and shapes its marsh vegetation.

freshwater inflow.name: Freshwater inflow
freshwater inflow.desc: The Caroni River meets the Gulf of Paria here, mixing fresh and salt water and carrying silt and nutrients into the swamp.

fringilla coelebs.name: Common chaffinch
fringilla coelebs.desc: The most often recorded bird near the park. It eats seeds and fruit, and also insects.
fringilla coelebs.about: The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.

fritillaria purdyi.name: Purdy's fritillary
fritillaria purdyi.desc: Purdy's fritillary (Fritillaria purdyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
fritillaria purdyi.about: Fritillaria purdyi, the Purdy's fritillary, is a rare species of flowering plant in the lily family Liliaceae.

fulica americana.name: American Coot
fulica americana.desc: American Coot (Fulica americana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 247 times near the park in GBIF.
fulica americana.about: The American coot, also known as a mud hen or pouldeau, is a bird of the family Rallidae.

fulica ardesiaca.name: Slate-colored coot
fulica ardesiaca.desc: A waterbird that eats mostly aquatic plants, with Chara a main part of its diet. It nests among reeds or on floating vegetation.
fulica ardesiaca.about: The Andean coot, also known as the slate-colored coot, is a species of bird in subfamily Rallinae of family Rallidae, the rails, gallinules, and coots.

fulica atra.name: Eurasian coot
fulica atra.desc: A common waterbird of lagoons and reedbeds; GloBI records it eating common reed and other plants.
fulica atra.about: The Eurasian coot, also known as the common coot or Australian coot, is a member of the rail and crake bird family, the Rallidae.

fungi.name: Decomposers
fungi.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates that recycle fallen leaves, wood and carcasses.

fungi and bacteria.name: Decomposers
fungi and bacteria.desc: Break down dead leaves, wood and animals and return nutrients to the volcanic soil.

fungi and decomposers.name: Fungi and decomposers
fungi and decomposers.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil animals recycle fallen leaves, wood and carcasses back into the soil.

fungi and invertebrates.name: Decomposers
fungi and invertebrates.desc: Fungi, bacteria and litter animals that break down leaves, wood and dead seaweed and return nutrients to the soil.

fungi and soil microbes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
fungi and soil microbes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and spawned-out salmon and return nutrients to the soil.

fungi, bacteria & detritivores.name: Fungi, bacteria & detritivores
fungi, bacteria & detritivores.desc: Break down dead plants, animals and seaweed, and return nutrients to the soil and sea.

fungi, bacteria and invertebrates.name: Soil decomposers
fungi, bacteria and invertebrates.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dead leaves, wood and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

fungi, bacteria and termites.name: Leaf-litter decomposers
fungi, bacteria and termites.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and carcasses, returning nutrients to thin forest soil.

fungi, bacteria, termites.name: Soil decomposers
fungi, bacteria, termites.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the thin soil.

fungi, termites & bacteria.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
fungi, termites & bacteria.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the thin soil.

gadus chalcogrammus.name: Walleye pollock
gadus chalcogrammus.desc: A schooling cod relative of cold northern seas. It feeds on zooplankton and is key winter food for eagles and sea lions.
gadus chalcogrammus.about: The Alaska pollock also known as Pacific pollock or walleye pollock is a marine fish species of the cod genus Gadus and family Gadidae.

gaillardia aristata.name: Blanketflower
gaillardia aristata.desc: Blanketflower (Gaillardia aristata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
gaillardia aristata.about: Gaillardia aristata is a North American species of flowering plant in the sunflower family. It is known by the common names common blanketflower and common gaillardia.

gaillardia pulchella.name: Firewheel
gaillardia pulchella.desc: Firewheel (Gaillardia pulchella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
gaillardia pulchella.about: Gaillardia pulchella is a North American species of short-lived perennial or annual flowering plants in the sunflower family.

galax urceolata.name: Beetleweed
galax urceolata.desc: Beetleweed (Galax urceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 129 times near the park in GBIF.
galax urceolata.about: Galax, the wandplant, wandflower, or beetleweed, is a genus in the flowering plant family Diapensiaceae, containing a single species, Galax urceolata (syn. G. rotundifolia, G. aphylla).

galemys pyrenaicus.name: Pyrenean desman
galemys pyrenaicus.desc: A small, rare aquatic mole that eats mostly stream insect larvae, especially caddisflies. Its main predator is the otter.
galemys pyrenaicus.about: The Pyrenean desman, also known as the Iberian desman or trumpet rat, is a species of small semiaquatic mammal in the family Talpidae.

galeocerdo cuvier.name: Tiger shark
galeocerdo cuvier.desc: A large shark that eats sea turtles, fish and smaller sharks, and also scavenges dead animals.
galeocerdo cuvier.about: The tiger shark is a species of ground shark, and the only extant member of the genus Galeocerdo and family Galeocerdonidae.

galerella pulverulenta.name: Cape grey mongoose
galerella pulverulenta.desc: A small carnivore of scrub and fynbos that hunts rodents, reptiles and insects.
galerella pulverulenta.about: The Cape grey mongoose, also called the small grey mongoose, is a small mammal native to South Africa, Lesotho and southern Namibia.

galerida cristata.name: Crested lark
galerida cristata.desc: A common ground-feeding bird of open steppe that eats seeds and insects. It is among the most recorded birds here.
galerida cristata.about: The crested lark is a species of lark widespread across Eurasia and northern Africa. It is a non-migratory bird, but can occasionally be found as a vagrant in Great Britain.

galiniera saxifraga.name: Galiniera
galiniera saxifraga.desc: A montane shrub or small tree whose fruit is eaten by blue monkeys and several forest birds in recorded observations.
galiniera saxifraga.about: Galiniera is a genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. The genus is found in tropical Africa and Madagascar.

galium.name: Herbs and vines
galium.desc: Understory vines and herbs. Leaves, shoots and stems of such plants make up most of a gorilla's diet.
galium.about: Galium is a large genus of annual and perennial herbaceous plants in the family Rubiaceae, occurring in the temperate zones of both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

galium boreale.name: Northern Bedstraw
galium boreale.desc: Northern Bedstraw (Galium boreale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

galium palustre.name: Marsh bedstraw and meadow plants
galium palustre.desc: Plants of damp meadows and forest edges, grazed by bison, red deer and wild boar in GloBI records.
galium palustre.about: Galium palustre, the common marsh bedstraw or simply marsh-bedstraw, is a herbaceous annual plant of the family Rubiaceae.

gallinula chloropus.name: Common moorhen
gallinula chloropus.desc: A secretive omnivorous waterbird of reed edges that eats plants and small animals.
gallinula chloropus.about: The common moorhen, also known as the waterhen, is a bird species in the rail family (Rallidae). It is distributed across many parts of the Old World, across Africa, Europe, and Asia.

gallirallus sylvestris.name: Lord Howe woodhen
gallirallus sylvestris.desc: A flightless rail that eats worms, crustaceans and fruit, and sometimes shearwater eggs. Near 20 birds in the 1970s, it has recovered strongly after feral animals were removed.
gallirallus sylvestris.about: The Lord Howe woodhen also known as the Lord Howe Island woodhen, Lord Howe wood rail, Lord Howe rail or Lord Howe Island rail, is a flightless bird of the rail family, Rallidae.

gallus gallus.name: Red junglefowl
gallus gallus.desc: A ground-feeding forest bird, the wild ancestor of the chicken, and prey for cats and snakes.
gallus gallus.about: The red junglefowl, also known as the Indian red junglefowl, is a species of tropical, galliform bird in the phasianid family, found across much of Southeast Asia and parts of South Asia.

gambelia wislizenii.name: Long-nosed leopard lizard
gambelia wislizenii.desc: A sit-and-chase predator that eats insects and other lizards.
gambelia wislizenii.about: The long-nosed leopard lizard is a species of relatively large North American lizard in the family Crotaphytidae.

gambia river.name: Gambia River
gambia river.desc: The slow, wide river that holds the islands of the park and supports water plants, fish and wet forest.

gambusia holbrooki.name: Eastern mosquitofish
gambusia holbrooki.desc: A tiny generalist that eats zooplankton, insects, and detritus. Bass, catfish and bluegill eat it, and so do wading birds.
gambusia holbrooki.about: The eastern mosquitofish is a species of freshwater fish, closely related to the western mosquitofish, Gambusia affinis. It is a member of the family Poeciliidae of order Cyprinodontiformes.

gammarus.name: Freshwater shrimps
gammarus.desc: Small amphipod crustaceans that shred leaves and graze algae in streams and lake shallows. A favourite food of the dipper.
gammarus.about: Gammarus is an amphipod crustacean genus in the family Gammaridae. It contains more than 200 described species, making it one of the most species-rich genera of crustaceans.

garberia heterophylla.name: Garberia
garberia heterophylla.desc: Garberia (Garberia heterophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 71 times near the park in GBIF.

garrulus glandarius.name: Eurasian jay
garrulus glandarius.desc: A woodland crow that eats nuts, seeds and berries as well as small animals.
garrulus glandarius.about: The Eurasian jay is a species of passerine bird in the family Corvidae.

gastropoda.name: Endemic lake snails
gastropoda.desc: About 73 percent of freshwater snails in the basin are endemic. General ecology: many graze algae on the lake bed.
gastropoda.about: Freshwater snails are gastropod mollusks that live in fresh water. There are many different families.

gauja river and springs.name: Gauja River and springs
gauja river and springs.desc: The park follows the old valley of the Gauja River, with springs and sandstone cliffs. Water and wet floodplain soils feed riverside trees.

gaultheria hispidula.name: Creeping Snowberry
gaultheria hispidula.desc: Creeping Snowberry (Gaultheria hispidula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
gaultheria hispidula.about: Gaultheria hispidula, commonly known as the creeping snowberry or moxie-plum, and known to Mi'kmaq tribes of Newfoundland as manna teaberry, is a perennial spreading ground-level vine of the heath…

gaultheria mucronata.name: Prickly heath
gaultheria mucronata.desc: A low evergreen shrub with berries that GloBI records as food for birds such as the austral thrush.
gaultheria mucronata.about: Gaultheria mucronata is a species of flowering plant in the family Ericaceae, native to southern Argentina and Chile.

gaultheria procumbens.name: Checkerberry
gaultheria procumbens.desc: Wintergreen (Gaultheria procumbens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.
gaultheria procumbens.about: Gaultheria procumbens, also called the eastern teaberry, the checkerberry, the boxberry, or the American wintergreen, is a perennial species of Gaultheria native to northeastern North America from…

gaultheria shallon.name: Salal
gaultheria shallon.desc: An evergreen understory shrub with berries. Deer, elk, band-tailed pigeons and bears feed on it.
gaultheria shallon.about: Gaultheria shallon is an evergreen shrub in the heather family (Ericaceae), native to western North America. Common names include salal (), shallon, or (mainly in Britain) gaultheria.

gavia immer.name: Common Loon
gavia immer.desc: Dives for fish, mostly small ones including perch and walleye; eggs and chicks are taken by eagles, and fluctuating water can flood nests.
gavia immer.about: The common loon or great northern diver is a large member of the loon, or diver, family of birds.

gavialis gangeticus.name: Gharial
gavialis gangeticus.desc: A fish-eating crocodilian with a narrow snout. Wild numbers crashed and a breeding centre in the park has released young into the rivers since 1981.
gavialis gangeticus.about: The gharial, also known as gavial or fish-eating crocodile, is a crocodilian in the family Gavialidae and among the longest of all living crocodilians.
