gaylussacia baccata.name: Black Huckleberry
gaylussacia baccata.desc: Black Huckleberry (Gaylussacia baccata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

gaylussacia brachycera.name: Box huckleberry
gaylussacia brachycera.desc: Box huckleberry (Gaylussacia brachycera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

gayophytum diffusum.name: Spreading groundsmoke
gayophytum diffusum.desc: Spreading groundsmoke (Gayophytum diffusum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
gayophytum diffusum.about: Gayophytum diffusum is a species of flowering plant in the evening primrose family known by the common name spreading groundsmoke.

gazella arabica.name: Arabian gazelle
gazella arabica.desc: A selective browser of acacia and other woody plants. About a thousand live on the Farasan Islands.
gazella arabica.about: The Arabian gazelle is a species of gazelle from the Arabian Peninsula. There are approximately 5,000 – 7,000 mature individuals in the wild.

gazella dorcas.name: Dorcas gazelle
gazella dorcas.desc: A small, fast gazelle that grazes grasses and browses acacia and other shrubs, and is a staple prey of the Saharan cheetah.
gazella dorcas.about: The dorcas gazelle, also known as the ariel gazelle, is a small and common gazelle.

gazella gazella.name: Mountain gazelle
gazella gazella.desc: A small grazing antelope of the hills and open ground around the valley, and the most recorded mammal in this area.
gazella gazella.about: The mountain gazelle, also called the true gazelle or the Palestine mountain gazelle, is a species of gazelle that is widely but unevenly distributed.

gazella marica.name: Arabian sand gazelle
gazella marica.desc: The rheem, the native gazelle of Qatar. Gazelles of the Arabian peninsula browse mainly acacia and other woody plants.
gazella marica.about: The Arabian sand gazelle or reem (Arabic: ريم) is a species of gazelle native to the Arabian and Syrian Deserts.

gazella subgutturosa.name: Goitered gazelle
gazella subgutturosa.desc: A slender gazelle of open gravel plains and desert, and one of the most-recorded large herbivores near the park.
gazella subgutturosa.about: The goitered gazelle or black-tailed gazelle is a gazelle native to Turkey, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Iran, parts of Iraq and Pakistan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan,…

genetta cristata.name: Crested servaline genet
genetta cristata.desc: A small forest carnivore. A GloBI record shows it eating Tullberg's soft-furred mouse.
genetta cristata.about: The crested servaline genet, also known as the crested genet, is a genet species endemic to Nigeria and Cameroon.

genetta genetta.name: Common genet
genetta genetta.desc: A slender night hunter of small mammals, lizards, birds and insects, and sometimes fruit.
genetta genetta.about: The common genet is a small viverrid indigenous to Africa that was introduced to southwestern Europe.

genetta pardina.name: Pardine genet
genetta pardina.desc: A small spotted nocturnal carnivore of West African forests that hunts rodents and other small animals.
genetta pardina.about: The pardine genet, also known as the West African large spotted genet, is a genet species living in West Africa.

gentiana.name: Gentians and meadow herbs
gentiana.desc: Alpine and karst grasslands hold some 700 vascular plants in the park, including many gentians, with rare and endemic species. They are summer forage for chamois.
gentiana.about: Gentiana () is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the gentian family (Gentianaceae), the tribe Gentianeae, and the monophyletic subtribe Gentianinae.

gentiana affinis.name: Pleated gentian
gentiana affinis.desc: Pleated gentian (Gentiana affinis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

gentiana algida.name: Arctic gentian
gentiana algida.desc: Arctic gentian (Gentiana algida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

gentiana andrewsii.name: Bottle Gentian
gentiana andrewsii.desc: Bottle Gentian (Gentiana andrewsii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

gentiana septemfida.name: Alpine wildflowers
gentiana septemfida.desc: Gentians and other flowering herbs, among the best-recorded plants near the park, that colour the summer meadows.
gentiana septemfida.about: Gentiana septemfida, the crested gentian or summer gentian, is a species of flowering plant in the family Gentianaceae, native to the Caucasus and Turkey.

gentiana verna.name: Spring gentian
gentiana verna.desc: A small blue wildflower of mountain meadows, recorded in the Sharr area, one of many alpine herbs there.
gentiana verna.about: Gentiana verna, the spring gentian, is a species of flowering plant in the family Gentianaceae, and one of its smallest members, normally only growing to a height of a few centimetres.

gentiana, primula, ranunculus.name: Alpine wildflowers
gentiana, primula, ranunculus.desc: Gentians, primroses and buttercups that marmots eat, along with other flowering plants of the high meadows.
gentiana, primula, ranunculus.about: Gentiana () is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the gentian family (Gentianaceae), the tribe Gentianeae, and the monophyletic subtribe Gentianinae.

geocapromys brownii.name: Jamaican hutia
geocapromys brownii.desc: A night-foraging rodent found only in Jamaica. It eats fruit, roots, bark and leaves from many plants.
geocapromys brownii.about: The Jamaican coney, also known as the Jamaican hutia or Brown's hutia, is a small, endangered, rat-like mammal found only on the island of Jamaica.

geocapromys ingrahami.name: Bahamian hutia
geocapromys ingrahami.desc: A mostly plant-eating rodent that was introduced to the park in 1973 as a conservation measure. It eats leaves, shoots, fruit and bark.
geocapromys ingrahami.about: The Bahamian hutia or Ingraham's hutia is a small, furry, rat-like mammal found only in the Bahamas.

geococcyx californianus.name: Greater roadrunner
geococcyx californianus.desc: A fast ground cuckoo that eats insects, spiders, mice, lizards and young rattlesnakes.
geococcyx californianus.about: The greater roadrunner is a long-legged bird in the cuckoo family, Cuculidae, from the Aridoamerica region in the Southwestern United States and Mexico.

geomys arenarius.name: Desert pocket gopher
geomys arenarius.desc: A burrowing rodent of sandy soil that feeds on roots and other plant parts underground.
geomys arenarius.about: The desert pocket gopher is a species of rodent in the family Geomyidae. It is found in the state of Chihuahua in Mexico and in Texas and New Mexico in the United States.

geospiza and relatives.name: Darwin's finches
geospiza and relatives.desc: A group of closely related finches whose beaks fit different foods. Some eat cactus fruit, flowers and buds, others seeds and insects.
geospiza and relatives.about: Darwin's finches (also known as the Galápagos finches) are a group of about 18 species of passerine birds.

geranium caespitosum.name: Pineywoods geranium
geranium caespitosum.desc: Pineywoods geranium (Geranium caespitosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
geranium caespitosum.about: Geranium caespitosum, the purple cluster geranium or pineywoods geranium, is a perennial herb native to the western United States and northern Mexico.

geranium lucidum.name: Shining Crane's-bill
geranium lucidum.desc: Shining Crane's-bill (Geranium lucidum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

geranium maculatum.name: Spotted Crane's-bill
geranium maculatum.desc: Spotted Crane's-bill (Geranium maculatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
geranium maculatum.about: Geranium maculatum, the wild geranium, spotted geranium, or wood geranium, is a perennial plant native to woodlands in eastern North America, from southern Manitoba and southwestern Quebec south to…

geranium molle.name: Dove's-foot Crane's-bill
geranium molle.desc: Dove's-foot Crane's-bill (Geranium molle): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

geranium richardsonii.name: Richardson's crane's-bill
geranium richardsonii.desc: Richardson's crane's-bill (Geranium richardsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
geranium richardsonii.about: Geranium richardsonii is a species of geranium known by the common name Richardson's geranium.

geranium robertianum.name: Herb-Robert
geranium robertianum.desc: Herb-Robert (Geranium robertianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

geranium sanguineum.name: Bloody crane's-bill
geranium sanguineum.desc: A magenta-flowered perennial of the limestone grassland and pavement, among the most recorded plants in the area.
geranium sanguineum.about: Geranium sanguineum, common name bloody crane's-bill or bloody geranium, is a species of hardy flowering herbaceous perennial plant in the cranesbill family Geraniaceae.

geranoaetus melanoleucus.name: Black-chested buzzard-eagle
geranoaetus melanoleucus.desc: Raptor that mostly hunts mid-sized mammals, with introduced rabbits a key prey, and will take carrion when needed.
geranoaetus melanoleucus.about: The black-chested buzzard-eagle is a bird of prey of the hawk and eagle family (Accipitridae). It lives in open regions of South America.

geronticus eremita.name: Northern bald ibis
geronticus eremita.desc: Rediscovered near Palmyra in 2002. It probes the steppe for lizards and darkling beetles. The colony has since died out.
geronticus eremita.about: The northern bald ibis, hermit ibis, or Waldrapp is a migratory Old World ibis found in open areas such as grasslands, rocky mountains, and semi-deserts, often close to running water.

geukensia demissa.name: Atlantic ribbed mussel
geukensia demissa.desc: A filter feeder living in cordgrass beds. Its waste adds nitrogen and its mounds help cordgrass take hold.
geukensia demissa.about: Geukensia demissa is a species of mussel, a marine bivalve mollusk in the family Mytilidae, the true mussels. This species is native to the Atlantic coast of North America.

geum idahoense.name: Geum idahoense
geum idahoense.desc: Geum idahoense (Geum idahoense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

geum rossii.name: Ross's avens
geum rossii.desc: Ross's avens (Geum rossii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
geum rossii.about: Geum rossii is a species of flowering plant in the rose family known by the common names Ross' avens and alpine avens.

geum triflorum.name: Old-man's-whiskers
geum triflorum.desc: Old-man's-whiskers (Geum triflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.
geum triflorum.about: Geum triflorum, commonly known as prairie smoke, old man's whiskers, or three-flowered avens, is a spring-blooming perennial herbaceous plant of the Rosaceae family.

gilbertiodendron splendidum.name: Gilbertiodendron
gilbertiodendron splendidum.desc: Legume canopy trees that Wikipedia names among the characteristic trees of Sapo National Park.
gilbertiodendron splendidum.about: Gilbertiodendron is a genus of legumes in the family Fabaceae. It consists of about 35–40 species of tree, native to west and west-central tropical Africa.

gilia malior.name: Scrub gilia
gilia malior.desc: Scrub gilia (Gilia malior): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

gilia ochroleuca.name: Volcanic gilia
gilia ochroleuca.desc: Volcanic gilia (Gilia ochroleuca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

ginglymostoma cirratum.name: Nurse shark
ginglymostoma cirratum.desc: Bottom-feeding shark that eats conch, lobsters and other invertebrates, often resting under reef ledges by day.
ginglymostoma cirratum.about: The nurse shark is an elasmobranch fish in the family Ginglymostomatidae. The conservation status of the nurse shark is globally assessed as vulnerable in the IUCN List of Threatened Species.

giraffa camelopardalis.name: Giraffe
giraffa camelopardalis.desc: Browses the tops of acacias that no other herbivore can reach.
giraffa camelopardalis.about: Giraffes (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals. They are the tallest living terrestrial animals and the largest ruminants on Earth.

giraffa giraffa.name: Angolan giraffe
giraffa giraffa.desc: Etosha giraffes belong to the Angolan form of the southern giraffe and browse leaves, shoots and fruits of acacias and other trees.
giraffa giraffa.about: The southern giraffe, also known as two-horned giraffe, is a species of giraffe native to Southern Africa. The IUCN recognises four giraffe species, with several recognised subspecies.

giraffa thornicrofti.name: Thornicroft's giraffe
giraffa thornicrofti.desc: The Luangwa Valley giraffe browses leaves, including mopane, above where other herbivores can reach.
giraffa thornicrofti.about: Thornicroft's giraffe, also known as the Rhodesian giraffe or Luangwa giraffe, is a subspecies of giraffe. It is sometimes considered a species in its own right or a subspecies of the Masai giraffe.

glacial lake.name: Glacial lakes
glacial lake.desc: The park has 118 glacial lakes, and Snezhnika, Europe's southernmost glacier, still survives.

glacial meltwater.name: Glacial meltwater
glacial meltwater.desc: Cold, silty meltwater flows into the fjords and mixes with sea water, affecting where plankton grows.

glacial rivers.name: Glacial rivers
glacial rivers.desc: Glaciers cover a large part of the park and feed the silty rivers that salmon run up from the coast.

glacier meltwater.name: Glacier meltwater
glacier meltwater.desc: The Aletsch Glacier is the longest in the Alps. Its ice and meltwater feed streams and wet ground below, while its retreat leaves fresh moraine for plants to colonise.

glaciers and snowmelt.name: Glaciers and snowmelt
glaciers and snowmelt.desc: About a dozen small glaciers and alpine tarns feed streams but are shrinking fast and may vanish within decades.

glaucomys sabrinus.name: Northern flying squirrel
glaucomys sabrinus.desc: A nocturnal glider of old forest that eats fungi, lichens and seeds, and is the main prey of the spotted owl.
glaucomys sabrinus.about: The northern flying squirrel is one of three species of the genus Glaucomys, the only flying squirrels found in North America.

glaucomys volans.name: Southern flying squirrel
glaucomys volans.desc: Southern flying squirrel (Glaucomys volans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
glaucomys volans.about: The southern flying squirrel, sometimes called the assapan or polatouche, is a species of squirrel in the family Sciuridae. G.

glaucopsyche lygdamus.name: Silvery Blue
glaucopsyche lygdamus.desc: Silvery Blue (Glaucopsyche lygdamus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
glaucopsyche lygdamus.about: Glaucopsyche lygdamus, the silvery blue, is a small butterfly native to North America.

glechoma hederacea.name: Ground-ivy
glechoma hederacea.desc: Ground-ivy (Glechoma hederacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
glechoma hederacea.about: Glechoma hederacea is an aromatic, perennial, evergreen creeper of the mint family Lamiaceae.

gleditsia aquatica.name: Swamp-locust
gleditsia aquatica.desc: Swamp-locust (Gleditsia aquatica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

gleditsia triacanthos.name: Honey locust
gleditsia triacanthos.desc: Honey locust (Gleditsia triacanthos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 196 times near the park in GBIF.
gleditsia triacanthos.about: The honey locust, also known as the thorny locust or thorny honeylocust, is a deciduous tree in the family Fabaceae, native to central North America where it is mostly found in the moist soil of…

glis glis.name: Edible dormouse
glis glis.desc: A tree-dwelling rodent that eats beech seeds and fruit and hibernates in winter.
glis glis.about: The European edible dormouse, also known as the European dormouse or European fat dormouse, is a large dormouse and one of only two living species in the genus Glis, found in most of Europe and parts…

glyceria striata.name: Fowl manna grass
glyceria striata.desc: Fowl manna grass (Glyceria striata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
glyceria striata.about: Glyceria striata is a species of Glyceria which is known by the common names fowl mannagrass and ridged glyceria.

glycyrrhiza lepidota.name: American licorice
glycyrrhiza lepidota.desc: American licorice (Glycyrrhiza lepidota): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

gnaphalium uliginosum.name: Marsh Cudweed
gnaphalium uliginosum.desc: Marsh Cudweed (Gnaphalium uliginosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

goodyera oblongifolia.name: Rattlesnake plantain
goodyera oblongifolia.desc: Rattlesnake plantain (Goodyera oblongifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.
goodyera oblongifolia.about: Goodyera oblongifolia is a species of orchid known by the common names western rattlesnake plantain and giant rattlesnake plantain.

goodyera pubescens.name: Downy Rattlesnake-plantain
goodyera pubescens.desc: Downy Rattlesnake-plantain (Goodyera pubescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
goodyera pubescens.about: Goodyera pubescens, the downy rattlesnake plantain, is one of the most common orchids native to eastern North America.

gopherus agassizii.name: Desert tortoise
gopherus agassizii.desc: Threatened grazer that eats grasses, wildflowers and cactus and spends most of its life in burrows. Ravens take juveniles.
gopherus agassizii.about: The desert tortoise is a species of tortoise in the family Testudinidae.

gopherus morafkai.name: Sonoran desert tortoise
gopherus morafkai.desc: A herbivore that eats mostly grasses and wildflowers, plus cactus fruit and growth. Eggs and young are taken by ravens, badgers and coyotes.
gopherus morafkai.about: The Sonoran Desert tortoise, or Morafka's desert tortoise, is a species of terrestrial chelonian reptile of the family Testudinidae (tortoises) native to the Sonoran Desert.

gordonia lasianthus.name: Loblolly bay
gordonia lasianthus.desc: Loblolly bay (Gordonia lasianthus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

gorilla beringei.name: Mountain gorilla
gorilla beringei.desc: Mostly eats leaves, shoots, stems and pith, with some fruit. Bwindi holds almost half of all mountain gorillas.
gorilla beringei.about: The mountain gorilla is one of the two subspecies of the eastern gorilla. It is listed as endangered by the IUCN as of 2018.

gorilla beringei beringei.name: Mountain gorilla
gorilla beringei beringei.desc: Eats mostly leaves, shoots and stems, with some bark and roots, and also giant senecio centres. The park protects about a third of the world population.
gorilla beringei beringei.about: The mountain gorilla is one of the two subspecies of the eastern gorilla. It is listed as endangered by the IUCN as of 2018.

gorilla gorilla.name: Western lowland gorilla
gorilla gorilla.desc: Mainly eats fruit, shoots, leaves and herbaceous stems, switching toward leaves and herbs when fruit is scarce. Listed among the primates of Monte Alen.
gorilla gorilla.about: The western lowland gorilla is one of two critically endangered subspecies of the western gorilla that lives in montane, primary and secondary forest and lowland swampland in central Africa in Angola…

gorilla gorilla diehli.name: Cross River gorilla
gorilla gorilla diehli.desc: A rare gorilla of the Nigeria-Cameroon border hills. It eats fruit, herbs, bark and leaves, switching to herbs when fruit is scarce.
gorilla gorilla diehli.about: The Cross River gorilla is a critically endangered subspecies of the western gorilla.

gorilla gorilla gorilla.name: Western lowland gorilla
gorilla gorilla gorilla.desc: Prefers ripe fruit but switches to leaves, herbs and bark when fruit is scarce. Spreads seeds in its dung.
gorilla gorilla gorilla.about: The western lowland gorilla is one of two critically endangered subspecies of the western gorilla that lives in montane, primary and secondary forest and lowland swampland in central Africa in Angola…

granite-derived soil.name: Granite-derived soil
granite-derived soil.desc: Thin soils over granite hold nutrients that plants and meadows draw on.

grapsus grapsus.name: Sally Lightfoot crab
grapsus grapsus.desc: Bright red crab on the lava shore. It mainly grazes algae but is an opportunist that also eats animal matter and scavenges dead seals and birds.
grapsus grapsus.about: Grapsus grapsus is one of the most common crabs along the western coast of the Americas.

grassland fire.name: Grassland fire
grassland fire.desc: Periodic burning has kept tall grassland open, though Wikipedia notes it can also threaten pygmy hogs sheltering in it.

grassland fires.name: Grassland fires
grassland fires.desc: Seasonal bushfires burn off old grass in the park, and fresh growth follows for grazers such as gaur.

grewia.name: Grewia shrubs
grewia.desc: Shrubs of the dry coastal forest and thicket, recorded in GBIF data near the reserve. Browsers can eat their leaves.
grewia.about: Grewia is a large flowering plant genus in the mallow family Malvaceae, in the expanded sense as proposed by the Angiosperm Phylogeny Group.

grewia hexamita.name: Giant donkeyberry
grewia hexamita.desc: A woody shrub of dry bushveld whose leaves and berries are eaten by elephant and by duikers and bushbuck.
grewia hexamita.about: Grewia hexamita, the giant raisin, is a species of flowering plant in the family Malvaceae, native to Mozambique and adjoining countries. It is a large tree for a Grewia, reaching 5 m (16 ft).

grindelia hirsutula.name: Hairy gumweed
grindelia hirsutula.desc: Hairy gumweed (Grindelia hirsutula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
grindelia hirsutula.about: Grindelia hirsutula is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names hairy gumplant and hairy gumweed.

grindelia squarrosa.name: Curly-cup Gumweed
grindelia squarrosa.desc: Curly-cup Gumweed (Grindelia squarrosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 105 times near the park in GBIF.
grindelia squarrosa.about: Grindelia squarrosa, also known as a curly-top gumweed or curlycup gumweed, is a small North American biennial or short-lived perennial plant.

griselinia littoralis.name: Broadleaf
griselinia littoralis.desc: A common native forest tree whose leaves and fruit are eaten by browsing mammals and forest birds.
griselinia littoralis.about: Griselinia littoralis, commonly known as kapuka, New Zealand broadleaf or pāpāuma, is a fast-growing small to medium-sized evergreen tree that is native to New Zealand.

groundwater.name: Ephemeral river water
groundwater.desc: Dry rivers carry flood pulses and keep groundwater close to the surface, supporting trees, Welwitschia and elephants.

grus americana.name: Whooping crane
grus americana.desc: The park is the main breeding area of this endangered crane, which nests on marshes and eats animals, tubers and berries.
grus americana.about: The whooping crane is an endangered crane species, native to North America, named for its "whooping" calls.

grus canadensis.name: Sandhill crane
grus canadensis.desc: Up to 450,000 lesser sandhill cranes stop in the central Platte valley each year. They feed on waste grain, seeds and invertebrates in fields and wet meadows.
grus canadensis.about: The sandhill crane is a species of large crane of North America and extreme northeastern Siberia.

grus grus.name: Common crane
grus grus.desc: An omnivore that eats mostly plant matter, waste grain, insects, frogs and small rodents. Big numbers pass through Hungary on migration.
grus grus.about: The common crane, also known as the Eurasian crane, is a bird of the family Gruidae, the cranes.

grus japonensis.name: Red-crowned crane
grus japonensis.desc: An omnivorous wetland crane that eats fish, amphibians, insects, rodents and small reptiles, plus rice and reeds in winter. Wintering birds use the Korean peninsula.
grus japonensis.about: The red-crowned crane, also called the Japanese crane and the Manchurian crane, is a large Northeast Asian crane among the rarest cranes in the world.

grusonia clavata.name: Club cholla
grusonia clavata.desc: Club cholla (Grusonia clavata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
grusonia clavata.about: Grusonia clavata, the club-cholla, is a species of succulent flowering plant in the genus Grusonia, within the family Cactaceae. It is endemic to central New Mexico, in the southwestern United States.

gryllodes sigillatus.name: Indian house cricket
gryllodes sigillatus.desc: A widespread cricket that is recorded on the islands and is eaten by green anoles.
gryllodes sigillatus.about: Gryllodes sigillatus, the tropical house cricket, Indian house cricket or banded cricket, is a small cricket probably native to southwestern Asia, but has spread throughout tropical regions…

grylloprociphilus imbricator.name: Beech Blight Aphid
grylloprociphilus imbricator.desc: Beech Blight Aphid (Grylloprociphilus imbricator): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

guarea glabra.name: Alligatorwood
guarea glabra.desc: A common tree of the forest understorey in the GBIF records here. Birds such as manakins and thrushes are recorded eating its fruit.

guarea macrophylla.name: Guarea tree
guarea macrophylla.desc: A rainforest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for tapirs and toucans.
guarea macrophylla.about: Guarea is a genus of evergreen trees or shrubs in the family Meliaceae, native to tropical Africa and Central and South America.

guatteria punctata.name: Guatteria
guatteria punctata.desc: A rainforest understorey tree whose fruits are eaten by birds and primates, which spread its seeds.
guatteria punctata.about: Guatteria is a genus of Central and South American flowering plants in the family Annonaceae. It is the largest genus in the family in South America, and the dominant genus in mature tropical forest.

guazuma ulmifolia.name: Bastardcedar
guazuma ulmifolia.desc: A common tree of dry ground and forest islands whose fruit is eaten by peccaries and other forest animals.
guazuma ulmifolia.about: Guazuma ulmifolia, commonly known as West Indian elm or bay cedar, is a medium-sized tree normally found in pastures and disturbed forests.

gulo gulo.name: Wolverine
gulo gulo.desc: A strong scavenger and predator. GloBI records it eating caribou, ground squirrels, ptarmigan and voles.
gulo gulo.about: The wolverine, also called the carcajou or quickhatch (from East Cree, kwiihkwahaacheew), is the largest land-dwelling member of the family Mustelidae.

gunnera magellanica.name: Gunnera
gunnera magellanica.desc: A small ground-hugging plant of damp, shaded ground, recorded as a main food of huemul in a Chilean fjord study.
gunnera magellanica.about: Gunnera magellanica is a perennial rhizomatous dioeceous herb native to Chile, Argentina and the Falkland Islands, and Andean areas of Peru and Ecuador.

gymnocarpium continentale.name: Asian oak fern
gymnocarpium continentale.desc: Asian oak fern (Gymnocarpium continentale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

gymnocarpium robertianum.name: Limestone Fern
gymnocarpium robertianum.desc: Limestone Fern (Gymnocarpium robertianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

gymnocladus dioicus.name: Kentucky coffeetree
gymnocladus dioicus.desc: Kentucky coffeetree (Gymnocladus dioicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
gymnocladus dioicus.about: The Kentucky coffeetree, also known as American coffee berry, Kentucky mahogany, nicker tree, and stump tree, is a tree in the subfamily Caesalpinioideae of the legume family Fabaceae, native to the…

gymnogyps californianus.name: California condor
gymnogyps californianus.desc: A large scavenger released near the canyon in 1996. It eats carrion of large mammals such as deer, and lead from ammunition in carcasses is a main threat.
gymnogyps californianus.about: The California condor is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.

gymnopleurus puncticollis.name: Dung beetles
gymnopleurus puncticollis.desc: Dung beetles are among the most recorded animals here. They bury dung, which returns nutrients to the soil.
gymnopleurus puncticollis.about: Gymnopleurus is a genus of Scarabaeidae or dung beetles in the superfamily Scarabaeoidea.

gymnorhinus cyanocephalus.name: Pinyon jay
gymnorhinus cyanocephalus.desc: A social jay that feeds heavily on pinyon seeds and is well recorded in the park area.
gymnorhinus cyanocephalus.about: The pinyon jay is a species of jay, and is the only member of the genus Gymnorhinus.

gymnoschoenus sphaerocephalus.name: Buttongrass
gymnoschoenus sphaerocephalus.desc: The dominant plant of Tasmania's moorlands. Its rhizomes are eaten by burrowing crayfish, and the community is adapted to burning.
gymnoschoenus sphaerocephalus.about: Gymnoschoenus sphaerocephalus, commonly known as buttongrass, is a species of tussock-forming sedge from southeastern Australia. It forms part of a unique habitat in Tasmania.

gymnothorax chilospilus.name: Lipspot moray
gymnothorax chilospilus.desc: A small moray eel living in reef crevices, and the main prey of the New Caledonian sea krait.
gymnothorax chilospilus.about: The lipspot moray eel, also known as the textile moray, white-lipped moray or white-lipped reef eel, is a moray eel found in coral reefs in the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

gymnothorax spp..name: Moray eel
gymnothorax spp..desc: Ambushes fish from crevices in the reef.
gymnothorax spp..about: Moray eels, or Muraenidae (), are a family of eels whose members are found worldwide.

gypaetus barbatus.name: Bearded vulture
gypaetus barbatus.desc: Lives on bone, mostly 85 to 90 percent of an adult's diet, and drops big bones from the air to crack them.
gypaetus barbatus.about: The bearded vulture, also known as the lammergeier and ossifrage, is a very large bird of prey in the monotypic genus Gypaetus.

gypohierax angolensis.name: Palm-nut vulture
gypohierax angolensis.desc: An unusual vulture that lives mainly on oil and raffia palm fruit, but also takes fish, crabs, frogs and carrion.
gypohierax angolensis.about: The palm-nut vulture or vulturine fish eagle, is a large bird of prey in the family Accipitridae (which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as kites, buzzards and harriers, vultures, and…

gyps africanus.name: White-backed vulture
gyps africanus.desc: Scavenges carcasses of elephant, buffalo, zebra and antelope.
gyps africanus.about: The white-backed vulture is an Old World vulture in the family Accipitridae, which also includes eagles, kites, buzzards and hawks. It is the most common vulture species in the continent of Africa.

gyps coprotheres.name: Cape vulture
gyps coprotheres.desc: A cliff-nesting scavenger that eats the soft tissue of carcasses and breeds in Lesotho. Endangered.
gyps coprotheres.about: The Cape vulture, also known as Cape griffon and Kolbe's vulture, is an Old World vulture in the family Accipitridae.

gyps fulvus.name: Griffon vulture
gyps fulvus.desc: A large scavenger of mountain carcasses, recorded often around the massif.
gyps fulvus.about: The Eurasian griffon vulture is a large Old World vulture in the bird of prey family Accipitridae.

gyps himalayensis.name: Himalayan griffon
gyps himalayensis.desc: A big vulture that feeds on carrion of hoofed animals and is among the most often recorded birds here.
gyps himalayensis.about: The Himalayan vulture or Himalayan griffon vulture is an Old World vulture native to the Himalayas and foothills in North and Northeastern India, as well as the adjacent Tibetan Plateau.

gyps rueppelli.name: Rüppell's vulture
gyps rueppelli.desc: Circles on thermals and arrives fast at carcasses, stripping them within hours.
gyps rueppelli.about: Rüppell's vulture, also called Rüppell's griffon vulture or Rüppell's griffon, a species of vulture named after Eduard Rüppell, is a large, resident bird of prey, mainly native to the Sahel region…

gypsum sand.name: Gypsum sand
gypsum sand.desc: The dunes are made of gypsum left by dried lakes in a basin with no outlet. Only salt- and gypsum-tolerant plants thrive in it.

haaniella echinata.name: Prickly stick insect
haaniella echinata.desc: A large leaf-eating stick insect of Bornean forests, recorded repeatedly near the park.
haaniella echinata.about: The Phasmatodea are an order of insects whose members are variously known as stick insects, stick bugs, walkingsticks, stick animals, or bug sticks.

hadenoecus subterraneus.name: Mammoth Cave cricket
hadenoecus subterraneus.desc: Eats whatever it can find. Wikipedia says its guano, eggs and carcasses feed many cave communities.
hadenoecus subterraneus.about: Hadenoecus subterraneus, the common cave cricket, or Mammoth Cave cricket is a species of camel cricket in the family Rhaphidophoridae. It is found in North America.

haematopus ostralegus.name: Eurasian oystercatcher
haematopus ostralegus.desc: Uses its strong bill to open cockles and mussels or to dig up worms. Despite its name, oysters are not a major food.
haematopus ostralegus.about: The Eurasian oystercatcher or European oystercatcher, also known as the common pied oystercatcher, or (in Europe) just oystercatcher, is a wader in the oystercatcher bird family Haematopodidae.

haemorhous mexicanus.name: House Finch
haemorhous mexicanus.desc: House Finch (Haemorhous mexicanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 43 times near the park in GBIF.
haemorhous mexicanus.about: The house finch is a North American bird in the finch family. It is native to Mexico and southwestern United States, but has since been introduced to the eastern part of North America and Hawaiʻi,…

hagenia abyssinica.name: Hagenia tree
hagenia abyssinica.desc: A highland tree of the montane woodland whose leaves are among the foods of the mountain nyala.
hagenia abyssinica.about: Hagenia is a monotypic genus of flowering plant with the sole species Hagenia abyssinica, native to the high-elevation Afromontane regions of central and eastern Africa.

hagenius brevistylus.name: Dragonhunter
hagenius brevistylus.desc: Dragonhunter (Hagenius brevistylus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.
hagenius brevistylus.about: The dragonhunter is a clubtail dragonfly of the eastern United States and southeastern Canada.

haliaeetus albicilla.name: White-tailed eagle
haliaeetus albicilla.desc: A large raptor that takes fish and, per the seal article, can prey on seal pups that leave their dens.
haliaeetus albicilla.about: The white-tailed eagle, sometimes known as the "sea eagle", is a large bird of prey, widely distributed across temperate Eurasia.

haliaeetus leucocephalus.name: Bald eagle
haliaeetus leucocephalus.desc: A large raptor that eats fish and carrion along the bay. Its numbers recovered after the DDT era.
haliaeetus leucocephalus.about: The bald eagle is a bird of prey found in North America. A sea eagle, it has two known subspecies and forms a species pair with the white-tailed eagle, which occupies the same niche as the bald eagle…

haliaeetus leucogaster.name: White-bellied sea eagle
haliaeetus leucogaster.desc: A coastal raptor that takes fish about half of its diet, and also hunts waterbirds and reptiles. Nests in tall trees by water.
haliaeetus leucogaster.about: The white-bellied sea eagle, also known as the white-breasted sea eagle, is a large diurnal bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.

haliaeetus pelagicus.name: Steller's sea eagle
haliaeetus pelagicus.desc: Prefers salmon and trout in rivers and eats waterbirds on the coast. Dead spawned salmon feed those wintering inland.
haliaeetus pelagicus.about: Steller's sea eagle, also known as the Pacific sea eagle or white-shouldered eagle, is a very large diurnal bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.

haliaeetus sanfordi.name: Sanford's sea eagle
haliaeetus sanfordi.desc: Found only in the Solomon Islands. It eats mostly carrion along the tideline plus fish, and sometimes birds and fruit bats from the canopy.
haliaeetus sanfordi.about: Sanford's sea eagle, also known as Sanford's fish eagle or the Solomon eagle, is a sea eagle endemic to the Solomon Islands archipelago.

haliaeetus vocifer.name: African fish eagle
haliaeetus vocifer.desc: Hunts fish from perches over open water, and also takes waterbirds and carrion.
haliaeetus vocifer.about: The African fish eagle or the African sea eagle is a large species of eagle found throughout sub-Saharan Africa wherever large bodies of open water with an abundant food supply occur.

haliaeetus vociferoides.name: Madagascar fish eagle
haliaeetus vociferoides.desc: Critically endangered eagle of western wetlands and lakes that hunts fish.
haliaeetus vociferoides.about: The Madagascar fish eagle or Madagascar sea-eagle, is a large bird of prey in the family Accipitridae which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as kites, buzzards and harriers.

haliastur indus.name: Brahminy kite
haliastur indus.desc: Mainly a scavenger of dead animals. It occasionally hunts live prey such as bats.
haliastur indus.about: The brahminy kite, also known as the red-backed sea-eagle, is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors, such as eagles, buzzards, and…

haliastur sphenurus.name: Whistling kite
haliastur sphenurus.desc: Hunts small mammals, birds, fish and reptiles and eats carrion. It hovers at grass fires to catch fleeing prey.
haliastur sphenurus.about: The whistling kite is a medium-sized diurnal raptor found throughout Australia (including coastal islands), New Caledonia and much of New Guinea (excluding the central mountains and the northwest).

halichoerus grypus.name: Grey seal
halichoerus grypus.desc: Hunts fish, especially sand eels, and hauls out in large numbers on outer Cape beaches.
halichoerus grypus.about: The grey seal, or gray seal in the United States, is a large seal of the family Phocidae, which are commonly referred to as "true seals" or "earless seals".

halictus confusus.name: Confusing metallic furrow bee
halictus confusus.desc: Confusing metallic furrow bee (Halictus confusus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 46 times near the park in GBIF.

halictus ligatus.name: Ligated furrow bee
halictus ligatus.desc: Ligated furrow bee (Halictus ligatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

halictus parallelus.name: Parallel Furrow Bee
halictus parallelus.desc: Parallel Furrow Bee (Halictus parallelus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

halictus tripartitus.name: Tripartite Sweat Bee
halictus tripartitus.desc: Tripartite Sweat Bee (Halictus tripartitus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 206 times near the park in GBIF.
halictus tripartitus.about: Halictus tripartitus is a species of sweat bee in the family Halictidae. It is partially eusocial, with nests connected underground and some workers capable of reproducing.

halimeda.name: Reef algae
halimeda.desc: Chalky green seaweed growing on reefs and sandy flats. Grazed by parrotfish and snails.
halimeda.about: Halimeda is a genus of green macroalgae. The algal body (thallus) is composed of calcified green segments.

halimeda spp..name: Macroalgae
halimeda spp..desc: Seaweeds on reef flats that grazers keep from smothering the coral.
halimeda spp..about: Halimeda is a genus of green macroalgae. The algal body (thallus) is composed of calcified green segments.

haliotis cracherodii.name: Black abalone
haliotis cracherodii.desc: A herbivorous snail that feeds mostly on drift algae and kelp. Critically endangered after overfishing and withering syndrome.
haliotis cracherodii.about: Haliotis cracherodii, the black abalone, is a species of large edible sea snail, a marine gastropod mollusk in the family Haliotidae, the abalone.

halocnemum strobilaceum.name: Saltmarsh glasswort
halocnemum strobilaceum.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of saline coastal marshes around the Persian Gulf, which binds salty ground at the edge of the tidal flats.
halocnemum strobilaceum.about: Halocnemum strobilaceum is a species of flowering plant in the subfamily Salicornioideae of the family Amaranthaceae.

halodule.name: Seagrass
halodule.desc: Underwater meadows in shallow lagoons and bays, grazed by green turtles and, in places, manatees.
halodule.about: Seagrasses are the only embryophytes (commonly referred to as "land plants") which grow in marine environments.

halodule uninervis.name: Seagrass
halodule uninervis.desc: Underwater meadows that shelter young fish and feed turtles and dugongs.
halodule uninervis.about: Seagrasses are the only embryophytes (commonly referred to as "land plants") which grow in marine environments.

halogeton glomeratus.name: Barilla
halogeton glomeratus.desc: Barilla (Halogeton glomeratus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 97 times near the park in GBIF.
halogeton glomeratus.about: Halogeton glomeratus is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae known by the common names saltlover, Aral barilla, and halogeton.

halophila.name: Seagrass
halophila.desc: Fast-growing seagrass of shallow sandy bottoms; Halophila is a favoured food of dugongs.
halophila.about: Halophila is a genus of seagrasses in the family Hydrocharitaceae, the tape-grasses. It was described as a genus in 1806.

halophila ovalis.name: Paddle weed
halophila ovalis.desc: A small, fast-growing seagrass that quickly colonises bare patches. Halophila is among the seagrasses dugongs eat most.
halophila ovalis.about: Halophila ovalis, commonly known as paddle weed, spoon grass or dugong grass, is a seagrass in the family Hydrocharitaceae.

haloxylon ammodendron.name: Black saxaul
haloxylon ammodendron.desc: A tough desert shrub or small tree of loose sand. In the Gobi it is often the only tree, and its roots help hold dunes in place.
haloxylon ammodendron.about: Haloxylon ammodendron, variously called the saxaul (Russian: саксау́л, romanized: saksaúl), black saxaul, also spelled sacsaoul or saksaul is a plant belonging to the family Amaranthaceae.

haloxylon persicum.name: White saxaul
haloxylon persicum.desc: A shrubby saxaul of shifting sands, one of the best-recorded plants in the area.
haloxylon persicum.about: Haloxylon persicum, the white saxaul, is a small tree belonging to the family Amaranthaceae.

halyomorpha halys.name: Marmorated brown stink bug
halyomorpha halys.desc: Marmorated brown stink bug (Halyomorpha halys): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
halyomorpha halys.about: The brown marmorated stink bug is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

halysidota harrisii.name: Sycamore Tussock Moth
halysidota harrisii.desc: Sycamore Tussock Moth (Halysidota harrisii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

halysidota tessellaris.name: Banded Tussock Moth
halysidota tessellaris.desc: Banded Tussock Moth (Halysidota tessellaris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
halysidota tessellaris.about: Halysidota tessellaris, also called the pale tiger moth, banded tussock moth, and tessellated halisidota, is in the family Erebidae and the tribe Arctiini, the tiger moths.

hamanumida daedalus.name: Guinea-fowl butterfly
hamanumida daedalus.desc: A savanna butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes and whose adults are eaten by bee-eaters.
hamanumida daedalus.about: Hamanumida daedalus, the guineafowl butterfly, is a butterfly of the family Nymphalidae and only member of the genus Hamanumida.

hamelia patens.name: Scarletbush
hamelia patens.desc: Shrub with nectar-rich flowers and small fruit; GloBI records bats, birds and butterflies feeding on it.
hamelia patens.about: Hamelia patens is a large evergreen perennial shrub or small tree in the family Rubiaceae, that is native to the American subtropics and tropics.

harmonia axyridis.name: Harlequin ladybird
harmonia axyridis.desc: Harlequin ladybird (Harmonia axyridis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
harmonia axyridis.about: Harmonia axyridis is a lady beetle or ladybird species that is most commonly known as the harlequin, Asian, or multicoloured Asian lady beetle.

harpia harpyja.name: Harpy eagle
harpia harpyja.desc: Plucks sloths and monkeys from the canopy with enormous talons.
harpia harpyja.about: The harpy eagle is a large neotropical species of eagle. It is also called the American harpy eagle to distinguish it from the Papuan eagle, which is sometimes known as the New Guinea harpy eagle or…

harpyopsis novaeguineae.name: Papuan eagle
harpyopsis novaeguineae.desc: A big forest eagle that hunts from the canopy. It takes possums, tree-kangaroos, forest wallabies and woolly rats, as well as birds and reptiles.
harpyopsis novaeguineae.about: The Papuan eagle is a large bird of prey. It is also known by several other names, including Papuan harpy eagle, New Guinea eagle, New Guinea harpy eagle, or kapul eagle, the latter name from the…

heaven lake and meltwater.name: Heaven Lake and meltwater
heaven lake and meltwater.desc: The crater lake on the summit feeds the Songhua, Tumen and Yalu rivers, and its shores support a few hundred plant species.

heavy pacific rain.name: Heavy Pacific rain
heavy pacific rain.desc: Wet maritime weather feeds the temperate rainforest and the many streams and lakes that run to the sea.

heavy rain.name: Heavy rain
heavy rain.desc: Wet tropical climate across the park, from the Arafura coast to the summits.

heavy rain and fog.name: Heavy rain and fog
heavy rain and fog.desc: Winter rain and summer fog drip keep the forest constantly wet; the Hoh and Quinault valleys are among the rainiest places in the continental US.

heavy rainfall.name: Heavy rainfall
heavy rainfall.desc: Over 7,000 mm of rain a year feeds more than 200 waterfalls and the cloud forest, the only humid tropical forest on an oceanic island in the region.

hediste diversicolor.name: Ragworm
hediste diversicolor.desc: A common mudflat worm that feeds on surface mud and organic particles. Fish, crabs and shorebirds hunt it.
hediste diversicolor.about: Hediste diversicolor, commonly known as a ragworm, is a polychaete worm in the family Nereididae.

hedone vibex.name: Hedone vibex
hedone vibex.desc: Hedone vibex (Hedone vibex): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

hedysarum alpinum.name: Alpine sweetvetch
hedysarum alpinum.desc: Alpine sweetvetch (Hedysarum alpinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
hedysarum alpinum.about: Hedysarum alpinum is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by the common name alpine sweetvetch, bear root, or eskimo potato.

helarctos malayanus.name: Sun bear
helarctos malayanus.desc: An omnivore that eats insects such as termites and ants, honey and fruit including figs. The tiger is its main predator.
helarctos malayanus.about: The sun bear is a bear species in the family Ursidae found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia.

helenium amarum.name: Bitter sneezeweed
helenium amarum.desc: Bitter sneezeweed (Helenium amarum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
helenium amarum.about: Helenium amarum is a species of annual herb in the daisy family known by the common names yellowdicks, yellow sneezeweed, fiveleaf sneezeweed, and bitter sneezeweed.

heleobia.name: Heleobia snails
heleobia.desc: Tiny freshwater snails, many found only in the lake. They graze on the lake bottom and are eaten by frogs and fish.
heleobia.about: Heleobia is a genus of small freshwater and brackish water snails with a gill and an operculum, aquatic gastropod mollusks in the family Cochliopidae and the superfamily Truncatelloidea.

heliamphora.name: Tepui pitcher plants
heliamphora.desc: Carnivorous plants of the tepuis that trap insects, mostly ants, in leaf pitchers to make up for scarce nutrients; many rely on bacteria to digest the prey.
heliamphora.about: The genus Heliamphora contains 24 species of pitcher plants endemic to South America.

helianthus annuus.name: Sunflower
helianthus annuus.desc: Sunflower (Helianthus annuus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
helianthus annuus.about: The common sunflower is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae. The most common varieties have large yellow orange flowers heads, that are a tall stem.

helianthus divaricatus.name: Divergent Sunflower
helianthus divaricatus.desc: Divergent Sunflower (Helianthus divaricatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

helianthus laciniatus.name: Jagged-edge sunflower
helianthus laciniatus.desc: Jagged-edge sunflower (Helianthus laciniatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

helianthus mollis.name: Ashy Sunflower
helianthus mollis.desc: Ashy Sunflower (Helianthus mollis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
helianthus mollis.about: Helianthus mollis is a species of sunflower known by the common names ashy sunflower or downy sunflower.

helianthus petiolaris.name: Lesser Sunflower
helianthus petiolaris.desc: An annual sunflower of sandy, disturbed soil whose seeds suit seed-eating rodents.
helianthus petiolaris.about: Helianthus petiolaris is a North American plant species in the family Asteraceae, commonly known as the prairie sunflower or lesser sunflower.

helianthus tuberosus.name: Jerusalem Artichoke
helianthus tuberosus.desc: Jerusalem Artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

helichrysum.name: Everlasting shrubs
helichrysum.desc: Shrubby everlastings of the highlands; their spread into rodent habitat is listed as a pressure on the Ethiopian wolf.
helichrysum.about: The genus Helichrysum consists of an estimated 600 species of flowering plants in the sunflower family (Asteraceae). The type species is Helichrysum orientale.

helichrysum luteoalbum.name: Daisy
helichrysum luteoalbum.desc: Daisy (Helichrysum luteoalbum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
helichrysum luteoalbum.about: Pseudognaphalium luteoalbum, synonyms including Helichrysum luteoalbum, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. In the United Kingdom, it is known as the Jersey cudweed.

heliconia.name: Heliconia
heliconia.desc: Large-leaved herbs of forest openings and edges, common in the lowlands of Costa Rica.
heliconia.about: Heliconia is a genus of flowering plants in the monotypic family Heliconiaceae.

helicoverpa zea.name: Bollworm
helicoverpa zea.desc: Bollworm (Helicoverpa zea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

heliomeris multiflora.name: Showy goldeneye
heliomeris multiflora.desc: Showy goldeneye (Heliomeris multiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

heliotropium curassavicum.name: Seaside Heliotrope
heliotropium curassavicum.desc: Seaside Heliotrope (Heliotropium curassavicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
heliotropium curassavicum.about: Heliotropium curassavicum, commonly called salt heliotrope, is a species of flowering plant in the family Heliotropiaceae.

heliotropium indicum.name: Indian Heliotrope
heliotropium indicum.desc: Indian Heliotrope (Heliotropium indicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
heliotropium indicum.about: Heliotropium indicum, commonly known as Indian heliotrope or Indian turnsole, is an annual, hirsute plant. It has a curved arrangement of small flowers and velvety broad green leaves.

heloderma suspectum.name: Gila monster
heloderma suspectum.desc: A slow venomous lizard that raids burrows and nests for eggs and small animals.
heloderma suspectum.about: The Gila monster is a species of venomous lizard native to the Southwestern United States and the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora.

hemaris diffinis.name: Bumblebee Moth
hemaris diffinis.desc: Bumblebee Moth (Hemaris diffinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
hemaris diffinis.about: Hemaris diffinis, the snowberry clearwing, is a moth of the family Sphingidae. This moth is sometimes called "hummingbird moth" or "flying lobster".

hemerocallis fulva.name: Orange Day-lily
hemerocallis fulva.desc: Orange Day-lily (Hemerocallis fulva): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
hemerocallis fulva.about: Hemerocallis fulva, the orange day-lily, tawny daylily, corn lily, tiger daylily, fulvous daylily, ditch lily or Fourth of July lily (also railroad daylily, roadside daylily, outhouse lily, track…

hemiargus ceraunus.name: Ceraunus Blue
hemiargus ceraunus.desc: Ceraunus Blue (Hemiargus ceraunus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

hemiargus hanno.name: Common Blue butterfly
hemiargus hanno.desc: A small butterfly whose caterpillars feed on legumes such as crab's eye. A source of insect food for lizards.
hemiargus hanno.about: Hemiargus hanno, the hanno blue is a species of butterfly in the family Lycaenidae. It is found in Suriname, Brazil, Colombia, Cuba, the Netherlands Antilles, Puerto Rico and Hispaniola.

hemiechinus auritus.name: Long-eared hedgehog
hemiechinus auritus.desc: A small desert hedgehog that hunts at night for beetles and other invertebrates, and also takes small lizards.
hemiechinus auritus.about: The long-eared hedgehog is a species of hedgehog native to Central Asian countries and some countries of the Middle East.

hemiphaga novaeseelandiae.name: Kererū (NZ pigeon)
hemiphaga novaeseelandiae.desc: Mainly eats fruit, plus leaves, flowers and buds. Possums and rats compete for fruit and take eggs; stoats and cats kill adults and young.
hemiphaga novaeseelandiae.about: The kererū, also known as kūkupa (northern Māori dialects), New Zealand pigeon or wood pigeon, is a species of pigeon native to New Zealand.

hemitomes congestum.name: Coneplant
hemitomes congestum.desc: Coneplant (Hemitomes congestum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

hemitragus jemlahicus.name: Himalayan tahr
hemitragus jemlahicus.desc: Grazes grasses and browses shrubs on steep rocky slopes, moving downslope in winter. Snow leopards prey on it.
hemitragus jemlahicus.about: The Himalayan tahr is a large even-toed ungulate native to the Himalayas in southern Tibet, northern India, western Bhutan and Nepal.

hepatica acutiloba.name: Sharp-lobed hepatica
hepatica acutiloba.desc: Sharp-lobed hepatica (Hepatica acutiloba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
hepatica acutiloba.about: Hepatica acutiloba, the sharp-lobed hepatica, is a herbaceous flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae. It is sometimes considered part of the genus Anemone, as Anemone acutiloba, A.

hepatica americana.name: American hepatica
hepatica americana.desc: American hepatica (Hepatica americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
hepatica americana.about: Hepatica americana, the round-lobed hepatica, is a herbaceous flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae. It is native to the eastern United States and Canada.

heptapleurum actinophyllum.name: Umbrella tree
heptapleurum actinophyllum.desc: Its fruit is eaten by birds, spectacled flying foxes, musky rat-kangaroos and red-legged pademelons. Its leaves feed tree-kangaroos.
heptapleurum actinophyllum.about: Heptapleurum actinophyllum is a tree in the family Araliaceae.

heracleum maximum.name: Cow parsnip
heracleum maximum.desc: Cow parsnip (Heracleum maximum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 721 times near the park in GBIF.
heracleum maximum.about: Heracleum maximum, commonly known as cow parsnip, is the only member of the genus Heracleum native to North America.

heritiera fomes.name: Sundri
heritiera fomes.desc: The tree that gives the Sundarbans its name. UNESCO-listed forest descriptions and Wikipedia note it is very sensitive to rising salinity.
heritiera fomes.about: Heritiera fomes is a species of mangrove tree in the family Malvaceae. Its common names include sunder, sundri, jekanazo and pinlekanazo.

herpestes ichneumon.name: Egyptian mongoose
herpestes ichneumon.desc: A common Iberian carnivore that hunts rabbits, birds, reptiles and amphibians. The Iberian lynx often kills it.
herpestes ichneumon.about: The Egyptian mongoose, also known as ichneumon (), is a mongoose species native to the tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas, and shrublands of Africa and around the Mediterranean Basin in…

herpestes javanicus.name: Small Indian mongoose
herpestes javanicus.desc: An introduced predator and the most recorded mammal near the park. It eats rodents, insects, birds and eggs and was named as a predator of nēnē.
herpestes javanicus.about: The small Indian mongoose is a mongoose species native to Iraq and northern India; it has also been introduced to several Caribbean and Pacific islands.

hesperia comma.about: Hesperia comma, the silver-spotted skipper or common branded skipper, is a butterfly of the family Hesperiidae.

hesperis matronalis.name: Dame's-violet

hesperis matronalis.about: Hesperis matronalis is an herbaceous flowering plant species in the family Brassicaceae.

hesperostipa comata.name: Needle-and-thread grass

hesperostipa comata.about: Hesperostipa comata, commonly known as needle-and-thread grass, is a species of grass native to North America, especially the western third.
