hesperoyucca whipplei.desc: Our Lord's-candle (Hesperoyucca whipplei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 136 times near the park in GBIF.
hesperoyucca whipplei.about: Hesperoyucca whipplei, the chaparral yucca, our Lord's candle, Spanish bayonet, Quixote yucca or foothill yucca, is a species of flowering plant closely related to, and formerly usually included in,…

hetaerina americana.name: American Rubyspot
hetaerina americana.desc: American Rubyspot (Hetaerina americana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
hetaerina americana.about: The American rubyspot is a damselfly of the family Calopterygidae. Males have a lustrous red head and thorax and a large red spot at the base of each wing.

heteranthera limosa.name: Mud Plantain
heteranthera limosa.desc: Mud Plantain (Heteranthera limosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

heterodon platirhinos.name: Eastern Hognose Snake
heterodon platirhinos.desc: Eastern hognosed snake (Heterodon platirhinos): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
heterodon platirhinos.about: The eastern hog-nosed snake is a species of mildly venomous rear-fanged snake in the family Colubridae. The venom is specifically adapted to amphibian prey and is harmless to humans.

heterohyrax brucei.name: Bruce's yellow-spotted hyrax
heterohyrax brucei.desc: A rock-dwelling mammal that lives in colonies in rocky terrain. Hyraxes eat a wide variety of plants and are hunted by raptors, snakes and carnivores.
heterohyrax brucei.about: The yellow-spotted rock hyrax or bush hyrax is a species of hyrax in the family Procaviidae.

heteromeles arbutifolia.name: California-holly
heteromeles arbutifolia.desc: California-holly (Heteromeles arbutifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 349 times near the park in GBIF.

heteromys desmarestianus.name: Desmarest's spiny pocket mouse
heteromys desmarestianus.desc: A small forest-floor rodent that eats seeds and fruit and is prey for snakes and small cats.
heteromys desmarestianus.about: Desmarest's spiny pocket mouse is a species of rodent in the family Heteromyidae. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, and Panama.

heteropogon contortus.name: Black speargrass
heteropogon contortus.desc: Another tall savanna grass listed for the park, growing alongside kangaroo grass on the dry hillsides.
heteropogon contortus.about: Heteropogon contortus is a tropical, perennial tussock grass with a native distribution encompassing Southern Africa, southern Asia, Northern Australia, Oceania, and southwestern North America.

heterotheca subaxillaris.name: Camphorweed
heterotheca subaxillaris.desc: Camphorweed (Heterotheca subaxillaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
heterotheca subaxillaris.about: Heterotheca subaxillaris, known by the common name camphorweed, is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

heterotheca villosa.name: Hairy false goldenaster
heterotheca villosa.desc: Hairy false goldenaster (Heterotheca villosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
heterotheca villosa.about: Heterotheca villosa, commonly known as the hairy goldenaster, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae found in central and western North America.

heuchera richardsonii.name: Richardson's alumroot
heuchera richardsonii.desc: Richardson's alumroot (Heuchera richardsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.

hexaprotodon liberiensis.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
hexaprotodon liberiensis.desc: Forages at dusk on herbs, ferns, shoots and fallen fruit. Camera traps confirmed it in Sapo in 2008. Liberia holds most of the wild population.
hexaprotodon liberiensis.about: The pygmy hippopotamus or pygmy hippo is a small hippopotamid which is native to the forests and swamps of West Africa, primarily in Liberia, with small populations in Sierra Leone, Guinea, and Ivory…

hexastylis arifolia.name: Littlebrownjug
hexastylis arifolia.desc: Littlebrownjug (Hexastylis arifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 132 times near the park in GBIF.
hexastylis arifolia.about: Asarum arifolia (common names the little brown jug, arrowleaf, and heartleaf) is a perennial wildflower in the family Aristolochiaceae found in the southeastern United States, from Louisiana to…

hibiscus laevis.name: Scarlet rose-mallow
hibiscus laevis.desc: Scarlet rose-mallow (Hibiscus laevis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
hibiscus laevis.about: Hibiscus laevis, the halberd-leaf rosemallow, is a herbaceous perennial flower native to central and eastern North America.

hibiscus moscheutos.name: Common Rose-mallow
hibiscus moscheutos.desc: Common Rose-mallow (Hibiscus moscheutos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
hibiscus moscheutos.about: Muenchhusia moscheutos, the rose mallow, swamp rose-mallow, crimsoneyed rosemallow, or eastern rosemallow, is a species of flowering plant in the family Malvaceae.

hieraaetus pennatus.name: Booted eagle
hieraaetus pennatus.desc: A small eagle that hunts birds, lizards and small mammals. GloBI records link it to chukar, ground squirrels and many small birds.
hieraaetus pennatus.about: The booted eagle is a medium-sized mostly migratory bird of prey with a wide distribution in the Palearctic and southern Asia, wintering in the tropics of Africa and Asia, with a small, disjunct…

hierophis cypriensis.name: Cyprus whip snake
hierophis cypriensis.desc: Endemic to Cyprus and widespread in Troodos; eats lizards, amphibians, insects and other snakes.
hierophis cypriensis.about: The Cyprus whip snake is a species of snake in the family Colubridae. It is endemic to Cyprus.

hierophis gemonensis.name: Balkan racer
hierophis gemonensis.desc: A fast, slender snake of the Balkans that hunts lizards and small mammals.
hierophis gemonensis.about: The Balkan whip snake is a species of snake in the family Colubridae.

highland mist.name: Highland mist
highland mist.desc: Cliffs and mountains catch cloud and mist, creating wetter refuges where many endemic plants grow.

highland soil.name: Highland soil
highland soil.desc: Nutrients recycled from dead plants and dung in the cool plateau soil feed the grasses, heath and lobelia.

hilaria rigida.name: Big galleta
hilaria rigida.desc: Tough bunchgrass of sandy and rocky desert ground, one of the main grasses available to grazers here.
hilaria rigida.about: Hilaria rigida is a species of clumping perennial grass that is widespread in California deserts. It is commonly known as big galleta.

himatione sanguinea.name: ʻApapane
himatione sanguinea.desc: A native honeycreeper that drinks ʻōhiʻa nectar and pollinates it. It also takes insects and spiders, mostly moths and butterflies in one study.
himatione sanguinea.about: The ʻapapane is a small, crimson species of Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the Hawaiian Islands.

hippocamelus bisulcus.name: Huemul
hippocamelus bisulcus.desc: An endangered Andean deer of scrub and forest borders. Lenga is a common item in its diet, and the puma is its only natural predator.
hippocamelus bisulcus.about: The south Andean deer, also known as the southern guemal, south Andean huemul, southern huemul, or Chilean huemul or güemul ( WAY-mool, Spanish: [weˈmul]), is an endangered species of deer native to…

hippodamia convergens.name: Convergent lady beetle
hippodamia convergens.desc: Convergent lady beetle (Hippodamia convergens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
hippodamia convergens.about: Hippodamia convergens, commonly known as the convergent lady beetle, is one of the most common lady beetles in North America and is found throughout the continent.

hippophae rhamnoides.name: Sea buckthorn
hippophae rhamnoides.desc: Thorny shrub of riverbeds and valleys whose roots host nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Its berries are eaten by magpies and other birds.
hippophae rhamnoides.about: Sea-buckthorn, also known as sea buckthorn, sandthorn, sallowthorn or seaberry, is a species of flowering plant in the family Elaeagnaceae, native to cold-temperate regions of Eurasia.

hippopotamus amphibius.name: Hippopotamus
hippopotamus amphibius.desc: Grazes grass on land at night and rests in water by day. Its dung moves land nutrients into rivers, where it feeds fish and invertebrates.
hippopotamus amphibius.about: The hippopotamus, often shortened to hippo (pl.: hippos), further qualified as the common hippopotamus, Nile hippopotamus and river hippopotamus, is a large semiaquatic mammal native to sub-Saharan…

hipposideros armiger.name: Great roundleaf bat
hipposideros armiger.desc: A large cave-roosting bat recorded often in the area. Ten threatened bat species have been recorded in the park, and bats eat flying insects at night.
hipposideros armiger.about: The great roundleaf bat, also known as the great Himalayan leaf-nosed bat is a species of bat in the family Hipposideridae found in South Asia, Southeast Asia, and China.

hipposideros cervinus.name: Fawn leaf-nosed bat
hipposideros cervinus.desc: An insect-eating cave-roosting bat; it takes beetles and moths in flight close to vegetation, and is the most recorded mammal near Santo.
hipposideros cervinus.about: The fawn leaf-nosed bat is a species of bat in the family Hipposideridae found in Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vanuatu.

hippotragus equinus.name: Roan antelope
hippotragus equinus.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of Sudanian savanna, recorded often in the Arly area.
hippotragus equinus.about: The roan antelope is a large, savanna-dwelling antelope found in Western, Southern, and parts of Central and Eastern Africa.

hodotermitidae.name: Harvester termites
hodotermitidae.desc: Termites that gather dry grass and carry it underground, turning scarce plant matter into food for other animals.
hodotermitidae.about: The Hodotermitidae (from Greek ὁδός (hodós), travelling; Latin termes, woodworm) are a basal Old World family of termites known as the harvester termites.

holbrookia maculata.name: Bleached earless lizard
holbrookia maculata.desc: A pale lizard of the White Sands dunes that eats insects and spiders. Its pale colour matches the sand.
holbrookia maculata.about: Holbrookia maculata, commonly known as the lesser earless lizard, is a species of lizard in the family Phrynosomatidae.

holcosus undulatus.name: Rainbow ameiva
holcosus undulatus.desc: A fast ground lizard of forest floors that forages for insects and other small invertebrates.
holcosus undulatus.about: Holcosus undulatus, also known commonly as the barred whiptail, the metallic ameiva, and the rainbow ameiva, is a species of lizard in the family Teiidae.

homalosorus pycnocarpos.name: Narrow-leaved glade fern
homalosorus pycnocarpos.desc: Narrow-leaved glade fern (Homalosorus pycnocarpos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

honckenya peploides.name: Sea Sandwort
honckenya peploides.desc: Sea Sandwort (Honckenya peploides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
honckenya peploides.about: Honckenya peploides, the sea sandwort (UK) or seaside sandplant (Canada), is the only species in the genus Honckenya of the plant family Caryophyllaceae.

hopea.name: Hopea and other lowland trees
hopea.desc: Evergreen tropical wet forest on limestone below 800 m covers about three quarters of the park. Hopea is one of its listed trees, and the leaves and fruit of such trees feed primates and other forest animals.
hopea.about: Hopea is a genus of plants in the family Dipterocarpaceae. It contains some 114 species, distributed from Sri Lanka and southern India to the Andaman Islands, Myanmar, southern China, and southward…

hoplitis pilosifrons.name: Hairy-fronted Small-Mason
hoplitis pilosifrons.desc: Hairy-fronted Small-Mason (Hoplitis pilosifrons): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

hordeum jubatum.name: Foxtail Barley
hordeum jubatum.desc: Foxtail Barley (Hordeum jubatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
hordeum jubatum.about: Hordeum jubatum, with common names foxtail barley, bobtail barley, squirreltail barley, and intermediate barley, is a perennial plant species in the grass family Poaceae.

hordeum spontaneum.name: Wild barley
hordeum spontaneum.desc: A wild grass that GBIF records often in the reserve. Seed-eating birds such as blackbirds are recorded eating barley in GloBI.
hordeum spontaneum.about: Barley, a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.

hordeum vulgare.name: Six-rowed Barley
hordeum vulgare.desc: Six-rowed Barley (Hordeum vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

hot, salty shallow water.name: Hot, salty shallow water
hot, salty shallow water.desc: The Gulf is shallow and very saline. Its seagrasses tolerate a wide range of salinity, which helps them hold the shallows.

hottonia inflata.name: American Featherfoil
hottonia inflata.desc: American Featherfoil (Hottonia inflata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

houbaropsis bengalensis.name: Bengal florican
houbaropsis bengalensis.desc: Endangered bird of tall grassland; Manas holds the largest population anywhere according to Wikipedia.
houbaropsis bengalensis.about: The Bengal florican, also called the Bengal bustard, is a bustard species native to the Indian subcontinent, Cambodia, and Vietnam.

houstonia caerulea.name: Azure Bluet
houstonia caerulea.desc: Azure Bluet (Houstonia caerulea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 43 times near the park in GBIF.
houstonia caerulea.about: Houstonia caerulea, commonly known as azure bluet, Quaker ladies, or bluets, is a perennial species in the family Rubiaceae.

houstonia longifolia.name: Longleaf bluet
houstonia longifolia.desc: Longleaf bluet (Houstonia longifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

houstonia procumbens.name: Roundleaf bluet
houstonia procumbens.desc: Roundleaf bluet (Houstonia procumbens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
houstonia procumbens.about: Houstonia procumbens, the roundleaf bluet, is a perennial species in the family Rubiaceae.

houstonia purpurea.name: Venus' pride
houstonia purpurea.desc: Venus' pride (Houstonia purpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

houstonia pusilla.name: Tiny bluet
houstonia pusilla.desc: Tiny bluet (Houstonia pusilla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
houstonia pusilla.about: Houstonia pusilla (tiny bluet) is a plant in the family Rubiaceae native to the United States and common in the southeastern and central parts of the country, from Texas to Florida north to Long…

howea forsteriana.name: Kentia palm
howea forsteriana.desc: A palm found naturally only on Lord Howe Island, and a defining tree of its forests. Wild seeds are collected for a regulated export trade.
howea forsteriana.about: Howea forsteriana, the Kentia palm, thatch palm or palm court palm, is a species of flowering plant in the palm family, Arecaceae, endemic to Lord Howe Island in Australia.

hudsonia tomentosa.name: Beach heath
hudsonia tomentosa.desc: Beach heath (Hudsonia tomentosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.
hudsonia tomentosa.about: Hudsonia tomentosa is a species of flowering plant in the rockrose family known by the common names woolly beachheather, beach heather, and sand heather.

human food waste.name: Human food waste
human food waste.desc: Trash, compost, pet food and bird-feeder seed are an extra food supply for raccoons, coyotes, squirrels and urban birds.

humulus scandens.name: Japanese Hop
humulus scandens.desc: Japanese Hop (Humulus scandens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
humulus scandens.about: Humulus japonicus is a species of flowering plant in family Cannabaceae. This ornamental plant is sometimes referred to by the common name Japanese hops.

hurricane winds.name: Hurricane winds
hurricane winds.desc: Hugo, Georges, Irma and Maria damaged the forest and cut parrot numbers. Open gaps let pioneer trees such as pumpwood take over.

huso huso.name: Beluga sturgeon
huso huso.desc: Giant migratory fish that runs up the Danube to spawn. Adults eat mainly large fish; it is critically endangered.
huso huso.about: The beluga (), also known as the beluga sturgeon or great sturgeon, is a species of sturgeon, which are anadromous fish of the family Acipenseridae of the order Acipenseriformes.

hyaena hyaena.name: Striped hyena
hyaena hyaena.desc: A shy scavenger of the dry forest that cleans up carcasses left by tigers and leopards.
hyaena hyaena.about: The striped hyena is a species of hyena native to North and East Africa, the Middle East, the Caucasus, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent. It is the only extant species in the genus Hyaena.

hyalella.name: Hyalella amphipods
hyalella.desc: Small freshwater crustaceans, many endemic to the lake. They are a main food of the Titicaca water frog.
hyalella.about: Hyalella is a genus of amphipods found in the Americas. They are mainly found in freshwater habitats.

hydrangea arborescens.name: Smooth Hydrangea
hydrangea arborescens.desc: Smooth Hydrangea (Hydrangea arborescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.
hydrangea arborescens.about: Hydrangea arborescens, commonly known as smooth hydrangea or sevenbark, is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydrangeaceae.

hydrangea quercifolia.name: Oak-leaf hydrangea
hydrangea quercifolia.desc: Oak-leaf hydrangea (Hydrangea quercifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 62 times near the park in GBIF.
hydrangea quercifolia.about: Hydrangea quercifolia, commonly known as oakleaf hydrangea or oak-leaved hydrangea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Hydrangeaceae.

hydrastis canadensis.name: Goldenseal
hydrastis canadensis.desc: Goldenseal (Hydrastis canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
hydrastis canadensis.about: Goldenseal, also called orangeroot or yellow puccoon, is a perennial herb in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae, native to North America.

hydrilla verticillata.name: Hydrilla
hydrilla verticillata.desc: Hydrilla (Hydrilla verticillata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

hydrocharis morsus-ranae.name: Frogbit
hydrocharis morsus-ranae.desc: Frogbit (Hydrocharis morsus-ranae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.
hydrocharis morsus-ranae.about: Hydrocharis morsus-ranae L. is a species of the genus Hydrocharis known by the common name European frog-bit. It is a free-floating flowering plant that bears small white flowers.

hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.name: Capybara
hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.desc: The world's largest rodent grazes riverbank plants and rests in water to avoid predators.
hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.about: The capybara ( kap-ih-BAR-uh) or greater capybara is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.

hydrocotyle bonariensis.name: Largeleaf pennywort
hydrocotyle bonariensis.desc: Largeleaf pennywort (Hydrocotyle bonariensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
hydrocotyle bonariensis.about: Hydrocotyle bonariensis, the largeleaf pennywort, once a member of the family Apiaceae, now in the family Araliaceae and of the genus Hydrocotyle, is a hairless and creeping perennial.

hydrocynus forskahlii.name: Elongate tigerfish
hydrocynus forskahlii.desc: A fast predatory fish recorded in the Sudd system that hunts smaller fish.
hydrocynus forskahlii.about: Hydrocynus forskahlii, the elongate tigerfish, is a species of predatory characin from the family Alestidae which is found in northern and western Africa.

hydrophyllum appendiculatum.name: Great waterleaf
hydrophyllum appendiculatum.desc: Great waterleaf (Hydrophyllum appendiculatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
hydrophyllum appendiculatum.about: Hydrophyllum appendiculatum, commonly known as great waterleaf, appendage waterleaf, or woolen breeches, is native to central and eastern North America where it is found primarily in the Midwest and…

hydrophyllum virginianum.name: Eastern Waterleaf
hydrophyllum virginianum.desc: Eastern Waterleaf (Hydrophyllum virginianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

hydropotes inermis.name: Chinese water deer
hydropotes inermis.desc: Lives among tall reeds, swamps and fields along rivers. Wikipedia says the DMZ has given it protected habitat, and that its Korean boom is linked to the loss of tigers and leopards.
hydropotes inermis.about: The water deer is a small deer species native to Korea and China. It has prominent tusks, unlike all other living true deer.

hydroprogne caspia.name: Caspian tern
hydroprogne caspia.desc: Large tern that plunges for fish, hunting over bays and sometimes travelling far from its colony to feed.
hydroprogne caspia.about: The Caspian tern is the world's largest species of tern, with a subcosmopolitan but scattered distribution. Despite its extensive range, it is monotypic of its genus, and has no accepted subspecies.

hydrurga leptonyx.name: Leopard seal
hydrurga leptonyx.desc: Apex predator that eats penguins, other seals and krill, which it strains through its teeth.
hydrurga leptonyx.about: The leopard seal, also referred to as the sea leopard, is a long and muscular seal native to the Southern Ocean of Antarctica and southern Patagonia.

hylaeus affinis.name: Eastern Masked Bee
hylaeus affinis.desc: Eastern Masked Bee (Hylaeus affinis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
hylaeus affinis.about: Hylaeus affinis is a species of hymenopteran in the family Colletidae. It is found in North America.

hylaeus annulatus.name: Annulate Masked Bee
hylaeus annulatus.desc: Annulate Masked Bee (Hylaeus annulatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

hylaeus leptocephalus.name: Slender-faced Masked Bee
hylaeus leptocephalus.desc: Slender-faced Masked Bee (Hylaeus leptocephalus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
hylaeus leptocephalus.about: Hylaeus leptocephalus is a species of hymenopteran in the family Colletidae. It is native to the Palearctic but can, since 1912, also be found in North America.

hylaeus mesillae.name: Mesilla Masked Bee
hylaeus mesillae.desc: Mesilla Masked Bee (Hylaeus mesillae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

hylaeus modestus.name: Yellow-faced bee
hylaeus modestus.desc: Yellow-faced bee (Hylaeus modestus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

hyles lineata.name: White-lined sphinx moth
hyles lineata.desc: A hawk-moth whose caterpillars and adults feed on desert flowers and shrubs, and which is eaten by birds and lizards.
hyles lineata.about: Hyles lineata, also known as the white-lined sphinx moth, is a moth of the family Sphingidae.

hylobates funereus.name: Eastern grey gibbon
hylobates funereus.desc: Wikipedia calls it the best-known arboreal mammal of the park, living mostly in the canopy. Gibbons mainly eat fruit.
hylobates funereus.about: The eastern grey gibbon or northern grey gibbon is a primate in the gibbon family, Hylobatidae.

hylobates lar.name: White-handed gibbon
hylobates lar.desc: Mostly eats fruit (about half its diet), plus leaves, insects and flowers; figs are a favourite. Long-term studies of its social life were done at Khao Yai.
hylobates lar.about: The lar gibbon, also known as the white-handed gibbon, is an endangered primate in the gibbon family, Hylobatidae. It is one of the better-known gibbons and is often kept in captivity.

hylodesmum glutinosum.name: Large-flowered Tickclover
hylodesmum glutinosum.desc: Large-flowered Tickclover (Hylodesmum glutinosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

hylodesmum nudiflorum.name: Bare-stemmed tick-trefoil
hylodesmum nudiflorum.desc: Bare-stemmed tick-trefoil (Hylodesmum nudiflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

hylotelephium telephioides.name: Live-for-ever
hylotelephium telephioides.desc: Live-for-ever (Hylotelephium telephioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
hylotelephium telephioides.about: Hylotelephium telephioides is a flowering plant in the stonecrop family Crassulaceae. Its common names include Allegheny stonecrop and live-forever.

hymenocallis occidentalis.name: Carolina spider-lily
hymenocallis occidentalis.desc: Carolina spider-lily (Hymenocallis occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
hymenocallis occidentalis.about: Hymenocallis occidentalis is a plant species native to the southern United States.

hymenocallis rotata.name: Spring-run spider-lily
