juglans cinerea.name: White walnut
juglans cinerea.desc: White walnut (Juglans cinerea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

juglans microcarpa.name: Texas walnut
juglans microcarpa.desc: Texas walnut (Juglans microcarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

juglans regia.name: Wild walnut
juglans regia.desc: Feral walnut trees grow in the river flood-land forests of the reserve. The nuts are a rich food for animals such as wild boar.
juglans regia.about: Juglans regia, known by various common names including the common walnut, English walnut, or Persian walnut amongst other names, is a species of walnut.

junco hyemalis.name: Dark-eyed Junco
junco hyemalis.desc: Dark-eyed Junco (Junco hyemalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,078 times near the park in GBIF.
junco hyemalis.about: The dark-eyed junco is a species of junco, a group of small, grayish New World sparrows. The species is common across much of temperate North America and in summer it ranges far into the Arctic.

juncus biflorus.name: Bog rush
juncus biflorus.desc: Bog rush (Juncus biflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus dudleyi.name: Dudley Rush
juncus dudleyi.desc: Dudley Rush (Juncus dudleyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
juncus dudleyi.about: Juncus dudleyi is a widespread species of rush native to North America, and introduced to northern South America, Japan, Great Britain and central Europe. Its diploid chromosome number is 2n=80.

juncus effusus.name: Soft Rush
juncus effusus.desc: Soft Rush (Juncus effusus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
juncus effusus.about: Juncus effusus is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant species in the rush family Juncaceae, with the common names common rush or soft rush.

juncus ensifolius.name: Sword-leaved Rush
juncus ensifolius.desc: Sword-leaved Rush (Juncus ensifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
juncus ensifolius.about: Juncus ensifolius is a species of rush known by the common names swordleaf rush, sword-leaved rush, and three-stamened rush.

juncus maritimus.name: Sea rush and salt meadow
juncus maritimus.desc: Rushes and salt-tolerant grasses of the brackish meadows where semi-wild horses and cattle graze.
juncus maritimus.about: Juncus maritimus, known as the sea rush, is a species of rush that grows on coastlines. It is sometimes considered conspecific with Juncus kraussii.

juncus pelocarpus.name: Brownfruit Rush
juncus pelocarpus.desc: Brownfruit Rush (Juncus pelocarpus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
juncus pelocarpus.about: Juncus pelocarpus, the brown-fruit rush, is a species of flowering plant in the family Juncaceae, native to British Columbia and eastern Canada, and the north-central and eastern United States.

juncus torreyi.name: Torrey's rush
juncus torreyi.desc: Torrey's rush (Juncus torreyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus validus.name: Roundhead rush
juncus validus.desc: Roundhead rush (Juncus validus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

juncus xiphioides.name: Irisleaf rush
juncus xiphioides.desc: Irisleaf rush (Juncus xiphioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
juncus xiphioides.about: Juncus xiphioides is a species of flowering plant in the family Juncaceae. It is sometimes referred to by the common name Irisleaf Rush.

juniperus communis.name: Common Juniper
juniperus communis.desc: Common Juniper (Juniperus communis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 40 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus deppeana.name: Checker-bark juniper
juniperus deppeana.desc: Checker-bark juniper (Juniperus deppeana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
juniperus deppeana.about: Juniperus deppeana is a small to medium-sized tree reaching 10–15 metres (33–49 feet) in height. It is native to central and northern Mexico and the southwestern United States.

juniperus drupacea.name: Syrian juniper
juniperus drupacea.desc: A juniper of the mountain slopes that grows alongside cedar in Lebanon and Turkey.
juniperus drupacea.about: Juniperus drupacea, the Syrian juniper, is a species of juniper native to the eastern Mediterranean region from southern Greece (mount Parnon in the Peloponnese), southern Turkey, western Syria,…

juniperus monosperma.name: Oneseed Juniper
juniperus monosperma.desc: Oneseed Juniper (Juniperus monosperma): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus occidentalis.name: Western juniper
juniperus occidentalis.desc: Western juniper (Juniperus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
juniperus occidentalis.about: Juniperus occidentalis, known as the western juniper, is a shrub or tree native to the Western United States, growing in mountains at altitudes of 800–3,000 meters (2,600–9,800 ft) and rarely down to…

juniperus osteosperma.name: Utah juniper
juniperus osteosperma.desc: Utah Juniper (Juniperus osteosperma): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
juniperus osteosperma.about: Juniperus osteosperma is a shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States.

juniperus phoenicea.name: Phoenician juniper
juniperus phoenicea.desc: An evergreen tree of the reserve highlands. Its berry-like cones are mainly spread by birds that eat them.
juniperus phoenicea.about: Juniperus phoenicea, the Phoenicean juniper or Arâr, is a species of juniper found in the western Mediterranean region.

juniperus pinchotii.name: Copper-berry juniper
juniperus pinchotii.desc: Copper-berry juniper (Juniperus pinchotii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

juniperus polycarpos.name: Juniper
juniperus polycarpos.desc: The dominant tree of the reserve in sparse stands at mid altitude. Cinereous vultures nest on the old trees.
juniperus polycarpos.about: Juniperus polycarpos, commonly known as Persian juniper, is species of juniper native to western Asia. Some authorities classify it as a subspecies or variety of Juniperus excelsa.

juniperus procera.name: African juniper
juniperus procera.desc: Evergreen conifer that dominates the Daallo escarpment forest alongside wild olive. Its blue-black berry-like cones feed birds such as bulbuls and pigeons.
juniperus procera.about: Juniperus procera is a coniferous tree native to mountainous areas in Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. It is a characteristic tree of the Afromontane flora.

juniperus sabina.name: Savin juniper
juniperus sabina.desc: Low evergreen shrub of dry slopes. Ibex browse juniper twigs in winter, and birds eat the cones.
juniperus sabina.about: Juniperus sabina, the savin juniper or savin, is a species of juniper native to the mountains of central and southern Europe and western and central Asia, from Spain to eastern Siberia, typically…

juniperus scopulorum.name: Rocky Mountain juniper
juniperus scopulorum.desc: Rocky Mountain juniper (Juniperus scopulorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
juniperus scopulorum.about: Juniperus scopulorum, the Rocky Mountain juniper, is a species of juniper native to western North America, from southwest Canada to the Great Plains of the United States and small areas of northern…

juniperus virginiana.name: Virginian Juniper
juniperus virginiana.desc: Virginian Juniper (Juniperus virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
juniperus virginiana.about: Juniperus virginiana, also known as eastern red cedar, red cedar, Virginian juniper, eastern juniper, red juniper, and other local names, is a species of juniper native to eastern North America from…

junonia atlites.name: Grey pansy
junonia atlites.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on rice and other plants of open, wet ground.
junonia atlites.about: Junonia atlites, the grey pansy, is a species of nymphalid butterfly found in South Asia.

junonia coenia.name: Common Buckeye
junonia coenia.desc: Common Buckeye (Junonia coenia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
junonia coenia.about: Junonia coenia, known as the common buckeye or buckeye, is a butterfly in the family Nymphalidae.

junonia grisea.name: Gray buckeye
junonia grisea.desc: Gray buckeye (Junonia grisea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
junonia grisea.about: Junonia grisea, also known as the gray buckeye, grey buckeye, or Western buckeye, is a species in the butterfly family Nymphalidae. It is found in North America, west of the Rocky Mountains.

kalahari sand and soil.name: Kalahari sand and soil
kalahari sand and soil.desc: Sandy soils recycle dung and dead plants into nutrients for grasses and trees.

kallstroemia grandiflora.name: Arizona-poppy
kallstroemia grandiflora.desc: Arizona-poppy (Kallstroemia grandiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

kalmia latifolia.name: Calico-bush
kalmia latifolia.desc: Mountain laurel (Kalmia latifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
kalmia latifolia.about: Kalmia latifolia, the mountain laurel, calico-bush, or spoonwood, is a flowering plant and one of the 10 species in the genus of Kalmia belonging to the heath(er) family Ericaceae.

kaloula pulchra.name: Banded bullfrog
kaloula pulchra.desc: Burrowing frog that eats ants, termites and other small insects.
kaloula pulchra.about: The banded bullfrog is a species of frog in the narrow-mouthed frog family Microhylidae.

karst groundwater.name: Karst groundwater
karst groundwater.desc: Rain sinks straight through the porous limestone and surfaces as cenotes and springs, supplying the freshwater that wetlands and mangroves depend on.

karst limestone soil.name: Karst limestone soil
karst limestone soil.desc: The park sits on a forested karst landscape of limestone, with sinkholes, caves and thin soils.

karst springs and prespa seepage.name: Karst springs and Prespa seepage
karst springs and prespa seepage.desc: Springs on the eastern shore give about half of the lake's inflow, and over a fifth comes underground from Lake Prespa.

kentropyx calcarata.name: Striped forest whiptail
kentropyx calcarata.desc: A fast ground lizard of Amazonian and Guianan forests. It is recorded as prey of the fer-de-lance.
kentropyx calcarata.about: Kentropyx calcarata, commonly known as the striped forest whiptail, is a species of lizard endemic to South America.

kerodon rupestris.name: Rock cavy
kerodon rupestris.desc: A rodent introduced by the military in the 1960s as game. Feral cats prey on it.
kerodon rupestris.about: The rock cavy or mocó is a species of cavy that is endemic to eastern Brazil. It has also been introduced to the Atlantic island of Fernando de Noronha.

kinyongia tavetana.name: Kilimanjaro two-horned chameleon
kinyongia tavetana.desc: A chameleon found only on the mountain that hunts insects.
kinyongia tavetana.about: Kinyongia tavetana, the Kilimanjaro two-horned chameleon or Kilimanjaro blade-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon in the genus Kinyongia.

kniphofia foliosa.name: Red hot poker
kniphofia foliosa.desc: Tall flowering plant of the highlands. Mountain nyala eat it, and Ethiopian wolves have been seen drinking its nectar.

kobuk river.name: Kobuk River
kobuk river.desc: The river divides the park. Caribou cross it each year, and its valley is a wetland that supports willows and sedges.

kobus ellipsiprymnus.name: Waterbuck
kobus ellipsiprymnus.desc: The most recorded large mammal near the park. Mostly grazes grass and stays close to water.
kobus ellipsiprymnus.about: The waterbuck is a large antelope found widely in sub-Saharan Africa. It is in the genus Kobus of the family Bovidae.

kobus kob.name: Kob
kobus kob.desc: A grassland antelope, most numerous of the large herbivores recorded here. It feeds on grasses and stays near water.
kobus kob.about: The kob is an antelope found across Central Africa and parts of West Africa and East Africa.

kobus leche.name: Southern lechwe
kobus leche.desc: A floodplain antelope that grazes wet ground and is hunted by lions, leopards and wild dogs.
kobus leche.about: The lechwe, red lechwe, or southern lechwe is an antelope found in wetlands of south-central Africa.

kobus megaceros.name: Nile lechwe
kobus megaceros.desc: An endangered, semi-aquatic antelope of the Sudd floodplains that grazes marsh vegetation in shallow water.
kobus megaceros.about: The Nile lechwe or Mrs Gray's lechwe is an endangered species of antelope found in swamps and grasslands in South Sudan and Ethiopia.

kobus vardonii.name: Puku
kobus vardonii.desc: A floodplain antelope of grassland near water and the best-recorded large grazer in the park area.
kobus vardonii.about: The puku is a medium-sized antelope found in wet grasslands in southern Democratic Republic of Congo, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia and more concentrated in the Okavango Delta in Botswana.

koeberlinia spinosa.name: Crown of thorns
koeberlinia spinosa.desc: Crown of thorns (Koeberlinia spinosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
koeberlinia spinosa.about: Koeberlinia spinosa is a species of flowering plant native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico known by several common names, including crown of thorns, allthorn, smokebush, and…

koeleria.name: Tussock grass
koeleria.desc: Tufted grasses of the open moorland and tussock grassland above the tree line.
koeleria.about: Koeleria is a common and widespread genus of plants in the grass family, found on all continents except Antarctica and on various oceanic islands. It includes species known generally as Junegrasses.

krascheninnikovia ceratoides.name: Pamirian winterfat
krascheninnikovia ceratoides.desc: A low, hardy shrub of dry mountain steppe and one of the most recorded plants near the park.
krascheninnikovia ceratoides.about: Krascheninnikovia ceratoides, or the Pamirian winterfat, is a plant species native to Central Europe and Southern Europe, North Africa, and parts of Asia.

krascheninnikovia lanata.name: Winterfat
krascheninnikovia lanata.desc: Winterfat (Krascheninnikovia lanata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.
krascheninnikovia lanata.about: Krascheninnikovia lanata is a species of flowering plant currently placed in the family Amaranthaceae (previously, Chenopodiaceae), known by the common names winterfat, white sage, and wintersage.

krigia biflora.name: Orange dwarf-dandelion
krigia biflora.desc: Orange dwarf-dandelion (Krigia biflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
krigia biflora.about: Krigia biflora, also known as two-flower cynthia or two-flower dwarf dandelion, is a species of plant in the family Asteraceae.

krigia virginica.name: Virginia Dwarf-dandelion
krigia virginica.desc: Virginia Dwarf-dandelion (Krigia virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
krigia virginica.about: Krigia virginica, also known as dwarf dandelion or Virginia dwarf dandelion, is a North American species of plants in the family Asteraceae.

kuroshio warm current.name: Kuroshio warm current
kuroshio warm current.desc: A warm ocean current flows past the Ryukyu islands and keeps the sea around the island warm, supporting its plankton and marine life.

labridae.name: Wrasses
labridae.desc: A varied family of reef fishes that eat small invertebrates; wrasses are common on coral reefs.
labridae.about: The wrasses are a family, Labridae, of marine ray-finned fish, many of which are brightly colored.

lactuca graminifolia.name: Grassleaf lettuce
lactuca graminifolia.desc: Grassleaf lettuce (Lactuca graminifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
lactuca graminifolia.about: Lactuca graminifolia, the grassleaf lettuce is a North American species of wild lettuce.

ladeania lanceolata.name: Dune Scrufpea
ladeania lanceolata.desc: Dune Scrufpea (Ladeania lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
ladeania lanceolata.about: Ladeania lanceolata is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by several common names, including lemon scurfpea, wild lemonweed, and dune scurfpea.

lagarosiphon.name: Aquatic plants
lagarosiphon.desc: Submerged water plants of the river channels and lagoons, a food base for plant-eating fish.
lagarosiphon.about: Lagarosiphon is a genus of aquatic plants described as a genus in 1841. It is native to Africa and Madagascar.

lagenorhynchus acutus.name: Atlantic White-sided Dolphin
lagenorhynchus acutus.desc: Atlantic White-sided Dolphin (Lagenorhynchus acutus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

lagidium viscacia.name: Southern viscacha
lagidium viscacia.desc: A rock-dwelling rodent of the Andes that eats grasses, moss and lichens. The Andean mountain cat preys on it.
lagidium viscacia.about: The southern viscacha is a species of viscacha, a rodent in the family Chinchillidae found in Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

lagoon water.name: Warm, clear lagoon water
lagoon water.desc: Shallow, sheltered water inside the barrier reefs lets light reach seagrass beds and reef flats. Heat waves and silt are threats to such water.

lagopus lagopus.name: Willow ptarmigan
lagopus lagopus.desc: A ground bird of tundra and shrubland that eats berries, buds and willow, and is prey for foxes, wolves, lynx and eagles.
lagopus lagopus.about: The willow ptarmigan is a bird in the grouse tribe Tetraonini of the pheasant family Phasianidae. It is also known as the willow grouse.

lagopus leucura.name: White-tailed Ptarmigan
lagopus leucura.desc: White-tailed Ptarmigan (Lagopus leucura): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
lagopus leucura.about: The white-tailed ptarmigan, also known as the snow quail, is the smallest bird in the grouse tribe.

lagopus muta.name: Rock ptarmigan
lagopus muta.desc: The only bird that stays in Svalbard through winter, living on buds, twigs and seeds of low tundra plants.
lagopus muta.about: The rock ptarmigan is a medium-sized game bird in the grouse tribe. It is known simply as the ptarmigan in Europe.

lagostrophus fasciatus.name: Banded hare-wallaby
lagostrophus fasciatus.desc: A nocturnal vegetarian that shelters in dense thickets, favouring dune wattle scrub. Natural populations survive only on Bernier and Dorre islands; reintroduced to Dirk Hartog Island.
lagostrophus fasciatus.about: The banded hare-wallaby, mernine, or munning is a marsupial currently found on the islands of Bernier and Dorre off western Australia.

lagothrix lagothricha.name: Brown woolly monkey
lagothrix lagothricha.desc: Mostly eats fruit, switching to leaves and insects when fruit is scarce. It is an effective seed disperser that keeps seeds in its gut for a long time.
lagothrix lagothricha.about: The common woolly monkey, brown woolly monkey, or Humboldt's woolly monkey is a woolly monkey from Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Brazil, and Venezuela.

laguncularia racemosa.name: White mangrove
laguncularia racemosa.desc: White mangrove (Laguncularia racemosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.
laguncularia racemosa.about: Laguncularia is a genus of plants in the family Combretaceae. The only species in the genus is Laguncularia racemosa, the white mangrove.

lake edward and rivers.name: Lake Edward and rivers
lake edward and rivers.desc: The lake and the Rutshuru and other rivers hold the hippos, fish and crocodiles and feed the plankton.

lake ira lalaro wetland.name: Lake Ira Lalaro wetland
lake ira lalaro wetland.desc: The park's large freshwater lake and flood plain; its marshy margins grow grasses and are grazed by village livestock.

lake issyk-kul.name: Lake Issyk-Kul
lake issyk-kul.desc: A huge, deep lake with no outlet. It is slightly salty (about 0.6%), so it rarely freezes even at 1,607 m, and it holds many wintering waterbirds.

lake magadi.name: Lake Magadi
lake magadi.desc: A shallow, seasonal soda lake in the south-west of the crater, fed mainly by the Munge Stream. Its alkaline water grows the algae flamingos eat.

lake michigan & wetlands.name: Lake Michigan & wetlands
lake michigan & wetlands.desc: The park runs along the lake shore, and Wikipedia says extensive wetlands fill many depressions between the dune ridges.

lake superior.name: Lake Superior
lake superior.desc: The cold lake surrounds the island and strongly shapes its lowland temperatures. Sheltered bays and inland lakes hold aquatic plants.

lake urema floods.name: Lake Urema floods
lake urema floods.desc: Seasonal flooding spreads water over the floodplain, from about 10 km2 in dry spells to about 200 km2 in wet years.

lake water.name: Lake water
lake water.desc: Cool, clear freshwater at high altitude with oxygen that is limited by elevation. Reeds and underwater plants grow in its shallows.

lake water and nutrients.name: Lake water and nutrients
lake water and nutrients.desc: A huge, deep, clear freshwater lake. Its nutrients and plankton carry the open-water food chains.

lakes & waterholes.name: Lakes & waterholes
lakes & waterholes.desc: The park holds many lakes and streams, Padam Talao being the largest. In a dry landscape they draw grazers and the crocodiles that live in them.

lakes and clear water.name: Lakes and clear water
lakes and clear water.desc: Rainy, Kabetogama, Namakan and Sand Point lakes make up a large share of the park and hold its fish, algae and loon nesting waters.

lakes and rivers.name: Lakes and rivers
lakes and rivers.desc: Glacial lakes and rivers such as Lake Clark and the Kvichak watershed carry sockeye to spawning grounds and feed lake algae.

lakes, ponds & wetlands.name: Lakes, ponds & wetlands
lakes, ponds & wetlands.desc: Thousands of lakes and ponds and a huge network of streams make water central to life in the park.

lama glama.name: Llama
lama glama.desc: Herded by local communities for wool and meat. Grazing by llamas and alpacas is a conservation concern in the reserve.
lama glama.about: The llama is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era. Llamas are social animals and live with others as a herd.

lama guanicoe.name: Guanaco
lama guanicoe.desc: A wild camelid that grazes grasses, shrubs, herbs and lichens on the steppe. Its natural predators include the puma and the culpeo.
lama guanicoe.about: The guanaco is a camelid native to South America, closely related to the domesticated llama.

lamium amplexicaule.name: Henbit Dead-nettle
lamium amplexicaule.desc: Henbit Dead-nettle (Lamium amplexicaule): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
lamium amplexicaule.about: Lamium amplexicaule, commonly known as henbit dead-nettle, is a species of Lamium native to most of Europe, Asia and northern Africa.

lamium purpureum.name: Red Dead-nettle
lamium purpureum.desc: Red Dead-nettle (Lamium purpureum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
lamium purpureum.about: Lamium purpureum, known as red dead-nettle, purple dead-nettle, or purple archangel, is an annual herbaceous flowering plant in the mint family (Lamiaceae).

lampropeltis calligaster.name: Prairie kingsnake
lampropeltis calligaster.desc: Prairie kingsnake (Lampropeltis calligaster): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

lampropeltis nigra.name: Black Kingsnake
lampropeltis nigra.desc: Black Kingsnake (Lampropeltis nigra): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

lampropeltis triangulum.name: Milk snake
lampropeltis triangulum.desc: Milk snake (Lampropeltis triangulum): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
lampropeltis triangulum.about: The milk snake or milksnake, is a species of kingsnake; there were once up to 24 subspecies recognized, however fewer are officially recognized today.

land-clearing fires.name: Land-clearing fires
land-clearing fires.desc: UNESCO lists regular fires set for farming and grazing around the reserve as a threat. Fire also shapes the grassland.

lanius collaris.name: Southern fiscal
lanius collaris.desc: A shrike that perches in the open and hunts insects and small vertebrates. GloBI records it eating striped mice.
lanius collaris.about: The southern fiscal or fiscal shrike is a member of the shrike family found through most of southern Africa.

lanius collurio.name: Red-backed shrike
lanius collurio.desc: A small predatory songbird that hunts insects, lizards and small birds from perches.
lanius collurio.about: The red-backed shrike is a carnivorous passerine bird and member of the shrike family, Laniidae. Its breeding range stretches from Western Europe east to central Russia.

lanius cristatus.name: Brown shrike
lanius cristatus.desc: A small predatory bird that eats insects and small lizards. GloBI records it eating the brown mabuya skink.
lanius cristatus.about: The brown shrike is a bird in the shrike family that is found mainly in Asia. It is closely related to the red-backed shrike (L. collurio) and isabelline shrike (L. isabellinus).

lanius excubitor.name: Great grey shrike
lanius excubitor.desc: A predatory songbird that takes small rodents, birds and large insects, and impales prey on thorns.
lanius excubitor.about: The great grey shrike is a large and predatory songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae). It forms a superspecies with a number of large, similar-looking parapatric relatives.

lanius ludovicianus.name: Loggerhead shrike
lanius ludovicianus.desc: A songbird that hunts like a hawk, taking lizards, mice, insects and small birds.
lanius ludovicianus.about: The loggerhead shrike is a passerine bird in the family Laniidae. It is the only member of the shrike family endemic to North America; the related northern shrike (L.

lanius nubicus.name: Masked shrike
lanius nubicus.desc: Eats mostly large insects, occasionally small vertebrates, and impales prey on thorns. Breeds on Cyprus.
lanius nubicus.about: The masked shrike is a species of bird in the shrike family, Laniidae.

lanius schach.name: Long-tailed shrike
lanius schach.desc: A predatory songbird that hunts large insects and small vertebrates from perches.
lanius schach.about: The long-tailed shrike or rufous-backed shrike is a member of the bird family Laniidae, the shrikes. They are found widely distributed across Asia and there are variations in plumage across the range.

lantana camara.name: Lantana
lantana camara.desc: A shrub of forest edges and clearings. Monkeys eat its fruit and butterflies visit its flowers.
lantana camara.about: Lantana camara (common lantana) is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family (Verbenaceae), native to the tropics of the Americas.

laphamia megalocephala.name: Laphamia megalocephala
laphamia megalocephala.desc: Laphamia megalocephala (Laphamia megalocephala): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

laportea canadensis.name: Canada Lettuce
laportea canadensis.desc: Canada Lettuce (Laportea canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
laportea canadensis.about: Laportea canadensis, commonly called Canada nettle or wood-nettle, is an annual or perennial herbaceous plant of the nettle family Urticaceae, native to eastern and central North America.

large japanese field mouse.name: Large Japanese field mouse
large japanese field mouse.desc: A forest mouse that feeds mainly on seeds and nuts such as acorns, and is prey for many predators.
large japanese field mouse.about: The large Japanese field mouse is a nocturnal species of rodent in the family Muridae. It is endemic to Japan.

larix decidua.name: European larch
larix decidua.desc: The most common tree of the valley floors in the park, mixed with spruce and Swiss stone pine. It marks the upper forest edge.
larix decidua.about: Larix decidua, the European larch, is a species of larch native to the mountains of central Europe, in the Alps and Carpathian Mountains, with small disjunct lowland populations in northern Poland.

larix gmelinii.name: Dahurian larch
larix gmelinii.desc: A hardy larch of the northern forests, among the most recorded plants around these volcanoes.
larix gmelinii.about: Larix gmelinii, the Dahurian larch or East Siberian larch, is a species of larch native to eastern Siberia and adjacent northeastern Mongolia, northeastern China (Heilongjiang), and the Korean…

larix laricina.name: Tamarack
larix laricina.desc: A deciduous conifer of wet bogs and fens that drops its needles each autumn.
larix laricina.about: Larix laricina, commonly known as the tamarack, hackmatack, eastern larch, black larch, red larch, or American larch, is a species of larch native to Canada, from eastern Yukon and Inuvik, Northwest…

larix occidentalis.name: Hackmatack
larix occidentalis.desc: Hackmatack (Larix occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
larix occidentalis.about: The western larch is a species of larch native to the mountains of western North America (Pacific Northwest, Inland Northwest); in Canada in southeastern British Columbia and southwestern Alberta,…

larix sibirica.name: Siberian larch
larix sibirica.desc: A deciduous conifer that is among the most recorded plants near the site and forms much of the forest belt on the slopes.
larix sibirica.about: Larix sibirica, the Siberian larch or Russian larch, is a frost-hardy tree native to western Russia, from close to the Finnish border east to the Yenisei valley in central Siberia, where it…

larrea tridentata.name: Creosote bush
larrea tridentata.desc: A common evergreen desert shrub of the Chihuahuan Desert flats. Its flowers feed bees, and GloBI records show honey bees and other insects using it.
larrea tridentata.about: Larrea tridentata, also called creosote bush, greasewood as a plant, and chaparral as a medicinal herb. In Sonora, it is more commonly called hediondilla; Spanish hediondo = "smelly".

larus argentatus.name: Herring gull
larus argentatus.desc: A scavenging shore bird that picks up dead fish, including alewife die-offs, from the beach.
larus argentatus.about: The European herring gull or simply herring gull is a large gull, up to 66 cm (26 in) long. It breeds throughout the northern and western coasts of Europe.

larus californicus.name: California Gull
larus californicus.desc: California Gull (Larus californicus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 756 times near the park in GBIF.

larus canus.name: Mew gull
larus canus.desc: Coastal and lakeshore gull that eats voles and scavenges salmon remains.
larus canus.about: The common gull is a medium-sized gull that breeds in cool temperate regions of the Palearctic from Iceland and Scotland east to Kamchatka in the Russian Far East.

larus delawarensis.name: Ring-billed Gull
larus delawarensis.desc: Ring-billed Gull (Larus delawarensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 104 times near the park in GBIF.
larus delawarensis.about: The ring-billed gull is a medium-sized gull native to North America, breeding in Canada and the northern Contiguous United States, and wintering mainly in the United States and northern Mexico.

larus dominicanus.name: Kelp gull
larus dominicanus.desc: An omnivorous gull that scavenges and hunts. Since at least 1996 it has pecked at living right whales off Valdés.
larus dominicanus.about: The kelp gull, also known as the Dominican gull, is a gull that breeds on coasts and islands through much of the Southern Hemisphere. The nominate L. d.

larus fuscus.name: Lesser black-backed gull
larus fuscus.desc: Abundant gull of the flats and shores; it takes crabs and other shore prey and also preys on other waterbirds.
larus fuscus.about: The lesser black-backed gull is a large gull that breeds on the Atlantic and Arctic coasts of Europe. It is migratory, wintering from the British Isles south to West Africa.

larus glaucescens.name: Glaucous-winged gull
larus glaucescens.desc: The most often recorded bird here. Gulls scavenge the remains bears leave from salmon.
larus glaucescens.about: The glaucous-winged gull is a large, white-headed gull. The genus name is from Latin Larus which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.

larus hyperboreus.name: Glaucous gull
larus hyperboreus.desc: Eats eggs, chicks and carrion, often following polar bears and foxes.
larus hyperboreus.about: The glaucous gull is a large gull, the second-largest gull in the world. The genus name is from Latin larus, which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.

larus marinus.name: Great Black-backed Gull
larus marinus.desc: Great Black-backed Gull (Larus marinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 25,148 times near the park in GBIF.
larus marinus.about: The great black-backed gull is the largest member of the gull and tern family Laridae.

larus michahellis.name: Yellow-legged gull
larus michahellis.desc: Opportunistic gull that scavenges. Around the Mediterranean it accounts for about half of the predation on flamingo eggs and chicks.
larus michahellis.about: The yellow-legged gull or western yellow-legged gull is a large gull found in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, which has only recently achieved wide recognition as a distinct species.

larus occidentalis.name: Western gull
larus occidentalis.desc: A gull that breeds on the islands and feeds on fish and scavenged carcasses; GloBI records it eating sea lion and seal.
larus occidentalis.about: The western gull is a large white-headed gull that lives on the west coast of North America and the Pacific Ocean. The western gull ranges from British Columbia, Canada, to Baja California, Mexico.

larus pacificus.name: Pacific gull
larus pacificus.desc: A big gull that eats fish, crabs, cephalopods and other seashore animals, and scavenges scraps. Drops shellfish onto rocks to break them.
larus pacificus.about: The Pacific gull is a gull, native to the coasts of Australia.

larus smithsonianus.name: American herring gull
larus smithsonianus.desc: A generalist that eats shore invertebrates such as mussels, fish, eggs and carrion. It drops shellfish on rocks to crack them.
larus smithsonianus.about: The American herring gull, also known as the Arctic herring gull or Smithsonian gull, is a large gull that breeds in North America, where it is treated by the American Ornithological Society as…

lasioglossum acuminatum.name: Pointed Sweat Bee
lasioglossum acuminatum.desc: Pointed Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum acuminatum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum admirandum.name: Admirable Sweat Bee
lasioglossum admirandum.desc: Admirable Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum admirandum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum cressonii.name: Cresson's Dialictus
lasioglossum cressonii.desc: Cresson's Dialictus (Lasioglossum cressonii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 152 times near the park in GBIF.
lasioglossum cressonii.about: Lasioglossum cressonii (Robertson, 1890) is a species in the sweat bee genus Lasioglossum, family Halictidae.

lasioglossum imitatum.name: Coarse-haired Metallic-Sweat bee
lasioglossum imitatum.desc: Coarse-haired Metallic-Sweat bee (Lasioglossum imitatum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum leucozonium.name: Sweat Bee
lasioglossum leucozonium.desc: Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum leucozonium): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum marinum.name: Lasioglossum marinum
lasioglossum marinum.desc: Lasioglossum marinum (Lasioglossum marinum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 248 times near the park in GBIF.
lasioglossum marinum.about: Lasioglossum marinum is a species of sweat bee in the family Halictidae.

lasioglossum paraforbesii.name: Bald-spot Sweat Bee
lasioglossum paraforbesii.desc: Bald-spot Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum paraforbesii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.

lasioglossum pilosum.name: Hairy Sweat Bee
lasioglossum pilosum.desc: Hairy Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum pilosum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 965 times near the park in GBIF.
lasioglossum pilosum.about: Lasioglossum pilosum is a species of sweat bees in the family Halictidae. The species is a generalist and known to pollinate flowers as well as commercial fruits like apples.

lasioglossum sisymbrii.name: Tansy Mustard Sweat Bee
lasioglossum sisymbrii.desc: Tansy Mustard Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum sisymbrii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 752 times near the park in GBIF.
lasioglossum sisymbrii.about: Lasioglossum sisymbrii is a species of sweat bee in the family Halictidae.

lasioglossum titusi.name: Titus' Lasioglossum
lasioglossum titusi.desc: Titus' Lasioglossum (Lasioglossum titusi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 848 times near the park in GBIF.
lasioglossum titusi.about: Lasioglossum titusi is a species of sweat bee in the family Halictidae. It is a solitary bee that nests in the soil, often in flat, bare ground.

lasioglossum versatum.name: Experienced Sweat Bee
lasioglossum versatum.desc: Experienced Sweat Bee (Lasioglossum versatum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
lasioglossum versatum.about: Lasioglossum versatum is a species of sweat bee in the family Halictidae. A common name is Experienced sweat bee.

lates calcarifer.name: Barramundi
lates calcarifer.desc: Predatory fish of estuaries and rivers that eats smaller fish, crustaceans and molluscs. Mangrove and tidal areas are used for breeding and feeding.
lates calcarifer.about: The barramundi, Asian sea bass, Asian sea lates, giant sea lates, or giant sea perch is a species of catadromous fish in the family Latidae of the order Carangiformes.

lathyrus brachycalyx.name: Bonneville pea
lathyrus brachycalyx.desc: Bonneville pea (Lathyrus brachycalyx): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

lathyrus decaphyllus.name: Prairie vetchling
lathyrus decaphyllus.desc: Prairie vetchling (Lathyrus decaphyllus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

lathyrus eucosmus.name: Semmly vetchling
lathyrus eucosmus.desc: Semmly vetchling (Lathyrus eucosmus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

lathyrus japonicus.name: Sea Pea
lathyrus japonicus.desc: Sea Pea (Lathyrus japonicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
lathyrus japonicus.about: Lathyrus japonicus, the sea pea, beach pea, circumpolar pea or sea vetchling, is a species of flowering plant in the legume family Fabaceae, native to temperate coastal areas of the Northern…

laticauda saintgironsi.name: Yellow-lipped sea krait
laticauda saintgironsi.desc: A sea snake endemic to New Caledonia that hunts mostly eel-like fishes, about half of them lipspot morays.
laticauda saintgironsi.about: The New Caledonian sea krait is a species of venomous snake in the subfamily Laticaudinae of the family Elapidae. The species is native to the waters around New Caledonia.

lava and volcanic soil.name: Lava and volcanic soil
lava and volcanic soil.desc: New flows start as bare rock, and pioneers such as ʻōhiʻa colonise them and slowly build soil.

leaf litter and alluvial soil.name: Leaf litter and alluvial soil
leaf litter and alluvial soil.desc: Forest floor and river deposits where nutrients are recycled for trees and grasses.

leavenworthia stylosa.name: Cedar gladecress
leavenworthia stylosa.desc: Cedar gladecress (Leavenworthia stylosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 133 times near the park in GBIF.

lebia viridis.name: Flower Lebia Beetle
lebia viridis.desc: Flower Lebia Beetle (Lebia viridis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

leersia lenticularis.name: Catchfly grass
leersia lenticularis.desc: Catchfly grass (Leersia lenticularis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

leersia oryzoides.name: Cut-grass
leersia oryzoides.desc: Cut-grass (Leersia oryzoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
leersia oryzoides.about: Leersia oryzoides is a species of grass known by the common name rice cutgrass or just cut-grass.

leitneria floridana.name: Corkwood
leitneria floridana.desc: Corkwood (Leitneria floridana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
leitneria floridana.about: Leitneria floridana (corkwood), the sole species in the genus Leitneria, is a deciduous dioecious shrub or small tree, found only in the southern United States states of Arkansas, Florida, Georgia,…

lemmiscus curtatus.name: Sagebrush vole
lemmiscus curtatus.desc: Sagebrush vole (Lemmiscus curtatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.
lemmiscus curtatus.about: The sagebrush vole is a tiny vole found in western North America. It is the only member of the genus Lemmiscus.

lemmus lemmus.name: Norway lemming
lemmus lemmus.desc: Eats mainly sedges, grasses and moss. Its population booms and crashes every three to four years, which in turn drives its predators.
lemmus lemmus.about: The Norway lemming, also known as the Norwegian lemming, is a common species of lemming found in northern Fennoscandia, where it is the only vertebrate species endemic to the region.

lemmus trimucronatus.name: Brown lemming
lemmus trimucronatus.desc: A tundra rodent that eats sedges and other plants and is a common prey of foxes and stoats.
lemmus trimucronatus.about: The West Siberian lemming or Western Siberian brown lemming is a true lemming species found in the Russian Federation. Like other lemmings, it belongs to the family Cricetidae of rodents.

lemna gibba.name: Fat Duckweed
lemna gibba.desc: Fat Duckweed (Lemna gibba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
lemna gibba.about: Lemna gibba, the gibbous duckweed, swollen duckweed, or fat duckweed, is a species of Lemna (duckweed).

lemna trisulca.name: Ivy-leaved Duckweed
lemna trisulca.desc: Ivy-leaved Duckweed (Lemna trisulca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
lemna trisulca.about: Lemna trisulca L. (syn. Staurogeton trisulcus (L.) Schur; star duckweed; ivy-leaved duckweed) is a species of aquatic plants in the arum family Araceae.

lemna valdiviana.name: Pale Duckweed
lemna valdiviana.desc: Pale Duckweed (Lemna valdiviana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
lemna valdiviana.about: Lemna valdiviana is a species of duckweed known by the common name Valdivia duckweed. It is native to much of the Americas.

lemniscomys striatus.name: Typical striped grass mouse
lemniscomys striatus.desc: A small rodent of grassland, forest edge and secondary forest up to about 1,700 m. GloBI records the rhinoceros viper eating it.
lemniscomys striatus.about: The typical striped grass mouse is a small rodent of the suborder Myomorpha in the family Muridae.

lemur catta.name: Ring-tailed lemur
lemur catta.desc: Opportunistic omnivore eating mainly fruit and leaves. Tamarind can make up a big share of its diet in the dry season.
lemur catta.about: The ring-tailed lemur is a medium- to larger-sized strepsirrhine (wet-nosed) primate and the most internationally recognized lemur species, owing to its long, black-and-white, ringed tail.

leonia glycycarpa.name: Leonia tree
leonia glycycarpa.desc: A rainforest tree whose fruit is recorded in GloBI as food for monkeys and many fruit-eating birds.
leonia glycycarpa.about: Violaceae is a family of flowering plants established in 1802, consisting of about 1000 species in about 25 genera. It takes its name from the genus Viola, the violets and pansies.

leonurus cardiaca.name: Motherwort
leonurus cardiaca.desc: Motherwort (Leonurus cardiaca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
leonurus cardiaca.about: Leonurus cardiaca, known as motherwort, is an herbaceous perennial plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae. Other common names include throw-wort, lion's ear, and lion's tail.

leopardus geoffroyi.name: Geoffroy's cat
leopardus geoffroyi.desc: A small spotted cat. GloBI records it eating guinea pigs and young capybara among other prey.
leopardus geoffroyi.about: Geoffroy's cat is a small wild cat native to the southern and central regions of South America. It is around the size of a domestic cat.

leopardus pardalis.name: Ocelot
leopardus pardalis.desc: A nocturnal hunter of agoutis, birds and small mammals.
leopardus pardalis.about: The ocelot is a medium-sized spotted wild cat that reaches 40–50 cm (16–20 in) at the shoulders and weighs between 7 and 15.5 kg (15 and 34 lb) on average.

leopardus tigrinus.name: Oncilla
leopardus tigrinus.desc: A small forest cat that hunts rodents, lizards, birds, eggs and invertebrates, and climbs well. Listed for El Imposible.
leopardus tigrinus.about: The oncilla, also known as the northern tiger cat, little spotted cat, and tigrillo, is a small spotted cat ranging from Central America to central Brazil.

lepidium davisii.name: Davis' peppercress
lepidium davisii.desc: Davis' peppercress (Lepidium davisii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidium draba.name: Hoary cress
lepidium draba.desc: A crucifer of open ground and field edges; crucifers are among the plants great bustards eat.
lepidium draba.about: Lepidium draba, commonly known as hoary cress, whitetop, whiteweed, or peppergrass, is a perennial plant species in the mustard family, Brassicaceae.

lepidium lasiocarpum.name: Hairy-pod pepperwort
lepidium lasiocarpum.desc: Hairy-pod pepperwort (Lepidium lasiocarpum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

lepidium latifolium.name: Dittander
lepidium latifolium.desc: Dittander (Lepidium latifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
lepidium latifolium.about: Lepidium latifolium, known by several common names including perennial pepperweed, broadleaved pepperweed, pepperwort, peppergrass, dittander, dittany, and tall whitetop, is a perennial plant that is…

lepidium montanum.name: Mountain pepperplant
lepidium montanum.desc: Mountain pepperplant (Lepidium montanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
lepidium montanum.about: Lepidium montanum is a species of flowering plant in the mustard family known by the common names mountain pepperweed, mountain peppergrass, mountain pepperwort, and mountain pepperplant.

lepidium perfoliatum.name: Perfoliate Pepperwort
lepidium perfoliatum.desc: Perfoliate Pepperwort (Lepidium perfoliatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
lepidium perfoliatum.about: Lepidium perfoliatum is a species of flowering plant in the mustard family known by the common names clasping pepperweed and perfoliate pepperwort.

lepidium virginicum.name: Least Pepperwort
lepidium virginicum.desc: Least Pepperwort (Lepidium virginicum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
lepidium virginicum.about: Lepidium virginicum, also known as least pepperwort or Virginia pepperweed, is an herbaceous plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae).

lepidochelys kempii.name: Kemp's ridley turtle
lepidochelys kempii.desc: A small sea turtle that feeds mainly on crabs.
lepidochelys kempii.about: Kemp's ridley sea turtle, also called commonly the Atlantic ridley sea turtle, Kemp's ridley turtle, and Kemp's ridley, is a species of turtle in the family Cheloniidae. L.

lepidoptera.name: Moths
lepidoptera.desc: Night-flying insects whose caterpillars eat desert plants. Wikipedia lists moths first among the prey of Mexican free-tailed bats.
lepidoptera.about: Moths are a group of winged insects of the order Lepidoptera, the other well-known members of which are butterflies; they are characterized by dark or dull patterned wings.

lepomis macrochirus.name: Bluegill & lagoon fish
lepomis macrochirus.desc: Sunfish and other fish stocked in Forest Park's lakes, which the Missouri Department of Conservation helps manage. Bluegill feed largely on small aquatic insects.
lepomis macrochirus.about: The bluegill, sometimes referred to as "bream", "brim", "sunny", or, in Texas, "copper nose", is a species of North American freshwater fish, native to and commonly found in streams, rivers, lakes,…

leptailurus serval.name: Serval
leptailurus serval.desc: A slender cat that hunts rodents, and is recorded in the park among the root-rat predators.
leptailurus serval.about: The serval is a wild small cat native to Africa. It is widespread in sub-Saharan countries, where it inhabits grasslands, wetlands, moorlands and bamboo thickets.

leptecophylla tameiameiae.name: Pūkiawe
leptecophylla tameiameiae.desc: A native shrub of forests, bogs and alpine shrubland. Nēnē and other birds eat its berries and spread the seeds.
leptecophylla tameiameiae.about: Leptecophylla tameiameiae, known as pūkiawe or maiele in the Hawaiian language, is a species of flowering plant that is native to the Hawaiian and Marquesas Islands.

leptinotarsa decemlineata.name: Colorado Beetle
leptinotarsa decemlineata.desc: Colorado Beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
leptinotarsa decemlineata.about: The Colorado potato beetle is a beetle known for being a major pest of potato crops.

leptobrachium montanum.name: Montane large-eyed litter frog
leptobrachium montanum.desc: A frog of the forest floor that eats small invertebrates.
leptobrachium montanum.about: Leptobrachium montanum is a species of frog from the family Megophryidae.

leptonychotes weddellii.name: Weddell seal
leptonychotes weddellii.desc: Dives deep for fish, notably toothfish, and squid. Leopard seals and orcas may take it.
leptonychotes weddellii.about: The Weddell seal is a relatively large and abundant true seal with a circumpolar distribution surrounding Antarctica.

leptonycteris yerbabuenae.name: Lesser long-nosed bat
leptonycteris yerbabuenae.desc: A migratory nectar-feeding bat and the main night pollinator of saguaro and agave flowers.
leptonycteris yerbabuenae.about: The lesser long-nosed bat is a medium-sized bat found in Central and North America.

leptopelis kivuensis.name: Kivu tree frog
leptopelis kivuensis.desc: The most recorded amphibian near the park, a tree frog that feeds on small insects in the forest.
leptopelis kivuensis.about: Leptopelis kivuensis is a species of frog in the family Arthroleptidae.

leptoptilos crumenifer.name: Marabou stork
leptoptilos crumenifer.desc: A big scavenging stork recorded feeding at carcasses of large mammals.
leptoptilos crumenifer.about: The marabou stork is a large wading bird in the stork family Ciconiidae native to sub-Saharan Africa. It breeds in both wet and arid habitats, often near human habitation, especially landfill sites.

leptoptilos dubius.name: Greater adjutant
leptoptilos dubius.desc: A stork that mostly eats carrion and offal but also catches fish and frogs. Kaziranga once held the only known breeding site.
leptoptilos dubius.about: The greater adjutant is a member of the stork family, Ciconiidae. Its genus includes the lesser adjutant of Asia and the marabou stork of Africa.

leptosiphon floribundum.name: Many-flower linanthus
leptosiphon floribundum.desc: Many-flower linanthus (Leptosiphon floribundum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 409 times near the park in GBIF.

leptosiphon parviflorus.name: Leptosiphon parviflorus
leptosiphon parviflorus.desc: Leptosiphon parviflorus (Leptosiphon parviflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
leptosiphon parviflorus.about: Leptosiphon parviflorus is a species of flowering plant in the phlox family known by the common name variable linanthus.

leptosiphon rattanii.name: Rattan's linanthus
leptosiphon rattanii.desc: Rattan's linanthus (Leptosiphon rattanii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
leptosiphon rattanii.about: Leptosiphon rattanii is a rare species of flowering plant in the phlox family known by the common name Rattan's linanthus.

leptotes marina.name: Marine Blue
leptotes marina.desc: Marine Blue (Leptotes marina): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

leptotila verreauxi.name: White-tipped dove
leptotila verreauxi.desc: A ground-feeding dove of forest floor and edges. It is recorded eating the berries of West Indian milkberry.
leptotila verreauxi.about: The white-tipped dove is a large New World tropical dove. Its scientific name commemorates the French naturalists Jules and Edouard Verreaux.

lepus americanus.name: Snowshoe hare
lepus americanus.desc: Snowshoe hare (Lepus americanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
lepus americanus.about: The snowshoe hare, also called the varying hare or snowshoe rabbit, is a species of hare found in North America.

lepus arcticus.name: Arctic hare
lepus arcticus.desc: A large hare of the tundra that browses low plants such as heather and willow.
lepus arcticus.about: The Arctic hare is a species of hare highly adapted to living in the Arctic tundra and other icy biomes.

lepus californicus.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit

lytta magister.desc: Large desert beetle that feeds on plants such as brittlebush, according to GloBI records.
lytta magister.about: Lytta magister, the desert blister beetle or master blister beetle, is a species of blister beetle found in southwestern North America. Typically 16 to 33 mm (0.6 to 1.3 in) in length, L.

macaca arctoides.name: Stump-tailed macaque
macaca arctoides.desc: One of several macaques in the park. An omnivore that eats fruit, seeds and other plant matter, and also takes some small animals.
macaca arctoides.about: The stump-tailed macaque, also called the bear macaque, is a species of macaque native to South Asia and Southeast Asia.

macaca cyclopis.name: Formosan rock macaque
macaca cyclopis.desc: Taiwan's only monkey, living in troops. It eats fruit, young leaves, buds and grass stems, plus insects, snails and bird eggs.
macaca cyclopis.about: The Formosan rock macaque, also known as the Formosan rock monkey or Taiwanese macaque, is a macaque endemic to the island of Taiwan, which has also been introduced to Japan.

macaca fascicularis.name: Long-tailed macaque
macaca fascicularis.desc: A fruit-eating monkey recorded often on the islands, an omnivore that forages for fruit.
macaca fascicularis.about: Macaca fascicularis, variously known by common names such as crab-eating macaque, long-tailed macaque, or cynomolgus monkey, is a macaque species native to Southeast Asia.

macaca fuscata.name: Yakushima macaque
macaca fuscata.desc: A subspecies of the Japanese macaque that eats young leaves, seeds, flowers, fruit and insects, with its diet shifting with season and temperature.
macaca fuscata.about: The Yakushima macaque is a subspecies of Japanese macaque that is indigenous to Yakushima Island (Kagoshima Prefecture). It is also known as the Yaku macaque.

macaca leonina.name: Northern pig-tailed macaque
macaca leonina.desc: One of the most recorded mammals around the park. GloBI records it eating fruit and shrubs such as jambolan and melastome.
macaca leonina.about: The northern pig-tailed macaque is a vulnerable species of macaque in the subfamily Cercopithecidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

macaca mulatta.name: Rhesus macaque
macaca mulatta.desc: The most-recorded monkey in GBIF near the bay. A flexible omnivore that eats fruit and leaves of island forests.
macaca mulatta.about: The rhesus macaque, colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.

macaca nemestrina.name: Southern pig-tailed macaque
macaca nemestrina.desc: A ground and tree foraging monkey that eats fruit. Wikipedia lists it among tiger prey in Sumatra.
macaca nemestrina.about: The southern pig-tailed macaque, also known as the Sundaland pig-tailed macaque and the Sunda pig-tailed macaque, is a medium-sized macaque that lives in Sundaland, southern Thailand, Malaysia, and…

macaca silenus.name: Lion-tailed macaque
macaca silenus.desc: An endangered omnivore of the rainforest canopy that eats fruit, seeds, flowers and insects, and spreads seeds.
macaca silenus.about: The lion-tailed macaque, locally called wanderoo, is an Old World monkey endemic to the Western Ghats of South India.

macaca sinica.name: Toque macaque
macaca sinica.desc: An omnivorous monkey of Sri Lanka that eats fruit, seeds and insects.
macaca sinica.about: The toque macaque is a reddish-brown-coloured Old World monkey endemic to Sri Lanka, where it is known as the riḷawā (Sinhala: රිළවා),.

macaranga.name: Macaranga
macaranga.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree genus of African montane forest; the species here is common in the Kibira area and used for chimpanzee nests.
macaranga.about: Macaranga is a large genus of Old World tropical trees of the family Euphorbiaceae and the only genus in the subtribe Macaranginae (tribe Acalypheae).

macaranga dioica.name: Macaranga
macaranga dioica.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree that colonises gaps in the forest and is often recorded around Santo.
macaranga dioica.about: Macaranga is a large genus of Old World tropical trees of the family Euphorbiaceae and the only genus in the subtribe Macaranginae (tribe Acalypheae).

macaranga tanarius.name: Macaranga
macaranga tanarius.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree of forest gaps. GloBI records show langurs, hornbills and doves eating its fruit.
macaranga tanarius.about: Macaranga tanarius is a species of flowering plant found in South East Asia, Thailand, Papua New Guinea, South China, Taiwan, and eastern Australia.

macaria brunneata.name: Rannoch Looper
macaria brunneata.desc: Rannoch Looper (Macaria brunneata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
macaria brunneata.about: Macaria brunneata, the Rannoch looper, is a moth of the family Geometridae. The species was first described by Carl Peter Thunberg in 1784.

machaeranthera tanacetifolia.name: Takhoka-daisy
machaeranthera tanacetifolia.desc: Takhoka-daisy (Machaeranthera tanacetifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
machaeranthera tanacetifolia.about: Machaeranthera tanacetifolia is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names tansyleaf tansyaster and Tahoka daisy.

maclura pomifera.name: Osage-Orange
maclura pomifera.desc: Osage-Orange (Maclura pomifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
maclura pomifera.about: Maclura pomifera, commonly known as the Osage orange ( OH-sayj), is a small deciduous tree or large shrub, native to the south-central United States. It is a member of the mulberry family, Moraceae.

macoma balthica.name: Baltic tellin
macoma balthica.desc: A small clam that lies buried in the mud and feeds at the surface. Red knots like this bivalve on European mudflats.
macoma balthica.about: Limecola balthica, commonly called the Baltic macoma, Baltic clam or Baltic tellin, is a small saltwater clam, a marine bivalve mollusk in the family Tellinidae (the macomas and tellins).

macrocystis pyrifera.name: Giant kelp
macrocystis pyrifera.desc: Fast-growing brown alga anchored to rock that forms a floating canopy. Many animals depend on it for food or shelter.
macrocystis pyrifera.about: Macrocystis, commonly known as giant kelp, is a monospecific genus of kelp (large brown algae). Previously, several species had been reognized, including M. pyrifera, M. angustifolia, M.

macroglossus minimus.name: Northern blossom bat
macroglossus minimus.desc: A small fruit and nectar bat. GloBI records show it eating fig fruit, and it helps pollinate and spread forest plants.
macroglossus minimus.about: The long-tongued nectar bat, also known as the northern blossom bat, honey nectar bat, least blossom-bat, dagger-toothed long-nosed fruit bat, and lesser long-tongued fruit bat, is a species of…

macrohectopus branickii.name: Pelagic amphipod
macrohectopus branickii.desc: An open-water amphipod, often compared to krill. Golomyanka and Baikal seals eat it.
macrohectopus branickii.about: Macrohectopus branickii is a species of amphipod (a group containing the scuds) living in the pelagic zone of Lake Baikal, believed to be the only species of amphipod in this niche within freshwater.

macronectes giganteus.name: Southern giant petrel
macronectes giganteus.desc: Large seabird that scavenges carcasses of seals and penguins.
macronectes giganteus.about: The southern giant petrel, also known as the Antarctic giant petrel, giant fulmar, stinker, and stinkpot, is a large seabird of the southern oceans.

macrophthalmus.name: Sentinel crabs
macrophthalmus.desc: A genus of soft-bottom crabs living on tidal flats of the Indo-Pacific, hunted by shorebirds that specialise on crabs.
macrophthalmus.about: Macrophthalmus is a genus of crabs which are widespread across the Indo-Pacific.

macropus agilis.name: Agile wallaby
macropus agilis.desc: Grazes mainly at night on grasses and herbs, often near rivers and billabongs. It is the most recorded mammal near the park and a staple prey of crocodiles and dingoes.
macropus agilis.about: The agile wallaby, also known as the sandy wallaby, is a species of wallaby found in northern Australia and southern New Guinea. It is the most common wallaby in north Australia.

macrotermes.name: Termites & fungi
macrotermes.desc: Termites and the fungi that work with them break down dead grass and wood, and their mounds seed new islands.

macrotermes carbonarius.name: Fungus-growing termites
macrotermes carbonarius.desc: Termites that gather dead plant matter and recycle it; a food source for frogs and other small animals.
macrotermes carbonarius.about: Macrotermes is a genus of termites belonging to the subfamily Macrotermitinae and widely distributed throughout Africa and South-East Asia. Well-studied species include Macrotermes natalensis and M.

macrotermes spp..name: Termites
macrotermes spp..desc: Chew dead grass and wood, and their mounds enrich the soil around them.
macrotermes spp..about: Termites are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

macrotus californicus.name: California Leaf-nosed Bat
macrotus californicus.desc: California Leaf-nosed Bat (Macrotus californicus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

madia elegans.name: Elegant Tarweed
madia elegans.desc: Elegant Tarweed (Madia elegans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

madoqua saltiana.name: Salt's dik-dik
madoqua saltiana.desc: A tiny antelope of bushland and thickets in the Horn of Africa. It feeds mainly on leaves and shoots of acacia and other shrubs.
madoqua saltiana.about: Salt's dik-dik is a small antelope found in semidesert, bushland, and thickets in the Horn of Africa, but marginally also in northern Kenya and eastern Sudan.

maesa lanceolata.name: Maesa
maesa lanceolata.desc: A common African shrub or small tree of forest edges and clearings. Its berries are eaten by many forest birds.
maesa lanceolata.about: Maesa lanceolata, or the false assegai, is a tree species that is widespread in the Afrotropics, including Madagascar.

magicicada septendecim.name: Periodical Cicada

magicicada septendecim.about: Magicicada septendecim, sometimes called the Pharaoh cicada or the 17-year locust, is native to Canada and the United States and is the largest and most northern species of periodical cicada with a…

magnolia acuminata.name: Cucumber-tree

magnolia macrophylla.about: Magnolia macrophylla, the bigleaf magnolia, is a deciduous magnolia native to the southeastern United States.

magnolia virginiana.name: Sweetbay

mahonia aquifolium.name: Hollyleaved barberry

mahonia aquifolium.about: Berberis aquifolium, the Oregon grape, holly-leaved barberry, or Mahonia, is a North American species of flowering plant in the family Berberidaceae.

mahonia nervosa.name: Cascade barberry
mahonia nervosa.desc: Cascade barberry (Mahonia nervosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 75 times near the park in GBIF.
mahonia nervosa.about: Berberis nervosa, commonly known as dwarf Oregon-grape, Cascade barberry, Cascade Oregon-grape, or dull Oregon-grape, is a North American flowering plant.

mahonia repens.name: Oregon grape
mahonia repens.desc: Oregon grape (Mahonia repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 105 times near the park in GBIF.

maianthemum canadense.desc: Canada Mayflower (Maianthemum canadense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

maianthemum racemosum.desc: False Solomon's-seal (Maianthemum racemosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 88 times near the park in GBIF.
maianthemum racemosum.about: Maianthemum racemosum, the treacleberry, feathery false lily of the valley, false Solomon's seal, Solomon's plume or false spikenard, is a species of flowering plant native to North America.

maianthemum trifolium.about: Maianthemum trifolium (Three-leaf Solomon's-seal, three-leaf Solomon's-plume, threeleaf false lily of the valley, smilacine trifoliée) is a species of flowering plant that is associated with…

malaclemys terrapin.name: Diamondback terrapin
malaclemys terrapin.desc: A salt-marsh turtle that eats crabs, snails, clams, worms and fish. Raccoons are its main nest predator.
malaclemys terrapin.about: The diamondback terrapin or simply terrapin is a species of terrapin native to the brackish coastal tidal marshes of the East Coast of the United States and the Gulf of Mexico coast, as well as in…

malacosoma americana.name: Eastern Tent Caterpillar
malacosoma americana.desc: Eastern Tent Caterpillar (Malacosoma americana): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
malacosoma americana.about: The eastern tent caterpillar is a species of moth in the family Lasiocampidae, the tent caterpillars or lappet moths. It is univoltine, producing one generation per year.

malacosoma californica.name: Malacosoma californica
malacosoma californica.desc: Malacosoma californica (Malacosoma californica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

malacosoma constricta.name: Pacific Tent Caterpillar
malacosoma constricta.desc: Pacific Tent Caterpillar (Malacosoma constricta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 230 times near the park in GBIF.

malacosoma disstria.name: Forest Tent Caterpillar
malacosoma disstria.desc: Forest Tent Caterpillar (Malacosoma disstria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

malacothamnus fasciculatus.name: Sant Cruz Island bush-mallow
malacothamnus fasciculatus.desc: Sant Cruz Island bush-mallow (Malacothamnus fasciculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 418 times near the park in GBIF.

malayopython reticulatus.name: Reticulated python
malayopython reticulatus.desc: A giant constrictor. Wikipedia lists pythons as potential orangutan predators, and one swallowed a sun bear in Borneo.
malayopython reticulatus.about: The reticulated python is a python species native to South and Southeast Asia. It is the world's longest snake, and the third heaviest after the green anaconda and Burmese python.

malayopython timoriensis.name: Timor python
malayopython timoriensis.desc: A python of the Lesser Sunda islands that preys on rodents and birds. It is a top land predator in this web.
malayopython timoriensis.about: The Timor python is a Malayopython species native to Southeast Asia. It is a dwarf species, and no subspecies are recognized as being valid.

mallomys rothschildi.name: Rothschild's woolly rat
mallomys rothschildi.desc: A giant rodent of New Guinea forests that eats karuka nuts. It is one of the larger rats recorded in the park.
mallomys rothschildi.about: Rothschild's woolly rat is a species of rodent in the family Muridae. It is found on the island of New Guinea: both in the West Papua region of Indonesia and Papua New Guinea.

malosma laurina.name: Malosma
malosma laurina.desc: Malosma (Malosma laurina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 719 times near the park in GBIF.

malus baccata.name: Siberian Crab
malus baccata.desc: Siberian Crab (Malus baccata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

malus fusca.name: Oregon crab apple
malus fusca.desc: Oregon crab apple (Malus fusca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
malus fusca.about: Malus fusca, with the common names Oregon crabapple and Pacific crabapple, is a species of crabapple native to western North America.

malus ioensis.name: Iowa crab apple
malus ioensis.desc: Iowa crab apple (Malus ioensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

malvaviscus arboreus.name: Wax mallow
malvaviscus arboreus.desc: A leafy understory shrub with red flowers and berry-like fruit that birds feed on.
malvaviscus arboreus.about: Malvaviscus arboreus is a species of flowering plant in the hibiscus family, Malvaceae, that is native to the American South, Mexico, Central America, and South America.

mammillaria lasiacantha.name: Lace-spine Nipple Cactus
mammillaria lasiacantha.desc: Lace-spine Nipple Cactus (Mammillaria lasiacantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
mammillaria lasiacantha.about: Mammillaria lasiacantha is a species of cactus in the subfamily Cactoideae, with the common names lacespine nipple cactus, small pincushion cactus, and biznaga de espinas pubescentes (Spanish).

manas river floods.name: Manas River floods
manas river floods.desc: The Manas River and its tributaries spread silt across the plains and keep the early-growth riverside grassland renewed.

mandrillus leucophaeus.name: Drill
mandrillus leucophaeus.desc: An omnivorous monkey that prefers fruit, including figs, and also eats leaves, seeds, mushrooms and invertebrates such as ants.
mandrillus leucophaeus.about: The drill is a primate of the family Cercopithecidae, related to baboons and even more closely to the mandrill. The average wild drill has a lifespan of 20 years.

mandrillus sphinx.name: Mandrill
mandrillus sphinx.desc: A large ground-living monkey of the forest that eats fruit, seeds and invertebrates. Recorded near the park and listed among its primates.
mandrillus sphinx.about: The mandrill is a large Old World monkey native to west central Africa. It is one of the most colorful mammals in the world, with red and blue skin on its face and posterior.

manduca quinquemaculatus.name: Tomato Hornworm
manduca quinquemaculatus.desc: Tomato Hornworm (Manduca quinquemaculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

manilkara.name: Coastal forest trees
manilkara.desc: Trees of the Somali coastal forest. A sapote relative, Manilkara sulcata, is recorded in GBIF data near the reserve.
manilkara.about: Manilkara is a genus of trees in the family Sapotaceae. They are widespread in tropical and semitropical locations, in Africa, Madagascar, Asia, Australia, and Latin America, as well as various…

manilkara zapota.name: Sapodilla (chicozapote)
manilkara zapota.desc: A large native tree of southern Mexico and Central America. Its sweet fruit is eaten widely and its latex is the source of chicle.
manilkara zapota.about: Manilkara zapota, commonly known as sapodilla (Spanish: [ˌsapoˈðiʝa]), sapote, chicozapote, chico, chicoo, chicle, naseberry, nispero, or soapapple, among other names, is an evergreen tree native to…

maniola jurtina.name: Meadow brown
maniola jurtina.desc: A common grassland butterfly whose caterpillars eat grasses; adults and larvae feed birds and frogs.
maniola jurtina.about: The meadow brown is a butterfly found in the Palearctic realm. Its range includes Europe south of 62°N, Russia eastwards to the Urals, Asia Minor, Iraq, Iran, North Africa and the Canary Islands.

many species.name: Desert annuals & grasses
many species.desc: Wildflowers and grasses that sprout after winter and monsoon rains and set seed quickly.
many species.about: An annual plant is a plant that completes its life cycle – from germination to the production of seeds – within one growing season, and then dies.

marah oregana.name: Manroot
marah oregana.desc: Manroot (Marah oregana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 210 times near the park in GBIF.

marantaceae.name: Marantaceae herbs
marantaceae.desc: Broad-leaved herbs that carpet openings in the forest understory and feed gorillas and elephants.
marantaceae.about: The Marantaceae are a family, the arrowroot family, or the prayer plant family, of flowering plants consisting of 28 genera and around 530 species, defining it as one of the most species-rich…

marcgravia rectiflora.name: Lira vine
marcgravia rectiflora.desc: A climbing vine whose fruit and nectar are recorded in the diet of several forest birds.
marcgravia rectiflora.about: Marcgravia is a genus of plants in the family Marcgraviaceae native to the region spanning from Mexico to tropical South America. It is commonly eaten by the dwarf little fruit bat.

margarops fuscatus.name: Pearly-eyed thrasher
margarops fuscatus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore that eats insects, fruit, lizards and frogs, and the eggs and nestlings of other birds. It competes with parrots for nest cavities.
margarops fuscatus.about: The pearly-eyed thrasher is a bird in the thrasher family Mimidae.

marine algae.name: Ocean phytoplankton
marine algae.desc: Microscopic algae at the base of the ocean food web that feeds young salmon.
marine algae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

marisma flooding.name: Marisma flooding
marisma flooding.desc: Seasonal flooding of the Guadalquivir delta marshes makes the shallow lagoons that waterbirds and wintering waterfowl depend on.

marmaronetta angustirostris.name: Marbled duck
marmaronetta angustirostris.desc: A threatened dabbling duck of shallow wetlands. The marshes are reported to hold a large share of the world population.
marmaronetta angustirostris.about: The marbled duck or marbled teal is a medium-sized species of duck from southern Europe, northern Africa, and western and central Asia.

marmota baibacina.name: Gray marmot
marmota baibacina.desc: A burrowing rodent of mountain meadows and steppe that eats grasses and flowering plants. Many predators take it, including wolves, foxes and birds of prey.
marmota baibacina.about: The gray marmot, grey marmot, or Altai marmot is a species of rodent in the squirrel family Sciuridae. It is one of the larger marmots in the genus Marmota.

marmota bobak.name: Bobak marmot
marmota bobak.desc: Burrowing steppe rodent that lives in colonies and feeds on grasses and herbs.
marmota bobak.about: The bobak marmot, also known as the steppe marmot, is a species of marmot that inhabits the steppes of Eastern Europe and Central Asia.

marmota caligata.name: Hoary marmot
marmota caligata.desc: A large ground squirrel of alpine meadows that eats plants and is prey for bears and other carnivores.
marmota caligata.about: The hoary marmot is a species of marmot that inhabits the mountains of northwest North America. Hoary marmots live near the tree line on slopes with grasses and forbs to eat and rocky areas for cover.

marmota camtschatica.name: Black-capped marmot
marmota camtschatica.desc: A burrowing alpine rodent of north-eastern Siberia and Kamchatka that grazes herbs and is prey for bears and foxes.
marmota camtschatica.about: The black-capped marmot is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae.

marmota caudata.name: Long-tailed marmot
marmota caudata.desc: A burrowing herbivore of alpine meadow and steppe that hibernates from about September to spring.
marmota caudata.about: The long-tailed marmot or golden marmot is a marmot species in the family Sciuridae.

marmota flaviventris.name: Yellow-bellied marmot
marmota flaviventris.desc: A burrowing rodent of rocky meadows that eats green plants and hibernates through the long snow season.
marmota flaviventris.about: The yellow-bellied marmot, also known as the rock chuck, is a large, stout-bodied ground squirrel in the marmot genus.

marmota himalayana.name: Himalayan marmot
marmota himalayana.desc: Colonial burrowing grazer of alpine grassland. Snow leopards, wolves, red foxes and golden eagles hunt it.
marmota himalayana.about: The Himalayan marmot is a marmot species that inhabits alpine grasslands throughout the Himalayas and on the Tibetan Plateau.

marmota marmota.name: Alpine marmot
marmota marmota.desc: Colonial burrower that grazes meadows through summer, fattens up, then hibernates for months. Sentinels whistle when predators approach.
marmota marmota.about: The alpine marmot is a large ground-dwelling squirrel, from the genus of marmots.

marmota monax.name: Groundhog
marmota monax.desc: Groundhog (Marmota monax): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
marmota monax.about: The groundhog, also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.

marsh mud & nutrients.name: Marsh mud & nutrients
marsh mud & nutrients.desc: Tidal sediment holds the nutrients that marsh plants draw on.

marshes and fishponds.name: Marshes and fishponds
marshes and fishponds.desc: Marshes and artificial fishponds, first dug in 1914-1918 and again in the 1950s, add reed beds and open water to the grassland.

martes americana.name: American marten
martes americana.desc: Slender forest carnivore. GloBI records show it eating red squirrels and snowshoe hares.
martes americana.about: The American marten, also known as the American pine marten, is a species of North American mammal, a member of the family Mustelidae. The species is sometimes referred to as simply the pine marten.

martes caurina.name: Pacific marten
martes caurina.desc: A forest predator that favours deep-snow country and hunts rodents and birds.
