martes caurina.about: The Pacific marten is a species of North American mammal, a member of the family Mustelidae. It is found throughout western North America.

martes flavigula.name: Yellow-throated marten
martes flavigula.desc: An agile omnivorous marten that hunts small animals and may take panda cubs.
martes flavigula.about: The yellow-throated marten is a marten species native to the Himalayas, Southeast and East Asia.

martes foina.name: Beech marten
martes foina.desc: An agile omnivorous hunter that takes small mammals, birds and fruit. The nearby pine marten is also on the park list.
martes foina.about: The beech marten, also known as the stone marten, house marten or white breasted marten, is a species of marten native to much of Europe and Central Asia, though it has established a feral population…

martes martes.name: European pine marten
martes martes.desc: Agile forest hunter that eats rodents and birds and also fruit such as rowan berries and bilberries.
martes martes.about: The European pine marten, also known as the pine marten, is a mustelid native to and widespread in most of Europe, Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria.

martes zibellina.name: Sable
martes zibellina.desc: A forest-dwelling marten of the taiga. It can take seal pups that leave their ice dens.
martes zibellina.about: The sable is a species of marten, a small omnivorous mammal primarily inhabiting the forest environments of Russia, from the Ural Mountains throughout Siberia, and northern Mongolia.

matteuccia struthiopteris.name: Ostrich Fern
matteuccia struthiopteris.desc: Ostrich Fern (Matteuccia struthiopteris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

mauritia flexuosa.name: Buriti palm
mauritia flexuosa.desc: A palm of wet ground that Wikipedia says tapirs, peccaries, fish and monkeys depend on for its fruit. It marks the vereda wetlands.
mauritia flexuosa.about: Mauritia flexuosa, known as the moriche palm, ité palm, ita, buriti, muriti, miriti (Brazil), canangucho (Colombia), morete or acho (Ecuador), palma real (Bolivia), or aguaje (Peru), is a palm tree.

mayflies, caddisflies and midges.name: Aquatic insect larvae
mayflies, caddisflies and midges.desc: Larvae living in mud and on wood. They feed on algae and detritus and are a main food for freshwater drum.
mayflies, caddisflies and midges.about: Aquatic insects or water insects live some portion of their life cycle in the water. They feed in the same ways as other insects.

mayflies, stoneflies, caddisflies.name: Stream insects
mayflies, stoneflies, caddisflies.desc: Larvae in cold streams feed on leaf litter and algae, and in turn feed trout and stream salamanders.
mayflies, stoneflies, caddisflies.about: The caddisflies (order Trichoptera) are a group of insects with aquatic larvae and terrestrial adults.

maylandia.name: Mbuna
maylandia.desc: Colourful, mostly endemic rock-dwelling cichlids, often specialised feeders on algae growing on rocks.
maylandia.about: Mbuna (pronounced boo-nuh (the "m" is silent), though some pronounce it umm-boo-nuh ) is the common name for a large group of African cichlids from Lake Malawi, and are members of the haplochromine…

mazama americana.name: Red brocket
mazama americana.desc: A forest deer recorded near the park that browses leaves and eats fruit and fungi; prey for jaguars.
mazama americana.about: The red brocket is a species of brocket deer from forests in South America, ranging from northern Argentina to Colombia and the Guianas. It also occurs on the Caribbean island of Trinidad.

mazama gouazoubira.name: Gray brocket
mazama gouazoubira.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and fruit; reported as a viable population in the park.
mazama gouazoubira.about: The gray brocket, also known as the brown brocket, is a species of brocket deer from northern Argentina, Bolivia, southern Peru, eastern and southern Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

mazama temama.name: Central American red brocket
mazama temama.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and picks up fallen fruit. It is a prey animal of the big cats.
mazama temama.about: The Central American or Mexican red brocket, as it is sometimes called, is a species of brocket deer native to Mexico, Central America, and northern Colombia.

meandering rivers.name: Meandering rivers
meandering rivers.desc: Rivers and oxbow lakes carry fish and keep shifting the floodplain forest.

medeola virginiana.name: Indian Cucumber
medeola virginiana.desc: Indian Cucumber (Medeola virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
medeola virginiana.about: Medeola virginiana, known as Indian cucumber, cucumber root, or Indian cucumber-root, is an eastern North American plant species in the lily family, Liliaceae.

medicago lupulina.name: Black Medick
medicago lupulina.desc: Black Medick (Medicago lupulina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

medicago sativa.name: Alfalfa
medicago sativa.desc: Alfalfa (Medicago sativa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile gemula.name: Tan-cheeked Leafcutter
megachile gemula.desc: Tan-cheeked Leafcutter (Megachile gemula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile inermis.name: Unarmed Leafcutter
megachile inermis.desc: Unarmed Leafcutter (Megachile inermis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.
megachile inermis.about: Megachile inermis is a species of bee in the family Megachilidae. It was described by Provancher in 1888.

megachile latimanus.name: Leafcutting bee
megachile latimanus.desc: Leafcutting bee (Megachile latimanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 39 times near the park in GBIF.
megachile latimanus.about: Megachile latimanus, or the broad-handed leafcutter, is a species of bee in the family Megachilidae. It was described by Thomas Say in 1823.

megachile mendica.name: Flat-tailed Leaf-cutter Bee
megachile mendica.desc: Flat-tailed Leaf-cutter Bee (Megachile mendica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
megachile mendica.about: Megachile mendica, the flat-tailed leafcutter bee, is a species of solitary bee in the family Megachilidae. It was described by Ezra Townsend Cresson in 1878.

megachile parallela.name: Parallel Leaf-cutter Bee
megachile parallela.desc: Parallel Leaf-cutter Bee (Megachile parallela): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

megachile relativa.name: Golden-tailed Leafcutter Bee
megachile relativa.desc: Golden-tailed Leafcutter Bee (Megachile relativa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 41 times near the park in GBIF.
megachile relativa.about: Megachile relativa is a species of bee in the family Megachilidae. It was described by Ezra Townsend Cresson in 1878.

megachile xylocopoides.name: Carpenter-mimic Leaf-cutter Bee
megachile xylocopoides.desc: Carpenter-mimic Leaf-cutter Bee (Megachile xylocopoides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

megacyllene robiniae.name: Locust Borer
megacyllene robiniae.desc: Locust Borer (Megacyllene robiniae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 69 times near the park in GBIF.
megacyllene robiniae.about: Megacyllene robiniae, commonly known as the locust borer, is a species of longhorn beetle endemic to eastern North America.

megalopyge crispata.name: Black-waved Flannel Moth
megalopyge crispata.desc: Black-waved Flannel Moth (Megalopyge crispata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.
megalopyge crispata.about: Megalopyge crispata, the black-waved flannel moth, crinkled flannel moth or white flannel moth, is a moth of the Megalopygidae family.

megapodius reinwardt.name: Orange-footed scrubfowl
megapodius reinwardt.desc: A megapode that eats seeds, fallen fruit and invertebrates, incubating eggs in mounds of rotting leaf litter.
megapodius reinwardt.about: The orange-footed scrubfowl, also known as orange-footed megapode or just scrubfowl, is a small megapode of the family Megapodiidae native to many islands in the Lesser Sunda Islands as well as…

megaptera novaeangliae.name: Humpback whale
megaptera novaeangliae.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. It feeds on krill and small schooling fish in the bay in summer.
megaptera novaeangliae.about: The humpback whale is a species of baleen whale. It is a rorqual (a member of the family Balaenopteridae) and is the only species in the genus Megaptera.

megascolecidae.name: Earthworms
megascolecidae.desc: Soil animals that eat leaf litter and mix it into the soil. They are the food of the long-beaked echidna.
megascolecidae.about: An earthworm is a soil-dwelling terrestrial invertebrate that belongs to the phylum Annelida.

megastigmus albifrons.name: Megastigmus albifrons
megastigmus albifrons.desc: Megastigmus albifrons (Megastigmus albifrons): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

megatibicen dorsatus.name: Bush Cicada
megatibicen dorsatus.desc: Bush Cicada (Megatibicen dorsatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

mekong sediment and nutrients.name: Mekong sediment and nutrients
mekong sediment and nutrients.desc: Floodwater from the Mekong carries silt and nutrients into the lake; sediment-bound phosphorus helps feed its algae.

melaleuca viridiflora.name: Paperbark
melaleuca viridiflora.desc: A paperbark tree of wet lowlands and floodplain edges. Its flowers are visited by honeyeaters.
melaleuca viridiflora.about: Melaleuca viridiflora, commonly known as broad-leaved paperbark, is a plant in the myrtle family Myrtaceae, and is native to woodlands, swamps and streams in monsoonal areas of northern Australia and…

melampodium leucanthum.name: Plains blackfoot
melampodium leucanthum.desc: Plains blackfoot (Melampodium leucanthum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 81 times near the park in GBIF.
melampodium leucanthum.about: Melampodium leucanthum, the plains blackfoot or blackfoot daisy, is an herbaceous perennial plant in the family Asteraceae found on rocky slopes in the southwest U.S.

melanerpes carolinus.name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
melanerpes carolinus.desc: Red-bellied Woodpecker (Melanerpes carolinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.
melanerpes carolinus.about: The red-bellied woodpecker is a medium-sized woodpecker of the family Picidae. It breeds mainly in the eastern United States, ranging as far south as Florida and as far north as Canada.

melanerpes erythrocephalus.name: Red-headed Woodpecker
melanerpes erythrocephalus.desc: Red-headed Woodpecker (Melanerpes erythrocephalus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
melanerpes erythrocephalus.about: The red-headed woodpecker is a mid-sized woodpecker found in temperate North America. Its breeding habitat is open country across southern Canada and the east-central United States.

melanerpes formicivorus.name: Acorn woodpecker
melanerpes formicivorus.desc: In California acorns make up half or more of its diet, which it stores in drilled granary trees, also eating sap and insects. One of the best-recorded birds near the park.
melanerpes formicivorus.about: The acorn woodpecker is a medium-sized woodpecker with a length of around 20 cm (8 in), and an average weight of 85 g (3.0 oz).

melanerpes portoricensis.name: Puerto Rican woodpecker
melanerpes portoricensis.desc: An endemic woodpecker. GloBI records it eating fruit and the lizard Anolis krugi.
melanerpes portoricensis.about: The Puerto Rican woodpecker is the only woodpecker endemic to the archipelago of Puerto Rico and is one of the five species of the genus Melanerpes that occur in the Antilles.

melanerpes uropygialis.name: Gila woodpecker
melanerpes uropygialis.desc: Digs a new nest hole in saguaros each season; abandoned holes shelter elf owls, flycatchers and other birds.
melanerpes uropygialis.about: The Gila woodpecker is a medium-sized woodpecker of the desert regions of the southwestern United States and western Mexico.

melanoplus bivittatus.name: Two-striped grasshopper
melanoplus bivittatus.desc: Two-striped Grasshopper (Melanoplus bivittatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
melanoplus bivittatus.about: Melanoplus bivittatus, the two-striped grasshopper, is a species of grasshopper belonging to the family Acrididae.

melanoplus borealis.name: Northern grasshopper
melanoplus borealis.desc: Chews grasses and wildflowers in summer and feeds birds, mice and other small predators.
melanoplus borealis.about: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.

melanoplus differentialis.name: Differential Grasshopper
melanoplus differentialis.desc: Differential Grasshopper (Melanoplus differentialis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
melanoplus differentialis.about: The differential grasshopper is a species of grasshopper belonging to the genus Melanoplus. It is found throughout northern Mexico, the central United States and southern Ontario, Canada.

melanoplus femurrubrum.name: Red-legged Grasshopper
melanoplus femurrubrum.desc: Red-legged Grasshopper (Melanoplus femurrubrum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
melanoplus femurrubrum.about: Melanoplus femurrubrum, the red-legged grasshopper, is a species of grasshopper belonging to the genus Melanoplus.

melanoplus sanguinipes.name: Migratory Grasshopper
melanoplus sanguinipes.desc: Migratory Grasshopper (Melanoplus sanguinipes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
melanoplus sanguinipes.about: Melanoplus sanguinipes, known generally as migratory grasshopper, is a species of spur-throated grasshopper in the family Acrididae.

melanosuchus niger.name: Black caiman
melanosuchus niger.desc: The largest predator in the flooded forest, eating fish, capybaras and anything else it can ambush.
melanosuchus niger.about: The black caiman is a crocodilian reptile endemic to South America.

melanotaenia.name: Rainbowfish
melanotaenia.desc: Small schooling fish of creeks and billabongs, part of the park's rich freshwater fish fauna. They graze algae and small insects and feed larger fish.
melanotaenia.about: Melanotaenia is a genus of rainbowfish from Australia, Indonesia (West Papua), New Guinea, and nearby smaller islands. As presently recognized, this genus is probably not monophyletic.

melanthera nivea.name: Snow Squarestem
melanthera nivea.desc: Snow Squarestem (Melanthera nivea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
melanthera nivea.about: Melanthera nivea, also known as pineland squarestem, snow squarestem and Spanish: yerba de cabra, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It grows in the Americas.

melanthium woodii.name: Wood's bunchflower
melanthium woodii.desc: Wood's bunchflower (Melanthium woodii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

melastoma malabathricum.name: Malabar melastome
melastoma malabathricum.desc: A shrub of open and disturbed ground. GloBI records elephants and macaques eating it.
melastoma malabathricum.about: Melastoma malabathricum, known also as Malabar melastome, Indian rhododendron, Singapore rhododendron, planter's rhododendron and senduduk, is a flowering plant in the family Melastomataceae native…

meleagris gallopavo.name: Wild Turkey
meleagris gallopavo.desc: Leans on hard mast such as acorns in fall and winter and on insects in summer. Poults depend almost entirely on insects for their first month.
meleagris gallopavo.about: The wild turkey is an upland game bird native to North America, one of two extant species of turkey and the heaviest member of the order Galliformes. It is the ancestor to the domestic turkey (M. g.

meleagris ocellata.name: Ocellated turkey
meleagris ocellata.desc: Found only on the Yucatan Peninsula. It eats insects, seeds, nuts and leaves, and roosts in trees to avoid jaguars.
meleagris ocellata.about: The ocellated turkey is a species of turkey residing primarily in the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico, as well as in parts of Belize and Guatemala.

meles meles.name: European badger
meles meles.desc: An omnivore that eats earthworms, small mammals, amphibians and fruit. Recorded in the area.
meles meles.about: The European badger, also known as the Eurasian badger, is a species of badger in the family Mustelidae native to Europe and West Asia and parts of Central Asia.

melicope elleryana.name: Pink-flowered doughwood
melicope elleryana.desc: The favoured food plant of the Ulysses butterfly caterpillar.
melicope elleryana.about: Melicope elleryana, commonly known as pink flowered doughwood, pink evodia, corkwood, or saruwa, is a species of rainforest shrub or tree in the family Rutaceae, and is native to New Guinea, parts of…

melilotus albus.name: White Melilot
melilotus albus.desc: White Melilot (Melilotus albus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

melilotus officinalis.name: Ribbed Melilot
melilotus officinalis.desc: Yellow sweetclover (Melilotus officinalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 46 times near the park in GBIF.
melilotus officinalis.about: Melilotus officinalis, known as sweet yellow clover, yellow melilot, ribbed melilot and common melilot, is a species of legume native to Eurasia and introduced in North America, Africa, and Australia.

melissodes agilis.name: Agile Long-horned Bee
melissodes agilis.desc: Agile Long-horned Bee (Melissodes agilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
melissodes agilis.about: Melissodes agilis, the agile long-horned bee, is a species of long-horned bee in the family Apidae. It is found in Central America and North America.

melissodes bimaculatus.name: Two-spotted Longhorn
melissodes bimaculatus.desc: Two-spotted Longhorn (Melissodes bimaculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 145 times near the park in GBIF.
melissodes bimaculatus.about: Melissodes bimaculatus, the two-spotted longhorn, is a species of long-horned bee in the family Apidae.

melissodes trinodis.name: Dark-veined Long-horned Bee
melissodes trinodis.desc: Dark-veined Long-horned Bee (Melissodes trinodis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

melithreptus albogularis.name: White-throated honeyeater
melithreptus albogularis.desc: Small bird of savanna woodland and paperbarks that feeds on nectar and insects.
melithreptus albogularis.about: The white-throated honeyeater is a bird of the honeyeater family Meliphagidae native to New Guinea and eastern and northern Australia.

melitta melittoides.name: Lyonia Blunt-horn
melitta melittoides.desc: Lyonia Blunt-horn (Melitta melittoides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

melosira arctica.name: Ice algae
melosira arctica.desc: Algae growing on the underside of sea ice that start the spring bloom.

melospiza melodia.name: Song Sparrow
melospiza melodia.desc: Song Sparrow (Melospiza melodia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 58 times near the park in GBIF.
melospiza melodia.about: The song sparrow is a medium-sized New World sparrow. Among the native sparrows in North America, it is easily one of the most abundant, variable, and adaptable species.

melozone aberti.name: Abert's Towhee
melozone aberti.desc: Abert's Towhee (Melozone aberti): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 155 times near the park in GBIF.
melozone aberti.about: Abert's towhee is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to a small range in southwestern North America, generally the lower Colorado River and Gila River watersheds, nearly endemic to Arizona,…

melozone crissalis.name: California Towhee
melozone crissalis.desc: California Towhee (Melozone crissalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 77 times near the park in GBIF.
melozone crissalis.about: The California towhee is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to the coastal regions of western Oregon and California in the United States and Baja California and Baja California Sur in Mexico.

meltwater and rivers.name: Meltwater and rivers
meltwater and rivers.desc: Snow and glacier melt feeds the lakes, mires and the river delta that wets the valleys and lowlands of the site.

melursus ursinus.name: Sloth bear
melursus ursinus.desc: Eats termites and ants, plus fruit and honey. Chitwan is said to hold a high density of them. Tigers are its main predator.
melursus ursinus.about: The sloth bear, also known as the Indian bear, is a myrmecophagous bear species native to the Indian subcontinent. It feeds on fruits, ants and termites.

mentzelia laevicaulis.name: Blazingstar mentzelia
mentzelia laevicaulis.desc: Blazingstar mentzelia (Mentzelia laevicaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 136 times near the park in GBIF.
mentzelia laevicaulis.about: Mentzelia laevicaulis is a showy biennial or short-lived perennial wildflower native to western North America. Its common names include giant blazingstar and smoothstem blazingstar.

mentzelia nuda.name: Bractless blazingstar
mentzelia nuda.desc: Bractless blazingstar (Mentzelia nuda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
mentzelia nuda.about: Mentzelia nuda, the bractless blazingstar, is a species of flowering plant in the family Loasaceae.

mephitis macroura.name: Hooded skunk
mephitis macroura.desc: Hooded skunk (Mephitis macroura): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

mephitis mephitis.name: Striped skunk
mephitis mephitis.desc: Striped skunk (Mephitis mephitis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
mephitis mephitis.about: The striped skunk is a skunk of the genus Mephitis that occurs across much of North America, including southern Canada, the United States, and northern Mexico.

mercenaria mercenaria.name: Northern quahog
mercenaria mercenaria.desc: A hard clam buried in bay sediments that filters plankton from the water. Long harvested in Rhode Island.
mercenaria mercenaria.about: The hard clam, also known as the round clam, hard-shell (or hard-shelled) clam, or the quahog, is an edible marine bivalve mollusk that is native to the eastern shores of North America and Central…

mergus merganser.name: Common Merganser
mergus merganser.desc: Common Merganser (Mergus merganser): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

meriones tristrami.name: Tristram's jird
meriones tristrami.desc: A burrowing rodent that eats seeds and leaves. One of the most-recorded mammals in the area, and small prey for many predators.
meriones tristrami.about: Tristram's jird is a species of rodent that lives in the Middle East. It is named after the Reverend Henry Baker Tristram who collected the first specimens.

merops bulocki.name: Red-throated bee-eater
merops bulocki.desc: A very commonly recorded insect-hunting bird that catches prey in flight near riverbanks.
merops bulocki.about: The red-throated bee-eater is a species of bird in the family Meropidae. This species is native to the Sudan (region).

merops ornatus.name: Rainbow bee-eater
merops ornatus.desc: A bird that catches flying insects in the air, including dragonflies, and was recorded often around the park.
merops ornatus.about: The rainbow bee-eater is a bird species in the bee-eater family Meropidae.

merops pusillus.name: Little bee-eater
merops pusillus.desc: A small bird that catches flying insects on the wing; recorded in GBIF data near the reserve.
merops pusillus.about: The little bee-eater is a bird species in the bee-eater family, Meropidae. They are found in Sub-Saharan Africa.

merops viridis.name: Blue-throated bee-eater
merops viridis.desc: A bird that catches flying insects in the air. GloBI records it eating the giant honey bee near the park.
merops viridis.about: The blue-throated bee-eater is a species of bird in the bee-eater family. It is found in much of southeast Asia, in subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.

mertensia franciscana.name: Franciscan bluebells
mertensia franciscana.desc: Franciscan bluebells (Mertensia franciscana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

mertensia lanceolata.name: Prairie bluebells
mertensia lanceolata.desc: Prairie bluebells (Mertensia lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.

mertensia macdougalii.name: Macdougal's bluebells
mertensia macdougalii.desc: Macdougal's bluebells (Mertensia macdougalii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

mertensia virginica.name: Virginia bluebells
mertensia virginica.desc: Virginia bluebells (Mertensia virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
mertensia virginica.about: Mertensia virginica is a spring ephemeral plant in the Boraginaceae (borage) family with bell-shaped sky-blue flowers, native to eastern North America.

mesa soils.name: Mesa soils
mesa soils.desc: Thin, well-drained soils on the mesa tops hold the roots of the woodland and recycle nutrients from dead matter.

mesalina brevirostris.name: Blanford's short-nosed desert lizard
mesalina brevirostris.desc: A small desert lizard recorded in the area. It feeds on small invertebrates and is prey for wheatears, shrikes and monitors.
mesalina brevirostris.about: Mesalina brevirostris, also known as Blanford's short-nosed desert lizard, is a species of sand-dwelling lizard in the family Lacertidae.

mesocentrotus franciscanus.name: Red sea urchin
mesocentrotus franciscanus.desc: Grazes kelp. Without sea otters, which were hunted out in the fur trade, urchins can multiply and threaten kelp forests.
mesocentrotus franciscanus.about: The red sea urchin is a sea urchin found in the northeastern Pacific Ocean from Alaska to Baja California.

metopium brownei.name: Black poisonwood
metopium brownei.desc: A common Yucatan tree with oily fruits that birds such as toucans and parrots are recorded eating.
metopium brownei.about: Metopium brownei is a species of plant in the family Anacardiaceae.

metrosideros polymorpha.name: ʻŌhiʻa lehua
metrosideros polymorpha.desc: A native tree whose flowers give nectar to honeycreepers. It grows in many Hawaiian forests and is a foundation of the native forest.
metrosideros polymorpha.about: Metrosideros polymorpha, the ʻōhiʻa lehua, is a species of flowering evergreen tree in the myrtle family, Myrtaceae, that is endemic to the six largest islands of Hawaiʻi.

metrosideros umbellata.name: Southern rata
metrosideros umbellata.desc: A flowering tree of the southern forests. Possums are recorded eating its foliage.
metrosideros umbellata.about: Metrosideros umbellata, commonly known as southern rātā, is an evergreen tree in the family Myrtaceae.

metroxylon sagu.name: Sago palm
metroxylon sagu.desc: A palm of lowland swamp forests in New Guinea. Its trunk starch is a staple food for people along rivers such as the Sepik, and each stem flowers once and then dies while suckers carry on.
metroxylon sagu.about: Metroxylon sagu, the true sago palm, is a species of palm in the genus Metroxylon, native to tropical southeastern Asia. The tree is a major source of sago starch.

miconia.name: Miconia shrubs
miconia.desc: Small-fruited melastome plants that are common in the forest understory. GloBI records show many bats, birds and mammals feeding on their fruit.
miconia.about: Miconia is a genus of flowering plants in the glory bush family, Melastomataceae, native to warm temperate to tropical regions of the Americas.

miconia ciliata.name: Miconia
miconia ciliata.desc: A small tree or shrub of the melastome family with berries that many forest birds eat.
miconia ciliata.about: Miconia is a genus of flowering plants in the glory bush family, Melastomataceae, native to warm temperate to tropical regions of the Americas.

micranthes marshallii.name: Marshall's saxifrage
micranthes marshallii.desc: Marshall's saxifrage (Micranthes marshallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

micranthes virginiensis.name: Virginia saxifrage
micranthes virginiensis.desc: Virginia saxifrage (Micranthes virginiensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

microbes and fungi.name: Decomposers
microbes and fungi.desc: Microbes and fungi break down dead plants, droppings and carcasses slowly in the cold and return nutrients to the soil.

microcarbo pygmaeus.name: Pygmy cormorant
microcarbo pygmaeus.desc: A fish-eating bird nesting in reeds and willows. The delta holds the largest colony of the species.
microcarbo pygmaeus.about: The pygmy cormorant is a member of the Phalacrocoracidae (cormorant) family of seabirds. It breeds in south-eastern Europe and south-western Asia.

microcoleus.name: Biological soil crust
microcoleus.desc: A living skin of cyanobacteria, lichens, mosses, algae and microfungi. It binds sand grains against erosion, soaks up scarce rain and fixes nitrogen, but is easily broken by footsteps.
microcoleus.about: Biological soil crusts, often abbreviated as biocrusts, are communities of living organisms inhabiting the surface of soils in arid and semi-arid ecosystems, which form stable aggregates of soil…

microphytobenthos.name: Mud-surface diatoms
microphytobenthos.desc: Microscopic algae living in the top millimetres of tidal mud. They feed many deposit-feeding animals when the flats are exposed.

micropogonias undulatus.name: Atlantic croaker
micropogonias undulatus.desc: Hunts worms, small crustaceans and other bottom prey.
micropogonias undulatus.about: The Atlantic croaker is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Sciaenidae and is closely related to the black drum, the silver perch, the spot croaker, the red drum, the spotted…

micropotamogale lamottei.name: Nimba otter shrew
micropotamogale lamottei.desc: A small nocturnal semi-aquatic insectivore living along creeks in the Nimba area. Mining runoff threatens its streams.
micropotamogale lamottei.about: The Nimba otter shrew is a dwarf otter shrew and belongs to the mammal family Potamogalidae. Otter shrews are shrew-like afrotherian mammals found in sub-Saharan Africa.

micropterus dolomieu.name: Smallmouth bass
micropterus dolomieu.desc: Cool, clear Ozark streams with rock or gravel bottoms. Eats minnows, crayfish and large aquatic insects, and its eggs and fry are eaten by sunfish.
micropterus dolomieu.about: The smallmouth bass is a species of freshwater fish in the sunfish family (Centrarchidae) of the order Centrarchiformes.

micropterus salmoides.name: Largemouth bass
micropterus salmoides.desc: A fish predator of sloughs and canals that eats small fish and crayfish.
micropterus salmoides.about: The largemouth bass is a carnivorous, freshwater, ray-finned fish in the Centrarchidae (sunfish) family, native to the eastern and central United States, southeastern Canada and northern Mexico.

microscopic algae.name: Phytoplankton
microscopic algae.desc: Drifting microscopic algae that feed filter feeders such as mussels. General ecological knowledge.
microscopic algae.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

microscopic animals.name: Zooplankton
microscopic animals.desc: Tiny drifting animals that graze algae and are eaten by fish larvae and small fish.
microscopic animals.about: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive.

microtus agrestis.name: Field vole
microtus agrestis.desc: Small grass-eating rodent of damp meadows and a staple prey for foxes, buzzards and cranes.
microtus agrestis.about: The short-tailed field vole, short-tailed vole, or simply field vole, is a grey-brown vole, around 10 cm in length, with a short tail.

microtus arvalis.name: Common vole
microtus arvalis.desc: A small grass-eating rodent of open ground, the staple prey of many small predators.
microtus arvalis.about: The common vole is a European rodent.

microtus californicus.name: California vole
microtus californicus.desc: California vole (Microtus californicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.

microtus chrotorrhinus.name: Rock vole
microtus chrotorrhinus.desc: Rock vole (Microtus chrotorrhinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
microtus chrotorrhinus.about: The rock vole, also known as the yellow-nosed vole, is a medium-sized species of vole found in eastern North America.

microtus gregalis.name: Narrow-headed vole
microtus gregalis.desc: A small grass-eating vole of steppe and meadow; foxes, stoats, eagles and bears are recorded eating it in GloBI.
microtus gregalis.about: The narrow-headed vole is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae.

microtus ilaeus.name: Kazakhstan vole
microtus ilaeus.desc: Small grass-eating rodent of Tian Shan meadows, and a food source for many predators.
microtus ilaeus.about: Voles are small rodents that are relatives of lemmings and hamsters, but with a stouter body; a longer, hairy tail; a slightly rounder head; smaller eyes and ears; and differently formed molars…

microtus longicaudus.name: Long-tailed vole
microtus longicaudus.desc: A small plant-eating rodent of meadows and shrubby ground, recorded often in the area. Food for bears and other predators.
microtus longicaudus.about: The long-tailed vole, in some areas known as the San Bernardino long-tailed vole, is a small vole found in western North America. They have short ears and a long tail.

microtus montanus.name: Montane vole
microtus montanus.desc: A small grass-eating rodent and a staple for foxes, coyotes, hawks and eagles.
microtus montanus.about: The montane vole is a species of vole native to the western United States and Canada.

microtus ochrogaster.name: Prairie vole
microtus ochrogaster.desc: Prairie vole (Microtus ochrogaster): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
microtus ochrogaster.about: The prairie vole is a small vole found in central North America.

microtus oeconomus.name: Tundra vole
microtus oeconomus.desc: A small rodent of wet tundra and a well-recorded species here. It eats sedges and other plants, and is prey for foxes, stoats and wolves.
microtus oeconomus.about: The tundra vole or root vole is a medium-sized vole found in Northern and Central Europe, Asia, and northwestern North America, including Alaska and northwestern Canada.

microtus pennsylvanicus.name: Meadow vole
microtus pennsylvanicus.desc: Meadow vole (Microtus pennsylvanicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
microtus pennsylvanicus.about: The eastern meadow vole, sometimes called the field mouse or meadow mouse, is a North American vole found in eastern Canada and the United States.

microtus pinetorum.name: Woodland vole
microtus pinetorum.desc: Woodland vole (Microtus pinetorum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
microtus pinetorum.about: The woodland vole is a small vole found in eastern North America. It is also known as the pine vole.

microtus socialis.name: Social vole
microtus socialis.desc: A small rodent of open grassy ground that feeds on plants and is prey for many predators.
microtus socialis.about: The social vole is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae. It is found in China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Syria, Turkey, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Ukraine.

midnight sun.name: Midnight sun
midnight sun.desc: Long summer daylight gives a short, intense growing season on the tundra; winter is dark.

midnight sun & polar night.name: Midnight sun & polar night
midnight sun & polar night.desc: Plants and algae can only grow in the bright summer months, when the sun stays above the horizon for weeks; in winter the long polar night shuts growth down.

midnight sun and short summer.name: Midnight sun and short summer
midnight sun and short summer.desc: Above the Arctic Circle the summer sun barely sets, so plants race through a short growing season before long dark winters.

midsummer daylight.name: Midsummer daylight
midsummer daylight.desc: Near-continuous summer light drives a short, intense growing season, while the winters are dark and cold.

mild winters.name: Mild winters
mild winters.desc: The Atlantic coast climate is mild, one reason arctic-alpine and southern plants can grow side by side.

milvus migrans.name: Black kite
milvus migrans.desc: The most-recorded bird near the bay, a raptor that takes live prey and scavenges dead fish and scraps near boats and harbours.
milvus migrans.about: The black kite or fire kite is a medium-sized bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors.

milvus milvus.name: Red kite
milvus milvus.desc: Raptor and frequent scavenger. It takes small mammals and frogs, and feeds on carcasses.
milvus milvus.about: The red kite is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.

mimetes cucullatus.name: Common pagoda
mimetes cucullatus.desc: A fynbos shrub whose seeds are carried underground by native ants, which helps them survive fires.
mimetes cucullatus.about: Mimetes cucullatus is an evergreen shrub with several, mostly not branching, upright stems of 1–2 m (3–7 ft) high, that has been assigned to the family Proteaceae.

mimosa pigra.name: Giant sensitive-plant
mimosa pigra.desc: Giant sensitive-plant (Mimosa pigra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 176 times near the park in GBIF.

mimosa quadrivalvis.name: Fourvalve Mimosa
mimosa quadrivalvis.desc: Fourvalve Mimosa (Mimosa quadrivalvis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
mimosa quadrivalvis.about: Mimosa quadrivalvis, known as fourvalve mimosa, sensitive briar and cat's claw, is a trailing vine native to North America, Central America, and the Caribbean.

mimus polyglottos.name: Northern Mockingbird
mimus polyglottos.desc: Northern Mockingbird (Mimus polyglottos): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.
mimus polyglottos.about: The northern mockingbird is a mockingbird commonly found in North America, of the family Mimidae. The species is also found in some parts of the Caribbean, as well as on the Hawaiian Islands.

mineral licks.name: Mineral licks
mineral licks.desc: Natural mineral-rich spots that forest ungulates, elephants and tapirs visit to supplement their diet.

mineral salt lick.name: Mineral salt lick
mineral salt lick.desc: The Poung Nyied salt lick draws sambar and other animals from a wide area, giving them minerals.

mineral soils and salts.name: Mineral soils and salts
mineral soils and salts.desc: Volcanic, mineral-rich ground and salt flats around the lake. Little organic matter builds up in the heat.

mirounga leonina.name: Southern elephant seal
mirounga leonina.desc: Dives deep for squid and fish and also eats krill. Valdés is the only continental breeding colony, and orcas take weaned pups and juveniles.
mirounga leonina.about: The southern elephant seal is one of two species of elephant seals.

mist & seasonal rain.name: Mist & seasonal rain
mist & seasonal rain.desc: The scarp catches moisture rising from the Gulf of Aden coast, and the two main rains (April to June and October to November) support the forest.

mitchella repens.name: Partridgeberry
mitchella repens.desc: Partridge-berry (Mitchella repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 97 times near the park in GBIF.
mitchella repens.about: Mitchella repens is the best known plant in the genus Mitchella. It is a creeping prostrate herbaceous woody shrub occurring in North America belonging to the madder family (Rubiaceae).

mitella diphylla.name: Bishop's-cap
mitella diphylla.desc: Bishop's-cap (Mitella diphylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.

mitoura gryneus.name: Callophrys gryneus
mitoura gryneus.desc: Callophrys gryneus (Mitoura gryneus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

mitragyna.name: Riverside forest trees
mitragyna.desc: Trees of the wet riverbank forest whose leaves and overhanging branches feed monkeys and manatees.
mitragyna.about: Mitragyna is a genus of trees in the family Rubiaceae found in the tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa. Members of this genus contain antimalarial and analgesic indole alkaloids.

mixed ornamental and food plants.name: Gardens & fruiting plants
mixed ornamental and food plants.desc: Flower beds, vegetable plots and berry-bearing shrubs that give seeds, fruit and foliage to birds, rabbits and insects.
mixed ornamental and food plants.about: A garden is a planned space, usually outdoors, set aside for the cultivation, display, and enjoyment of plants and other forms of nature.

mniotilta varia.name: Black-and-white Warbler
mniotilta varia.desc: Black-and-white Warbler (Mniotilta varia): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.

mobula alfredi.name: Reef manta ray
mobula alfredi.desc: Filters zooplankton from the water with its wide mouth.
mobula alfredi.about: The reef manta ray or hāhālua is a species of ray in the family Mobulidae, one of the largest rays in the world.

moist dune sand.name: Moist dune sand
moist dune sand.desc: Wikipedia says moist sand just under the surface lets dune plants, the tiger beetle and Ord's kangaroo rat survive here.

mole-rat soil.name: Mole-rat soil
mole-rat soil.desc: Burrowing giant root-rats loosen the ground, and the refilled tunnels hold looser, more nutrient-rich soil than the surrounding turf.

molinia caerulea.name: Purple moor-grass
molinia caerulea.desc: Tussock grass that spreads over drained or degraded bog. It is named as one of the problems restoration projects try to reverse.
molinia caerulea.about: Molinia caerulea, known by the common name purple moor-grass, is a species of grass that is native to Europe, west Asia, and north Africa.

moloch horridus.name: Thorny devil
moloch horridus.desc: A spiny lizard that eats mostly ants and drinks by channelling dew and damp sand to its mouth. Birds and goannas prey on it.
moloch horridus.about: The thorny devil, also known commonly as the mountain devil, thorny lizard, thorny dragon, and moloch, is a species of lizard in the family Agamidae. The species is endemic to Australia.

momotus lessonii.name: Lesson's motmot
momotus lessonii.desc: A large forest bird that eats insects, small lizards and fruit.
momotus lessonii.about: Lesson's motmot or the blue-diademed motmot, is a colorful bird found in forests and woodlands of southern Mexico to western Panama.

monachus monachus.name: Mediterranean monk seal
monachus monachus.desc: Rare seal of Cap Blanc, home to the largest surviving colony; it eats octopus, squid, mullet and sardines.
monachus monachus.about: The Mediterranean monk seal is a monk seal belonging to the family Phocidae.

monarda bradburiana.name: Eastern beebalm
monarda bradburiana.desc: Eastern beebalm (Monarda bradburiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.
monarda bradburiana.about: Monarda bradburiana, the eastern beebalm or Bradbury's beebalm, is a species of perennial flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, that is native to much of the southeastern United States.

monarda citriodora.name: Lemon beebalm
monarda citriodora.desc: Lemon beebalm (Monarda citriodora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
monarda citriodora.about: Monarda citriodora is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, that is native to the southern United States and northern Mexico.

monarda fistulosa.name: Mintleaf Beebalm
monarda fistulosa.desc: Mintleaf Beebalm (Monarda fistulosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
monarda fistulosa.about: Monarda fistulosa, the wild bergamot or bee balm, is a wildflower in the mint family Lamiaceae, widespread and abundant as a native plant in much of North America.

monarda punctata.name: Spotted Beebalm
monarda punctata.desc: Spotted Beebalm (Monarda punctata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 64 times near the park in GBIF.

moneses uniflora.name: One-flowered Wintergreen
moneses uniflora.desc: One-flowered Wintergreen (Moneses uniflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
moneses uniflora.about: Moneses uniflora, the one-flowered wintergreen (British Isles), single delight, wax-flower, shy maiden, star of Bethlehem (Aleutians), St.

monochamus scutellatus.name: Whitespotted sawyer
monochamus scutellatus.desc: Whitespotted sawyer (Monochamus scutellatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.
monochamus scutellatus.about: Monochamus scutellatus, commonly known as the white-spotted sawyer or spruce sawyer or spruce bug or a hair-eater, is a common wood-boring beetle found throughout North America.

monotropa uniflora.name: Indianpipe
monotropa uniflora.desc: Indian-pipe (Monotropa uniflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.
monotropa uniflora.about: Monotropa uniflora, also known as the American Indian ghost pipe plant, is a herbaceous, parasitic, non-photosynthesizing, perennial flowering plant native to North America, Latin America, and East…

monsoon and typhoon rain.name: Monsoon and typhoon rain
monsoon and typhoon rain.desc: Heavy seasonal rain keeps the mountain forests wet and feeds the streams that carve the steep valleys.

monsoon floods.name: Monsoon floods
monsoon floods.desc: Wet-season rain floods the plains for months, spreading nutrients and filling billabongs that support plants, fish and waterbirds.

monsoon rain.name: Monsoon rain
monsoon rain.desc: Summer monsoon rain waters the lower slopes and forests.

monsoon rain and mist.name: Monsoon rain and mist
monsoon rain and mist.desc: Moist air from the Sichuan basin rises against the mountains, giving the wet climate that keeps the forest and bamboo lush.

monsoon rainfall.name: Monsoon rainfall
monsoon rainfall.desc: Heavy seasonal rain keeps the lowland forest wet year round and feeds the rivers that cross the reserve.

monsoon rains.name: Monsoon rains
monsoon rains.desc: Heavy monsoon rain feeds the rivers and keeps the forest evergreen.

monsoon upwelling.name: Monsoon upwelling
monsoon upwelling.desc: Summer monsoon winds draw nutrient-rich water to the surface of the Arabian Sea, making it one of the most productive seas on Earth.

montane rainfall and mist.name: Montane rainfall and mist
montane rainfall and mist.desc: Frequent rain and cloud on the Congo-Nile divide keep this high-altitude forest moist and growing.

morelia viridis.name: Green tree python
morelia viridis.desc: Eats mainly small mammals, with some lizards. Wikipedia names green tree pythons as predators of birds in New Guinea.
morelia viridis.about: The green tree python, is a species of snake in the family Pythonidae. The species is native to New Guinea, some islands in Indonesia, and the Cape York Peninsula in Australia.

morone saxatilis.name: Striped bass
morone saxatilis.desc: The bay is one of the biggest breeding areas for this large predator, which eats menhaden, herring, shad and other fish.
morone saxatilis.about: The striped bass, also called the Atlantic striped bass, striper, linesider, rock, or rockfish, is an anadromous perciform fish of the family Moronidae found primarily along the Atlantic coast of…

morus alba.name: White Mulberry
morus alba.desc: White Mulberry (Morus alba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

morus rubra.name: Red mulberry
morus rubra.desc: Red mulberry (Morus rubra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.

moschus berezovskii.name: Forest musk deer
moschus berezovskii.desc: A small, shy deer of the forest and thickets that browses leaves, shoots and lichens.

moschus chrysogaster.name: Alpine musk deer
moschus chrysogaster.desc: A shy browser of herbs, shrub leaves, mosses and lichens in high conifer and shrub forest.
moschus chrysogaster.about: The alpine musk deer is a musk deer species native to the eastern Himalayas in Nepal, Bhutan and India to the highlands of Tibet.

moschus fuscus.name: Black musk deer
moschus fuscus.desc: Small, secretive deer of high forest that feeds on plants and lichen. Preyed on by dholes and other carnivores.
moschus fuscus.about: The black musk deer or dusky musk deer is a species of even-toed ungulate in the family Moschidae. It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, and Nepal.

moschus moschiferus.name: Siberian musk deer
moschus moschiferus.desc: A small, nocturnal, fanged but herbivorous deer that lives on rocky forested slopes; lichens make up about 99% of its winter diet.
moschus moschiferus.about: The Siberian musk deer is a musk deer found in the mountain forests of Northeast Asia.

motacilla cinerea.name: Gray wagtail
motacilla cinerea.desc: A slim bird of mountain streams that catches insects, including butterflies.
motacilla cinerea.about: The grey wagtail is a member of the wagtail family, Motacillidae, measuring around 18–19 cm overall length.

mountain rain and cloud.name: Mountain rain and cloud
mountain rain and cloud.desc: Rainfall on the slopes, heaviest on the south-east, sets the forest and bamboo belts and fills the rivers that supply the region.

mountain soil.name: Mountain soil
mountain soil.desc: Thin, nutrient-poor mountain soils. Pitcher plants make up for scarce nitrogen by catching insects and animal droppings.

mountain soil and leaf litter.name: Mountain soil and leaf litter
mountain soil and leaf litter.desc: Forest litter and mountain soils hold the nutrients that trees and meadow plants draw on.

mountain soil and litter.name: Mountain soil and litter
mountain soil and litter.desc: Forest litter and meadow soil hold the nutrients that rhododendron, bamboo and conifers draw on.

mountain soils.name: Mountain soils
mountain soils.desc: Thin soils on rock and glacial debris supply nutrients to plants, topped up as dead matter is broken down.

mountain springs.name: Mountain springs
mountain springs.desc: About fifty springs make Nimba a water tower for the Cavally, Cestos and Sassandra rivers.

mountain streams.name: Mountain streams
mountain streams.desc: Cold, clean, fast-flowing rivers are the habitat blue ducks need.

mountain streams and pools.name: Mountain streams and pools
mountain streams and pools.desc: Headwater streams, pools and waterfalls of the plateau, part of a wider area that supplies fresh water to Lesotho, South Africa and Namibia.

mountain streams and rivers.name: Mountain streams and rivers
mountain streams and rivers.desc: Rivers such as the Tes carry mountain water down to the basin, which has no outflow to the sea.

moving sand dunes.name: Moving sand dunes
moving sand dunes.desc: Wind-shifted dunes up to about 30 m high hold salt-tolerant, sand-adapted plants that anchor the sand.

mud and nutrients.name: Mud and nutrients
mud and nutrients.desc: Intertidal mud holds the nutrients that mangroves, seagrass and algae use, and is where much dead matter ends up.

muddy tidal flats.name: Muddy tidal flats
muddy tidal flats.desc: Sheltered, muddy intertidal shores and salt flats where mangroves root, and where dead plant matter is broken down.

mugil.name: Mullet
mugil.desc: Schooling coastal fish of lagoons and mangrove channels. Crocodiles and pelicans eat them.

mugil cephalus.name: Flathead grey mullet
mugil cephalus.desc: A schooling fish of shallow bays that feeds on algae and detritus; common prey of birds, dolphins and crocodiles.
mugil cephalus.about: The striped mullet is an important food fish species in the mullet family Mugilidae. It is found in coastal temperate, subtropical, and tropical waters worldwide.

muhlenbergia pungens.name: Sandhill muhly
muhlenbergia pungens.desc: Sandhill muhly (Muhlenbergia pungens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
muhlenbergia pungens.about: Muhlenbergia pungens, the sandhill muhly or wickiup grass, is a variety of muhly grass which is found in the arid regions of western North America.

muhlenbergia sobolifera.name: Cliff Muhly
muhlenbergia sobolifera.desc: Cliff Muhly (Muhlenbergia sobolifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

mullidae.name: Goatfishes
mullidae.desc: Fish that probe the sand for small animals. Goatfish make up about two-thirds of the diet of wedge-tailed shearwaters.
mullidae.about: The goatfishes, or mullets, are ray-finned fish of the family Mullidae, the only family in the suborder Mulloidei of the order Syngnathiformes.

munida gregaria.name: Lobster krill
munida gregaria.desc: A small red squat lobster that swarms in the waters around the Falklands and southern South America and feeds many seabirds and fish.
munida gregaria.about: Munida gregaria, commonly known as the gregarious squat lobster, is a species of squat lobster found along the eastern seaboard of the South Island of New Zealand, around the southern coast of…

muntiacus muntjak.name: Indian muntjac
muntiacus muntjak.desc: A small forest deer that browses and eats fallen fruit. Prey of dholes and tigers.
muntiacus muntjak.about: The northern red muntjac is a species of muntjac. It is found in numerous countries of south-central and southeast Asia.

muntiacus reevesi.name: Formosan Reeves's muntjac
muntiacus reevesi.desc: A small forest deer that eats herbs, shoots, fruits, fungi and nuts. It is the most recorded mammal in the surrounding area.
muntiacus reevesi.about: Reeves's muntjac, also known as the Chinese muntjac, is a species of muntjac found widely in south-eastern China (from Gansu to Yunnan) and Taiwan.

muntiacus vuquangensis.name: Giant muntjac
muntiacus vuquangensis.desc: A large forest deer listed in the park, a browser on leaves and fruit, and one of the hoofed animals bears are reported to kill.
muntiacus vuquangensis.about: The giant muntjac, sometimes referred to as the large-antlered muntjac, is a species of muntjac deer.

muntingia calabura.name: Strawberry tree
muntingia calabura.desc: A fast-growing fruit tree of village edges and dry land around the lake, eaten by fruit bats.
muntingia calabura.about: Muntingia is a genus of plants in the family Muntingiaceae, comprising only one species, Muntingia calabura, named in honour of Abraham Munting.

mus musculoides.name: Temminck's mouse
mus musculoides.desc: A small African rodent of grassy and bushy habitats; prey for the Great Lakes bush viper.
mus musculoides.about: Temminck's mouse is a species of the genus Mus and of the subgenus Nannomys. It is found throughout West Africa, Central Africa, and East Africa.

mus musculus.name: House mouse
mus musculus.desc: House mouse (Mus musculus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
mus musculus.about: The house mouse is a small mammal of the rodent family Muridae, characteristically having a pointed snout, large rounded ears, and a long and almost hairless tail.

muscardinus avellanarius.name: Hazel dormouse
muscardinus avellanarius.desc: A small arboreal rodent of hazel-rich woods that eats nuts, buds, flowers and some insects.
muscardinus avellanarius.about: The hazel dormouse or common dormouse is a small dormouse species native to Europe and the only living species in the genus Muscardinus.

mustela erminea.name: Stoat
mustela erminea.desc: A small weasel that hunts voles, lemmings and birds. GloBI records both foxes and wolves eating it.
mustela erminea.about: The stoat, also known as the Eurasian ermine or ermine, is a species of mustelid native to Eurasia and the northern regions of North America.

mustela nigripes.name: Black-footed ferret
mustela nigripes.desc: Lives in prairie dog burrows and eats mostly prairie dogs. Reintroduced near the park; about 100 live in the park.
mustela nigripes.about: The black-footed ferret, also known as the American polecat or prairie dog hunter, is a mustelid species native to central North America.

mustela sibirica.name: Siberian weasel
mustela sibirica.desc: A small hunter of voles, hares and birds in forests and meadows.
mustela sibirica.about: The Siberian weasel or kolonok is a medium-sized weasel native to Asia, where it is widely distributed and inhabits various forest habitats and open areas.

mya truncata.name: Clams & seafloor worms
mya truncata.desc: Filter sinking algae from the seafloor and feed walruses.
mya truncata.about: Mya truncata, common name the blunt gaper or truncate softshell, is a species of edible saltwater clam, a marine bivalve mollusk in the family Myidae.

myadestes obscurus.name: ʻŌmaʻo
myadestes obscurus.desc: A native thrush that mainly eats fruit, and also takes insects and small invertebrates.
myadestes obscurus.about: The ʻōmaʻo, also called the Hawaiian thrush, is an endemic species of robin-like bird found only on the island of Hawaii.

mycteria americana.name: Wood stork
mycteria americana.desc: An endangered wader that feeds on fish concentrated in drying pools. Pythons have been found to eat storks.
mycteria americana.about: The wood stork is a large wading bird in the family Ciconiidae (storks).

mycteria leucocephala.name: Painted stork
mycteria leucocephala.desc: Wading bird that sweeps its bill through shallows for small fish and frogs; nests in colonies in trees near water.
mycteria leucocephala.about: The painted stork is a large wader in the stork family. It is found in the wetlands of the plains of tropical Asia south of the Himalayas in the Indian subcontinent and extending into Southeast Asia.

myctophidae.name: Lanternfish
myctophidae.desc: Small deep-water fish that rise toward the surface at night to feed on plankton. Spinner dolphins hunt small fish of this kind.
myctophidae.about: Lanternfish (or myctophids, from the Greek μυκτήρ myktḗr, "nose" and ophis, "serpent") are small mesopelagic fish of the large family Myctophidae.

myiagra vanikorensis.name: Vanikoro flycatcher
myiagra vanikorensis.desc: Mainly catches insects from a perch, and also takes lizards and small fruits.
myiagra vanikorensis.about: The Vanikoro flycatcher is a species of monarch flycatcher in the family Monarchidae. It has a slightly disjunct distribution, occurring on Vanikoro island and in Fiji.

myiarchus barbirostris.name: Sad flycatcher
myiarchus barbirostris.desc: A Jamaican flycatcher that hunts insects. The Jamaican boa is known to eat flycatcher nests.
myiarchus barbirostris.about: The sad flycatcher is a species of bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is endemic to Jamaica.

myiarchus crinitus.name: Great Crested Flycatcher
myiarchus crinitus.desc: Great Crested Flycatcher (Myiarchus crinitus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2,013 times near the park in GBIF.

myocastor coypus.name: Coypu
myocastor coypus.desc: Coypu (Myocastor coypus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
myocastor coypus.about: The nutria () or coypu () is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent native to South America.

myodes gapperi.name: Gapper's Red-backed Mouse
myodes gapperi.desc: A small forest-floor rodent that eats plants, seeds and fungi and is a staple for owls.
myodes gapperi.about: The southern red-backed vole or Gapper's red-backed vole is a small slender vole found in Canada and the northern United States.

myodes glareolus.name: Bank vole
myodes glareolus.desc: The most recorded mammal near the forest. It eats seeds, berries and herbs, and feeds foxes and owls.
myodes glareolus.about: The bank vole is a small vole with red-brown fur and some grey patches, with a tail about half as long as its body.

myodes rufocanus.name: Grey red-backed vole
myodes rufocanus.desc: A common small rodent of forest and shrubland that eats bilberry and is food for many predators.
myodes rufocanus.about: The grey red-backed vole or the grey-sided vole is a species of vole. An adult grey red-backed vole weighs 20-50 grams.

myodes rutilus.name: Northern red-backed vole
myodes rutilus.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. A small woodland vole eating seeds, berries, fungi and lichen, and preyed on by foxes and wolverines.
myodes rutilus.about: The northern red-backed vole is a small slender vole found in Alaska, northern Canada, Scandinavia and northern Russia.

myophonus borneensis.name: Bornean whistling thrush
myophonus borneensis.desc: A bird of mountain streams and forest floor that feeds on insects and other small animals.
myophonus borneensis.about: The Bornean whistling thrush is a species of bird in the family Muscicapidae. It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia, where it is endemic to the island of Borneo.

myopus schisticolor.name: Wood lemming
myopus schisticolor.desc: A small rodent of mossy spruce forest that eats mosses and the shoots of dwarf shrubs such as cowberry.
myopus schisticolor.about: The wood lemming is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae. It belongs to the rodent subfamily Arvicolinae, so is a relative of the voles, lemmings, and muskrats.

myosotis scorpioides.name: Water Forget-me-not
myosotis scorpioides.desc: Water Forget-me-not (Myosotis scorpioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

myosurus minimus.name: Mousetail
myosurus minimus.desc: Mousetail (Myosurus minimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
myosurus minimus.about: Myosurus minimus is a species of flowering plant in the family Ranunculaceae known by the common name tiny mousetail or just mousetail.

myotis grisescens.name: Gray bat
myotis grisescens.desc: Roosts in limestone caves and hunts insects over rivers and riverside forest.
myotis grisescens.about: The gray bat is a species of microbat endemic to North America.

myotis lucifugus.name: Little Brown Bat
myotis lucifugus.desc: Little Brown Bat (Myotis lucifugus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
myotis lucifugus.about: The little brown bat or little brown myotis is an endangered species of mouse-eared microbat found in North America. It has a small body size and glossy brown fur.

myotis sodalis.name: Indiana bat
myotis sodalis.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. Eats only flying insects such as moths and beetles and hibernates in cold caves.
myotis sodalis.about: The Indiana bat is a medium-sized mouse-eared bat native to North America. It lives primarily in Southern and Midwestern U.S. states and is listed as an endangered species.

myrcia.name: Myrcia trees
myrcia.desc: Myrtle-family trees and shrubs with small berries. Many birds are recorded eating Myrcia fruit.
myrcia.about: Myrcia is a genus of plants in the family Myrtaceae, containing about 794 species as of 2025.

myrianthus preussii.name: Myrianthus trees
myrianthus preussii.desc: A recorded understory tree of the Cross River forests with edible fruit; fleshy forest fruits like this feed primates and rodents.
myrianthus preussii.about: Myrianthus is a genus of flowering plants in the nettle family (Urticaceae). They are mainly found in Tropical Africa.

myriophyllum aquaticum.name: Parrot's Feather
myriophyllum aquaticum.desc: Parrot's Feather (Myriophyllum aquaticum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
myriophyllum aquaticum.about: Myriophyllum aquaticum is a flowering plant, a vascular dicot, commonly called parrot's-feather and parrot feather watermilfoil.

myriophyllum sibiricum.name: Siberian water-milfoil
myriophyllum sibiricum.desc: Siberian water-milfoil (Myriophyllum sibiricum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
myriophyllum sibiricum.about: Myriophyllum sibiricum is a species of water milfoil known by the common names shortspike watermilfoil, northern watermilfoil, and Siberian water-milfoil.

myriophyllum spicatum.name: Spiked Water-milfoil
myriophyllum spicatum.desc: Spiked Water-milfoil (Myriophyllum spicatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 56 times near the park in GBIF.
myriophyllum spicatum.about: Myriophyllum spicatum is a submerged perennial aquatic plant which grows in still or slow-moving water.

myriopteris gracilis.name: Fee's lip fern
myriopteris gracilis.desc: Fee's lip fern (Myriopteris gracilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
myriopteris gracilis.about: Myriopteris gracilis, commonly known as slender lip fern or Fee's lip fern, is a small fern native to western North America, with a few scattered populations in the east.

myrmecophaga tridactyla.name: Giant anteater
myrmecophaga tridactyla.desc: Rips open ant and termite nests and licks up thousands of insects.
myrmecophaga tridactyla.about: The giant anteater is a large insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America. It is the largest of the four living species of anteaters, which are classified with sloths in the order Pilosa.

mysis diluviana.name: Mysis
mysis diluviana.desc: A native shrimp-like crustacean of cold deep water. It eats mainly zooplankton, or algae and detritus when zooplankton is scarce.
mysis diluviana.about: Mysis diluviana is a mysid crustacean (opossum shrimp) found in freshwater lakes of northern North America.

mytilus.name: Blue mussels
mytilus.desc: Shellfish of rocky shores that filter plankton from the water. Sea otters crack them open.

mytilus californianus.name: California mussel
mytilus californianus.desc: Filters plankton from the water on wave-washed rock. Sea otters feed on mussels and so open up space on the rock for other species.
mytilus californianus.about: The California mussel is a large edible mussel, a marine bivalve mollusk in the family Mytilidae.

mytilus edulis.name: Blue mussel
mytilus edulis.desc: A filter feeder that clamps onto rocks in the tidal zone. Sea stars, whelks, gulls and eiders eat it.
mytilus edulis.about: The blue mussel, also known as the common mussel, is a medium-sized edible marine bivalve mollusc in the family Mytilidae, the only extant family in the order Mytilida, known as "true mussels".

mytilus trossulus.name: Bay mussel
mytilus trossulus.desc: Filter-feeding shellfish on rocky shores that eat plankton. Sea otters eat mussels.
mytilus trossulus.about: Mytilus trossulus, the Pacific blue mussel, bay mussel or foolish mussel, is a medium-sized edible marine bivalve mollusc in the family Mytilidae.

n/a.name: Sunlight
n/a.desc: Light that reaches the forest floor in clearings and leaf-fall seasons drives plant growth.

nadata gibbosa.name: White-dotted Prominent
nadata gibbosa.desc: White-dotted Prominent (Nadata gibbosa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

naemorhedus caudatus.name: Long-tailed goral
naemorhedus caudatus.desc: A cliff-dwelling goat-antelope that eats grasses in summer and twigs, leaves and acorns in winter. A small endangered population lives in the DMZ.
naemorhedus caudatus.about: The long-tailed goral or Amur goral is a species of ungulate of the family Bovidae found in the mountains of eastern and northern Asia, including Russia, China, and Korea.

naja arabica.name: Arabian cobra
naja arabica.desc: A venomous snake that hunts lizards and other small animals among the rocks of the highlands.
naja arabica.about: The Arabian cobra is a species of venomous snake in the family Elapidae. The species is endemic to the Arabian Peninsula.

naja oxiana.name: Caspian cobra
naja oxiana.desc: A venomous snake of dry scrub that mainly eats small mammals, and also takes birds and other snakes.
naja oxiana.about: The Caspian cobra, also called the Persian cobra or Russian cobra, is a species of highly venomous snake in the family Elapidae. The species is endemic to Central Asia.

najas minor.name: Brittle Waternymph
najas minor.desc: Brittle Waternymph (Najas minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.
najas minor.about: Najas minor, known as brittle naiad or brittle waternymph, is an annual aquatic plant, a submersed herb.

nandina domestica.name: Heavenly Bamboo
nandina domestica.desc: Heavenly Bamboo (Nandina domestica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

nandinia binotata.name: African palm civet
nandinia binotata.desc: A tree-living nocturnal omnivore that eats fruit as well as small animals.
nandinia binotata.about: The African palm civet, also known as the two-spotted palm civet, is a small feliform mammal widely distributed in sub-Saharan Africa. It is listed as least concern on the IUCN Red List.

nanger soemmerringii.name: Soemmerring's gazelle
nanger soemmerringii.desc: One of the most commonly recorded antelopes of Djibouti's dry country, helped by the hunting ban of the early 1970s.
nanger soemmerringii.about: Soemmerring's gazelle, also known as the Abyssinian mohr, is a gazelle species native to the Horn of Africa.

nannopterum auritum.name: Double-crested cormorant
nannopterum auritum.desc: A diving fish-eating bird. Alewife is believed to have created good feeding conditions for Great Lakes colonies.
nannopterum auritum.about: The double-crested cormorant is a member of the cormorant family of water birds.

narcissus poeticus.name: Pheasant's-eye Daffodil
narcissus poeticus.desc: Pheasant's-eye Daffodil (Narcissus poeticus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
narcissus poeticus.about: Narcissus poeticus, the poet's daffodil, poet's narcissus, nargis, pheasant's eye, findern flower or pinkster lily, was one of the first daffodils to be cultivated, and is frequently identified as…

nardus stricta.name: Mat-grass pasture
nardus stricta.desc: A tough tussock grass that makes up much of the upland summer pasture grazed by flocks and wild herbivores.
nardus stricta.about: Nardus is a genus of plants belonging to the grass family, containing the single species Nardus stricta, known as matgrass. It is placed in its own tribe Nardeae within the subfamily Pooideae.

nastra lherminier.name: Swarthy Skipper
nastra lherminier.desc: Swarthy Skipper (Nastra lherminier): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

nasturtium officinale.name: Watercress
nasturtium officinale.desc: Watercress (Nasturtium officinale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

nasua narica.name: White-nosed coati
nasua narica.desc: An omnivore that forages on the ground for insects, small vertebrates, eggs, carrion and fruit.
nasua narica.about: The white-nosed coati, also known as the coatimundi (), is a species of coati and a member of the family Procyonidae (raccoons and their relatives).

nasua nasua.name: South American coati
nasua nasua.desc: An omnivore that climbs to eat fruit, hunts invertebrates and eggs, and is itself preyed on by jaguars.
nasua nasua.about: The South American coati, also known as the ring-tailed coati or brown-nosed coati, is a coati species and a member of the raccoon family (Procyonidae), found in the tropical and subtropical parts of…

nathalis iole.name: Dainty Sulphur
nathalis iole.desc: Dainty Sulphur (Nathalis iole): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

natrix natrix.name: Grass snake
natrix natrix.desc: A semi-aquatic snake that hunts frogs and other amphibians around ponds and wet meadows.
natrix natrix.about: The grass snake, sometimes called the ringed snake or water snake, is a Eurasian semi-aquatic non-venomous colubrid snake. It is often found near water and feeds almost exclusively on amphibians.

natrix tessellata.name: Dice snake
natrix tessellata.desc: A semi-aquatic snake that hunts fish and amphibians in water.
natrix tessellata.about: The dice snake or water snake is a Eurasian nonvenomous snake in the family Colubridae, subfamily Natricinae. Its average length is 1.0–1.3 m (39–51 in).

necrosyrtes monachus.name: Hooded vulture
necrosyrtes monachus.desc: A small scavenging vulture recorded feeding on carcasses of hippo, waterbuck and elephant.
necrosyrtes monachus.about: The hooded vulture is an Old World vulture in the order Accipitriformes, which also includes eagles, kites, buzzards and hawks.

nectarinia famosa.name: Malachite sunbird
nectarinia famosa.desc: A long-tailed nectar-feeding bird that visits heaths and other flowering plants and also takes insects.
nectarinia famosa.about: The malachite sunbird is a small nectarivorous bird found from the highlands of Ethiopia southwards to South Africa.

negaprion acutidens.name: Sicklefin lemon shark
negaprion acutidens.desc: An Indian Ocean shark that uses shallow sheltered waters such as mangrove creeks as a nursery.
negaprion acutidens.about: The sicklefin lemon shark or sharptooth lemon shark is a species of requiem shark belonging to the family Carcharhinidae, widely distributed in the tropical waters of the Indo-Pacific.

nelumbo lutea.name: American lotus
nelumbo lutea.desc: American lotus (Nelumbo lutea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
nelumbo lutea.about: Nelumbo lutea is a species of flowering plant in the family Nelumbonaceae. Common names include American lotus, yellow lotus, water-chinquapin, and volée.

nemastylis geminiflora.name: Prairie celestial
nemastylis geminiflora.desc: Prairie celestial (Nemastylis geminiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
nemastylis geminiflora.about: Nemastylis geminiflora, commonly known as prairie celestial, celestial, prairie pleatleaf, or celestial lily is a perennial herb in the Iridaceae (iris) family.

nemoria bistriaria.name: Red-fringed Emerald
nemoria bistriaria.desc: Red-fringed Emerald (Nemoria bistriaria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

neocalanus.name: Copepods and zooplankton
neocalanus.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze the spring bloom and pass its energy on to young salmon and schooling fish.
neocalanus.about: Copepods are a group of small crustaceans found in nearly every freshwater and saltwater habitat.

neofelis diardi.name: Sunda clouded leopard
neofelis diardi.desc: A tree-climbing cat. Wikipedia lists it as a potential predator of orangutans at Sikundur.
neofelis diardi.about: The Sunda clouded leopard is a medium-sized wild cat native to Borneo and Sumatra.

neofelis nebulosa.name: Clouded leopard
neofelis nebulosa.desc: A tree-climbing cat of dense forest, recorded in the reserve's evergreen forest. It hunts deer and other mammals.
neofelis nebulosa.about: The clouded leopard, also called mainland clouded leopard, is a wild cat that has large dusky-grey blotches and irregular spots and stripes reminiscent of clouds.

neophocaena phocaenoides.name: Finless porpoise
neophocaena phocaenoides.desc: A small coastal porpoise recorded near the bay. It eats whatever is available, such as fish, crustaceans and cephalopods; gill nets are a main threat.
neophocaena phocaenoides.about: The Indo-Pacific finless porpoise is one of eight porpoise species.

neophron percnopterus.name: Egyptian vulture
neophron percnopterus.desc: A small, opportunistic vulture and the most recorded bird in the area. It feeds mainly on carrion and also takes insects and eggs.
neophron percnopterus.about: The Egyptian vulture, also called the white scavenger vulture or pharaoh's chicken, is a small, Old World vulture in the monotypic genus Neophron.

neotoma albigula.name: White-throated woodrat
neotoma albigula.desc: White-throated woodrat (Neotoma albigula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
neotoma albigula.about: The white-throated woodrat is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae. It is found from central Mexico north to Utah and Colorado in the United States.

neotoma lepida.name: Desert woodrat
neotoma lepida.desc: A pack-rat of rocky desert slopes that feeds on cacti, juniper and other plants.
neotoma lepida.about: The desert woodrat is a species of pack rat native to desert regions of western North America.

neotoma leucodon.name: White-toothed woodrat
neotoma leucodon.desc: A packrat for which cacti, especially cholla and prickly pear, are a major part of the diet.
neotoma leucodon.about: Neotoma leucodon is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae.

neotoma mexicana.name: Mexican woodrat
neotoma mexicana.desc: A generalist that eats berries, nuts, acorns and foliage. It shelters in rock crevices and caves.

neotoma micropus.name: Southern plains woodrat
neotoma micropus.desc: Southern plains woodrat (Neotoma micropus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

neotoma stephensi.name: Stephen's Woodrat
neotoma stephensi.desc: Stephen's Woodrat (Neotoma stephensi): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 72 times near the park in GBIF.
neotoma stephensi.about: Stephen's woodrat is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae found in Arizona, New Mexico and Utah in the United States.

neotomodon alstoni.name: Mexican volcano mouse
neotomodon alstoni.desc: A burrowing rodent of high-elevation forest on the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt, and a recorded prey of the dusky rattlesnake.
neotomodon alstoni.about: The Mexican volcano mouse is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae endemic to high elevation areas of the Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt.

neotragus pygmaeus.name: Royal antelope
neotragus pygmaeus.desc: One of the smallest antelopes in the world, a shy browser of leaves, shoots and fallen fruit in dense forest.
neotragus pygmaeus.about: The royal antelope is a West African antelope recognized as the world's smallest. It was first described by Swedish zoologist Carl Linnaeus in 1758.

nepenthes rajah.name: Giant pitcher plant
nepenthes rajah.desc: A carnivorous plant and the most notable pitcher plant of the park. Tree shrews and summit rats lick nectar from its lid and defecate into the pitcher.
nepenthes rajah.about: Nepenthes rajah is a carnivorous pitcher plant species of the family Nepenthaceae. It is endemic to Mount Kinabalu and neighbouring Mount Tambuyukon in Sabah, Malaysian Borneo.

nephelodes minians.name: Bronzed Cutworm
nephelodes minians.desc: Bronzed Cutworm (Nephelodes minians): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

nephrolepis cordifolia.name: Tuber ladder fern
nephrolepis cordifolia.desc: Tuber ladder fern (Nephrolepis cordifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

nereocystis luetkeana.name: Bull kelp
