nereocystis luetkeana.desc: A canopy kelp of central and northern California coasts, eaten by black abalone there along with drift algae.
nereocystis luetkeana.about: Nereocystis (Greek, 'mermaid's bladder') is a monotypic genus of subtidal kelp containing the species Nereocystis luetkeana.

nerisyrenia linearifolia.name: White Sands fan mustard
nerisyrenia linearifolia.desc: White Sands fan mustard (Nerisyrenia linearifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

nerodia erythrogaster.name: Plain-bellied water snake
nerodia erythrogaster.desc: A swamp snake recorded eating frogs, and a regular visitor of floodplain pools.
nerodia erythrogaster.about: Nerodia erythrogaster, also known as the plain-bellied water snake or plainbelly water snake, is a common species of semi-aquatic, non-venomous colubrid snake endemic to the United States.

nerodia fasciata.name: Banded water snake
nerodia fasciata.desc: A common water snake that eats frogs and toads.
nerodia fasciata.about: The banded water snake or southern water snake is a species of mostly aquatic, nonvenomous, colubrid snakes most commonly found in the Midwest, Southeastern United States.

nesotriccus ridgwayi.name: Cocos flycatcher
nesotriccus ridgwayi.desc: One of three endemic land birds; a small insect-catching bird of the island forest.
nesotriccus ridgwayi.about: The Cocos tyrannulet, also known as the Cocos flycatcher, is a vulnerable species of bird in subfamily Elaeniinae of family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers.

nestor notabilis.name: Kea
nestor notabilis.desc: Alpine parrot that eats roots, leaves, berries and insects, and also scavenges carrion.
nestor notabilis.about: The kea is a species of large parrot in the family Strigopidae that is endemic to the forested and alpine regions of the South Island of New Zealand.

new river & streams.name: New River & streams
new river & streams.desc: Water carved the gorge, and the riparian zone is the park's most biologically diverse area.

nicotiana glauca.name: Tree Tobacco
nicotiana glauca.desc: Tree Tobacco (Nicotiana glauca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
nicotiana glauca.about: Nicotiana glauca is a species of flowering plant in the tobacco genus Nicotiana of the nightshade family Solanaceae. It is known by the common name tree tobacco.

nicotiana sylvestris.name: South American Tobacco
nicotiana sylvestris.desc: South American Tobacco (Nicotiana sylvestris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.

nicrophorus americanus.name: American burying beetle
nicrophorus americanus.desc: An endangered beetle present here in summer. Adults need small carcasses to breed and bury them to feed their young.
nicrophorus americanus.about: Nicrophorus americanus, also known as the American burying beetle or giant carrion beetle, is a critically endangered species of beetle endemic to North America.

nilgiritragus hylocrius.name: Nilgiri tahr
nilgiritragus hylocrius.desc: An endangered mountain goat of the shola-grassland mosaic that grazes grass and small shrubs on rocky slopes.
nilgiritragus hylocrius.about: The Nilgiri tahr is an ungulate that is endemic to the Nilgiri Hills and the southern portion of the Western Ghats in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

nimbaphrynoides occidentalis.name: Nimba viviparous toad
nimbaphrynoides occidentalis.desc: A critically endangered toad found only in the high grasslands of Nimba at about 1,200 to 1,680 m. It gives birth to live young and does not tolerate disturbed ground.
nimbaphrynoides occidentalis.about: Nimbaphrynoides is a monotypic genus of true toads from highlands in the Mount Nimba region of the West African countries of Guinea, Liberia, and Côte d'Ivoire.

nimbochromis.name: Predatory haps
nimbochromis.desc: Large cichlids that prey on other fish. Livingstoni plays dead to lure prey close.
nimbochromis.about: Nimbochromis livingstonii, Livingston's cichlid or, kalingono (in Chichewa), is a freshwater mouthbrooding cichlid native to Lake Malawi, an African Rift Lake.

nisaetus nipalensis.name: Mountain hawk-eagle
nisaetus nipalensis.desc: A forest raptor that nests in the park. In a Taiwan nest study giant flying squirrels and Pallas's squirrels were its main prey.
nisaetus nipalensis.about: The mountain hawk-eagle or Hodgson's hawk-eagle, is a large bird of prey native to Asia.

nitraria sibirica.name: Siberian nitraria
nitraria sibirica.desc: A salt-tolerant spiny shrub of sandy hollows and dune edges, recorded often in the park area.

nitrogen and phosphorus.name: Nutrient runoff
nitrogen and phosphorus.desc: Nitrogen and phosphorus from farms, towns, sewage and air pollution wash into the bay and fuel algal blooms.

nitrogen from land and sewage.name: Nitrogen from land and sewage
nitrogen from land and sewage.desc: Nitrogen is a key nutrient for the bay's algae. Cuts in wastewater nitrogen since 2006 have been followed by smaller annual phytoplankton blooms.

nitrophila occidentalis.name: Boraxweed
nitrophila occidentalis.desc: Boraxweed (Nitrophila occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
nitrophila occidentalis.about: Nitrophila occidentalis is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae known by the common name boraxweed and sometimes western niterwort.

nitrosalsola vermiculata.name: Shrubby saltbush
nitrosalsola vermiculata.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub, named as a climax plant of the Syrian steppe, and a mainstay of grazing land.
nitrosalsola vermiculata.about: Caroxylon vermiculatum, commonly known as Mediterranean saltwort, is a perennial plant in the family Amaranthaceae. It has many synonyms, including Salsola vermiculata and Nitrosalsola vermiculata.

niviventer culturatus.name: Taiwan white-bellied rat
niviventer culturatus.desc: A rodent of primary hemlock forest, recorded in Yushan National Park. Rodents like this are food for snakes and weasels.
niviventer culturatus.about: The Oldfield white-bellied rat or soft-furred Taiwan niviventer is a species of rodent in the family Muridae. It is found only in Taiwan.

nomascus leucogenys.name: Northern white-cheeked gibbon
nomascus leucogenys.desc: A tree-dwelling ape that eats mainly fruit with some leaves and buds. About 57 groups were estimated in this reserve in 2019.
nomascus leucogenys.about: The northern white-cheeked gibbon is a Critically Endangered species of gibbon native to South East Asia.

notamacropus rufogriseus.name: Red-necked wallaby
notamacropus rufogriseus.desc: A grazing wallaby of open forest and heath, preyed on by devils, quolls and eagles.
notamacropus rufogriseus.about: The red-necked wallaby or Bennett's wallaby is a medium-sized macropod marsupial (wallaby), common in the more temperate and fertile parts of eastern Australia, including Tasmania.

nothofagus.name: Southern beech
nothofagus.desc: New Guinea beeches characterise lower and upper montane rain forest. UNESCO notes the park's beech forests are well represented and are hit by Phytophthora dieback.
nothofagus.about: Nothofagus, also known as the southern beeches, is a genus of 43 species of trees and shrubs native to the Southern Hemisphere, found across southern South America (Chile, Argentina) and eastern and…

nothofagus antarctica.name: Ñire
nothofagus antarctica.desc: A hardy southern beech of the forest edge, where the Magellanic forest meets the dry Patagonian steppe.
nothofagus antarctica.about: Nothofagus antarctica is a deciduous tree or shrub native to southern Chile and Argentina from about 36°S to Tierra del Fuego (56° S), where it grows mainly in the diminishing temperate rainforest.

nothofagus cliffortioides.name: Mountain beech
nothofagus cliffortioides.desc: A beech tree of the park's cooler forests; Wikipedia names beech forest as one of the main forest types around Tongariro and Ruapehu.
nothofagus cliffortioides.about: Nothofagus cliffortioides, commonly called mountain beech (Māori: tawhai rauriki), is a species of southern beech tree and is endemic to New Zealand.

nothofagus cunninghamii.name: Myrtle beech
nothofagus cunninghamii.desc: The main canopy tree of Tasmania's cool temperate rainforest, sharing the canopy with sassafras, leatherwood and conifers.
nothofagus cunninghamii.about: Nothofagus cunninghamii, commonly known as myrtle beech or Tasmanian myrtle, is the dominant species of cool temperate rainforests in Tasmania and Southern Victoria.

nothofagus menziesii.name: Silver beech
nothofagus menziesii.desc: A dominant tree of Fiordland forests. Its heavy seed years feed rodent booms that in turn feed stoats.
nothofagus menziesii.about: Nothofagus menziesii, commonly known as silver beech, is a species of evergreen tree in the family Nothofagaceae. It is endemic to New Zealand and is widespread in the North and South Islands.

nothofagus pumilio.name: Lenga beech
nothofagus pumilio.desc: A deciduous southern beech that forms the dense high-latitude forests of the southern Andes. It tolerates hard frost and heavy snow and regrows easily after fire.
nothofagus pumilio.about: Nothofagus pumilio, the lenga beech, is a deciduous tree or shrub in the Nothofagaceae family that is native to the southern Andes range, in the temperate forests of Chile and Argentina to Tierra del…

notholithocarpus densiflorus.name: Tan-oak
notholithocarpus densiflorus.desc: Tan-oak (Notholithocarpus densiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 268 times near the park in GBIF.

nothoscordum bivalve.name: Crow-poison
nothoscordum bivalve.desc: Crow-poison (Nothoscordum bivalve): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

notomys alexis.name: Spinifex hopping mouse
notomys alexis.desc: A small hopping rodent of central Australia that lives in burrows on spinifex and mulga flats. It takes plant food and is prey for many predators.
notomys alexis.about: The spinifex hopping mouse, also known as the tarkawara or tarrkawarra, occurs throughout the central and western Australian arid zones, occupying both spinifex-covered sand flats and stabilised sand…

nucifraga caryocatactes.name: Eurasian nutcracker
nucifraga caryocatactes.desc: A crow-family bird that feeds on conifer seeds, especially pine seeds, and stores them in caches.
nucifraga caryocatactes.about: The northern nutcracker, previously known as the spotted nutcracker and Eurasian nutcracker, is a passerine bird in the crow family Corvidae.

nucifraga columbiana.name: Clark's nutcracker
nucifraga columbiana.desc: Feeds mainly on pine seeds, caches more than it needs, and also eats insects and carrion. It helps spread limber and whitebark pines.
nucifraga columbiana.about: Clark's nutcracker, also known as Clark's crow, is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to the mountains of western North America.

numenius arquata.name: Eurasian curlew
numenius arquata.desc: Large wader whose long curved bill reaches worms and crabs buried in soft mud.
numenius arquata.about: The Eurasian curlew or common curlew is a very large wader in the family Scolopacidae. It is one of the most widespread of the curlews, breeding across temperate Europe and Asia.

numida meleagris.name: Helmeted guineafowl
numida meleagris.desc: Ground-feeding flocks that eat seeds and insects, and nest on the ground.
numida meleagris.about: The helmeted guinea fowl is the best known of the guinea fowl bird family, Numididae, and the only member of the genus Numida.

nuphar.name: Pond lilies
nuphar.desc: Floating-leaved aquatic plants of ponds and slow water, a food for moose and beavers.
nuphar.about: Nuphar is a genus of aquatic plants in the family Nymphaeaceae, with a temperate to subarctic Northern Hemisphere distribution.

nuphar advena.name: Spatter-dock
nuphar advena.desc: Spatter-dock (Nuphar advena): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

nuphar polysepala.name: Rocky Mountain pond-lily
nuphar polysepala.desc: Rocky Mountain pond-lily (Nuphar polysepala): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
nuphar polysepala.about: Nuphar polysepala, also known as the great yellow pond-lily, wokas, or wocus, is a perennial, rhizomatous, aquatic herb in the genus Nuphar. It has floating green leaves and yellow flowers.

nuphar variegata.name: Varigated Yellow Pond-Lily
nuphar variegata.desc: Varigated Yellow Pond-Lily (Nuphar variegata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
nuphar variegata.about: Nuphar variegata is rhizomatous, perennial, aquatic herb in the water lily family Nymphaeaceae native to much of Canada and the northernmost of the United States.

nura river and snowmelt.name: Nura River and snowmelt
nura river and snowmelt.desc: Spring snowmelt and the Nura River fill the lake basins; water levels vary from season to season.

nutrient-poor sandstone soil.name: Nutrient-poor sandstone soil
nutrient-poor sandstone soil.desc: Acidic soils from sandstone are low in nutrients, which shapes the stunted shrubs and the carnivorous plants.

nutrient-poor sandy soil.name: Nutrient-poor sandy soil
nutrient-poor sandy soil.desc: Fynbos grows on poor, acid sands from Table Mountain sandstone and similar rocks.

nutrient-poor soil.name: Nutrient-poor soil
nutrient-poor soil.desc: Heavy rain washes minerals out, so most nutrients are held in living plants and leaf litter.

nutrient-rich deep water.name: Nutrient-rich deep water
nutrient-rich deep water.desc: Currents lift nutrient-rich deep ocean water along the peninsula. Together with melting ice, it fuels spring plankton blooms.

nutrient-rich mud.name: Nutrient-rich mud
nutrient-rich mud.desc: Oxygen-poor mangrove mud holds the nutrients released by decomposing leaves and wood.

nutrients.name: Nutrients
nutrients.desc: Upwelling and river runoff supply nitrogen and phosphorus. Too much feeds algae at the coral's expense.

nutrients and runoff.name: Nutrients and runoff
nutrients and runoff.desc: Nutrients from land and recycled from dead matter feed plankton and algae. Excess runoff favours algae over coral.

nyctereutes procyonoides.name: Raccoon dog
nyctereutes procyonoides.desc: Common on the island though not native. It digs into sea turtle nests and takes baby turtles.
nyctereutes procyonoides.about: Nyctereutes (Ancient Greek: νύξ, νυκτ- [nýx, nykt-] 'night' + ἐρέυτης [eréutēs] 'wanderer') is a genus of Asian canid with two extant species, the raccoon dogs: the common raccoon dog and the…

nymphaea alba.name: White water-lily
nymphaea alba.desc: Floating-leaved plant of the still channels and lakes. Muskrats and mute swans are recorded eating it.
nymphaea alba.about: Nymphaea alba – commonly called the white water lily, European white water lily, or white nenuphar ( NEN-yuu-far) – is an aquatic flowering plant in the family Nymphaeaceae.

nymphaea and utricularia.name: Waterlilies and bladderwort
nymphaea and utricularia.desc: Submerged and floating plants of the open sloughs that give food and cover to aquatic animals.
nymphaea and utricularia.about: Nymphaea odorata, also known as the American white waterlily, fragrant water-lily, beaver root, fragrant white water lily, white water lily, sweet-scented white water lily, and sweet-scented water…

nymphaea lotus.name: Water lotus
nymphaea lotus.desc: A floating water plant of slow river channels and backwaters.
nymphaea lotus.about: Nymphaea lotus, the white Egyptian lotus, tiger lotus, white lotus, or Egyptian water-lily, is a flowering plant of the family Nymphaeaceae.

nymphaea odorata.name: American Waterlily
nymphaea odorata.desc: A floating-leaved plant of the open lakes and wet prairies, which cover about 60,000 acres of the refuge.
nymphaea odorata.about: Nymphaea odorata, also known as the American white waterlily, fragrant water-lily, beaver root, fragrant white water lily, white water lily, sweet-scented white water lily, and sweet-scented water…

nymphalidae.name: Butterflies
nymphalidae.desc: Many butterflies live here, and the park is known for them. Caterpillars chew leaves, adults feed on fruit, sap or nectar.
nymphalidae.about: The Nymphalidae are the largest family of butterflies, with more than 6,000 species distributed throughout most of the world.

nymphalis antiopa.name: Mourningcloak
nymphalis antiopa.desc: Mourningcloak (Nymphalis antiopa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
nymphalis antiopa.about: Nymphalis antiopa, known as the mourning cloak in North America and the Camberwell beauty in Britain, is a large butterfly native to Eurasia and North America.

nymphalis californica.name: California Tortoiseshell
nymphalis californica.desc: California Tortoiseshell (Nymphalis californica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
nymphalis californica.about: The California tortoiseshell is a butterfly of the family Nymphalidae.

oarisma garita.name: Garita Skipperling
oarisma garita.desc: Garita Skipperling (Oarisma garita): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

oasis groundwater.name: Oasis groundwater
oasis groundwater.desc: Water close to the surface at oases and in wadis lets trees and palms grow where the surrounding desert is bare.

oasis springs.name: Oasis springs
oasis springs.desc: Scattered springs and seeps are the water that desert plants, wild asses, camels and bears gather around.

oasis springs and wadi.name: Oasis springs and wadi
oasis springs and wadi.desc: Springs such as Efqa and the small al-Qubur wadi water the Palmyra oasis, which supports palms and gardens amid dry desert.

occidryas chalcedona.name: Occidryas chalcedona
occidryas chalcedona.desc: Occidryas chalcedona (Occidryas chalcedona): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

ocean currents.name: Ocean currents
ocean currents.desc: The island is the first landmark met by the North Equatorial Countercurrent, where currents meet and carry larvae and plankton across the Pacific.

ocean currents & nutrients.name: Ocean currents & nutrients
ocean currents & nutrients.desc: Open-ocean water around the islands carries nutrients and plankton that the reefs and fish depend on.

ocean passages.name: Ocean passages
ocean passages.desc: Natural gaps in the barrier reef, such as the Boulari passage, let ocean water flow into and out of the lagoon.

ochlodes sylvanoides.name: Woodland Skipper
ochlodes sylvanoides.desc: Woodland Skipper (Ochlodes sylvanoides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
ochlodes sylvanoides.about: Ochlodes sylvanoides, the woodland skipper, is a butterfly of the family Hesperiidae.

ochotona alpina.name: Alpine pika
ochotona alpina.desc: A small lagomorph living among scree and rocks that eats meadow plants. Snow leopards also hunt small mammals such as pikas.
ochotona alpina.about: The alpine pika is a species of small mammal in the pika family, Ochotonidae.

ochotona coreana.name: Korean pika
ochotona coreana.desc: A small rock-dwelling relative of rabbits found in the mountains of northern North Korea and the Changbai range.
ochotona coreana.about: The Korean pika, also known as the Korean piping hare, is a species of mammal in the family Ochotonidae.

ochotona macrotis.name: Large-eared pika
ochotona macrotis.desc: A small lagomorph of rocky high slopes that eats grasses and herbs. Predators here are inferred from general knowledge.
ochotona macrotis.about: The large-eared pika is a species of small mammal in the family Ochotonidae.

ochotona pallasi.name: Pallas's pika
ochotona pallasi.desc: A small herbivore of rocky ground, among the most-recorded mammals near the park and food for small carnivores.
ochotona pallasi.about: Pallas's pika, also known as the Mongolian pika, is a species of small mammals in the pika family, Ochotonidae. It is found mainly in the mountains of western Mongolia.

ochotona princeps.name: American pika
ochotona princeps.desc: A small herbivore of rock slopes that eats grasses and wildflowers and stores hay for winter. Hawks and eagles prey on it.
ochotona princeps.about: The American pika is a small, herbivorous mammal of the family Ochotonidae, closely related to rabbits and hares (order Lagomorpha).

ochotona thibetana.name: Moupin pika
ochotona thibetana.desc: Colonial burrower of rocky ground under rhododendron and bamboo that stores haypiles of plants.
ochotona thibetana.about: The Moupin pika, also known as Moupin-pika, and Manipuri pika, is a species of mammal in the pika family, Ochotonidae. It has many subspecies, some of which may be distinct species.

ocotea.name: Laurel family trees
ocotea.desc: Montane forest trees of the laurel family. Wikipedia notes laurels are among the fruit families Andean cock-of-the-rock eats.
ocotea.about: Ocotea is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Lauraceae. Many are evergreen trees with lauroid leaves.

ocotea leucoxylon.name: Ocotea
ocotea leucoxylon.desc: A tree of the laurel family. Its fruits are a food for forest birds and mammals.
ocotea leucoxylon.about: Ocotea is a genus of flowering plants belonging to the family Lauraceae. Many are evergreen trees with lauroid leaves.

ocotea usambarensis.name: Camphor wood
ocotea usambarensis.desc: A canopy tree of the wet southern montane forest, with ferns and epiphytes growing beneath and on it.
ocotea usambarensis.about: Kuloa usambarensis is a species of tree in the laurel family (Lauraceae).

octopus vulgaris.name: Common octopus
octopus vulgaris.desc: Seabed hunter of crabs and shellfish; octopus and squid are the chief food of Mediterranean monk seals.
octopus vulgaris.about: The common octopus is a mollusk belonging to the class Cephalopoda. Octopus vulgaris is one of the most studied of all the octopus species, and also one of the most intelligent.

ocypode.name: Ghost crab
ocypode.desc: A burrowing beach crab that scavenges carrion and takes turtle hatchlings.
ocypode.about: Ghost crabs are semiterrestrial crabs of the subfamily Ocypodinae, from Ancient Greek ὠκύς (okús), meaning "swift", and πούς (poús), meaning "foot".

odobenus rosmarus.name: Walrus
odobenus rosmarus.desc: Digs clams out of the seabed with its whiskers.
odobenus rosmarus.about: The walrus is a large pinniped marine mammal with discontinuous distribution about the North Pole in the Arctic Ocean and subarctic seas of the Northern Hemisphere.

odocoileus hemionus.name: Mule deer
odocoileus hemionus.desc: Mule deer (Odocoileus hemionus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
odocoileus hemionus.about: The mule deer is a deer indigenous to western North America; it is named for its ears, which are large like those of the mule. Two subspecies of mule deer are grouped into the black-tailed deer.

odocoileus virginianus.name: White-tailed deer
odocoileus virginianus.desc: White-tailed deer (Odocoileus virginianus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
odocoileus virginianus.about: The white-tailed deer, also known commonly as the whitetail and the Virginia deer, is a medium-sized species of deer native to North and South America.

odontomachus bauri.name: Trap-jaw ant
odontomachus bauri.desc: A leaf-litter ant that feeds on sugary fruit and nectar and on small invertebrates.
odontomachus bauri.about: Odontomachus is a genus of ants commonly called trap-jaw ants found in the tropics and subtropics throughout the world.

odontotermes.name: Termites
odontotermes.desc: Build mounds and recycle dry grass and wood. They are the main food of sloth bears.
odontotermes.about: Termites are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

oecophylla smaragdina.name: Asian weaver ant
oecophylla smaragdina.desc: Builds leaf nests in the canopy and hunts other insects in large colonies.
oecophylla smaragdina.about: Oecophylla smaragdina is a species of arboreal ant found in tropical Asia and Australia.

oenanthe cypriaca.name: Cyprus wheatear
oenanthe cypriaca.desc: Breeds only on Cyprus, often in woodland. Hunts insects and, in GloBI records, small lizards.
oenanthe cypriaca.about: The Cyprus wheatear or Cyprus pied wheatear is a small, 14–15 cm long passerine bird that was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family Turdidae, but is now more generally considered to be an…

oenanthe deserti.name: Desert wheatear
oenanthe deserti.desc: An insectivore that picks ants, beetles and other insects from the ground. GloBI records show it eating small lizards too.
oenanthe deserti.about: The desert wheatear is a wheatear, a small passerine bird that was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family Turdidae, but is now more generally considered to be an Old World flycatcher…

oenanthe isabellina.name: Isabelline wheatear
oenanthe isabellina.desc: A migratory insect-eating bird that winters in open country and is a prey item of wildcats in GloBI records.
oenanthe isabellina.about: The isabelline wheatear is a small passerine bird that was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family Turdidae, but is now more generally considered to be an Old World flycatcher in the family…

oenothera biennis.name: Common Evening-primrose
oenothera biennis.desc: Common Evening-primrose (Oenothera biennis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera cespitosa.name: Tufted evening-primrose
oenothera cespitosa.desc: Tufted evening-primrose (Oenothera cespitosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera curtiflora.name: Velvetweed
oenothera curtiflora.desc: Velvetweed (Oenothera curtiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera deltoides.name: Basket evening-primrose
oenothera deltoides.desc: Basket evening-primrose (Oenothera deltoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 192 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera fruticosa.name: Narrow-leaf Evening-primrose
oenothera fruticosa.desc: Narrow-leaf Evening-primrose (Oenothera fruticosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.
oenothera fruticosa.about: Oenothera fruticosa, the narrowleaf evening primrose or narrow-leaved sundrops, is a species of flowering plant in the evening primrose family.

oenothera glaucifolia.name: False gaura
oenothera glaucifolia.desc: False gaura (Oenothera glaucifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera hartwegii.name: Hartweg's Evening Primrose
oenothera hartwegii.desc: Hartweg's Evening Primrose (Oenothera hartwegii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
oenothera hartwegii.about: Oenothera hartwegii, Hartweg's sundrops, is a species of flowering plant in the evening primrose family Onagraceae.

oenothera macrocarpa.name: Ozark sundrop
oenothera macrocarpa.desc: Ozark sundrop (Oenothera macrocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
oenothera macrocarpa.about: Oenothera macrocarpa, the bigfruit evening primrose, Ozark sundrops, Missouri evening primrose, or Missouri primrose, is a species of flowering plant in the evening primrose family Onagraceae, native…

oenothera pallida.name: Pale evening primrose
oenothera pallida.desc: Pale evening primrose (Oenothera pallida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera rhombipetala.name: Four-Points evening-primrose
oenothera rhombipetala.desc: Four-Points evening-primrose (Oenothera rhombipetala): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera serrulata.name: Plains yellow primrose
oenothera serrulata.desc: Plains yellow primrose (Oenothera serrulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

oenothera suffrutescens.name: Scarlet beeblossom
oenothera suffrutescens.desc: Scarlet beeblossom (Oenothera suffrutescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

okapia johnstoni.name: Okapi
okapia johnstoni.desc: A shy forest giraffe relative that browses leaves, buds, ferns and fruit in the understory. Its main natural predator is the leopard.
okapia johnstoni.about: The okapi, also known as forest giraffe and zebra giraffe, is an artiodactyl mammal that is endemic to the northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is the only species in the genus Okapia.

olea.name: Wild olive
olea.desc: An evergreen tree that grows with juniper on the rocky scarp and helps form the dry montane forest canopy.
olea.about: Olea ( OH-lee-ə) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Oleaceae.

olneya tesota.name: Desert ironwood
olneya tesota.desc: Desert ironwood (Olneya tesota): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 157 times near the park in GBIF.
olneya tesota.about: Olneya tesota is a perennial flowering tree of the family Fabaceae, legumes (peas, beans, etc.), which is commonly known as ironwood, desert ironwood, or palo fierro in Spanish.

omocestus.name: Steppe grasshoppers
omocestus.desc: Grasshoppers eat steppe grasses and are prey for frogs and other small predators.
omocestus.about: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.

omocestus viridulus.name: Common green grasshopper
omocestus viridulus.desc: A grass-feeding grasshopper of meadows, recorded in the area.
omocestus viridulus.about: Omocestus viridulus, known in the British Isles as the common green grasshopper, is a Palearctic species of grasshopper in the subfamily Gomphocerinae.

omura congrua.name: Gaudy grasshopper
omura congrua.desc: A leaf-eating grasshopper of the forest understorey, food for lizards and other insect-eaters.
omura congrua.about: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.

oncopeltus fasciatus.name: Large Milkweed Bug
oncopeltus fasciatus.desc: Large Milkweed Bug (Oncopeltus fasciatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
oncopeltus fasciatus.about: Oncopeltus fasciatus, known as the large milkweed bug, is a medium-sized hemipteran (true bug) of the family Lygaeidae.

oncorhynchus.name: Pacific salmon
oncorhynchus.desc: Salmon feed at sea, then return to streams to spawn and die. Their bodies carry ocean energy to bears, eagles, wolves and scavengers.
oncorhynchus.about: Oncorhynchus is a genus of ray-finned fish in the subfamily Salmoninae of the family Salmonidae, native to coldwater tributaries of the North Pacific basin.

oncorhynchus clarkii bouvieri.name: Cutthroat trout
oncorhynchus clarkii bouvieri.desc: Yellowstone's native trout. Eats mayflies and fallen grasshoppers, and feeds otters, ospreys, eagles and bears.
oncorhynchus clarkii bouvieri.about: The Yellowstone cutthroat trout is a subspecies of Rocky Mountain cutthroat trout. It is a freshwater fish in the salmon family (family Salmonidae).

oncorhynchus gorbuscha.name: Pink salmon
oncorhynchus gorbuscha.desc: Feeds on plankton, invertebrates and small fish at sea, then returns to streams to spawn. Spawned-out carcasses feed bears and stream life.
oncorhynchus gorbuscha.about: Pink salmon or humpback salmon is a species of euryhaline ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.

oncorhynchus mykiss.name: Rainbow trout
oncorhynchus mykiss.desc: An introduced predator. Wikipedia attributes the likely extinction of one Orestias species to competition and predation by introduced trout and silverside.
oncorhynchus mykiss.about: The rainbow trout is a species of trout native to cold-water tributaries of the Pacific Ocean in North America and Asia.

oncorhynchus nerka.name: Sockeye salmon
oncorhynchus nerka.desc: A landlocked sockeye that eats plankton. Fish were introduced to the lake, which likely had no native fish.
oncorhynchus nerka.about: The sockeye salmon, also called red salmon, kokanee salmon, blueback salmon, or simply sockeye, is an anadromous species of salmon found in the Northern Pacific Ocean and rivers discharging into it.

oncorhynchus spp..name: Pacific salmon
oncorhynchus spp..desc: Grow at sea, then swim up rivers to spawn and die, bringing ocean nutrients into the forest.
oncorhynchus spp..about: Oncorhynchus is a genus of ray-finned fish in the subfamily Salmoninae of the family Salmonidae, native to coldwater tributaries of the North Pacific basin.

oncorhynchus tshawytscha.name: Chinook salmon
oncorhynchus tshawytscha.desc: Stocked since 1967 to control alewife. Adults eat mostly fish, and the population depends on yearly stocking.
oncorhynchus tshawytscha.about: The Chinook salmon is the largest and most valuable species of Pacific salmon. Its common name is derived from the Chinookan peoples.

oncosiphon pilulifer.name: Common Stinkweed
oncosiphon pilulifer.desc: Common Stinkweed (Oncosiphon pilulifer): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.
oncosiphon pilulifer.about: Oncosiphon pilulifer, also known as globe chamomile and stinknet, is a flowering plant in the daisy family (Asteraceae) native to South Africa and Lesotho.

ondatra zibethicus.name: Muskrat
ondatra zibethicus.desc: Muskrat (Ondatra zibethicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
ondatra zibethicus.about: The muskrat or common muskrat is a medium-sized semiaquatic rodent. Adult muskrats weigh 0.6–2 kg (1+1⁄4–4+1⁄2 lb), with a body length (excluding the tail) of 20–35 cm (8–14 in).

onoclea sensibilis.name: Sensitive fern
onoclea sensibilis.desc: Sensitive fern (Onoclea sensibilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 37 times near the park in GBIF.
onoclea sensibilis.about: Onoclea sensibilis, the sensitive fern, also known as the bead fern, is a coarse-textured, medium to large-sized deciduous perennial fern.

onychognathus frater.name: Socotra starling
onychognathus frater.desc: An island endemic that eats grasshoppers and figs, and the berries of the dragon's blood tree, spreading its seeds.
onychognathus frater.about: The Socotra starling is a species of starling in the family Sturnidae. It is endemic to Socotra island, which is off the southeast coast of Yemen.

onychognathus tristramii.name: Tristram's starling
onychognathus tristramii.desc: The most-recorded bird here. It eats fruit and insects, nests on cliffs, and likely spreads desert plant seeds over long distances.
onychognathus tristramii.about: Tristram's starling, also known as Dead Sea starling or Tristram's grackle, is a species of starling native to the Middle East.

onychomys arenicola.name: Grasshopper mouse
onychomys arenicola.desc: A carnivorous mouse that eats mostly insects and other invertebrates, plus small rodents like pocket mice.
onychomys arenicola.about: Mearns's grasshopper mouse or the Chihuahuan grasshopper mouse is a grasshopper mouse found in southwestern New Mexico, West Texas, and north-central Mexico.

onychomys leucogaster.name: Northern grasshopper mouse
onychomys leucogaster.desc: A small carnivorous mouse that hunts insects such as beetles and sometimes other small rodents.
onychomys leucogaster.about: The northern grasshopper mouse is a North American carnivorous rodent of the family Cricetidae.

onychoprion fuscatus.name: Sooty tern
onychoprion fuscatus.desc: Nests on Bush Key, the only US colony. Picks small fish from the sea surface, often far out over open water.
onychoprion fuscatus.about: The sooty tern is a tern in the family Laridae. It is a seabird of the tropical oceans and can fly for years at a time, skimming the sea surface for food, and returning to land only to breed, on…

opheodrys aestivus.name: Rough Green Snake
opheodrys aestivus.desc: Rough Green Snake (Opheodrys aestivus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
opheodrys aestivus.about: Opheodrys aestivus, commonly known as the rough green snake, is a species of nonvenomous North American snake in the subfamily Colubrinae of the family Colubridae.

ophiophagus hannah.name: King cobra
ophiophagus hannah.desc: Mainly eats other snakes and lizards, and lives in the Himalayan foothills including the Terai.
ophiophagus hannah.about: The king cobra is a species complex of snakes endemic to Asia.

ophisaurus ventralis.name: Eastern glass lizard
ophisaurus ventralis.desc: Eastern glass lizard (Ophisaurus ventralis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

opuntia.name: Prickly pear
opuntia.desc: Cacti like prickly pear store water in dry ground. GloBI records bighorn sheep eating cacti.
opuntia.about: Opuntia, commonly called the prickly pear cactus, is a genus of flowering plants in the cactus family Cactaceae, many known for their flavorful fruit and showy flowers.

opuntia basilaris.name: Woodbury beaver-tail cactus
opuntia basilaris.desc: A flat-padded prickly pear whose fleshy pads store water; bighorn sheep use their horns to break open cactus to eat.
opuntia basilaris.about: Opuntia basilaris, the beavertail cactus or beavertail pricklypear, is a cactus species found in the southwest United States.

opuntia drummondii.name: Cockspur Prickly Pear
opuntia drummondii.desc: Cockspur Prickly Pear (Opuntia drummondii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

opuntia engelmannii.name: Cowtongue cactus
opuntia engelmannii.desc: A pad-forming cactus whose pads and fruit are food for javelinas, rabbits and other desert animals.
opuntia engelmannii.about: Opuntia engelmannii is a prickly pear common across the south-central and Southwestern United States and northern Mexico.

opuntia humifusa.name: Prickly-pear cactus
opuntia humifusa.desc: Prickly-pear cactus (Opuntia humifusa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 114 times near the park in GBIF.
opuntia humifusa.about: Opuntia humifusa, commonly known as the devil's-tongue, eastern prickly pear or Indian fig, is a cactus of the genus Opuntia present in parts of the eastern United States, southeastern Canada, and…

opuntia macrocentra.name: Martin's blunt-spine prickly-pear
opuntia macrocentra.desc: Martin's blunt-spine prickly-pear (Opuntia macrocentra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

opuntia macrorhiza.name: Twistspine Pricklypear
opuntia macrorhiza.desc: Twistspine Pricklypear (Opuntia macrorhiza): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
opuntia macrorhiza.about: Opuntia macrorhiza, also known as the prairie pricklypear, western pricklypear, twistpine pricklypear, or plains pricklypear, is a common, widespread species of cactus native to North America.

opuntia phaeacantha.name: Tulip Pricklypear
opuntia phaeacantha.desc: One of the many cacti of Big Bend. Peccaries rely on prickly pear, and honey bees visit its flowers.
opuntia phaeacantha.about: Opuntia phaeacantha is a species of prickly pear cactus known by the common names brown-spine prickly pear, tulip prickly pear, and desert prickly pear, which is found across the southwestern United…

opuntia polyacantha.name: Cliff prickly-pear
opuntia polyacantha.desc: Cliff prickly-pear (Opuntia polyacantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
opuntia polyacantha.about: Opuntia polyacantha is a common species of cactus known by the common names plains pricklypear, starvation pricklypear, hairspine cactus, and panhandle pricklypear.

opuntia species.name: Prickly pear cactus
opuntia species.desc: Cactus whose pads, flowers and fruit feed tortoises and finches. On some islands it grows tree-like, which keeps its pads out of reach of grazers.
opuntia species.about: Opuntia, commonly called the prickly pear cactus, is a genus of flowering plants in the cactus family Cactaceae, many known for their flavorful fruit and showy flowers.

orcaella brevirostris.name: Irrawaddy dolphin
orcaella brevirostris.desc: A small dolphin of the Sundarbans waterways that hunts fish and shrimp in brackish water.
orcaella brevirostris.about: The Irrawaddy dolphin is a euryhaline species of oceanic dolphin found in scattered subpopulations near sea coasts and in estuaries and rivers in parts of the Bay of Bengal and Southeast Asia.

orcinus orca.name: Orca
orcinus orca.desc: Hunts seals, belugas and walruses as ice retreats and open water spreads.
orcinus orca.about: The orca, or killer whale, is a toothed whale and the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family.

orconectes pellucidus.name: Mammoth Cave crayfish
orconectes pellucidus.desc: An eyeless crayfish of cave streams, named for the park. Cave crayfish generally scavenge leaf litter and detritus washed in from above.
orconectes pellucidus.about: Orconectes pellucidus, the Mammoth Cave crayfish, is a freshwater crayfish native to karst landscapes in Kentucky and Tennessee in the United States.

oreamnos americanus.name: Mountain goat
oreamnos americanus.desc: The park symbol. Eats grasses, herbs, sedges, mosses and lichens high on cliffs and alpine slopes.
oreamnos americanus.about: The mountain goat, also known as the Rocky Mountain goat, is a cloven-footed mammal that is endemic to the remote and rugged mountainous areas of western North America.

oreochromis.name: Tilapia and bream
oreochromis.desc: Cichlid fish that feed on plants and algae. They are a main food of the African fish eagle.
oreochromis.about: Tilapia ( tih-LAH-pee-ə) is the common name for nearly a hundred species of cichlid fish from the coelotilapine, coptodonine, heterotilapine, oreochromine, pelmatolapiine, and tilapiine tribes…

oreochromis niloticus.name: Nile tilapia
oreochromis niloticus.desc: The main fish of Lake Edward fishery. It eats algae and is fed by hippo dung; fish eagles and crocodiles eat it.
oreochromis niloticus.about: The Nile tilapia is a species of tilapia, a cichlid occurring naturally in parts of Africa (such as its namesake Nile River) and the Levant, though numerous introduced populations exist outside its…

oreochromis spp..name: Tilapia
oreochromis spp..desc: River fish that graze algae and feed crocodiles.
oreochromis spp..about: Tilapia ( tih-LAH-pee-ə) is the common name for nearly a hundred species of cichlid fish from the coelotilapine, coptodonine, heterotilapine, oreochromine, pelmatolapiine, and tilapiine tribes…

oreoleuciscus potanini.name: Altai osman and lake fish
oreoleuciscus potanini.desc: A cyprinid fish of Mongolia and Tuva; the Uvs Lake area has about 29 fish species in all, and the osman is the one eaten by people.
oreoleuciscus potanini.about: Oreoleuciscus potanini, the Altai osman, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Leuciscidae, which contains the daces, chubs, true minnows and related species.

oreotragus oreotragus.name: Klipspringer
oreotragus oreotragus.desc: A small antelope of rocky ground, recorded in the park.
oreotragus oreotragus.about: The klipspringer is a small antelope found in eastern and southern Africa.

orestias.name: Orestias killifish
orestias.desc: A genus of pupfish, most of it endemic to Titicaca. Species eat crustaceans, snails, algae, plankton and other fish. Introduced trout and pollution threaten it.
orestias.about: Orestias is a genus of pupfish. Older systematics classified them into the own family Orestiidae.

orgyia pseudotsugata.name: Douglas-fir tussock moth
orgyia pseudotsugata.desc: Douglas-fir tussock moth (Orgyia pseudotsugata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

ornithogalum umbellatum.name: Garden Star-of-Bethlehem
ornithogalum umbellatum.desc: Garden Star-of-Bethlehem (Ornithogalum umbellatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
ornithogalum umbellatum.about: Ornithogalum umbellatum, the garden star-of-Bethlehem, grass lily, nap-at-noon, or eleven-o'clock lady, is a perennial bulbous flowering plant in the asparagus family (Asparagaceae). O.

orographic rain.name: Orographic rain
orographic rain.desc: Moist air rising up the southern slope drops its heaviest rain in the forest belt, while the northern slopes and alpine zone are much drier.

orthetrum sabina.name: Green marsh hawk
orthetrum sabina.desc: A common dragonfly of wetlands that hunts other flying insects, including smaller dragonflies, per GloBI.
orthetrum sabina.about: Orthetrum sabina, the slender skimmer or green marsh hawk, is a species of dragonfly in the family Libellulidae.

orthosia garmani.name: Garman's Quaker
orthosia garmani.desc: Garman's Quaker (Orthosia garmani): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

orthosia rubescens.name: Ruby Quaker
orthosia rubescens.desc: Ruby Quaker (Orthosia rubescens): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

oryctolagus cuniculus.name: European rabbit
oryctolagus cuniculus.desc: Grazes grasses and shoots and is the staple food of the Iberian lynx and Spanish imperial eagle. Disease has cut its numbers badly.
oryctolagus cuniculus.about: The European rabbit or coney is a species of rabbit native to the Iberian Peninsula and southwestern France. It has been introduced to hundreds of locations around the world.

oryx gazella.name: Gemsbok
oryx gazella.desc: A desert antelope that can meet its water needs from wild melons and cucumbers. Lions and hyenas are its natural predators in Africa.
oryx gazella.about: The gemsbok, or South African oryx, is a large antelope in the genus Oryx.

oryx leucoryx.name: Arabian oryx
oryx leucoryx.desc: Mostly a grass eater that follows rains to fresh growth and can go weeks without water. Semi-managed herds live in Qatar.
oryx leucoryx.about: The Arabian oryx or white oryx is a medium-sized antelope with a distinct shoulder bump, long, straight horns, and a tufted tail.

oryza.name: Wild and cultivated rice
oryza.desc: Wild rice and rice paddies cover parts of the floodplain and feed insects, rodents and wading birds.
oryza.about: Oryza is a genus of plants in the grass family. It includes the major food crop rice.

oryza barthii.name: Wild rice & riverbank grasses
oryza barthii.desc: Wild rice and other grasses growing on wet, flooded ground. Hippos graze on grasses.
oryza barthii.about: Oryza barthii, also called Barth's rice, wild rice, or African wild rice, is a grass in the rice genus Oryza. It is an annual, erect to semierect grass.

oryza sativa.name: Rice paddies
oryza sativa.desc: Farmland and paddies along the zone edges. Rice gleanings are an important winter food for red-crowned cranes in East Asia.
oryza sativa.about: Rice is a cereal grain and, in its domesticated form, is the staple food of over half of the world's population, particularly in Africa and Asia.

osmia bucephala.name: Bufflehead Mason Bee
osmia bucephala.desc: Bufflehead Mason Bee (Osmia bucephala): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.

osmia lignaria.name: Blue Orchard Bee
osmia lignaria.desc: Blue Orchard Bee (Osmia lignaria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 45 times near the park in GBIF.
osmia lignaria.about: Osmia lignaria, commonly known as the orchard mason bee or blue orchard bee, is a megachilid bee that makes nests in natural holes and reeds, creating individual cells for its brood that are…

osmunda spectabilis.name: American Royal Fern
osmunda spectabilis.desc: American Royal Fern (Osmunda spectabilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.
osmunda spectabilis.about: Osmunda spectabilis, known as American royal fern, is a species of fern native to a large area of the New World, from the eastern half of Canada and the United States to Argentina.

osmundastrum cinnamomeum.name: Cinnamon Fern
osmundastrum cinnamomeum.desc: Cinnamon Fern (Osmundastrum cinnamomeum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

osphranter rufus.name: Red kangaroo
osphranter rufus.desc: The largest marsupial of the desert, grazing mostly green grasses and forbs and browsing shrubs when food is scarce. It can go long periods without drinking.
osphranter rufus.about: The red kangaroo is the largest of all kangaroos, the largest terrestrial mammal native to Australia, and the largest extant marsupial.

osteolaemus.name: Congo dwarf crocodile
osteolaemus.desc: A small nocturnal crocodile of forest streams and swamps. In the Congo it eats mostly fish, with more crustaceans in the dry season.
osteolaemus.about: Osteolaemus (from Ancient Greek όστεον (ósteon), meaning "bone", and λαιμός (laimós), meaning "throat") is a genus of crocodiles.

osteopilus septentrionalis.name: Cuban tree frog
osteopilus septentrionalis.desc: Big, voracious frog that eats nearly anything it can swallow; knight anoles and various snakes prey on it.
osteopilus septentrionalis.about: The Cuban tree frog is a large species of tree frog that is native to Cuba, the Bahamas, and the Cayman Islands; but has become invasive in several other places around the Americas.

ostrya carpinifolia.name: European hop-hornbeam
ostrya carpinifolia.desc: A deciduous tree recorded in the area that grows with oaks in the lower broadleaf woodland.
ostrya carpinifolia.about: Ostrya carpinifolia, the European hop-hornbeam, is a tree in the family Betulaceae. It is the only species of the genus Ostrya that is native to Europe.

ostrya virginiana.name: American Hop-hornbeam
ostrya virginiana.desc: American Hop-hornbeam (Ostrya virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

otaria byronia.name: South American sea lion
otaria byronia.desc: Eats fish such as anchovies and hake, squid and sometimes penguins. At Valdés orcas beach themselves to grab it near shore.
otaria byronia.about: The South American sea lion, also called the southern sea lion and the Patagonian sea lion, is a sea lion found on the western and southeastern coasts of South America.

otaria flavescens.name: South American sea lion
otaria flavescens.desc: The Islas de Torres hold the region's largest colony. Eats fish and squid and sometimes fur seals.
otaria flavescens.about: The South American sea lion, also called the southern sea lion and the Patagonian sea lion, is a sea lion found on the western and southeastern coasts of South America.

otis tarda.name: Great bustard
otis tarda.desc: Hungary's national bird eats green plants, seeds and insects. Foxes and crows are serious predators of its eggs and chicks.
otis tarda.about: The great bustard is a bird in the bustard family, and the only living member of the genus Otis.

otocolobus manul.name: Pallas's cat
otocolobus manul.desc: A small, stocky wild cat of rocky steppe and desert that hunts pikas and small rodents.
otocolobus manul.about: Pallas's cat, also called manul, is a small wild cat with long and dense light grey fur, and rounded ears set low on the sides of the head.

otospermophilus beecheyi.name: California ground squirrel
otospermophilus beecheyi.desc: Mostly eats seeds, nuts and fruit, plus some insects. Rattlesnakes are its most frequent predators.
otospermophilus beecheyi.about: The California ground squirrel, also known as the Beechey ground squirrel, is a common and easily observed ground squirrel of the western United States and the Baja California Peninsula.

otospermophilus variegatus.name: Rock squirrel
otospermophilus variegatus.desc: Rock squirrel (Otospermophilus variegatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

oulanka river & its floods.name: Oulanka River & its floods
oulanka river & its floods.desc: The river with its rapids and sandy valleys shapes the park, and its banks and alluvial meadows add habitat variety.

outwash sands and volcanic soil.name: Outwash sands and volcanic soil
outwash sands and volcanic soil.desc: Young, nutrient-poor soils of glacial sand and volcanic ash that plants colonise slowly and that dead matter helps enrich.

ovibos moschatus.name: Muskox
ovibos moschatus.desc: Stays on the tundra all year, circling its calves when wolves approach.
ovibos moschatus.about: The muskox is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae. Native to the Arctic, it is noted for its thick coat and for the strong odor emitted by males during the seasonal rut, from which its name derives.

ovis ammon.name: Argali
ovis ammon.desc: The largest wild sheep, grazing grasses, sedges and herbs on open slopes. Wolves and snow leopards prey on it, and golden eagles take lambs.
ovis ammon.about: The argali, also known as the mountain sheep, is the largest species of wild sheep. It is native to the highlands of western East Asia, the Himalayas, Tibet, and the Altai Mountains.

ovis aries.name: Domestic sheep
ovis aries.desc: The main livestock of the summer pastures. Dead animals left on the mountain feed vultures and other scavengers.
ovis aries.about: Sheep (pl.: sheep) or domestic sheep are a domesticated ruminant mammal typically kept as livestock.

ovis canadensis.name: Bighorn sheep
ovis canadensis.desc: A sure-footed grazer of rocky canyon country, listed among Arches' wildlife. Cougars prey on bighorn sheep.
ovis canadensis.about: The bighorn sheep or bighorn is a species of sheep native to North America.

ovis canadensis nelsoni.name: Desert bighorn sheep
ovis canadensis nelsoni.desc: Eats mainly grasses and shifts to other plants and cactus when grass is scarce. It can go long periods without drinking and escapes predators on steep rocky ground.
ovis canadensis nelsoni.about: The desert bighorn sheep is a subspecies of bighorn sheep that is native to the deserts of the United States' Intermountain West and southwestern regions, as well as northwestern Mexico.

ovis canadensis sierrae.name: Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep
ovis canadensis sierrae.desc: An endangered high-country grazer of grasses and forbs that uses steep rocky ground to escape predators. Mountain lions are a major threat.
ovis canadensis sierrae.about: The Sierra Nevada bighorn sheep is subspecies of bighorn sheep unique to the Sierra Nevada mountains of California.

ovis dalli.name: Dall sheep
ovis dalli.desc: Grazes grasses, sedges and willow on steep alpine slopes, using lichens and mosses in winter. Denali was founded in part to protect the sheep.
ovis dalli.about: Dall sheep or thinhorn sheep, is a species of wild sheep native to northwestern North America. O.

ovis gmelini.name: Cyprus mouflon
ovis gmelini.desc: Endangered wild sheep, the national animal of Cyprus, living in the mountains of Paphos District. Eats leaves and grasses.
ovis gmelini.about: The Cyprus mouflon, also known as Cypriot mouflon, is an endangered subspecies of mouflon endemic only to Cyprus in the mountains of Paphos District.

ovis nivicola.name: Snow sheep
ovis nivicola.desc: A wild sheep of Siberian mountains that grazes alpine slopes. Records near the volcanoes are few.
ovis nivicola.about: The snow sheep, or Siberian bighorn sheep, is a species of sheep from the mountainous areas in the northeast of Siberia.

ovis vignei.name: Urial
ovis vignei.desc: A wild sheep native to the Hindu Kush and nearby ranges, found on grassland, open woodland and gentle slopes.
ovis vignei.about: The urial, also known as arkars, shapo, or shapu, is a wild sheep native to Central and South Asia. It is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

ovophis makazayazaya.name: Taiwan mountain pitviper
ovophis makazayazaya.desc: A montane pitviper of southeast Asia and Taiwan. A GloBI record shows it feeding on a Taiwan forest rodent.
ovophis makazayazaya.about: The Taiwan mountain pit viper, also known as the Eastern mountain pit viper or Oriental mountain pit viper, is a venomous snake native to southeast China, northern Vietnam, Laos, and Taiwan.

oxalis articulata.name: Pink-sorrel
oxalis articulata.desc: Pink-sorrel (Oxalis articulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
oxalis articulata.about: Oxalis articulata, known as pink-sorrel, pink wood sorrel, windowbox wood-sorrel, sourgrass, is a perennial species of flowering plant in the genus Oxalis native to Northern Argentina, Southern…

oxalis dillenii.name: Sussex Yellow-sorrel
oxalis dillenii.desc: Sussex Yellow-sorrel (Oxalis dillenii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

oxalis montana.name: Mountain Woodsorrel
oxalis montana.desc: Mountain Woodsorrel (Oxalis montana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
oxalis montana.about: Oxalis montana is a species of flowering plant in the family Oxalidaceae known by the common names mountain woodsorrel, wood shamrock, sours and white woodsorrel.

oxalis oregana.name: Oregon Oxalis
oxalis oregana.desc: Oregon Oxalis (Oxalis oregana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 187 times near the park in GBIF.

oxalis pes-caprae.name: Bermuda-buttercup
oxalis pes-caprae.desc: Bermuda-buttercup (Oxalis pes-caprae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 185 times near the park in GBIF.

oxalis violacea.name: Violet wood-sorrel
oxalis violacea.desc: Violet wood-sorrel (Oxalis violacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
oxalis violacea.about: Oxalis violacea, the violet wood-sorrel, is a perennial plant and herb in the family Oxalidaceae. It is native to the eastern and central United States.

oxydendrum arboreum.name: Sourwood
oxydendrum arboreum.desc: Sourwood (Oxydendrum arboreum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

oxytropis.name: Oxytropis
oxytropis.desc: Cushion-forming legumes of stony alpine ground, well recorded near the park, that give grazers protein-rich forage.
oxytropis.about: Oxytropis is a genus of plants in the legume family. It includes over 600 species native to subarctic to temperate regions of North America and Eurasia.

oxytropis glabra.name: Oxytropis glabra
oxytropis glabra.desc: Oxytropis glabra (Oxytropis glabra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

oxytropis sericea.name: Silky locoweed
oxytropis sericea.desc: Silky locoweed (Oxytropis sericea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.

oxytropis splendens.name: Showy crazyweed
oxytropis splendens.desc: Showy crazyweed (Oxytropis splendens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.
oxytropis splendens.about: Oxytropis splendens, commonly known as showy locoweed, is a flowering perennial in the legume family endemic to the east slope of the Rocky Mountains.

oxytropis, astragalus.name: Milkvetches
oxytropis, astragalus.desc: Many Oxytropis and Astragalus species are recorded in the Nuratau slopes, some of them local endemics. Their leaves and seeds feed herbivores.
oxytropis, astragalus.about: Oxytropis is a genus of plants in the legume family. It includes over 600 species native to subarctic to temperate regions of North America and Eurasia.

oxyura jamaicensis.name: Ruddy Duck
oxyura jamaicensis.desc: Ruddy Duck (Oxyura jamaicensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
oxyura jamaicensis.about: The ruddy duck is a species of duck, one of six extant species of stiff-tailed duck (genus Oxyura).

ozotoceros bezoarticus.name: Pampas deer
ozotoceros bezoarticus.desc: A Near Threatened grassland deer that eats new growth, herbs and shrubs and follows flowering plants. Pumas and jaguars hunt it.
ozotoceros bezoarticus.about: The Pampas deer is a species of deer that live in the grasslands of South America at low elevations. They are known as veado-campeiro in Portuguese and as venado or gama in Spanish.

pachnoda marginata.name: Marginated Congo chafer
pachnoda marginata.desc: A colourful beetle recorded near Nimba. Adults feed on fruit and flowers and are prey for birds and small mammals.
pachnoda marginata.about: Pachnoda marginata is a beetle from the subfamily Cetoniinae with a large number of subspecies that lives in west and central Africa. They are sometimes used as food for terrarium animals.

pachychilon pictum.name: Albanian roach
pachychilon pictum.desc: A small fish of large, nutrient-poor lakes in the Ohrid and Skadar drainages. One of eight endemic cyprinids in Ohrid.
pachychilon pictum.about: Pachychilon pictum, the Albanian roach or Albanian minnow, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Leuciscidae, which includes the daces, Eurasian minnows and related…

pachydactylus rangei.name: Web-footed gecko
pachydactylus rangei.desc: A night-active dune gecko with webbed feet. It eats small arthropods and gets most of its water from dew on plants.
pachydactylus rangei.about: Pachydactylus rangei, the Namib sand gecko or Namib web-footed gecko, is a species of small lizard in the family Gekkonidae.

packera crocata.name: Saffron ragwort
packera crocata.desc: Saffron ragwort (Packera crocata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

packera glabella.name: Cress-leaf groundsel
packera glabella.desc: Cress-leaf groundsel (Packera glabella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
packera glabella.about: Packera glabella is one of several plants with the common name butterweed. P. glabella has also been called cressleaf groundsel and yellowtop.

packera obovata.name: Round-leaf ragwort
packera obovata.desc: Round-leaf ragwort (Packera obovata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

paepalanthus anceps.name: Common bogbuttons
paepalanthus anceps.desc: Common bogbuttons (Paepalanthus anceps): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

pagophilus groenlandicus.name: Harp seal
pagophilus groenlandicus.desc: Harp seal (Pagophilus groenlandicus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

palafoxia sphacelata.name: Othake
palafoxia sphacelata.desc: Othake (Palafoxia sphacelata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

palisota bracteosa.name: Forest floor herbs
palisota bracteosa.desc: Understorey herbs of the shaded forest floor, recorded in the park area. Herbs and ferns are food for ground browsers such as the pygmy hippo.
palisota bracteosa.about: Palisota is a genus of plant in family Commelinaceae, first described in 1828. It is native to sub-Saharan Africa.

palthis asopialis.name: Faint-spotted Palthis
palthis asopialis.desc: Faint-spotted Palthis (Palthis asopialis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

pan paniscus.name: Bonobo
pan paniscus.desc: Mainly a fruit eater and the second-largest fruit eater in the Congo rainforest after elephants. It disperses seeds of many tree species and sometimes hunts duikers.
pan paniscus.about: The bonobo, also historically called the pygmy chimpanzee, is the smallest species of great ape and one of the two making up the genus Pan.

pan troglodytes.name: Chimpanzee
pan troglodytes.desc: Eats mostly fruit, but also fishes for termites with sticks and hunts monkeys and small antelope in groups.
pan troglodytes.about: The chimpanzee, commonly abbreviated to chimp, is a medium-sized great ape species found in the forests and savannas of equatorial Africa. It has four confirmed subspecies and a fifth proposed one.

pan troglodytes verus.name: Western chimpanzee
pan troglodytes verus.desc: Taï chimpanzees crack hard nuts with tools and hunt other primates, including red colobus. The subspecies is Critically Endangered.
pan troglodytes verus.about: The western chimpanzee or West African chimpanzee is a critically endangered subspecies of the common chimpanzee.

panda oleosa.name: Panda nut tree
panda oleosa.desc: A tall forest tree whose oily nuts are among the hardest foods in the forest.
panda oleosa.about: Panda is a plant genus of the family Pandaceae. It contains only one known species, Panda oleosa, native to western and central Africa (Liberia, Ghana, Guinea, Ivory Coast, Nigeria, Cabinda, Gabon,…

pandanus boninensis.name: Bonin screw pine
pandanus boninensis.desc: An endemic screw pine of the island forests and scrub. Its fruit is eaten by the Bonin flying fox.
pandanus boninensis.about: Pandanus is a genus of monocots with about 578 accepted species. They are palm-like, dioecious trees and shrubs native to the Old World tropics and subtropics.

pandanus julianettii.name: Karuka pandanus
pandanus julianettii.desc: A screwpine of montane forest between about 1,300 and 3,300 m. Its nuts are eaten by possums and several rodents, including Rothschild's woolly rat, as well as by people.
pandanus julianettii.about: The karuka is a species of tree in the screwpine family (Pandanaceae) and an important regional food crop in New Guinea.

pandanus tectorius.name: Screw pine
pandanus tectorius.desc: A coastal tree with fruit that flying foxes feed on.
pandanus tectorius.about: Pandanus tectorius is a species of Pandanus (screwpine) that is native to Malesia, Papuasia, eastern Australia, and the Pacific Islands.

pandion haliaetus.name: Osprey
pandion haliaetus.desc: Spends the northern winter fishing Amazon rivers and lakes, then flies north to breed. Ospreys nesting at Yellowstone belong to the same migratory population.
pandion haliaetus.about: The osprey, historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.

panesthia lata.name: Wood-feeding cockroach
panesthia lata.desc: A native cockroach that chews rotting wood and so helps break down dead timber on the forest floor.
panesthia lata.about: Panesthia is a large genus of burrowing giant cockroaches in the subfamily Panesthiinae.

pangasianodon gigas.name: Mekong giant catfish
pangasianodon gigas.desc: One of the largest freshwater fish; after its first year it mostly feeds on algae. Found in the Tonlé Sap, but now rare.
pangasianodon gigas.about: The Mekong giant catfish is a large species of catfish (order Siluriformes) in the shark catfish family (Pangasiidae), native to the Mekong basin in Southeast Asia and adjacent China.

panicum amarum.name: Bitter panicgrass
panicum amarum.desc: Bitter panicgrass (Panicum amarum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
panicum amarum.about: Panicum amarum is a species of grass known by the common name bitter panicum.

panicum coloratum.name: Klein grass
panicum coloratum.desc: A tufted grass recorded around the park. GloBI records list it as food of buffalo, waterbuck and zebra.
panicum coloratum.about: Panicum coloratum is a species of grass known by the common names kleingrass, blue panicgrass (USA), white buffalograss (southern Africa); Bambatsi panic, makarikari grass, and coolah grass…

panicum dichotomiflorum.name: Autumn Millet
panicum dichotomiflorum.desc: Autumn Millet (Panicum dichotomiflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

panicum repens.name: Torpedo grass
panicum repens.desc: A tough grass of wet margins and floodplains, among the most often recorded plants here and grazed by hippos and lechwe.
panicum repens.about: Panicum repens is a species of grass known by many common names, including torpedo grass, creeping panic, panic rampant, couch panicum, wainaku grass, quack grass, dog-tooth grass, and bullet grass.

panicum turgidum.name: Desert panic grass
panicum turgidum.desc: Tough perennial desert grass listed among the plants of Djibouti's wadis and lowlands.
panicum turgidum.about: Panicum turgidum is an old world clumping desert bunchgrass of the genus Panicum. It is a plant of arid regions across Africa and Asia, and has been introduced to other parts of the world.

panicum virgatum.name: Old Switch Panic Grass
panicum virgatum.desc: A tall native bunchgrass that grows with big bluestem and helps make up the dense tallgrass cover.
panicum virgatum.about: Panicum virgatum, commonly known as switchgrass and panic grass, is a perennial warm season bunchgrass native to North America, where it occurs naturally from 55°N latitude in Canada southwards into…

panthea virginarius.name: Cascades Panthea Moth
panthea virginarius.desc: Cascades Panthea Moth (Panthea virginarius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

panthera leo.name: Lion
panthera leo.desc: Lions on the Skeleton Coast prey on seals and shorebirds. Inland they also hunt oryx and springbok.
panthera leo.about: The lion is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

panthera onca.name: Jaguar
panthera onca.desc: Hunts capybaras, tapirs, sloths and caimans, with a bite strong enough to crush skulls and shells.
panthera onca.about: The jaguar is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.

panthera pardus.name: Leopard
panthera pardus.desc: The main natural predator of okapi and a hunter of duikers and monkeys in the forest.
panthera pardus.about: The leopard is one of the five extant cat species in the genus Panthera. It has a pale yellowish to dark golden fur with dark spots grouped in rosettes.

panthera pardus pardus.name: African leopard
panthera pardus pardus.desc: The main large predator of the forest, taking monkeys, hyraxes and small antelope.
panthera pardus pardus.about: The African leopard is the nominate subspecies of the leopard, native to Africa.

panthera pardus tulliana.name: Persian leopard
panthera pardus tulliana.desc: A big cat of the Caucasus mountains and a predator of wild goats and boar.
panthera pardus tulliana.about: Panthera pardus tulliana, also called the Persian leopard, Anatolian leopard and Caucasian leopard in different parts of its range, is a leopard subspecies native to the Iranian Plateau and the…

panthera tigris.name: Tiger
panthera tigris.desc: The top predator of the park. Hunts deer and wild boar, and also takes sloth bears and leopards.
panthera tigris.about: The tiger is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia.

panthera tigris altaica.name: Amur tiger
panthera tigris altaica.desc: Preys mainly on wapiti, wild boar, sika and roe deer. Tigers also suppress wolves, which are scarce in tiger forests.
panthera tigris altaica.about: The Siberian tiger or Amur tiger is a population of the tiger subspecies Panthera tigris tigris native to Northeast China, the Russian Far East, and possibly North Korea.

panthera tigris tigris.name: Bengal tiger
panthera tigris tigris.desc: The only tigers living in mangroves. They swim between islands and eat deer, boar, fish, crabs and monitors.
panthera tigris tigris.about: The Bengal tiger is a population of the Panthera tigris tigris subspecies. It ranks among the largest of wild cats.

panthera uncia.name: Snow leopard
panthera uncia.desc: Himalayan apex predator that lives above about 3,500 m. Blue sheep are its core prey, with tahr, musk deer and marmots also taken.
panthera uncia.about: The snow leopard is a felid species in the genus Panthera. It has a thick whitish to grey fur with black spots on the head and neck, with larger rosettes on the back, flanks and bushy tail.

pantherophis alleghaniensis.name: Eastern Rat Snake
pantherophis alleghaniensis.desc: Eastern Rat Snake (Pantherophis alleghaniensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
pantherophis alleghaniensis.about: The central ratsnake, also commonly known as the black ratsnake, chicken snake, gray ratsnake, midland ratsnake, and pilot black snake, is a species of nonvenomous snake in the subfamily Colubrinae…

pantherophis obsoletus.name: Black Rat Snake
pantherophis obsoletus.desc: Black Rat Snake (Pantherophis obsoletus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
pantherophis obsoletus.about: Pantherophis obsoletus, also known commonly as the western rat snake, black rat snake, pilot black snake, or simply black snake, is a nonvenomous species of snake in the family Colubridae.

pantherophis vulpinus.name: Eastern Fox Snake
pantherophis vulpinus.desc: Eastern Fox Snake (Pantherophis vulpinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
pantherophis vulpinus.about: Pantherophis vulpinus, commonly known as the foxsnake or the eastern fox snake, is a species of nonvenomous rat snake in the family Colubridae. The species is native to North America.

panulirus.name: Spiny lobsters
panulirus.desc: Crustaceans listed in the bay, which eat molluscs and other bottom animals and hide in rocky crevices.
panulirus.about: Spiny lobsters, also known as langustas, langoustes, or rock lobsters are marine decapod crustaceans belonging to the family Palinuridae.

panulirus argus.name: Caribbean spiny lobster
panulirus argus.desc: Young settle in seagrass and mangrove roots, adults shelter in reef holes. Eats snails, clams, urchins and carrion.
panulirus argus.about: Panulirus argus, the Caribbean spiny lobster, is a species of spiny lobster that lives on reefs and in mangrove swamps in the western Atlantic Ocean.

papilio.name: Swallowtail butterflies
papilio.desc: Forest butterflies such as the flying handkerchief swallowtail. They feed on flowers like lantana.
papilio.about: Papilio dardanus, the Saharan swallowtail, African swallowtail, mocker swallowtail or flying handkerchief, is a species of butterfly in the family Papilionidae (the swallowtails).

papilio canadensis.name: Canadian tiger swallowtail
papilio canadensis.desc: A northern butterfly whose caterpillars feed on aspen and other broadleaf trees.
papilio canadensis.about: Papilio canadensis, the Canadian tiger swallowtail, is a species of butterfly in the family Papilionidae. It was once classified as a subspecies of Papilio glaucus.

papilio cresphontes.name: Giant Swallowtail
papilio cresphontes.desc: Giant Swallowtail (Papilio cresphontes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio cresphontes.about: The eastern giant swallowtail is the largest butterfly in North America.

papilio eurymedon.name: Pale Swallowtail
papilio eurymedon.desc: Pale Swallowtail (Papilio eurymedon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio eurymedon.about: Papilio eurymedon, the pale swallowtail or pallid swallowtail, is a relatively common swallowtail butterfly found throughout much of the western North America.

papilio glaucus.name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail
papilio glaucus.desc: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail (Papilio glaucus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio glaucus.about: Papilio glaucus, the eastern tiger swallowtail, is a species of butterfly native to eastern North America.

papilio homerus.name: Homerus swallowtail
papilio homerus.desc: The largest butterfly in the Western Hemisphere. Adults sip nectar and females lay eggs on Ocotea. Blue and John Crow Mountains hold one of its two last populations.
papilio homerus.about: Papilio homerus, commonly known as the Homerus swallowtail or Jamaican swallowtail, is the largest butterfly species in the Western Hemisphere.

papilio machaon.name: Old World swallowtail
papilio machaon.desc: Old World Swallowtail (Papilio machaon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 23 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio machaon.about: Papilio machaon, the Old World swallowtail, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.

papilio multicaudata.name: Two-tailed Swallowtail
papilio multicaudata.desc: Two-tailed Swallowtail (Papilio multicaudata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio palamedes.name: Palamedes Swallowtail
papilio palamedes.desc: A large butterfly of southeastern swamps whose caterpillars feed on bay trees such as swamp bay.
papilio palamedes.about: Papilio palamedes, the Palamedes swallowtail or laurel swallowtail, is a North American butterfly in the family Papilionidae.

papilio polyxenes.name: American Swallowtail
papilio polyxenes.desc: American Swallowtail (Papilio polyxenes): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio polyxenes.about: Papilio polyxenes, the (eastern) black swallowtail, American swallowtail or parsnip swallowtail, is a butterfly found throughout much of North America.

papilio rutulus.name: Western Tiger Swallowtail
papilio rutulus.desc: Western Tiger Swallowtail (Papilio rutulus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

papilio troilus.name: Spicebush Swallowtail
papilio troilus.desc: Spicebush Swallowtail (Papilio troilus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio troilus.about: Papilio troilus, the spicebush swallowtail or green-clouded butterfly, is a common black swallowtail butterfly found in North America.

papilio ulysses.name: Ulysses butterfly
papilio ulysses.desc: Caterpillars eat leaves of doughwood and similar trees, and adults feed on its blossoms.
papilio ulysses.about: Papilio ulysses, the Ulysses butterfly, is a large swallowtail butterfly, in the subgenus Achillides, of Australia, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands.

papilio zelicaon.name: Anise Swallowtail
papilio zelicaon.desc: Anise Swallowtail (Papilio zelicaon): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 86 times near the park in GBIF.
papilio zelicaon.about: Papilio zelicaon, the Anise Swallowtail, is a common swallowtail butterfly of western North America.

papio anubis.name: Olive baboon
papio anubis.desc: An omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, leaves and grass. It forages on the ground and sleeps in trees.
papio anubis.about: The olive baboon, also called the Anubis baboon, is a member of the family Cercopithecidae Old World monkeys.

papio cynocephalus.name: Yellow baboon
papio cynocephalus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore of the park that eats fruit and seeds, including baobab.
papio cynocephalus.about: The yellow baboon is a baboon in the family of Old World monkeys. The species epithet means "dog-head" in Greek, due to the dog-like shape of the muzzle and head.

papio hamadryas.name: Hamadryas baboon
papio hamadryas.desc: Omnivore eating grasses, seeds, fruit, acacia leaves, insects and small animals. Depends on a few permanent waterholes in the dry season.
papio hamadryas.about: The hamadryas baboon is a species of baboon within the Old World monkey family.

papio papio.name: Guinea baboon
papio papio.desc: An opportunistic omnivore that eats fruit, roots, seeds, leaves and some small animals. Chimpanzees have been seen preying on it in Senegal.
papio papio.about: The Guinea baboon is a baboon from the Old World monkey family. Some (older) classifications list only two species in the genus Papio, this one and the hamadryas baboon.

papio ursinus.name: Chacma baboon
papio ursinus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore eating fruit, seeds, bulbs, insects and more. At Cape Point it also takes shellfish.
papio ursinus.about: The chacma baboon, also known as the Cape baboon, is, like all other baboons, from the Old World monkey family. It is one of the largest of all monkeys.

parabuteo unicinctus.name: Harris's hawk
