parabuteo unicinctus.desc: Hunts in family groups, which lets it take jackrabbits, plus ground squirrels, kangaroo rats and quail.
parabuteo unicinctus.about: Parabuteo unicinctus is a medium-large bird of prey that breeds from the southwestern United States south to Chile, central Argentina, and Brazil. It contains two subspecies, the Harris's hawk (P. u.

paradejeania rutilioides.name: Spiny Tachina Fly
paradejeania rutilioides.desc: Spiny Tachina Fly (Paradejeania rutilioides): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

paradisaea raggiana.name: Raggiana bird-of-paradise
paradisaea raggiana.desc: The national bird of Papua New Guinea. It eats mainly fruit and arthropods and is an important seed disperser for some New Guinea trees.
paradisaea raggiana.about: The Raggiana bird-of-paradise, also known as Count Raggi's bird-of-paradise, is a large bird in the bird-of-paradise family Paradisaeidae.

paradoxurus hermaphroditus.name: Asian palm civet
paradoxurus hermaphroditus.desc: An omnivorous nocturnal civet that eats fruit as well as small animals such as rats.
paradoxurus hermaphroditus.about: The Asian palm civet, also called common palm civet, toddy cat and musang, is a viverrid native to South and Southeast Asia.

parahyaena brunnea.name: Brown hyena
parahyaena brunnea.desc: Mostly a scavenger that lives near seal colonies on the Namib coast. It eats seal pups and often steals kills from jackals.
parahyaena brunnea.about: The brown hyena, also called the strandwolf, is a species of hyena found in Namibia, Botswana, western and southern Zimbabwe, southern Mozambique, western Eswatini, and South Africa.

paralaudakia himalayana.name: Himalayan agama
paralaudakia himalayana.desc: A rock-dwelling lizard recorded near the park that feeds mostly on insects.
paralaudakia himalayana.about: The Himalayan agama is an agamid lizard found in Central Asia and South Asia.

paranapiacaba tricincta.name: Checkered Melon Beetle
paranapiacaba tricincta.desc: Checkered Melon Beetle (Paranapiacaba tricincta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
paranapiacaba tricincta.about: Paranapiacaba tricincta, the checkered melon beetle, is a species of skeletonizing leaf beetle or flea beetle in the family Chrysomelidae. It is found in Central America and North America.

parastacoides tasmanicus.name: Burrowing crayfish
parastacoides tasmanicus.desc: Lives in burrows on moorland and eats buttongrass rhizomes; its burrows aerate the peat.

parietaria pensylvanica.name: Pennsylvania pellitory
parietaria pensylvanica.desc: Pennsylvania pellitory (Parietaria pensylvanica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

parinari excelsa.name: Guinea plum
parinari excelsa.desc: A large evergreen tree that gives its name to the mossy Parinari forests on Nimba. Its fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and other animals.
parinari excelsa.about: Parinari excelsa, the Guinea plum, is a species of large, evergreen tree in the family Chrysobalanaceae. It has a very wide distribution in tropical Africa and the Americas.

park & garden soil.name: Park & garden soil
park & garden soil.desc: The soil beneath parks, yards and gardens holds the nutrients plants use.

parkinsonia microphylla.name: Foothill palo verde
parkinsonia microphylla.desc: A green-barked desert tree that acts as a nurse plant, shading young saguaros and softening temperature extremes around them.
parkinsonia microphylla.about: Parkinsonia microphylla, the yellow paloverde, foothill paloverde or little-leaved palo verde; syn. Cercidium microphyllum), is a species of palo verde.

parnassia grandifolia.name: Largeleaf grass of Parnassus
parnassia grandifolia.desc: Largeleaf grass of Parnassus (Parnassia grandifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.
parnassia grandifolia.about: Parnassia grandifolia, also known as bigleaf grass of Parnassus, is a flowering herbaceous plant of the family Celastraceae.

parnassius apollo.name: Apollo butterfly
parnassius apollo.desc: A large, white alpine butterfly. Its caterpillars feed on stonecrops of rocky meadows.
parnassius apollo.about: The Apollo, also called the mountain Apollo, is a butterfly of the family Papilionidae.

parnassius smintheus.name: Mountain Parnassian
parnassius smintheus.desc: Mountain Parnassian (Parnassius smintheus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 439 times near the park in GBIF.
parnassius smintheus.about: Parnassius smintheus, the Rocky Mountain parnassian or Rocky Mountain apollo, is a high-altitude butterfly found in the Rocky Mountains throughout the United States and Canada.

paronychia sessiliflora.name: Low nailwort
paronychia sessiliflora.desc: Low nailwort (Paronychia sessiliflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
paronychia sessiliflora.about: Paronychia sessiliflora, the creeping nailwort, is a plant in the family Cayophyllaceae known from arid and semi arid environments in North America other common names include low nailwort.

parthenium integrifolium.name: American feverfew
parthenium integrifolium.desc: American feverfew (Parthenium integrifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
parthenium integrifolium.about: Parthenium integrifolium is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names wild quinine, common wild quinine, American feverfew, and eastern feverfew.

parthenocissus quinquefolia.name: Virginia-creeper
parthenocissus quinquefolia.desc: Virginia-creeper (Parthenocissus quinquefolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
parthenocissus quinquefolia.about: Parthenocissus quinquefolia, commonly known as Virginia creeper, woodbine, five-leaved ivy, or five-finger, is a species of flowering vine in the grape family Vitaceae.

parus major.name: Great tit
parus major.desc: A small woodland bird that eats seeds, fruit and insects, and is prey for hawks and woodpeckers.
parus major.about: The great tit is a small passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It is widespread and common throughout Europe, the Middle East, Central Asia and as far east as the Amur River.

pascopyrum smithii.name: Western wheatgrass
pascopyrum smithii.desc: A sod-forming perennial grass and South Dakota's state grass. Bison and prairie dogs eat it.
pascopyrum smithii.about: Pascopyrum is a monotypic genus of grass containing the sole species Pascopyrum smithii, which is known by the common names western wheatgrass and red-joint wheatgrass, after the red coloration of…

paspalum.name: Paspalum grasses
paspalum.desc: Warm-season grasses recorded often around the wetland. Grasses make up the largest share of the marsh deer diet, and grassland here evolved with fire.
paspalum.about: Paspalum is a genus of plants in the grass family. The group is widespread across much of Asia, Africa, Australia, and the Americas.

passer ammodendri.name: Saxaul sparrow
passer ammodendri.desc: A small sparrow tied to saxaul and desert shrubs that eats seeds and some insects. Prey for shrikes, owls and snakes.
passer ammodendri.about: The saxaul sparrow is a passerine bird of the sparrow family (Passeridae), found in parts of Central Asia.

passer domesticus.name: House Sparrow
passer domesticus.desc: House Sparrow (Passer domesticus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 63 times near the park in GBIF.
passer domesticus.about: The house sparrow is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz).

passer montanus.name: Eurasian tree sparrow
passer montanus.desc: Small seed- and fruit-eating bird of villages and shrub thickets around the lake.
passer montanus.about: The tree sparrow is a passerine bird in the sparrow family with a rich chestnut crown and nape and a black patch on each pure white cheek.

passerculus sandwichensis.name: Savannah Sparrow
passerculus sandwichensis.desc: Savannah Sparrow (Passerculus sandwichensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.

passerina ciris.name: Painted Bunting
passerina ciris.desc: Painted Bunting (Passerina ciris): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 578 times near the park in GBIF.
passerina ciris.about: The painted bunting is a species of bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. It is native to North America.

passerina cyanea.name: Indigo Bunting
passerina cyanea.desc: Indigo Bunting (Passerina cyanea): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 257 times near the park in GBIF.
passerina cyanea.about: The indigo bunting is a small seed-eating bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae.

passiflora aurantia.name: Orange passion flower
passiflora aurantia.desc: A passion-flower vine. GloBI records the eastern red lacewing butterfly feeding on it.
passiflora aurantia.about: Passiflora aurantia, the orange-petaled passion flower, is a species in the family Passifloraceae which produces edible but not particularly palatable fruit.

passiflora incarnata.name: Purple Passionflower
passiflora incarnata.desc: Purple passionflower (Passiflora incarnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.
passiflora incarnata.about: Passiflora incarnata, commonly known as maypop, purple passionflower, true passionflower, wild apricot, and wild passion vine, is a fast-growing perennial vine with climbing or trailing stems.

pastinaca sativa.name: Wild Parsnip
pastinaca sativa.desc: Wild Parsnip (Pastinaca sativa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.
pastinaca sativa.about: The parsnip is a root vegetable closely related to carrot and parsley, all belonging to the flowering plant family Apiaceae. It is a biennial plant usually grown as an annual.

patagioenas caribaea.name: Ring-tailed pigeon
patagioenas caribaea.desc: An endemic forest pigeon of Jamaica that feeds mostly on fruit and was among the most recorded birds near the park.
patagioenas caribaea.about: The ring-tailed pigeon is a species of bird in the family Columbidae. It is endemic to Jamaica.

patagioenas leucocephala.name: White-crowned pigeon
patagioenas leucocephala.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon, one of the best-recorded birds near the park. GloBI records link it to pigeon berry fruit.
patagioenas leucocephala.about: The white-crowned pigeon is a fruit and seed-eating species of bird in the dove and pigeon family Columbidae. It is found primarily in the Caribbean.

patagioenas squamosa.name: Scaly-naped pigeon
patagioenas squamosa.desc: A fruit-eating pigeon, with GloBI records of it eating pumpwood, lira vine and sierra palm fruit.
patagioenas squamosa.about: The scaly-naped pigeon, also known as the red-necked pigeon, is a bird belonging to the family Columbidae. The species occurs throughout the Caribbean.

patch-burn fire.name: Patch-burn fire
patch-burn fire.desc: The preserve burns roughly a third of the prairie each year. Fire keeps brush out and draws bison to fresh regrowth.

paulownia tomentosa.name: Foxglove-tree
paulownia tomentosa.desc: Foxglove-tree (Paulownia tomentosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.
paulownia tomentosa.about: Paulownia tomentosa, common names princess tree, empress tree, or foxglove-tree, is a deciduous hardwood tree in the family Paulowniaceae, native to central and eastern China and the Korean…

peace-athabasca delta floods.name: Peace-Athabasca Delta floods
peace-athabasca delta floods.desc: The inland delta of the Peace, Athabasca and Birch rivers; its water feeds the park's wetlands and meadows.

peat.name: Peat
peat.desc: Waterlogged, acid ground made of slowly decaying moss. Wikipedia says the High Fens bogs are over 10,000 years old.

peat and poor soils.name: Peat and poor soils
peat and poor soils.desc: Bogs on the coast are rich in peat, and the ultramafic Tablelands have stony, nutrient-poor soil. Plant growth is limited by what the ground supplies.

peat bogs and streams.name: Peat bogs and streams
peat bogs and streams.desc: The Bohemian Forest holds peat bogs and sources of rivers such as the Vltava, Otava and Uhlava, which keep soils wet.

peat soil.name: Peat soil
peat soil.desc: Slowly built organic soil in which marsh plants root.

peatland soil.name: Peatland soil
peatland soil.desc: Waterlogged swamp soils in the central basin store about 30 petagrams of carbon, roughly as much as all basin forests.

peaty acid soil.name: Peaty acid soil
peaty acid soil.desc: Cool, wet ground builds acidic peat soils under much of the moorland and bog, favouring heather and cottongrass.

pecari tajacu.name: Collared peccary
pecari tajacu.desc: Also called javelina. Its main foods are agaves and prickly pears, and its predators include cougars and coyotes.
pecari tajacu.about: The collared peccary is a peccary, a species of artiodactyl (even-toed) mammal in the family Tayassuidae. It is the only extant member of the genus Dicotyles.

pedicularis canadensis.name: Common lousewort
pedicularis canadensis.desc: Common lousewort (Pedicularis canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
pedicularis canadensis.about: Pedicularis canadensis, commonly called Canadian lousewort or wood betony, is a flowering plant in the family Orobanchaceae.

pedicularis centranthera.name: Dwarf lousewort
pedicularis centranthera.desc: Dwarf lousewort (Pedicularis centranthera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

pedicularis groenlandica.name: Pink-elephants
pedicularis groenlandica.desc: Pink-elephants (Pedicularis groenlandica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 107 times near the park in GBIF.
pedicularis groenlandica.about: Pedicularis groenlandica is a showy flowering plant in the family Orobanchaceae commonly known as elephant's head, little pink elephant, elephantella, or similar common names inspired by the…

pedicularis lanceolata.name: Swamp lousewort
pedicularis lanceolata.desc: Swamp lousewort (Pedicularis lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

pediocactus knowltonii.name: Knowlton's cactus
pediocactus knowltonii.desc: Knowlton's cactus (Pediocactus knowltonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

pediocactus simpsonii.name: Plains cactus
pediocactus simpsonii.desc: Ball Cactus (Pediocactus simpsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.
pediocactus simpsonii.about: Pediocactus simpsonii, known by the common names mountain cactus, snowball cactus, and mountain ball cactus, is a relatively common cactus that has adapted to survive in cold and dry environments in…

pediomelum argophyllum.name: Silverleaf Indian breadroot
pediomelum argophyllum.desc: Silverleaf Indian breadroot (Pediomelum argophyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
pediomelum argophyllum.about: Pediomelum argophyllum, synonym Psoralea argophylla, is a species of legume in the family Fabaceae.

pediomelum subacaule.name: Whiterim scurfpea
pediomelum subacaule.desc: Whiterim scurfpea (Pediomelum subacaule): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 101 times near the park in GBIF.

pekania pennanti.name: Fisher
pekania pennanti.desc: A generalist hunter whose main prey are snowshoe hares and porcupines. It also eats small mammals and carrion.
pekania pennanti.about: The fisher is a carnivorous mammal native to North America, a forest-dwelling creature whose range covers much of the boreal forest in Canada to the northern United States.

pelea capreolus.name: Grey rhebok
pelea capreolus.desc: A woolly-coated antelope of grassy highlands, a browser that gets much of its water from its food.
pelea capreolus.about: The grey rhebok, locally known as the vaalribbok in Afrikaans, is a species of antelope native to South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini. The specific name capreolus is Latin for 'little goat'.

pelecanus crispus.name: Dalmatian pelican
pelecanus crispus.desc: Nests on islands or in dense reeds in the delta. It swallows fish whole, including carp and pike.
pelecanus crispus.about: The Dalmatian pelican, also known as the curly-headed pelican, is the largest member of the pelican family and among the heaviest flying birds in the world.

pelecanus erythrorhynchos.name: American white pelican
pelecanus erythrorhynchos.desc: A winter visitor to Gulf bays and estuaries. Nests on lakes in the interior and also follows the Mississippi River in winter.
pelecanus erythrorhynchos.about: The American white pelican is a large aquatic soaring bird from the order Pelecaniformes. It breeds in interior North America, moving south and to the coasts, as far as Costa Rica, in winter.

pelecanus occidentalis.name: Brown pelican
pelecanus occidentalis.desc: A diving seabird that hunts schooling fish over the bay.
pelecanus occidentalis.about: The brown pelican is a bird of the pelican family, Pelecanidae, one of three species found in the Americas and one of two that feed by diving into water.

pelecanus onocrotalus.name: Great white pelican
pelecanus onocrotalus.desc: Large fish-eating bird that breeds on the site's islands and fishes in the shallows.
pelecanus onocrotalus.about: The great white pelican, also known as the eastern white pelican (in contrast to the western pelican of the Americas), rosy pelican or simply white pelican, is a bird in the pelican family.

pelecanus rufescens.name: Pink-backed pelican
pelecanus rufescens.desc: The most recorded bird near the islands. It scoops fish from shallow waters.
pelecanus rufescens.about: The pink-backed pelican is a bird of the pelican family. It is a resident breeder in the swamps and shallow lakes of Africa and southern Arabia; it has also been extirpated from Madagascar.

pelecyphora tuberculosa.name: Pelecyphora tuberculosa
pelecyphora tuberculosa.desc: Pelecyphora tuberculosa (Pelecyphora tuberculosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
pelecyphora tuberculosa.about: Pelecyphora tuberculosa, the corncob cactus, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cactaceae, native to the south-central United States, and northern Mexico.

pelecyphora vivipara.name: Pincushion cactus
pelecyphora vivipara.desc: Pincushion cactus (Pelecyphora vivipara): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
pelecyphora vivipara.about: Pelecyphora vivipara is a species of cactus known by several common names, including spinystar, viviparous foxtail cactus, pincushion cactus and ball cactus.

pellaea atropurpurea.name: Purple cliffbrake
pellaea atropurpurea.desc: Purple cliffbrake (Pellaea atropurpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
pellaea atropurpurea.about: Pellaea atropurpurea, commonly known as purple-stem cliffbrake or just purple cliffbrake, is a fern native to North and Central America. Brake is an old word for fern, related to the word bracken.

pellaea glabella.name: Dwarf cliffbrake
pellaea glabella.desc: Dwarf cliffbrake (Pellaea glabella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
pellaea glabella.about: Pellaea glabella is a fern with the common name smooth cliffbrake. It was once regarded as a reduced form or variety of Pellaea atropurpurea.

pelophylax ridibundus.name: Marsh frog
pelophylax ridibundus.desc: A large water frog of ponds and channels that eats insects; it is prey for herons, ibises, harriers and foxes in GloBI records.
pelophylax ridibundus.about: The marsh frog is a species of frog in the family Ranidae. It is native to continental Europe and parts of western Asia, where it inhabits bodies of water from puddles and ponds to lakes and rivers,…

pemphis acidula.name: Pemphis scrub
pemphis acidula.desc: Dense shrub that covers much of the higher, rocky ground of the atoll.
pemphis acidula.about: Pemphis acidula, commonly known as bantigue (pron. bahn-TEE-geh) or mentigi, is a species of flowering plant in the family Lythraceae.

penaeus and relatives.name: Shrimp
penaeus and relatives.desc: Young shrimp shelter among mangrove roots, and the forest supports commercial shrimp and crab catches.
penaeus and relatives.about: Penaeus monodon, commonly known as the giant tiger prawn, Asian tiger shrimp, black tiger shrimp, and other names, is a marine crustacean that is widely reared for food.

penaeus latisulcatus.name: Western king prawn
penaeus latisulcatus.desc: Bottom-dwelling prawn of sandy seabeds that makes up much of the catch of the Shark Bay prawn fishery. A food item for many fish.
penaeus latisulcatus.about: The western king prawn is an edible dendrobranch prawn endemic to western and southern Australia.

penaeus semisulcatus.name: Green tiger prawn
penaeus semisulcatus.desc: A prawn of sandy and muddy coastal waters whose juveniles favour estuaries; a commercially important species in the region.
penaeus semisulcatus.about: Penaeus semisulcatus, the green tiger prawn or grooved tiger prawn, is a commercially important species of prawn in the genus Penaeus.

penstemon angustifolius.name: Broadbeard beardtongue
penstemon angustifolius.desc: Broadbeard beardtongue (Penstemon angustifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon angustifolius.about: Penstemon angustifolius is a perennial semi-evergreen forb belonging to the plantain family. This species is 1 out of roughly 273 species of Penstemon.

penstemon barbatus.name: Beardlip penstemon
penstemon barbatus.desc: Beardlip penstemon (Penstemon barbatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon cobaea.name: Cobaea beardtongue
penstemon cobaea.desc: Cobaea beardtongue (Penstemon cobaea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon cobaea.about: Penstemon cobaea is a flowering plant in the plantain family, commonly known as Cobaea beardtongue, prairie penstemon or foxglove penstemon.

penstemon confertus.name: Lesser yellow beardtongue
penstemon confertus.desc: Lesser yellow beardtongue (Penstemon confertus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon confertus.about: Penstemon confertus is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family; its common name is the Yellow beardtoungue.

penstemon cyananthus.name: Wasatch penstemon
penstemon cyananthus.desc: Wasatch penstemon (Penstemon cyananthus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon cyananthus.about: Penstemon cyananthus, commonly the Wasatch penstemon, is a species in the veronica family from the northern United States in the Rocky Mountains.

penstemon cyanocaulis.name: Bluestem penstemon
penstemon cyanocaulis.desc: Bluestem penstemon (Penstemon cyanocaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 93 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon cyanocaulis.about: Penstemon cyanocaulis, the bluestem penstemon or bluestem beardtongue, is a perennial plant in the plantain family (Plantaginaceae) found in the Colorado Plateau and Canyonlands region of the…

penstemon deaveri.name: Mt. Graham beardtongue
penstemon deaveri.desc: Mt. Graham beardtongue (Penstemon deaveri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon deaveri.about: Penstemon deaveri, also known as Mount Graham penstemon and Deaver's Penstemon, is a penstemon species from the mountains of Arizona and New Mexico in the Southwestern United States.

penstemon deustus.name: Scabland penstemon
penstemon deustus.desc: Scabland penstemon (Penstemon deustus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 123 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon deustus.about: Penstemon deustus is a species of penstemon known by the common names hotrock penstemon and scabland penstemon.

penstemon eatonii.name: Eaton's penstemon
penstemon eatonii.desc: Eaton's penstemon (Penstemon eatonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon eatonii.about: Penstemon eatonii is a species of flowering plant in the genus Penstemon, known by the common name firecracker penstemon.

penstemon eriantherus.name: Fuzzytongue penstemon
penstemon eriantherus.desc: Fuzzytongue penstemon (Penstemon eriantherus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon eriantherus.about: Penstemon eriantherus is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family known by the common names fuzzytongue penstemon and crested penstemon.

penstemon fruticosus.name: Bush penstemon
penstemon fruticosus.desc: Bush penstemon (Penstemon fruticosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon fruticosus.about: Penstemon fruticosus, the bush penstemon or shrubby penstemon, is a species of penstemon native to the Pacific Northwest of North America.

penstemon palmeri.name: Palmer penstemon
penstemon palmeri.desc: Palmer penstemon (Penstemon palmeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon pseudospectabilis.name: Desert penstemon
penstemon pseudospectabilis.desc: Desert penstemon (Penstemon pseudospectabilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon pseudospectabilis.about: Penstemon pseudospectabilis a species of penstemon. It's native to the southwestern United States, where it grows in desert and plateau habitat types, such as sandy washes, scrub, and woodland.

penstemon purpusii.name: Snow Mountain beardtongue
penstemon purpusii.desc: Snow Mountain beardtongue (Penstemon purpusii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon purpusii.about: Penstemon purpusii is an uncommon species of penstemon known by the common name Snow Mountain beardtongue.

penstemon richardsonii.name: Richardson's beardtongue
penstemon richardsonii.desc: Richardson's beardtongue (Penstemon richardsonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon richardsonii.about: Penstemon richardsonii is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family; its common name is cutleaf beardtongue or Richardson's beardtongue.

penstemon secundiflorus.name: Sidebells penstemon
penstemon secundiflorus.desc: Sidebells penstemon (Penstemon secundiflorus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 96 times near the park in GBIF.

penstemon strictus.name: Rocky Mountain penstemon
penstemon strictus.desc: Rocky Mountain penstemon (Penstemon strictus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon strictus.about: Penstemon strictus, more commonly known as the Rocky Mountain penstemon, is a penstemon (common name beardtongue) with showy blue flowers.

penstemon virgatus.name: Upright blue beardtongue
penstemon virgatus.desc: Upright blue beardtongue (Penstemon virgatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
penstemon virgatus.about: Penstemon virgatus, the wandbloom penstemon, is a species of flowering plant from western North America. It grows as far south as southwestern Mexico and as far north as southern Wyoming.

penstemon whippleanus.name: Whipple's penstemon
penstemon whippleanus.desc: Whipple's penstemon (Penstemon whippleanus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 84 times near the park in GBIF.

pentaclethra macroloba.name: Cashew-nut tree
pentaclethra macroloba.desc: A leguminous tree recorded in the reserve area, common in wet and swampy lowland forest.
pentaclethra macroloba.about: Pentaclethra macroloba is a large and common leguminous tree in the genus Pentaclethra native to the wet tropical areas of the northern Neotropics, which can form monocultural stands in some…

pentadesma butyracea.name: Kanya
pentadesma butyracea.desc: A tree of damp forest and stream edges in West Africa, recorded near the reserve; it bears large fruits and is valued for its seed fat.
pentadesma butyracea.about: Pentadesma butyracea is a tree native to the forests of tropical Africa from Sierra Leone to Cameroon.

pepsis menechma.name: Elegant Tarantula-hawk Wasp
pepsis menechma.desc: Elegant Tarantula-hawk Wasp (Pepsis menechma): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
pepsis menechma.about: Pepsis menechma, the elegant tarantula hawk, is a species of spider wasp in the family Pompilidae, widely distributed from North America through South America.

perca flavescens.name: Yellow perch
perca flavescens.desc: A small lake fish that feeds on zooplankton and insects, and is prey for walleye and loons.
perca flavescens.about: The yellow perch, commonly referred to as perch, striped perch, American perch or preacher is a freshwater ray-finned fish from the perch family Percidae, native to much of central North America,…

perca fluviatilis.name: European perch
perca fluviatilis.desc: A predatory fish of the lagoon that eats smaller fish and invertebrates.
perca fluviatilis.about: The European perch, also known as the common perch, redfin perch, big-scaled redfin, English perch, Euro perch, Eurasian perch, Eurasian river perch, Hatch, poor man's rockfish or in Anglophone parts…

perennial springs.name: Perennial springs
perennial springs.desc: Springs such as Ein Prat, Ein Mabuah and Ein Qelt keep Wadi Qelt flowing in places and draw wildlife.

perideridia gairdneri.name: Common Yampah
perideridia gairdneri.desc: Common Yampah (Perideridia gairdneri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
perideridia gairdneri.about: Perideridia gairdneri is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae known by the common names common yampah, Gardner's yampah and Squaw root.

perilla frutescens.name: Perilla (beefsteak mint)
perilla frutescens.desc: Perilla (beefsteak mint) (Perilla frutescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.
perilla frutescens.about: Perilla frutescens is a species of Perilla in the mint family Lamiaceae.

peringia ulvae (hydrobia).name: Mudsnail
peringia ulvae (hydrobia).desc: A tiny snail that grazes the muddy surface in huge numbers. It is eaten by shrimp and by wading birds.
peringia ulvae (hydrobia).about: Peringia ulvae, commonly known as the Laver spire shell or mudsnail, is a European species of very small aquatic snail with gills and an operculum, a gastropod mollusk in the family Hydrobiidae.

periophthalmus.name: Mudskipper
periophthalmus.desc: Amphibious fish of mudflats and mangroves that hunt small invertebrates; prey for coastal herons.
periophthalmus.about: Mudskippers are any of the 25 extant species of amphibious fish from the subfamily Oxudercinae of the goby family Oxudercidae.

periophthalmus and relatives.name: Mudskippers
periophthalmus and relatives.desc: Amphibious fish that hop across exposed mudflats at low tide and eat small invertebrates.
periophthalmus and relatives.about: Mudskippers are any of the 25 extant species of amphibious fish from the subfamily Oxudercinae of the goby family Oxudercidae.

periphyton.name: River algae
periphyton.desc: Green films on rocks in the Mara and Grumeti rivers that feed fish.
periphyton.about: Periphyton is a complex mixture of algae, cyanobacteria, heterotrophic microbes, and detritus that is attached to submerged surfaces in most aquatic ecosystems.

periphyton and watercress.name: Stream algae & aquatic plants
periphyton and watercress.desc: Algae on rocks and plants in clear, cool spring-fed streams grow the food that aquatic insects and crayfish graze.
periphyton and watercress.about: Algae are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. It excludes the land plants (embryophytes).

perisoreus infaustus.name: Siberian jay
perisoreus infaustus.desc: A boreal forest bird named by Wikipedia as a park speciality. Recorded eating small birds and voles.
perisoreus infaustus.about: The Siberian jay is a small jay with a widespread distribution within the coniferous forests in North Eurasia. It has grey-brown plumage with a darker brown crown and a paler throat.

permafrost.name: Permafrost
permafrost.desc: Wikipedia describes the park's permafrost as discontinuous and the shallow permafrost as thawing. Frozen ground limits tree growth and holds water near the surface.

permafrost & peatlands.name: Permafrost & peatlands
permafrost & peatlands.desc: Cold, waterlogged bogs and fens that hold large stores of carbon. Black spruce, tamarack and mosses are among the plants that live there.

permafrost soil.name: Permafrost soil
permafrost soil.desc: Frozen ground limits roots to a thin summer layer and locks away carbon.

peromyscus boylii.name: Brush mouse
peromyscus boylii.desc: Brush mouse (Peromyscus boylii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
peromyscus boylii.about: The brush mouse is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae. It is a species of the genus Peromyscus, a closely related group of New World mice often called "deermice".

peromyscus californicus.name: California Deermouse
peromyscus californicus.desc: California Deermouse (Peromyscus californicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 58 times near the park in GBIF.

peromyscus eremicus.name: Cactus mouse
peromyscus eremicus.desc: Cactus mouse (Peromyscus eremicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.
peromyscus eremicus.about: The cactus mouse or cactus deermouse is a species of rodent in the family Cricetidae. It is a species of the genus Peromyscus, a closely related group of New World mice often called "deermice".

peromyscus leucopus.name: White-footed mouse
peromyscus leucopus.desc: White-footed mouse (Peromyscus leucopus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
peromyscus leucopus.about: The white-footed mouse is a rodent native to North America from southern Canada to the Southwestern United States and Mexico.

peromyscus maniculatus.name: Deer mouse

peromyscus maniculatus.about: The eastern deer mouse is a rodent native to eastern North America. It is a species of the genus Peromyscus, a closely related group of New World mice often called "deermice".

physaria filiformis.name: Limestone glade baldderpod
physaria filiformis.desc: Limestone glade baldderpod (Physaria filiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
physaria filiformis.about: Physaria filiformis is a rare species of flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae known by the common names Missouri bladderpod and limestone glade bladderpod.

physaria scrotiformis.name: West silver bladderpod
physaria scrotiformis.desc: West silver bladderpod (Physaria scrotiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

physematium obtusum.name: Blunt-lobed woodsia
physematium obtusum.desc: Blunt-lobed woodsia (Physematium obtusum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
physematium obtusum.about: Physematium obtusum, the bluntlobe cliff fern, is a common rock fern of Appalachia and eastern North America. It prefers a calcareous substrate, but also grows in neutral soils.

phytolacca americana.name: American Pokeweed
phytolacca americana.desc: American Pokeweed (Phytolacca americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
phytolacca americana.about: Phytolacca americana, also known as American pokeweed, pokeweed, polk salad, poke sallet, pokeberry, dragonberries, pigeonberry weed, and inkberry, is a poisonous, herbaceous, perennial plant in the…

phytoplankton.name: Phytoplankton
phytoplankton.desc: Drifting algae in the ocean water that feed zooplankton at the base of the open-water food chain.
phytoplankton.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

piaya cayana.name: Squirrel cuckoo
piaya cayana.desc: A long-tailed forest cuckoo that hunts large insects in the canopy and also eats fruit, such as milkberry.
piaya cayana.about: The common squirrel cuckoo is a large and active species of cuckoo found in wooded habitats from northwestern Mexico to northern Argentina and Uruguay, and on Trinidad.

pica hudsonia.name: Black-billed Magpie
pica hudsonia.desc: A clever, omnivorous bird that feeds at carcasses among other foods.
pica hudsonia.about: The black-billed magpie, also known as the American magpie, is a bird in the corvid family found in the western half of North America.

pica pica.name: Eurasian magpie
pica pica.desc: Omnivorous crow relative, the most recorded bird near the lake. Eats berries such as sea buckthorn along with insects and scraps.
pica pica.about: The Eurasian magpie or common magpie is a resident breeding bird throughout the northern part of the Eurasian continent.

picea abies.name: Norway spruce
picea abies.desc: A widespread conifer of the forest. Its seeds feed squirrels and its bark is where spruce bark beetles breed.
picea abies.about: Picea abies, the Norway spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.

picea glauca.name: White spruce
picea glauca.desc: A conifer whose seeds feed red squirrels and which forms the forest along park lakes and rivers.
picea glauca.about: Picea glauca, the white spruce, is a species of spruce native to the northern temperate and boreal forests in Canada and United States, North America.

picea mariana.name: Black spruce
picea mariana.desc: The most widespread tree of the northern forest. Wikipedia notes it tolerates shallow soil, permafrost and waterlogged ground, though it grows slowly.
picea mariana.about: Picea mariana, the black spruce, is a North American species of spruce tree in the pine family. It is widespread across Canada, found in all 10 provinces and all 3 territories.

picea orientalis.name: Oriental spruce
picea orientalis.desc: A conifer of the Caucasus forests. Winter-feeding chamois use conifer needles and bark, and squirrels take conifer seed.
picea orientalis.about: Picea orientalis, commonly known as the Oriental spruce or Caucasian spruce, is a species of spruce native to the Caucasus and adjacent northeast Turkey.

picea pungens.name: Colorado Spruce
picea pungens.desc: Colorado Spruce (Picea pungens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

picea rubens.name: Red Spruce
picea rubens.desc: Red Spruce (Picea rubens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

picea schrenkiana.name: Schrenk's spruce
picea schrenkiana.desc: The main conifer of the Tian Shan forests, forming important stands above about 2,000 m.
picea schrenkiana.about: Picea schrenkiana, Schrenk's spruce, or Asian spruce, is a spruce native to the Tian Shan mountains of Central Asia and also to western China (Xinjiang).

picea sitchensis.name: Sitka spruce
picea sitchensis.desc: A large conifer that forms the forest of the lower bay, on ground exposed by ice long ago.
picea sitchensis.about: Picea sitchensis, the Sitka spruce, is a large, coniferous, evergreen tree growing to just over 100 meters (330 ft) tall, with a trunk diameter at breast height that can exceed 5 m (16 ft).

pieris brassicae.name: Large White butterfly
pieris brassicae.desc: Butterfly whose caterpillars eat the leaves of herbs; adults and larvae feed insect-eating birds and lizards.
pieris brassicae.about: Pieris brassicae, the large white, also called cabbage butterfly, cabbage white, cabbage moth (erroneously), or in India the large cabbage white, is a butterfly in the family Pieridae.

pieris marginalis.name: Margined White
pieris marginalis.desc: Margined White (Pieris marginalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 132 times near the park in GBIF.

pieris rapae.name: Small White
pieris rapae.desc: Small White (Pieris rapae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
pieris rapae.about: Pieris rapae is a small-to-medium-sized butterfly species of the whites-and-yellows family Pieridae.

piliocolobus badius.name: Western red colobus
piliocolobus badius.desc: A leaf- and fruit-eating monkey of the high canopy. Wikipedia calls it a frequent prey of chimpanzees.
piliocolobus badius.about: The western red colobus, also known as the bay red colobus, rust red colobus or Upper Guinea red colobus, is a species of Old World monkey in West African forests from Senegal to Ghana.

piliocolobus preussi.name: Preuss's red colobus
piliocolobus preussi.desc: A rare leaf-eating monkey of the Cameroon-Nigeria forests, living high in the canopy.
piliocolobus preussi.about: Preuss's red colobus is a red colobus primate species endemic to the Cross-Sanaga Rivers ecoregion.

piliocolobus spp..name: Red colobus monkeys
piliocolobus spp..desc: Leaf-eating monkeys of the forest canopy. Chimpanzees and crowned eagles hunt them.
piliocolobus spp..about: The western red colobus, also known as the bay red colobus, rust red colobus or Upper Guinea red colobus, is a species of Old World monkey in West African forests from Senegal to Ghana.

piloblephis rigida.name: Wild pennyroyal
piloblephis rigida.desc: Wild pennyroyal (Piloblephis rigida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 195 times near the park in GBIF.

pilosella aurantiaca.name: Orange Hawkweed
pilosella aurantiaca.desc: Orange Hawkweed (Pilosella aurantiaca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
pilosella aurantiaca.about: Pilosella aurantiaca (fox-and-cubs, orange hawkweed, devil's paintbrush, and historically grim-the-collier) is a perennial flowering plant in the family Asteraceae.

pimenta racemosa.name: Bayrum tree
pimenta racemosa.desc: A forest tree recorded in the park; GloBI records fruit bats feeding on it.
pimenta racemosa.about: Pimenta racemosa is a species of plant in the myrtle family (Myrtaceae) that is native to the Caribbean region and Venezuela. Common names include West Indian bay tree, bay rum tree, and ciliment.

pinanga.name: Understorey palms
pinanga.desc: Small palms of the shady forest floor; the park also has abundant rattan, gingers and ferns beneath the canopy.
pinanga.about: Pinanga is a genus of flowering plant of the palm family in the subtribe Arecinae. It is native to eastern and southern Asia (India, China, Indo-China, Malesia) across to New Guinea.

pinaroloxias inornata.name: Cocos finch
pinaroloxias inornata.desc: Found only on Cocos Island, it eats berries and insects and uses varied foraging methods learned from other finches.
pinaroloxias inornata.about: The Cocos finch or Cocos Island finch, is the only one of Darwin's finches not native to the Galápagos Islands, and the only member of the genus Pinaroloxias.

pinus.name: Pines
pinus.desc: Pines share the mountain slopes with oaks between roughly 1,500 and 3,000 m, below the oyamel belt.
pinus.about: Pines (genus Pinus () are a genus of conifers in the family Pinaceae. Pinus is the sole genus in the subfamily Pinoideae.

pinus albicaulis.name: Whitebark pine
pinus albicaulis.desc: A high-elevation pine whose large seeds feed nutcrackers, squirrels and bears. Blister rust and pine beetles threaten it.
pinus albicaulis.about: Pinus albicaulis, known by the common names whitebark pine, white bark pine, white pine, pitch pine, scrub pine, and creeping pine, is a conifer tree native to the mountains of the western United…

pinus banksiana.name: Jack pine
pinus banksiana.desc: A pine of dry, sandy ground whose resin-sealed cones open after fire to release seed.
pinus banksiana.about: Jack pine, also known as grey pine or scrub pine, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a North American pine.

pinus brutia.name: Turkish pine
pinus brutia.desc: Covers about 175,000 hectares of Cyprus, roughly 90% of its woodland, and is the most important forestry tree.
pinus brutia.about: Pinus brutia, the Turkish pine or Calabrian pine, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine native to the eastern Mediterranean region.

pinus cembra.name: Swiss stone pine
pinus cembra.desc: A conifer of the uppermost forest belt in the Alps. On the Aletsch side it forms forest on moraine laid down after the glacier maximum around 1850.
pinus cembra.about: Pinus cembra, also known as Swiss pine, Swiss stone pine, Arolla pine, Austrian stone pine, or just stone pine, is a species of pine tree in the subgenus Strobus.

pinus contorta.name: Scrub Pine
pinus contorta.desc: A conifer that recolonizes old burn areas in the subalpine zone. It is a host of the mountain pine beetle.
pinus contorta.about: Pinus contorta, the lodgepole pine, shore pine, twisted pine, or contorta pine, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae.

pinus echinata.name: Arkansas Pine
pinus echinata.desc: Arkansas Pine (Pinus echinata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus echinata.about: The shortleaf pine or Pinus echinata is a species of coniferous tree in the family Pinaceae, a pine endemic to the United States.

pinus edulis.name: Pinyon pine
pinus edulis.desc: A slow-growing pine of the pinyon-juniper woodland that covers much of the rim. Its large seeds feed wildlife.
pinus edulis.about: Pinus edulis, the pinyon pine, Colorado pinyon, or simply pinyon, is a species of pinyon pine from the southwestern United States noted for its large, edible seeds.

pinus elliottii.name: Slash Pine
pinus elliottii.desc: Slash Pine (Pinus elliottii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus flexilis.name: Limber pine
pinus flexilis.desc: A high-elevation white pine with large seeds that Clark's nutcracker eats and caches.
pinus flexilis.about: Pinus flexilis, the limber pine, is a species of pine tree in the family Pinaceae that occurs in the mountains of the Western United States, Mexico, and Canada.

pinus halepensis.name: Aleppo pine
pinus halepensis.desc: A Mediterranean pine of the sandy coastal forests, which are increasingly dominated by pines.
pinus halepensis.about: Pinus halepensis, commonly known as the Aleppo pine, also known as the Jerusalem pine, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine native to the Mediterranean region.

pinus heldreichii.name: Bosnian pine
pinus heldreichii.desc: A tough high-mountain pine that reaches the alpine tree line. Baikushev's pine in Pirin is estimated to be over 1,300 years old, Bulgaria's oldest tree.
pinus heldreichii.about: Pinus heldreichii, the Bosnian pine or Heldreich's pine, is a species of pine native to mountainous regions of Southeast Europe and, to lesser extent, mountainous southern Italian Peninsula.

pinus jeffreyi.name: Jeffrey pine
pinus jeffreyi.desc: Jeffrey pine (Pinus jeffreyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 125 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus jeffreyi.about: Pinus jeffreyi, also known as Jeffrey pine, Jeffrey's pine, yellow pine and black pine, is a North American species of pine tree.

pinus koraiensis.name: Korean pine
pinus koraiensis.desc: Its seeds stay in the cones until birds such as the nutcracker carry them off. The mixed Korean pine and broadleaf forest is described as the tiger's home forest.
pinus koraiensis.about: Pinus koraiensis is a species of pine known commonly as the Korean pine. It is a relic species of the Tertiary, identified as a rare tree species by United Nations.

pinus lambertiana.name: California Sugar Pine
pinus lambertiana.desc: California Sugar Pine (Pinus lambertiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 489 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus longaeva.name: Great Basin bristlecone pine
pinus longaeva.desc: Grows in open stands near treeline on rocky, often dolomite soils where few other plants thrive. It is the oldest known living non-clonal organism.
pinus longaeva.about: Pinus longaeva is a long-living species of bristlecone pine tree found in the higher mountains of California, Nevada, and Utah.

pinus monophylla.name: Nut Pine
pinus monophylla.desc: Nut Pine (Pinus monophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus nigra.name: European black pine
pinus nigra.desc: Dense forests cover much of the park, including old stands with trees about 400 years old and over 50 m tall. Chamois eat conifers in winter.
pinus nigra.about: Pinus nigra, the European black pine, is a moderately variable species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine native across Southern Europe from the Iberian Peninsula and Lower Austria to the…

pinus occidentalis.name: Hispaniolan pine
pinus occidentalis.desc: The dominant pine of the open upper forest, whose seedlings do well after fire.
pinus occidentalis.about: Pinus occidentalis, the Hispaniolan pine, Hispaniola pine or pino criollo, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine tree endemic to the island of Hispaniola.

pinus palustris.name: Longleaf Pine
pinus palustris.desc: Longleaf pine (Pinus palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus palustris.about: The longleaf pine is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine native to the Southeastern United States, found along the coastal plain from East Texas to southern Virginia, extending into…

pinus peuce.name: Macedonian pine
pinus peuce.desc: One of the park's largest forest types, covering roughly 54 square kilometres of the mountain slopes.
pinus peuce.about: Pinus peuce is a species of pine native to the mountains of North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Albania, Montenegro, Kosovo, the extreme southwest of Serbia, and the extreme northwest of Greece, growing…

pinus ponderosa.name: Bull Pine
pinus ponderosa.desc: Bull Pine (Pinus ponderosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus ponderosa.about: Pinus ponderosa, commonly known as the ponderosa pine or western yellow pine, is a very large pine tree species of variable habitat native to mountainous regions of western North America.

pinus pumila.name: Siberian dwarf pine
pinus pumila.desc: A sprawling shrubby pine forming dense thickets above the treeline. Its seeds are harvested and spread by nutcrackers.
pinus pumila.about: Pinus pumila, the Siberian dwarf pine, dwarf Siberian pine, dwarf stone pine, Japanese stone pine, or creeping pine, is a tree in the family Pinaceae native to northeastern Asia and the Japanese…

pinus resinosa.name: Norway Pine
pinus resinosa.desc: Norway Pine (Pinus resinosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 182 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus rigida.name: Pitch Pine
pinus rigida.desc: Pitch Pine (Pinus rigida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus rigida.about: Pinus rigida, the pitch pine, is a small-to-medium-sized conifer in the family Pinaceae.

pinus sibirica.name: Siberian pine
pinus sibirica.desc: A five-needled pine of the mountain taiga whose large seeds are a food for birds such as the nutcracker.
pinus sibirica.about: Pinus sibirica, or Siberian pine, in the family Pinaceae is a species of pine tree that occurs in Siberia from 58°E in the Ural Mountains east to 126°E in the Stanovoy Range in southern Sakha…

pinus strobiformis.name: Border Limber Pine
pinus strobiformis.desc: Border Limber Pine (Pinus strobiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 103 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus strobiformis.about: Pinus strobiformis, also known as Chihuahua white pine, is a medium-sized white pine tree endemic to western Mexico in the Sierra Madre Occidental mountain range.

pinus strobus.name: Weymouth Pine
pinus strobus.desc: Weymouth Pine (Pinus strobus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus strobus.about: Pinus strobus, commonly called the eastern white pine, northern white pine, white pine, Weymouth pine (British), and soft pine is a large pine native to eastern North America.

pinus sylvestris.name: Scots pine
pinus sylvestris.desc: Conifer of the drier forest and bog edges, whose twigs and bark browsers use in winter.
pinus sylvestris.about: Pinus sylvestris is a species of conifer, a pine, in the family Pinaceae. It is native to Eurasia.

pinus taeda.name: Loblolly pine
pinus taeda.desc: Loblolly pine (Pinus taeda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.
pinus taeda.about: Pinus taeda, commonly known as loblolly pine, is a species of conifer in the family Pinaceae, a pine native to the Southeastern United States, from East Texas to Florida, up to southern New Jersey.

pinus thunbergii.name: Japanese Black Pine
pinus thunbergii.desc: Japanese Black Pine (Pinus thunbergii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

pinus virginiana.name: Scrub pine
pinus virginiana.desc: Scrub pine (Pinus virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

piper aequale.name: Piper
piper aequale.desc: A shrub of the pepper family. Fruit-eating bats such as Carollia are key dispersers of Piper seeds.
piper aequale.about: Piper, the pepper plants or pepper vines, is an economically and ecologically important genus in the family Piperaceae.

piper hostmannianum.name: Pepper plant
piper hostmannianum.desc: A forest understory shrub of the pepper genus. Its fruit is a favourite of Carollia fruit bats.
piper hostmannianum.about: Piper, the pepper plants or pepper vines, is an economically and ecologically important genus in the family Piperaceae.

pipilo erythrophthalmus.name: Eastern Towhee
pipilo erythrophthalmus.desc: Eastern Towhee (Pipilo erythrophthalmus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,175 times near the park in GBIF.
pipilo erythrophthalmus.about: The eastern towhee, also known as chewink, joree, or joree bird, is a large New World sparrow.

pipilo maculatus.name: Spotted Towhee
pipilo maculatus.desc: Spotted Towhee (Pipilo maculatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 131 times near the park in GBIF.
pipilo maculatus.about: The spotted towhee is a large New World sparrow. The taxonomy of the towhees has been debated in recent decades, and until 1995 this bird and the eastern towhee were considered a single species, then…

pipra pipra.name: White-crowned manakin
pipra pipra.desc: A small fruit-eating forest bird, recorded very often here, that takes berries such as Miconia.
pipra pipra.about: The white-crowned manakin is a small passerine bird in the manakin family Pipridae. This common and extremely widespread manakin is one of the most easily identified, even in female plumage.

piranga rubra.name: Summer Tanager
piranga rubra.desc: Summer Tanager (Piranga rubra): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 146 times near the park in GBIF.
piranga rubra.about: The summer tanager is a medium-sized American songbird. Formerly placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae), it and other members of its genus are now classified in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae).

pistacia atlantica.name: Mount Atlas mastic tree
pistacia atlantica.desc: A tough tree of dry hill country that is recorded in the reserve. GloBI records blackbirds eating from it.
pistacia atlantica.about: Pistacia atlantica is a species of pistachio tree known by the English common names Mt.

pistacia lentiscus.name: Mastic tree
pistacia lentiscus.desc: An evergreen Mediterranean shrub of coastal scrub, whose berries are eaten by some mammals.
pistacia lentiscus.about: Pistacia lentiscus is a dioecious evergreen shrub or small tree of the genus Pistacia native to the Mediterranean Basin.

pistia stratiotes.name: Water lettuce
pistia stratiotes.desc: Floating plant listed by UNESCO among the invasive aquatic plants that spread after the dam; warthogs are recorded eating it.
pistia stratiotes.about: Pistia is a genus of aquatic plants in the arum family, Araceae. It is the sole genus in the tribe Pistieae which reflects its systematic isolation within the family.

pitangus sulphuratus.name: Great kiskadee
pitangus sulphuratus.desc: One of the best-recorded birds here. GloBI records it eating Myrcia fruit, and it also takes insects and small prey.
pitangus sulphuratus.about: The great kiskadee is a passerine bird in the tyrant flycatcher family Tyrannidae. It is the only member of the genus Pitangus.

pitohui dichrous.name: Hooded pitohui
pitohui dichrous.desc: Eats mostly fruit, especially figs, plus insects and other invertebrates. Its skin and feathers carry batrachotoxin, which may deter predators.
pitohui dichrous.about: The hooded pitohui is a species of bird in the genus Pitohui found in New Guinea.

pittosporum viridiflorum.name: Cape pittosporum
pittosporum viridiflorum.desc: An evergreen forest tree whose fruit and foliage feed monkeys and many birds.
pittosporum viridiflorum.about: Pittosporum viridiflorum is a protected tree in South Africa.

pituophis catenifer.name: Bullsnake
pituophis catenifer.desc: Bullsnake (Pituophis catenifer): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
pituophis catenifer.about: Pituophis catenifer, the gopher snake, is a species of nonvenomous colubrid snake endemic to North America. Nine subspecies are currently recognized.

pituophis catenifer sayi.name: Bullsnake
pituophis catenifer sayi.desc: A large constrictor that eats rodents and birds. GloBI records include kangaroo rats, mice and doves.
pituophis catenifer sayi.about: The bullsnake is a large, nonvenomous, colubrid snake. It is a subspecies of the gopher snake.

pituophis melanoleucus.name: Northern pine snake
pituophis melanoleucus.desc: A big constrictor that hunts mice and other small mammals, often in their burrows. It favours sandy habitat that burns often, and foxes dig up its nests.
pituophis melanoleucus.about: Pituophis melanoleucus, commonly known as the eastern pine snake, is a species of nonvenomous snake in the family Colubridae. The species is native to the southeastern United States.

pityopsis falcata.name: Sickleleaf Silkgrass
pityopsis falcata.desc: Sickleleaf Silkgrass (Pityopsis falcata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
pityopsis falcata.about: Pityopsis falcata, commonly known as sickleleaf silkgrass, sickle-leaved golden aster, and New England Golden aster, is perennial plant in the family Asteraceae native to the northeastern Atlantic…

plagiodontia aedium.name: Hispaniolan hutia
plagiodontia aedium.desc: A threatened, nocturnal island rodent that mainly eats roots and fruits.
plagiodontia aedium.about: The Hispaniolan hutia is a small, rat-like mammal endemic to forests on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola. It lives in burrows or trees, and is active at night when it feeds on roots and fruits.

plagiosiphon emarginatus.name: Plagiosiphon
plagiosiphon emarginatus.desc: A rainforest tree or shrub of West Africa often found near rivers. Colobus monkeys are recorded eating it in GloBI.
plagiosiphon emarginatus.about: Plagiosiphon is a genus of plants in the family Fabaceae. It includes five species of trees or shrubs native to west and west-central Africa.

planera aquatica.name: Water-elm
planera aquatica.desc: Water-elm (Planera aquatica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
planera aquatica.about: Planera aquatica, the planertree or water elm, is a species of flowering plant.

plantago coronopus.name: Buck's-horn Plantain
plantago coronopus.desc: Buck's-horn Plantain (Plantago coronopus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
plantago coronopus.about: Plantago coronopus, the buck's-horn plantain, is a herbaceous annual to perennial flowering plant in the family Plantaginaceae. Other common names in the US and Italy include minutina and erba stella.

plantago lanceolata.name: Ribwort Plantain
plantago lanceolata.desc: Ribwort Plantain (Plantago lanceolata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
plantago lanceolata.about: Plantago lanceolata is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae.

plantago patagonica.name: Woolly Indianwheat
plantago patagonica.desc: Woolly Indianwheat (Plantago patagonica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
plantago patagonica.about: Plantago patagonica is a species of plantain known by the common name woolly plantain. It is native to much of North America and to Argentina in South America.

platalea leucorodia.name: Eurasian spoonbill
platalea leucorodia.desc: Wading bird that sweeps its bill through shallows for small fish and crustaceans; the site is a major wintering ground.
platalea leucorodia.about: The Eurasian spoonbill, or common spoonbill, is a wading bird of the ibis and spoonbill family Threskiornithidae, native to Europe, Africa and Asia.

platanista gangetica.name: Ganges river dolphin
platanista gangetica.desc: A freshwater dolphin that lives in the less salty channels and hunts fish and shrimp.
platanista gangetica.about: The Ganges river dolphin is a freshwater dolphin in the family Platanistidae. It lives in the Ganges and related rivers of South Asia, namely in the countries of India, Nepal, and Bangladesh.

platanthera ciliaris.name: Yellow fringed orchid
platanthera ciliaris.desc: Yellow fringed orchid (Platanthera ciliaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
platanthera ciliaris.about: Platanthera ciliaris, commonly known as the yellow fringed orchid or orange fringed orchid, is a large and showy species of orchid.

platanthera dilatata.name: White Bog Orchid
platanthera dilatata.desc: White Bog Orchid (Platanthera dilatata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
platanthera dilatata.about: Platanthera dilatata, known as tall white bog orchid, bog candle, or boreal bog orchid is a species of orchid, a flowering plant in the family Orchidaceae, native to North America.

platanthera grandiflora.name: Greater Purple Fringed Orchid
platanthera grandiflora.desc: Greater Purple Fringed Orchid (Platanthera grandiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

platanus occidentalis.name: Sycamore
platanus occidentalis.desc: Sycamore (Platanus occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
platanus occidentalis.about: Platanus occidentalis, also known as American sycamore or American planetree, is a species of Platanus native to the eastern and central United States, the mountains of northeastern Mexico, extreme…

platanus wrightii.name: Arizona sycamore
platanus wrightii.desc: Arizona sycamore (Platanus wrightii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 190 times near the park in GBIF.
platanus wrightii.about: Platanus wrightii, the Arizona sycamore, is a sycamore tree native to Arizona and New Mexico with its range extending south into the Mexican states of Sonora, Chihuahua, and Sinaloa.

platte river flow.name: Platte River flow
platte river flow.desc: Spring and summer flows keep channels open and wet meadows green, but Wikipedia says river water is overappropriated and has shrunk since the mid-20th century.

platystemon californicus.name: Cream-cups
platystemon californicus.desc: Cream-cups (Platystemon californicus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.
platystemon californicus.about: Platystemon is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the poppy family containing the single species Platystemon californicus, which is known by the common name creamcups.

plectrophenax nivalis.name: Snow bunting
plectrophenax nivalis.desc: A small songbird of rocky highlands and shores that eats seeds and berries of heath plants.
plectrophenax nivalis.about: The snow bunting is a passerine bird in the family Calcariidae. It is an Arctic specialist, with a circumpolar Arctic breeding range throughout the northern hemisphere.

plectropomus leopardus.name: Coral trout
plectropomus leopardus.desc: A reef predator that hunts damselfish and parrotfish.
plectropomus leopardus.about: The leopard coral grouper, also known as the common coral trout, leopard coral trout, blue-dotted coral grouper or spotted coral grouper, is a species of marine ray-finned fish, a grouper from the…

plegadis falcinellus.name: Glossy ibis
plegadis falcinellus.desc: Wades in very shallow water for insect larvae, worms, snails and crustaceans, plus the occasional frog.
plegadis falcinellus.about: The glossy ibis is a water bird in the order Pelecaniformes and the ibis and spoonbill family Threskiornithidae.

plegadis ridgwayi.name: Puna ibis
plegadis ridgwayi.desc: Probes shallow water and mud for invertebrates, and takes amphibians and small fish when it can. It nests in tall wetland vegetation.
plegadis ridgwayi.about: The puna ibis is a species of waterbird in the family Threskiornithidae, spoonbills and ibises. It can be found in Ecuador, Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, and Peru.

pleopeltis michauxiana.name: Resurrection fern
pleopeltis michauxiana.desc: Resurrection fern (Pleopeltis michauxiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

plethodon cinereus.name: Eastern red-backed salamander
plethodon cinereus.desc: Lungless salamander of the leaf litter that eats small invertebrates. It is among the most recorded animals near the park.
plethodon cinereus.about: The red-backed salamander is a small, hardy woodland salamander species in the family Plethodontidae.

plethodontidae.name: Lungless salamanders
plethodontidae.desc: The Smokies hold up to 31 salamander species, earning the title Salamander Capital of the World. These small amphibians eat tiny invertebrates.
plethodontidae.about: Plethodontidae, or lungless salamanders, are a family of salamanders. With over 500 species, lungless salamanders are by far the largest family of salamanders in terms of their diversity.

pleuronectes platessa.name: European plaice
pleuronectes platessa.desc: Young plaice settle on shallow flats and stay for a few months before moving to deeper water. They eat shrimp, then worms and bivalves.
pleuronectes platessa.about: The European plaice, commonly referred to as simply plaice, or schol in Dutch, is a species of marine flatfish in the genus Pleuronectes of the family Pleuronectidae.

ploceus capensis.name: Cape weaver
ploceus capensis.desc: A seed and insect eating bird of southern African grassland and scrub, a regular prey of shrikes.
ploceus capensis.about: The Cape weaver is a species of bird in the weaver family, Ploceidae, found in southern Africa.

pluchea odorata.name: Saltmarsh fleabane
pluchea odorata.desc: Saltmarsh fleabane (Pluchea odorata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

pluchea sericea.name: Arrow-weed
pluchea sericea.desc: Arrow-weed (Pluchea sericea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

pluvialis squatarola.name: Black-bellied Plover
pluvialis squatarola.desc: Black-bellied Plover (Pluvialis squatarola): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 254 times near the park in GBIF.
pluvialis squatarola.about: The grey plover or black-bellied plover is a large plover breeding in Arctic regions. It is a long-distance migrant, with a nearly worldwide coastal distribution when not breeding.

poa.name: Native grasses
poa.desc: Grasses of the meadows are a main food of Utah prairie dogs, which favour a few native grass species.
poa.about: Poa is a genus of about 570 species of grasses, native to the temperate regions of both hemispheres. Common names include meadow-grass, bluegrass (mainly in North America), tussock, and speargrass.

poa alpina.name: Alpine meadow-grass
poa alpina.desc: A common grass of high mountain meadows, grazed by insects and small mammals.
poa alpina.about: Poa alpina, commonly known as alpine meadow-grass or alpine bluegrass, is a species of grass with a primarily holarctic distribution.

poa annua.name: Annual Meadow-grass
poa annua.desc: Annual Meadow-grass (Poa annua): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
poa annua.about: Poa annua, or annual meadow grass, is a widespread low-growing turfgrass in temperate climates. Notwithstanding the reference to annual plant in its name, perennial biotypes do exist.

poa cookii.name: Cook's tussock grass
poa cookii.desc: Tussock grass of subantarctic coasts and slopes. Introduced rabbits graze it.
poa cookii.about: Poa is a genus of about 570 species of grasses, native to the temperate regions of both hemispheres. Common names include meadow-grass, bluegrass (mainly in North America), tussock, and speargrass.

poa fendleriana.name: Muttongrass
poa fendleriana.desc: Muttongrass (Poa fendleriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
poa fendleriana.about: Poa fendleriana is a species of grass known by the common name muttongrass. It is native to western North America, where its distribution extends from western Canada to northern Mexico.

poa flabellata.name: Tussac grass
poa flabellata.desc: A tall coastal grass that grows in dense clumps about 2 m high and dominates the shoreline where it grows. Penguins, albatrosses and seals use it for cover and nesting.
poa flabellata.about: Poa flabellata, commonly known as tussac grass or just tussac, is a tussock grass native to Patagonia, the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and other islands in the South Atlantic.

poa glauca.name: Arctic grasses
poa glauca.desc: Hardy grasses of dry slopes and gravel. GloBI records common redpolls eating Poa glauca.
poa glauca.about: Poa glauca is a species of grass known by the common names glaucous bluegrass, glaucous meadow-grass and white bluegrass.

poa pratensis.name: Smooth Meadow-grass
poa pratensis.desc: Smooth Meadow-grass (Poa pratensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

poa secunda.name: Sandberg's bluegrass
poa secunda.desc: Sandberg's bluegrass (Poa secunda): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
poa secunda.about: Poa secunda is a widespread species of perennial bunchgrass native to North and South America.

poaceae.name: Floodplain grasses
poaceae.desc: Grasses along rivers and swamp edges are grazed by hippos at night.
poaceae.about: Poaceae ( poh-AY-see-e(y)e), also called Gramineae ( grə-MIN-ee-e(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.

poaceae and carex.name: Alpine grasses & sedges
poaceae and carex.desc: Short-turf meadow plants above the treeline, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals and by marmots.
poaceae and carex.about: Poaceae ( poh-AY-see-e(y)e), also called Gramineae ( grə-MIN-ee-e(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.

poaceae and wildflowers.name: Mountain meadow grasses & wildflowers
poaceae and wildflowers.desc: Grasses and flowering plants of the wetter high meadows, eaten by elk, deer and small rodents.
poaceae and wildflowers.about: A meadow ( MED-oh) is an open habitat or field, vegetated by grasses, herbs, and other non-woody plants. Trees or shrubs may sparsely populate meadows, as long as they maintain an open character.

poanes viator.name: Broad-winged Skipper
poanes viator.desc: Broad-winged Skipper (Poanes viator): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
poanes viator.about: Poanes viator, the broad-winged skipper, is a skipper butterfly found in North America.

podarcis siculus.name: Italian Wall Lizard
podarcis siculus.desc: Italian Wall Lizard (Podarcis siculus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

podocarpus.name: Montane forest trees
podocarpus.desc: Podocarpus and other evergreen trees of the cloud forest on the middle slopes, home to monkeys, hyraxes and elephants.
podocarpus.about: Podocarpus () is a large genus of conifers, the most numerous and widely distributed of the family Podocarpaceae.

podocarpus urbanii.name: Blue Mountain yacca
podocarpus urbanii.desc: A native conifer of the high Blue Mountain forest, one of the plant species recorded most often in the park area.
podocarpus urbanii.about: Podocarpus () is a large genus of conifers, the most numerous and widely distributed of the family Podocarpaceae.

podoces panderi.name: Turkestan ground jay
podoces panderi.desc: A ground-living crow of sandy desert with low shrubs, and the best-recorded bird near the reserve. Forages on the ground.
podoces panderi.about: The Turkestan ground jay, grey ground jay or Pander's ground-jay is a species of bird in the crow and jay family, Corvidae.

podophyllum peltatum.name: Mayapple
podophyllum peltatum.desc: Mayapple (Podophyllum peltatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
podophyllum peltatum.about: Podophyllum peltatum is a North American herbaceous perennial plant in the family Berberidaceae. Its common names are mayapple, American mandrake, wild mandrake, and ground lemon.

poecile atricapillus.name: Black-capped Chickadee
poecile atricapillus.desc: Black-capped Chickadee (Poecile atricapillus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
poecile atricapillus.about: The black-capped chickadee is a small, nonmigratory, North American passerine bird that lives in deciduous and mixed forests. It is a member of the Paridae family, also known as tits.

poecile carolinensis.name: Carolina Chickadee
poecile carolinensis.desc: Carolina Chickadee (Poecile carolinensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 222 times near the park in GBIF.
poecile carolinensis.about: The Carolina chickadee is a small, non-migratory passerine bird in the tit family Paridae. It has a black cap and bib, and distinctive white cheeks.

poecile rufescens.name: Chestnut-backed Chickadee
poecile rufescens.desc: Chestnut-backed Chickadee (Poecile rufescens): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 38 times near the park in GBIF.
poecile rufescens.about: The chestnut-backed chickadee is a small passerine bird in the tit family, native to western North America.

poecilia latipinna.name: Sailfin molly
poecilia latipinna.desc: A small fish that grazes algae and plant matter. It is a staple prey for wading birds and larger fish.
poecilia latipinna.about: The sailfin molly is a livebearer fish typically found in both freshwater and brackish waterways along the East Coast of the United States, from North Carolina south to Florida, and around the Gulf…

pogoniulus bilineatus.name: Yellow-rumped tinkerbird
pogoniulus bilineatus.desc: A small forest barbet recorded eating Maesa and Tarenna fruits.
pogoniulus bilineatus.about: The yellow-rumped tinkerbird is a bird species in the family Lybiidae, which is native to the moist tropical and subtropical regions of sub-Saharan Africa.

pogonocichla stellata.name: White-starred robin
pogonocichla stellata.desc: A forest-floor songbird that feeds on insects and also takes fruit such as Ilex and Maesa berries.
pogonocichla stellata.about: The white-starred robin is a species of bird in the Old World flycatcher and chat family Muscicapidae. It is also sometimes more simply called the starred robin.

pogonomyrmex badius.name: Florida harvester ant
pogonomyrmex badius.desc: Florida harvester ant (Pogonomyrmex badius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 29 times near the park in GBIF.

pogonomyrmex californicus.name: California harvester ant
pogonomyrmex californicus.desc: Gathers seeds of desert plants for its nest and is prey for horned lizards.
pogonomyrmex californicus.about: Pogonomyrmex californicus, or the California harvester ant, is a species of ant in the subfamily Myrmicinae.

pogonomyrmex rugosus.name: Rough harvester ant
pogonomyrmex rugosus.desc: A seed-collecting ant that stores seeds in underground nests. It is a common insect of the park's dry grassland.
pogonomyrmex rugosus.about: Pogonomyrmex rugosus, the desert harvester ant or rough harvester ant, is a species of harvester ant in the subfamily Myrmicinae which is found in the southwestern United States,and Northern Mexico.

polemonium reptans.name: Greek Valerian
polemonium reptans.desc: Greek Valerian (Polemonium reptans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

polioptila caerulea.name: Blue-gray Gnatcatcher
polioptila caerulea.desc: Blue-gray Gnatcatcher (Polioptila caerulea): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 585 times near the park in GBIF.
polioptila caerulea.about: The blue-gray gnatcatcher is a very small gnatcatcher native to North America.

polistes dominula.name: Paper Wasp
polistes dominula.desc: Paper Wasp (Polistes dominula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
polistes dominula.about: The European paper wasp is one of the most common and well-known species of social wasps in the genus Polistes.

polistes exclamans.name: Paper wasp
polistes exclamans.desc: Paper wasp (Polistes exclamans): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
polistes exclamans.about: Polistes exclamans, the Guinea paper wasp, is a social wasp and is part of the family Vespidae of the order Hymenoptera.

polistes fuscatus.name: Common Paper Wasp
polistes fuscatus.desc: Common Paper Wasp (Polistes fuscatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
polistes fuscatus.about: Polistes fuscatus, whose common name is the dark or northern paper wasp, is widely found in eastern North America, from southern Canada through the southern United States.

polistes metricus.name: Metric Paper Wasp
polistes metricus.desc: Metric Paper Wasp (Polistes metricus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

polyboroides radiatus.name: Madagascar harrier-hawk
polyboroides radiatus.desc: Raptor that kills some sifaka infants and also takes lemurs and reptiles.
polyboroides radiatus.about: The Madagascar harrier-hawk is a medium-sized species of bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, endemic to Madagascar.

polyboroides typus.name: African harrier-hawk
polyboroides typus.desc: A raptor with flexible legs that probes cavities and nests for prey. It is often recorded near the park.
polyboroides typus.about: The African harrier-hawk, harrier hawk or gymnogene is a bird of prey. It is about 60–66 centimetres (24–26 in) in length.

polychaeta.name: Marine worms
polychaeta.desc: Bristle worms living in the mud, a major prey of shorebirds that probe the flats.
polychaeta.about: Polychaeta () is a paraphyletic class of generally marine annelid worms, commonly called bristle worms or polychaetes ().

polychaetes and bivalves.name: Seafloor worms & clams
