polychaetes and bivalves.desc: Bottom dwellers that feed on sinking algae and detritus. They suffocate when oxygen drops very low.
polychaetes and bivalves.about: Polychaeta () is a paraphyletic class of generally marine annelid worms, commonly called bristle worms or polychaetes ().

polygaloides paucifolia.name: Polygaloides paucifolia
polygaloides paucifolia.desc: Polygaloides paucifolia (Polygaloides paucifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
polygaloides paucifolia.about: Chamaebuxus paucifolia, synonyms including Polygaloides paucifolia and Polygala paucifolia, known as gaywings or fringed polygala, is a perennial plant of the family Polygalaceae.

polygonatum biflorum.name: American Solomon's-seal
polygonatum biflorum.desc: American Solomon's-seal (Polygonatum biflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonia comma.name: Eastern Comma
polygonia comma.desc: Eastern Comma (Polygonia comma): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
polygonia comma.about: Polygonia comma, the eastern comma, is a North American butterfly in the family Nymphalidae, subfamily Nymphalinae.

polygonia faunus.name: Green Comma
polygonia faunus.desc: Green Comma (Polygonia faunus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
polygonia faunus.about: Polygonia faunus, the green comma, is a butterfly of the family Nymphalidae.

polygonia gracilis.name: Hoary Comma
polygonia gracilis.desc: Hoary Comma (Polygonia gracilis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonia interrogationis.name: Question Mark
polygonia interrogationis.desc: Question Mark (Polygonia interrogationis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
polygonia interrogationis.about: Polygonia interrogationis, commonly called the question mark butterfly, is a North American nymphalid butterfly.

polygonia satyrus.name: Satyr Comma
polygonia satyrus.desc: Satyr Comma (Polygonia satyrus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 28 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonum kelloggii.name: Polygonum kelloggii
polygonum kelloggii.desc: Polygonum kelloggii (Polygonum kelloggii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 38 times near the park in GBIF.
polygonum kelloggii.about: Polygonum polygaloides is a North American species of flowering plants in the buckwheat family known by the common names milkwort knotweed and polygala knotweed.

polygonum paronychia.name: Dune knotweed
polygonum paronychia.desc: Dune knotweed (Polygonum paronychia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

polygonum polygaloides.name: Milkwort Knotweed
polygonum polygaloides.desc: Milkwort Knotweed (Polygonum polygaloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
polygonum polygaloides.about: Polygonum polygaloides is a North American species of flowering plants in the buckwheat family known by the common names milkwort knotweed and polygala knotweed.

polymnia canadensis.name: Whiteflower leafcup
polymnia canadensis.desc: Whiteflower leafcup (Polymnia canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
polymnia canadensis.about: Polymnia canadensis, commonly known as whiteflower leafcup, is a flowering perennial plant in the family Asteraceae.

polyodon spathula.name: Paddlefish
polyodon spathula.desc: A giant filter feeder that eats mainly zooplankton, with a few insect larvae and small fish.
polyodon spathula.about: Paddlefish are members of the ray-finned fish family Polyodontidae, which belong to the basal order Acipenseriformes, one of two living groups within this order alongside sturgeons (Acipenseridae).

polypedates cruciger.name: Hour-glass tree frog
polypedates cruciger.desc: A common tree frog of Sri Lanka that eats insects at night.
polypedates cruciger.about: Polypedates cruciger is a species of frog in the family Rhacophoridae endemic to Sri Lanka. It has been osbserved as high as 1600 meters above sea level.

polypedates leucomystax.name: Common tree frog
polypedates leucomystax.desc: A tree frog that catches insects at night; GloBI records it as prey of the striped bronzeback.
polypedates leucomystax.about: Polypedates leucomystax is a species in the shrub frog family Rhacophoridae.

polypodium virginianum.name: Rock Polypody
polypodium virginianum.desc: Rock Polypody (Polypodium virginianum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 50 times near the park in GBIF.

polystepha pilulae.name: Oak Leaf Gall Midge
polystepha pilulae.desc: Oak Leaf Gall Midge (Polystepha pilulae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
polystepha pilulae.about: Polystepha pilulae, the oak leaf gall midge, is a species of gall midge in the family Cecidomyiidae. It is found in eastern North America.

polystichum acrostichoides.name: Christmas Fern
polystichum acrostichoides.desc: Christmas Fern (Polystichum acrostichoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
polystichum acrostichoides.about: Polystichum acrostichoides, commonly denominated Christmas fern, is a perennial, evergreen fern native to eastern North America, from Nova Scotia west to Minnesota and south to Florida and eastern…

polystichum munitum.name: Western Swordfern
polystichum munitum.desc: Sword fern (Polystichum munitum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
polystichum munitum.about: Polystichum munitum, the western swordfern, is an evergreen perennial fern native to western North America, where it is one of the most abundant ferns in forested areas.

pomacea.name: Apple snails
pomacea.desc: Wikipedia calls them a keystone group of the Pantanal. They eat dead plant matter in oxygen-poor floodwater and are food for many animals.
pomacea.about: Pomacea is a genus of freshwater snails with gills and an operculum, aquatic gastropod mollusks in the family Ampullariidae, the apple snails.

pomacea paludosa.name: Florida apple snail
pomacea paludosa.desc: A large freshwater snail that grazes on algae and plants. It is nearly the only food of the snail kite.
pomacea paludosa.about: Pomacea paludosa, common name the Florida applesnail, is a species of freshwater snail with an operculum, an aquatic gastropod mollusk in the family Ampullariidae, the apple snails.

pomacentridae.name: Damselfish
pomacentridae.desc: Guards patches of algae and picks plankton from the water above the reef.
pomacentridae.about: Damselfish are fish within the subfamilies Abudefdufinae, Chrominae, Lepidozyginae, Pomacentrinae, and Stegastinae within the family Pomacentridae.

pomatomus saltatrix.name: Bluefish
pomatomus saltatrix.desc: A fast schooling predator that hunts forage fish such as menhaden.
pomatomus saltatrix.about: The bluefish is the only extant species of the family Pomatomidae. It is a marine pelagic fish found around the world in temperate and subtropical waters, except for the northern Pacific Ocean.

pongo abelii.name: Sumatran orangutan
pongo abelii.desc: Mainly a fruit eater that favours figs and gathers at fruiting fig trees. Insects, leaves and bark add to the diet. Wikipedia says the park is one of two remaining habitats.
pongo abelii.about: The Sumatran orangutan is one of the three species of orangutans.

pontederia azurea.name: Anchored waterhyacinth
pontederia azurea.desc: A rooted emergent water plant of marshes and lagoon edges. Pontederiaceae are a major part of what marsh deer eat.
pontederia azurea.about: Pontederia is a genus of tristylous aquatic plants, members of which are commonly known as pickerel weeds.

pontederia cordata.name: Pickerelweed
pontederia cordata.desc: Pickerelweed (Pontederia cordata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.
pontederia cordata.about: Pontederia cordata, common name pickerelweed (USA) or pickerel weed (UK), is a monocotyledonous aquatic plant native to the Americas.

pontederia crassipes.name: Aquatic plants
pontederia crassipes.desc: Water-hyacinth (Pontederia crassipes): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
pontederia crassipes.about: Pontederia crassipes, commonly known as common water hyacinth, is an aquatic plant native to South America, naturalized throughout the world, and often invasive outside its native range.

pontia beckerii.name: Becker's White
pontia beckerii.desc: Becker's White (Pontia beckerii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
pontia beckerii.about: Pontia beckerii, the Becker's white, Great Basin white, or sagebrush white, is a butterfly in the family Pieridae.

pontia protodice.name: Checkered White
pontia protodice.desc: Checkered White (Pontia protodice): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 74 times near the park in GBIF.
pontia protodice.about: Pontia protodice, the checkered white or southern cabbage butterfly, is a common North American butterfly in the family Pieridae. Its green larva is a type of cabbage worm.

pontoporia blainvillei.name: Franciscana
pontoporia blainvillei.desc: A small coastal dolphin, the best-recorded mammal here, that feeds on fish and squid in shallow water.
pontoporia blainvillei.about: The La Plata dolphin, franciscana or toninha is a species of river dolphin found in coastal Atlantic waters of southeastern South America.

pooecetes gramineus.name: Vesper Sparrow
pooecetes gramineus.desc: Vesper Sparrow (Pooecetes gramineus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
pooecetes gramineus.about: The vesper sparrow is a medium-sized New World sparrow. The only member of the genus Pooecetes, it is a pale sparrow with brown streaks that breeds across the grasslands of northern North America.

poor acidic soils.name: Poor acidic soils
poor acidic soils.desc: Cerrado soils are well drained and mostly acidic and low in nutrients, which helps set what can grow.

poor, dry soils.name: Poor, dry soils
poor, dry soils.desc: Thin soils over limestone and sand in the west and south, with low and erratic winter rain, favour drought-adapted plants.

poor, wet soils.name: Poor, wet soils
poor, wet soils.desc: Nutrient-poor ultisols that drain badly, so nutrients cycle quickly through living plants and leaf litter.

popillia japonica.name: Japanese Beetle
popillia japonica.desc: Japanese Beetle (Popillia japonica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
popillia japonica.about: The Japanese beetle is a species of scarab beetle. Due to the presence of natural predators, the Japanese beetle is not considered a pest in its native Japan.

populus alba.name: White Poplar
populus alba.desc: White Poplar (Populus alba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

populus deltoides.name: Necklace Poplar
populus deltoides.desc: Necklace Poplar (Populus deltoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
populus deltoides.about: Populus deltoides, the eastern cottonwood or necklace poplar, is a species of cottonwood poplar native to North America, growing throughout the eastern, central, and southwestern United States as…

populus deltoides, acer saccharinum.name: Cottonwood & silver maple
populus deltoides, acer saccharinum.desc: Bottomland forest trees that flood each spring. Beavers and deer use them.
populus deltoides, acer saccharinum.about: Populus deltoides, the eastern cottonwood or necklace poplar, is a species of cottonwood poplar native to North America, growing throughout the eastern, central, and southwestern United States as…

populus fremontii.name: Fremont cottonwood
populus fremontii.desc: A riverside tree of the canyon floor that grows along the Virgin River and shades the streamside community.
populus fremontii.about: Populus fremontii, commonly known as Frémont's cottonwood, is a cottonwood native to riparian zones of the Southwestern United States and northern through central Mexico.

populus grandidentata.name: Bigtooth Aspen
populus grandidentata.desc: Bigtooth Aspen (Populus grandidentata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

populus heterophylla.name: Swamp poplar
populus heterophylla.desc: Swamp poplar (Populus heterophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
populus heterophylla.about: Populus heterophylla, also known as downy poplar, swamp poplar and swamp cottonwood, is a large deciduous poplar belonging to the Populus genus of the family Salicaceae.

populus tremula.name: Aspen
populus tremula.desc: A fast-growing riverside and forest tree. Beavers fell it and moose and hares browse its bark and twigs.
populus tremula.about: Populus tremula is a species of poplar native to cool temperate regions of the Old World.

populus tremuloides.name: American Aspen
populus tremuloides.desc: A broadleaf tree that sprouts quickly after disturbance. Moose, hares and beavers eat its bark, twigs and shoots.
populus tremuloides.about: Populus tremuloides is a deciduous tree native to cooler areas of North America, one of several species referred to by the common name aspen.

porcella salvania.name: Pygmy hog
porcella salvania.desc: An omnivore of tall dense grassland that digs roots and tubers and shelters in grass-lined nests. The only known wild population is at Manas.
porcella salvania.about: The pygmy hog is a very small and endangered species of pig and the only species in the genus Porcula.

porifera.name: Marine sponges
porifera.desc: Filter feeders on the reef that strain tiny particles from the water. They are the main food of hawksbill turtles.
porifera.about: Sponges or sea sponges are primarily marine invertebrates of the animal phylum Porifera. They are filter feeders that are typically bound to the seabed, being sessile.

porphyrio hochstetteri.name: Takahe
porphyrio hochstetteri.desc: Large flightless rail rediscovered in the Murchison Mountains in 1948. It eats mainly the leaves of snow tussock.
porphyrio hochstetteri.about: The South Island takahē is a flightless swamphen indigenous to New Zealand and the largest living member of the rail family.

posidonia australis.name: Ribbonweed
posidonia australis.desc: A seagrass whose meadows in Shark Bay include one giant clone covering about 200 square km. Rhizomes anchor the sand and the leaves slow silt.
posidonia australis.about: Posidonia australis, also known as strapweed, tapeweed, ribbonweed or fibre-ball weed, is a species of seagrass that occurs in the southern coastal waters of Australia.

posoqueria latifolia.name: Needle flower
posoqueria latifolia.desc: A tropical understory tree with fragrant flowers and fruit that bats and birds in the area are recorded eating.
posoqueria latifolia.about: Posoqueria latifolia, also known as Needle Flower Tree, is a species of shrub or tree in the family Rubiaceae native to the region spanning from Mexico to tropical South America.

potamochoerus porcus.name: Red river hog
potamochoerus porcus.desc: A forest pig that forages for fruit, roots and plants. GloBI has a record of it feeding on forest elephant.
potamochoerus porcus.about: The red river hog or bushpig is a wild member of the pig family living in Africa, with most of its distribution in the Guinean and Congolian forests.

potamogeton.name: Pondweed & water lilies
potamogeton.desc: Aquatic plants of ponds and sheltered bays. Moose wade in to eat them, mainly for sodium.
potamogeton.about: Potamogeton is a genus of aquatic, mostly freshwater, plants of the family Potamogetonaceae.

potamogeton crispus.name: Curled Pondweed
potamogeton crispus.desc: Curled Pondweed (Potamogeton crispus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
potamogeton crispus.about: Potamogeton crispus, the crisp-leaved pondweed, curly pondweed, curly-leaf pondweed or curled pondweed, is a species of aquatic plant (hydrophyte) native to Eurasia but an introduced species and…

potamogeton foliosus.name: Leafy pondweed
potamogeton foliosus.desc: Leafy pondweed (Potamogeton foliosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

potamogeton lucens.name: Shining pondweed
potamogeton lucens.desc: A submerged aquatic plant recorded in the marsh area, providing food and cover in open water.
potamogeton lucens.about: Potamogeton lucens, or shining pondweed, is an aquatic perennial plant native to Eurasia and North Africa. It grows in relatively deep, still or slow-flowing, calcareous freshwater habitats.

potamogeton nodosus.name: Loddon Pondweed
potamogeton nodosus.desc: Loddon Pondweed (Potamogeton nodosus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

potentilla indica.name: Yellow-flowered Strawberry
potentilla indica.desc: Yellow-flowered Strawberry (Potentilla indica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
potentilla indica.about: Potentilla indica, known commonly as false strawberry, mock strawberry, or Indian strawberry, (also snakeberry in North America) is a flowering plant in the family Rosaceae, native to West Asia to…

potentilla supina.name: Bushy Cinquefoil
potentilla supina.desc: Bushy Cinquefoil (Potentilla supina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
potentilla supina.about: Potentilla supina is a species of flowering plant belonging to the family Rosaceae. Its native range is the temperate and subtropical Northern Hemisphere and Southern Africa.

prairie fire.name: Prairie fire
prairie fire.desc: Fire is one of the environmental factors the park manages, including prescribed burns that clear old growth.

prairie soil.name: Prairie soil
prairie soil.desc: Nutrients released by decay return to the soil and feed the next season of plant growth.

prairie soil & badland clays.name: Prairie soil & badland clays
prairie soil & badland clays.desc: Soils on the benches hold the grass roots; the eroding badland slopes stay mostly bare.

praomys jacksoni.name: Jackson's soft-furred mouse
praomys jacksoni.desc: The most-recorded mammal near the park; an abundant forest floor rodent that eats seeds, fruit and insects.
praomys jacksoni.about: Praomys is a genus of rodent in the family Muridae endemic to Sub-Saharan Africa.

praomys tullbergi.name: Tullberg's soft-furred mouse
praomys tullbergi.desc: A small forest rodent that forages on the forest floor and is prey for genets and snakes.
praomys tullbergi.about: Tullberg's soft-furred mouse or Tullberg's praomys is a species of rodent in the family Muridae in Africa.

prenolepis imparis.name: American Winter Ant
prenolepis imparis.desc: American Winter Ant (Prenolepis imparis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
prenolepis imparis.about: Prenolepis imparis, commonly known as the winter ant, false honey ant, or false honeypot ant, is a species of ant in the genus Prenolepis.

presbytis thomasi.name: Thomas's langur
presbytis thomasi.desc: A leaf-monkey of northern Sumatra. GloBI records show it eating fig and Macaranga fruit near the park.
presbytis thomasi.about: Thomas's langur, also known as the North Sumatran leaf monkey or Thomas's leaf monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

prestoea acuminata.name: Sierra palm
prestoea acuminata.desc: Dominates the palm forest zone on shallow soils at about 600 m. Its fruit is eaten by birds in the forest.
prestoea acuminata.about: Prestoea acuminata is a species of palm tree native to Central America, the West Indies and South America. It was formerly widely harvested in Ecuador for palmito.

primula.name: Alpine meadow flowers
primula.desc: Alpine meadows above the treeline are rich in primulas, gentians and grasses that grazers and small mammals eat.
primula.about: Primula () is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the family Primulaceae. They include the primrose (P. vulgaris), a familiar wildflower of banks and verges.

pringlea antiscorbutica.name: Kerguelen cabbage
pringlea antiscorbutica.desc: Edible cabbage-like plant of subantarctic islands. Introduced rabbits eat it, so it now survives mainly where rabbits cannot reach.
pringlea antiscorbutica.about: Pringlea antiscorbutica, commonly known as Kerguelen cabbage, is a flowering plant and the sole member of the monotypic genus Pringlea in the family Brassicaceae.

pringleophaga kerguelensis.name: Kerguelen flightless moth
pringleophaga kerguelensis.desc: Flightless moth whose larvae feed on Kerguelen cabbage, a major part of the native litter-feeding fauna.
pringleophaga kerguelensis.about: Tineidae is a family of moths in the order Lepidoptera described by Pierre André Latreille in 1810. Collectively, they are known as fungus moths or tineid moths.

priodontes maximus.name: Giant armadillo
priodontes maximus.desc: Eats mainly termites and ants, and its burrows are used by many other animals, making it a habitat engineer.
priodontes maximus.about: The giant armadillo, colloquially tatu-canastra, tatou, ocarro or tatú carreta, is the largest living species of armadillo (although their extinct relatives the glyptodonts were much larger).

prionailurus bengalensis.name: Leopard cat
prionailurus bengalensis.desc: Small wild cat that hunts small mammals; GloBI records include dusky leaf monkey and plantain squirrel.
prionailurus bengalensis.about: The leopard cat is a small wild cat with dark spots on the tawny-coloured body and limbs.

prionailurus viverrinus.name: Fishing cat
prionailurus viverrinus.desc: A wetland cat that ambushes prey at the water's edge. Fish are its main food, with crabs and rodents also taken.
prionailurus viverrinus.about: The fishing cat is a medium-sized wild cat of South and Southeast Asia. It has a deep yellowish-grey fur with black lines and spots.

pristurus sokotranus.name: Socotra rock gecko
pristurus sokotranus.desc: A small rock-dwelling gecko of the island, and one of its many endemic reptiles.
pristurus sokotranus.about: The Socotra rock gecko is a species of lizard in the Sphaerodactylidae family found on Socotra Island. Phylogenetic studies have shown that P.

problema bulenta.name: Rare Skipper
problema bulenta.desc: Rare Skipper (Problema bulenta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
problema bulenta.about: Problema bulenta, the rare skipper, is a butterfly of the family Hesperiidae. It is hard to find within the United States.

probole amicaria.name: Friendly Probole
probole amicaria.desc: Friendly Probole (Probole amicaria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

procambarus alleni.name: Slough crayfish
procambarus alleni.desc: A crayfish that grazes on plants and microbes, and survives the dry season in burrows and wet refuges. Many wading birds, fish and mammals eat it.
procambarus alleni.about: The Everglades crayfish, sometimes called the Florida crayfish, the blue crayfish, the electric blue crayfish, or the sapphire crayfish, is a species of freshwater crayfish endemic to Florida in the…

procambarus clarkii.name: Red swamp crayfish
procambarus clarkii.desc: A North American crayfish introduced to Spain for cultivation. It spreads easily in disturbed wetlands and now feeds many wading birds and otters.
procambarus clarkii.about: Procambarus clarkii, known variously as the red swamp crayfish, Louisiana crawfish or mudbug, is a species of cambarid crayfish native to freshwater bodies of northern Mexico, and southern and…

procavia capensis.name: Rock hyrax
procavia capensis.desc: A rock-dwelling herbivore of the mountain slopes, frequently recorded near the site.
procavia capensis.about: The rock hyrax, also called dassie, Rickaz, Cape hyrax, rock rabbit, or coney, is a medium-sized terrestrial hyrax native to Africa and the Middle East.

prochilodus lineatus.name: Curimbata & other detritus fish
prochilodus lineatus.desc: A migratory fish that feeds on fine organic matter. Most Pantanal fish are detritus eaters, which makes them a major food source for predators.
prochilodus lineatus.about: Prochilodus lineatus, the streaked prochilod, is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Prochilodontidae. It is native to the Paraná-Paraguay and Paraíba do Sul river basins in South America.

procolobus verus.name: Olive colobus
procolobus verus.desc: A small, secretive leaf-eating monkey of the lower forest levels, also recorded eating Plagiosiphon.
procolobus verus.about: The olive colobus monkey, also known as the green colobus or Van Beneden's colobus, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

procyon cancrivorus.name: Crab-eating raccoon
procyon cancrivorus.desc: Omnivore of marshy places in Trinidad that eats crabs, shellfish, fish, amphibians and fruit.
procyon cancrivorus.about: The crab-eating raccoon, southern raccoon, or South American raccoon is a species of raccoon native to marshy and jungle areas of Central and South America.

procyon lotor.name: Raccoon
procyon lotor.desc: Raccoon (Procyon lotor): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
procyon lotor.about: The raccoon, sometimes called the North American, northern or common raccoon (also spelled racoon) to distinguish it from other species of raccoon, is a mammal native to North America.

proechimys semispinosus.name: Tome's spiny rat
proechimys semispinosus.desc: A common forest rodent that eats seeds and fruit on the ground and is food for snakes, hawks and small cats.
proechimys semispinosus.about: Tome's spiny rat, also known as Tomes' spiny rat or the Central American spiny rat, is a species of spiny rat distributed from Honduras to Ecuador.

promerops cafer.name: Cape sugarbird
promerops cafer.desc: A nectar specialist that feeds on proteas and also takes insects and spiders. It is common in mature fynbos and almost absent from recently burned areas.
promerops cafer.about: The Cape sugarbird is one of the eight bird species endemic to the Fynbos biome of the Western Cape and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa.

propithecus verreauxi.name: Verreaux's sifaka
propithecus verreauxi.desc: Mostly a leaf eater, also taking fruit, flowers and bark. Infants are hunted by fossas and harrier-hawks.
propithecus verreauxi.about: Verreaux's sifaka, or the white sifaka, is a medium-sized primate in one of the lemur families, the Indriidae.

prosopeia personata.name: Masked shining parrot
prosopeia personata.desc: A big parrot found only on Viti Levu, living in lowland and hill forest and gardens.
prosopeia personata.about: The masked shining parrot, also known as the masked parrot, masked musk parrot, or the yellow-breasted musk parrot is a species of parrot in the family Psittaculidae.

prosopis alba.name: White carob (algarrobo)
prosopis alba.desc: A thorny, drought-tolerant Chaco tree that bears sugary pods; mammals and birds eat the pods and fruit.
prosopis alba.about: Neltuma alba is a South American tree species that grows in central Argentina, the Gran Chaco ecoregion, and part of the Argentine Mesopotamia, as well as Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay, and Peru.

prosopis glandulosa.name: Honey mesquite
prosopis glandulosa.desc: A deep-rooted desert shrub that can reach groundwater and stabilise sand around its base.
prosopis glandulosa.about: Neltuma glandulosa, formerly Prosopis glandulosa, commonly known as honey mesquite, is a species of small to medium-sized, thorny shrub or tree in the legume family (Fabaceae).

prosopis pubescens.name: Screw-bean
prosopis pubescens.desc: Screw-bean (Prosopis pubescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.
prosopis pubescens.about: Strombocarpa pubescens, commonly known as screwbean mesquite, is a species of flowering shrub or small tree in the pea family, Fabaceae, that is native to the southwestern United States and northern…

prosopis velutina.name: Velvet mesquite
prosopis velutina.desc: A desert tree whose seed pods and foliage feed many animals.
prosopis velutina.about: Neltuma velutina, commonly known as velvet mesquite, is a small to medium-sized tree. It is a legume adapted to a dry, desert climate.

prosthemadera novaeseelandiae.name: Tūī
prosthemadera novaeseelandiae.desc: A common native honeyeater of the park's forests, feeding on nectar and fruit.
prosthemadera novaeseelandiae.about: The tūī is a medium-sized bird native to New Zealand. It is blue, green, and bronze coloured with a distinctive white throat tuft (poi).

protea repens.name: Sugarbush protea
protea repens.desc: A common protea of the fynbos, recorded very often near the site. Its nectar-rich flower heads feed the Cape sugarbird.
protea repens.about: Protea repens, known as the common sugarbush and in Afrikaans as the suikerbossie, is an erect shrub growing in the southern Cape Provinces of South Africa.

proteles cristata.name: Aardwolf
proteles cristata.desc: A small hyena relative that specializes in eating termites.
proteles cristata.about: The aardwolf is an insectivorous hyaenid species, native to East and Southern Africa. Its name means "earth-wolf" in Afrikaans and Dutch.

protopterus aethiopicus.name: Marbled lungfish
protopterus aethiopicus.desc: An air-breathing fish of swamps that eats fish and molluscs; it is a key prey of the shoebill.
protopterus aethiopicus.about: The marbled lungfish is a lungfish of the family Protopteridae. Also known as the leopard lungfish, it is found in Eastern and Central Africa, as well as the Nile region.

protoxerus stangeri.name: Forest giant squirrel
protoxerus stangeri.desc: Forages for fruits and seeds of trees and lianas, cracking tough nuts, plus a few insects.
protoxerus stangeri.about: The forest giant squirrel or Stanger's squirrel is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae found in Angola, Benin, Burundi, Cameroon, the Central African Republic, the Republic of the Congo, the…

prunella vulgaris.name: Selfheal
prunella vulgaris.desc: Selfheal (Prunella vulgaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
prunella vulgaris.about: Prunella vulgaris, the common self-heal, heal-all, woundwort, heart-of-the-earth, carpenter's herb, brownwort or blue curls, is an herbaceous flowering plant in the mint family (Lamiaceae).

prunus africana.name: African cherry
prunus africana.desc: A big montane forest tree whose fruit is eaten by monkeys, birds and other forest animals.
prunus africana.about: Prunus africana, the African cherry, is an African species of cherry growing to 40 metres (130 feet) in height.

prunus americana.name: American Plum
prunus americana.desc: American Plum (Prunus americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus andersonii.name: Desert peach
prunus andersonii.desc: Desert peach (Prunus andersonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus arborea.name: Prunus arborea
prunus arborea.desc: A forest tree that GloBI records as eaten by Asian elephants near the park.
prunus arborea.about: Prunus arborea, most commonly known as xoan đào, is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae. It is distributed throughout Asia and parts of Melanesia.

prunus avium.name: Wild Cherry
prunus avium.desc: Wild Cherry (Prunus avium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus bucharica.name: Bukhara almond
prunus bucharica.desc: A wild almond of the Central Asian foothills that grows at roughly 1,000 to 1,800 m. The cinereous vulture nests in Bukhara almond trees in this range, per the Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet.
prunus bucharica.about: Prunus bucharica is a species of wild almond native to Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Afghanistan, preferring to grow at 1000-1800 m above sea level.

prunus cerasus.name: Dwarf Cherry
prunus cerasus.desc: Dwarf Cherry (Prunus cerasus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus emarginata.name: Bitter cherry
prunus emarginata.desc: Bitter cherry (Prunus emarginata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus gracilis.name: Oklahoma plum
prunus gracilis.desc: Oklahoma plum (Prunus gracilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus mahaleb.name: St Lucie Cherry
prunus mahaleb.desc: St Lucie Cherry (Prunus mahaleb): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus maritima.name: Beach Plum
prunus maritima.desc: Beach Plum (Prunus maritima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus padus.name: Bird cherry
prunus padus.desc: A small tree of moist floodplain woods, well recorded in the park. Its fruit and twigs feed many animals.
prunus padus.about: Prunus padus, the bird cherry, is a flowering plant in the rose family, the type species of the subgenus Padus, which have flowers in racemes. It is native to Europe and northern and northeast Asia.

prunus persica.name: Peach
prunus persica.desc: Peach (Prunus persica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus pumila.name: Sand cherry
prunus pumila.desc: Sand cherry (Prunus pumila): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

prunus serotina.name: Rum Cherry
prunus serotina.desc: Rum Cherry (Prunus serotina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
prunus serotina.about: Prunus serotina, commonly called black cherry, wild black cherry, rum cherry, or mountain black cherry, is a New World deciduous tree or shrub in the rose family, Rosaceae.

prunus virginiana.name: Bitter-berry
prunus virginiana.desc: A thicket-forming shrub of draws and slopes whose leaves and fruit are eaten by deer and other animals.
prunus virginiana.about: Prunus virginiana, commonly called bitter-berry, chokecherry, Virginia bird cherry, and western chokecherry (also black chokecherry for P. virginiana var.

psaltoda insularis.name: Lord Howe cicada
psaltoda insularis.desc: An insect of the island forest. Cicadas feed on plant sap, and many are prey for birds.
psaltoda insularis.about: Psaltoda is a genus of cicada found in eastern Australia. Originally described by Carl Stål, the type species is Psaltoda moerens known as the redeye, and P.

psammodynastes pulverulentus.name: Common mock viper
psammodynastes pulverulentus.desc: A small snake that hunts lizards, and GloBI records it eating the brown mabuya skink.
psammodynastes pulverulentus.about: Psammodynastes pulverulentus, the common mock viper, is a species of snake native to Asia.

psammophis lineolatus.name: Steppe ribbon racer
psammophis lineolatus.desc: A slender, fast snake of sandy deserts that eats lizards such as the steppe agama.
psammophis lineolatus.about: Psammophis lineolatus, commonly known as steppe ribbon racer or arrow snake, is a species of mildly venomous snake (not harmful to humans) in the family Lamprophiidae.

psammophis mossambicus.name: Olive grass snake
psammophis mossambicus.desc: A slender snake; GloBI records show it eating the African striped skink.
psammophis mossambicus.about: Psammophis mossambicus, the olive grass snake, is a snake species in the family Psammophiidae, the sand and whip snakes.

psammophylax rhombeatus.name: Rhombic skaapsteker
psammophylax rhombeatus.desc: A grassland snake that eats frogs, lizards and small mammals.
psammophylax rhombeatus.about: Psammophylax rhombeatus is a reptile commonly found throughout Southern Africa.

psarocolius montezuma.name: Montezuma oropendola
psarocolius montezuma.desc: A well-recorded colonial bird; GloBI shows it eating cocoplum, Davilla and coral-bean fruit.
psarocolius montezuma.about: The Montezuma oropendola is a New World tropical icterid bird.

pseudanthias.name: Reef planktivores
pseudanthias.desc: Small schooling reef fish that pick zooplankton from the water above the coral. Their role here is general reef ecology.
pseudanthias.about: Anthias are members of the family Anthiadidae in the order Perciformes.

pseudaspis cana.name: Mole snake
pseudaspis cana.desc: A constrictor that eats mainly rodents and other small vertebrates, a common snake of the Cape.
pseudaspis cana.about: The mole snake is a species of snake. It has been placed in the family Lamprophiidae, and more recently in the family Pseudaspididae, along with the genus Pythonodipsas.

pseudoedophrys hilleri.name: Weevil
pseudoedophrys hilleri.desc: Weevil (Pseudoedophrys hilleri): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

pseudognaphalium obtusifolium.name: Catfoot
pseudognaphalium obtusifolium.desc: Catfoot (Pseudognaphalium obtusifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

pseudois nayaur.name: Blue sheep (bharal)
pseudois nayaur.desc: A grazer of alpine meadows and rocky slopes. It is the favoured prey of snow leopards, and wolves also hunt it.
pseudois nayaur.about: The bharal, also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas.

pseudonympha varii.name: Vari's brown
pseudonympha varii.desc: A grassland butterfly of the Drakensberg; browns of this group have grass-feeding caterpillars. General ecology.
pseudonympha varii.about: Pseudonympha is a genus of butterflies from the subfamily Satyrinae in the family Nymphalidae.

pseudopanurgus aestivalis.name: Aestival Bare-miner
pseudopanurgus aestivalis.desc: Aestival Bare-miner (Pseudopanurgus aestivalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

pseudopus apodus.name: European glass lizard
pseudopus apodus.desc: A big legless lizard that eats insects, snails and small vertebrates, including other lizards in GloBI records.
pseudopus apodus.about: The sheltopusik, also spelled scheltopusik, sheltopusick, scheltopusick, sheltopusic, or scheltopusic, and also commonly known as Pallas's glass lizard, the European legless lizard, or the European…

pseudorca crassidens.name: False killer whale
pseudorca crassidens.desc: A toothed whale that preys on large fish such as adult yellowfin tuna.
pseudorca crassidens.about: The false killer whale is a species of oceanic dolphin that is the only extant representative of the genus Pseudorca. It is found in oceans worldwide but mainly in tropical regions.

pseudoroegneria.name: Bunchgrasses and sedges
pseudoroegneria.desc: Native grasses and sedges that grow among the sagebrush and in wet meadows, grazed by elk and bison.
pseudoroegneria.about: Pseudoroegneria spicata is a species of perennial bunchgrass known by the common name bluebunch wheatgrass. It is native to western North America.

pseudoroegneria spicata.name: Bluebunch wheatgrass
pseudoroegneria spicata.desc: A bunchgrass of the northern range and the base of the grazing chain for elk, bison and pronghorn.
pseudoroegneria spicata.about: Pseudoroegneria spicata is a species of perennial bunchgrass known by the common name bluebunch wheatgrass. It is native to western North America.

pseudoryx nghetinhensis.name: Saola
pseudoryx nghetinhensis.desc: A rare ox-like animal confined to the Annamite Range, listed in the park as possibly present. It feeds on leaves, including spleenwort, pulled into the mouth with a long tongue.
pseudoryx nghetinhensis.about: The saola, also called the spindlehorn, Asian unicorn, or infrequently, Vũ Quang bovid, is a forest-dwelling bovid native to the Annamite Range in Vietnam and Laos.

pseudotsuga menziesii.name: Douglas Fir
pseudotsuga menziesii.desc: A dominant tall conifer of the lower forests. Its seeds are eaten by Douglas squirrels, chickadees and other small animals.
pseudotsuga menziesii.about: The Douglas fir is a conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae. It is the tallest tree in the family.

psidium cattleianum.name: Strawberry guava
psidium cattleianum.desc: An introduced fruiting tree that invades native forest. Several birds and feral pigs eat its fruit and spread the seeds.
psidium cattleianum.about: Psidium cattleyanum, commonly known as Cattley guava, strawberry guava or cherry guava, is a small tree (2–6 m (6 ft 7 in – 19 ft 8 in) tall) in the Myrtaceae (myrtle) family.

psilocorsis reflexella.name: Dotted Leaftier
psilocorsis reflexella.desc: Dotted Leaftier (Psilocorsis reflexella): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
psilocorsis reflexella.about: Psilocorsis reflexella (dotted leaftier moth) is a species of moth of the family Depressariidae.

psilopogon pulcherrimus.name: Golden-naped barbet
psilopogon pulcherrimus.desc: A montane Bornean bird recorded thousands of times near the park; barbets in general take fruit such as figs.
psilopogon pulcherrimus.about: The golden-naped barbet is a member of the family Megalaimidae. It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia, where it is endemic to the island of Borneo.

psyche casta.name: Moth
psyche casta.desc: Moth (Psyche casta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

psychotria nervosa.name: Seminole Balsamo
psychotria nervosa.desc: Seminole Balsamo (Psychotria nervosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

psychotria tenuifolia.name: Wild coffee
psychotria tenuifolia.desc: Wild coffee (Psychotria tenuifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 34 times near the park in GBIF.

pteralopex taki.name: New Georgia monkey-faced bat
pteralopex taki.desc: A large fruit bat found in the Solomon Islands. Fruit bats eat fruit and are food for the Sanford's sea eagle.
pteralopex taki.about: The New Georgian monkey-faced bat or New Georgian flying monkey is a recently described species of megabat endemic to the New Georgia and Vangunu Islands.

pteridium aquilinum.name: Bracken
pteridium aquilinum.desc: A fern of forest clearings and edges that spreads across open ground.
pteridium aquilinum.about: Pteridium aquilinum, commonly called bracken, brake, pasture brake, common bracken, and also known as eagle fern, is a species of fern occurring in temperate and subtropical regions in both…

pterocles coronatus.name: Crowned sandgrouse
pterocles coronatus.desc: A ground-dwelling desert bird that feeds mainly on seeds.
pterocles coronatus.about: The crowned sandgrouse is a species of bird in the sandgrouse family, the Pteroclidae from North Africa and the Middle East.

pterodroma hypoleuca.name: Bonin petrel
pterodroma hypoleuca.desc: A seabird that nests in burrows on the islands and feeds at sea. Rats and cats are predators of burrow nests.
pterodroma hypoleuca.about: The Bonin petrel or nunulu is a seabird in the family Procellariidae. It is a small gadfly petrel that is found in the northwest Pacific Ocean.

pterois volitans.name: Red lionfish
pterois volitans.desc: Invasive fish that eats small fish and crustaceans on Caribbean reefs and can cut the numbers of native reef fish.
pterois volitans.about: The red lionfish is a venomous coral reef fish in the family Scorpaenidae, order Scorpaeniformes.

pteronura brasiliensis.name: Giant otter
pteronura brasiliensis.desc: Hunts fish in family groups along river banks.
pteronura brasiliensis.about: The giant otter or giant river otter is a South American carnivorous mammal. It is the longest member of the weasel family, Mustelidae, reaching up to 1.8 m (5 ft 11 in).

pteropus anetianus.name: Vanuatu flying fox
pteropus anetianus.desc: A fruit bat found only in Vanuatu and listed as Vulnerable. Flying foxes are fruit and nectar eaters and are hunted for food on Santo.
pteropus anetianus.about: The Vanuatu flying fox or white flying fox is a species of flying fox in the family Pteropodidae. It is endemic to Vanuatu.

pteropus conspicillatus.name: Spectacled flying fox
pteropus conspicillatus.desc: Feeds mainly on rainforest fruit and on flowers of Syzygium and eucalypts. Endangered, partly after a 2018-19 heatwave.
pteropus conspicillatus.about: The spectacled flying fox, also known as the spectacled fruit bat, is a megabat that lives in Australia's north-eastern regions of Queensland.

pteropus lylei.name: Lyle's flying fox
pteropus lylei.desc: A large fruit bat of Cambodia and nearby countries that roosts in trees and feeds on fruit such as strawberry tree.
pteropus lylei.about: Lyle's flying fox is a species of flying fox in the family Pteropodidae. It is found in Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam, with an outlying population in Yunnan, China.

pteropus pselaphon.name: Bonin flying fox
pteropus pselaphon.desc: Endemic fruit bat of the Ogasawara and Volcano Islands, listed as endangered. It eats fruit such as Pandanus and flowers.
pteropus pselaphon.about: The Bonin flying fox, also known as Bonin fruit bat, is a species of flying fox in the family Pteropodidae.

pteropus rufus.name: Madagascan flying fox
pteropus rufus.desc: A large fruit bat that roosts in groups and feeds at night on fruit and flowers.
pteropus rufus.about: The Madagascan flying fox, Madagascar flying-fox, or Madagascar fruit bat is a species of megabat in the genus Pteropus. It is endemic to Madagascar.

pteropus samoensis.name: Samoa flying fox
pteropus samoensis.desc: A fruit bat that feeds on fruit, leaves and flowers in forest. Hunting and forest clearance threaten it.
pteropus samoensis.about: The Samoa flying fox or Samoan flying fox is a species of flying fox in the family Pteropodidae. It is found in American Samoa, Fiji, and Samoa (where it is known as pe'a and pe'a vao).

pteropus tonganus.name: Pacific flying fox
pteropus tonganus.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, pollen and nectar, and pollinates some trees as it feeds.
pteropus tonganus.about: The insular flying fox or Pacific flying fox is a species of flying fox in the family Pteropodidae.

ptilinopus cinctus.name: Black-backed fruit dove
ptilinopus cinctus.desc: A very commonly recorded forest bird of the area that feeds mainly on fruit, including figs, and spreads seeds.
ptilinopus cinctus.about: The banded fruit dove or black-backed fruit dove is a large (38–44 cm in length, 450-570 g in weight) pigeon with white head, neck and upper breast; black back and upperwing grading to grey on rump;…

ptilinopus greyi.name: Red-bellied fruit dove
ptilinopus greyi.desc: A fruit dove of lowland forest in Vanuatu, New Caledonia and the Santa Cruz Islands, and one of the most recorded birds near Santo.
ptilinopus greyi.about: The red-bellied fruit dove is a species of bird in the family Columbidae.

ptilotus exaltatus.name: Pink mulla mulla
ptilotus exaltatus.desc: A showy desert wildflower that blooms after rain. Galahs have been recorded eating it.
ptilotus exaltatus.about: Ptilotus exaltatus, commonly known as tall mulla mulla, large pink pussy-tails, pink mulla mulla , lambs tail, or showy foxtail, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae and is…

ptyas mucosa.name: Oriental rat snake
ptyas mucosa.desc: A fast ground snake of forest and fields that eats small vertebrates and is itself prey of the king cobra.
ptyas mucosa.about: Ptyas mucosa, commonly known as the Oriental rat snake, or Indian rat snake, is a common non-venomous species of colubrid snake found in parts of South and Southeast Asia. These are large snakes.

ptyodactylus ragazzii.name: Ragazzi's fan-footed gecko
ptyodactylus ragazzii.desc: Rock-dwelling gecko recorded near the lake that hunts small insects such as locusts and other arthropods.
ptyodactylus ragazzii.about: Ptyodactylus is a genus of geckos, which are commonly known as fan-fingered geckos. The genus has 12 described species.

pueraria montana.name: Kudzu
pueraria montana.desc: Kudzu (Pueraria montana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

pugettia producta.name: Kelp crab
pugettia producta.desc: A crab of kelp holdfasts and canopy that grazes on kelp; kelp crabs are among the animals that eat kelp.
pugettia producta.about: Pugettia producta, known as the northern kelp crab or shield-backed kelp crab, is a species of crab in the family Epialtidae.

puma concolor.name: Puma
puma concolor.desc: Puma (Puma concolor): a top predator in this web. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
puma concolor.about: The cougar, also called puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther, is a large small cat native to the Americas.

puma concolor coryi.name: Florida panther
puma concolor coryi.desc: A rare big cat that hunts deer, hogs, raccoons and other mammals. Pythons eat the same prey.
puma concolor coryi.about: The Florida panther is a North American cougar population in South Florida. It lives in pinelands, tropical hardwood hammocks and mixed freshwater swamp forests.

purshia stansburiana.name: Stansbury cliffrose
purshia stansburiana.desc: A woody desert shrub. Wikipedia lists cliffrose among the plants mule deer commonly browse.
purshia stansburiana.about: Purshia stansburyana is a species of flowering plant in the rose family known by the common name Stansbury's cliffrose.

purshia tridentata.name: Antelope bitterbrush
purshia tridentata.desc: Antelope bitterbrush (Purshia tridentata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 161 times near the park in GBIF.
purshia tridentata.about: Purshia tridentata, with the common name bitterbrush, is a shrub in the genus Purshia of the family Rosaceae. It is native to mountainous areas of western North America.

pusa hispida.name: Ringed seal
pusa hispida.desc: Lives under the ice, keeping breathing holes open and hunting cod.
pusa hispida.about: The ringed seal is a small earless seal species found in Arctic and sub-Arctic regions. Its common name is derived from a distinctive patterning of dark spots surrounded by light gray rings.

pusa sibirica.name: Baikal seal (nerpa)
pusa sibirica.desc: The only seal living entirely in fresh water. Golomyanka make up most of its diet, and it digs breathing holes and dens in the ice.
pusa sibirica.about: The Baikal seal, also known as Lake Baikal seal or nerpa (нерпа), is a species of earless seal endemic to Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia.

pycnanthemum muticum.name: Blunt Mountain-mint
pycnanthemum muticum.desc: Blunt Mountain-mint (Pycnanthemum muticum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

pycnanthemum tenuifolium.name: Narrow-leaf Mountain-mint
pycnanthemum tenuifolium.desc: Narrow-leaf Mountain-mint (Pycnanthemum tenuifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

pycnonotus barbatus.name: Common bulbul
pycnonotus barbatus.desc: A common fruit-eating songbird; records show it eating the fruits of Ilex, Macaranga, Maesa and Tarenna.
pycnonotus barbatus.about: The common bulbul is a member of the bulbul family of passerine birds. It is widespread throughout most of Africa except for the very arid areas, and has recently begun breeding in southernmost Spain.

pycnonotus cafer.name: Red-vented bulbul
pycnonotus cafer.desc: A well-recorded songbird that eats fruit and insects. GloBI records include it eating Melastoma and being eaten by the green vine snake.
pycnonotus cafer.about: The red-vented bulbul is a member of the bulbul family of passerines. It is a resident breeder across South Asia extending east to Burma.

pycnonotus jocosus.name: Red-whiskered bulbul
pycnonotus jocosus.desc: The best-recorded bird in the surrounding area. It eats fruit and insects, and spreads seeds.
pycnonotus jocosus.about: The red-whiskered bulbul, or crested bulbul, is a passerine bird native to Asia. It is a member of the bulbul family.

pycnopodia helianthoides.name: Sunflower sea star
pycnopodia helianthoides.desc: A big predatory sea star that eats many urchins. Sea star wasting disease wiped it out from California waters from 2013, and urchins have been rising since.
pycnopodia helianthoides.about: Pycnopodia helianthoides, commonly known as the sunflower sea star, is a large sea star found in the northeastern Pacific Ocean.

pygathrix nemaeus.name: Red-shanked douc
pygathrix nemaeus.desc: A colourful leaf-eating monkey. Wikipedia says the park runs a semi-wild zone that protects primates such as the douc.
pygathrix nemaeus.about: The red-shanked douc is an arboreal and diurnal Old World monkey belonging to the Colobinae subfamily. They are endemic to Laos, Vietnam, and Cambodia.

pygocentrus nattereri.name: Red-bellied piranha
pygocentrus nattereri.desc: Hunts fish in groups and scavenges dead animals in the river.
pygocentrus nattereri.about: The red-bellied piranha, also known as the red piranha, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish belonging to the family Serrasalmidae, which includes the pacus, piranhas and related fishes.

pygoctenucha terminalis.name: Pygoctenucha terminalis
pygoctenucha terminalis.desc: Pygoctenucha terminalis (Pygoctenucha terminalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
pygoctenucha terminalis.about: Pygoctenucha terminalis, the blue-green lichen moth, is a moth in the family Erebidae. It was described by Francis Walker in 1854.

pygoscelis adeliae.name: Adelie penguin
pygoscelis adeliae.desc: Ice-dependent penguin that feeds on krill. Leopard seals hunt it.
pygoscelis adeliae.about: The Adélie penguin is a species of penguin common along the entire coast of the Antarctic continent.

pygoscelis papua.name: Gentoo penguin
pygoscelis papua.desc: Penguin of the Peninsula that eats krill and fish. Leopard seals prey on it.
pygoscelis papua.about: The gentoo penguin is a penguin species (and possibly species complex) in the genus Pygoscelis, most closely related to the Adélie penguin (P. adeliae) and the chinstrap penguin (P. antarcticus).

pylodictis olivaris.name: Flathead catfish
pylodictis olivaris.desc: Mostly eats fish once larger than about 25 cm. Prey includes gizzard shad, drum, carp and crayfish.
pylodictis olivaris.about: The flathead catfish, also called by several common names including mudcat or shovelhead cat, is a large species of North American freshwater catfish in the family Ictaluridae.

pyrisitia lisa.name: Little Sulphur
pyrisitia lisa.desc: Little Sulphur (Pyrisitia lisa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

pyrrharctia isabella.name: Banded Woollybear
pyrrharctia isabella.desc: Banded Woollybear (Pyrrharctia isabella): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

pyrrhocorax graculus.name: Alpine chough
pyrrhocorax graculus.desc: Cliff-nesting crow that eats insects in summer and berries in colder months. Golden eagles and ravens take choughs or their young.
pyrrhocorax graculus.about: The Alpine chough or yellow-billed chough is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax.

pyrus.name: Wild pears
pyrus.desc: The reserve is home to several wild pear species, including ones named after the area, whose fruit feeds many animals.
pyrus.about: Pears are a genus of trees, Pyrus , in the family Rosaceae, that bear an edible apple-like fruit of the same name.

python bivittatus.name: Burmese python
python bivittatus.desc: An invasive constrictor released from the pet trade. It eats mammals and birds, and has caused steep declines in medium-sized mammals.
python bivittatus.about: The Burmese python is one of the largest species of snakes. It is native to a large area of Southeast Asia and is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

python molurus.name: Indian rock python
python molurus.desc: A large constrictor that GloBI records eating hog deer.
python molurus.about: The Indian python is a large python species native to tropical and subtropical regions of the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

python natalensis.name: African rock python
python natalensis.desc: An ambush predator that takes birds and medium-sized mammals such as impala.
python natalensis.about: The Central African rock python is a species of large constrictor snake in the family Pythonidae. The species is native to sub-Saharan Africa.

python regius.name: Ball python
python regius.desc: A constrictor that eats rodents and other small vertebrates; recorded prey includes forest rodents and the forest giant squirrel.
python regius.about: The ball python, also called the royal python, is a python species native to West and Central Africa, where it lives in grasslands, shrublands and open forests.

python sebae.name: African rock python
python sebae.desc: A large forest snake. Wikipedia names a rock python among predators of young pygmy hippos.
python sebae.about: The Central African rock python is a species of large constrictor snake in the family Pythonidae. The species is native to sub-Saharan Africa.

qualea.name: Fire-adapted cerrado trees
qualea.desc: Qualea trees dominate much of the Cerrado. Many Cerrado trees have thick corky bark that protects them from fire.
qualea.about: Qualea is a flowering plant genus in the family Vochysiaceae. These plants occur in the Neotropics and their wood makes good timber and firewood and is used in construction.

quercus.name: Oaks
quercus.desc: Black oak dominates savanna on sandy soils per Wikipedia, which lists Indiana Dunes as a remnant oak savanna. Acorns feed many animals.
quercus.about: An oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family. They have spirally arranged leaves, often with lobed edges, and a nut called an acorn, borne within a cup.

quercus agrifolia.name: California live oak
quercus agrifolia.desc: California live oak (Quercus agrifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 193 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus alba.name: White Oak
quercus alba.desc: White Oak (Quercus alba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus alba.about: Quercus alba, the white oak, is one of the preeminent hardwoods of eastern and central North America.

quercus alnifolia.name: Golden oak
quercus alnifolia.desc: Endemic to Cyprus; the main broadleaved tree of the conifer forests. Its stands hold soil on stony slopes and build humus.
quercus alnifolia.about: Quercus alnifolia, commonly known as the golden oak, is an evergreen oak species of Cyprus. Its common English name refers to the golden coloured lower surface of its leaves.

quercus aquifolioides.name: Hengduan Mountain oak
quercus aquifolioides.desc: An evergreen mountain oak recorded often around the area. Its acorns and leaves feed forest animals.
quercus aquifolioides.about: Quercus aquifolioides is a species of oak native to south-central China and Tibet. It is in the subgenus Cerris, section Ilex.

quercus castaneifolia.name: Chestnut-leaved oak
quercus castaneifolia.desc: A Hyrcanian forest oak, recorded often near the park. Its acorns are food for forest mammals.
quercus castaneifolia.about: Quercus castaneifolia, the chestnut-leaved oak, is a species of oak in the turkey oak section Quercus sect. Cerris.

quercus chrysolepis.name: Canyon live oak
quercus chrysolepis.desc: CANYON LIVE OAK (Quercus chrysolepis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 77 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus chrysolepis.about: Quercus chrysolepis, commonly termed canyon live oak, canyon oak, golden cup oak or maul oak, is a North American species of evergreen oak.

quercus coccinea.name: Scarlet Oak
quercus coccinea.desc: Scarlet Oak (Quercus coccinea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus douglasii.name: Blue oak
quercus douglasii.desc: Dominant tree of the dry blue oak woodland in the Sierra foothills, alongside gray pine and other oaks. Its acorns are eaten by wildlife.
quercus douglasii.about: Quercus douglasii, known as blue oak, is a species of oak endemic to California, common in the Coast Ranges and the foothills of the Sierra Nevada.

quercus emoryi.name: Emory oak
quercus emoryi.desc: Emory oak (Quercus emoryi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus falcata.name: Spanish oak
quercus falcata.desc: Spanish oak (Quercus falcata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus fusiformis.name: Texas live oak
quercus fusiformis.desc: Texas live oak (Quercus fusiformis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus gambelii.name: Gambel oak
quercus gambelii.desc: Oak scrub of the canyon rim. Deer browse it and squirrels and bears eat the acorns; it regrows from root sprouts after fire.
quercus gambelii.about: Quercus gambelii, with the common name Gambel oak, is a deciduous small tree or large shrub that is widespread in the foothills and lower mountains of western North America.

quercus geminata.name: Sand live oak
quercus geminata.desc: Sand live oak (Quercus geminata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus giffordii.name: Quercus giffordii
quercus giffordii.desc: Quercus giffordii (Quercus giffordii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus hypoleucoides.name: Silverleaf oak
quercus hypoleucoides.desc: Silverleaf oak (Quercus hypoleucoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 127 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus hypoleucoides.about: Quercus hypoleucoides, the silverleaf oak or the whiteleaf oak, is a North American species of oak tree or shrub. It grows in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico.

quercus ilicifolia.name: Bear Oak
quercus ilicifolia.desc: Bear Oak (Quercus ilicifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus imbricaria.name: Shingle oak
quercus imbricaria.desc: Shingle oak (Quercus imbricaria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus infectoria, quercus coccifera.name: Oaks
quercus infectoria, quercus coccifera.desc: Oak woodland, including kermes oak, is among the most recorded vegetation near the reserve. Acorns feed wild boar.
quercus infectoria, quercus coccifera.about: Quercus coccifera, commonly known as kermes oak, holly oak, or Palestine oak, is an evergreen oak shrub or tree in section Ilex of the genus. It has many synonyms, including Quercus calliprinos.

quercus john-tuckeri.name: Tucker's oak
quercus john-tuckeri.desc: Tucker's oak (Quercus john-tuckeri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus john-tuckeri.about: Quercus john-tuckeri is a North American species of oak known by the common name Tucker oak, or Tucker's oak.

quercus kelloggii.name: California black oak
quercus kelloggii.desc: A mid-elevation oak whose acorns and leaves feed deer, bears and rodents.
quercus kelloggii.about: Quercus kelloggii, the California black oak or Kellogg oak, is an oak in the red oak section (genus Quercus, section Lobatae, series Agrifoliae) native to western North America.

quercus laevis.name: Catesby's oak
quercus laevis.desc: Catesby's oak (Quercus laevis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus laevis.about: Quercus laevis, the turkey oak, is a member of the red oak group of oaks. It is native to the southeastern United States.

quercus lobata.name: Roble
quercus lobata.desc: Roble (Quercus lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 161 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus macranthera.name: Caucasian oak
quercus macranthera.desc: Forms the oak woodland at higher elevations, producing acorns and shade for the forest community.
quercus macranthera.about: Quercus macranthera, commonly called as the Caucasian oak, or the Persian oak, is a species of deciduous tree native to Western Asia that is occasionally grown as an ornamental tree in Europe growing…

quercus macrocarpa.name: Bur oak
quercus macrocarpa.desc: Bur oak (Quercus macrocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus macrocarpa.about: Quercus macrocarpa, the bur oak or burr oak, is a species of oak tree native to central and eastern North America. It is in the white oak section, Quercus sect.

quercus marilandica.name: Blackjack oak
quercus marilandica.desc: Blackjack oak (Quercus marilandica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus marilandica.about: Quercus marilandica, the blackjack oak, is a small oak, one of the red oak group Quercus sect. Lobatae.

quercus michauxii.name: Basket oak
quercus michauxii.desc: A bottomland oak of the floodplain whose acorns are mast for deer, squirrels and hogs. Congaree holds many champion trees.
quercus michauxii.about: Quercus michauxii, the swamp chestnut oak, is a species of oak in the white oak section Quercus section Quercus in the beech family.

quercus mongolica.name: Mongolian oak
quercus mongolica.desc: One of the main trees of the peninsula lowland forests. Its acorns are a food for bears and rodents.
quercus mongolica.about: Quercus mongolica, commonly known as Mongolian oak, is a species of oak native to Japan, northern China, Korea, Mongolia, and southeastern Siberia. The species can grow to be 30 metres (98 feet) tall.

quercus montana.name: Chestnut oak
quercus montana.desc: Chestnut oak (Quercus montana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus muehlenbergii.name: Chinkapin oak
quercus muehlenbergii.desc: Chinkapin oak (Quercus muehlenbergii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus muehlenbergii.about: Quercus muehlenbergii, the chinquapin (or chinkapin) oak, is a deciduous species of tree in the white oak group.

quercus nigra.name: Water Oak
quercus nigra.desc: Water Oak (Quercus nigra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus nigra.about: Quercus nigra, the water oak, is an oak in the red oak group, native to the eastern and south-central United States, found in all the coastal states from New Jersey to Texas, and inland as far as…

quercus oglethorpensis.name: Oglethorpe oak
quercus oglethorpensis.desc: Oglethorpe oak (Quercus oglethorpensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus petraea.name: Sessile oak
quercus petraea.desc: A widespread forest oak in the area and the best recorded tree in the GBIF records. Its acorns feed deer, boar, jays and rodents.
quercus petraea.about: Quercus petraea, commonly known as the sessile oak, Welsh oak, Cornish oak, Irish oak or durmast oak, is a species of deciduous oak tree in the flowering plant family Fagaceae.

quercus phellos.name: Willow oak
quercus phellos.desc: Willow oak (Quercus phellos): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus robur.name: Pedunculate oak
quercus robur.desc: Giant old oaks, some individually named, grow in the forest. Their acorns and shoots feed boar, deer and voles.
quercus robur.about: Quercus robur, pedunculate oak, European oak, or English oak, is a species of flowering plant in the beech and oak family, Fagaceae.

quercus rubra.name: Red Oak
quercus rubra.desc: Red Oak (Quercus rubra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus rubra.about: Quercus rubra, the northern red oak or common red oak, is an oak tree in the red oak group.

quercus rugosa.name: Netleaf oak
quercus rugosa.desc: Netleaf oak (Quercus rugosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 104 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus rugosa.about: Quercus rugosa, commonly known as the netleaf oak, is a broad-leaved tree in the beech and oak family Fagaceae. It is native to southern North America.

quercus spp..name: Oaks (white oak and relatives)
quercus spp..desc: The dominant upland trees. The MDC lists white oak acorns as food for turkeys, deer, squirrels, jays, raccoons and mice, with acorns ripening in autumn.
quercus spp..about: Quercus alba, the white oak, is one of the preeminent hardwoods of eastern and central North America.

quercus stellata.name: Post Oak
quercus stellata.desc: Post Oak (Quercus stellata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus suber.name: Cork oak
quercus suber.desc: An evergreen oak of the park's Mediterranean woodland. Red deer and wild boar feed on its acorns and foliage.
quercus suber.about: Quercus suber, commonly called the cork oak, is a medium-sized, evergreen oak tree in the section Quercus sect. Cerris.

quercus texana.name: Texas red oak
quercus texana.desc: Texas red oak (Quercus texana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus turbinella.name: Sonoran scrub oak
quercus turbinella.desc: Sonoran scrub oak (Quercus turbinella): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

quercus velutina.name: Black Oak
quercus velutina.desc: Black Oak (Quercus velutina): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus velutina.about: Quercus velutina (Latin 'velutina', "velvety") , the black oak, is a species of oak in the red oak group, native and widespread in eastern and central North America.

quercus virginiana.name: Live oak
quercus virginiana.desc: Live oak (Quercus virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
quercus virginiana.about: Quercus virginiana, also known as the southern live oak, is an semi-evergreen oak tree native to the Southeastern United States Coastal Plain.

quercus, carya.name: Oaks & hickories
quercus, carya.desc: Dominant trees of the drier forest. Their acorns and nuts are the fall mast that bears, turkeys, deer and squirrels fatten on.
quercus, carya.about: An oak is a hardwood tree or shrub in the genus Quercus of the beech family. They have spirally arranged leaves, often with lobed edges, and a nut called an acorn, borne within a cup.

quincula lobata.name: Purple-ground-cherry
quincula lobata.desc: Purple-ground-cherry (Quincula lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
quincula lobata.about: Quincula is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the nightshade family, Solanaceae.

quiscalus major.name: BOAT-TAILED GRACKLE
quiscalus major.desc: BOAT-TAILED GRACKLE (Quiscalus major): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 339 times near the park in GBIF.
quiscalus major.about: The boat-tailed grackle is a passerine bird of the family Icteridae found as a permanent resident on the coasts of the Southeastern and Mid-Atlantic United States.

quiscalus mexicanus.name: Great-tailed Grackle
quiscalus mexicanus.desc: Great-tailed Grackle (Quiscalus mexicanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

quiscalus quiscula.name: Common Grackle
quiscalus quiscula.desc: Common Grackle (Quiscalus quiscula): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
quiscalus quiscula.about: The common grackle is an icterid bird found in large numbers through much of North America. It was first described in 1758 by Carl Linnaeus and has three officially recognized subspecies.

rafetus euphraticus.name: Euphrates softshell turtle
rafetus euphraticus.desc: An opportunistic omnivore of rivers and marshes, eating crabs, plants, insects and fish and readily taking carcasses.
rafetus euphraticus.about: The Euphrates softshell turtle, also known as the Mesopotamian softshell turtle, is a species of softshell turtle in the family Trionychidae.

rafflesia keithii.name: Rafflesia
rafflesia keithii.desc: A parasitic flowering plant that lives inside a host vine and shows itself only as a huge flower; endemic to Sabah.
rafflesia keithii.about: Rafflesia Keithii is a part of the largest parasitic genus of flowers in the world that is currently endangered. The plant is native to Sabah.1 Sabah is a state that is located in northern Malaysia.

rain.name: Rain
rain.desc: Wet Pacific air dumps heavy precipitation on the mountain, feeding the old-growth forest on its lower slopes.

rain & cloud moisture.name: Rain & cloud moisture
rain & cloud moisture.desc: Cool, humid summers and dry winters, with cloud-forest moisture, support the oyamel forest.

rain & humidity.name: Rain & humidity
rain & humidity.desc: Wet, humid air keeps ravines moist for hemlock and rhododendron.

rain & meltwater.name: Rain & meltwater
rain & meltwater.desc: Water from rain and melting snow feeds streams and waterfalls such as the Krimml Waterfalls and keeps the alpine meadows watered.

rain & mountain fog.name: Rain & mountain fog
rain & mountain fog.desc: Heavy rainfall and cool, moist air keep the high forests and streams wet.

rain & mountain moisture.name: Rain & mountain moisture
rain & mountain moisture.desc: The park gets roughly 50 inches of rain a year with no dry season, plus winter snow, which keeps the ridge forests and streams moist.

rain & river floods.name: Rain & river floods
rain & river floods.desc: Daily rain and yearly river floods carry nutrients and open the forest to fish.

rain & rock creek.name: Rain & Rock Creek
rain & rock creek.desc: Rain feeds Rock Creek, the stream running through the park. Stormwater runoff from the surrounding city pollutes the waterways.

rain & snow.name: Rain & snow
rain & snow.desc: Precipitation is scarce in this semi-arid country, and it controls how green the grass gets.

rain & snowfall.name: Rain & snowfall
rain & snowfall.desc: The west side gets far more precipitation than the east, with deep snowpacks of 10 to 25 feet at their early March peak in the mountains.

rain & snowmelt.name: Rain & snowmelt
rain & snowmelt.desc: Under 10 inches of rain fall a year, and unpredictably. The soil crust absorbs and holds what does arrive.

rain & spring recharge.name: Rain & spring recharge
rain & spring recharge.desc: Rain soaking into the mountains feeds the hot springs and the forest, which is why the park is managed to protect the water system.

rain & tepui mist.name: Rain & tepui mist
rain & tepui mist.desc: The Gran Sabana gets roughly 1,600 to 2,200 mm of rain a year, with a rainy season of about ten months.

rain and cloud.name: Rain and cloud
rain and cloud.desc: Wet windward slopes feed the rainforest, while the dry Kaʻū side stays arid.

rain and cloud mist.name: Rain and cloud mist
rain and cloud mist.desc: Heavy rainfall and cloud on the Andean slope feed the park's forests and bromeliads.

rain and mist.name: Rain and mist
rain and mist.desc: Frequent cloud and rain on the volcano slopes keep the montane forest, bamboo and vine zones growing.

rain and river mist.name: Rain and river mist
rain and river mist.desc: Wikipedia gives the Alto Parana forest roughly 1,200 to 1,600 mm of rain a year, with a drier season from April to September.

rain and rivers.name: Rain and rivers
rain and rivers.desc: The park drains to the Soča (Adriatic) and the Sava (Black Sea), with waterfalls, gorges and glacial lakes.

rain and rock run-off.name: Rain and rock run-off
rain and rock run-off.desc: Rainfall is low and irregular. Rain also pours off the rock domes and concentrates water and nutrients in drainage lines and at their bases.

rain and sea mist.name: Rain and sea mist
rain and sea mist.desc: Moist ocean air rising over the Serra do Mar slopes brings heavy rain to the escarpment forests, which keeps them lush.

rain and snow.name: Rain and snow
rain and snow.desc: Mount Washington receives very high precipitation, about 91 inches a year, feeding moist forests and alpine plants.

rain and snowmelt.name: Rain and snowmelt
rain and snowmelt.desc: Water sinks quickly into the limestone, and underground rivers drain some of the glacial lakes, so streams and lakes matter more than the dry slopes suggest.

rain and streams.name: Rain and streams
rain and streams.desc: Abundant precipitation feeds the mountain streams, beaver ponds and forest wetlands.

rain and typhoons.name: Rain and typhoons
rain and typhoons.desc: Rain waters the islands, which have no big rivers, and typhoon winds shape the wind-clipped scrub on ridges and cliffs.

rain, fog and snow.name: Rain, fog and snow
rain, fog and snow.desc: Moisture from the Gulf of St. Lawrence and a snowy winter shape the plants that grow here, from forest to coastal bog.

rainfall.name: Rainfall
rainfall.desc: Rain and river water set how much the plants can grow.

rainfall and cloud.name: Rainfall and cloud
rainfall and cloud.desc: Trade winds rise over the mountains and drop heavy rain, in places over six metres a year, with no distinct dry season.

rainforest soil.name: Rainforest soil
rainforest soil.desc: Nutrients held in thin, wet soils are recycled quickly from fallen leaves and dead wood.

rainwater depressions (rawdat).name: Rainwater depressions (rawdat)
rainwater depressions (rawdat).desc: Shallow depressions called rawdat collect rainwater and hold richer plant life than the surrounding rocky desert.

rainy season.name: Rainy season
rainy season.desc: Seasonal rain raises the river and floods low ground, and manatees move up rivers in the wet season.

ramganga and reservoir.name: Ramganga and reservoir
ramganga and reservoir.desc: The Ramganga runs through the reserve and the Kalagarh dam flooded about 80 km2 of riverine land, creating habitat for fish and gharial.

ramphastos dicolorus.name: Red-breasted toucan
ramphastos dicolorus.desc: A large-billed bird that swallows fruit whole, including palm fruit, and drops the seeds away from the parent plant.
ramphastos dicolorus.about: The red-breasted toucan or green-billed toucan is a bird in the family Ramphastidae, the toucans, toucanets, and aracaris. It is found in Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay.

ramphastos sulfuratus.name: Keel-billed toucan
ramphastos sulfuratus.desc: Eats mainly fruit, including black poisonwood and wax mallow, and also takes small animals such as birds.
ramphastos sulfuratus.about: The keel-billed toucan, also known as rainbow-billed toucan or sulphur-breasted toucan, is a species of toucan native to southern Mexico, Central America and the far northwest of South America, and…

ramphastos toco.name: Toco toucan
ramphastos toco.desc: Swallows whole fruit and drops the seeds far from the parent tree.
ramphastos toco.about: The toco toucan is a species of bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.

ramphastos tucanus.name: White-throated toucan
ramphastos tucanus.desc: The most recorded bird near Yasuni. Large-billed fruit eater that swallows fruit whole.
ramphastos tucanus.about: The white-throated toucan is a bird in the family Ramphastidae found in South America throughout the Amazon Basin including the adjacent Tocantins and Araguaia River drainage.

rana iberica.name: Iberian frog
rana iberica.desc: Frog of cool mountain streams, catching small invertebrates; widely eaten by snakes, birds and mammals.
rana iberica.about: The Iberian frog, also known as Iberian stream frog, is a species of frog in the family Ranidae found in Portugal and Spain. Its natural habitats are rivers, mountain streams and swamps.

rana temporaria.name: Common frog
rana temporaria.desc: Amphibian of wet heath and pools that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Snakes, foxes and raptors eat it.
