rana temporaria.about: The common frog or grass frog, also known as the European common frog, European common brown frog, European grass frog, European Holarctic true frog, European pond frog, European brown frog, or…

rangifer tarandus.name: Caribou
rangifer tarandus.desc: Migrates in large herds, eating lichen in winter and sedges in summer.
rangifer tarandus.about: The reindeer or caribou is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to the Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.

rangifer tarandus caribou.name: Woodland caribou
rangifer tarandus caribou.desc: Feeds heavily on lichens. Wikipedia lists boreal woodland caribou as threatened.
rangifer tarandus caribou.about: The reindeer or caribou is a species of deer with circumpolar distribution, native to the Arctic, subarctic, tundra, boreal, and mountainous regions of Northern Europe, Siberia, and North America.

ranunculus glaberrimus.name: Sagebrush buttercup
ranunculus glaberrimus.desc: Sagebrush buttercup (Ranunculus glaberrimus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
ranunculus glaberrimus.about: Ranunculus glaberrimus, the sagebrush buttercup, is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family, Ranunculaceae.

ranunculus harveyi.name: Harvey's buttercup
ranunculus harveyi.desc: Harvey's buttercup (Ranunculus harveyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.

ranunculus hispidus.name: Bristly buttercup
ranunculus hispidus.desc: Bristly buttercup (Ranunculus hispidus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
ranunculus hispidus.about: Ranunculus hispidus is a species of perennial flowering plant in the buttercup family, Ranunculaceae. It is commonly known as bristly buttercup or hispid buttercup.

ranunculus recurvatus.name: Blisterwort
ranunculus recurvatus.desc: Blisterwort (Ranunculus recurvatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

ranunculus sceleratus.name: Celery-leaved Buttercup
ranunculus sceleratus.desc: Celery-leaved Buttercup (Ranunculus sceleratus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
ranunculus sceleratus.about: Ranunculus sceleratus known by the common names celery-leaved buttercup, celery-leaf buttercup, and cursed buttercup is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae.

raphanus raphanistrum.name: Wild Radish
raphanus raphanistrum.desc: Wild Radish (Raphanus raphanistrum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

raphia.name: Raffia palms
raphia.desc: Palms of swamps and wet ground. Their fruit is a main food of the palm-nut vulture.

rare rainfall.name: Rare rainfall
rare rainfall.desc: Rain is scarce and unpredictable across the Sahara. A shower can briefly turn dry wadis and sand green with grasses.

rare winter rain.name: Rare winter rain
rare winter rain.desc: Rain is scarce and irregular. After a shower, desert plants leaf out quickly and herds can follow the new growth.

ratibida columnifera.name: Yellow coneflower
ratibida columnifera.desc: Yellow coneflower (Ratibida columnifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 46 times near the park in GBIF.
ratibida columnifera.about: Ratibida columnifera, commonly known as upright prairie coneflower, rocketflower, Mexican hat, and longhead prairie coneflower, is a perennial species of flowering plant in the genus Ratibida in the…

ratibida pinnata.name: Drooping prairie-coneflower
ratibida pinnata.desc: Drooping prairie-coneflower (Ratibida pinnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
ratibida pinnata.about: Ratibida pinnata is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names pinnate prairie coneflower, gray-head coneflower, yellow coneflower, and prairie coneflower.

rattus argentiventer.name: Ricefield rat
rattus argentiventer.desc: A rodent of rice fields and wet grassland that eats rice and is prey for snakes, birds and otters.
rattus argentiventer.about: The ricefield rat is a species of rat found throughout Southeast Asia.

rattus baluensis.name: Summit rat
rattus baluensis.desc: A night-active rat that licks nectar from giant pitcher lids and defecates into them; one of the most recorded mammals near the park.
rattus baluensis.about: The summit rat is a species of rodent in the family Muridae. It is found only on Mount Kinabalu and Mount Tambuyukon, Malaysia, and has been recorded at altitudes of 2,040 to 2,477 m on Mt.

rattus colletti.name: Dusky rat
rattus colletti.desc: Rodent of the cracking-clay floodplains, found in large numbers when the grass is lush. It is food for dingoes, kites and small carnivores.
rattus colletti.about: The dusky rat is an indigenous species of rodent in the family Muridae found in Australia.

rattus exulans.name: Polynesian rat
rattus exulans.desc: An omnivore spread across the Pacific by settlers. It eats seeds, fruit, insects, lizards and bird eggs.
rattus exulans.about: The Polynesian rat, Pacific rat or little rat, or kiore, is the third most widespread species of rat in the world behind the brown rat and black rat.

rattus rattus.name: Black rat
rattus rattus.desc: Introduced omnivore that eats eggs and hatchlings of tortoises and iguanas and has wiped out young tortoises on some islands.
rattus rattus.about: The black rat, also known as the roof rat, ship rat, or house rat, is a common long-tailed rodent of the stereotypical rat genus Rattus, in the subfamily Murinae.

ratufa indica.name: Malabar giant squirrel
ratufa indica.desc: A large canopy squirrel that feeds on fruit, flowers, nuts and bark. Leopards are recorded eating it.
ratufa indica.about: The Indian giant squirrel or Malabar giant squirrel is a large multi-coloured tree squirrel species endemic to forests and woodlands in India.

ratufa macroura.name: Sri Lankan giant squirrel
ratufa macroura.desc: A large tree squirrel of the forest canopy that feeds on fruit, seeds and bark.

recurvirostra americana.name: American Avocet
recurvirostra americana.desc: American Avocet (Recurvirostra americana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,460 times near the park in GBIF.
recurvirostra americana.about: The American avocet is a large wader in the avocet and stilt family, Recurvirostridae, found in North America.

recurvirostra andina.name: Andean avocet
recurvirostra andina.desc: A wader of high salt lakes that sweeps its upturned bill through shallow water for small invertebrates. Well recorded in the area.
recurvirostra andina.about: The Andean avocet is a large wader in the avocet and stilt bird family, Recurvirostridae.

red and green seaweeds.name: Intertidal algae
red and green seaweeds.desc: Red and green seaweeds grow on the rocky shore in the cold, nutrient-rich water. Marine iguanas and crabs graze them.
red and green seaweeds.about: Algae are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. It excludes the land plants (embryophytes).

red sand and limestone country.name: Red sand and limestone country
red sand and limestone country.desc: Arid sandy land of the peninsulas and islands, home to the shrubs, grasses and ground-dwelling animals of the terrestrial side.

redunca redunca.name: Bohor reedbuck
redunca redunca.desc: A grazing antelope of wet grassland. Ethiopian wolves have taken reedbuck calves.
redunca redunca.about: The bohor reedbuck is an antelope native to central Africa. The animal is placed under the genus Redunca and in the family Bovidae.

reef water.name: Cool, clear reef water
reef water.desc: Corals live close to their heat limit. During marine heatwaves they bleach and can die, while reef algae spread.

regulus calendula.name: Ruby-crowned Kinglet
regulus calendula.desc: Ruby-crowned Kinglet (Regulus calendula): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 4,618 times near the park in GBIF.
regulus calendula.about: The ruby-crowned kinglet is a very small passerine bird found throughout North America. It is a member of the kinglet family.

reithrodontomys megalotis.name: Western harvest mouse
reithrodontomys megalotis.desc: A small seed and plant eater of grassy cover. One of the most recorded rodents near the park.
reithrodontomys megalotis.about: The western harvest mouse is a small neotomine mouse native to most of the western United States.

restio.name: Restios
restio.desc: Reed-like plants that are a defining part of fynbos. The Cape mountain zebra eats young restio shoots.
restio.about: The Restionaceae, also called restiads and restios, are a family of flowering plants native to the Southern Hemisphere; they vary from a few centimeters to 3 meters in height.

retreating glaciers.name: Retreating glaciers
retreating glaciers.desc: Glaciers have been receding for decades, leaving bare ground where plants then colonise in stages.

reynoutria japonica.name: Japanese Knotweed
reynoutria japonica.desc: Japanese Knotweed (Reynoutria japonica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

rhabdomys dilectus.name: Four-striped grass mouse
rhabdomys dilectus.desc: Small rodent of the open montane grassland and the most recorded mammal in the GBIF data here.
rhabdomys dilectus.about: Rhabdomys is a largely Southern African genus of muroid rodents slightly larger than house mice. They are known variously as striped or four-striped mice or rats.

rhabdomys pumilio.name: Striped mouse
rhabdomys pumilio.desc: A common small rodent of open shrubland that eats plant matter and insects, and is prey for many predators.
rhabdomys pumilio.about: The four-striped grass mouse or four-striped grass rat is a species of rodent in the family Muridae.

rhacophorus malabaricus.name: Malabar flying frog
rhacophorus malabaricus.desc: One of the many endemic tree frogs of the Ghats. It hunts insects at night in wet forest.
rhacophorus malabaricus.about: The Malabar gliding frog or Malabar flying frog is a rhacophorid tree frog species found in the Western Ghats of India. It is the state amphibian of Kerala.

rhamnus cathartica.name: Buckthorn
rhamnus cathartica.desc: Buckthorn (Rhamnus cathartica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
rhamnus cathartica.about: Rhamnus cathartica, the European buckthorn, common buckthorn, purging buckthorn, or just buckthorn, is a species of small tree in the flowering plant family Rhamnaceae.

rhanterium epapposum.name: Arfaj
rhanterium epapposum.desc: A yellow-flowered shrub native to Qatar, regarded as a main desert forage plant for camels and sheep. It leafs out quickly after rain.
rhanterium epapposum.about: Rhanterium epapposum is a plant of the family Asteraceae. Native to the deserts of the Arabian Peninsula including Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Qatar where it is known locally as arfaj (Arabic: عرفج).

rhapidophyllum hystrix.name: Porcupine palm
rhapidophyllum hystrix.desc: Porcupine palm (Rhapidophyllum hystrix): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 91 times near the park in GBIF.

rhea americana.name: Greater rhea
rhea americana.desc: A large flightless bird that mainly eats broad-leaved plants, seeds and fruit, plus insects and small animals. Cougars are its main predator.
rhea americana.about: The greater rhea is a species of flightless bird native to eastern South America.

rhea pennata.name: Darwin's rhea
rhea pennata.desc: A flightless bird of Patagonian scrub that eats mostly plants, plus the odd lizard or insect, and outruns predators.
rhea pennata.about: Darwin's rhea or the lesser rhea is a large flightless bird, the smaller of the two extant species of rheas. It is found in the Altiplano and Patagonia in South America.

rhincodon typus.name: Whale shark
rhincodon typus.desc: The biggest fish, a filter feeder on plankton, seen in the island waters.
rhincodon typus.about: The whale shark is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.

rhinella marina.name: Cane toad
rhinella marina.desc: An introduced toad that eats ants and many other small animals.
rhinella marina.about: The cane toad, also known as the giant neotropical toad or marine toad, is a large, terrestrial true toad native to South and mainland Central America, but which has been introduced to various…

rhinoceros sondaicus.name: Javan rhinoceros
rhinoceros sondaicus.desc: Critically endangered browser of shoots, twigs and fallen fruit. Ujung Kulon holds its only known wild population, about 82 animals per Wikipedia.
rhinoceros sondaicus.about: The Javan rhinoceros, also called Javan rhino, Sunda rhinoceros and lesser one-horned rhinoceros is a critically endangered member of the genus Rhinoceros of the family Rhinocerotidae, and one of the…

rhinoceros unicornis.name: Indian rhinoceros
rhinoceros unicornis.desc: A grazer of tall alluvial grasslands that also eats leaves, fruits and water plants. Chitwan holds most of Nepal's rhinos.
rhinoceros unicornis.about: The Indian rhinoceros, also known as the greater one-horned rhinoceros, great Indian rhinoceros or Indian rhino, is a rhinoceros species native to the Indian subcontinent.

rhinolophus pearsonii.name: Pearson's horseshoe bat
rhinolophus pearsonii.desc: One of many insect-eating bats recorded in the forest. It hunts flying insects at night.
rhinolophus pearsonii.about: Pearson's horseshoe bat is a species of bat in the family Rhinolophidae. It is found in Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and Vietnam.

rhinopithecus bieti.name: Black snub-nosed monkey
rhinopithecus bieti.desc: Endemic to northwest Yunnan and neighbouring Tibet. It lives higher than any other non-human primate and lives mostly on lichen.
rhinopithecus bieti.about: The black-and-white snub-nosed monkey, also known as the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey, is a large black and white primate that lives only in the southern Chinese province of Yunnan, where it is known to…

rhinopithecus roxellana.name: Golden snub-nosed monkey
rhinopithecus roxellana.desc: A leaf-eating primate of the high mixed and conifer forests that moves lower in winter.
rhinopithecus roxellana.about: The golden snub-nosed monkey is an Old World monkey in the subfamily Colobinae. It is endemic to a small area in temperate, mountainous forests of central and Southwest China.

rudbeckia laciniata.desc: Coneflower (Rudbeckia laciniata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

rudbeckia subtomentosa.name: Sweet coneflower
rudbeckia subtomentosa.desc: Sweet coneflower (Rudbeckia subtomentosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
rudbeckia subtomentosa.about: Rudbeckia subtomentosa, the sweet coneflower, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is found in the central United States.

ruellia humilis.name: Fringe-leaf ruellia
ruellia humilis.desc: Fringe-leaf ruellia (Ruellia humilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
ruellia humilis.about: Ruellia humilis (wild petunia, fringeleaf wild petunia, hairy petunia, low wild petunia) is a species of flowering plant in the family Acanthaceae. It is native to the eastern United States.

rumex crispus.name: Curled Dock
rumex crispus.desc: Curled Dock (Rumex crispus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

rumex fueginus.name: American golden dock
rumex fueginus.desc: American golden dock (Rumex fueginus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

rumex hymenosepalus.name: Ganagra
rumex hymenosepalus.desc: Ganagra (Rumex hymenosepalus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 146 times near the park in GBIF.

rumex longifolius.name: Northern Dock
rumex longifolius.desc: Northern Dock (Rumex longifolius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

rupicapra pyrenaica.name: Pyrenean chamois (izard)
rupicapra pyrenaica.desc: A sure-footed mountain goat-antelope that browses grass, lichens and buds on steep slopes up to about 3,000 m. It is the best-recorded large animal here.
rupicapra pyrenaica.about: The Pyrenean chamois is a goat-antelope that lives in the Pyrenees and Cantabrian Mountains of Spain, France and Andorra, and the Apennine Mountains of central Italy.

rupicapra rupicapra.name: Chamois
rupicapra rupicapra.desc: Eats alpine grasses and herbs in summer and conifers in winter, moving down to pine forest. A main prey of wolves and a regular carrion source.
rupicapra rupicapra.about: The chamois, or Alpine chamois, is a species of goat-antelope native to mountainous parts of Europe and Western Asia, from the Pyrenees and the Cantabrian Mountain Range, the Alps, the Apennines, the…

rupicola peruvianus.name: Andean cock-of-the-rock
rupicola peruvianus.desc: A cloud-forest bird of ravines and streams. It eats mostly fruit plus insects, and its leks attract predators such as jaguars and ocelots.
rupicola peruvianus.about: The Andean cock-of-the-rock, also known as tunki (Quechua), is a large passerine bird of the cotinga family native to Andean cloud forests in South America. It is the national bird of Peru.

rupornis magnirostris.name: Roadside hawk
rupornis magnirostris.desc: A common medium-sized raptor of forest edges that hunts lizards, small mammals and large insects.
rupornis magnirostris.about: The roadside hawk is a relatively small bird of prey found in the Americas. This vocal species is often the most common raptor in its range.

rusa timorensis.name: Timor deer (Javan rusa)
rusa timorensis.desc: Grazes grass, leaves and fallen fruit. It is the main prey of the Komodo dragon on the park islands.
rusa timorensis.about: The Javan rusa or Sunda sambar is a large deer species native to Indonesia and Timor-Leste. Introduced populations exist in a wide variety of locations in the Southern Hemisphere.

rusa unicolor.name: Sambar
rusa unicolor.desc: A large forest deer that browses and grazes. A favoured prey of tigers.
rusa unicolor.about: The sambar is a large deer native to the Indian subcontinent, South China and Southeast Asia.

rutilus rutilus.name: Roach
rutilus rutilus.desc: A freshwater fish of reedy lakes, typical of the small and medium fish that Dalmatian pelicans swallow whole.
rutilus rutilus.about: The roach, or rutilus roach, also known as the common roach, is a fresh- and brackish-water fish of the family Cyprinidae, native to most of Europe and western Asia.

río plátano floods.name: Río Plátano floods
río plátano floods.desc: The river and its lagoons carry water and silt through the lowlands and shape the wetlands and gallery forest.

sabal minor.name: Dwarf Palmetto
sabal minor.desc: Dwarf Palmetto (Sabal minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
sabal minor.about: Sabal minor, commonly known as the dwarf palmetto, is a small species of palm. It is native to the deep southeastern and south-central United States and northeastern Mexico.

sabal palmetto.name: Cabbage palm
sabal palmetto.desc: Cabbage palm (Sabal palmetto): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
sabal palmetto.about: Sabal palmetto (, SAY-bəl), also known as cabbage palm, cabbage palmetto, sabal palm, palmetto palm, blue palmetto, Carolina palmetto, common palmetto, and swamp cabbage, is one of 15 species of…

saccharum.name: Tall elephant grasses
saccharum.desc: Tall grasses cover the largest share of the park, and regrow quickly after the monsoon floods and winter burns that open new feeding ground.
saccharum.about: Saccharum spontaneum (wild sugarcane, kans grass) is a grass native throughout much of tropical and subtropical Asia, northern Australia, and eastern and northern Africa.

saccharum spontaneum.name: Kans grass
saccharum spontaneum.desc: A tall grass that is among the first plants to colonise fresh sandbanks. Tall grasslands cover roughly a fifth of the park.
saccharum spontaneum.about: Saccharum spontaneum (wild sugarcane, kans grass) is a grass native throughout much of tropical and subtropical Asia, northern Australia, and eastern and northern Africa.

sagittaria lancifolia.name: Bulltongue
sagittaria lancifolia.desc: Bulltongue (Sagittaria lancifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.
sagittaria lancifolia.about: Sagittaria lancifolia, the bulltongue arrowhead, is a New World perennial, monocot plant in the family Alismataceae, genus Sagittaria, with herbaceous growth patterns.

sagittaria montevidensis.name: Giant arrowhead
sagittaria montevidensis.desc: Giant arrowhead (Sagittaria montevidensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
sagittaria montevidensis.about: Sagittaria montevidensis is a species of flowering plant in the water-plantain family Alismataceae. Common names include giant arrowhead and California arrowhead.

saiga tatarica.name: Saiga antelope
saiga tatarica.desc: Nomadic steppe grazer that eats many plants, including some poisonous to other animals. Wolves are the main threat to adults.
saiga tatarica.about: The saiga antelope, or simply saiga, is a species of antelope which during antiquity inhabited a vast area of the Eurasian steppe, spanning the foothills of the Carpathian Mountains in the northwest…

salicornia.name: Glasswort and saltbush
salicornia.desc: Salt-tolerant plants of the lake shores and saline flats; glasswort and saltbush were both recorded near the reserve.
salicornia.about: Salicornia is a genus of succulent, halophytic (salt tolerant) flowering plants in the family Amaranthaceae that grow in salt marshes, on beaches, and among mangroves.

salicornia europaea.name: Glasswort
salicornia europaea.desc: A salt-tolerant succulent of salt marshes and lagoon margins, among the well-recorded plants around the lagoon.
salicornia europaea.about: Salicornia europaea, known as marsh samphire, common glasswort or just glasswort, is a halophytic annual dicot flowering plant.

salicornia fruticosa.name: Glasswort
salicornia fruticosa.desc: A succulent salt-tolerant shrub of the saline flats, recorded commonly around the lagoons; one of the plants adapted to the salty conditions.
salicornia fruticosa.about: Salicornia is a genus of succulent, halophytic (salt tolerant) flowering plants in the family Amaranthaceae that grow in salt marshes, on beaches, and among mangroves.

salicornia rubra.name: Rocky Mountain glasswort
salicornia rubra.desc: Rocky Mountain glasswort (Salicornia rubra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
salicornia rubra.about: Salicornia rubra, commonly known as the red glasswort or Rocky Mountain glasswort, is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae.

saline lake water.name: Saline lake water
saline lake water.desc: Uvs Lake is shallow and salty, at roughly half the salinity of the ocean, because salts build up in a basin with no outlet.

saline limestone soils.name: Saline limestone soils
saline limestone soils.desc: Alkaline, mineral-rich soils around the pan. Salty dust blown from the pan adds minerals to soils downwind.

salix.name: Willows
salix.desc: Shrubs of lowland and tundra that moose browse, according to the park service. Hares, ptarmigan, ground squirrels and Dall sheep eat them too.
salix.about: Willows, also called sallows and osiers, of the genus Salix, comprise around 350 species (plus numerous hybrids) of typically deciduous trees and shrubs.

salix alba.name: White willow
salix alba.desc: Tree of the wet river levees and floodplain, rooted in the seasonally flooded ground.
salix alba.about: Salix alba, the white willow, is a species of willow native to Europe and western and Central Asia. The name derives from the white tone to the undersides of the leaves.

salix amygdaloides.name: Peach-leaf willow
salix amygdaloides.desc: Peach-leaf willow (Salix amygdaloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

salix arctica.name: Arctic willow
salix arctica.desc: A dwarf willow hugging the ground on tundra. Willows are the most commonly eaten plant for muskoxen in winter.
salix arctica.about: Salix arctica, the Arctic willow, is a tiny creeping willow (family Salicaceae). It is adapted to survive in Arctic conditions, specifically tundras.

salix atrocinerea.name: Rusty willow
salix atrocinerea.desc: Streamside willow whose leaves fall into the water and feed stream insects.
salix atrocinerea.about: Salix atrocinerea, commonly called grey willow or large gray willow, is a species of willow. It is a bush or small tree up to 12 m (39 ft) tall.

salix bebbiana.name: Beak Willow
salix bebbiana.desc: A willow of wet ground. Wood bison eat willow leaves in summer, and beavers and moose browse willows.
salix bebbiana.about: Salix bebbiana is a species of willow indigenous to Canada and the northern United States, from Alaska and Yukon south to California and Arizona and northeast to Newfoundland and New England.

salix caprea.name: Goat willow
salix caprea.desc: A willow of forest edges and river banks whose shoots and bark are browsed by hares and moose.
salix caprea.about: Salix caprea, known as goat willow, pussy willow or great sallow, is a common species of willow native to Europe and western and central Asia.

salix caroliniana.name: Carolina willow
salix caroliniana.desc: Carolina willow (Salix caroliniana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
salix caroliniana.about: Salix caroliniana, commonly known as the coastal plain willow, is a shrub or small tree native to the southeastern United States, Mexico and parts of Central America and the Caribbean.

salix eriocephala.name: Heart-leaf willow
salix eriocephala.desc: Heart-leaf willow (Salix eriocephala): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.

salix exigua.name: Sandbar willow
salix exigua.desc: Sandbar willow (Salix exigua): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

salix geyeriana.name: Geyer's willow
salix geyeriana.desc: Geyer's willow (Salix geyeriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
salix geyeriana.about: Salix geyeriana is a species of willow known by the common names Geyer's willow, Geyer willow and silver willow.

salix glauca.name: Grayleaf willow
salix glauca.desc: Low shrubby willows of the tundra and river valleys. Willow ptarmigan are recorded eating grayleaf willow.
salix glauca.about: Salix glauca is a species of flowering plant in the willow family known by the common names gray willow, grayleaf willow, white willow, and glaucous willow.

salix gooddingii.name: Gooding's black willow
salix gooddingii.desc: Gooding's black willow (Salix gooddingii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

salix humilis.name: Prairie Willow
salix humilis.desc: Prairie Willow (Salix humilis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
salix humilis.about: Salix humilis, known as prairie willow, is a species of willow native to the United States and Canada, east of the Rockies. Male and female flowers are found on separate plants.

salix interior.name: Sandbar willow
salix interior.desc: Sandbar willow (Salix interior): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
salix interior.about: Salix exigua is a species of willow native to most of North America except for the southeast and far north, occurring from Alaska east to New Brunswick, and south to northern Mexico.

salix irrorata.name: Blue-stem willow
salix irrorata.desc: Blue-stem willow (Salix irrorata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

salix lanata.name: Woolly willow
salix lanata.desc: A low, silvery willow of Icelandic heaths and river plains; willow shoots and buds are a staple for grazers and ptarmigan.
salix lanata.about: Salix lanata, the woolly willow, is a subarctic species of willow native to Iceland, the Faeroe Islands and Finland, through to eastern Siberia.

salix lemmonii.name: Lemmon's willow
salix lemmonii.desc: Lemmon's willow (Salix lemmonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

salix lucida.name: Shining Willow
salix lucida.desc: Shining Willow (Salix lucida): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
salix lucida.about: Salix lucida, the shining willow, Pacific willow, red willow, or whiplash willow, is a species of willow native to northern and western North America, occurring in wetland habitats.

salix nigra.name: Black willow
salix nigra.desc: Colonizes new sandbars and banks. Beavers, muskrats and deer all browse it.
salix nigra.about: Salix nigra, or the black willow, is a species of willow native to a large portion of North America, from New Brunswick and southern Ontario west to Arizona and California, and south to northern…

salix polaris.name: Polar willow
salix polaris.desc: A tiny creeping arctic willow of tundra and rocky slopes, recorded as food for reindeer.
salix polaris.about: Salix polaris, the polar willow, is a species of willow with a circumpolar distribution in the high arctic tundra, extending north to the limits of land, and south of the Arctic in the mountains of…

salix pycnostachya.name: Willow
salix pycnostachya.desc: Willows are shrubs and trees of damp ground and are recorded near the park. Local people collect shrubs for fuel and winter fodder.
salix pycnostachya.about: Willows, also called sallows and osiers, of the genus Salix, comprise around 350 species (plus numerous hybrids) of typically deciduous trees and shrubs.

salix spp..name: Willow
salix spp..desc: Streamside shrubs that feed moose and beaver and hold the banks that trout streams run between.
salix spp..about: Willows, also called sallows and osiers, of the genus Salix, comprise around 350 species (plus numerous hybrids) of typically deciduous trees and shrubs.

salmo letnica.name: Ohrid trout
salmo letnica.desc: An endemic, endangered trout that preys on smaller fish. Overfishing and illegal fishing have cut its numbers.
salmo letnica.about: Ohrid trout or the Lake Ohrid brown trout is an endemic species of trout in Lake Ohrid and in its tributaries and outlet, the Black Drin river, in North Macedonia and Albania.

salmo trutta.name: Brown trout
salmo trutta.desc: A fish of cold, clear mountain rivers and lakes that eats aquatic insects and smaller fish. Prey for otters.
salmo trutta.about: The brown trout is a species of carnivorous ray-finned fish and the most widely distributed species of the salmonid genus Salmo, endemic to most of Europe, West Asia and parts of North Africa, and…

salmon-borne nitrogen.name: Salmon-borne nitrogen
salmon-borne nitrogen.desc: Nitrogen from the ocean arrives in spawning salmon and is spread along streams by floods and by animals that carry and eat the carcasses.

salmon-borne nutrients.name: Salmon-borne nutrients
salmon-borne nutrients.desc: Salmon bring ocean-grown nutrients inland, and their remains are broken down into nutrients that feed streamside soil and lakes.

salpa thompsoni.name: Salps
salpa thompsoni.desc: Free-floating filter feeders. In low-ice years they tend to replace krill and may compete with them for food.
salpa thompsoni.about: A salp (pl.: salps) or salpa is a barrel-shaped, planktonic tunicate in the family Salpidae.

salsola tragus.name: Prickly Russian Thistle
salsola tragus.desc: Prickly Russian Thistle (Salsola tragus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

salt and brine.name: Salt and brine
salt and brine.desc: Lagoons cut off from the sea by sandbars and long-used salt pans hold salty water. Brine shrimp tolerate salinity that keeps most fish out.

salt-lake water.name: Salt-lake water
salt-lake water.desc: Shallow, salty, mineral-rich lagoons with borates and sulfates set the home of the algae, diatoms and brine shrimp.

salvator merianae.name: Argentine tegu
salvator merianae.desc: A big omnivorous lizard eating insects, eggs, fruit and carrion. Cougars and jaguars are among its predators.
salvator merianae.about: The Argentine black and white tegu, also commonly known as the Argentine giant tegu, the black and white tegu, the blue tegu, and the huge tegu, is a species of lizard in the family Teiidae.

salvelinus alpinus.name: Arctic char
salvelinus alpinus.desc: A cold-water fish found in lakes. Landlocked populations eat insects, bottom invertebrates and zooplankton.
salvelinus alpinus.about: The Arctic char or Arctic charr is a cold-water fish in the family Salmonidae, native to alpine lakes, as well as Arctic and subarctic coastal waters in the Holarctic.

salvelinus fontinalis.name: Brook trout
salvelinus fontinalis.desc: The park's only native trout, now mostly in cold high streams after non-native rainbow and brown trout took over lower reaches. Eats insects and small animals.
salvelinus fontinalis.about: The brook trout is a species of freshwater fish in the char genus Salvelinus of the salmon family Salmonidae native to Eastern North America in the United States and Canada.

salvelinus namaycush.name: Lake trout
salvelinus namaycush.desc: The native top predator, nearly wiped out by lampreys and overfishing. Hatchery stocking helps rebuild it.
salvelinus namaycush.about: The lake trout is a freshwater char living mainly in lakes in Northern North America. Other names for it include mackinaw, namaycush, lake char (or charr), touladi, togue, laker, and grey trout.

salvia dorrii.name: Purple sage
salvia dorrii.desc: Grayball sage (Salvia dorrii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
salvia dorrii.about: Salvia dorrii, the purple sage, Dorr's sage, fleshy sage, mint sage, or tobacco sage, is a perennial spreading shrub in the family Lamiaceae.

salvia elegans.name: Pineapple sage
salvia elegans.desc: One of many sages and wildflowers recorded around the reserve. Its nectar feeds monarchs, bees and hummingbirds.
salvia elegans.about: Salvia elegans is a perennial shrub native to Mexico. It has a number of variants, including pineapple sage and tangerine sage.

salvia leucophylla.name: Purple sage
salvia leucophylla.desc: Purple sage (Salvia leucophylla): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 182 times near the park in GBIF.

salvia lyrata.name: Lyreleaf sage
salvia lyrata.desc: Lyreleaf sage (Salvia lyrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
salvia lyrata.about: Salvia lyrata (lyre-leaf sage, lyreleaf sage, wild sage, cancerweed), is a herbaceous perennial in the family Lamiaceae that is native to the United States, from Connecticut west to Missouri, and in…

salvia spathacea.name: Crimson pitcher sage
salvia spathacea.desc: Crimson pitcher sage (Salvia spathacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.
salvia spathacea.about: Salvia spathacea, the California hummingbird sage or pitcher sage, is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to southern and central California growing from sea level to 610 m…

salvinia minima.name: Water fern
salvinia minima.desc: Water fern (Salvinia minima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

salvinia molesta.name: Giant salvinia
salvinia molesta.desc: Giant salvinia (Salvinia molesta): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 49 times near the park in GBIF.

sambucus canadensis.name: American elderberry
sambucus canadensis.desc: American elderberry (Sambucus canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
sambucus canadensis.about: Sambucus canadensis, the American black elderberry, Canada elderberry, or common elderberry, is a New World species of elderberry that forms a shrub primarily in temperate regions.

sambucus cerulea.name: Mexican elder
sambucus cerulea.desc: Mexican elder (Sambucus cerulea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

sambucus ebulus.name: Dwarf elder
sambucus ebulus.desc: A tall herb whose berries are eaten by birds, and whose foliage feeds the caterpillars of the Jersey tiger moth.
sambucus ebulus.about: Sambucus ebulus, also known as danewort, dane weed, danesblood, dwarf elder or European dwarf elder, walewort, dwarf elderberry, elderwort and blood hilder, is a herbaceous species of elder, native…

sambucus racemosa.name: Red-berried Elder
sambucus racemosa.desc: Red-berried Elder (Sambucus racemosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

san juan and bartola rivers.name: San Juan and Bartola rivers
san juan and bartola rivers.desc: Rivers along and through the reserve that bring water and carry nutrients through the forest.

sand dunes & soil.name: Sand dunes & soil
sand dunes & soil.desc: Dunes rise to nearly 200 feet inland from the beach, and the NPS says all stages of plant succession can be seen on the youngest ones.

sand dunes & soils.name: Sand dunes & soils
sand dunes & soils.desc: Fixed and mobile dunes and sandy soils carry the pine, scrub and cork oak woodland beside the marsh.

sander vitreus.name: Walleye
sander vitreus.desc: A top sport fish of the big lakes; adults eat mostly fish, often yellow perch.
sander vitreus.about: The walleye, also called the walleyed pike, yellow pike, yellow pikeperch or yellow pickerel, is a freshwater perciform fish native to most of Canada and to the Northern United States.

sandy acidic soil.name: Sandy acidic soil
sandy acidic soil.desc: Sandy, acid, nutrient-poor soil is why the region is called the Barrens.

sandy cays.name: Sandy cays
sandy cays.desc: The park has about 144 acres of land, mostly low sand keys. Bush Key is closed in Feb to Sep to protect nesting terns and noddies.

sandy desert soil.name: Sandy desert soil
sandy desert soil.desc: Thin, easily eroded soils of the Colorado Plateau. Nitrogen and nutrients are scarce and the crust helps hold the soil in place.

sandy soil.name: Sandy soil
sandy soil.desc: Loose sand and gravel soils are poor in nutrients; dead matter returning to them is what lets plants grow.

sandy soil and dunes.name: Sandy soil and dunes
sandy soil and dunes.desc: Loose sand holds little organic matter. Deep-rooted shrubs help anchor it, and returning nutrients feed the plants.

sandy, nutrient-poor soil.name: Sandy, nutrient-poor soil
sandy, nutrient-poor soil.desc: Sand and gravel hold little organic matter. Windblown dust is one source of nutrients.

sandy, nutrient-poor soils.name: Sandy, nutrient-poor soils
sandy, nutrient-poor soils.desc: Some forest here grows on pure white sand, where nutrients are scarce and recycled quickly from fallen leaves and wood.

sandy, salty steppe soil.name: Sandy, salty steppe soil
sandy, salty steppe soil.desc: Thin, dry ground broken by salt lakes supports mostly low shrubs.

sanguinaria canadensis.name: Red puccoon
sanguinaria canadensis.desc: Red puccoon (Sanguinaria canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.
sanguinaria canadensis.about: Sanguinaria canadensis, bloodroot, is a perennial, herbaceous flowering plant native to eastern North America.

sapajus apella.name: Tufted capuchin
sapajus apella.desc: An omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, including Guatteria, and also insects and small animals.
sapajus apella.about: The tufted capuchin, also known as brown capuchin, black-capped capuchin, or pin monkey, is a New World primate from South America and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

sapajus nigritus.name: Black capuchin
sapajus nigritus.desc: A monkey that eats fruit, seeds and other foods. GloBI records it feeding on Miconia and Psychotria fruit, and pumas prey on it.
sapajus nigritus.about: The black capuchin, also known as the black-horned capuchin, is a capuchin monkey from the Atlantic Forest in south-eastern Brazil and far north-eastern Argentina.

sarcobatus vermiculatus.name: Greasewood
sarcobatus vermiculatus.desc: Greasewood (Sarcobatus vermiculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
sarcobatus vermiculatus.about: Sarcobatus is a North American genus of two species of flowering plants, formerly considered to be a single species. Common names for S. vermiculatus include greasewood, seepwood, and saltbush.

sarcodes sanguinea.name: Snowplant
sarcodes sanguinea.desc: Snowplant (Sarcodes sanguinea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 889 times near the park in GBIF.

sarcophilus harrisii.name: Tasmanian devil
sarcophilus harrisii.desc: The world's largest surviving marsupial carnivore, mainly a scavenger that favours wombats. Devil facial tumour disease has cut its numbers sharply.
sarcophilus harrisii.about: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

sarcoramphus papa.name: King vulture
sarcoramphus papa.desc: Finds carcasses by smell and opens them up for smaller vultures.
sarcoramphus papa.about: The king vulture is a large bird found in Central and South America. It is a member of the New World vulture family Cathartidae.

sardinella.name: Sardines
sardinella.desc: Schooling plankton-feeding fish that carry energy from plankton up to seabirds, dolphins and ospreys.
sardinella.about: Sardinella is a genus of fish in the family Dorosomatidae found in the Atlantic, Indian and Pacific Oceans. They are abundant in warmer waters of the tropical and subtropical oceans.

sardinella aurita.name: Round sardinella
sardinella aurita.desc: A schooling fish that filters plankton and is prey for seabirds and larger fish.
sardinella aurita.about: The round sardinella, sometimes known as Spanish sardine, is a species of ray-finned fish in the genus Sardinella found in both sides of the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. S.

sardinella longiceps.name: Indian oil sardine
sardinella longiceps.desc: A schooling fish of the Arabian Sea that feeds on plankton and is a key prey fish for birds, dolphins and larger fish.
sardinella longiceps.about: The Indian oil sardine is a species of ray-finned fish in the genus Sardinella. It is one of the two most important commercial fishes in India (with the mackerel).

sardines and similar.name: Sardines and small schooling fish
sardines and similar.desc: Small schooling fish eating plankton. Sea lions, penguins and cormorants hunt them, and they die off or move away in El Niño years.
sardines and similar.about: Sardine and pilchard are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.

sarracenia alata.about: Sarracenia alata, also known as yellow trumpets, pale pitcher plant or pale trumpet, is a carnivorous plant in the genus Sarracenia. Specifically, S.

sarracenia flava.name: Yellow Pitcherplant
sarracenia flava.desc: Yellow Pitcherplant (Sarracenia flava): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 156 times near the park in GBIF.
sarracenia flava.about: Sarracenia flava, the yellow pitcherplant, is a carnivorous plant in the family Sarraceniaceae. Like all the Sarraceniaceae, it is native to the New World.

sarracenia minor.name: Rainhat-trumpet
sarracenia minor.desc: Rainhat-trumpet (Sarracenia minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 107 times near the park in GBIF.

sarracenia purpurea.desc: Frog's-britches (Sarracenia purpurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
sarracenia purpurea.about: Sarracenia purpurea, the purple pitcher plant, northern pitcher plant, turtle socks, or side-saddle flower, is a carnivorous plant in the family Sarraceniaceae.

sasa kurilensis.name: Kuril bamboo grass
sasa kurilensis.desc: A dwarf bamboo that carpets the forest floor and clearings of Hokkaido, a staple browse for deer.

sassafras albidum.name: Sassafras
sassafras albidum.desc: Sassafras (Sassafras albidum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
sassafras albidum.about: Sassafras albidum is a species of Sassafras native to eastern North America. It has a number of culinary and other uses.

sauromalus ater.name: Common chuckwalla
sauromalus ater.desc: A large plant-eating lizard that feeds on desert shrubs such as creosote bush and wedges into rock crevices.
sauromalus ater.about: Sauromalus ater, also known as the common chuckwalla or northern chuckwalla, is a species of lizard in the family Iguanidae.

saururus cernuus.name: Lizard's tail
saururus cernuus.desc: Lizard's tail (Saururus cernuus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 55 times near the park in GBIF.
saururus cernuus.about: Saururus cernuus (lizard's tail, water-dragon, dragon's tail, swamp root) is a species of herbaceous perennial plant. The plant grows up to about 1 metre (3+1⁄2 ft) tall.

saussurea falconeri.name: Saussurea
saussurea falconeri.desc: A flowering herb of the summer wildflower meadows that bloom across the plateau after the snow retreats.
saussurea falconeri.about: Saussurea is a genus of about 300 species of flowering plants in the tribe Cardueae within the family Asteraceae, native to cool temperate and arctic regions of East Asia, Europe, and North America,…

savanna soil.name: Savanna soil
savanna soil.desc: Shallow soils on the rocky cliffs and deeper soils on summits and escarpments support different woodland.

sayornis nigricans.name: Black Phoebe
sayornis nigricans.desc: Black Phoebe (Sayornis nigricans): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 9,658 times near the park in GBIF.
sayornis nigricans.about: The black phoebe is a passerine bird in the tyrant-flycatcher family. It breeds from southwest Oregon and California south through Central and South America.

sayornis phoebe.name: Eastern Phoebe
sayornis phoebe.desc: Eastern Phoebe (Sayornis phoebe): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 361 times near the park in GBIF.
sayornis phoebe.about: The eastern phoebe is a small passerine bird. The genus name Sayornis is constructed from the specific part of Charles Lucien Bonaparte's name for Say's phoebe, Muscicapa saya, and Ancient Greek…

scarce rain.name: Scarce rain
scarce rain.desc: Rainfall in the park ranges from about 10 inches a year at Castolon to 18 in the Chisos Basin. Plant growth depends on it.

scarce rain and flash floods.name: Scarce rain and flash floods
scarce rain and flash floods.desc: The park averages only about 200 mm of precipitation a year. Late-summer storms bring most of it, often as sudden flash floods.

scarce rain and snow.name: Scarce rain and snow
scarce rain and snow.desc: The park is cold semi-arid, with about 413 mm of precipitation a year, so water is the main limit on plant growth.

scarce rain and snowmelt.name: Scarce rain and snowmelt
scarce rain and snowmelt.desc: The puna is dry. Meltwater and rare rain feed the grasslands, bogs and lagoons.

scarce rainfall.name: Scarce rainfall
scarce rainfall.desc: Rain is scarce and irregular; the park lost roughly 39% of its annual precipitation between 1895 and 2016, and plants and animals depend on it.

scarce seasonal rain.name: Scarce seasonal rain
scarce seasonal rain.desc: Only roughly 100 to 200 mm of rain falls a year in the Afar region, so brief wadi flows matter for plants and animals.

scarce, seasonal rain.name: Scarce, seasonal rain
scarce, seasonal rain.desc: The islands have one of the driest climates in Indonesia, with roughly 800 to 1,000 mm of rain a year, so growth is tied to the wet season.

scarus.name: Parrotfish
scarus.desc: Reef fish that scrape algae from rock and coral. Grazing keeps algae from smothering the reef.
scarus.about: Parrotfish (named because their mouths resemble a parrot's beak) are a clade of fish placed in the subfamily Scarinae of the wrasse family (Labridae).

scarus spp..name: Parrotfish
scarus spp..desc: Scrapes algae off the reef with a beak and excretes the ground limestone as sand.
scarus spp..about: Parrotfish (named because their mouths resemble a parrot's beak) are a clade of fish placed in the subfamily Scarinae of the wrasse family (Labridae).

sceliphron caementarium.name: Mud Dauber
sceliphron caementarium.desc: Mud Dauber (Sceliphron caementarium): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sceliphron caementarium.about: Sceliphron caementarium, also known as the yellow-legged mud-dauber wasp (within the US) or black-waisted mud-dauber wasp (outside of the US), is a species of sphecid wasp.

sceloporus becki.name: Island fence lizard
sceloporus becki.desc: A lizard of the islands that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Island foxes eat lizards.
sceloporus becki.about: Sceloporus becki, also known as the island fence lizard, is a species of lizard endemic to the Channel Islands of California.

sceloporus graciosus.name: Sagebrush lizard
sceloporus graciosus.desc: A small lizard of open, sunny ground that eats insects and is itself eaten by snakes and hawks.
sceloporus graciosus.about: The sagebrush lizard or sagebrush swift is a common species of phrynosomatid lizard found at mid to high altitudes in the western United States.

sceloporus grammicus.name: Mesquite lizard
sceloporus grammicus.desc: A common small lizard of the mountain forests that hunts insects.
sceloporus grammicus.about: Sceloporus grammicus is a species of lizard from Mexico and the southern United States. It is sometimes referred to as the mesquite lizard or graphic spiny lizard.

sceloporus occidentalis.name: Western Fence Lizard
sceloporus occidentalis.desc: A common lizard of rocks and brush that eats insects and other small invertebrates.
sceloporus occidentalis.about: The western fence lizard is a species of lizard native to Arizona, New Mexico, and California, as well as Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, Washington, and Northern Mexico.

sceloporus undulatus.name: Eastern fence lizard
sceloporus undulatus.desc: A sun-loving lizard of open sandy pine woods that hunts insects. Black racers hunt it.
sceloporus undulatus.about: The eastern fence lizard is a medium-sized species of lizard in the family Phrynosomatidae.

sceptridium dissectum.name: Cutleaf Grapefern
sceptridium dissectum.desc: Cutleaf Grapefern (Sceptridium dissectum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.

schefflera.name: Schefflera
schefflera.desc: Montane forest trees and shrubs whose fruit is a main food of the splendid astrapia.
schefflera.about: Schefflera is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araliaceae with 13 species native to New Zealand and some Pacific islands.

schinus terebinthifolia.name: Christmas berry
schinus terebinthifolia.desc: Christmas berry (Schinus terebinthifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

schismus arabicus.name: Spring annual grasses
schismus arabicus.desc: Short-lived grasses and herbs that sprout after rain and set seed quickly, a seasonal feast for seed and leaf eaters.
schismus arabicus.about: Schismus is a genus of African and Eurasian plants in the grass family. Two species are naturalized in North America, where they are known as Mediterranean grass.

schistocerca gregaria.name: Desert locust
schistocerca gregaria.desc: Eats about its own weight in green plants daily. After good rains it can form huge swarms that strip vegetation.
schistocerca gregaria.about: The desert locust is a species of locust in the grasshopper family, Acrididae.

schizachyrium scoparium.name: Little bluestem
schizachyrium scoparium.desc: A shorter bunchgrass of drier prairie ground.
schizachyrium scoparium.about: Schizachyrium scoparium, commonly known as little bluestem or beard grass, is a species of North American prairie grass native to most of the contiguous United States (except California, Nevada, and…

schoenoplectus californicus.name: Totora reed
schoenoplectus californicus.desc: A tall sedge growing in shallow water, mainly less than 3 m deep. Its reed belt is breeding habitat for the Titicaca grebe, and the Uru people build their floating islands from it.
schoenoplectus californicus.about: Schoeneoplectus californicus is a species of sedge known by the common names California bulrush, southern bulrush and giant bulrush.

schoenoplectus pungens.name: Sharp Club-rush
schoenoplectus pungens.desc: Sharp Club-rush (Schoenoplectus pungens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

schoenoplectus tabernaemontani.name: Grey Club-rush
schoenoplectus tabernaemontani.desc: Grey Club-rush (Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
schoenoplectus tabernaemontani.about: Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani is a species of flowering plant in the sedge family known by the common names grey club-rush, softstem bulrush, and great bulrush.

sciaenops ocellatus.name: Red drum
sciaenops ocellatus.desc: Hunts crabs, shrimp and fish in marshes and bays.
sciaenops ocellatus.about: The red drum, also known as redfish, channel bass, puppy drum, spottail bass, or simply red, is a game fish found in the Atlantic Ocean from Massachusetts to Florida and in the Gulf of Mexico from…

scirpus atrocinctus.name: Blackgirdle Bulrush
scirpus atrocinctus.desc: Blackgirdle Bulrush (Scirpus atrocinctus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

scirpus cyperinus.name: Woolgrass
scirpus cyperinus.desc: Woolgrass (Scirpus cyperinus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
scirpus cyperinus.about: Scirpus cyperinus, commonly known as woolgrass, is an emergent wetland herb that is native to the eastern United States and eastern Canada.

scirpus microcarpus.name: Panicled Bulrush
scirpus microcarpus.desc: Panicled Bulrush (Scirpus microcarpus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

scirpus pedicellatus.name: Stalked bulrush
scirpus pedicellatus.desc: Stalked bulrush (Scirpus pedicellatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

sciurus aberti.name: Abert's Squirrel
sciurus aberti.desc: Abert's Squirrel (Sciurus aberti): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sciurus aberti.about: Abert's squirrel or the tassel-eared squirrel is a tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus native to the southern Rocky Mountains from the United States to the northern Sierra Madre Occidental of Mexico,…

sciurus anomalus.name: Caucasian squirrel
sciurus anomalus.desc: A tree squirrel of the northeastern forests that feeds on seeds and nuts.
sciurus anomalus.about: The Caucasian squirrel or Persian squirrel is a tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus found in temperate broadleaf and mixed forests in south-western Asia.

sciurus arizonensis.name: Arizona Gray Squirrel
sciurus arizonensis.desc: Arizona Gray Squirrel (Sciurus arizonensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

sciurus carolinensis.name: Eastern gray squirrel
sciurus carolinensis.desc: Eastern gray squirrel (Sciurus carolinensis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sciurus carolinensis.about: The eastern gray squirrel, spelled as grey squirrel outside of the United States, is a species of tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus.

sciurus deppei.name: Deppe's squirrel
sciurus deppei.desc: A tree squirrel of tropical forests that eats fruit and seeds. Recorded within the circle around the site.
sciurus deppei.about: Deppe's squirrel is a species of tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus native to Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, and Nicaragua.

sciurus griseus.name: Western Gray Squirrel
sciurus griseus.desc: Western Gray Squirrel (Sciurus griseus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 121 times near the park in GBIF.
sciurus griseus.about: The western gray squirrel is a tree squirrel found along the western coast of the United States and Mexico.

sciurus niger.name: Fox squirrel
sciurus niger.desc: Fox squirrel (Sciurus niger): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sciurus niger.about: The fox squirrel, also known as the eastern fox squirrel or Bryant's fox squirrel, is the largest species of tree squirrel native to North America.

sciurus vulgaris.name: Red squirrel
sciurus vulgaris.desc: Eats conifer seeds, nuts and buds in the canopy, and is taken by foxes and lynx.
sciurus vulgaris.about: The red squirrel, also called Eurasian red squirrel, is a species of tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus. It is an arboreal and primarily herbivorous rodent and common throughout Eurasia.

scleractinia.name: Reef corals
scleractinia.desc: Hard corals on the outer reefs and in the lagoon. Bleaching in 2016 cut hard coral cover on seaward reefs by over half, and juveniles have since returned.
scleractinia.about: Scleractinia, also called stony corals or hard corals, are marine animals in the phylum Cnidaria that build themselves a hard skeleton.

sclerocarya birrea.name: Marula
sclerocarya birrea.desc: A large fruiting tree common in the central woodlands. Elephants eat its bark, leaves and fruit.
sclerocarya birrea.about: Sclerocarya birrea commonly known as marula, is a medium-sized deciduous fruit-bearing tree, indigenous to the miombo woodlands of Southern Africa, the Sudano-Sahelian range of West Africa, the…

scolecocampa liburna.name: Dead-wood Borer Moth
scolecocampa liburna.desc: Dead-wood Borer Moth (Scolecocampa liburna): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

scolia dubia.name: Blue-winged Scoliid Wasp
scolia dubia.desc: Blue-winged Scoliid Wasp (Scolia dubia): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
scolia dubia.about: Scolia dubia, also known as the two-spotted scoliid wasp or a blue-winged scoliid wasp, is a species in the family Scoliidae.

scoliopus bigelovii.name: Foetid adder's-tongue
scoliopus bigelovii.desc: Foetid adder's-tongue (Scoliopus bigelovii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 659 times near the park in GBIF.

scopus umbretta.name: Hamerkop
scopus umbretta.desc: A wading bird of shallow water that mainly eats amphibians and fish, and a generalist hunter.
scopus umbretta.about: The hamerkop, also called the umbrette, is a medium-sized water bird with brown plumage.

scutellaria bushii.name: Bush's skullcap
scutellaria bushii.desc: Bush's skullcap (Scutellaria bushii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

scutellaria galericulata.name: Skullcap
scutellaria galericulata.desc: Skullcap (Scutellaria galericulata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
scutellaria galericulata.about: Scutellaria galericulata, the common skullcap, marsh skullcap or hooded skullcap, is a hardy perennial herb native to northern areas of the Northern Hemisphere, including Europe, Asia, and almost all…

scylla serrata.name: Mud crab
scylla serrata.desc: A large crab of estuaries and mangroves. Juveniles stay in the mangroves and the species is highly cannibalistic.
scylla serrata.about: Scylla serrata is an ecologically important species of crab found in the estuaries and mangroves of Africa, Australia, and Asia.

scyphozoa.name: Jellyfish
scyphozoa.desc: Drifting predators of plankton and a main food of loggerhead turtles at sea.
scyphozoa.about: Jellyfish, also known as sea jellies or simply jellies, are the medusa-phase of certain gelatinous members of the subphylum Medusozoa, which is a major part of the phylum Cnidaria.

sea ice.name: Sea ice
sea ice.desc: A platform for algae, seals and bears. It shrinks every year as the Arctic warms.

seabed sediment.name: Seabed sediment
seabed sediment.desc: Sandy and muddy bottom where seagrass roots, burrowing animals and buried organic matter are found.

seasonal fire.name: Seasonal fire
seasonal fire.desc: Fire shapes the Cerrado, and many of its plants have thick, corky bark or other traits that let them survive it.

seasonal flood.name: Seasonal flood
seasonal flood.desc: Rain on the Angolan highlands sends a pulse of water that reaches the delta in the dry season and spreads over the sands.

seasonal flood pulse.name: Seasonal flood pulse
seasonal flood pulse.desc: Monsoon rains reverse the flow of the Tonlé Sap River, and the lake swells from roughly 2,500 km2 to over 16,000 km2, drowning forest and fields.

seasonal flooding.name: Seasonal flooding
seasonal flooding.desc: Rivers flood the swamp forests and riverbank grasses, spreading water and nutrients.

seasonal floodwater.name: Seasonal floodwater
seasonal floodwater.desc: Chobe and Linyanti floodwater spreads across the floodplains in the wet season and shrinks in the dry season.

seasonal grazing (transhumance).name: Seasonal grazing (transhumance)
seasonal grazing (transhumance).desc: Flocks and herds are driven to high summer pastures each year, a long-running practice that helps keep the uplands open.

seasonal rain.name: Seasonal rain
seasonal rain.desc: Rain on the steep, rocky hillsides drives growth in the dry forest and runs off to the bays.

seasonal rain and mist.name: Seasonal rain and mist
seasonal rain and mist.desc: The cold current brings drizzle for much of the year, and rainfall swings wildly between years, with El Niño years much wetter.

seasonal rainfall.name: Seasonal rainfall
seasonal rainfall.desc: A wet season from about October to April brings most of the water. Baobab trunks swell and shrink with it, and the long dry season leaves the forest mostly leafless.

seasonal rains.name: Seasonal rains
seasonal rains.desc: Rain arrives in two seasons and sets the timing of the whole migration.

seasonal rains and river floods.name: Seasonal rains and river floods
seasonal rains and river floods.desc: The wet season fills the Comoé River and its tributaries and its seasonal ponds; many ponds dry out in the dry season.

seasonal river flooding.name: Seasonal river flooding
seasonal river flooding.desc: The Essequibo, Siparuni and Burro-Burro rivers bound and cross the reserve. Rising water spreads into low forest and swamp.

seawater & currents.name: Seawater & currents
seawater & currents.desc: Warm, clear water carries plankton and keeps temperature in the narrow range corals tolerate.

seawater and nutrients.name: Seawater and nutrients
seawater and nutrients.desc: Salty, nutrient-bearing water of the bay and its tidal flats, which feeds plankton and mangroves. Pollution and silt cloud it.

sebastes spp..name: Rockfish
sebastes spp..desc: Use the kelp understory for shelter and feeding, taking small invertebrates there.
sebastes spp..about: Sebastes is a genus of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the subfamily Sebastinae part of the family Scorpaenidae, most of which have the common name of rockfish.

sediment & nutrients.name: Sediment & nutrients
sediment & nutrients.desc: Silt carries nitrogen and phosphorus onto the floodplain. Much of it travels downriver to the Gulf of Mexico.

sedum lanceolatum.name: Lance-leaf stonecrop
sedum lanceolatum.desc: Lance-leaf stonecrop (Sedum lanceolatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

sedum nuttallii.name: Yellow stonecrop
sedum nuttallii.desc: Yellow stonecrop (Sedum nuttallii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 117 times near the park in GBIF.
sedum nuttallii.about: Sedum nuttallii, the yellow stonecrop (a name it shares with other members of its genus), is a species of flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae, native to the central United States.

sedum pulchellum.name: Widowscross
sedum pulchellum.desc: Widowscross (Sedum pulchellum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
sedum pulchellum.about: Sedum pulchellum is a species of flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae known by the common names widowscross and widow's cross.

sedum spathulifolium.name: Colorado stonecrop
sedum spathulifolium.desc: Colorado stonecrop (Sedum spathulifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
sedum spathulifolium.about: Sedum spathulifolium is a species of flowering plant in the family Crassulaceae known by the common names broadleaf stonecrop, yellow stonecrop, and spoon-leaved stonecrop.

sedum ternatum.name: Wild stonecrop
sedum ternatum.desc: Wild stonecrop (Sedum ternatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
sedum ternatum.about: Sedum ternatum is the most widespread native Sedum species in eastern North America, commonly known as woodland stonecrop. It has white flowers, blooming April to May.

seiurus aurocapilla.name: Ovenbird
seiurus aurocapilla.desc: Ovenbird (Seiurus aurocapilla): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.
seiurus aurocapilla.about: The ovenbird is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Seiurus.

selasphorus platycercus.name: Broad-tailed Hummingbird
selasphorus platycercus.desc: Broad-tailed Hummingbird (Selasphorus platycercus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

selenia aurea.name: Golden selenia
selenia aurea.desc: Golden selenia (Selenia aurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
selenia aurea.about: Selenia aurea, the golden selenia, is a flowering plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae).

semicossyphus pulcher.name: California sheephead
semicossyphus pulcher.desc: A reef fish that eats sea urchins, crabs and molluscs. Wikipedia calls it a keystone predator of urchins in southern California.
semicossyphus pulcher.about: The California sheephead (Bodianus pulcher, is a species of wrasse native to the eastern Pacific Ocean. Its range is from Monterey Bay, California, to the Gulf of California, Mexico.

semnopithecus entellus.name: Northern plains gray langur
semnopithecus entellus.desc: A leaf-and-fruit-eating monkey that is regular prey for tigers and leopards and sometimes for crocodiles.
semnopithecus entellus.about: The northern plains gray langur, also known as the sacred langur, Bengal sacred langur and Hanuman langur, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

semnopithecus hector.name: Tarai gray langur
semnopithecus hector.desc: A leaf and fruit eating monkey of the forest and its edges, hunted by leopards and tigers.
semnopithecus hector.about: The Tarai gray langur is an Old World monkey, and was formerly considered a subspecies of the northern plains gray langur.

semnopithecus johnii.name: Nilgiri langur
semnopithecus johnii.desc: A leaf- and fruit-eating monkey of the southern Western Ghats; GloBI records langurs eating figs and jamun.
semnopithecus johnii.about: The Nilgiri langur is an Asian langur of the Old World monkey. It has glossy, black fur and an orangey-golden brown, hair-like mane on its head.

semnopithecus vetulus.name: Purple-faced langur
semnopithecus vetulus.desc: A mostly leaf-eating monkey of closed-canopy wet-zone forest that also eats fruit, flowers and seeds. Its range is now small and fragmented.
semnopithecus vetulus.about: The purple-faced langur, also known as the purple-faced leaf monkey, is a species of Old World monkey that is endemic to Sri Lanka.

sempervivum.name: Houseleeks
sempervivum.desc: Succulent rosettes on rock and thin soil. They are the caterpillar food plant of the Apollo butterfly, which also takes a bitter compound from them.
sempervivum.about: Sempervivum () is a genus of about 40 species of flowering plants in the family Crassulaceae, commonly known as houseleeks.

senecio flaccidus.name: Threadleaf groundsel
senecio flaccidus.desc: Threadleaf groundsel (Senecio flaccidus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

senecio spartioides.name: Broom groundsel
senecio spartioides.desc: Broom groundsel (Senecio spartioides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
senecio spartioides.about: Senecio spartioides is a species of flowering plant in the aster family known by the common name broom-like ragwort.

senecio vulgaris.name: Groundsel
senecio vulgaris.desc: Groundsel (Senecio vulgaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

senegal river floodwater.name: Senegal River floodwater
senegal river floodwater.desc: The sanctuary lies in the Senegal River delta, a chain of lakes, backwaters and channels that depend on river water.

senegalia greggii.name: Texas-mimosa
senegalia greggii.desc: Texas-mimosa (Senegalia greggii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 269 times near the park in GBIF.

senegalia nigrescens.name: Knobthorn
senegalia nigrescens.desc: A thorny savanna tree, browsed by giraffes and a main tree on the eastern grazing lands.
senegalia nigrescens.about: Senegalia nigrescens, the knobthorn, is a deciduous African tree, growing up to 18 m tall, that is found in savanna regions from West Africa to South Africa.

senna roemeriana.name: Twoleaf senna
senna roemeriana.desc: Twoleaf senna (Senna roemeriana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
senna roemeriana.about: Senna roemeriana, the twoleaf senna, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae, native to the US states of New Mexico and Texas, and to northern Mexico.

senna tora.name: Sickle senna
senna tora.desc: A common weedy shrub of the park area. GloBI records show chital and sambar eating it.
senna tora.about: This page is about the Cassia tora described by Linnaeus. Later authors usually applied the taxon to Senna obtusifolia.

sepia.name: Cuttlefish
sepia.desc: Wikipedia lists cuttlefish among the bay species. They hunt small fish and crustaceans.
sepia.about: Cuttlefish, or cuttles, are marine molluscs of the family Sepiidae. They belong to the class Cephalopoda which also includes squid, octopuses, and nautiluses.

sequoia sempervirens.name: Coast redwood
sequoia sempervirens.desc: The tallest tree on Earth. It takes up fog water through its leaves and bark, and its canopy builds soil that holds life high above ground.
sequoia sempervirens.about: Sequoia sempervirens (), the coast redwood, is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family, Cupressaceae. Other common names include coastal redwood and California redwood.

sequoiadendron giganteum.name: Giant sequoia
sequoiadendron giganteum.desc: Grows in scattered groves on the western slope. Thick bark protects mature trees from fire, and fire clears the ground for seedlings.
sequoiadendron giganteum.about: Sequoiadendron giganteum is a species of coniferous tree, classified in the family Cupressaceae in the subfamily Sequoioideae. Giant sequoia specimens are the largest trees on Earth.

seriola lalandi.name: Yellowtail kingfish
seriola lalandi.desc: A fast open-water fish that eats other fish and squid. Visitors can hand-feed kingfish at Ned's Beach.
seriola lalandi.about: The yellowtail amberjack, yellowtail kingfish, hiramasa or great amberjack is a large fish found in the oceans of the Southern Hemisphere.

serrasalmus.name: Piranha
serrasalmus.desc: Omnivorous river fish whose diet varies widely: fish and other animals, but also fruit, seeds and leaves. They often scavenge.
serrasalmus.about: A piranha is any of a number of freshwater fish species in the subfamily Serrasalminae, of the family Serrasalmidae, in the order Characiformes.

sesarmidae.name: Mangrove crabs
sesarmidae.desc: Small crabs of mangrove mud that feed on fallen mangrove leaves and so move mangrove nutrients into the mud and other animals.
sesarmidae.about: The Sesarmidae are a family of crabs, previously included in the Grapsidae by many authors. Several species, namely in Geosesarma, Metopaulias, and Sesarma, are true terrestrial crabs.

sesuvium revolutifolium.name: Sesuvium revolutifolium
sesuvium revolutifolium.desc: Sesuvium revolutifolium (Sesuvium revolutifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
sesuvium revolutifolium.about: Sesuvium portulacastrum is a sprawling perennial herb in the family Aizoaceae that grows in coastal and mangrove areas throughout much of the world.

setaria parviflora.name: Knotroot Bristle-grass
setaria parviflora.desc: Knotroot Bristle-grass (Setaria parviflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.

setaria viridis.name: Grasses & meadow herbs
setaria viridis.desc: Bristle-grass, dandelion, clover and other open-ground plants that geese and small herbivores graze.
setaria viridis.about: Setaria viridis is a species of grass known by many common names, including green foxtail, green bristlegrass, and wild foxtail millet. It is sometimes considered a subspecies of Setaria italica.

setophaga aestiva.name: American Yellow Warbler
setophaga aestiva.desc: American Yellow Warbler (Setophaga aestiva): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

setophaga and leiothlypis spp..name: Boreal warblers
setophaga and leiothlypis spp..desc: Insect-eating songbirds. Some warblers are linked to spruce budworm outbreaks, which supply abundant caterpillar food.
setophaga and leiothlypis spp..about: The Cape May warbler is a species of New World warbler. It breeds in northern North America.

setophaga caerulescens.name: Black-throated Blue Warbler
setophaga caerulescens.desc: Black-throated Blue Warbler (Setophaga caerulescens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 162 times near the park in GBIF.

setophaga coronata.name: Yellow-rumped Warbler
setophaga coronata.desc: Yellow-rumped Warbler (Setophaga coronata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 370 times near the park in GBIF.
setophaga coronata.about: The yellow-rumped warbler is a North American bird species that can be commonly observed all across the continent. Its extensive range connects both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts of the U.S.

setophaga occidentalis.name: Hermit Warbler
setophaga occidentalis.desc: Hermit Warbler (Setophaga occidentalis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,884 times near the park in GBIF.
setophaga occidentalis.about: The hermit warbler is a small perching bird. It is a species of New World warbler or wood-warbler.

setophaga petechia.name: Yellow Warbler
setophaga petechia.desc: Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 580 times near the park in GBIF.
setophaga petechia.about: The mangrove warbler or mangrove yellow warbler is a New World warbler species. It a small bright yellow bird that is found in mangroves on the Atlantic and Pacific coasts of the tropical Americas.

setophaga pinus.name: Pine Warbler
setophaga pinus.desc: Pine Warbler (Setophaga pinus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 72 times near the park in GBIF.
setophaga pinus.about: The pine warbler is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae.

setophaga ruticilla.name: American Redstart
setophaga ruticilla.desc: American Redstart (Setophaga ruticilla): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 223 times near the park in GBIF.

setophaga virens.name: Black-throated Green Warbler
setophaga virens.desc: Black-throated Green Warbler (Setophaga virens): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 705 times near the park in GBIF.

shallow lagoons.name: Shallow lagoons
shallow lagoons.desc: Warm, sheltered lagoons where eelgrass grows. They are the calving grounds for gray whales each winter.

shallow saline lakes.name: Shallow saline lakes
shallow saline lakes.desc: Tengiz is a shallow salt lake, about 2.5 m deep on average, and the neighbouring Korgalzhyn lake is the northernmost nesting site of greater flamingos.

shallow salty groundwater.name: Shallow salty groundwater
shallow salty groundwater.desc: Groundwater lies only a few feet under the dunes, deeper to the east and shallower to the west, and it is very salty.

shepherdia argentea.name: Buffalo-berry
shepherdia argentea.desc: Buffalo-berry (Shepherdia argentea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

shepherdia canadensis.name: Canadian buffaloberry
shepherdia canadensis.desc: A berry-bearing shrub of open forest. GloBI records show bears eating the berries and snowshoe hares eating the plant.
shepherdia canadensis.about: Shepherdia canadensis, commonly called Canada buffaloberry, russet buffaloberry, soopolallie, soapberry, or foamberry (Ktunaxa: kupaʔtiⱡ) is one of a small number of shrubs of the genus Shepherdia…

shepherdia rotundifolia.name: Roundleaf buffaloberry
shepherdia rotundifolia.desc: Roundleaf buffaloberry (Shepherdia rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 52 times near the park in GBIF.
shepherdia rotundifolia.about: Shepherdia rotundifolia, the roundleaf buffaloberry or silverleaf, is a 3-to-6-foot (1-to-2-meter) evergreen shrub in the oleaster family (Elaeagnaceae) that grows only in the Colorado Plateau…

sherardia arvensis.name: Field Madder
sherardia arvensis.desc: Field Madder (Sherardia arvensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
sherardia arvensis.about: Sherardia is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae.

shifting sand dunes.name: Shifting sand dunes
shifting sand dunes.desc: Wind and waves keep the sandy shore moving; only plants adapted to salt spray and drifting sand can hold it.

shorea robusta.name: Sal
shorea robusta.desc: The dominant tree of the park, making up about 70 percent of the cover and forming the purest stands in the central lowlands.
shorea robusta.about: Shorea robusta, the sal tree, shala, sakhua, or sarai, is a species of tree in the family Dipterocarpaceae. The tree is native to India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Tibet and across the Himalayan regions.

short mountain summer.name: Short mountain summer
short mountain summer.desc: At high elevation the growing season is brief, so plants grow fast in summer and animals feed, store fat or hibernate.

short summer sun.name: Short summer sun
short summer sun.desc: Meadow plants have only a brief snow-free season, so they flower and set seed quickly once the snow melts.

sialia currucoides.name: Mountain Bluebird
sialia currucoides.desc: Mountain Bluebird (Sialia currucoides): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.
sialia currucoides.about: The mountain bluebird is a migratory small thrush that is found in mountainous districts of western North America. It has a light underbelly and black eyes.

sialia mexicana.name: Western Bluebird
sialia mexicana.desc: Western Bluebird (Sialia mexicana): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 5,858 times near the park in GBIF.
sialia mexicana.about: The western bluebird is a small North American thrush.

sialia sialis.name: Eastern Bluebird
sialia sialis.desc: Eastern Bluebird (Sialia sialis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 53 times near the park in GBIF.
sialia sialis.about: The eastern bluebird is a small North American migratory thrush found in open woodlands, farmlands, and orchards.
