sibbaldia tridentata.desc: Mountain cinquefoil (Sibbaldia tridentata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 126 times near the park in GBIF.

sicyos angulatus.name: Bur Cucumber
sicyos angulatus.desc: Bur Cucumber (Sicyos angulatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
sicyos angulatus.about: Sicyos angulatus, the oneseed bur cucumber or star-cucumber is an annual vine in the gourd family, Cucurbitaceae, native to eastern North America. The plant forms mats or climbs using tendrils.

sida abutilifolia.name: Creeping sida
sida abutilifolia.desc: Creeping sida (Sida abutilifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

sidalcea malviflora.name: California checkerbloom

sidalcea neomexicana.name: New Mexico checker
sidalcea neomexicana.desc: New Mexico checker (Sidalcea neomexicana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
sidalcea neomexicana.about: Sidalcea neomexicana is a species of flowering plant in the mallow family known by the common names salt spring checkerbloom, Rocky Mountain checker-mallow, and New Mexico checker.

sideritis.name: Mountain herbs
sideritis.desc: Aromatic herbs such as mountain tea (Sideritis raeseri) grow here and have long been gathered by local healers.
sideritis.about: Sideritis, also known as ironwort, mountain tea and shepherd's tea, is a genus of flowering plants known for their use as herbal medicine, commonly as a herbal tea.

siganus.name: Rabbitfish
siganus.desc: Plant-eating reef fish that graze seagrass and algae. They are a typical link from seagrass beds to larger fish.
siganus.about: Siganidae, the rabbitfishes, are a small family of ray-finned fishes in the order Perciformes. The only extant genus is Siganus, the rabbitfish and spinefoot.

siganus canaliculatus.name: White-spotted spinefoot
siganus canaliculatus.desc: A herbivorous fish of the Gulf that eats mainly benthic algae and some seagrass; it is trapped by local fishers.
siganus canaliculatus.about: Siganus canaliculatus, the white-spotted spinefoot, white-spotted rabbitfish, pearly spinefoot, seagrass rabbitfish, slimy spinefoot or smudgespot spinefoot is a species of marine ray-finned fish, a…

sigaus piliferus.name: North Island grasshopper
sigaus piliferus.desc: A short-horned grasshopper restricted to alpine and sub-alpine habitats of the North Island, including the central volcanic region.
sigaus piliferus.about: Sigaus piliferus is a species of short-horned grasshopper in the family Acrididae. It is found in New Zealand.

sigmodon hispidus.name: Hispid cotton rat
sigmodon hispidus.desc: HISPID COTTON RAT (Sigmodon hispidus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.
sigmodon hispidus.about: The hispid cotton rat is a rat long thought to occur in parts of South America, Central America, and southern North America.

silene acaulis.desc: Low cushion plants, such as moss campion, make up the tundra vegetation, which covers over a third of the park. Recovery from trampling takes centuries.
silene acaulis.about: Silene acaulis, known as moss campion or cushion pink, is a small wildflower that is common all over the high arctic and tundra and in high mountains of Eurasia and North America (Alps, Carpathians,…

silene coronaria.name: Crown-pink
silene coronaria.desc: Crown-pink (Silene coronaria): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

silene csereii.about: Silene csereii, the Balkan catchfly, is a species of flowering plant found in countries surrounding the Black Sea and northern Caspian Sea.

silene laciniata.name: Cardinal catchfly

silene laciniata.about: Silene laciniata is a perennial herb in the family (Caryophyllaceae), commonly known as fringed Indian pink, cardinal catchfly, Mexican campion, Mexican-pink, and campion.

silene stellata.about: Silene stellata, known by the common names starry campion, widow's frill, and whorled catchfly, is a perennial herbaceous summer forb with white flowers, native to the central and eastern United…

silene virginica.name: Fire-pink
silene virginica.desc: Fire-pink (Silene virginica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 33 times near the park in GBIF.
silene virginica.about: Silene virginica, the fire pink, is a perennial wildflower native to eastern and central North America that belongs to the pink family, Caryophyllaceae.

silene vulgaris.name: Bladder Campion
silene vulgaris.desc: Bladder Campion (Silene vulgaris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
silene vulgaris.about: Silene vulgaris, the bladder campion or maidenstears, is a plant species of the genus Silene within the family Caryophyllaceae.

sillaginidae.name: Whitings
sillaginidae.desc: Small bottom-feeding fish of shallow sandy bays that eat small crustaceans and worms. Prey for dolphins, cormorants and sharks.
sillaginidae.about: The Sillaginidae, commonly known as the smelt-whitings, whitings, sillaginids, sand borers and sand-smelts, are a family of benthic coastal marine fish historically classified in the order…

silphium laciniatum.name: Prairie wildflowers
silphium laciniatum.desc: Compass plant, gayfeather, milkweed and many other wildflowers add most of the prairie plant diversity and feed insects and browsers.
silphium laciniatum.about: Silphium laciniatum is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known commonly as compassplant or compass plant.

silphium perfoliatum.name: Cup-plant
silphium perfoliatum.desc: Cup-plant (Silphium perfoliatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

silphium terebinthinaceum.name: Basal-leaf rosinweed
silphium terebinthinaceum.desc: Basal-leaf rosinweed (Silphium terebinthinaceum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

simalia kinghorni.name: Scrub python
simalia kinghorni.desc: A large ambush predator of the rainforest that takes flying foxes, wallabies and tree-kangaroos.

simmondsia chinensis.name: Jojoba
simmondsia chinensis.desc: Jojoba (Simmondsia chinensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
simmondsia chinensis.about: Jojoba – also commonly called goat nut, deer nut, pignut, wild hazel, quinine nut, coffeeberry, and gray box bush – is an evergreen, dioecious shrub native to the Southwestern United States and…

sisyrinchium bellum.desc: Western blue-eyed grass (Sisyrinchium bellum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.
sisyrinchium bellum.about: Sisyrinchium bellum, the western blue-eyed grass or Californian blue-eyed grass, is the common blue-eyed grass of California and Oregon in and west of the Sierra Nevada, its range extending south…

sitta canadensis.about: The red-breasted nuthatch is a small songbird. The adult has blue-grey upperparts with cinnamon underparts, a white throat and face with a black stripe through the eyes, a straight grey bill and a…

sitta carolinensis.name: White-breasted Nuthatch
sitta carolinensis.desc: White-breasted Nuthatch (Sitta carolinensis): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 105 times near the park in GBIF.
sitta carolinensis.about: The white-breasted nuthatch is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is a medium-sized nuthatch, measuring approximately 15.5 cm (6.1 in) in length.

sitta pygmaea.name: Pygmy Nuthatch
sitta pygmaea.desc: Pygmy Nuthatch (Sitta pygmaea): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 511 times near the park in GBIF.
sitta pygmaea.about: The pygmy nuthatch is a tiny songbird, native to western North America.

sium suave.name: Hemlock Water-parsnip
sium suave.desc: Hemlock Water-parsnip (Sium suave): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
sium suave.about: Sium suave, the water parsnip or hemlock waterparsnip, is a perennial wildflower in the family Apiaceae. It is native to many areas of both Asia and North America.

smallanthus uvedalia.name: Bear's-foot
smallanthus uvedalia.desc: Bear's-foot (Smallanthus uvedalia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.
smallanthus uvedalia.about: Smallanthus uvedalia, known as hairy leafcup, bear's foot, and yellow flower leafcup, is a herbaceous perennial native to the Central and Eastern United States.

smartweeds and millets.name: Moist-soil plants
smartweeds and millets.desc: Plants that sprout on exposed mud flats when floods recede. Their seeds feed ducks.
smartweeds and millets.about: Persicaria is a genus of herbaceous flowering plants in the knotweed family, Polygonaceae. Plants of the genus are known commonly as knotweeds or smartweeds.

smilax auriculata.name: Wild bamboo
smilax auriculata.desc: Wild bamboo (Smilax auriculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

smilax bona-nox.about: Smilax bona-nox, the saw greenbrier, is a species of plant in the family Smilacaceae. It is native to the Southern United States, and eastern Mexico.

smilax laurifolia.name: Bamboovine
smilax laurifolia.desc: Bamboovine (Smilax laurifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

smilax pumila.name: Sarsaparilla-vine

smilax rotundifolia.name: Common Greenbrier
smilax rotundifolia.desc: Common Greenbrier (Smilax rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

smilax tamnoides.name: Bristly greenbrier
smilax tamnoides.desc: Bristly greenbrier (Smilax tamnoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

smilax walteri.name: Coral greenbrier
smilax walteri.desc: Coral greenbrier (Smilax walteri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

snake river and wetlands.name: Snake River and wetlands
snake river and wetlands.desc: Rises on the Yellowstone Plateau and runs through the valley, with side channels and wetlands such as Willow Flats and Oxbow Bend that support willow, cottonwood and aspen.

snow.name: Winter snowpack
snow.desc: Lake Helen gets roughly 600 to 700 inches a year, and meltwater feeds meadows and forests into summer.

snow & glacier melt.name: Snow & glacier melt
snow & glacier melt.desc: The park holds glaciers such as the Pasterze; winter snow cover and summer meltwater shape which plants grow and where animals can feed.

snow & winter cold.name: Snow & winter cold
snow & winter cold.desc: Long cold winters bury forage, so winter food and shelter shape which animals thrive.

snow and cold winters.name: Snow and cold winters
snow and cold winters.desc: Deep snow and cold shape winter foraging, and heavy snowfall on the high peaks feeds streams in spring.

snow and glacier melt.name: Snow and glacier melt
snow and glacier melt.desc: Snow and ice cap the summit. Most of the ice cover has vanished since 1912, and the forest below acts as the main water reservoir.

snow and ice melt.name: Snow and ice melt
snow and ice melt.desc: Winter snow and the ice field of Yolyn Am feed meltwater into the mountain valleys and the dry plains below.

snow and snowfields.name: Snow and snowfields
snow and snowfields.desc: Snow insulates the ground in winter and its meltwater wets the tundra in spring. Perennial snowfields in the Brooks Range have shrunk a great deal since 1985.

snow and snowmelt.name: Snow and snowmelt
snow and snowmelt.desc: Winter snow supplies much of the moisture the rim plants use; the park averages about 120 inches of snowfall a year.

snow and winter cold.name: Snow and winter cold
snow and winter cold.desc: Deep winter snow and cold limit food for herbivores and cover carcasses, shaping when bears, wolves and ravens eat.

snow cover.name: Snow cover
snow cover.desc: Long winters bury willow and lichen under snow, forcing caribou to dig for food. Meltwater feeds tundra plants in spring.

snow cover & ice crusts.name: Snow cover & ice crusts
snow cover & ice crusts.desc: Snow shelters tundra plants through winter and melts into summer water. Rain falling on snow can freeze into an ice crust that locks reindeer out of their food.

snowmelt & streams.name: Snowmelt & streams
snowmelt & streams.desc: Winter snowpack melts into the rivers and soils that carry algae, willows and meadow grasses through the dry summer.

snowmelt and glacier meltwater.name: Snowmelt and glacier meltwater
snowmelt and glacier meltwater.desc: Meltwater from snowfields and glaciers feeds meadows and streams in spring and summer.

snowmelt and glacier water.name: Snowmelt and glacier water
snowmelt and glacier water.desc: Meltwater from winter snow and the glaciers around Belukha feeds the meadows and the rivers below.

snowmelt and marsh.name: Snowmelt and marsh
snowmelt and marsh.desc: Melting snow feeds streams and the deep marshy soil of the flat ground between mountains, watering the plateau through summer.

snowmelt and medano creek.name: Snowmelt and Medano Creek
snowmelt and medano creek.wiki: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve
snowmelt and medano creek.desc: Mountain snowmelt feeds Medano Creek and the water table. Wikipedia says peak creek flow is usually late May to early June.

snowmelt and summer rain.name: Snowmelt and summer rain
snowmelt and summer rain.desc: The park receives roughly 15 to 18 inches of precipitation a year, more than nearby Zion, and it feeds the plateau's trees and meadows.

snowpack.name: Snowpack
snowpack.desc: Winter snow cover decides when meadows green up and pushes animals such as chamois down to lower, forested slopes.

snowpack & glacier meltwater.name: Snowpack & glacier meltwater
snowpack & glacier meltwater.desc: Winter snow and glaciers feed the headwaters of major rivers rising in the mountains and water the valleys through summer.

snowpack & glaciers.name: Snowpack & glaciers
snowpack & glaciers.desc: Deep winter snow buries the high meadows and sets how early plants can grow. Its melt feeds the streams.

snowpack & kaweah meltwater.name: Snowpack & Kaweah meltwater
snowpack & kaweah meltwater.desc: Most precipitation falls in winter, as heavy snow at Lodgepole elevation. Meltwater feeds the Kaweah River drainage and the forests and woodlands it crosses.

snowpack & meltwater.name: Snowpack & meltwater
snowpack & meltwater.desc: The mountains collect snow that feeds streams, springs and meadows in dry surroundings; the park even holds a small glacier.

snowpack & snowmelt.name: Snowpack & snowmelt
snowpack & snowmelt.desc: Winter snow feeds meadows and streams through the dry summer. The park page says warming brings earlier melt, drier summers and a longer fire season.

snowpack and glacier melt.name: Snowpack and glacier melt
snowpack and glacier melt.desc: Winter snow and melting glaciers feed the streams and lakes and set the length of the growing season on the high slopes. Glaciers in the park have shrunk sharply since the 1800s.

snowpack and meltwater.name: Snowpack and meltwater
snowpack and meltwater.desc: Winter snow insulates low shrubs and hares, and the spring melt waters the tundra.

snowpack and snowmelt.name: Snowpack and snowmelt
snowpack and snowmelt.desc: Winter snow on the high slopes melts into streams and glacial lakes, watering the pastures below.

soil.name: Volcanic soil
soil.desc: Soils on volcanic rock supply nutrients to the park's forests and meadows.

soil & leaf litter.name: Soil & leaf litter
soil & leaf litter.desc: Forest litter and thin karst soils hold the nutrients the trees draw on.

soil & nutrients.name: Soil & nutrients
soil & nutrients.desc: Thin, rocky soils on volcanic rock. Nutrients return to them as dead plants and animals are broken down.

soil & peat.name: Soil & peat
soil & peat.desc: Nutrients in wetland soils feed the plants.

soil and limestone minerals.name: Soil and limestone minerals
soil and limestone minerals.desc: Thin northern soils, built on limestone in much of the region, hold the nutrients that plants draw on.

soil and nutrients.name: Soil and nutrients
soil and nutrients.desc: Soil holds the nutrients plants take up.

soil and peat nutrients.name: Soil and peat nutrients
soil and peat nutrients.desc: Nutrients held in wetland soil are recycled from dead plants and animals and feed new plant growth.

soil and sediment nutrients.name: Nutrients
soil and sediment nutrients.desc: Nutrients from forest litter, mangrove mud and recycled dead matter support plant growth on land and in the shallows.

soil and soil crust.name: Soil and soil crust
soil and soil crust.desc: Crusts of lichens, algae, fungi and cyanobacteria slow erosion, add nitrogen and help soil hold moisture.

soil fungi and bacteria.name: Decomposers
soil fungi and bacteria.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, including fallen saguaros, and return nutrients to the soil.

soil nutrients.name: Soil nutrients
soil nutrients.desc: Weathered volcanic rock and rotting leaf litter feed the forest trees.

soils and geology.name: Soils and geology
soils and geology.desc: Granite in the west and basalt in the east shape the soils and so the plant communities.

solanum americanum.name: Small-flowered Nightshade
solanum americanum.desc: Small-flowered Nightshade (Solanum americanum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
solanum americanum.about: Solanum americanum, commonly known as American black nightshade, small-flowered nightshade or glossy nightshade, is a herbaceous flowering plant.

solanum angustifolium.name: Buffalobur Nightshade
solanum angustifolium.desc: Buffalobur Nightshade (Solanum angustifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum carolinense.name: Horse-nettle
solanum carolinense.desc: Horse-nettle (Solanum carolinense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
solanum carolinense.about: Solanum carolinense, the Carolina horsenettle, is not a true nettle, but a member of the Solanaceae, or nightshade family.

solanum dimidiatum.name: Torrey Nightshade
solanum dimidiatum.desc: Torrey Nightshade (Solanum dimidiatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum dulcamara.name: Bittersweet
solanum dulcamara.desc: Bittersweet (Solanum dulcamara): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
solanum dulcamara.about: Solanum dulcamara is a species of vine in the genus Solanum (which also includes the potato and the tomato) of the family Solanaceae.

solanum elaeagnifolium.name: White Nightshade
solanum elaeagnifolium.desc: White Nightshade (Solanum elaeagnifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
solanum elaeagnifolium.about: Solanum elaeagnifolium, the silverleaf nightshade or silver-leaved nightshade, is a species of plant in the nightshade family native to North and South America.

solanum houstonii.name: Solanum
solanum houstonii.desc: Solanum (Solanum houstonii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

solanum lycocarpum.name: Wolf apple
solanum lycocarpum.desc: A tomato-like fruit that Wikipedia says can make up 40 to 90 percent of the maned wolf's diet and is available all year.
solanum lycocarpum.about: Solanum lycocarpum, or wolf apple, is common in the Brazilian Cerrado ecoregion. In Portuguese, the plant is called lobeira (lit. 'wolf's plant') or fruta-do-lobo ('wolf's fruit').

solanum sisymbriifolium.name: Sticky nightshade
solanum sisymbriifolium.desc: Sticky nightshade (Solanum sisymbriifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
solanum sisymbriifolium.about: Solanum sisymbriifolium is commonly known as vila-vila, sticky nightshade, red buffalo-bur, the fire-and-ice plant, litchi tomato, or Morelle de Balbis.

solar energy.name: Sunlight
solar energy.desc: Light powers the algae, eelgrass and marsh grass that start the estuary food web.

solenodon paradoxus.name: Hispaniolan solenodon
solenodon paradoxus.desc: An endangered nocturnal insectivore that probes soil and rotten logs for arthropods and also takes snails and small reptiles.
solenodon paradoxus.about: The Hispaniolan solenodon, also known as the agouta, is a small, furry, shrew-like mammal endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola.

solidago caesia.name: Axillary Goldenrod
solidago caesia.desc: Axillary Goldenrod (Solidago caesia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

solidago curtisii.name: Mountain decumbent goldenrod
solidago curtisii.desc: Mountain decumbent goldenrod (Solidago curtisii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

solidago flexicaulis.name: Zig-zag goldenrod
solidago flexicaulis.desc: Zig-zag goldenrod (Solidago flexicaulis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

solidago rugosa.name: Rough-stemmed Goldenrod
solidago rugosa.desc: Rough-stemmed Goldenrod (Solidago rugosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

solidago sempervirens.name: Salt-marsh Goldenrod
solidago sempervirens.desc: Salt-marsh Goldenrod (Solidago sempervirens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
solidago sempervirens.about: Solidago sempervirens, the seaside goldenrod or salt-marsh goldenrod, is a plant species in the genus Solidago of the family Asteraceae.

solidago uliginosa.name: Bog Goldenrod
solidago uliginosa.desc: Bog Goldenrod (Solidago uliginosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
solidago uliginosa.about: Solidago uliginosa, or bog goldenrod, is a North American species of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.

somateria mollissima.name: Common eider
somateria mollissima.desc: A sea duck that dives for mussels and crabs along the rocky coast. Wikipedia lists mussels as a favorite food.
somateria mollissima.about: The common eider (pronounced ), also called St. Cuthbert's duck or Cuddy's duck, is a large (50–71 cm (20–28 in) in body length) sea-duck that is distributed over the northern coasts of Europe, North…

sophora chrysophylla.name: Māmane
sophora chrysophylla.desc: A native subalpine tree whose flowers are nectar for ʻamakihi and ʻiʻiwi. It grows on the high slopes of Hawaiian volcanoes.
sophora chrysophylla.about: Sophora chrysophylla, known as māmane in Hawaiian, is a species of flowering plant in the pea and bean family, Fabaceae, that is endemic to Hawaii.

sorbus americana.name: American mountain-ash
sorbus americana.desc: American mountain-ash (Sorbus americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

sorbus aucuparia.name: Rowan
sorbus aucuparia.desc: A small tree whose berries are eaten by foxes, martens and many birds.
sorbus aucuparia.about: Sorbus aucuparia, commonly called rowan (, also UK: ) and mountain-ash, is a species of deciduous tree or shrub in the rose family.

sorex araneus.name: Common shrew
sorex araneus.desc: A tiny insectivore of the leaf litter that hunts beetles, worms and other invertebrates.
sorex araneus.about: The common shrew, also known as the Eurasian shrew, is the most common shrew, and one of the most common mammals, throughout Northern Europe, including Great Britain, but excluding Ireland.

sorghastrum nutans.name: Indiangrass
sorghastrum nutans.desc: Indian Grass (Sorghastrum nutans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
sorghastrum nutans.about: Sorghastrum nutans, known as Indiangrass, is a North American prairie grass found in the United States and Canada, especially in the Great Plains and tallgrass prairies.

sorghastrum nutans, panicum virgatum.name: Indiangrass & switchgrass
sorghastrum nutans, panicum virgatum.desc: Tall warm-season grasses that grow alongside big bluestem.
sorghastrum nutans, panicum virgatum.about: Sorghastrum nutans, known as Indiangrass, is a North American prairie grass found in the United States and Canada, especially in the Great Plains and tallgrass prairies.

sorghum.name: Savanna grasses
sorghum.desc: Tall grasses of the open woodland understorey. Fresh green shoots after a burn draw in wallabies and other grazers.
sorghum.about: Sorghum bicolor, commonly called sorghum () and also known as broomcorn, great millet, Indian millet, Guinea corn, jowar, or milo, is a species in the grass genus Sorghum.

sorghum halepense.name: Johnson-grass
sorghum halepense.desc: Johnson-grass (Sorghum halepense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sorindeia grandifolia.name: Sorindeia trees
sorindeia grandifolia.desc: A forest tree whose fruit has been recorded as food for the Guinea turaco, piping hornbill and African green pigeon.
sorindeia grandifolia.about: Sorindeia is a genus of flowering plants in the cashew family, Anacardiaceae. It includes ten species native to tropical Africa, Madagascar, and the Comoro Islands.

sousa plumbea.name: Indian Ocean humpback dolphin
sousa plumbea.desc: A shallow coastal dolphin that mostly eats sciaenid fish, cephalopods and crustaceans.
sousa plumbea.about: The Indian Ocean humpback dolphin is a member of the Delphinidae family occupying coastal areas ranging from Southern Africa to Western Indochina.

sousa teuszii.name: Atlantic humpback dolphin
sousa teuszii.desc: Rare coastal dolphin that herds mullet and other inshore fish, sometimes towards Imraguen fishers' nets.
sousa teuszii.about: The Atlantic humpback dolphin is a species of humpback dolphin that is found in coastal areas of West Africa.

south nahanni river and meltwater.name: South Nahanni River and meltwater
south nahanni river and meltwater.desc: The river and its tributaries run the length of the reserve and water the willow thickets, sedge meadows and river flats.

southern patagonian ice field.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
southern patagonian ice field.desc: The great ice cap feeds dozens of glaciers such as Perito Moreno, which end in Lake Argentino and shape the valleys and rivers.

spaelotis clandestina.name: Clandestine Dart Moth
spaelotis clandestina.desc: Clandestine Dart Moth (Spaelotis clandestina): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 121 times near the park in GBIF.
spaelotis clandestina.about: The clandestine dart or w-marked cutworm is a moth of the family Noctuidae.

sparisoma viride.name: Stoplight parrotfish
sparisoma viride.desc: A reef grazer that scrapes algae off coral rock, helping keep corals from being smothered.
sparisoma viride.about: The stoplight parrotfish is a species of marine ray-finned fish, a parrotfish from the family Scaridae, inhabiting coral reefs in Florida, Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, Bermuda and as far south as…

sparse stony soil.name: Sparse stony soil
sparse stony soil.desc: Sandy, well-drained, nutrient-poor ground that yareta prefers and the grasses must make do with.

spartina alterniflora.name: Smooth cordgrass
spartina alterniflora.desc: Fringe marshes that shelter young shrimp, crabs and fish.
spartina alterniflora.about: Sporobolus alterniflorus, or synonymously known as Spartina alterniflora, the smooth cordgrass, saltmarsh cordgrass, or salt-water cordgrass, is a perennial deciduous grass which is found in…

spartium junceum.name: Spanish broom
spartium junceum.desc: Spanish broom (Spartium junceum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 59 times near the park in GBIF.
spartium junceum.about: Spartium junceum, known as Spanish broom, rush broom, or weaver's broom, it is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and the sole species in the genus Spartium.

spathodea campanulata.name: African tulip tree
spathodea campanulata.desc: An introduced, invasive tree with nectar-rich flowers that attract birds and insects.
spathodea campanulata.about: Spathodea is a genus in the plant family Bignoniaceae. The single species it contains, Spathodea campanulata, is commonly known as the African tulip tree or the Nandi Flame.

spatula clypeata.name: Northern Shoveler
spatula clypeata.desc: Northern Shoveler (Spatula clypeata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1,413 times near the park in GBIF.
spatula clypeata.about: The northern shoveler, often known simply as the shoveler where other related species do not occur, is a common and widespread duck.

spatula discors.name: Blue-winged Teal
spatula discors.desc: Blue-winged Teal (Spatula discors): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 7,235 times near the park in GBIF.
spatula discors.about: The blue-winged teal is a species of bird in the duck, goose, and swan family Anatidae.

spawning rivers and streams.name: Spawning rivers and streams
spawning rivers and streams.desc: Small, short rivers where salmon and other salmonids return to spawn, carrying ocean nutrients inland.

spermophilus citellus.name: European ground squirrel
spermophilus citellus.desc: A burrowing grazer that needs short turf, which grazing maintains. It eats plants, seeds and insects and is a main prey of saker falcons.
spermophilus citellus.about: The European ground squirrel, also known as the European souslik, is a species from the squirrel family, Sciuridae. It is among the few European species in the genus Spermophilus.

spermophilus fulvus.name: Yellow ground squirrel
spermophilus fulvus.desc: A large burrowing ground squirrel of Central Asian deserts and steppe. It eats plants and is prey for raptors and foxes.
spermophilus fulvus.about: The yellow ground squirrel is a large and sturdy ground squirrel species native to Afghanistan, China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Russia.

spermophilus relictus.name: Relict ground squirrel
spermophilus relictus.desc: Burrowing rodent of Central Asian mountains found in Kyrgyzstan, a plant eater and prey for raptors.
spermophilus relictus.about: The relict ground squirrel is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae. It is found in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

spermophilus xanthoprymnus.name: Asia Minor ground squirrel
spermophilus xanthoprymnus.desc: A burrowing ground squirrel of open steppe that eats plants and is taken by buzzards and kestrels.
spermophilus xanthoprymnus.about: The Asia Minor ground squirrel, also known as Anatolian souslik, Anatolian ground squirrel, is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae. It is found in Armenia, Iran, and Turkey.

speyeria aphrodite.name: Aphrodite Fritillary
speyeria aphrodite.desc: Aphrodite Fritillary (Speyeria aphrodite): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 74 times near the park in GBIF.

speyeria atlantis.name: Atlantis Fritillary
speyeria atlantis.desc: Atlantis Fritillary (Speyeria atlantis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
speyeria atlantis.about: Speyeria atlantis, the Atlantis fritillary, is a butterfly of the family Nymphalidae of North America.

speyeria cybele.name: Great Spangled Fritillary
speyeria cybele.desc: Great Spangled Fritillary (Speyeria cybele): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
speyeria cybele.about: The great spangled fritillary is a North American butterfly of the family Nymphalidae.

speyeria idalia.name: Regal fritillary
speyeria idalia.desc: A butterfly the MDC names among the species that cannot persist without prairie. Adults feed on nectar from flowers such as milkweed and coneflower.
speyeria idalia.about: The regal fritillary is a striking nymphalid butterfly found in tallgrass and mixed-grass prairies in the east-central United States.

sphaeralcea coccinea.name: Moss-rose
sphaeralcea coccinea.desc: A low orange-flowered wildflower of dry prairie that prairie dogs favour in late summer and fall.
sphaeralcea coccinea.about: Sphaeralcea coccinea, commonly known as the scarlet globemallow, scarlet mallow, cowboy's delight, prairie mallow, red false mallow, or simply as globe mallow is a perennial plant growing 10–30 cm…

sphaeralcea laxa.name: Caliche globemallow
sphaeralcea laxa.desc: Caliche globemallow (Sphaeralcea laxa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

sphaeralcea munroana.name: Munro's globemallow
sphaeralcea munroana.desc: Munro's globemallow (Sphaeralcea munroana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
sphaeralcea munroana.about: Sphaeralcea munroana is a species of flowering plant in the mallow family known by the common names Munro's globemallow, Munro's desert-mallow and orange globe mallow.

sphaerophysa salsula.name: Austrian peaweed
sphaerophysa salsula.desc: Austrian peaweed (Sphaerophysa salsula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
sphaerophysa salsula.about: Sphaerophysa salsula is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by the common names alkali swainsonpea, Austrian peaweed, and red bladder-vetch.

sphaeropteris lunulata.name: Tree fern
sphaeropteris lunulata.desc: A tree fern recorded often in the wetter forest, part of the layered understorey.
sphaeropteris lunulata.about: Sphaeropteris lunulata is a species of tree fern in the family Cyatheaceae, native from Sulawesi in Malesia and the Bismarck Archipelago in Papuasia to the western Pacific.

sphagnum.name: Peat moss
sphagnum.desc: Moss that builds the raised bogs. Wikipedia says its slowly decaying remains accumulate as peat and its wet carpets hold many times their dry weight in water.
sphagnum.about: Sphagnum is a genus of approximately 380 species of mosses, commonly known as sphagnum moss, also bog moss and quacker moss (although that term is also sometimes used for peat).

sphecius speciosus.name: Cicada Killer
sphecius speciosus.desc: Cicada Killer (Sphecius speciosus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
sphecius speciosus.about: Sphecius speciosus, the eastern cicada-killer wasp, is a large, solitary digger wasp species in the family Bembicidae. They are so named because they hunt cicadas and provision their nests with them.

spheniscus magellanicus.name: Magellanic penguin
spheniscus magellanicus.desc: Eats small fish such as anchoita, plus squid and krill. Wikipedia reports about 150,000 breeding pairs at the peninsula.
spheniscus magellanicus.about: The Magellanic penguin is a South American penguin, breeding in coastal Patagonia, including Argentina, Chile, and the Falkland Islands, with some migrating to Brazil and Uruguay, where they are…

spheniscus mendiculus.name: Galápagos penguin
spheniscus mendiculus.desc: The only penguin living on the equator. It depends on cold Cromwell Current upwelling to supply the small fish it eats.
spheniscus mendiculus.about: The Galápagos penguin is a penguin endemic to the Galápagos Islands of Ecuador. It is the only penguin found north of the equator.

sphex ichneumoneus.name: American Golden Digger Wasp
sphex ichneumoneus.desc: American Golden Digger Wasp (Sphex ichneumoneus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sphingidae.name: Hawk moths
sphingidae.desc: Night-flying moths that carry baobab pollen from tree to tree while feeding on nectar.
sphingidae.about: The Sphingidae are a family of moths commonly called sphinx moths, also colloquially known as hawk moths; many of their caterpillars are known as hornworms. The family includes about 1,450 species.

sphyraena barracuda.name: Great barracuda
sphyraena barracuda.desc: An ambush predator of reefs and shallows; young stay in mangroves and seagrass.
sphyraena barracuda.about: Sphyraena barracuda, commonly known as the great barracuda, is a species of barracuda, a genus of 27 species of large ray-finned fish found in subtropical oceans worldwide.

sphyrapicus varius.name: Yellow-bellied Sapsucker
sphyrapicus varius.desc: Yellow-bellied Sapsucker (Sphyrapicus varius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 156 times near the park in GBIF.

sphyrna.name: Hammerhead sharks
sphyrna.desc: Hammerheads are reported in the park, which records eleven shark species, and hunt fish and squid around the reef.
sphyrna.about: The hammerhead sharks are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil.

sphyrna lewini.name: Scalloped hammerhead
sphyrna lewini.desc: A schooling shark that eats mainly bony fish, along with squid and octopus. It is an opportunist that takes what is abundant.
sphyrna lewini.about: The scalloped hammerhead is a species of hammerhead shark in the family Sphyrnidae. It was originally known as Zygaena lewini.

spigelia marilandica.name: Indian-pink
spigelia marilandica.desc: Indian-pink (Spigelia marilandica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
spigelia marilandica.about: Spigelia marilandica, the woodland pinkroot or Indian pink is a herbacious perennial wildflower in the Loganiaceae family native to inland areas of the Southeastern and Midwestern United States.

spilornis cheela.name: Crested serpent eagle
spilornis cheela.desc: A forest raptor that hunts snakes and lizards from perches under the canopy and is one of the best-recorded birds nearby.
spilornis cheela.about: The crested serpent eagle is a medium-sized bird of prey that is found in forested habitats across tropical Asia.

spinulum annotinum.name: Interrupted Clubmoss
spinulum annotinum.desc: Interrupted Clubmoss (Spinulum annotinum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
spinulum annotinum.about: Spinulum annotinum, synonym Lycopodium annotinum, known as interrupted club-moss, or stiff clubmoss, is a species of clubmoss native to forests of the colder parts of North America, as well as Asia…

spinus pinus.name: Pine Siskin
spinus pinus.desc: Pine Siskin (Spinus pinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 389 times near the park in GBIF.
spinus pinus.about: The pine siskin is a North American bird in the finch family. It is a migratory bird with an extremely sporadic winter range.

spinus psaltria.name: Lesser Goldfinch
spinus psaltria.desc: Lesser Goldfinch (Spinus psaltria): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 64 times near the park in GBIF.
spinus psaltria.about: The lesser goldfinch is a small finch in the genus Spinus native to the Americas. As is the case for most species in the genus Spinus, lesser goldfinch males have a black forehead, which females lack.

spinus spinus.name: Eurasian siskin
spinus spinus.desc: A small finch that eats seeds of alder and birch, and is prey for forest jays and stoats.
spinus spinus.about: The Eurasian siskin is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is also called the European siskin, common siskin or just siskin.

spinus tristis.name: American Goldfinch
spinus tristis.desc: American Goldfinch (Spinus tristis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 129 times near the park in GBIF.
spinus tristis.about: The American goldfinch is a small North American bird in the finch family.

spiraea alba.name: Pale Bridewort
spiraea alba.desc: Pale Bridewort (Spiraea alba): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
spiraea alba.about: Spiraea alba, commonly known as meadowsweet, white meadowsweet, narrowleaf meadowsweet, the botanical pale bridewort, or pipestem, is native to the wet soils of the Allegheny Mountains and other…

spiranthes incurva.name: Sphinx ladies’ tresses
spiranthes incurva.desc: Sphinx ladies’ tresses (Spiranthes incurva): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

spiranthes lacera.name: Northern Slender Ladies'-tresses
spiranthes lacera.desc: Northern Slender Ladies'-tresses (Spiranthes lacera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
spiranthes lacera.about: Spiranthes lacera, commonly called the slender ladies'-tresses, is a species of orchid that is native to Eastern North America.

spiranthes ochroleuca.name: Yellow Nodding Lady's Tresses
spiranthes ochroleuca.desc: Yellow Nodding Lady's Tresses (Spiranthes ochroleuca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

spiranthes tuberosa.name: Little Ladies'-tresses
spiranthes tuberosa.desc: Little Ladies'-tresses (Spiranthes tuberosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

spirogyra.name: River algae
spirogyra.desc: Green algae growing in the slow rivers, oxbow lakes and pools, the base of the aquatic food chain.
spirogyra.about: Spirogyra (common names include water silk, mermaid's tresses, and blanket weed) is a genus of filamentous charophyte green algae of the family Spirogyraceae, named for the helical or spiral…

spiza americana.name: Dickcissel
spiza americana.desc: A grassland songbird that nests in prairie and eats insects and seeds.
spiza americana.about: The dickcissel is a small seed-eating migratory bird in the family Cardinalidae.

spizella breweri.name: Brewer's Sparrow
spizella breweri.desc: Brewer's Sparrow (Spizella breweri): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 609 times near the park in GBIF.
spizella breweri.about: Brewer's sparrow is a small, slim species of American sparrow in the family Passerellidae. This bird was named after the ornithologist Thomas Mayo Brewer.

spizella pallida.name: Clay-colored Sparrow
spizella pallida.desc: Clay-colored Sparrow (Spizella pallida): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 324 times near the park in GBIF.
spizella pallida.about: The clay-colored sparrow or clay-coloured sparrow is a small New World sparrow of North America. Adults have light brown upperparts and pale underparts, with darker streaks on the back.

spizella passerina.name: Chipping Sparrow
spizella passerina.desc: Chipping Sparrow (Spizella passerina): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4,028 times near the park in GBIF.
spizella passerina.about: The chipping sparrow is a species of New World sparrow, a passerine bird in the family Passerellidae. It is widespread, fairly tame, and common across most of its North American range.

spizella pusilla.name: Field Sparrow
spizella pusilla.desc: Field Sparrow (Spizella pusilla): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5,558 times near the park in GBIF.
spizella pusilla.about: The field sparrow is a small New World sparrow in the family Passerellidae. It is about 140 mm (6 in) long and weighs about 12.5 g (0.4 oz).

sporobolus.name: Pan-edge salt grass
sporobolus.desc: Salt-tolerant Sporobolus grass grows on the otherwise bare pan margins. It is protein-rich and eaten by wildebeest and springbok.
sporobolus.about: Sporobolus is a nearly cosmopolitan genus of plants in the grass family.

sporobolus airoides.name: Alkali sacaton
sporobolus airoides.desc: A bunchgrass that tolerates alkaline soil. The park notes that such grasses feed many small animals, and their seeds feed rodents.
sporobolus airoides.about: Sporobolus airoides is a species of grass known by the common name alkali sacaton.

sporobolus alopecuroides.name: Foxtail Pricklegrass
sporobolus alopecuroides.desc: Foxtail Pricklegrass (Sporobolus alopecuroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

sporobolus pyramidalis.name: West Indian dropseed
sporobolus pyramidalis.desc: A tall tussock grass recorded often in the area. GloBI has records of hippos, elephants, warthogs and hartebeest eating it.
sporobolus pyramidalis.about: Sporobolus pyramidalis is a species of grass native to Africa and Yemen. It does not have a distinct established English name, but it is one of the two species of giant rat's tail grasses.

sporobolus virginicus.name: Tortoise turf
sporobolus virginicus.desc: A short mix of grasses and herbs, dwarfed by constant grazing, that grows in the tortoises' pastures.
sporobolus virginicus.about: Sporobolus virginicus, known by numerous common names including seashore dropseed, marine couch, sand couch, salt couch grass, saltwater couch, coastal rat-tail grass, and nioaka, is a species of…

spring rain & snowmelt.name: Spring rain & snowmelt
spring rain & snowmelt.desc: Moisture comes mainly in the cooler months, so plant growth surges in spring and slows in the hot dry summer.

spring-fed water.name: Spring-fed water
spring-fed water.desc: Springs keep Ozark streams cool and clear year round, the habitat that hellbenders and smallmouth bass need.

springs & seeps.name: Springs & seeps
springs & seeps.desc: Rattlesnake Springs and Oak Spring are rare permanent water in the park, and Rattlesnake Springs is a wooded oasis with over 300 bird species recorded.

springs & waterholes.name: Springs & waterholes
springs & waterholes.desc: Dry-season waterholes fed by springs concentrate wildlife, so animals gather and are easier for predators to find.

springs and oases.name: Springs and oases
springs and oases.desc: Natural oases, springs and seeps are rare water sources vital to resident wildlife, and support the native fan palm.

springtails, snails, worms.name: Leaf-litter invertebrates
springtails, snails, worms.desc: Tiny animals that eat decaying leaves and fungi on the forest floor. They are food for salamanders and firefly larvae.
springtails, snails, worms.about: Springtails (class Collembola) form the largest of the three lineages of modern hexapods that are no longer considered insects, the others being Protura and Diplura.

stachys tenuifolia.name: Smooth hedgenettle
stachys tenuifolia.desc: Smooth hedgenettle (Stachys tenuifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
stachys tenuifolia.about: Stachys tenuifolia, the smooth hedgenettle, is a herbaceous perennial plant in the family Lamiaceae.

standing and fallen deadwood.name: Standing and fallen deadwood
standing and fallen deadwood.desc: In unmanaged old forest, dead trees are left to stand and rot. They house beetles, fungi and the birds that feed on them.

stanleya pinnata.name: Desert prince's-plume
stanleya pinnata.desc: Desert prince's-plume (Stanleya pinnata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
stanleya pinnata.about: Stanleya pinnata is a species of flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae known as desert prince's-plume. It is a perennial herb or shrub native to North America.

staphida everetti.name: Chestnut-crested yuhina
staphida everetti.desc: A busy flocking bird that takes insects and fruit; one of the most recorded birds near the park.
staphida everetti.about: The chestnut-crested yuhina is a species of bird in the white-eye family Zosteropidae.

staphylea trifolia.name: American bladdernut
staphylea trifolia.desc: American bladdernut (Staphylea trifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
staphylea trifolia.about: Staphylea trifolia, the American bladdernut, is native to eastern North America, from southern Ontario and southwestern Quebec west to Nebraska and Arkansas, and south to Florida.

stellaria pubera.name: Star chickweed
stellaria pubera.desc: Star chickweed (Stellaria pubera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

stenaria nigricans.name: Prairie bluets
stenaria nigricans.desc: Prairie bluets (Stenaria nigricans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

stenella longirostris.name: Spinner dolphin
stenella longirostris.desc: Resident in large numbers. It eats small mesopelagic fish, squid and shrimp, and is preyed on by sharks.
stenella longirostris.about: The spinner dolphin is a small dolphin found in off-shore tropical waters around the world.

stenocara and other darkling beetles.name: Fog-basking beetles
stenocara and other darkling beetles.desc: Darkling beetles that harvest fog on their bumpy backs and drink the droplets that roll to their mouths. They scavenge wind-blown plant debris.
stenocara and other darkling beetles.about: Stenocara gracilipes, the racingstripe darkling beetle, is a species of beetle that is native to the Namib Desert in southern Africa.

stenocereus gummosus.name: Dagger cactus
stenocereus gummosus.desc: A sprawling columnar cactus of the Baja desert. Pronghorn include cacti in their diet, and succulents are a water source for desert animals.
stenocereus gummosus.about: Stenocereus gummosus is a flowering plant in the family Cactaceae that is found in Baja California, Mexico at elevations of 9 to 134 meters

stenocereus thurberi.name: Organpipe cactus
stenocereus thurberi.desc: Organpipe cactus (Stenocereus thurberi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1,003 times near the park in GBIF.
stenocereus thurberi.about: Stenocereus thurberi, the organ pipe cactus, is a species of cactus native to Mexico and the United States. The species is found in rocky desert.

stephanoaetus coronatus.name: Crowned eagle
stephanoaetus coronatus.desc: A powerful forest eagle that mostly takes monkeys, with duikers, bats and other small animals also on the menu.
stephanoaetus coronatus.about: The crowned eagle, also known as the African crowned eagle or the crowned hawk-eagle, is a large bird of prey found in sub-Saharan Africa; in Southern Africa, it is restricted to more easterly areas.

steppe and desert soil.name: Steppe and desert soil
steppe and desert soil.desc: Dry, often salty soils hold the nutrients that grasses, shrubs and trees draw on, and are replenished by decomposers.

stercorarius antarcticus.name: Brown skua
stercorarius antarcticus.desc: A bold seabird that takes eggs and chicks from penguin colonies and scavenges carcasses.
stercorarius antarcticus.about: The brown skua, also known as the Antarctic skua, Subantarctic skua, southern great skua, southern skua, or hākoakoa (Māori), is a large seabird that breeds in the subantarctic and Antarctic zones…

stercorarius longicaudus.name: Long-tailed jaeger
stercorarius longicaudus.desc: A tundra-nesting seabird that hunts lemmings and small birds in summer.
stercorarius longicaudus.about: The long-tailed jaeger or long-tailed skua is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae.

stercorarius maccormicki.name: South polar skua
stercorarius maccormicki.desc: Seabird that robs penguin colonies of eggs and chicks and scavenges carrion.
stercorarius maccormicki.about: The south polar skua is a large seabird in the skua family, Stercorariidae.

stercorarius parasiticus.name: Parasitic jaeger
stercorarius parasiticus.desc: A seabird of prey that nests on the tundra and takes lemmings and the eggs and chicks of other birds.
stercorarius parasiticus.about: The parasitic jaeger or arctic skua, also known as the parasitic skua or arctic jaeger, is a seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae.

stercorarius skua.name: Great skua
stercorarius skua.desc: Nests on the sands by the lagoon; it kills seabirds, steals fish from other birds and eats carrion.
stercorarius skua.about: The great skua, sometimes known by the name bonxie in Britain, is a large seabird in the skua family Stercorariidae. It is roughly the size of a herring gull.

sterna paradisaea.name: Arctic tern
sterna paradisaea.desc: Nests near the lagoon in large numbers and dives for herring and other small fish.
sterna paradisaea.about: The Arctic tern is a tern in the family Laridae. This bird has a circumpolar breeding distribution covering the Arctic and subarctic regions of Europe (as far south as Brittany), Asia, and North…

stetsonia coryne.name: Toothpick cactus
stetsonia coryne.desc: A tall columnar cactus of the dry Chaco, one of the succulents that store water through the dry season.
stetsonia coryne.about: Stetsonia coryne, the toothpick cactus, is the sole species in the cactus genus Stetsonia.

stipa.name: Needlegrasses
stipa.desc: Low, drought-hardy bunch grasses are among the main plants of the Gobi, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals.
stipa.about: Stipa is a genus of about 140 species of large perennial hermaphroditic grasses collectively known as feather grass, needle grass, and spear grass.

stipa barbata.name: Feather grass
stipa barbata.desc: A tussock grass named among the climax plants of the Syrian Desert. Overgrazing has replaced such plants with grasses of lower feed value.
stipa barbata.about: Stipa barbata, commonly known as the bearded feather grass or silver feather grass, is a species of perennial grass native to southern Europe, North Africa, and the Levant in the Mediterranean Basin,…

stipagrostis.name: Desert bunch grasses
stipagrostis.desc: Grasses of sandy desert that green up after rain. Related Stipagrostis grasses are the main food of Arabian oryx in Oman.
stipagrostis.about: Stipagrostis is a genus of African, Asian, and Russian plants in the grass family.

stipagrostis and others.name: Desert grasses
stipagrostis and others.desc: Tough, drought-adapted grasses grow in sparse tufts and sprout quickly after rain. Their leaves and seeds feed many desert animals.
stipagrostis and others.about: Stipagrostis is a genus of African, Asian, and Russian plants in the grass family.

stipagrostis species.name: Dune grasses
stipagrostis species.desc: Tussock grasses that grow on Namib dunes and gravel plains and feed grazers, seed eaters and termites.
stipagrostis species.about: Stipagrostis is a genus of African, Asian, and Russian plants in the grass family.

stolephorus.name: Anchovies
stolephorus.desc: Small schooling fish that feed on zooplankton in the open bay and are food for larger fish, seabirds and porpoises.
stolephorus.about: Stolephorus is a genus of ray-finned fish in the family Engraulidae.

stony mountain soil.name: Stony mountain soil
stony mountain soil.desc: Thin, rocky soils on dry slopes hold the steppe, juniper and oak communities, which cover the reserve in altitude bands.

stony, salty soils.name: Stony, salty soils
stony, salty soils.desc: The plateau is limestone with chert gravel, and run-off ends in salt flats. Poor soil and little water limit plant cover.

strangalepta abbreviata.name: Strangalepta Flower Longhorn
strangalepta abbreviata.desc: Strangalepta Flower Longhorn (Strangalepta abbreviata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

streams & gallery forest.name: Streams & gallery forest
streams & gallery forest.desc: Strips of forest along watercourses hold moisture through the dry season and shelter plants and animals that need damp ground.

streams and swamps.name: Streams and swamps
streams and swamps.desc: Rivers and wet hollows give shy water-loving animals such as the pygmy hippo daytime cover and cool, moist ground.

strepera graculina.name: Pied currawong
strepera graculina.desc: An omnivorous bird eating insects, fruit and the eggs and young of other birds. The island has its own vulnerable subspecies.
strepera graculina.about: The pied currawong is a black passerine bird native to eastern Australia and Lord Howe Island.

streptanthus maculatus.name: Clasping jewelflower
streptanthus maculatus.desc: Clasping jewelflower (Streptanthus maculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 42 times near the park in GBIF.

streptopelia decaocto.name: Eurasian Collared Dove
streptopelia decaocto.desc: Eurasian Collared-Dove (Streptopelia decaocto): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 58 times near the park in GBIF.
streptopelia decaocto.about: The Eurasian collared dove, often called the collared dove, is a dove species from the genus Streptopelia.

strix aluco.name: Tawny owl
strix aluco.desc: A woodland owl hunting small mammals such as voles at night.
strix aluco.about: The tawny owl, also called the brown owl, is a stocky, medium-sized owl in the family Strigidae.

strix nebulosa.name: Great gray owl
strix nebulosa.desc: Hunts small rodents by sound, even under snow, and sometimes takes squirrels or hares. Nests in old raptor nests and broken-topped trees.
strix nebulosa.about: The great grey owl (also great gray owl in American English) is a true owl, and is the world's largest species of owl by length.

strix occidentalis caurina.name: Northern spotted owl
strix occidentalis caurina.desc: Lives in old-growth forest and eats mostly small mammals, especially flying squirrels; competes with invading barred owls.
strix occidentalis caurina.about: The northern spotted owl is one of three spotted owl subspecies.

strix varia.name: Barred owl
strix varia.desc: The park highlights it as a signature species. It hunts small mammals, frogs and some snakes in old-growth bottomland forest.
strix varia.about: The barred owl, also known as the northern barred owl, striped owl, or more informally, hoot owl or eight hooter, is a North American large species of owl.

strombosia scheffleri.name: Strombosia trees
strombosia scheffleri.desc: Understory and mid-canopy rainforest trees whose fruit is eaten by chimpanzees and guenons, according to GloBI records.
strombosia scheffleri.about: Strombosia is a plant genus of about 10 species in the family Olacaceae. It has also been classified in the family Strombosiaceae.

strongylocentrotus purpuratus.name: Purple sea urchin
strongylocentrotus purpuratus.desc: Grazes kelp, often eating drifting pieces. Without enough predators it can multiply and strip an area bare, leaving an urchin barren.
strongylocentrotus purpuratus.about: Strongylocentrotus purpuratus is a species of sea urchin in the family Strongylocentrotidae, which is commonly known as the purple sea urchin or Pacific purple sea urchin.

strongylopus grayii.name: Clicking stream frog
strongylopus grayii.desc: A small frog of streams and wet grass that feeds on insects and is eaten by shrikes and snakes.
strongylopus grayii.about: Gray's stream frog is a fairly small species of frog in the family Pyxicephalidae.

strophostyles helvola.name: BEACH PEA
strophostyles helvola.desc: BEACH PEA (Strophostyles helvola): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
strophostyles helvola.about: Strophostyles helvola, commonly called amberique-bean, annual sand bean, or trailing fuzzybean is a species of flowering plant in the legume family.

struthio camelus.name: Common ostrich
struthio camelus.desc: A huge flightless bird that eats plants, seeds and some insects on open desert plains.
struthio camelus.about: The common ostrich, or simply ostrich, is a species of flightless bird native to certain areas of Africa (and historically, Arabia) and is the largest living species of bird.

struthiopteris spicant.name: Hard-fern
struthiopteris spicant.desc: Hard-fern (Struthiopteris spicant): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 270 times near the park in GBIF.

strymon melinus.name: Cotton Square Borer
strymon melinus.desc: Cotton Square Borer (Strymon melinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
strymon melinus.about: The gray hairstreak is also called the bean lycaenid or cotton square borer.

strymon sylvinus.name: Strymon sylvinus
strymon sylvinus.desc: Strymon sylvinus (Strymon sylvinus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

stuckenia pectinata.name: Fennel Pondweed
stuckenia pectinata.desc: Fennel Pondweed (Stuckenia pectinata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 25 times near the park in GBIF.
stuckenia pectinata.about: Stuckenia pectinata, commonly called sago pondweed or fennel pondweed, and sometimes called ribbon weed, is a cosmopolitan water plant species that grows in fresh and brackish water on all continents…

stuckenia vaginata.name: Sheathed pondweed
stuckenia vaginata.desc: Sheathed pondweed (Stuckenia vaginata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

sturnella magna.name: Eastern Meadowlark
sturnella magna.desc: Eastern Meadowlark (Sturnella magna): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 44 times near the park in GBIF.
sturnella magna.about: The eastern meadowlark is a medium-sized icterid bird, very similar in appearance to its sister species, the western meadowlark.

sturnella neglecta.name: Western Meadowlark
sturnella neglecta.desc: Western Meadowlark (Sturnella neglecta): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 179 times near the park in GBIF.
sturnella neglecta.about: The western meadowlark is a medium-sized icterid bird, about 20 cm (7.9 in) in length.

sturnus vulgaris.name: European Starling
sturnus vulgaris.desc: European Starling (Sturnus vulgaris): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 143 times near the park in GBIF.
sturnus vulgaris.about: The common starling, also known simply as the starling in Great Britain and Ireland, and as the European starling in North America, is a medium-sized passerine bird in the starling family, Sturnidae.

stylophorum diphyllum.name: Celandine-poppy
stylophorum diphyllum.desc: Celandine-poppy (Stylophorum diphyllum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.
stylophorum diphyllum.about: Stylophorum diphyllum, commonly called the celandine poppy or wood poppy, is an herbaceous plant in the poppy family (Papaveraceae).

styrax redivivus.name: Snowdrop bush
styrax redivivus.desc: Snowdrop bush (Styrax redivivus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 76 times near the park in GBIF.
styrax redivivus.about: Styrax redivivus, with common names that include snowdrop bush, California styrax, bitternut, drug snowbell, and chaparral snowbell, is a species of flowering plant in the family Styracaceae.

suaeda nigra.name: Bush seepweed
suaeda nigra.desc: Bush seepweed (Suaeda nigra): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
suaeda nigra.about: Suaeda nigra, often still known by the former name Suaeda moquinii, is a species of flowering plant in the amaranth family, known by the vernacular names bush seepweed or Mojave sea-blite.

sula dactylatra.name: Masked booby
sula dactylatra.desc: A seabird that plunge-dives for flying fish and squid. Its eggs are open to rats and other egg predators.
sula dactylatra.about: The masked booby, also called the masked gannet or the blue-faced booby, is a large seabird of the booby and gannet family, Sulidae.

sula leucogaster.name: Brown booby
sula leucogaster.desc: Plunge-diving seabird that feeds on flying fish and other fish near the surface.
sula leucogaster.about: The brown booby is a large seabird in the booby and gannet family Sulidae, of which it is one of the most common and widespread species.

sula sula.name: Red-footed booby
sula sula.desc: Nests in the trees and shrubs and hunts flying fish and squid at sea.
sula sula.about: The red-footed booby is a large seabird of the booby family, Sulidae. Adults always have red feet, but the colour of the plumage varies.

sulu sea currents.name: Sulu Sea currents
sulu sea currents.desc: Ocean currents move water, larvae and plankton across the isolated atolls and carry them to the reef edges.

summer light.name: Summer light
summer light.desc: The park lies north of the Arctic Circle, so growth is crammed into a short summer of very long days.

summer monsoon rain.name: Summer monsoon rain
summer monsoon rain.desc: About 42 percent of the park's scarce rain falls from July to September, triggering the main burst of grass and wildflower growth.

summer rain.name: Summer rain
summer rain.desc: Rain wets the sand sheet and shrublands and helps seeds sprout.

summer rains.name: Summer rains
summer rains.desc: Rains fill pans and swell the rivers, and turn the grasslands green.

summer sun.name: Summer sun
summer sun.desc: Short alpine summers drive the growth of meadows and scrub above the tree line.

summer sun and long days.name: Summer sun and long days
summer sun and long days.desc: North of the Arctic Circle the summer sun barely sets, giving plants a short, intense growing season.

summer sunlight.name: Summer sunlight
summer sunlight.desc: Long summer days power a short, intense growing season on the tundra.

sun.name: Sun
sun.desc: Sunlight powers the marsh plants and grasses.

sun and altitude.name: Sun and altitude
sun and altitude.desc: Short alpine summers and cold winters set the growing season, from about 450 m in the canyons to over 2,500 m on the peaks.

suncus etruscus.name: Etruscan shrew
suncus etruscus.desc: One of the smallest mammals on Earth and one of Socotra's few native mammals. It hunts small invertebrates.
suncus etruscus.about: The Etruscan shrew, also known as the Etruscan pygmy shrew, white-toothed pygmy shrew and Savi's pygmy shrew, is the smallest known extant mammal by mass, weighing only about 1.8 g (0.063 oz) on…

sundasciurus jentinki.name: Jentink's squirrel
sundasciurus jentinki.desc: A small squirrel of montane Borneo forest, recorded often near the park.
sundasciurus jentinki.about: Jentink's squirrel is a species of rodent in the family Sciuridae. It is named in honor of the Dutch zoologist Fredericus Anna Jentink.

sunlight.name: Sunlight
sunlight.desc: Plants turn sunlight into food, which starts the whole web.

sunlight and altitude.name: Sunlight and altitude
sunlight and altitude.desc: Strong high-altitude light drives growth in meadows and forests between the gorges and the snowline.

sunlight and dry-season heat.name: Sunlight and dry-season heat
sunlight and dry-season heat.desc: Strong sun and heat, up to about 40 C in the May to October dry season, drive the savanna growth and its seasonal browning.

sunlight and heat.name: Sunlight and heat
sunlight and heat.desc: Intense light powers the sparse plant life, but extreme summer heat and dryness limit where plants and animals can live.

sus barbatus.name: Bornean bearded pig
sus barbatus.desc: A forest pig that roots through the leaf litter for fallen fruit, seeds and invertebrates.

sus scrofa.name: Wild boar
sus scrofa.desc: Feral pig (Sus scrofa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sus scrofa.about: The wild boar, also known as the wild swine, common wild pig, Eurasian wild pig, or simply wild pig, is a suid native to much of Eurasia and North Africa and has been introduced to the Americas and…

swamps & rivers.name: Swamps & rivers
swamps & rivers.desc: Swamp and seasonally flooded forest make up about a quarter of the park, with the Sinoe River on its west side. Home to the pygmy hippo.

swampy lowlands.name: Swampy lowlands
swampy lowlands.desc: Low wet ground between the limestone ridges where water collects and forest meets wetland.

swietenia macrophylla.name: Big-leaf mahogany
swietenia macrophylla.desc: Planted here in the mid 1900s, it now forms much of the tall canopy beside the older native trees.
swietenia macrophylla.about: Swietenia macrophylla, commonly known as mahogany, Honduran mahogany, Honduras mahogany, or big-leaf mahogany is a species of plant in the Meliaceae family.

syagrus romanzoffiana.name: Queen palm
syagrus romanzoffiana.desc: Its sticky orange-pulped fruit is eaten by toucans, coatis, tapirs, agoutis and many birds, which spread the seeds.
syagrus romanzoffiana.about: Syagrus romanzoffiana, the queen palm, cocos palm or Jerivá, is a palm native to South America, introduced throughout the world as a popular ornamental garden tree. S.

sylvia curruca.name: Lesser whitethroat
sylvia curruca.desc: A very commonly recorded warbler near the park. It hunts insects in shrubs and is eaten by red foxes in GloBI records.
sylvia curruca.about: The lesser whitethroat is a common and widespread Old World warbler which breeds in temperate Europe, except the southwest, and in the western and central Palearctic.

sylvicapra grimmia.name: Common duiker
sylvicapra grimmia.desc: Small antelope browsing leaves and fruit, seen above the timberline.
sylvicapra grimmia.about: The common duiker, also known as the gray duiker or bush duiker, is a small antelope and the only member of the genus Sylvicapra.

sylvilagus aquaticus.name: SWAMP RABBIT
sylvilagus aquaticus.desc: Swamp rabbit (Sylvilagus aquaticus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
sylvilagus aquaticus.about: The swamp rabbit, also known as the cane cutter, swamper, or cane jake, is a species of cottontail rabbit found in the swamps and wetlands of the southern United States.

sylvilagus audubonii.name: Desert cottontail
sylvilagus audubonii.desc: Desert cottontail (Sylvilagus audubonii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sylvilagus audubonii.about: The desert cottontail, also known as Audubon's cottontail, is a New World cottontail rabbit, and a member of the family Leporidae.

sylvilagus bachmani.name: Brush rabbit
sylvilagus bachmani.desc: Eats plants and, per Wikipedia, preys on young redwood seedlings. Prey for foxes and cougars.
sylvilagus bachmani.about: The brush rabbit, or western brush rabbit, or Californian brush rabbit, is a species of cottontail rabbit found in western coastal regions of North America, from the Columbia River in Oregon to the…

sylvilagus floridanus.name: Eastern cottontail
sylvilagus floridanus.desc: Eastern cottontail (Sylvilagus floridanus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sylvilagus floridanus.about: The eastern cottontail is a species of rabbit in the family Leporidae.

sylvilagus nuttallii.name: Mountain cottontail
sylvilagus nuttallii.desc: Mountain cottontail (Sylvilagus nuttallii): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
sylvilagus nuttallii.about: The mountain cottontail or Nuttall's cottontail is a species of rabbit found in western Canada and the United States.

sylvilagus palustris.name: Marsh rabbit
sylvilagus palustris.desc: A grass-eating rabbit of wet prairies and hammock edges. Pythons have sharply cut its numbers where they are established.
sylvilagus palustris.about: The marsh rabbit is a small cottontail rabbit found in marshes and swamps of coastal regions of the Eastern and Southern United States, from Virginia to the lower Florida Keys.

sylvisorex vulcanorum.name: Volcano forest shrew
sylvisorex vulcanorum.desc: A small insect-eating mammal of Albertine Rift forest floors, among the more recorded mammals near the park.
sylvisorex vulcanorum.about: The forest shrews are the members of the genus Sylvisorex. They are mammals in the family Soricidae and are found only in Africa.

symbiodiniaceae.name: Zooxanthellae
symbiodiniaceae.desc: Microscopic algae living inside coral that pass sugars to their host.
symbiodiniaceae.about: Zooxanthellae is a colloquial term for photosynthetic single-celled organisms capable of symbiosis with diverse marine invertebrates such as corals, jellyfish, demosponges, and nudibranchs.

symphoricarpos albus.name: Common Snowberry
symphoricarpos albus.desc: Common Snowberry (Symphoricarpos albus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

symphoricarpos occidentalis.name: Wolfberry
symphoricarpos occidentalis.desc: Wolfberry (Symphoricarpos occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

symphoricarpos orbiculatus.name: Buck Brush
symphoricarpos orbiculatus.desc: Buck Brush (Symphoricarpos orbiculatus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
symphoricarpos orbiculatus.about: Symphoricarpos orbiculatus, commonly called coralberry, buckbrush or Indian currant is a woody species of flowering plant in the honeysuckle family.

symphyotrichum campestre.name: Western meadow aster
symphyotrichum campestre.desc: Western meadow aster (Symphyotrichum campestre): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
symphyotrichum campestre.about: Symphyotrichum campestre is a species of flowering plant of the family Asteraceae commonly known as western meadow aster.

symphyotrichum drummondii.name: Ozark heart-leaf aster
symphyotrichum drummondii.desc: Ozark heart-leaf aster (Symphyotrichum drummondii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum ericoides.name: Heath Aster
symphyotrichum ericoides.desc: Heath Aster (Symphyotrichum ericoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum falcatum.name: Creeping white prairie aster
symphyotrichum falcatum.desc: Creeping white prairie aster (Symphyotrichum falcatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum lateriflorum.name: Calico Aster
symphyotrichum lateriflorum.desc: Calico Aster (Symphyotrichum lateriflorum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
symphyotrichum lateriflorum.about: Symphyotrichum lateriflorum is a species of flowering plant in the aster family (Asteraceae).

symphyotrichum novae-angliae.name: Hairy Michaelmas-daisy
symphyotrichum novae-angliae.desc: Hairy Michaelmas-daisy (Symphyotrichum novae-angliae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

symphyotrichum racemosum.name: Small-head aster
symphyotrichum racemosum.desc: Small-head aster (Symphyotrichum racemosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
symphyotrichum racemosum.about: Symphyotrichum racemosum is a species of flowering plant native to parts of the United States and introduced in Canada. It is known as smooth white oldfield aster and small white aster.

symplocarpus foetidus.name: Polecatweed
symplocarpus foetidus.desc: Polecatweed (Symplocarpus foetidus): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 75 times near the park in GBIF.
symplocarpus foetidus.about: Symplocarpus foetidus, commonly known as skunk cabbage or eastern skunk cabbage, is a low-growing plant that grows in wetlands and moist hill slopes of eastern North America.

synandra hispidula.name: Synandra
synandra hispidula.desc: Synandra (Synandra hispidula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

synanthedon exitiosa.name: Peachtree Borer
synanthedon exitiosa.desc: Peachtree Borer (Synanthedon exitiosa): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
synanthedon exitiosa.about: Synanthedon exitiosa, the peachtree borer, is a species of moth in the family Sesiidae that is native to North America. The adult female of the species has a wingspan of about 3.5 centimeters.

syncerus caffer.name: African buffalo
syncerus caffer.desc: Herds graze tall, coarse grass and are hard for most predators to take down.
syncerus caffer.about: The African buffalo is a large bovine native to sub-Saharan Africa. First described in 1779 by Swedish naturalist Anders Sparrman, it is the only extant species of the genus Syncerus.

syncerus caffer nanus.name: Forest buffalo
syncerus caffer nanus.desc: A smaller forest form of the African buffalo that feeds on herbs and grasses in forest clearings and along the swamps.
syncerus caffer nanus.about: The African buffalo is a large bovine native to sub-Saharan Africa. First described in 1779 by Swedish naturalist Anders Sparrman, it is the only extant species of the genus Syncerus.

synthliboramphus antiquus.name: Ancient murrelet
synthliboramphus antiquus.desc: A burrow-nesting seabird; about half the world population breeds on Haida Gwaii. Eats small fish and crustaceans.
synthliboramphus antiquus.about: The ancient murrelet is a bird in the auk family. The English term "murrelet" is a diminutive of "murre", a word of uncertain origins, but which may imitate the call of the common guillemot.

syzygium.name: Satinash and lilly pilly
syzygium.desc: Rainforest trees whose fruit and flowers feed cassowaries and spectacled flying foxes.
syzygium.about: Syzygium () is a genus of flowering plants that belongs to the myrtle family, Myrtaceae.

syzygium cumini.name: Jamun
syzygium cumini.desc: A fruiting forest tree. GloBI records elephants, macaques, squirrels and many birds eating its fruit.
syzygium cumini.about: Syzygium cumini, also known as Java plum, Malabar plum, jambolan, black plum, jamun, jambul, is an evergreen tropical tree in the flowering plant family Myrtaceae, and favored for its fruit, timber,…

tachyoryctes macrocephalus.name: Giant root-rat
tachyoryctes macrocephalus.desc: Burrowing rodent found only in the Bale highlands. It forages on grasses and herbs from burrow mouths and is the main prey of the Ethiopian wolf.
tachyoryctes macrocephalus.about: The giant root-rat, also known as the Ethiopian African mole rat, is a species of rodent in the genus Tachyoryctes.

tadarida brasiliensis.name: Mexican free-tailed bat
tadarida brasiliensis.desc: The cave's famous summer bat colony flies out at dusk to feed on moths and other flying insects. Their guano carries insect energy into the cave.
tadarida brasiliensis.about: The Mexican free-tailed bat or Brazilian free-tailed bat is a medium-sized bat native to North, Central, and South America and the Caribbean, so named because its tail can be almost half its total…

tadorna ferruginea.name: Ruddy shelduck
tadorna ferruginea.desc: Omnivorous duck of lakes and rivers that eats grasses, shoots, water plants and invertebrates. Breeds in Central Asia from March and April.
tadorna ferruginea.about: The ruddy shelduck is a bird species in the family Anatidae. It is a distinctive waterfowl, 58 to 70 cm (23 to 28 in) in length with a wingspan of 110 to 135 cm (43 to 53 in).

taeniatherum caput-medusae.name: Steppe grasses
taeniatherum caput-medusae.desc: Grasses and sedges cover about 45% of the Nuratau site (grassland), growing fast in the damp spring. They are the main forage on the lower slopes and desert fringe.
taeniatherum caput-medusae.about: Taeniatherum is a genus of Eurasian and North African plants in the grass family.

tamarindus indica.name: Tamarind
tamarindus indica.desc: A leafy tree whose pods are a key dry-season food for ring-tailed lemurs.
tamarindus indica.about: Tamarind is a leguminous tree bearing edible fruit that is indigenous to tropical Africa and naturalized in Asia. The genus Tamarindus is monotypic, meaning that it contains only this species.

tamarix ramosissima.name: Salt cedar
tamarix ramosissima.desc: Salt cedar (Tamarix ramosissima): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
tamarix ramosissima.about: Tamarix ramosissima, commonly known as saltcedar salt cedar, or tamarisk, is a deciduous arching shrub with reddish stems, feathery, pale green foliage, and characteristic small pink flowers.

tamias dorsalis.name: Cliff chipmunk
tamias dorsalis.desc: Cliff chipmunk (Tamias dorsalis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.
tamias dorsalis.about: The cliff chipmunk is a small, bushy-tailed squirrel that typically lives along cliff walls or boulder fields bordering Pinyon-juniper woodlands in the Western United States and Mexico (commonly…

tamias merriami.name: Merriam's Chipmunk
tamias merriami.desc: Merriam's Chipmunk (Tamias merriami): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 107 times near the park in GBIF.

tamias minimus.name: Least chipmunk
tamias minimus.desc: Least chipmunk (Tamias minimus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 354 times near the park in GBIF.
