tamias minimus.about: The least chipmunk is the smallest species of chipmunk and the most widespread in North America.

tamias sibiricus.name: Siberian chipmunk
tamias sibiricus.desc: A small seed-eating ground rodent of the forest, and a prey item for foxes, sables and bears in GloBI records.
tamias sibiricus.about: The Siberian chipmunk, also called common chipmunk, is a species of chipmunk native to northern Asia from central Russia to China, Korea, and Hokkaidō in northern Japan.

tamias striatus.name: Eastern chipmunk
tamias striatus.desc: Eastern chipmunk (Tamias striatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
tamias striatus.about: The eastern chipmunk is a chipmunk species found in eastern North America. It is the only living member of the genus Tamias.

tamias umbrinus.name: Uinta chipmunk
tamias umbrinus.desc: The most recorded mammal near the park. A small forest rodent that feeds mainly on seeds and is prey for hawks.
tamias umbrinus.about: The Uinta chipmunk or hidden forest chipmunk is a species of chipmunk in the family Sciuridae. It is endemic to the United States.

tamiasciurus douglasii.name: Douglas squirrel
tamiasciurus douglasii.desc: Stores conifer cones in middens; bears raid these for whitebark pine seeds.
tamiasciurus douglasii.about: The Douglas squirrel is a pine squirrel found in western North America, from the Pacific Northwest (including the northwestern coastal states of the United States as well as the southwestern coast of…

tamiasciurus hudsonicus.name: American red squirrel
tamiasciurus hudsonicus.desc: American red squirrel (Tamiasciurus hudsonicus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.
tamiasciurus hudsonicus.about: The American red squirrel is one of three species of tree squirrels currently classified in the genus Tamiasciurus, known as the pine squirrels.

tanacetum parthenium.name: Feverfew
tanacetum parthenium.desc: Feverfew (Tanacetum parthenium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

tanacetum vulgare.name: Tansy
tanacetum vulgare.desc: Tansy (Tanacetum vulgare): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.
tanacetum vulgare.about: Tansy is a perennial, herbaceous flowering plant in the genus Tanacetum in the family Asteraceae, native to temperate Europe and Asia.

tapinoma sessile.name: Odorous House Ant
tapinoma sessile.desc: Odorous House Ant (Tapinoma sessile): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
tapinoma sessile.about: Tapinoma sessile is a species of small ant that goes by the common names odorous house ant, sugar ant, stink ant, and coconut ant.

tapirella bairdii.name: Baird's tapir
tapirella bairdii.desc: Browses leaves and twigs of understory plants and eats fruit in season. Some hard seeds, such as sapodilla, pass through it intact.
tapirella bairdii.about: The Baird's tapir, also known as the Central American tapir, is a species of tapir native to Mexico, Central America, and northwestern South America.

tapirus bairdii.name: Baird's tapir
tapirus bairdii.desc: A large browser of leaves and twigs in wet forest and swamp. Adults have few natural predators besides jaguars and big crocodiles.
tapirus bairdii.about: The Baird's tapir, also known as the Central American tapir, is a species of tapir native to Mexico, Central America, and northwestern South America.

tapirus terrestris.name: Lowland tapir
tapirus terrestris.desc: Eats fruit and leaves, and spreads seeds across the forest in its dung.
tapirus terrestris.about: The South American tapir, also commonly called the Brazilian tapir, the Amazonian tapir, the maned tapir, the lowland tapir, anta (Brazilian Portuguese), and sachavaca, is one of the four recognized…

taraxacum officinale.name: Dandelion
taraxacum officinale.desc: Dandelion (Taraxacum officinale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
taraxacum officinale.about: Taraxacum officinale, the dandelion or common dandelion, is a herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the daisy family, Asteraceae.

taraxia tanacetifolia.name: Tansyleaf evening primrose
taraxia tanacetifolia.desc: Tansyleaf evening primrose (Taraxia tanacetifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.
taraxia tanacetifolia.about: Taraxia tanacetifolia is a species of evening primrose known by the common name tansyleaf evening primrose.

tarenna.name: Tarenna
tarenna.desc: A shrubby understorey plant of Afromontane forest whose small fruits are eaten by birds.
tarenna.about: Tarenna is a genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. There are about 193 species distributed across the old world tropics of Africa, Asia, Australia, and the Pacific Islands.

tauraco schuettii.name: Black-billed turaco
tauraco schuettii.desc: A fruit-eating forest bird; GloBI records show it eating Ilex mitis and Maesa lanceolata fruits.
tauraco schuettii.about: The black-billed turaco is a medium-sized turaco, an endemic family to sub-Saharan Africa.

taurotragus oryx.name: Common eland
taurotragus oryx.desc: Africa's largest antelope, which feeds on grasses and shrubs. Rarely recorded near the reserve.
taurotragus oryx.about: The common eland, also known as the southern eland or eland antelope, is a large savannah and plains antelope found in East and Southern Africa.

taxidea taxus.name: American badger
taxidea taxus.desc: American badger (Taxidea taxus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
taxidea taxus.about: The American badger is a North American badger similar in appearance to the European badger, although not closely related.

taxodium distichum.name: Bald cypress
taxodium distichum.desc: Bald cypress (Taxodium distichum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
taxodium distichum.about: Taxodium distichum, the bald cypress, bald-cypress, baldcypress, or swamp cypress; French: cyprès chauve; cipre in Louisiana) is a deciduous conifer in the cypress family, Cupressaceae.

taxus canadensis.name: Canada Yew
taxus canadensis.desc: Canada Yew (Taxus canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.

tayassu pecari.name: White-lipped peccary
tayassu pecari.desc: A herd-living forest pig that eats fruits, seeds and roots and is prey for jaguars and pumas.
tayassu pecari.about: The white-lipped peccary is a species of peccary found in Central and South America and the only extant member of the genus Tayassu. Multiple subspecies have been identified.

tegeticula synthetica.name: Yucca moth
tegeticula synthetica.desc: Pollinates Joshua trees while laying eggs in the flowers; its larvae eat some of the seeds.

telmatobius culeus.name: Titicaca water frog
telmatobius culeus.desc: A fully aquatic frog that eats mainly amphipods and snails, and adults also take Orestias fish. Overcollection, pollution and trout have cut its numbers.
telmatobius culeus.about: Telmatobius culeus, commonly known as the Titicaca water frog or Lake Titicaca frog, is a medium-large to very large and endangered species of frog in the family Telmatobiidae.

tenaxia.name: Highland grasses
tenaxia.desc: Montane and afroalpine grasslands cover much of the plateau and are the main food of geladas.
tenaxia.about: Poaceae ( poh-AY-see-e(y)e), also called Gramineae ( grə-MIN-ee-e(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.

tenebrionidae.name: Darkling beetles
tenebrionidae.desc: Hardy ground beetles of sandy deserts that feed on plant matter and debris, and feed many lizards and birds.
tenebrionidae.about: Darkling beetle is the common name for members of the beetle family Tenebrionidae, comprising over 20,000 species in a cosmopolitan distribution.

tenrecidae.name: Tenrecs
tenrecidae.desc: Small insect-eating mammals unique to Madagascar, hunted by the fossa.
tenrecidae.about: A tenrec () is a mammal belonging to any species within the afrotherian family Tenrecidae, which is endemic to Madagascar.

tenualosa ilisha.name: Hilsa
tenualosa ilisha.desc: A plankton-feeding fish that lives in estuaries and swims up rivers to spawn. It is Bangladesh's national fish.
tenualosa ilisha.about: The ilish (Bengali: ইলিশ, romanized: iliś), also known as the ilishi, hilsa, pulasa, hilsa herring or hilsa shad, is a species of fish related to the herring, in the family Clupeidae.

tephrosia virginiana.name: Goat's rue
tephrosia virginiana.desc: Goat's rue (Tephrosia virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
tephrosia virginiana.about: Tephrosia virginiana, also known as goat-rue, goat's rue, catgut, rabbit pea, Virginia tephrosia, hoary pea, and devil's shoestring is a perennial dicot in family Fabaceae.

terathopius ecaudatus.name: Bateleur
terathopius ecaudatus.desc: A short-tailed eagle that eats both live prey, such as snakes and birds, and a good deal of carrion.
terathopius ecaudatus.about: The bateleur, also known as the bateleur eagle, is a medium-sized eagle in the family Accipitridae.

teratoscincus scincus.name: Common wonder gecko
teratoscincus scincus.desc: A nocturnal gecko of sand dunes that shelters in a deep burrow by day and eats insects and other lizards.
teratoscincus scincus.about: Teratoscincus scincus, commonly referred to as the common wonder gecko or the frog-eyed gecko, is a species of lizard in the family Sphaerodactylidae.

termites, scarab beetles, fungi, bacteri.name: Decomposers
termites, scarab beetles, fungi, bacteri.desc: Beetles, termites and microbes break down dung, dead plants and carcasses, returning nutrients to the sand.

termitidae.name: Termites
termitidae.desc: Feed on dead wood and plant litter, and are a main food of giant anteaters and giant armadillos.
termitidae.about: Termites are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

termitoidae.name: Termites
termitoidae.desc: Break down dead wood and leaf litter and recycle nutrients. Chimpanzees fish them out of mounds with sticks.
termitoidae.about: Termites are a group of eusocial insects which consume a variety of decaying plant material, generally in the form of wood, leaf litter, and soil humus.

terpsiphone viridis.name: African paradise flycatcher
terpsiphone viridis.desc: Insect-catching forest bird, also recorded taking Lantana fruit.
terpsiphone viridis.about: The African paradise flycatcher is a medium-sized passerine bird. The two central tail feathers of the male are extended into streamers that commonly are more than twice as long as the body.

tetrao urogallus.name: Western capercaillie
tetrao urogallus.desc: Huge grouse of the old pinewoods, feeding on pine shoots and bilberry; its eggs, chicks and adults are taken by predators.
tetrao urogallus.about: The western capercaillie, also known as the Eurasian capercaillie, wood grouse, heather cock, cock-of-the-woods, or simply capercaillie , is a heavy member of the grouse tribe and the largest of all…

tetraogallus himalayensis.name: Himalayan snowcock
tetraogallus himalayensis.desc: A large alpine game bird that feeds on plants on open high slopes, and lives in the park per Wikipedia.
tetraogallus himalayensis.about: The Himalayan snowcock is a snowcock in the pheasant family Phasianidae found across the Himalayan ranges and parts of the adjoining Pamir range of Asia.

tetraopes femoratus.name: Milkweed Borer
tetraopes femoratus.desc: Milkweed Borer (Tetraopes femoratus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

tetraopes tetrophthalmus.name: Red Milkweed Beetle
tetraopes tetrophthalmus.desc: Red Milkweed Beetle (Tetraopes tetrophthalmus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

tettigonia caudata.name: Bush-cricket
tettigonia caudata.desc: A large bush-cricket of dry shrubby ground. It chews leaves and some other insects and feeds lizards and bats.
tettigonia caudata.about: Tettigonia caudata is a species of bush-crickets belonging to the family Tettigoniidae subfamily Tettigoniinae. It is found over most of Europe mainly in the East.

teucrium canadense.name: American Germander
teucrium canadense.desc: American Germander (Teucrium canadense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
teucrium canadense.about: Teucrium canadense, commonly known as Canada germander, American germander, or wood sage, is a perennial herb in the family Lamiaceae.

thalassarche melanophris.name: Black-browed albatross
thalassarche melanophris.desc: The Falklands hold the largest breeding population in the world. It eats fish, squid, crustaceans, carrion and fishery discards.
thalassarche melanophris.about: The black-browed albatross, also known as the black-browed mollymawk, is a large seabird of the albatross family Diomedeidae; it is the most widespread and common member of its family.

thalasseus bengalensis.name: Lesser crested tern
thalasseus bengalensis.desc: Plunge-dives for fish in salt water and breeds in island colonies; the archipelago is an Important Bird Area.
thalasseus bengalensis.about: The lesser crested tern is a tern in the family Laridae.

thalasseus bergii.name: Great crested tern
thalasseus bergii.desc: A fish-eating tern that plunge-dives for small schooling fish along the shore.
thalasseus bergii.about: The greater crested tern, also called crested tern, swift tern, or great crested tern, is a tern in the family Laridae that nests in dense colonies on coastlines and islands in the tropical and…

thalassia testudinum.name: Turtle grass
thalassia testudinum.desc: The main seagrass of the bay. Its meadows shelter young fish and invertebrates, and its dead leaves supply much of the detritus.
thalassia testudinum.about: Thalassia testudinum, commonly known as turtlegrass, is a species of marine seagrass in the family Hydrocharitaceae.

thalassiosira.name: Phytoplankton
thalassiosira.desc: Microscopic drifting algae in the surrounding sea, the base of the open-water food chain.
thalassiosira.about: Phytoplankton () are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.

thalassodendron.name: Seagrass
thalassodendron.desc: Meadows in the shallow lagoon that green turtles graze.
thalassodendron.about: Seagrasses are the only embryophytes (commonly referred to as "land plants") which grow in marine environments.

thalassodendron ciliatum.name: Seagrass
thalassodendron ciliatum.desc: A seagrass of shallow East African and Indian Ocean waters, forming meadows that feed grazers and shelter small fish.
thalassodendron ciliatum.about: Thalassodendron ciliatum, the sickle-leaved cymodocea, is a species of plant in the Thalassodendron genus of seagrasses in the family Cymodoceaceae.

thalictrum thalictroides.name: Rue-anemone
thalictrum thalictroides.desc: Rue-anemone (Thalictrum thalictroides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
thalictrum thalictroides.about: Thalictrum thalictroides, the rue-anemone or windflower, is a herbaceous perennial plant native to woodland in eastern North America.

thamnophis sirtalis.name: Common garter snake
thamnophis sirtalis.desc: A widespread snake of wet ground that eats small mammals and amphibians and is prey for herons and foxes.
thamnophis sirtalis.about: The common garter snake is a species of snake in the subfamily Natricinae of the family Colubridae. The species is indigenous to North America and found widely across the continent.

thamnosma montana.name: Mohave desertrue
thamnosma montana.desc: Mohave desertrue (Thamnosma montana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 129 times near the park in GBIF.
thamnosma montana.about: Thamnosma montana, the turpentine broom, or Mojave desert-rue, is a shrub in the citrus family Rutaceae. It is native to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northern Mexico.

thelesperma filifolium.name: Stiff greenthread
thelesperma filifolium.desc: Stiff greenthread (Thelesperma filifolium): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 83 times near the park in GBIF.
thelesperma filifolium.about: Thelesperma filifolium, commonly known as stiff greenthread, or plains greenthread, is a species of flowering plant in the aster family, Asteraceae. It is often found growing in shallow soils.

thelypodium brachycarpum.name: Short-podded thelypody
thelypodium brachycarpum.desc: Short-podded thelypody (Thelypodium brachycarpum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
thelypodium brachycarpum.about: Thelypodium brachycarpum is a species of flowering plant in the mustard family known by the common names shortpod thelypody and short-podded thelypodium.

thelypteris palustris.name: Marsh Fern
thelypteris palustris.desc: Marsh Fern (Thelypteris palustris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.
thelypteris palustris.about: Thelypteris palustris, the marsh fern, or eastern marsh fern, is a species of fern native to eastern North America and across Eurasia.

themeda triandra.name: Red grass
themeda triandra.desc: The tall grass of the plains. Fire and grazing keep it growing back each year.
themeda triandra.about: Themeda triandra is a species of C4 perennial tussock-forming grass widespread in Africa, Australia, Asia and the Pacific.

themeda, cymbopogon, arundinella.name: Shola grasses
themeda, cymbopogon, arundinella.desc: Frost- and fire-resistant tussock grasses cover the high montane grasslands between the shola forest patches.
themeda, cymbopogon, arundinella.about: Themeda is a genus of plants in the grass family native to Asia, Africa, Australia, and Papuasia. There are about 18 to 26 species, many of which are native to Southeast Asia.

theobroma subincanum.name: Wild cacao relative
theobroma subincanum.desc: A forest tree whose fruit is eaten by peccaries, deer, agoutis and monkeys, according to GloBI feeding records.
theobroma subincanum.about: Theobroma is a genus of flowering plants in the mallow family, Malvaceae. It was previously classified as a member of Sterculiaceae, which has been incorporated into Malvaceae to make it monophyletic.

theropithecus gelada.name: Gelada
theropithecus gelada.desc: A grazing primate of the Ethiopian Highlands, with grass blades making up most of its diet; it sleeps on cliff ledges.
theropithecus gelada.about: The gelada, sometimes called the bleeding-heart monkey or the gelada baboon, is a species of Old World monkey found only in the Ethiopian Highlands, living at elevations of 1,800–4,400 m…

thin alpine soil.name: Thin alpine soil
thin alpine soil.desc: Poor, shallow soils above the treeline; plants there are dwarfed and deep rooted.

thin boreal soil.name: Thin boreal soil
thin boreal soil.desc: Soils on the island are thin, so shallow-rooted trees dominate and nutrients cycle quickly through leaf litter.

thin cold soil.name: Thin cold soil
thin cold soil.desc: Plants face strong winds, thin soils and a short growing season, according to the park service.

thin desert soil.name: Thin desert soil
thin desert soil.desc: Hot, dry conditions limit soil formation, so slopes stay stony and plants depend on what nutrients decomposers release.

thin glacial soils.name: Thin glacial soils
thin glacial soils.desc: Granite bedrock and thin soils shaped by glaciers hold the forest's nutrients, which are recycled from dead matter.

thin limestone soil.name: Thin limestone soil
thin limestone soil.desc: Shallow soil over limestone; litter decay by microbes recycles nutrients to the forest.

thin mountain soil.name: Thin mountain soil
thin mountain soil.desc: Cold, thin soils slow plant growth and nutrient release.

thin rocky soil.name: Thin rocky soil
thin rocky soil.desc: Shallow soils on the canyon rim hold little water and nutrients, so decomposers recycling dead matter matter to the plants.

thin soil on ancient rock.name: Thin soil on ancient rock
thin soil on ancient rock.desc: The park sits on very old Canadian Shield bedrock, with glacial scours and deposits shaping where soil and water collect.

thin tundra soil.name: Thin tundra soil
thin tundra soil.desc: Cold, thin soils keep most trees and shrubs small, according to Wikipedia.

thin tundra soil & bird guano.name: Thin tundra soil & bird guano
thin tundra soil & bird guano.desc: Soils are thin and thaw only in summer. Seabird droppings below bird cliffs fertilise the slopes, where the lushest vegetation grows.

thlaspi arvense.name: Field Penny-cress
thlaspi arvense.desc: Field Penny-cress (Thlaspi arvense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

thomomys bottae.name: Botta's pocket gopher
thomomys bottae.desc: Botta's pocket gopher (Thomomys bottae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
thomomys bottae.about: Botta's pocket gopher is a pocket gopher native to western North America. It is also known in some areas as valley pocket gopher, particularly in California.

thraupis palmarum.name: Palm tanager
thraupis palmarum.desc: A common fruit-eating songbird; GloBI records show it eating Miconia fruit.
thraupis palmarum.about: The palm tanager is a medium-sized passerine bird. This tanager is a resident breeder from Nicaragua south to Bolivia, Paraguay, and southern Brazil.

thrinax radiata.name: Florida thatch palm
thrinax radiata.desc: A coastal palm that is one of the most recorded plants near the reserve. Its fruit is eaten by animals such as spider monkeys.
thrinax radiata.about: Thrinax radiata, also known as the Florida thatch palm, is a medium to slow growing palm in the family Arecaceae.

thryothorus ludovicianus.name: Carolina Wren
thryothorus ludovicianus.desc: Carolina Wren (Thryothorus ludovicianus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 702 times near the park in GBIF.
thryothorus ludovicianus.about: The Carolina wren is a species of wren common in the eastern United States, the extreme south of Ontario, Canada, the northeast and southeast of Mexico, and into northern Central America.

thuja occidentalis.name: Northern White-cedar
thuja occidentalis.desc: Northern White-cedar (Thuja occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.

thuja plicata.name: Western Red-cedar
thuja plicata.desc: Western Red-cedar (Thuja plicata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 7 times near the park in GBIF.
thuja plicata.about: Thuja plicata is a large coniferous tree in the cypress family, Cupressaceae, native to the Pacific Northwest of North America. Its common name is western redcedar, although it is not a true cedar.

thunnus albacares.name: Yellowfin tuna
thunnus albacares.desc: Fast open-water hunter of flying fish and other baitfish. Industrial fisheries are its main cause of death.
thunnus albacares.about: The yellowfin tuna is a species of tuna found in pelagic waters of tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide.

thylogale billardierii.name: Tasmanian pademelon
thylogale billardierii.desc: A small wallaby that rests in thick cover by day and feeds on grass and shoots in open ground near the forest edge after dark.
thylogale billardierii.about: The Tasmanian pademelon, also known as the rufous-bellied pademelon or red-bellied pademelon, is the sole species of pademelon found in Tasmania, and was formerly found throughout southeastern…

thylogale stigmatica.name: Red-legged pademelon
thylogale stigmatica.desc: A small rainforest wallaby that eats umbrella tree fruit.
thylogale stigmatica.about: The red-legged pademelon is a species of small macropod found on the northeastern coast of Australia and in New Guinea.

thymus praecox.name: Mother of thyme
thymus praecox.desc: A creeping, aromatic herb of thin limestone soils that flowers in the short turf.
thymus praecox.about: Thymus praecox is a species of thyme. A common name is mother of thyme, but "creeping thyme" and "wild thyme" may be used where Thymus serpyllum, which also shares these names, is not found.

thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis.name: Common bagworm
thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis.desc: Common bagworm (Thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
thyridopteryx ephemeraeformis.about: The evergreen bagworm, commonly known as bagworm, eastern bagworm, common bagworm, common basket worm, or North American bagworm, is a moth that spins its cocoon in its larval life, decorating it…

tian shan meltwater.name: Tian Shan meltwater
tian shan meltwater.desc: Snowmelt and glacier streams from the surrounding mountains: about 118 rivers and streams feed the lake and water the valleys and shores.

tiarella trifoliata.name: Sugar-scoop
tiarella trifoliata.desc: Sugar-scoop (Tiarella trifoliata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
tiarella trifoliata.about: Tiarella trifoliata, the three-leaf foamflower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Saxifragaceae.

tidal flats and sabkha.name: Tidal flats and sabkha
tidal flats and sabkha.desc: Tidal mudflats and salt flats line the coast of the reserve islands and host wintering waders and mangroves.

tidal flooding.name: Tidal flooding
tidal flooding.desc: Seawater floods and drains the low mudflats and salt marshes, bringing food in and exposing invertebrates to wading birds at low tide.

tidal lagoon.name: Tidal lagoon
tidal lagoon.desc: A large, shallow lagoon of seagrass, mudflats and mangroves that empties and refills with the tides.

tidal lagoons (khaurs).name: Tidal lagoons (khaurs)
tidal lagoons (khaurs).desc: Lagoons such as Khaur Jarama have mudflats, scattered mangroves and fish nursery habitat, and feed wintering waders.

tidal mixing.name: Tides and salt water
tidal mixing.desc: Tides reach about 58 miles up the river, mixing fresh and salt water and flooding the marsh twice a day.

tidal mudflats.name: Tidal mudflats
tidal mudflats.desc: Vast intertidal flats and sand banks hold the seagrass beds and feed the wintering shorebirds.

tidal salinity.name: Tidal salinity
tidal salinity.desc: Tides and the balance of fresh and salt water set which trees survive. Rising sea level and less river flow push salt further inland.

tidal sea water.name: Tidal sea water
tidal sea water.desc: Twice-daily tides flood the coastal mangroves and bring in salt water and sediment.

tidal sediment.name: Marsh mud and nutrients
tidal sediment.desc: Muddy marsh soil holds the nutrients that cordgrass takes up.

tides.name: Tides
tides.desc: Rising and falling tides wet and expose the rocky shore twice a day and set where seaweeds and shellfish can live.

tides and brackish water.name: Tides and brackish water
tides and brackish water.desc: Tides flood the channels and lagoons twice a day, setting the salinity that mangroves tolerate and moving crabs, fish and larvae in and out.

tides and cool ocean water.name: Tides and cool ocean water
tides and cool ocean water.desc: Tides and ocean exchange flush the bay, bringing cooler, saltier water in from Rhode Island Sound.

tides and currents.name: Tides and currents
tides and currents.desc: Tides flush the mangroves and shallow banks, carrying nutrients and larvae.

tides and lagoons.name: Tides and lagoons
tides and lagoons.desc: Tides flood the mangrove and seagrass shallows with salt water and move nutrients and larvae in and out.

tides and river flooding.name: Tides and river flooding
tides and river flooding.desc: Coastal tides and flooding rivers soak the swamps and mangroves along the Pacific side of the site.

tides and salt water.name: Tides and salt water
tides and salt water.desc: Tides flood and drain the mangrove mud twice a day, bringing salt water that mangroves tolerate and most other plants do not.

tigris-euphrates floodwater.name: Tigris-Euphrates floodwater
tigris-euphrates floodwater.desc: The marshes depend on river flow. Drainage and upstream dams cut it, and reflooding after 2003 let wetlands partly recover.

tilapia and others.name: Freshwater fish
tilapia and others.desc: Fish of the seasonal rivers and lakes that graze on algae and small aquatic life.
tilapia and others.about: A fish is an aquatic, anamniotic, gill-bearing vertebrate with a tough cranium to protect the brain. Many fish have fins that they use for directional stability and propulsion.

tilia americana.name: American Basswood
tilia americana.desc: American Basswood (Tilia americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

tillandsia bartramii.name: Bartram's airplant
tillandsia bartramii.desc: Bartram's airplant (Tillandsia bartramii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 31 times near the park in GBIF.

tillandsia setacea.name: Southern needleleaf
tillandsia setacea.desc: Southern needleleaf (Tillandsia setacea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

tillandsia usneoides.name: Spanish moss
tillandsia usneoides.desc: Spanish moss (Tillandsia usneoides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.
tillandsia usneoides.about: Spanish moss is an epiphytic flowering plant that often grows upon large trees in tropical and subtropical climates.

timane river and waterholes.name: Timane River and waterholes
timane river and waterholes.desc: The Timane River runs through old channels toward Cerro Leon and feeds an inland basin; seasonal pools matter for wildlife in a dry land.

tipularia discolor.name: Crippled cranefly
tipularia discolor.desc: Crippled Cranefly (Tipularia discolor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
tipularia discolor.about: Tipularia discolor, the crippled cranefly or crane-fly orchid, is a perennial terrestrial woodland orchid, a member of the family Orchidaceae.

tisza river floods.name: Tisza River floods
tisza river floods.desc: The Tisza shaped this plain; its changing course is thought to have started the alkalinisation of the soils about 10,000 years ago.

tockus deckeni.name: Von der Decken's hornbill
tockus deckeni.desc: A hornbill of dry bush and coastal woodland in East Africa. It eats insects and other small prey, and fruit.
tockus deckeni.about: Von der Decken's hornbill is a hornbill found in East Africa, especially to the east of the East African Rift, from Ethiopia south to Tanzania.

todiramphus sacer.name: Pacific kingfisher
todiramphus sacer.desc: A perch-and-pounce hunter that takes insects, lizards, frogs and crabs, and is found across the South Pacific including Vanuatu.
todiramphus sacer.about: The Pacific kingfisher is a medium-sized kingfisher belonging to the subfamily Halcyoninae, the tree kingfishers.

todus mexicanus.name: Puerto Rican tody
todus mexicanus.desc: A tiny insect-eating bird endemic to the island. GloBI also records it taking fruit of pumpwood.
todus mexicanus.about: The Puerto Rican tody, locally known in Spanish as San Pedrito ("little Saint Peter"), is a bird endemic to the main island of Puerto Rico.

todus todus.name: Jamaican tody
todus todus.desc: A tiny endemic bird that catches insects and other small invertebrates in the forest understory.
todus todus.about: The Jamaican tody is a species of bird in the genus Todus endemic to Jamaica. Local names for the Jamaican tody include rasta bird, robin and robin redbreast.

tolypeutes matacus.name: Southern three-banded armadillo
tolypeutes matacus.desc: An armadillo that can roll into a ball; it feeds mainly on ants and termites and some plant matter.
tolypeutes matacus.about: The southern three-banded armadillo, also known as La Plata three-banded armadillo or Azara's domed armadillo, is an armadillo species from South America.

tomostima cuneifolia.name: Wedge Leaf Whitlow-grass
tomostima cuneifolia.desc: Wedge Leaf Whitlow-grass (Tomostima cuneifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
tomostima cuneifolia.about: Tomostima cuneifolia is a species of flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae known as the wedgeleaf draba or wedgeleaf whitlow-grass.

tor putitora.name: Golden mahseer
tor putitora.desc: A large river fish of Himalayan rivers that grazes algae and other foods and feeds the gharial.
tor putitora.about: Tor putitora, known as the golden mahseer, putitor mahseer, or Himalayan mahseer, is an endangered species of cyprinid fish that is found in rapid streams, riverine pools, and lakes in the Himalayan…

torreya taxifolia.name: Florida Torreya
torreya taxifolia.desc: Florida Torreya (Torreya taxifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 113 times near the park in GBIF.

townsendia texensis.name: Texas Townsend daisy
townsendia texensis.desc: Texas Townsend daisy (Townsendia texensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 32 times near the park in GBIF.

toxicodendron diversilobum.name: Pacific poison-oak
toxicodendron diversilobum.desc: Pacific poison-oak (Toxicodendron diversilobum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 63 times near the park in GBIF.
toxicodendron diversilobum.about: Toxicodendron diversilobum, commonly named Pacific poison oak or western poison oak, is a woody vine or shrub in the sumac family, Anacardiaceae.

toxicodendron radicans.name: Poison Ivy
toxicodendron radicans.desc: Poison Ivy (Toxicodendron radicans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
toxicodendron radicans.about: Toxicodendron radicans, commonly known as eastern poison ivy or poison ivy, is a species of allergenic flowering plant. It has numerous subtaxons and forms both vines and shrubs.

toxicodendron rydbergii.name: Poison Ivy
toxicodendron rydbergii.desc: Poison Ivy (Toxicodendron rydbergii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 47 times near the park in GBIF.

toxicodendron vernix.name: Poison Sumac
toxicodendron vernix.desc: Poison Sumac (Toxicodendron vernix): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

toxomerus geminatus.name: Eastern Calligrapher
toxomerus geminatus.desc: Eastern Calligrapher (Toxomerus geminatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

toxomerus marginatus.name: Syrphid Fly
toxomerus marginatus.desc: Syrphid Fly (Toxomerus marginatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

toxostoma curvirostre.name: Curve-billed Thrasher
toxostoma curvirostre.desc: Curve-billed Thrasher (Toxostoma curvirostre): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 2,230 times near the park in GBIF.
toxostoma curvirostre.about: The curve-billed thrasher is a medium-sized mimid native to most of Mexico and to the deserts of southwestern United States.

trachylepis atlantica.name: Noronha skink
trachylepis atlantica.desc: An endemic island lizard, the most recorded reptile near the site. Small insects are its likely food.
trachylepis atlantica.about: The Noronha skink is a species of skink from the island of Fernando de Noronha off northeastern Brazil.

trachylepis striata.name: African striped skink
trachylepis striata.desc: A lizard that hunts insects and is preyed on by snakes.
trachylepis striata.about: The African striped skink, commonly called the striped skink, is a species of lizard in the skink family (Scincidae). The species is widespread in East Africa and Southern Africa.

trachypithecus geei.name: Golden langur
trachypithecus geei.desc: A tree-dwelling leaf, fruit, seed and flower eater found only in a small area of Bhutan and Assam.
trachypithecus geei.about: Gee's golden langur, also known as simply the golden langur, is an Old World monkey found in a small region of Western Assam, India and the neighboring foothills of the Black Mountains of Bhutan.

trachypithecus hatinhensis.name: Hatinh langur
trachypithecus hatinhensis.desc: A leaf-eating monkey of limestone forest that sleeps in cliff crevices and caves. Wikipedia says the park holds the largest known population in the world.
trachypithecus hatinhensis.about: The Hatinh langur is a highly threatened Old World monkey found in limestone forests in Vietnam, primarily in the Quảng Bình Province. They are a primarily black, arboreal, and diurnal monkey.

trachypithecus obscurus.name: Dusky leaf monkey
trachypithecus obscurus.desc: Tree-living monkey that eats mainly leaves, along with fruit and flowers.
trachypithecus obscurus.about: The dusky leaf monkey, also known as the spectacled langur or the spectacled leaf monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

trachypithecus poliocephalus.name: Cat Ba langur
trachypithecus poliocephalus.desc: A critically endangered primate found only on Cat Ba Island. Over 70% of its diet is leaves, and it can drink salt water.
trachypithecus poliocephalus.about: The Cat Ba langur, also known as the golden-headed langur, is a critically endangered species of langur endemic to Cát Bà Island, Vietnam.

trachypithecus shortridgei.name: Shortridge's langur
trachypithecus shortridgei.desc: An endangered leaf-eating monkey of northern Myanmar forests that lives in the canopy and feeds on leaves and fruit.
trachypithecus shortridgei.about: The Shortridge's langur is an Old World monkey native to Burma and China.

tradescantia occidentalis.name: Prairie spiderwort
tradescantia occidentalis.desc: Prairie spiderwort (Tradescantia occidentalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 68 times near the park in GBIF.
tradescantia occidentalis.about: Tradescantia occidentalis, the prairie spiderwort or western spiderwort, is a plant in the dayflower family, Commelinaceae.

tradescantia ohiensis.name: Smooth spiderwort
tradescantia ohiensis.desc: Smooth spiderwort (Tradescantia ohiensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
tradescantia ohiensis.about: Tradescantia ohiensis, commonly known as bluejacket or Ohio spiderwort, is an herbaceous plant species in the genus Tradescantia native to eastern and central North America.

tradescantia ozarkana.name: Ozark spiderwort
tradescantia ozarkana.desc: Ozark spiderwort (Tradescantia ozarkana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

tradescantia subaspera.name: Wide-leaf spiderwort
tradescantia subaspera.desc: Wide-leaf spiderwort (Tradescantia subaspera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.
tradescantia subaspera.about: Tradescantia subaspera, the zigzag spiderwort, is a species of flowering plant in the family Commelinaceae, native to the eastern United States.

tradescantia virginiana.name: White spiderwort
tradescantia virginiana.desc: White spiderwort (Tradescantia virginiana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 57 times near the park in GBIF.
tradescantia virginiana.about: Tradescantia virginiana, the Virginia spiderwort, is a species of flowering plant in the family Commelinaceae (the spiderwort family).

tragelaphus buxtoni.name: Mountain nyala
tragelaphus buxtoni.desc: Large antelope found only in the Ethiopian Highlands east of the Rift. It mostly browses herbs and shrubs, and the leopard is its main predator.
tragelaphus buxtoni.about: The mountain nyala (Amharic: የደጋ አጋዘን) or balbok, is a large antelope found in high altitude woodlands in a small part of central Ethiopia.

tragelaphus scriptus.name: Bushbuck
tragelaphus scriptus.desc: A shy antelope of forest edges and thickets that browses leaves and shoots.

tragelaphus spekii.name: Sitatunga
tragelaphus spekii.desc: A swamp antelope that feeds on sedges, fresh grasses and herbs at wetland edges. It hides in deep water, partly submerged, when threatened.
tragelaphus spekii.about: The sitatunga or marshbuck is a swamp-dwelling medium-sized antelope found throughout central Africa, centering on the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of the Congo, Cameroon, parts of…

tragelaphus strepsiceros.name: Greater kudu
tragelaphus strepsiceros.desc: A woodland browser of leaves and shoots. Kudu are a main prey of spotted hyenas in Etosha.
tragelaphus strepsiceros.about: The greater kudu is a large woodland antelope, found throughout eastern and southern Africa.

tragia ramosa.name: Branched noseburn
tragia ramosa.desc: Branched noseburn (Tragia ramosa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 16 times near the park in GBIF.

tragopogon dubius.name: Common Salsify
tragopogon dubius.desc: Common Salsify (Tragopogon dubius): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.

tragulus kanchil.name: Lesser mouse-deer
tragulus kanchil.desc: Tiny hoofed mammal of the forest floor that eats fallen fruit and leaves.
tragulus kanchil.about: The lesser mouse-deer, lesser oriental chevrotain, lesser Malay chevrotain, or kanchil is a species of even-toed ungulate in the family Tragulidae.

trapa natans.name: Water Nut
trapa natans.desc: Water Nut (Trapa natans): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 96 times near the park in GBIF.
trapa natans.about: Trapa natans, the water caltrop, is a widespread species of flowering plant in the genus Trapa, family Lythraceae, grown as a food crop.

trapelus sanguinolentus.name: Steppe agama
trapelus sanguinolentus.desc: A common desert lizard that hunts insects by day. It is recorded as prey of the steppe ribbon racer.
trapelus sanguinolentus.about: Trapelus sanguinolentus, the steppe agama, is a species of agama found in Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and China.

travertine lake water.name: Travertine lake water
travertine lake water.desc: Mineral-rich water deposited calcium carbonate that built the travertine dams holding the six lakes, which sustain the shoreline vegetation.

trema orientale.name: Trema
trema orientale.desc: A fast-growing pioneer tree recorded near the reserve, found in forest edges and clearings where it makes small fruits.
trema orientale.about: Trema orientale is a species of flowering tree in the hemp family, Cannabaceae.

tremarctos ornatus.name: Spectacled bear
tremarctos ornatus.desc: South America's only bear, mostly vegetarian: bromeliads, palm nuts, fallen fruit and a little meat. Cloud forest is its best habitat.
tremarctos ornatus.about: The spectacled bear, also known as the Andean bear, is a species of bear native to the Andes Mountains in northern and western South America.

triadenum fraseri.name: Fraser's Marsh St. Johnswort
triadenum fraseri.desc: Fraser's Marsh St. Johnswort (Triadenum fraseri): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.
triadenum fraseri.about: Triadenum fraseri, commonly known as bog St. John's wort, Fraser's St.

triadica sebifera.name: Chinese tallow
triadica sebifera.desc: Chinese tallow (Triadica sebifera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

triaenodon obesus.name: Whitetip reef shark
triaenodon obesus.desc: A reef shark that rests in caves by day and hunts reef fish, octopus and crustaceans at night; Tubbataha is noted for very high densities of it.
triaenodon obesus.about: The whitetip reef shark is a species of requiem shark, in the family Carcharhinidae. It is the only extant species of genus Triaenodon.

trianthema portulacastrum.name: Desert Horse-Purslane
trianthema portulacastrum.desc: Desert Horse-Purslane (Trianthema portulacastrum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

tribulus terrestris.name: Small Caltrops
tribulus terrestris.desc: Small Caltrops (Tribulus terrestris): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
tribulus terrestris.about: Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.

trichechus manatus.name: West Indian manatee
trichechus manatus.desc: A slow, gentle grazer of seagrass that visits the bay. Boat strikes are a main danger.
trichechus manatus.about: The West Indian manatee, also known as the North American manatee, is a large, aquatic mammal native to warm coastal areas of the Caribbean, from the Eastern United States to northern Brazil.

trichechus senegalensis.name: West African manatee
trichechus senegalensis.desc: Lives in the Gambia River. River manatees mostly eat vegetation overhanging the banks and have few natural enemies besides crocodiles and people.
trichechus senegalensis.about: The African manatee, also known as the West African manatee, is a species of manatee that inhabits much of Western Africa – from Senegal to Angola.

trichodes ornatus.name: Common Checkered Beetle
trichodes ornatus.desc: Common Checkered Beetle (Trichodes ornatus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.
trichodes ornatus.about: Trichodes ornatus, commonly known as ornate checkered beetle, is a beetle species of checkered beetles belonging to the family Cleridae, subfamily Clerinae which can be found only in North America.

trichoglossus haematodus.name: Rainbow lorikeet
trichoglossus haematodus.desc: A nectar and fruit feeder. Eucalypt nectar is an important food, and it also takes figs.
trichoglossus haematodus.about: The rainbow lorikeet is a species of parrot found in Australia. It is common along the eastern seaboard, from northern Queensland to South Australia.

trichoptera.name: Caddisfly larvae
trichoptera.desc: Aquatic larvae that graze algae and plant matter on stones and are food for trout and dippers.
trichoptera.about: The caddisflies (order Trichoptera) are a group of insects with aquatic larvae and terrestrial adults.

trichoscypha.name: Trichoscypha
trichoscypha.desc: Forest trees with fleshy fruit. GloBI records show several monkeys and a forest mouse feeding on them.
trichoscypha.about: Trichoscypha is a genus of plants in the family Anacardiaceae. It includes 32 species native to tropical Africa.

trichostema lanatum.name: Woolly blue-curls
trichostema lanatum.desc: Woolly blue-curls (Trichostema lanatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 48 times near the park in GBIF.
trichostema lanatum.about: Trichostema lanatum, also known as woolly bluecurls, is a small evergreen shrub or sub-shrub native to arid coastal chaparral regions of California down to the northern tip of Baja California, Mexico.

trichosurus vulpecula.name: Common brushtail possum
trichosurus vulpecula.desc: Introduced from Australia. It eats the leaves of native trees and continues to damage the forest.
trichosurus vulpecula.about: The common brushtail possum is a nocturnal, semiarboreal marsupial of the family Phalangeridae, native to Australia and invasive in New Zealand, and the second-largest of the Australasian possums.

triepeolus concavus.name: Concave Cuckoo Nomad Bee
triepeolus concavus.desc: Concave Cuckoo Nomad Bee (Triepeolus concavus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

trifolium alpinum.name: Alpine clover
trifolium alpinum.desc: Flowering legume of high pastures. Herbs like this are eaten by grazers in summer, and it is a larval food plant for the mountain clouded yellow butterfly.
trifolium alpinum.about: Trifolium alpinum is a species of flowering plant in the legume family known by the common name alpine clover. It is native to the Alps.

trifolium arvense.name: Hare's-foot Clover
trifolium arvense.desc: Hare's-foot Clover (Trifolium arvense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.

trifolium depauperatum.name: Dwarf sack clover
trifolium depauperatum.desc: Dwarf sack clover (Trifolium depauperatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
trifolium depauperatum.about: Trifolium depauperatum is a species of clover known by the common names cowbag clover, poverty clover, and balloon sack clover.

trifolium gymnocarpon.name: Tufted clover
trifolium gymnocarpon.desc: Tufted clover (Trifolium gymnocarpon): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

trifolium pratense.name: Red Clover
trifolium pratense.desc: Red Clover (Trifolium pratense): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
trifolium pratense.about: Trifolium pratense (from Latin prātum, meaning meadow), red clover, is a herbaceous species of flowering plant in the bean family, Fabaceae.

trifolium repens.name: White Clover
trifolium repens.desc: White Clover (Trifolium repens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
trifolium repens.about: Trifolium repens, the white clover, is a herbaceous perennial plant in the bean family, Fabaceae (also known as Leguminosae).

trifolium wormskioldii.name: Cow clover
trifolium wormskioldii.desc: Cow clover (Trifolium wormskioldii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 17 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium.name: Spring wildflowers
trillium.desc: Trilliums, mayapple, phlox and other woodland flowers that carpet the forest floor in spring and are recorded often in the park.
trillium.about: Trillium (trillium, wakerobin, toadshade, tri flower, birthroot, birthwort, and sometimes "wood lily") is a genus of about fifty flowering plant species in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium catesbaei.name: Bashful wakerobin
trillium catesbaei.desc: Bashful wakerobin (Trillium catesbaei): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 96 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium catesbaei.about: Trillium catesbaei, also known as bashful wakerobin or rosy wake-robin, is a spring flowering perennial plant found in the southeastern United States.

trillium cernuum.name: Whip-Poor-Will Flower
trillium cernuum.desc: Whip-Poor-Will Flower (Trillium cernuum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium cuneatum.name: Little sweet Betsy
trillium cuneatum.desc: Little sweet Betsy (Trillium cuneatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium cuneatum.about: Trillium cuneatum, the little sweet betsy, also known as whip-poor-will flower, large toadshade, purple toadshade, and bloody butcher, is a species of flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium erectum.name: Red Trillium
trillium erectum.desc: Red Trillium (Trillium erectum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 51 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium erectum.about: Trillium erectum, the red trillium, also known as wake robin, purple trillium, bethroot, or stinking benjamin, is a species of flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium grandiflorum.name: Large white trillium
trillium grandiflorum.desc: A spring woodland wildflower of the forest floor. GloBI records white-tailed deer browsing it.
trillium grandiflorum.about: Trillium grandiflorum, the white trillium, large-flowered trillium, great white trillium, white wake-robin or in French: trille blanc, is a species of flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium nivale.name: Dwarf white trillium
trillium nivale.desc: Dwarf white trillium (Trillium nivale): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium nivale.about: Trillium nivale, the snow trillium or dwarf white trillium, is a species of flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium ovatum.name: Pacific trillium
trillium ovatum.desc: Pacific trillium (Trillium ovatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium ovatum.about: Trillium ovatum, commonly known as the Pacific trillium, western wakerobin, western white trillium, or western trillium, is a species of flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium pusillum.name: Dwarf wakerobin
trillium pusillum.desc: Dwarf wakerobin (Trillium pusillum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium recurvatum.name: Prairie trillium
trillium recurvatum.desc: Prairie trillium (Trillium recurvatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium recurvatum.about: Trillium recurvatum, the prairie trillium, toadshade, or bloody butcher, is a species of perennial herbaceous flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trillium sessile.name: Sessile trillium
trillium sessile.desc: Sessile trillium (Trillium sessile): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium sessile.about: Trillium sessile is a species of flowering plant in the bunchflower family Melanthiaceae.

trillium stamineum.name: Blue Ridge wakerobin
trillium stamineum.desc: Blue Ridge wakerobin (Trillium stamineum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 20 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium underwoodii.name: Longbract wakerobin
trillium underwoodii.desc: Longbract wakerobin (Trillium underwoodii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 77 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium undulatum.name: Painted trillium
trillium undulatum.desc: Painted trillium (Trillium undulatum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 30 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium undulatum.about: Trillium undulatum, commonly called painted trillium, painted lady (not to be confused with the painted lady butterfly), or trille ondulé in French, is a species of flowering plant in the bunchflower…

trillium vaseyi.name: Sweet wakerobin
trillium vaseyi.desc: Sweet wakerobin (Trillium vaseyi): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 14 times near the park in GBIF.

trillium viridescens.name: Tapertip wakerobin
trillium viridescens.desc: Tapertip wakerobin (Trillium viridescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.
trillium viridescens.about: Trillium viridescens, also known as the Ozark trillium or tapertip wakerobin, is a species of flowering plant in the family Melanthiaceae.

trimeresurus albolabris.name: White-lipped pit viper
trimeresurus albolabris.desc: A tree-dwelling venomous snake that ambushes lizards and other small animals.
trimeresurus albolabris.about: Trimeresurus albolabris, the white-lipped pit viper or white-lipped tree viper, is a venomous pit viper species endemic to Southeast Asia.

trimeresurus insularis.name: White-lipped island pitviper
trimeresurus insularis.desc: A venomous tree snake and the most recorded reptile near the park. GloBI records show it eating tree frogs.
trimeresurus insularis.about: Trimeresurus insularis, commonly known as the Indonesian pit viper, Lesser Sunda Islands pit viper, Komodo Island pit viper, Sunda white-lipped pit viper or red-tailed pit viper, also popularly known…

trimeresurus sabahi.name: Sabah bamboo pitviper
trimeresurus sabahi.desc: A Bornean pitviper of mountain forest, usually seen on branches of shrubs; it takes small vertebrates such as frogs and rodents.
trimeresurus sabahi.about: Trimeresurus sabahi, commonly known as the Sabah pit viper or Sabah bamboo pitviper, is a venomous pitviper species. If defined narrowly, it is endemic to the island of Borneo.

tringa melanoleuca.name: Greater Yellowlegs
tringa melanoleuca.desc: Greater Yellowlegs (Tringa melanoleuca): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1,365 times near the park in GBIF.

tringa semipalmata.name: Willet
tringa semipalmata.desc: Willet (Tringa semipalmata): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 78 times near the park in GBIF.
tringa semipalmata.about: The saltmarsh willet or willet is a large shorebird in the family Scolopacidae. It is a relatively large and robust sandpiper and is the largest of the species called "shanks" in the genus Tringa.

trioceros cristatus.name: Crested chameleon
trioceros cristatus.desc: A forest chameleon of Cameroon and neighbouring countries that is recorded near the reserve and feeds on small invertebrates.
trioceros cristatus.about: The crested chameleon, also known as the sail backed chameleon, is a species of chameleon native to forests and semi-open wooded habitats in Central Africa.

trioceros johnstoni.name: Johnston's chameleon
trioceros johnstoni.desc: A highland forest chameleon of the Albertine Rift that catches insects in the shrub layer.
trioceros johnstoni.about: Trioceros johnstoni, known commonly as Johnston's chameleon, Johnston's three-horned chameleon, and the Ruwenzori three-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family…

triodia.name: Spinifex
triodia.desc: Spiky hummock grasses that cover much of the red sandplain and dunes of central Australia.
triodia.about: Triodia is a large genus of hummock grass endemic to Australia. The species of this genus are known by the common name spinifex, although they are not a part of the coastal genus Spinifex.

triphora trianthophoros.name: Three birds orchid
triphora trianthophoros.desc: Three birds orchid (Triphora trianthophoros): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 35 times near the park in GBIF.

triphosa haesitata.name: Tissue Moth
triphosa haesitata.desc: Tissue Moth (Triphosa haesitata): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 12 times near the park in GBIF.
triphosa haesitata.about: Triphosa haesitata, the tissue moth or American tissue moth, is a species of geometrid moth in the family Geometridae. It is found in North America.

triphysaria eriantha.name: Johnny-tuck
triphysaria eriantha.desc: Johnny-tuck (Triphysaria eriantha): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 18 times near the park in GBIF.

tripsacum dactyloides.name: Eastern Gamagrass
tripsacum dactyloides.desc: Eastern Gamagrass (Tripsacum dactyloides): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
tripsacum dactyloides.about: Tripsacum dactyloides, commonly called eastern gamagrass, or Fakahatchee grass, is a warm-season, sod-forming bunch grass.

trirhabda bacharidis.name: Groundselbush beetle
trirhabda bacharidis.desc: Groundselbush beetle (Trirhabda bacharidis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 26 times near the park in GBIF.
trirhabda bacharidis.about: Trirhabda bacharidis, known generally as the groundselbush beetle or groundsel bush leaf beetle, is a species of skeletonizing leaf beetle in the family Chrysomelidae.

triteleia laxa.name: Triplet-lily
triteleia laxa.desc: Triplet-lily (Triteleia laxa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

triticum monococcum.name: Einkorn
triticum monococcum.desc: Einkorn (Triticum monococcum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 8 times near the park in GBIF.

trochilus polytmus.name: Red-billed streamertail
trochilus polytmus.desc: Jamaica's national bird, the most recorded species here. It feeds mainly on nectar and also catches small insects.
trochilus polytmus.about: The red-billed streamertail, also known as the doctor bird, or swallow tail hummingbird, is a species of hummingbird in the "emeralds", tribe Trochilini of the subfamily Trochilinae.

troglodytes aedon.name: House Wren
troglodytes aedon.desc: House Wren (Troglodytes aedon): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 700 times near the park in GBIF.

trollius europaeus and others.name: Mountain meadow herbs
trollius europaeus and others.desc: Globeflower and many other flowering herbs of the pastures and meadows above the tree line, part of a flora of about 2,600 plant species.
trollius europaeus and others.about: Trollius europaeus, the globeflower, is a perennial flowering plant of the family Ranunculaceae. The plant is native to Europe and Western Asia and is a protected species in Russia and Bulgaria.

troodos rock and thin soil.name: Troodos rock and thin soil
troodos rock and thin soil.desc: The massif is an uplifted slab of ancient oceanic crust; the golden oak is restricted to its igneous rocks.

tropical rain.name: Heavy rainfall
tropical rain.desc: The islands are wet. Rain feeds the rainforest and runs down steep slopes to the sea.

tropical rainfall.name: Tropical rainfall
tropical rainfall.desc: Heavy, year-round rain feeds the rivers and keeps the lowland forest and peat swamps wet.

tropical sun.name: Sunlight
tropical sun.desc: Strong year-round sun powers the rainforest canopy and the algae and plankton of the reef.

tropical sunlight.name: Tropical sunlight
tropical sunlight.desc: Year-round warmth and light drive the forest canopy.

tropidacris cristata.name: Giant red-winged grasshopper
tropidacris cristata.desc: A very large tropical grasshopper that chews leaves, and is prey for lizards and birds.
tropidacris cristata.about: Tropidacris cristata, the giant red-winged grasshopper, is a widespread species of lubber grasshopper in the family Romaleidae from tropical South and Central America, and Mexico.

tsuga canadensis.name: Eastern Hemlock-spruce
tsuga canadensis.desc: Eastern Hemlock-spruce (Tsuga canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 82 times near the park in GBIF.
tsuga canadensis.about: Tsuga canadensis, also known as Canadian hemlock, eastern hemlock-spruce, or eastern hemlock, and in the French-speaking regions of Canada as pruche du Canada, is a coniferous tree in the pine…

tsuga chinensis.name: Chinese hemlock
tsuga chinensis.desc: A conifer that dominates a mid-elevation forest belt in the park, roughly between 2,500 and 3,500 m. It shelters many forest animals.
tsuga chinensis.about: Tsuga chinensis, commonly referred to as the Taiwan or Chinese hemlock, is a coniferous tree species in the pine family, Pinaceae, native to China, Taiwan, and Vietnam.

tsuga heterophylla.name: Western hemlock
tsuga heterophylla.desc: A shade-tolerant conifer of the lower, wetter forests where the old-growth stands are found.
tsuga heterophylla.about: Tsuga heterophylla, the western hemlock or western hemlock-spruce, is a species of conifer in the pine family, Pinaceae.

tsuga mertensiana.name: Mountain hemlock
tsuga mertensiana.desc: A conifer of deep-snow subalpine forest and one of the most recorded trees around the rim.
tsuga mertensiana.about: Tsuga mertensiana, known as mountain hemlock, is a species of conifer in the pine family, Pinaceae.

tundra soil.name: Tundra soil
tundra soil.desc: Thin, cold soils over permafrost where nutrients are released slowly.

tundra soil and permafrost.name: Tundra soil and permafrost
tundra soil and permafrost.desc: Island ground that was never glaciated. Its thin, cold soil feeds sedges, willows and the meadows of the warmer valleys.

tupaia montana.name: Mountain treeshrew
tupaia montana.desc: Eats mostly arthropods plus wild fruit, and licks nectar from pitcher plants including N. rajah, leaving droppings in them. Endemic to Borneo.
tupaia montana.about: The mountain treeshrew is a treeshrew species within the Tupaiidae.

turdus falcklandii.name: Austral thrush
turdus falcklandii.desc: A common thrush of forests and gardens that eats berries and invertebrates.
turdus falcklandii.about: The austral thrush is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. It is found in Argentina, Chile, and the Falkland Islands.

turdus grayi.name: Clay-colored thrush
turdus grayi.desc: A widespread thrush that eats fruit, recorded on milkberry, alligatorwood and wax mallow.
turdus grayi.about: The clay-colored thrush is a common Middle American bird of the thrush family (Turdidae). It is the national bird of Costa Rica, where it is well known as the yigüirro (Spanish: [ʝi'ɣwiro]).

turdus merula.name: Eurasian blackbird
turdus merula.desc: A thrush that GloBI records eating barley and Pistacia atlantica. It is itself prey for foxes, jackals and kestrels.
turdus merula.about: The common blackbird is a species of true thrush. It is also known as the Eurasian blackbird, or simply the blackbird.

turdus migratorius.name: American Robin
turdus migratorius.desc: American Robin (Turdus migratorius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 322 times near the park in GBIF.
turdus migratorius.about: The American robin is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.

turdus plumbeus.name: Red-legged thrush
turdus plumbeus.desc: Thrush that eats fruit and invertebrates, GloBI records it taking scarletbush.
turdus plumbeus.about: The Western red-legged thrush is a species of bird in the family Turdidae. Native to the Caribbean, it is found in the Bahamas, Cayman Islands, and Cuba.

tursiops aduncus.name: Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin
tursiops aduncus.desc: Eats a wide range of fish and squid. Some Shark Bay dolphins wear marine sponges on their snouts, seemingly as tools to probe the seabed for fish.
tursiops aduncus.about: The Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphin is a species of bottlenose dolphin. This dolphin grows to 2.6 m (8.5 ft) long, and weighs up to 230 kg (510 lb).

tursiops truncatus.name: Bottlenose dolphin
tursiops truncatus.desc: Visits the bay seasonally or year-round and eats fish including menhaden.
tursiops truncatus.about: The common bottlenose dolphin or Atlantic bottlenose dolphin is one of three species of bottlenose dolphin in the genus Tursiops.

tympanuchus cupido.name: Greater prairie-chicken
tympanuchus cupido.desc: Eats seeds, fruit, green plants and insects such as grasshoppers. Wikipedia says Missouri once held hundreds of thousands but only about 500 remain, and that the MDC is bringing birds in from Kansas and Nebraska.
tympanuchus cupido.about: The greater prairie-chicken or pinnated grouse, sometimes called a boomer, is a large bird in the grouse tribe.

typha.name: Cattails
typha.desc: Tall emergent plants of the park's marshes and beaver ponds, eaten by muskrats and beavers.
typha.about: Typha is a genus of about 30 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Typhaceae.

typha angustifolia.name: Lesser Bulrush
typha angustifolia.desc: Lesser Bulrush (Typha angustifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 27 times near the park in GBIF.
typha angustifolia.about: Typha angustifolia is a perennial herbaceous plant in the genus Typha, native throughout most of Eurasia and locally in northwest Africa; it also occurs widely in North America, where its native…

typha domingensis.name: Southern cattail
typha domingensis.desc: A tall emergent marsh plant that grows with reeds in the shallow water of the marshes.
typha domingensis.about: Typha domingensis, known commonly as southern cattail or cumbungi, is a perennial herbaceous plant of the genus Typha.

typha latifolia.name: Bulrush
typha latifolia.desc: Bulrush (Typha latifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
typha latifolia.about: Typha latifolia is a perennial herbaceous wetland plant in the genus Typha.

tyrannus tyrannus.name: Eastern Kingbird
tyrannus tyrannus.desc: Eastern Kingbird (Tyrannus tyrannus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 24 times near the park in GBIF.

tyria jacobaeae.name: Cinnabar
tyria jacobaeae.desc: Cinnabar (Tyria jacobaeae): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
tyria jacobaeae.about: The cinnabar moth is a brightly coloured Arctiinae moth found as a native species in Europe and western and central Asia then east across the Palearctic to Siberia to China.

tyto glaucops.name: Ashy-faced owl
tyto glaucops.desc: A night hunter that preys on solenodons, which evolved with few land predators.
tyto glaucops.about: The ashy-faced owl is a species of bird in the barn-owl family Tytonidae. It is found on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, on Dominica, and on several other islands of the Lesser Antilles.

uca.name: Fiddler crabs
uca.desc: Burrowing crabs that sift mud for algae, microbes and detritus, and are a main food for wading birds and other predators here.
uca.about: The fiddler crab or calling crab is any of the hundred species of semiterrestrial marine crabs in the family Ocypodidae.

uca and related genera.name: Fiddler crabs
uca and related genera.desc: Burrowing crabs that sift mud for algae, microbes and detritus. Many predators hunt them, and they rework the sediment as they feed.
uca and related genera.about: The fiddler crab or calling crab is any of the hundred species of semiterrestrial marine crabs in the family Ocypodidae.

ulex minor.name: Dwarf gorse
ulex minor.desc: Spiny evergreen shrub that, with heather, dominates the shrublands covering most of the site.
ulex minor.about: Ulex minor, the dwarf furze or dwarf gorse is an evergreen dwarf shrub in the family Fabaceae, native to eastern England, France, Spain and Portugal. It is restricted to lowland heathland habitats.

ulva.name: Green seaweed
ulva.desc: Sea lettuce and other algae grow on the shallow reefs and are a food for green turtles.
ulva.about: The sea lettuces comprise the genus Ulva, a group of edible green algae that are widely distributed along the coasts of the world's oceans.

ulva and others.name: Benthic algae
ulva and others.desc: Over 305 species of seaweed have been recorded in the marine park, about 15 percent of them found nowhere else. They are the grazing base of the reef.
ulva and others.about: Algae are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. It excludes the land plants (embryophytes).

uniola paniculata.name: Seaoats
uniola paniculata.desc: Seaoats (Uniola paniculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
uniola paniculata.about: Uniola paniculata, also known as sea oats, seaside oats, araña, and arroz de costa, is a tall subtropical grass that is an important component of coastal sand dune and beach plant communities in the…

unionidae.name: Freshwater mussels
unionidae.desc: The upper river has dozens of mussel species. They filter algae from the water, and freshwater drum eat them. The NPS reports their numbers are recovering.
unionidae.about: The Unionidae are a family of freshwater mussels, the largest in the order Unionida, the bivalve molluscs sometimes known as river mussels, or simply as unionids.

urena lobata.name: Caesar Weed
urena lobata.desc: Caesar Weed (Urena lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 11 times near the park in GBIF.

uria lomvia.name: Thick-billed murre
uria lomvia.desc: A seabird that dives deep for cod and nests on crowded cliffs.
uria lomvia.about: The thick-billed murre or Brünnich's guillemot is a bird in the auk family (Alcidae). This bird is named after the Danish zoologist Morten Thrane Brünnich.

urnisa guttulosa.name: Grasshoppers
urnisa guttulosa.desc: Plant-eating insects that boom after rain and feed lizards, birds and small marsupials.
urnisa guttulosa.about: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.

urochloa.name: Signalgrass
urochloa.desc: Grasses of open patches among the thorn forest, one of the well-recorded plant groups near the park; seeds feed doves and others.
urochloa.about: Urochloa, commonly known as signalgrass, is a genus of plants in the grass family, native to tropical and subtropical regions of Eurasia, Africa, Australia, the Americas, and various islands.

urocissa ornata.name: Sri Lanka blue magpie
urocissa ornata.desc: An endemic forest bird that eats mainly insects, frogs and small lizards, plus some fruit, and may take eggs or chicks of other birds.
urocissa ornata.about: The Sri Lanka blue magpie or Ceylon magpie is a brightly coloured member of the family Corvidae, found exclusively in Sri Lanka.

urocitellus armatus.name: Uinta ground squirrel
urocitellus armatus.desc: Common on the valley floor, eats plants and seeds and is prey for coyotes, eagles and bears.
urocitellus armatus.about: The Uinta ground squirrel, commonly called a "chisler" and Potgut in northern Utah, is a species of rodent native to the western United States.

urocitellus columbianus.name: Columbian Ground Squirrel
urocitellus columbianus.desc: Burrowing squirrel of meadows and slopes that eats plants and bulbs. It is a prey of many predators and one of the best-recorded mammals near the park.
urocitellus columbianus.about: The Columbian ground squirrel is a species of rodent common in certain regions of Canada and the northwestern United States.

urocitellus parryii.name: Arctic ground squirrel
urocitellus parryii.desc: Eats willows, berries, seeds and some insects and stores food for winter. Predators include foxes, wolves, bears, lynx and eagles.
urocitellus parryii.about: The Arctic ground squirrel (Inuktitut: ᓯᒃᓯᒃ, siksik) is a species of ground squirrel in the squirrel family Sciuridae that is native to the Arctic and Subarctic regions of the Northern Hemisphere,…

urocitellus undulatus.name: Long-tailed ground squirrel
urocitellus undulatus.desc: A burrowing ground squirrel of steppe and meadows and the most recorded mammal near the site. Steppe eagles and foxes take it.
urocitellus undulatus.about: The long-tailed ground squirrel or Eversmann's souslik is a species of rodent in the squirrel family Sciuridae. It is found in China, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, and Russia.

urocyon cinereoargenteus.name: Gray fox
urocyon cinereoargenteus.desc: Gray fox (Urocyon cinereoargenteus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
urocyon cinereoargenteus.about: The gray fox, or grey fox, is an omnivorous mammal of the family Canidae, widespread throughout North America and Central America.

urocyon littoralis.name: Island fox
urocyon littoralis.desc: A small fox found only on the islands. It eats fruit, insects, lizards, birds and deer mice.
urocyon littoralis.about: The island fox is a small fox species that is endemic to six of the eight Channel Islands of California. They evolved from their larger mainland gray fox ancestor (U.

uromastyx aegyptia.name: Egyptian mastigure
uromastyx aegyptia.desc: A large spiny-tailed lizard of open, gravelly desert. It shelters in burrows and feeds mainly on plants and seeds.
uromastyx aegyptia.about: Uromastyx aegyptia is a species of lizard in the family Agamidae. The species is native to North Africa and the Middle East.

ursus americanus.name: Black bear
ursus americanus.desc: Black bear (Ursus americanus): a top predator in this web. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.
ursus americanus.about: The American black bear, or simply black bear, is a species of medium-sized bear which is endemic to North America. It is the continent's smallest and most widely distributed bear species.

ursus americanus carlottae.name: Haida Gwaii black bear
ursus americanus carlottae.desc: Largest native land mammal of the archipelago. Eats salmon, shellfish and plants, and carries salmon remains into the forest.
ursus americanus carlottae.about: Ursus americanus carlottae, the Haida Gwaii black bear or Queen Charlotte Islands black bear, is a morphologically distinct subspecies of the American black bear.

ursus arctos.name: Brown bear
ursus arctos.desc: Roams the taiga shore. It is the only known natural predator of adult Baikal seals, though attacks are thought to be rare.
ursus arctos.about: The brown bear is a large bear native to Eurasia and North America.

ursus arctos beringianus.name: Kamchatka brown bear
ursus arctos beringianus.desc: Eats berries, pine nuts, salmon and small mammals. Males can exceed 600 kg before winter.
ursus arctos beringianus.about: The Kamchatka brown bear, also known as the Far Eastern brown bear, is a subspecies of brown bear native to the Russian Kamchatka Peninsula.

ursus arctos gobiensis.name: Gobi bear
ursus arctos gobiensis.desc: A rare brown bear living near desert oases. It eats mostly plants and roots, with a little animal food such as rodents.
ursus arctos gobiensis.about: The Gobi bear, known in Mongolian as the Mazaalai (Мазаалай), is a critically endangered subspecies of the brown bear found in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia.

ursus arctos horribilis.name: Grizzly bear
ursus arctos horribilis.desc: The reserve is thought to hold around 500 grizzlies. They eat ground squirrels, moose, caribou and sheep, as well as plants.
ursus arctos horribilis.about: The grizzly bear, also known as the North American brown bear or simply grizzly, is a population or subspecies of the brown bear inhabiting North America.

ursus arctos lasiopus.name: Ussuri brown bear
ursus arctos lasiopus.desc: Mostly vegetarian, eating acorns, Korean pine seeds and berries. Bears steal about 35% of tiger kills in Sikhote-Alin and can also kill tigers.
ursus arctos lasiopus.about: The Ussuri brown bear, also known as the Ezo brown bear, or the black grizzly bear, is a subspecies of the brown bear or a population of the Eurasian brown bear (U. a. arctos).

ursus maritimus.name: Polar bear
ursus maritimus.desc: Hunts seals from the sea ice, so it depends on that ice to feed.
ursus maritimus.about: The polar bear is a large bear native to the Arctic and nearby areas. It is closely related to the brown bear, and the two species can interbreed.

ursus thibetanus.name: Asian black bear
ursus thibetanus.desc: An omnivore that eats bamboo shoots, nuts and fruit and also meat. It can prey on panda cubs.
ursus thibetanus.about: The Asian black bear, also known as the Asiatic black bear, moon bear and white-chested bear, is a medium-sized bear species native to Asia that is largely adapted to an arboreal lifestyle.

urtica dioica.name: Common nettle
urtica dioica.desc: A nutrient-loving plant of clearings and stream edges. Its leaves are the food plant of Small tortoiseshell caterpillars.
urtica dioica.about: Urtica dioica, often known as common nettle, burn nettle, stinging nettle, nettle leaf, or just a nettle or stinger, is a herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Urticaceae.

usnea.name: Tree lichens
usnea.desc: Lichens growing on trunks and branches. They are the near-total winter food of musk deer.
usnea.about: A lichen ( LY-kən, UK also LITCH-ən) is a hybrid colony of algae or cyanobacteria living symbiotically among filaments of multiple fungus species, along with bacteria embedded in the cortex, or…

uta stansburiana.name: Side-blotched lizard
uta stansburiana.desc: A small, very commonly recorded lizard that hunts insects and is prey for snakes, other lizards and hawks.
uta stansburiana.about: The common side-blotched lizard is a species of side-blotched lizard in the family Phrynosomatidae. The species is native to dry regions of the western United States and northern Mexico.

uvularia grandiflora.name: Bellwort

uvularia grandiflora.about: Uvularia grandiflora, the large-flowered bellwort or merrybells, is a species of flowering plant in the family Colchicaceae, native to eastern and central North America.

uvularia sessilifolia.name: Sessile-leaf Bellwort

vaccinium.name: Cowberry and bilberry

vaccinium and others.about: Vaccinium ( vak-SIN-ee-əm) is a common and widespread genus of shrubs or dwarf shrubs in the heath family (Ericaceae).

vaccinium angustifolium.name: Lowbush blueberry

vaccinium myrtillus.about: Vaccinium myrtillus is a holarctic species of shrub with edible fruit of blue color, known by the common names bilberry, blaeberry, and whortleberry.

vaccinium reticulatum.about: Vaccinium reticulatum, known as ʻōhelo ʻai in Hawaiian, is a species of Hawaiian Vaccinium.

vaccinium uliginosum.about: Vaccinium uliginosum is a Eurasian and North American flowering plant in the heath family. The berries are edible.
