vaccinium vitis-idaea.about: Vaccinium vitis-idaea is a small evergreen shrub in the heath family, Ericaceae. It is known colloquially as the lingonberry, partridgeberry, foxberry, mountain cranberry, or cowberry.

vachellia xanthophloea.about: Vachellia xanthophloea is a tree in the family Fabaceae, commonly known in English as the fever tree.

valley soil.name: Valley soil
valley soil.desc: Soil of the valley floor holds the mopane woodland and grassland; dung and dead matter return nutrients to it.

valley soils.name: Valley soils
valley soils.desc: Alluvial valley soils and forest litter supply nutrients to the plants.

vallisneria and potamogeton spp..name: Wild celery & pondweeds

varanus bengalensis.name: Bengal monitor
varanus bengalensis.desc: A large lizard of dry forest and scrub that eats insects and small animals and scavenges carrion.
varanus bengalensis.about: The Bengal monitor, also called the common Indian monitor, is a species of monitor lizard distributed widely in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia and West Asia.

varanus giganteus.name: Perentie
varanus giganteus.desc: Australia's largest lizard, an apex predator of rocky arid country that eats reptiles, small mammals and carrion.
varanus giganteus.about: The perentie is a species of monitor lizard. It is one of the largest living lizards, after the Komodo dragon, Asian water monitor, and the crocodile monitor.

varanus gouldii.name: Sand goanna
varanus gouldii.desc: A relentless forager on mice, small mammals, birds, lizards and eggs. Adults also eat carrion.
varanus gouldii.about: The sand goanna, also known commonly as Gould's monitor, the racehorse goanna, and the sand monitor, is a species of large Australian monitor lizard in the family Varanidae.

varanus griseus.name: Desert monitor
varanus griseus.desc: A large lizard that hunts small mammals, reptiles and insects across sand and gravel plains.
varanus griseus.about: The desert monitor is a species of monitor lizard of the order Squamata found living throughout North Africa and Central and South Asia.

varanus komodoensis.name: Komodo dragon
varanus komodoensis.desc: The largest lizard. Adults ambush deer, pigs and buffalo and also eat carrion; young eat insects, birds, eggs and small reptiles.
varanus komodoensis.about: The Komodo dragon, also known as the Komodo monitor, is a large reptile of the monitor lizard family Varanidae that is endemic to the Indonesian islands of Komodo, Rinca, Flores, Gili Dasami, and…

varanus nebulosus.name: Clouded monitor
varanus nebulosus.desc: Common large lizard of the forest that eats frogs and other small animals.
varanus nebulosus.about: The clouded monitor is a species of monitor lizard, native to Myanmar, Thailand and Laos, Vietnam, to West Malaysia, Singapore, Sumatra, and Java. They are excellent tree climbers.

varanus niloticus.name: Nile monitor
varanus niloticus.desc: A water-loving lizard recorded near the park. Eats fish, crabs, frogs, eggs, small animals and invertebrates, as well as carrion.
varanus niloticus.about: The Nile monitor is a large member of the monitor family (Varanidae) found throughout most of Sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in drier regions, and along the Nile River and its tributaries in East…

varanus salvadorii.name: Crocodile monitor
varanus salvadorii.desc: A very long arboreal lizard of lowland rainforest and mangrove swamps. It eats birds, eggs, rats, bandicoots, frogs and carrion.
varanus salvadorii.about: The crocodile monitor, also known as the Papuan monitor or Salvadori's monitor, is a species of monitor lizard endemic to New Guinea.

varanus salvator.name: Water monitor
varanus salvator.desc: A large lizard that forages along creeks and mudflats. Tiger remains in the Sundarbans have included water monitors.
varanus salvator.about: The Asian water monitor is a large varanid lizard native to South and Southeast Asia. It is widely considered to be the second-largest lizard species, after the Komodo dragon.

varanus varius.name: Lace monitor
varanus varius.desc: Mainly eats carrion but also takes eggs, birds and small mammals, and often raids brushturkey nest mounds.
varanus varius.about: The lace monitor, also known as the tree goanna, is a member of the monitor lizard family native to eastern Australia.

various cephalopods.name: Antarctic squid
various cephalopods.desc: Squid are among the animals that eat krill, and they in turn feed seals and other predators.
various cephalopods.about: A squid (pl. squid) is a mollusc with an elongated soft body, large eyes, eight arms, and two tentacles in the orders Myopsida, Oegopsida, and Bathyteuthida.

vatnajökull ice cap.name: Vatnajökull ice cap
vatnajökull ice cap.desc: Europe's largest ice cap by volume sits at the heart of the park and feeds the rivers, outwash plains and glacial lagoons around it.

vicia americana.name: Peavine
vicia americana.desc: Peavine (Vicia americana): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.
vicia americana.about: Vicia americana is a species of legume in the vetch genus known by the common names American vetch and purple vetch. It includes a subspecies known as mat vetch.

vicugna vicugna.name: Vicuña
vicugna vicugna.desc: Wild camelid that grazes low clump grasses on open plains and rests on the slopes at night. Pumas and culpeos prey on it.
vicugna vicugna.about: The vicuña or vicuna is a wild South American camelid which lives in high alpine areas of the Andes.

vigna unguiculata.name: Wild cowpeas
vigna unguiculata.desc: Climbing legumes of the savanna. Their leaves are food for caterpillars of the guinea-fowl butterfly.
vigna unguiculata.about: The cowpea is an annual herbaceous legume from the genus Vigna. It can be erect, semierect (trailing), or climbing.

vinca minor.name: Lesser Periwinkle
vinca minor.desc: Lesser Periwinkle (Vinca minor): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

viola beckwithii.name: Beckwith's violet
viola beckwithii.desc: Beckwith's violet (Viola beckwithii): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

viola canadensis.name: Canada violet
viola canadensis.desc: Canada violet (Viola canadensis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

viola eriocarpa.name: Smooth yellow forest violet
viola eriocarpa.desc: Smooth yellow forest violet (Viola eriocarpa): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

viola hastata.name: Spear-leaf violet
viola hastata.desc: Spear-leaf violet (Viola hastata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 19 times near the park in GBIF.

viola hirsutula.name: Southern wood violet
viola hirsutula.desc: Southern wood violet (Viola hirsutula): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

viola labradorica.name: American dog violet
viola labradorica.desc: American dog violet (Viola labradorica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

viola lobata.name: Pine violet
viola lobata.desc: Pine violet (Viola lobata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 142 times near the park in GBIF.

viola pedata.name: Bird-foot Violet
viola pedata.desc: Bird-foot Violet (Viola pedata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.
viola pedata.about: Viola pedata, the birdsfoot violet, bird's-foot violet, or mountain pansy, is a violet native to sandy areas in central and eastern North America.

viola pedunculata.name: California golden violet
viola pedunculata.desc: California golden violet (Viola pedunculata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 381 times near the park in GBIF.

viola rostrata.name: Long-spur violet
viola rostrata.desc: Long-spur violet (Viola rostrata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 36 times near the park in GBIF.

viola sempervirens.name: Evergreen violet
viola sempervirens.desc: Evergreen violet (Viola sempervirens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 196 times near the park in GBIF.

viola sororia.name: Bayou Violet
viola sororia.desc: Bayou Violet (Viola sororia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.
viola sororia.about: Viola sororia ( vy-OH-lə sə-ROR-ee-ə), known commonly as the common blue violet, is a short-stemmed herbaceous perennial plant native to eastern North America.

vipera ammodytes.name: Nose-horned viper
vipera ammodytes.desc: A venomous snake of rocky Balkan slopes that eats lizards, small mammals and birds.
vipera ammodytes.about: Vipera ammodytes, commonly known as horned viper, long-nosed viper, nose-horned viper, and sand viper, is a species of viper found in northern Italy, the Balkans, and parts of Asia Minor.

vipera aspis.name: Asp viper
vipera aspis.desc: Venomous snake of sunny rocky slopes. GloBI records it eating voles, lizards and small mammals.
vipera aspis.about: Vipera aspis is a viper species found in southwestern Europe. Its common names include asp, asp viper, European asp, and aspic viper, among others.

vipera berus.name: Common adder
vipera berus.desc: A venomous snake of forest edges that eats small mammals, lizards and amphibians.
vipera berus.about: Vipera berus, commonly known as the common European adder and the common European viper, is a species of venomous snake in the family Viperidae.

vireo bellii.name: Bell's Vireo
vireo bellii.desc: Bell's Vireo (Vireo bellii): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
vireo bellii.about: Bell's vireo is a songbird that migrates between a breeding range in Western North America and a winter range in Central America. It is dull olive-gray above and whitish below.

vireo gilvus.name: Warbling Vireo
vireo gilvus.desc: Warbling Vireo (Vireo gilvus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 72 times near the park in GBIF.

vireo griseus.name: White-eyed Vireo
vireo griseus.desc: White-eyed Vireo (Vireo griseus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 208 times near the park in GBIF.
vireo griseus.about: The white-eyed vireo is a small songbird of the family Vireonidae.

vireo olivaceus.name: Red-eyed Vireo
vireo olivaceus.desc: Red-eyed Vireo (Vireo olivaceus): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 73 times near the park in GBIF.
vireo olivaceus.about: The red-eyed vireo is a small American songbird. It is somewhat warbler-like but not closely related to the New World warblers (Parulidae).

vireo solitarius.name: Blue-headed Vireo
vireo solitarius.desc: Blue-headed Vireo (Vireo solitarius): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.

virgin river.name: Virgin River
virgin river.desc: Its North Fork carved Zion Canyon, and the river corridor supports cottonwood, willow and boxelder along its banks.

vitellaria paradoxa.name: Shea tree
vitellaria paradoxa.desc: A savanna tree whose fruit is eaten by fruit bats and baboons in GloBI records.
vitellaria paradoxa.about: Vitellaria paradoxa, commonly known as shea tree, shi tree (, also ), or vitellaria, is a tree of the family Sapotaceae. It is the only species in the genus Vitellaria, and is indigenous to Africa.

vitis aestivalis.name: Summer Grape
vitis aestivalis.desc: Summer Grape (Vitis aestivalis): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 2 times near the park in GBIF.

vitis arizonica.name: Canyon grape
vitis arizonica.desc: Canyon grape (Vitis arizonica): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 9 times near the park in GBIF.

vitis riparia.name: River-Bank Grape
vitis riparia.desc: River-Bank Grape (Vitis riparia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 22 times near the park in GBIF.

vitis rotundifolia.name: Muscadine Grape
vitis rotundifolia.desc: Muscadine Grape (Vitis rotundifolia): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 3 times near the park in GBIF.

vitis vinifera.name: Grape vine
vitis vinifera.desc: Wild and grown vines on the sunny shores. GloBI records link its fruit to foxes, bears, martens and dormice.
vitis vinifera.about: Vitis vinifera, the common grape vine, is a species of flowering plant, native to the Mediterranean region, Central Europe, and southwestern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal north to southern Germany…

vittaria lineata.name: Shoestring Fern
vittaria lineata.desc: Shoestring Fern (Vittaria lineata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 21 times near the park in GBIF.

volcanic ash soil.name: Volcanic ash soil
volcanic ash soil.desc: Ash and pumice from the eruption of Mount Mazama left sandy, fast-draining soils that hold little water.

volcanic island soils.name: Volcanic island soils
volcanic island soils.desc: Thin soils over rugged volcanic hills support the savanna grasses and dry deciduous woodland of the islands.

volcanic mountain soil.name: Volcanic mountain soil
volcanic mountain soil.desc: Thin, young soils built on volcanic rock and glacial debris support the forests and meadows.

volcanic soil.name: Volcanic soil
volcanic soil.desc: Young lava and ash soils hold the nutrients the plants draw on, and are returned by decomposers.

volcanic soils.name: Volcanic soils
volcanic soils.desc: Pumice and ash soils are nutrient-poor, but red tussock tolerates them across the volcanic plateau.

vombatus ursinus.name: Common wombat
vombatus ursinus.desc: A burrowing grazer of grass and other plants. Its tunnels are used by many other animals and its digging turns over the soil.
vombatus ursinus.about: The common wombat, also known as the bare-nosed wombat, is a marsupial, one of three extant species of wombats and the sole extant member of the genus Vombatus.

vossia cuspidata.name: Hippo grass
vossia cuspidata.desc: A robust floodplain grass of the Sudd that grows in deeper water and is a main swamp plant.
vossia cuspidata.about: Vossia is a monotypic genus in the grass family, found in Asia and Africa.

vulpes corsac.name: Corsac fox
vulpes corsac.desc: A small steppe fox that hunts jerboas, hares and waterbirds, with GloBI records of these meals.
vulpes corsac.about: The Corsac fox, also known as a corsac, is a medium-sized fox found in steppes, semi-deserts and deserts in Central Asia, ranging into Mongolia and northern China.

vulpes lagopus.name: Arctic fox
vulpes lagopus.desc: Hunts lemmings, raids nests and follows polar bears and wolves to scavenge.
vulpes lagopus.about: The Arctic fox, also known as the white fox, polar fox, or snow fox, is a small species of fox native to the Arctic regions of the Northern Hemisphere and common throughout the Arctic tundra.

vulpes macrotis.name: Kit fox
vulpes macrotis.desc: A small nocturnal fox that mainly eats rodents, notably kangaroo rats, plus rabbits, reptiles, insects and carrion.
vulpes macrotis.about: The kit fox is a fox species that inhabits arid and semi-arid regions of the Southwestern United States and northern and central Mexico.

vulpes velox.name: Swift fox
vulpes velox.desc: A small desert fox. GloBI records it eating rodents such as brush mice and cotton rats.
vulpes velox.about: The swift fox is a small light orange-tan fox around the size of a domestic cat found in the western Great Plains grasslands of North America, such as Montana, Colorado, New Mexico, Kansas, Oklahoma…

vulpes vulpes.name: Red fox
vulpes vulpes.desc: Red fox (Vulpes vulpes): hunts or scavenges other animals. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
vulpes vulpes.about: The red fox is the largest of the true foxes, and the most widely distributed member of the order Carnivora.

vulpes vulpes necator.name: Sierra Nevada red fox
vulpes vulpes necator.desc: A rare montane fox with a small Lassen population. Its diet is mostly rodents and mule deer, plus birds, insects and manzanita berries.
vulpes vulpes necator.about: The Sierra Nevada red fox, also known as the High Sierra fox, is a subspecies of red fox found in the Oregon Cascades and the Sierra Nevada.

vulpes zerda.name: Fennec fox
vulpes zerda.desc: A small, omnivorous fox with big ears. In Algeria it eats insects, small vertebrates and date palm fruit.
vulpes zerda.about: The fennec fox is a small fox native to the deserts of North Africa, ranging from Western Sahara and Mauritania to the Sinai Peninsula.

vultur gryphus.name: Andean condor
vultur gryphus.desc: A huge scavenger that glides over the steppe and ice field, feeding on carcasses of guanacos, hares and livestock.
vultur gryphus.about: The Andean condor is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur. It is found in the Andes mountains and adjacent Pacific coasts of western South America.

waisila creek.name: Waisila Creek
waisila creek.desc: Streams and pools run through the reserve and feed the creeks and rivers downstream.

warm clear ocean water.name: Warm clear ocean water
warm clear ocean water.desc: The northern Florida Reef sits in warm subtropical water; the park protects the reef section that makes up about half its area.

warm clear water.name: Warm clear water
warm clear water.desc: Warm, nutrient-poor water from the Gulf Stream system keeps the water clear. A 1977 cold snap killed about 96% of shallow branching coral here.

warm lagoon water.name: Warm lagoon water
warm lagoon water.desc: The enclosed lagoon is shallow, averaging about 25 m deep, and warm and clear enough for reef corals and seagrass to thrive.

warm sea temperature.name: Warm sea temperature
warm sea temperature.desc: Corals live in a narrow warm band. Marine heat waves cause bleaching, which hit the Belize reef in 1998.

warm shallow sea.name: Warm shallow sea
warm shallow sea.desc: The Red Sea around the islands is warm and salty, with shallow banks where seagrass beds and coral grow.

warm subtropical sea.name: Warm subtropical sea
warm subtropical sea.desc: Warm, clear open ocean around the islands supports reef algae, plankton and the fish that seabirds and whales feed on.

warm sunlight.name: Warm sunlight
warm sunlight.desc: Year-round warmth and light in the subtropical latitudes support tall, layered forest growth.

warm, salty red sea water.name: Warm, salty Red Sea water
warm, salty red sea water.desc: The enclosed Red Sea is warm and salty, and its clear water carries drifting plankton across the shallow shelf around the islands.

warm, shallow, sheltered bay.name: Warm, shallow, sheltered bay
warm, shallow, sheltered bay.desc: The bay is shallow, about 9 m deep on average, and its sheltered sandy floors carry some of the largest seagrass meadows known.

washingtonia filifera.name: California fan palm
washingtonia filifera.desc: The only palm native to California; grows in the park only at oases with year-round water.
washingtonia filifera.about: Washingtonia filifera, commonly known as the California fan palm, cotton palm or desert fan palm, is a flowering plant in the family Arecaceae, native to the far southwestern United States and…

wasmannia auropunctata.name: Forest ants
wasmannia auropunctata.desc: Ants are abundant in the leaf litter and on plants. They take nectar and sugary foods and are a main prey for small lizards, frogs and birds.
wasmannia auropunctata.about: The little fire ant, also known as the electric ant, is a small (approx 1.5 mm (1⁄16 in) long), light to golden brown (ginger) social ant native to Central and South America, now spread to parts of…

water.name: River pools
water.desc: The Arly, Pendjari and Mekrou rivers and their pools hold water for animals in the dry season and feed the riverside forest.

waterholes & pans.name: Waterholes & pans
waterholes & pans.desc: Shallow pans and waterholes. In the dry winter, wildebeest, zebra and impala gather at them.

waterlogged peat.name: Waterlogged peat
waterlogged peat.desc: Peat layers built up over thousands of years underlie the bogs and marshes; they hold water and nutrients that the plants draw on.

weinmannia.name: Weinmannia
weinmannia.desc: A cloud-forest tree genus, with Weinmannia pinnata among the broadleaf trees reported in the park.
weinmannia.about: Weinmannia is a genus of trees and shrubs in the family Cunoniaceae.

welwitschia mirabilis.name: Welwitschia
welwitschia mirabilis.desc: A long-lived plant with two strap-like leaves. It takes up moisture from fog as well as from groundwater.
welwitschia mirabilis.about: Welwitschia is a monotypic genus of gnetophytes containing only the species Welwitschia mirabilis. It is named after the Austrian botanist Friedrich Welwitsch, who documented the plant in the 1850s.

westerly rain.name: Westerly rain
westerly rain.desc: Moist westerly winds off the Tasman Sea drop more than seven metres of rain a year on much of the park, feeding the temperate rainforest.

westerly rain and snow.name: Westerly rain and snow
westerly rain and snow.desc: The Andes catch Pacific moisture on the west side, leaving the steppe to the east dry. This sets the line between forest and grassland.

wet coastal ground.name: Wet coastal ground
wet coastal ground.desc: Tussac forms dense stands on wet ground close to the shore, and dead plant matter and seabird waste are recycled there.

wet river valleys and meadows.name: Wet river valleys and meadows
wet river valleys and meadows.desc: The forest sits on the Baltic-Black Sea watershed and holds river valleys and wetlands. UNESCO notes that wet meadows need continued water flow and management.

wet, windswept soil.name: Wet, windswept soil
wet, windswept soil.desc: Kerguelen cabbage grows where soil water stays high, in a climate with constant wind.

wet-season rain.name: Wet-season rain
wet-season rain.desc: Rain falls mainly from May to November and feeds the grasslands, lakes and the Harenna Forest.

wet-season rain and floods.name: Wet-season rain and floods
wet-season rain and floods.desc: About 1,100 mm of rain falls a year, mostly June to November, and the Pendjari River floods seasonally.

wet-season rains.name: Wet-season rains
wet-season rains.desc: Rain falls mostly in the wet season, and the Cerrado has a strong dry season from about April to September.

white nile flood pulse.name: White Nile flood pulse
white nile flood pulse.desc: Water from upstream spreads across the flat clay plain each wet season, flooding the swamp and shrinking back in the dry season. It sets which plants grow where.

wildfire.name: Wildfire
wildfire.desc: A natural recurring disturbance that renews the forest and opens jack pine cones. It creates young forest where aspen, berries and moose food thrive.

wildland fire.name: Wildland fire
wildland fire.desc: Shortleaf pine responds well to fire, which reduces competing trees and prepares soil for seedlings. Fire management is part of the park's work.

windblown sediment.name: Windblown sediment
windblown sediment.desc: Sediment blown in from the continent adds nutrients and organic matter to the shallow sea.

winter & monsoon rain.name: Winter & monsoon rain
winter & monsoon rain.desc: Two rainy seasons, winter rain and the summer monsoon, give this desert unusually rich plant life.

winter and monsoon rain.name: Winter and monsoon rain
winter and monsoon rain.desc: Two rainy seasons feed the desert, and water is one of the main reasons it holds so many species. Washes run only after storms and can flash flood.

winter burning.name: Winter burning
winter burning.desc: Park staff burn tall grass in winter, and animals gather on the burnt patches to eat new shoots.

winter cold.name: Winter cold
winter cold.desc: Joshua tree blooming depends on timely rain and a winter freeze.

winter ice.name: Winter ice
winter ice.desc: The lake is frozen for about four to five months, and the clear ice lets light in for under-ice algae. Seals dig dens in it.

winter rain.name: Winter rain
winter rain.desc: Most rain on the islands falls in the cooler months, which sets the growing season for scrub and wildflowers.

winter rain and flash floods.name: Winter rain and flash floods
winter rain and flash floods.desc: Rain is scarce because mountain ranges block moisture. Rare wet winters trigger wildflower blooms and brief shallow lakes on the valley floor.

winter rain and rain shadow.name: Winter rain and rain shadow
winter rain and rain shadow.desc: Rain falls mostly in winter and drops steeply from the Judean hills to the Dead Sea side, a rain shadow effect that makes the eastern slopes desert.

winter rain and snow.name: Winter rain and snow
winter rain and snow.desc: Most of the range's precipitation falls in winter; around 790 mm a year at Prodromos on the high slopes.

winter rainfall.name: Winter rainfall
winter rainfall.desc: Mediterranean climate with rain falling mostly in winter, which suits fynbos plants.

winter snow.name: Winter snow
winter snow.desc: Deep mountain snow covers the high meadows for months and pushes grazers down into the forest; meltwater feeds the slopes in spring.

winter snow and frost.name: Winter snow and frost
winter snow and frost.desc: Snowfall and hard frost shape the high plateau, and snowmelt feeds the streams and pools that supply water downstream.

winter snow and ice.name: Winter snow and ice
winter snow and ice.desc: Snow lies long on the high massif and pushes chamois and other animals down to forest in winter. A relict ice cave records past glaciation.

winter snow cover.name: Winter snow cover
winter snow cover.desc: Deep winter snow covers the ground plants and small mammals live under, and makes food hard to reach for grazers and ground-feeding birds.

winter snowpack.name: Winter snowpack
winter snowpack.desc: Crater Lake gets several metres of snow a year and it lingers for about eight months. It waters the slopes as it melts and feeds the lake.

wisteria frutescens.name: American wisteria
wisteria frutescens.desc: American wisteria (Wisteria frutescens): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

woody lianas and saplings.name: Understory shrubs and vines
woody lianas and saplings.desc: Shrubs and woody vines are staple foods for okapi, which browse leaves and buds of many such plants.
woody lianas and saplings.about: A liana ( lee-ANN-ə, also -⁠AH-nə) is a long-stemmed woody vine that is rooted in the soil at ground level and uses trees, as well as other means of vertical support, to climb up to the canopy in…

xanthippus corallipes.name: Grasshoppers
xanthippus corallipes.desc: Chew leaves of shrubs and flowers through summer and feed lizards and birds.
xanthippus corallipes.about: Grasshoppers are a group of insects belonging to the suborder Caelifera.

xanthisma spinulosum.name: Cut-leaf ironplant
xanthisma spinulosum.desc: Cut-leaf ironplant (Xanthisma spinulosum): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 79 times near the park in GBIF.
xanthisma spinulosum.about: Xanthisma spinulosum, the spiny goldenweed, is a species of flowering plant of the genus Xanthisma native to western North America.

xanthocephalus xanthocephalus.name: Yellow-headed Blackbird
xanthocephalus xanthocephalus.desc: Yellow-headed Blackbird (Xanthocephalus xanthocephalus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 802 times near the park in GBIF.
xanthocephalus xanthocephalus.about: The yellow-headed blackbird is a medium-sized blackbird with a yellow head. It is the only member of the genus Xanthocephalus.

xerospermophilus tereticaudus.name: Round-tailed Ground Squirrel
xerospermophilus tereticaudus.desc: Round-tailed Ground Squirrel (Xerospermophilus tereticaudus): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.
xerospermophilus tereticaudus.about: The round-tailed ground squirrel, known as "Ardillón cola redonda" in Spanish, live in the desert of the Southwestern United States and Northwestern Mexico.

xestospongia muta.name: Giant barrel sponge
xestospongia muta.desc: A reef sponge that filters tiny particles from the water. Sponges are the main food of hawksbill turtles.
xestospongia muta.about: The giant barrel sponge is the largest species of sponge found growing on Caribbean coral reefs.

xyleborus.name: Ambrosia beetles
xyleborus.desc: Wood-boring beetles recorded in large numbers on the island; they tunnel into woody plants and farm fungus in the galleries.

xylocopa californica.name: California Carpenter Bee
xylocopa californica.desc: California Carpenter Bee (Xylocopa californica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

xylocopa virginica.name: Carpenter bee
xylocopa virginica.desc: Carpenter bee (Xylocopa virginica): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 4 times near the park in GBIF.
xylocopa virginica.about: Xylocopa virginica, sometimes referred to as the eastern carpenter bee, is a species of bee that extends through the eastern United States and into Canada.

xylopia.name: Xylopia
xylopia.desc: Pepper-fruit trees of the forest. GloBI records show Xylopia quintasii eaten by red colobus, Diana monkeys and mangabeys.
xylopia.about: Xylopia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Annonaceae. The genus primarily consists of trees, with some species also being shrubs.

xyphon triguttatum.name: Xyphon triguttatum
xyphon triguttatum.desc: Xyphon triguttatum (Xyphon triguttatum): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 151 times near the park in GBIF.

year-round rain.name: Year-round rain
year-round rain.desc: About 1,700 to 2,200 mm falls each year. The south has no real dry season.

young soils.name: Young soils
young soils.desc: Thin soils left behind by ice build up as plants grow and die and as nitrogen is added.

yucca baccata.name: Banana yucca
yucca baccata.desc: Banana yucca (Yucca baccata): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 113 times near the park in GBIF.
yucca baccata.about: Yucca baccata is a common species of yucca native to the deserts of the Southwestern United States and three states in Northern Mexico.

yucca brevifolia.name: Joshua tree
yucca brevifolia.desc: The park namesake, dominant in the open Mojave areas. Pollinated by yucca moths, its seeds are moved by ground squirrels.
yucca brevifolia.about: Yucca brevifolia, commonly known as the Joshua tree, yucca palm, tree yucca, or palm tree yucca, is a plant species belonging to the genus Yucca.

yucca elata.name: Soaptree yucca
yucca elata.desc: A tall succulent that stores water through hot summers and helps hold the dune edges in place. Yucca moth larvae bore into its trunk.
yucca elata.about: Yucca elata is a perennial plant, with common names that include soaptree, soaptree yucca, soapweed, and palmella.

yucca glauca.name: Bear-grass
yucca glauca.desc: Soapweed yucca (Yucca glauca): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 13 times near the park in GBIF.
yucca glauca.about: Yucca glauca is a species of perennial evergreen plant, adapted to xeric (dry) growth conditions.

yucca harrimaniae.name: Harriman's yucca
yucca harrimaniae.desc: Harriman's yucca (Yucca harrimaniae): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 15 times near the park in GBIF.

yucca schidigera.name: Mohave yucca
yucca schidigera.desc: Mohave yucca (Yucca schidigera): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 148 times near the park in GBIF.
yucca schidigera.about: Yucca schidigera, also known as the Mojave yucca or Spanish dagger, is a perennial plant in the asparagus family Asparagaceae, native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico.

yushania alpina.name: Mountain bamboo
yushania alpina.desc: Forms a nearly continuous belt above the forest, thinner on the drier north side, and shades out most other plants.
yushania alpina.about: Oldeania alpina, the African alpine bamboo, is a perennial bamboo of the family Poaceae and the genus Oldeania.

yushania niitakayamensis.name: Yushan cane
yushania niitakayamensis.desc: A hardy bamboo of the high mountains that forms dense grassy stands in the subalpine and alpine zone, an open ground-level food source for browsers.
yushania niitakayamensis.about: Yushania is a genus of bamboo in the grass family. Recent classification systems place Yushania in the tribe Arundinarieae.

zaglossus bruijnii.name: Long-beaked echidna
zaglossus bruijnii.desc: An egg-laying mammal of hill and montane forest that feeds mainly on earthworms, unlike the ant-eating short-beaked echidna.
zaglossus bruijnii.about: The western long-beaked echidna, also called Bruijin's long-beaked echidna, is one of the four extant echidnas and one of three species of Zaglossus that occurs in New Guinea.

zalophus californianus.name: California sea lion
zalophus californianus.desc: Hunts fish around kelp forest edges and is a main target of white sharks off California.
zalophus californianus.about: The California sea lion is a coastal eared seal native to western North America. It is one of six species of sea lions.

zalophus wollebaeki.name: Galápagos sea lion
zalophus wollebaeki.desc: Eats mainly sardines plus squid, octopus and crustaceans. Sharks hunt it, and its numbers fall when El Niño drives away its prey.
zalophus wollebaeki.about: The Galápagos sea lion is a species of sea lion that lives and breeds on the Galápagos Islands and, in smaller numbers, on Isla de la Plata (Ecuador). They are the smallest sea lion species.

zambezi floodwater.name: Zambezi floodwater
zambezi floodwater.desc: After the rains the floodplain becomes a set of lakes and pools. As they shrink, big animals gather near the water that is left.

zanda funerea.name: Yellow-tailed black cockatoo
zanda funerea.desc: A large cockatoo that feeds on seeds, including those of silver wattle.
zanda funerea.about: The yellow-tailed black cockatoo is a large cockatoo native to the south-east of Australia measuring 55–65 cm (22–26 in) in length. It has a short crest on the top of its head.

zapus hudsonius.name: Meadow jumping mouse
zapus hudsonius.desc: Meadow jumping mouse (Zapus hudsonius): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 1 times near the park in GBIF.

zapus princeps.name: Western Jumping Mouse
zapus princeps.desc: Western Jumping Mouse (Zapus princeps): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 10 times near the park in GBIF.
zapus princeps.about: The western jumping mouse, is a species of rodent in the family Zapodidae. It is found in Canada and the United States.

zea mays.name: Maize
zea mays.desc: A farm crop around the lake. GloBI records show wood mice and brown bears eating it.
zea mays.about: Maize, also known as corn, is a tall stout grass that produces cereal grain.

zenaida asiatica.name: White-winged Dove
zenaida asiatica.desc: One of the most commonly recorded birds in the park area. It eats seeds and fruit and is taken by coyotes.
zenaida asiatica.about: The white-winged dove is a dove whose native range extends from the Southwestern United States through Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean.

zenaida auriculata.name: Eared dove
zenaida auriculata.desc: A seed-eating dove found in open country, and a common prey bird for small raptors.
zenaida auriculata.about: The eared dove is a New World dove. It is a resident breeder throughout South America from Colombia to southern Argentina and Chile, and on the offshore islands from the Grenadines southwards.

zenaida macroura.name: Mourning Dove
zenaida macroura.desc: Mourning Dove (Zenaida macroura): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 60 times near the park in GBIF.
zenaida macroura.about: The mourning dove is a member of the dove family, Columbidae. The bird is also known as the American mourning dove, the rain dove, and colloquially as the turtle dove, and it was once known as the…

zephyranthes atamasco.name: Atamasco Lily
zephyranthes atamasco.desc: Atamasco Lily (Zephyranthes atamasco): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 5 times near the park in GBIF.
zephyranthes atamasco.about: Zephyranthes atamasca, commonly known as the atamasco lily, occasionally as the Easter lily or more generally a rain-lily, is native to the Southern United States.

zinnia grandiflora.name: Rocky Mountain zinnia
zinnia grandiflora.desc: Rocky Mountain zinnia (Zinnia grandiflora): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 107 times near the park in GBIF.
zinnia grandiflora.about: Zinnia grandiflora is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae known by the common names Rocky Mountain zinnia and plains zinnia. It produces a subshrub with yellow-orange flowers.

zizia aurea.name: Golden alexanders
zizia aurea.desc: Golden alexanders (Zizia aurea): a plant that turns sunlight into food. Recorded 6 times near the park in GBIF.

ziziphus mauritiana.name: Indian jujube
ziziphus mauritiana.desc: A thorny dry-country fruit tree recorded in the area, offering fruit to birds and mammals.
ziziphus mauritiana.about: Ziziphus mauritiana, also known as Indian jujube, Indian plum, Chinese apple, ber (Hindi: बेर) and dunks, is a tropical, spiny, evergreen shrub or small tree in the buckthorn family Rhamnaceae.

ziziphus mucronata.name: Buffalo thorn
ziziphus mucronata.desc: A thorny savanna tree whose fruit and leaves are eaten by many animals.
ziziphus mucronata.about: Ziziphus mucronata, known as the buffalo thorn, is a species of tree in the family Rhamnaceae, native to southern Africa. It is deciduous and may grow up to 17 metres tall.

zonotrichia albicollis.name: White-throated Sparrow
zonotrichia albicollis.desc: White-throated Sparrow (Zonotrichia albicollis): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 338 times near the park in GBIF.
zonotrichia albicollis.about: The white-throated sparrow is a passerine bird of the New World sparrow family Passerellidae. It breeds in northern North America and winters in the southern United States.

zonotrichia capensis.name: Rufous-collared sparrow
zonotrichia capensis.desc: A very common small bird that eats seeds, insects and fruit, including hedge cactus fruit.
zonotrichia capensis.about: The rufous-collared sparrow or Andean sparrow is an American sparrow found in a wide range of habitats, often near humans, from the extreme south-east of Mexico to Tierra del Fuego, and the island of…

zonotrichia leucophrys.name: White-crowned Sparrow
zonotrichia leucophrys.desc: White-crowned Sparrow (Zonotrichia leucophrys): eats plants or other primary food sources. Recorded 2,500 times near the park in GBIF.
zonotrichia leucophrys.about: The white-crowned sparrow is a species of passerine bird native to North America.

zooplankton.name: Zooplankton
zooplankton.desc: Drifting animals that graze phytoplankton and feed small fish.
zooplankton.about: Zooplankton are the heterotrophic component of the planktonic community, having to consume other organisms to thrive.

zostera japonica.name: Dwarf eelgrass
zostera japonica.desc: A seagrass recorded in GBIF near the bay. Seagrass beds shelter young fish and feed grazers, and have been lost to jetty building.
zostera japonica.about: Zostera japonica is a species of aquatic plant in the Zosteraceae family.

zostera marina.name: Eelgrass
zostera marina.desc: A flowering seagrass of sheltered flats. Meadows give young animals cover, and shore crabs eat its seeds.
zostera marina.about: Zostera marina is a flowering vascular plant species as one of many kinds of seagrass, with this species known primarily by the English name of common eelgrass or eelgrass, with seawrack much less…

zostera noltei.name: Dwarf eelgrass
zostera noltei.desc: Seagrass of sheltered intertidal flats; its beds shelter invertebrates and young fish, and its dead leaves enrich the sediment.
zostera noltei.about: Zostera noltii is a species of seagrass known by the common name dwarf eelgrass.

zosterops japonicus.name: Japanese white-eye
zosterops japonicus.desc: A very common introduced songbird that eats berries, nectar and insects. It is prey for cats and owls.
zosterops japonicus.about: The Japanese white-eye is a former species designation of birds in the white-eye family.

zosterops lateralis.name: Silvereye
zosterops lateralis.desc: A small bird eating fruit, nectar and insects. It is one of the most commonly recorded birds on the island.
zosterops lateralis.about: The silvereye or wax-eye, also known by its Māori name tauhou, is a very small omnivorous passerine bird of the south-west Pacific.
